0003aa60-b9ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cavendish Astrophysics Group Ryle Radio Telescope is a 5-kilometer array telescope located at the Mullard Radio Astronomy Observatory in Europe, operating within the radio waveband.
0003aa60-b9ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Cavendish Astrophysics Group Ryle Radio Telescope (5 km Array) at Mullard Radio Astronomy Observatory

00138094-b91c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Large Monolithic Imager (LMI)** is a high-resolution CCD camera with 6144x6150 pixels, each 15 micrometers square, providing a field of view of 12.3 x 12.3 arcminutes and a pixel scale of 0.120"/pixel, currently featuring a known bad column at position 1597 when binned 2x2.
00138094-b91c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Large Monolithic Imager on Discovery Channel 4.3m Telescope

00222d88-b129-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover rear Hazard Avoidance Cameras (Hazcams), specifically the right camera labeled as "rhaz_right_a," are designed to assist with navigation and safety during the rover's movement on Mars by providing high-resolution images to detect potential obstacles behind the rover.
00222d88-b129-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Rear Hazard Avoidance Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

00226540-b79c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Fluxgate Magnetometer for Average Fields** (also known as experiment E3) on Helios-A is a boom-mounted, triaxial fluxgate magnetometer designed to measure magnetic fields with high precision, featuring an automatic range switching system and a sensor flipper for zero level determination.
00226540-b79c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer for Average Fields part of Helios-A

0023ab4a-b6b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RF-15I instrument on the Interball Tail Probe is a photometer designed to study solar flare X-ray radiation, featuring soft and hard X-ray detectors and a tomograph for imaging solar flare emissions.
0023ab4a-b6b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Soft and Hard X-Ray Photometer on Interball Tail Probe

0029c69c-b5de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Exploration Rover (MER) mission, launched in 2003, involved two rovers, Spirit and Opportunity, which explored the Martian surface to investigate signs of past water activity and conduct geological studies.
0029c69c-b5de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Exploration Rover Mission

002c6978-b904-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mercury Surface, Space Environment, Geochemistry and Ranging (MESSENGER) mission was a NASA space probe designed to study the characteristics and environment of Mercury from orbit. Launched in 2004, MESSENGER became the first spacecraft to orbit Mercury in 2011 and collected data until its planned impact on the planet's surface in 2015.
002c6978-b904-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma Ray Spectrometer on Mercury Surface, Space Environment, Geochemistry and Ranging

0041dee2-b5f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tampa Geomagnetic Observatory (TPA), located in Tampa, Florida, is a ground-based facility part of the IUGONET observatories network. It specializes in geomagnetic measurements using instruments such as magnetometers.
0041dee2-b5f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tampa Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

004a92f0-b62e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: San José dos Campos was a ground-based observatory in São Paulo, Brazil, operational from 1973 to 1975, equipped with magnetometers for geomagnetic field measurements.
004a92f0-b62e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at São José dos Campos Observatory, Brazil

004ad6d0-ba6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Phutuy is a ground-based magnetometer observatory located in Gia Lâm District, Hà Nội, Vietnam, which has been operational since January 1978.
004ad6d0-ba6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Phutuy Observatory, Vietnam

004c67ca-b9a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Oakley Southern Sky Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Coonabarabran Airport in New South Wales, Australia. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to studying the southern sky.
004c67ca-b9a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Oakley Southern Sky Observatory, Australia

005431e8-b8ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Aerosol Collector Pyrolyser (ACP)** on the Huygens Probe was an instrument designed to collect and analyze aerosols in Titan's atmosphere at different altitudes, using pyrolysis to vaporize volatiles and separate organic materials for chemical composition analysis.
005431e8-b8ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Aerosol Collector Pyrolyser on Huygens Probe

00559d76-b7be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetometers at Watheroo (WAT) were instruments used to measure the Earth's magnetic field from 1919 to 1958 as part of the IAGA investigation.
00559d76-b7be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Watheroo Observatory

006272f8-b5e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Chandrayaan-2 Orbiter**: An Indian spacecraft designed to orbit the Moon and conduct detailed remote sensing of its surface, part of India's Chandrayaan-2 mission launched in 2019. It carries multiple instruments for mapping lunar topography, mineralogy, and other scientific studies.
006272f8-b5e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: CHANDRAYAAN-2 ORBITER

0064cc96-b7c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fluxgate Magnetometer (FGM) on Cluster-3 is an instrument used to measure the magnetic field in space. It consists of two triaxial fluxgate magnetometers and a data processing unit, with one sensor located at the end of a radial boom to minimize magnetic interference from the spacecraft.
0064cc96-b7c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer on Cluster-3

008cce90-b64c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** H68 is a ground-based observatory station equipped with an automated magnetometer, located near Syowa Station in Antarctica at coordinates -69.2 latitude and 41.05 longitude.
008cce90-b64c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Syowa Station, Antarctica

008d4134-bb6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EISCAT Digital Camera Imager is an instrument located at the EISCAT Tromsø radar site, designed to capture digital images within a hut.
008d4134-bb6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager part of European Incoherent Scatter Scientific Association

009309b0-b8b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Godthaab observatory (IAGA identifier GHB), operational from 1883 to 1941 as part of the IAGA investigation.
009309b0-b8b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Godthaab Observatory

009d6266-b997-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Observatorio Arcosur** is a ground-based observatory located at Avenida Canal de Izas in the Arcosur district of Zaragoza, Spain. It facilitates astronomical observations and research activities within Europe.
009d6266-b997-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Arcosur, Zaragoza

009fa848-b8fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The pLIBS Z-903 is a portable, hand-held instrument developed by SciAps for Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS). It is used to collect spectra from reference targets under ambient atmospheric conditions.
009fa848-b8fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Portable Laser Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy Z903

00a5011c-bbb1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Fort Conger is a ground-based observatory located in the Qikiqtaaluk Region, Nunavut, Canada. It operates as part of the IAGA Observatories network and features a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements, having been established since 1883.
00a5011c-bbb1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fort Conger Observatory, Canada

00af3a84-b629-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The MAO Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Chaabet Ain Laqsab, Benslimane Province, Morocco. It is situated on Earth at coordinates 33.601394° N, 7.017970° W and serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
00af3a84-b629-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Chaabet Ain Laqsab

00c98bbc-b883-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Inuvik station with the IAGA identifier INK, part of the neutron monitor observatory in Bartol.
00c98bbc-b883-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Inuvik

00cbcd14-b860-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High-Energy Neutral Atom Imager (HENA) on the IMAGE spacecraft is designed to observe Earth's magnetospheric environment by detecting and imaging neutral atoms in the energy range of 10-500 keV, providing insights into their velocity, trajectory, energy, and mass.
00cbcd14-b860-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High-Energy Neutral Atom Imager on IMAGE

00d38740-b836-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Stone Edge Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in El Verano, California, dedicated to ground-based observations.
00d38740-b836-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stone Edge Observatory, United States

00d47ea4-b618-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Taurus Hill Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Kangaslampi, Varkaus, Finland. Operated by the Warkauden Kassiopeia society and opened in 2004, it is used for ground-based observations and research.
00d47ea4-b618-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Taurus Hill Observatory, Finland

00d62f6c-b661-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at Valentia Observatory is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of Earth's magnetic field, operational since January 1899 as part of the IAGA investigation.
00d62f6c-b661-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kyoto Observatory

00ef6644-b7d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The EISCAT Tromsø VHF Radar is an incoherent scatter radar system operated by the EISCAT Scientific Association, used to study electron density and temperature, as well as ion density, temperature, and velocity in the Earth's upper atmosphere. It is part of a network located primarily in Northern Scandinavia and Svalbard, with this particular radar situated near Tromsø, Norway.
00ef6644-b7d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VHF Radar at EISCAT Observatory, Norway

00f02224-bb38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Space Environmental Monitor (SEM) on NOAA 13 was an instrument designed to measure proton and electron fluxes and energy spectra in the upper atmosphere. It included two main components: the Total Energy Detector (TED) for measuring particles between 300 eV and 20 keV, and the Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector (MEPED) for higher energy ranges up to >60 MeV.
00f02224-bb38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Environmental Monitor on NOAA 13

00f49b46-b7ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1H X-ray Instrument (XRI)** is a scintillation detector designed to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It operates within an energy range from 10 keV to 10 MeV, utilizing a NaI crystal scintillator and a photomultiplier tube for detection.
00f49b46-b7ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-Ray Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

00fb6014-b84d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2A magnetometer (TCM2) is a three-axis instrument designed to measure magnetic field components with high resolution. It is used aboard the BARREL payloads to detect substorm activity and ULF oscillations, aiding in the study of relativistic electron losses in near-Earth space.
00fb6014-b84d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

00fbfcaa-b5e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Valdivia (VLD) Geomagnetic Observatory** is a ground-based facility located in Mariquina, Provincia de Valdivia, Chile, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity.
00fbfcaa-b5e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Valdivia, Chile

00ff9e36-b7ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at CNT is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument located in Cañete, Peru, designed to measure magnetic field variations as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
00ff9e36-b7ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observatory

0101f5d6-b862-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Sagastyr is a ground-based observatory located in the Sakha Republic, Russia, primarily known for its magnetometer instrument used to study geomagnetic activity. It has been operational since 1883 and is part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network.
0101f5d6-b862-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sagastyr Observatory, Russia

0103f688-bac4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Herrsching Observatory (MPC ID: 564) is an astronomical observatory located in Badeweg, Hechendorf, Seefeld, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
0103f688-bac4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Herrsching Observatory, Germany

010b0298-b821-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The ALICE instrument is a far-UV imaging spectrograph onboard the Rosetta spacecraft, designed to perform spectroscopy in the 700-2050 angstrom range with high spectral resolution using a holographic reflection grating and microchannel plate detector.
010b0298-b821-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Far Ultraviolet Alice Spectrometer on Rosetta Orbiter

010dfba8-bae0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Entity Definition**:

"Suisei," meaning "Comet" in Japanese, was a spacecraft launched on August 18, 1985 to fly by Comet P/Halley and conduct UV imaging of its hydrogen corona. It operated until it was lost behind the Sun in August 20, 1992, and had plans for additional comet encounters before hydrazine depletion in 1991 led to their cancellation.
010dfba8-bae0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: UV Imaging System and Solar Wind Instrument on Suisei

012380ee-bb4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A VLF/ELF crossed loop antenna is an instrument used for detecting very low frequency and extremely low frequency electromagnetic signals. This particular antenna, located in Kagoshima, Japan, features a two-turn design with a 15-meter tower and was operational from 2001 to October 2009.
012380ee-bb4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Low Frequency / Extremely Low Frequency Crossed Loop Antenna part of IUGONET Observatory, Japan

0134c984-b6aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Entity Definition:** The CTIO 1.5-meter Cassegrain spectrograph is an ultraviolet transmitting grating spectrograph used at the f/7.5 focus, with a plate scale of 18.1 arcseconds/mm, and is identical to a similar instrument at Kitt Peak National Observatory.
0134c984-b6aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory 1.5m Cassegrain Spectrograph at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory

01383f3c-bb83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISEE Magnetometer station at Paratunka, Russia, is a ground-based observatory located in the Kamchatka Krai region, dedicated to magnetic field measurements and research. It is operated by the Institute of Cosmophysical Research and Radio Wave Propagation (ИКИР ДВО РАН).
01383f3c-bb83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Paratunka, Russia

01547cee-b848-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cincinnati Observatory, also known as Mt. Lookout Observatory, is the oldest professional observatory in the United States, located on Mount Lookout in Cincinnati, Ohio, and houses historical telescopes for public viewing and educational programs.
01547cee-b848-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cincinnati Observatory, United States

01551334-b7b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High Resolution Instrument (HRI) Visible CCD Imager for Deep Impact was a 30.0 cm classical Cassegrain telescope with a dichroic beam splitter and a field of view of 2.0 milliradians, used for direct imaging in the visible spectrum aboard the Deep Impact spacecraft.
01551334-b7b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Resolution Instrument Visible CCD Imager on Deep Impact

0157f0ac-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAVEN Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectrometer (NGIMS) is a high-sensitivity quadrupole mass spectrometer designed to measure the composition and isotope abundances of thermal neutral atoms and ions in the Martian atmosphere. It operates on the MAVEN spacecraft, with objectives including profiling major atmospheric species and determining neutral temperature and isotope ratios from the homopause to above the exobase.
0157f0ac-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectrometer part of MAVEN

016405e6-b5f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kawane Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with ID 884.
016405e6-b5f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mitsuboshi Observatory, Japan

01642418-b7db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Darksky Observatory Fluxgate Magnetometer is an instrument used at the MEASURE Magnetometer Array to measure variations in Earth's magnetic field, located at the Darksky Observatory. It is part of a larger geomagnetic observatory network managed by the Space Physics community.
01642418-b7db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer Instrument at Darksky Observatory

01651f52-b5b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover Accelerometer for Entry, Descent and Landing is a set of highly accurate sensors onboard the Curiosity rover used primarily to measure acceleration and orientation during its descent to Mars' surface. Although not originally intended for gravitational measurements, these instruments have been adapted by scientists to gather valuable data on Martian gravity.
01651f52-b5b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Accelerometer on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

016d5978-bb66-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **Magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The **IGPP-LANL Air Force Academy Fluxgate Magnetometer** specifically refers to a magnetometer located at the IGPP-LANL Air Force Academy station, designed for detailed magnetic field observations as part of its investigations.
016d5978-bb66-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IGPP-LANL Magnetometer Array

01721c32-bb08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **NOAA 19**, also known as **NOAA-N Prime**, is a polar-orbiting operational environmental satellite launched on February 6, 2009. It collects global data on atmospheric, terrestrial, and space environment conditions using various instruments, including radiometers, sounders, and search and rescue systems.
01721c32-bb08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label:
Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer/3 on NOAA 19 Satellite
Solar Backscatter Ultraviolet Radiometer/2 on NOAA 19 Satellite
High Resolution Infrared Radiation Sounder on NOAA 19 Satellite
Advanced Microwave Sounding Unit-A on NOAA 19 Satellite
Microwave Humidity Sounder on NOAA 19 Satellite
Space Environment Monitor/2 on NOAA 19 Satellite
Advanced Data Collection System on NOAA 19 Satellite
Search and Rescue Repeater on NOAA 19 Satellite
Search and Rescue Processor on NOAA 19 Satellite

01783dac-b792-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe (WMAP) Satellite Mission was a space mission designed to measure temperature differences across the cosmic microwave background radiation in the millimeter waveband, providing crucial data for understanding the universe's age, composition, and geometry.
01783dac-b792-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: millimeter NASA Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe Satellite Mission

019b179a-b5ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NOAA 10 Space Environmental Monitor (SEM) is a particle detector instrument designed to measure proton flux, electron flux density, and energy spectrum in the upper atmosphere. It consists of two detector systems—MEPED and TED—and a data processing unit, extending the capabilities of previous solar-proton monitoring experiments.
019b179a-b5ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Environmental Monitor part of NOAA 10

01a6e7f2-b76e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The W. M. Keck Observatory at Mauna Kea is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Hawaii that operates two 10-meter telescopes known as Keck I and Keck II, facilitating high-resolution observations of the universe.
01a6e7f2-b76e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 10m W. M. Keck Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatory

01a86b1c-b797-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Geotail is a geomagnetic research satellite developed by Japan's ISAS in collaboration with NASA to study the Earth’s magnetosphere and its interaction with the solar wind. Launched on July 24, 1992, it focuses on measuring energy flow and transformation in the magnetotail to enhance understanding of fundamental magnetospheric processes.
01a86b1c-b797-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: International Solar Terrestrial Physics Science Initiative

01c75e2a-badd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fred L. Whipple Observatory, located at the observatory facility in Florida, is a ground-based astronomical observatory that includes the 1.3m telescope used for the Two Micron All Sky Survey (2MASS).
01c75e2a-badd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2MASS 1m3 Telescope at Fred L. Whipple Observatory

01cb2b7c-b899-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magalofes Observatory, located in Fene, A Coruña, Spain, is a ground-based observatory dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
01cb2b7c-b899-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magalofes Observatory, Fene, Spain

01ce3be2-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Litchfield Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at Hamilton College in Clinton, New York. It was established in 1856 and is known for its ground-based observations.
01ce3be2-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Litchfield Observatory at Hamilton College

01d52f44-b706-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2Y magnetometer is a three-axis instrument used to measure magnetic field components with high resolution and cadence, aiding in the study of substorm activity and ULF oscillations for relativistic electron loss investigations.
01d52f44-b706-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

01d5318e-b7ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kazan Geomagnetic Observatory (KZN), located in Zaimishche, Kazan, Russia, is a ground-based facility that conducted geomagnetic measurements from 1892 to 1992.
01d5318e-b7ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kazan Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

01d814b2-b6b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Athens Observatory was a ground-based facility located in Athens, Greece, that operated from January 1, 1899, to December 31, 1908. It was part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network and featured magnetometer instruments.
01d814b2-b6b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Athens Observatory, Greece

01e968b0-b7e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Onnens Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Noréaz, Prez, Switzerland. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with the code 172 and is situated at coordinates 46.793619 N, 7.0364 E.
01e968b0-b7e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Onnens Observatory, Switzerland

01f42eb2-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 0.48m Swedish Vacuum Solar Telescope (SVST) is an optical telescope located at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory, designed for observing solar phenomena with a high level of detail and clarity.
01f42eb2-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.48m optical Swedish Vacuum Solar Telescope at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory

01f798ba-bae7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Old Naval Observatory** is a historic astronomical observatory located in Washington, D.C., which served as the site for the United States Naval Observatory from 1844 to 1893 and is now designated as a National Historic Landmark.
01f798ba-bae7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Old Naval Observatory, United States

01f9857e-b5ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Ancon observatory, part of the IUGONET and WDC-Kyoto network, used for geomagnetic field measurements starting from January 1990.
01f9857e-b5ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iugonet Observatory

02186e60-bbb8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The FOAH Observatory (V23) is an astronomical observatory located in Magdalena, New Mexico, United States. It is a ground-based facility situated at Road 534, Socorro County.
02186e60-bbb8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magdalena Observatory

02204446-b69a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electric Field and Waves (EFW) instrument is a scientific device deployed on the Cluster 2/FM8 (Tango) spacecraft as part of the Cluster mission. It features four spherical sensors mounted on cable booms to measure electric fields, plasma density fluctuations, and other related phenomena in various frequency ranges.
