03a07968-b6a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LaCaille Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Pretoria, South Africa, known for its ground-based observations.
03a07968-b6a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: LaCaille Observatory, South Africa

03a57792-b964-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AEOS is a 3.7-meter optical telescope operated by the U.S. Air Force, located at the Maui Space Surveillance Complex on Mount Haleakala in Hawaii. It is used for space situational awareness and astronomical observations.
03a57792-b964-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.7m Advanced Electro Optical Systems Telescope at Haleakala Observatory

03b9e1d2-bb3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Phoenix Lander Surface Stereo Imager (SSI) was a camera system on the Phoenix Mars Lander designed to capture high-resolution color images of the Martian surface and provide critical data for geological and climatic analysis.
03b9e1d2-bb3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Surface Stereo Imager on Phoenix Lander

03bffcec-b951-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Space Place at Carter Observatory is an observatory located in Wellington, New Zealand, known for its astronomy education and public stargazing events.
03bffcec-b951-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Place at Carter Observatory, New Zealand

03c5da0a-ba3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Brorfelde Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Holbæk Municipality, Denmark, dedicated to the observation and study of Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since 1980 and is funded by the Technical University of Denmark.
03c5da0a-ba3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Brorfelde Observatory, Denmark

03c77d2e-b671-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on Prognoz 9, designated as SG-70 and provided by IZMIRAN's Space Magnetic Research Laboratory, was an instrument used to measure magnetic fields with a range of ±60 nT and an accuracy of about 0.3 nT, making one vector measurement every 10.24 seconds during the Prognoz satellite missions from 1977-1984.
03c77d2e-b671-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on Prognoz 9

03c9bc18-ba01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Japal-Rangapur Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Bugga Thanda, Ranga Reddy district, Telangana, India. It is a ground-based observatory used for studying celestial objects and phenomena.
03c9bc18-ba01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Japal-Rangapur Observatory, India

03d0430e-b5e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System (ATLAS) is a survey located on Earth that monitors the sky in optical wavebands to detect potentially hazardous asteroids and provide early warnings of impending impacts.
03d0430e-b5e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System

03d4be92-bc4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mount Graham International Observatory (MGIO) is an astronomical observatory located in southeastern Arizona's Pinaleño Mountains near Mount Graham. It is a division of Steward Observatory, the research arm for the Department of Astronomy at the University of Arizona.
03d4be92-bc4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 12m Sub-Millimeter Telescope at Mount Graham International Observatory, United States

03e12a6c-bb49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rosetta mission was an interplanetary endeavor aimed at rendezvousing with and performing in-situ measurements of the comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko, scheduled for 2014/2015. The spacecraft carried the Philae lander, which it deployed onto the comet's surface to study its composition and characteristics.
03e12a6c-bb49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer and plasma monitor on Rosetta Space Telescope

03e441e8-b757-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Val Joyeux Geomagnetic Observatory (VLJ) was a ground-based facility in France that operated from 1900 to 1936, primarily focused on geomagnetic measurements. It was located in Villepreux, near Versailles, and contributed data to the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto.
03e441e8-b757-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Val Joyeux Geomagnetic Observatory, France

03e5aef0-b867-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Campocatino Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Collepardo, Italy. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is known for its automated telescope systems.
03e5aef0-b867-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Campocatino Observatory

03ec3482-b696-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Hainan Island Station** is an astronomical observatory located on Hainan Island, China. It operates under the Purple Mountain Observatory and is situated at coordinates 109.5514 longitude and 34.94545 latitude.
03ec3482-b696-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hainan Island Station part of Purple Mountain Observatory, China

03edced6-b683-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Prince George (PGEO) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Prince George, Canada, primarily dedicated to geophysical research and observations. It is part of the THEMIS network and features instruments such as magnetometers for monitoring Earth's magnetic field.
03edced6-b683-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Prince George Geophysical Observatory

03f53b94-bb74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Solar Tower (BST-1) is an optical telescope located at the Crimean Astrophysical Observatory in Europe, designed for observing the Sun.
03f53b94-bb74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical The Solar Tower BST-1 at Crimean Astrophysical Observatory

0401b5f8-bbb6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: Perkins Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Delaware, Ohio, owned and operated by Ohio Wesleyan University.
0401b5f8-bbb6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Perkins Observatory

04069e20-b831-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kandalaksha Geomagnetic Observatory (KND), located in the rural settlement of Lovozero, Russia, is a ground-based facility dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity on Earth.
04069e20-b831-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kandalaksha Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

040c203e-b6a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 16 Orbital Mass Spectrometer (OMS) Experiment was an instrument carried on board the Command and Service Module during the Apollo 16 mission, designed to measure the composition of the lunar atmosphere by analyzing gases present around the moon.
040c203e-b6a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Orbital Mass Spectrometer on Apollo 16 Command and Service Module

040ca4f4-b71a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Isarwinkel Observatory (also known as the Isarwinkel Observatory, Bad Tölz) is an astronomical observatory located in Bad Tölz, Bavaria, Germany. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
040ca4f4-b71a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bad Tolz Observatory, Germany

0411bd16-b18b-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity represents the **AstroVal Observatory**, an astronomical facility located in Le Sentier, Switzerland.
0411bd16-b18b-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: AstroVal Observatory at Le Chenit, Switzerland

0417e6ec-bb8f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Lahti Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Hollola, Finland. Established in 1979, it serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
0417e6ec-bb8f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lahti Observatory, Finland

042c0928-b83e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The San Juan Geomagnetic Observatory (SJG), located in Cayey, Puerto Rico, is a ground-based facility dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity. It operates as part of the INTERMAGNET network and includes instruments like magnetometers managed by the WDC for Geomagnetism, Kyoto.
042c0928-b83e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at San Juan Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

042d0d22-bbc8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The G. Pascoli Observatory in Barga, Italy, is a ground-based astronomical facility located at La foresta di sopra, Castelvecchio Pascoli, operational since June 2023.
042d0d22-bbc8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: G. Pascoli Observatory, Italy

04315f76-b655-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1R Data Processing Unit (DPU)** is a versatile instrument controller used in the BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) project, responsible for acquiring data from various sensors and managing communication and control systems.
04315f76-b655-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

043492f6-bc48-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ukhta Geomagnetic Observatory (UKH), located in Russia, is a ground-based facility established in 1974 to monitor geomagnetic activity on Earth's surface.
043492f6-bc48-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ukhta Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

043ad32c-b78a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Venetia Burney Student Dust Counter (SDC) is a scientific instrument aboard the uncrewed New Horizons space probe designed to characterize dust particles in the outer solar system. It was named after Venetia Burney, who suggested the name "Pluto" for the dwarf planet.
043ad32c-b78a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Venetia Burney Student Dust Counter on New Horizons

043ce7d4-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Haleakala Neutron Monitor** is a scientific instrument located in Haleakalā, Hawaii. It was established in 1991 and consists of a standard 12-tube IGY monitor and an 18-tube NM-64 supermonitor, used for long-term monitoring of energetic particles.
043ce7d4-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument at Haleakalā Observatory

043ff3cc-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF Husafell station in Augastaðir, Borgarbyggð, Iceland is a ground-based observatory equipped with a crossed loop antenna for Very Low Frequency (VLF) and Extremely Low Frequency (ELF) measurements, established by Prof. Shiokawa of the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research (ISEE), in collaboration with the National Institute of Polar Research and the University of Iceland.
043ff3cc-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Low Frequency and Extremely Low Frequency Crossed Loop Antenna at Húsafell Observatory, Iceland

044c94fe-b94c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Digital Wave Processor (DWP), also known as Salsa, is a key instrument on Cluster 2 responsible for coordinating the operations of the Wave Experiment Consortium (WEC). It synchronizes data sampling, tags time series data, and implements various data compression methods to analyze waveforms in space plasmas.
044c94fe-b94c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digital Wave Processor part of Cluster 2

04549d8e-b753-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The JPL SynTrack Robotic Telescope 3 is an astronomical observatory located in Flagstaff, Arizona. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
04549d8e-b753-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: JPL SynTrack Robotic Telescope at Flagstaff Observatory, United States

04587e2c-b9dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Plaisance Geomagnetic Observatory (PLS), located in Plaine Magnien VCA, Grand Port, Mauritius, is a ground-based facility that operated from 1966 to 1976 and was part of the IAGA observatory network.
04587e2c-b9dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Plaisance Observatory, Mauritius

045e3ba0-bb6d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Sassoeiros Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Cascais, Portugal, designed for ground-based observations.
045e3ba0-bb6d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sassoeiros Observatory, Portugal

0464eede-b76f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Phoenix Lander Microscopy, Electrochemistry, and Conductivity Analyzer (MECA) Wet Chemistry Laboratory was a component of the MECA instrument suite on the Phoenix Mars lander, designed to analyze Martian soil and ice through wet chemistry experiments to understand the planet's chemical composition and potential habitability.
0464eede-b76f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wet Chemistry Laboratory part of Phoenix Mars Lander

046cdab2-b5fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital receiver installed in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan, designed for measuring ionospheric total electron content (TEC) using Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite beacon signals at 150 and 400 MHz. It utilizes GNU Radio software on a Linux PC and USRP hardware to process the received signals efficiently.
046cdab2-b5fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver part of IUGONET at Shionomisaki Observatory, Japan

048c2cf2-bb5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Ultraviolet Spectral Irradiance Monitor (SUSIM) is a dual dispersion spectrometer onboard the UARS observatory, designed to measure the solar spectrum in the 115-410 nm range with high resolution.
048c2cf2-bb5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Ultraviolet Spectral Irradiance Monitor on Upper Atmosphere Research Satellite

0497802a-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Eskdalemuir Observatory is a UK national environmental observatory located in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, specializing in geomagnetic measurements.
0497802a-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Eskdalemuir Observatory, United Kingdom

049cc75c-b777-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nimbus 7 satellite, launched in 1978, was a research and development platform designed to test advanced systems for collecting data related to pollution, oceanography, and meteorology. It carried eight specialized experiments and operated until 1993.
049cc75c-b777-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label:
limb infrared monitoring of the stratosphere on Nimbus 7 spacecraft
stratospheric and mesopheric sounder on Nimbus 7 spacecraft
coastal-zone color scanner on Nimbus 7 spacecraft
stratospheric aerosol measurement II on Nimbus 7 spacecraft
earth radiation budget on Nimbus 7 spacecraft
scanning multichannel microwave radiometer on Nimbus 7 spacecraft
solar backscatter UV and total ozone mapping spectrometer on Nimbus 7 spacecraft
temperature-humidity infrared radiometer on Nimbus 7 spacecraft

04ac85de-ba1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ion Composition Instrument (ICI)** was a specialized spectrometer onboard the International Cometary Explorer designed to analyze the ionic composition of the solar wind using a stigmatic Wien filter and a hemispherical electrostatic energy analyzer.
04ac85de-ba1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Composition Instrument on International Cometary Explorer

04b67706-b641-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EISCAT 4-wavelength photometer in Tromsø is an instrument designed to measure specific band and line emissions from atmospheric gases, including N2+ and OI, at wavelengths of 427.8 nm, 630.0 nm, 670.5 nm, and 844.6 nm. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network and is used for studying auroral phenomena and other atmospheric processes.
04b67706-b641-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 4-wavelength Photometer part of EISCAT Investigation

04b6a360-b5ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Dertingen Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Dertingen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. It is a ground-based facility used for sky observation and research.
04b6a360-b5ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dertingen Observatory, Germany

04d06a40-ba37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Dalby Station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Dalby, Australia, part of the CPMN magnetometer network, used for observing and recording magnetic field data.
04d06a40-ba37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at CPMN Observatory, Australia

04d21f0e-bb57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pommier Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Chapdes-Beaufort, France. It operates as a ground-based facility for conducting various astronomical observations and research.
04d21f0e-bb57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatoire de Pommier, France

04e3742e-b80b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Rørvik Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, which has been operational since December 30, 2006.
04e3742e-b80b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission

04e63f16-b62a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Arizona Radio Observatory (ARO) 12m Telescope is a millimeter-wave telescope located at the Kitt Peak National Observatory in North America, featuring a 12.0-meter aperture.
04e63f16-b62a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 12.0m millimeter Arizona Radio Observatory Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory

04ee9c94-b173-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The HISCALE Composition Aperture (CA) is a high-sensitivity detection system used on the Ulysses spacecraft to measure ion composition in space through multiparameter techniques and sophisticated prioritization methods. It employs pairs of silicon detectors and logic channels for discrete ion analysis, ensuring accurate measurements of various ion species based on their occurrence frequency.
04ee9c94-b173-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Composition Aperture system on Ulysses Spacecraft

04f2f27a-ba48-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sabhawala Geomagnetic Observatory (SAB)** is a ground-based facility located in Sabhawala, India, that operates geomagnetic instruments to monitor and study the Earth's magnetic field.
04f2f27a-ba48-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sabhawala Geomagnetic Observatory, India

04ff4f3a-b993-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Kawatabi HF Log Periodic Antenna** is an instrument used for radio observations, particularly in the frequency range from 20 to 40 MHz. It is part of a 100km interferometer designed for detecting Jovian and galactic radio emissions and is located at Tohoku University's observatory within the IUGONET network.
04ff4f3a-b993-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kawatabi HF Log Periodic Antenna at Tohoku University Observatory

05015a06-ba87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Astronomical Observatories of China (NAOC) Xinglong Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Xinglong County, Chengde, Hebei Province, China. It is situated at coordinates 40.39425° N latitude and 117.57588° E longitude.
05015a06-ba87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fibre Spectroscopic Telescope at Xinglong Observatory, China

0502d994-bc71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Karachi Geomagnetic Observatory (KRC)** is a ground-based facility located in Karachi, Pakistan, that operated from 1988 to 2008 for the purpose of monitoring geomagnetic activity.
0502d994-bc71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Karachi Geomagnetic Observatory, Pakistan

05145e8c-b60c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Solar Orbiter** is a spacecraft developed by the European Space Agency (ESA) designed to observe and study the Sun, particularly focusing on x-ray emissions and phenomena such as neutrinos, particles, and gravitational waves.
05145e8c-b60c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray Solar Orbiter on European Space Agency Solar Orbiter

051874b6-b93d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) is a global network of radio telescopes designed to observe the immediate environment of black holes, specifically operating in the millimeter and submillimeter wavebands using Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI).
051874b6-b93d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter and Submillimeter Very Long Baseline Interferometry Event Horizon Telescope

051dc768-b631-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Visible Imaging System (VIS)** on Polar is an instrument designed to capture high-resolution images of nighttime polar and auroral emissions at visible wavelengths using three low-light cameras. It aims to study energy dissipation in the auroral ionosphere and other magnetospheric phenomena as part of the International Solar-Terrestrial Physics campaign.
051dc768-b631-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible Imaging System part of Polar

051e72d2-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Toyota Observatory (Q115216404) is an astronomical observatory located in Toyota, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with ID 881 and functions as a ground-based observatory for studying celestial bodies.
051e72d2-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Toyota Observatory, Japan

05348f3a-b8e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Provencal Baronnies Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Moydans, France. It is a ground-based facility that began operations on January 1, 2013.
05348f3a-b8e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Provencal Baronnies Observatory, France

0539deca-b60f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mini-RF (Miniature Radio Frequency) instrument is a synthetic aperture radar on the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter designed to search for water-ice deposits in lunar polar regions and characterize surface roughness.
0539deca-b60f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Synthetic Aperture Radar on Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter

053c58d2-b7c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Australian National University (ANU) 1.3m Skymapper Telescope at Siding Spring Observatory (SSO) is an optical telescope located in Australia, designed for sky surveys and astronomical research.
053c58d2-b7c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.3m SkyMapper Telescope at Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

0543940e-b102-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF Kagoshima (Maenohama) station in Japan was an observatory for very low frequency and extremely low-frequency radio waves, operational from April 1976 to 2001.
0543940e-b102-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Low Frequency/Extremely Low Frequency Kagoshima Maenohama Station, Japan

0544d736-b9fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Atlante Observatory (J51) is an astronomical facility located in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is situated at Calle Felipe Pedrell, Salud Bajo, Cruz del Señor.
0544d736-b9fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Atlante Observatory, Spain

05492e26-b9bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Eureka Magnetic Observatory (EUA) is a ground-based facility located in Eureka, Nunavut, Canada, sponsored by the U.S.A., and operating since 2007 to monitor magnetic field variations on Earth's surface.
05492e26-b9bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eureka Magnetic Observatory

05502b02-b9ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The "Magnetometers at Martin De Vivies" are specific instruments located at the Martin De Vivies observatory, part of an investigation under the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA), operational since January 1981.
05502b02-b9ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Martin De Vivies Observatory

05544b40-b991-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Lusaka station is a ground-based magnetometer observatory located in the Chibombo District, Central Province of Zambia. It is part of the international MAGDAS network and operates to monitor geomagnetic activity on Earth's surface.
05544b40-b991-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lusaka Observatory, Zambia

0554bc26-bbc4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: Cluster 4 (also known as FM8 or Tango) is one of four identical magnetospheric research satellites in the Cluster II constellation, launched by ESA and NASA to study small-scale structures in the Earth's plasma environment.
0554bc26-bbc4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cluster II-FM8 part of Solar-Terrestrial Science Program

055dd260-bb2f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Iitate Observatory, operated by Tohoku University, is a ground-based facility located in Fukushima, Japan, dedicated to radio observations.
055dd260-bb2f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Iitate Observatory

056a1028-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Red Lion Observatory** is a ground-based observatory located in Southampton Township, New Jersey, United States. It is situated at 39.88726 latitude and -74.72996 longitude (285.27004 in positive degrees).
056a1028-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Red Lion Observatory, United States

056e6f44-b8dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Space Plasma Simulation Group (SPSG), established in 1976 and based in the Earth's equatorial region, conducts numerical simulations focused on space plasma physics.
056e6f44-b8dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Plasma Simulation Group

05781588-bbbd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: GOES 5 was a geosynchronous weather satellite developed by NASA and operated by NOAA, launched in 1981 to monitor Earth's atmosphere and space environment. It carried instruments for cloud imaging, atmospheric sounding, data collection, and space environment monitoring.
05781588-bbbd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared VISSR on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite

05877144-ba29-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Longwave Infrared Camera (LWIR) is a specialized instrument designed to capture thermal observations of the lunar surface within the 8.0 to 9.5-micron spectral range, utilizing a catadioptric lens and a cryogenically cooled mercury cadmium telluride focal plane array.
05877144-ba29-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Long Wavelength Infrared Camera on Clementine

058911ae-b694-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, particularly the Earth's magnetic field. The San.Juan.1-2-3 Magnetometer, part of the IAGA investigation at the San Juan Observatory, has been operational since January 1903.
058911ae-b694-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at San Juan Observatory

05a2553c-ba73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plasma Electron and Current Experiment (PEACE) on Cluster 2 is an instrument designed to measure the velocity moments of electron distribution functions in space, using two sensors (LEEA and HEEA) that cover energy ranges from 0.67 eV to 30 KeV.
05a2553c-ba73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Electron and Current Experiment on Cluster 2

05a61cd2-b611-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Miyazu Magnetometer is a ground-based facility located in Fukuchiyama, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan, established in 1973 as part of the IAGA observatory network. It operates on Earth's surface and contributes to magnetic field observations for scientific research.
05a61cd2-b611-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Miyazu Observatory, Japan

05a88a24-b906-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AGO P4 SearchCoil Instrument is a scientific tool located at the AGO P4 ground station, designed to conduct investigations using search coils.
05a88a24-b906-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil on Automatic Geophysical Observatory 4

05b4d052-b8ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Vykhodnoy Magnetometer** was an instrument used at the IAGA Vykhodnoy station from January 1949 to December 31, 1955, designed to measure variations in Earth's magnetic field.
05b4d052-b8ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Vykhodnoy Observatory

05b5eee2-bb2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Clixby Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Cleethorpes, North East Lincolnshire, England, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
05b5eee2-bb2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cleethorpes Observatory

05be540e-b630-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sainte-Clotilde Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Denis on Réunion Island, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
05be540e-b630-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Saint-Clotilde Observatory, France

05c5a440-b8cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Minamitory.Shima Magnetometer is an instrument located at the IAGA-designated station in Minamitori Shima, used for measuring magnetic fields since 1941.
05c5a440-b8cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Minamitory Shima Observatory

05c786ca-b827-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at Manzaoli (MZL) is a scientific instrument used to measure magnetic fields and is part of the observatory network managed by the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto.
05c786ca-b827-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Manzaoli Observatory

05c9d4b0-b7dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Sendai Municipal Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Aoba Ward, Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan.
05c9d4b0-b7dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sendai Municipal Observatory, Japan

05cb3d7a-b736-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IAGA:POL Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields at a specific station identified by the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) with the code POL. It was operational from January 1, 1881, to December 31, 1922.
05cb3d7a-b736-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pola Observatory

05cbdd48-bbbe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Janow Observatory was a ground-based facility located in Stradch, Ukraine, operational from January 1, 1933, to December 31, 1934, primarily known for its magnetometer instruments.
05cbdd48-bbbe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Janow Observatory, Ukraine

05cc8f98-b85f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Islamabad Magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field, located at the IAGA observatory in Islamabad. It has been operational since January 1, 2008, and is part of the global network of geomagnetic monitoring stations.
05cc8f98-b85f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Islamabad Observatory

05df179a-b8e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Akatsuki ("Dawn"), also known as the Venus Climate Orbiter (VCO) and Planet-C, is a Japanese Space Agency (JAXA) mission designed to study the atmospheric dynamics of Venus from orbit. Launched in 2010, it focuses on understanding the super-rotation and three-dimensional motion within Venus's atmosphere using multi-wavelength imaging.
05df179a-b8e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Imager on Venus Climate Orbiter

05e798fe-bb8b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Magnetometers at Apatity (APA) are instruments used to measure magnetic field strength and direction, part of the IUGONET observatory in Kyoto since 1973.
05e798fe-bb8b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Apatity Observatory

05ec177e-b7d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Albanyà Observatory, located in Albanyà, Catalonia, Spain, is a ground-based astronomical observatory established in 2017. It is situated at the coordinates 42.306713 N, 2.7114 E and is known for its contributions to astronomical research.
05ec177e-b7d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Albanyà Observatory, Spain

05ee5e3e-b67f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **PHOBOS-2 spacecraft position and velocity** dataset provides the spatial coordinates and velocities of the Phobos 2 spacecraft in various reference frames (HEE, MSO, GSE) with different time resolutions spanning from July 1988 to March 1989. It is archived as part of the CDPP-Archive at CNES Observatory.
05ee5e3e-b67f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform on Phobos-2 Space Probe

05f5eb54-b80a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy's 100m Effelsberg Radio Telescope, located in Europe, is a large radio telescope with an aperture of 100 meters, used primarily for astronomical observations.
05f5eb54-b80a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 100.0m Effelsberg Radio Telescope at Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy

05f6c382-ba7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
POETS (Portable Occultation, Eclipse, and Transit System) is an astronomical instrument optimized for occultation and related observations, featuring a high-performance camera with low read noise and high frame rates.
05f6c382-ba7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Portable Occultation, Eclipse, and Transit System

05fafb74-b7a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Infrared Spectrometer (IKS) on Vega 1 was a three-channel system designed to conduct chemical analysis of cometary matter and measure thermal emission from the nucleus, covering spectral ranges from 2.5 to 14 microns.
05fafb74-b7a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Spectrometer on Vega 1

060a79d0-b6bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTIs) Istok station near Norilsk, Russia is a ground-based observatory developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research at Nagoya University to study upper atmosphere dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions.
060a79d0-b6bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Istok Observatory near Norilsk, Russia

0610ac3a-bb40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** SOLSTICE (SOlar STellar Irradiance Comparison Experiment) is a set of ultraviolet grating spectrometers on the SORCE satellite, designed to measure solar and stellar irradiance in the 115-320 nm range with high precision and accuracy. It uses stable stars as calibrators to track instrument variability over time.
0610ac3a-bb40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Stellar Irradiance Comparison Experiment part of SORCE

06146480-b896-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1A Optical Photometer is an instrument designed to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm, specifically during relativistic electron precipitation events, to determine the presence of accompanying protons and support theories on electromagnetic ion cyclotron wave scattering as a precipitation mechanism.
06146480-b896-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

061853a4-b5f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) Wewak station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Wewak, Papua New Guinea, operating as part of the ISEE network to monitor geomagnetic activity.
061853a4-b5f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Wewak Observatory, Papua New Guinea

0620d7e8-b7b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The OVM Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Chiesa in Valmalenco, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for observing celestial objects and phenomena.
0620d7e8-b7b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chiesa in Valmalenco Observatory, Italy

062c756a-b7fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 14 Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP) was a suite of scientific instruments carried by the Apollo 14 lunar module, deployed on the moon to study seismic activity, lunar environment, and other aspects of the lunar surface.
062c756a-b7fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Apollo 14 Lunar Surface Experiments Package part of Apollo 14

062d48fc-b7f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cosmic Origins Spectrograph (COS) is an ultraviolet spectrograph on the Hubble Space Telescope designed to study the large-scale structure of the universe. It operates in two channels: Far Ultraviolet (90-215 nm) and Near Ultraviolet (170-320 nm).
062d48fc-b7f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Cosmic Origins Spectrograph on Hubble Space Telescope

06330b98-b5c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Brignoles Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Brignoles, Var, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
06330b98-b5c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Brignoles Observatory, France

0634d07e-b9ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Anchorage Geomagnetic Observatory (AMU) was a ground facility located in Anchorage, Alaska, operating from 1957 to 1959, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements.
0634d07e-b9ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Anchorage Geomagnetic Observatory

063cc944-ba75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tigh Speuran Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Framingham, Massachusetts, United States. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
063cc944-ba75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tigh Speuran Observatory

063e8fa4-bb4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Eielson Air Force Base station (IAGA identifier ENB) that was operational from 1966-01-01 to 1972-12-31 as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
063e8fa4-bb4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eielson Air Force Base Observatory

065b0214-b864-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Air Force Maui Optical and Supercomputing Observatory (AMOS), located at the Haleakala Observatory in Maui, Hawaii, is a U.S. Space Force facility dedicated to space surveillance research and development, as well as high-performance computing operations.
065b0214-b864-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.67m Advanced Electro-Optical System Telescope at Haleakala Observatory, United States

065dddb4-b746-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Hawaii 2.2-meter Telescope, also known as the UH88, is an optical telescope located at the Mauna Kea Observatory in North America, with an aperture of 2.2 meters.
065dddb4-b746-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: University of Hawaii 2.2m Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatory

0661a70c-b8de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Pontianak station is a ground-based facility located in Ngoro, Mojokerto, East Java, Indonesia, part of the CPMN magnetometer network used for geomagnetic observations.
0661a70c-b8de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pontianak Observatory, Indonesia

0666561e-bb52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CLPS Task Order 19D Regolith Adherence Characterization (RAC) experiment involves photographing sample materials over time as they are exposed to the Lunar environment, using multiple cameras to characterize regolith changes on the samples.
0666561e-bb52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Regolith Adherence Characterization part of CLPS Task Order 19D

066eabc6-b6ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory is a radio astronomy observatory located in Cambridge, Tasmania, operated by the University of Tasmania and featuring three radio astronomy antennas and the Grote Reber Museum.
066eabc6-b6ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio Mount Pleasant Antenna at Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory, Australia and 14m Vela Antenna at Mount Pleasant Radio Observatory, Australia

067350c4-baaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL 1L Optical Photometer is an instrument designed to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm during relativistic electron precipitation events, specifically aimed at determining the presence of protons accompanying these electrons. It operates by collecting photons through a collimator tube and using a photomultiplier tube to generate charge pulses for counting, thereby measuring the flux of precipitating protons.
067350c4-baaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

067817a2-b9e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Uzurano Observatory (also known as Kasai Station) is an astronomical observatory located in Besshocho, Kasai, Hyogo Prefecture, Japan. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 375 and primarily functions as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
067817a2-b9e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Uzurano Observatory, Japan

068b364e-b85c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: PEACE (Plasma Electron And Current Experiment) is an instrument on the Double Star 1 spacecraft that measures thermal electron counts and velocities to determine the positive potential of the spacecraft. This data supports the operation of ASPOC, another onboard instrument.
068b364e-b85c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Electron and Current Experiment on Double Star 1

068f2e6c-b8f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Logrono Geomagnetic Observatory (LGR), located in Logroño, Spain, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1957 to 1966 and specialized in geophysical measurements.
068f2e6c-b8f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Logroño Geomagnetic Observatory, Spain

0691d204-baca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **6ROADS Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Wojnówko, Poland. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
0691d204-baca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 6ROADS Observatory at Wojnowko, Poland

069d9a68-b803-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Southern Queensland Observatory (USQO) is an astronomical facility located at Mount Kent in the Toowoomba Regional area of Queensland, Australia, dedicated to ground-based observations and research.
069d9a68-b803-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mount Kent Observatory, Australia

06ab2c1e-ba4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Energetic Particle Monitor (EPM) on GOES 7 was an instrument designed to measure the flux of energetic particles in space. It consisted of three detector assemblies that monitored protons, alpha particles, and electrons across various energy ranges, providing data through 25 channels with different sampling rates.
06ab2c1e-ba4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Monitor on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 7

06ad9700-bb42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Winnipeg Geomagnetic Observatory (WNP), located in Glenlea, Manitoba, Canada, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1969 to 1975 to monitor geomagnetic activity.
06ad9700-bb42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Winnipeg Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

06b7a812-bb56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Danastro Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Romerée, Belgium. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
06b7a812-bb56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Danastro Observatory at Romerée, Belgium

06b9913a-b8eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Entity:** Pioneer 6 (1965-105A)

**Definition:** Pioneer 6 was a NASA space probe launched in 1965 to study interplanetary phenomena from solar orbit, including solar wind, cosmic rays, and magnetic fields. It was the first in a series of spin-stabilized, solar-powered satellites designed for continuous data collection.
06b9913a-b8eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pioneer 6 part of Pioneer Program

06b9a672-b704-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Can Roig Observatory (C99) is an astronomical observatory located in Llagostera, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility and is situated at Biblioteca Julià Cutiller, 2, Carrer de Lleó I, Cantallops, Fonollerons, Llagostera, Gironès, Girona, Catalonia, 17240, Spain.
06b9a672-b704-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Can Roig Observatory, Spain

06c4d1da-bab7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Junk Bond Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Sonoran Desert at Sierra Vista, Arizona, United States.
06c4d1da-bab7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Junk Bond Observatory

06cbdabe-bb4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
DMSP-F18 is a US Department of Defense weather satellite launched in 2009 to monitor meteorological, oceanographic, and solar-terrestrial physics environments from a near-polar, sun-synchronous orbit.
06cbdabe-bb4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Defense Meteorological Satellite Program 5D-3 F18

06cc746e-b7b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Mount Wilson-TIE Observatory is an astronomical facility located on Mount Wilson in Los Angeles County, California. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting various astronomical observations and research.
06cc746e-b7b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mount Wilson Observatory, United States

06d6a654-b98f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU)** is a navigation instrument aboard the Mars Exploration Rover Spirit that measures three-axis rotation rate and acceleration using Fiber Optic Gyro sensors and silicon accelerometers.
06d6a654-b98f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Inertial Measurement Unit on Mars Exploration Rover Spirit

06d8c296-b790-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Manises Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Manises, Valencia, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility and contributes to astronomical research from its location on Earth.
06d8c296-b790-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio de Manises, Spain

06dff83c-b8d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Havana (HVN) Observatory in Cuba is a ground-based facility established in 1897 and located at 277.85 longitude and 22.967 latitude in San José de las Lajas, Mayabeque. It is part of the World Data Center Kyoto and operates primarily to study geophysical phenomena using instruments such as magnetometers.
06dff83c-b8d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Havana Observatory, Cuba

06e8ac8e-b70d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The instrument is an all-sky EMCCD (Electron Multiplying Charge Coupled Device) imager equipped with a N2 1P wideband filter located in Tromsø, Norway, as part of the Pulsating Aurora Project. It utilizes the ImagEM X2 EMCCD camera produced by Hamamatsu Photonics for capturing detailed images of auroral phenomena.
06e8ac8e-b70d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: All-sky Electron Multiplying Charge Coupled Device Imager in nitrogen wideband on Pulsating Aurora Project

06eea82a-bbac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bay Mills Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation. It is located at the Bay Mills Geophysical Observatory and has been operational since September 27, 2005.
06eea82a-bbac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bay Mills Geophysical Observatory

06f0b04a-ba47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1Q Optical Photometer** is an instrument designed to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm during relativistic electron precipitation events, aiming to determine the presence of protons and support the mechanism of scattering by electromagnetic ion cyclotron waves.
06f0b04a-ba47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

06f9dfbc-b826-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS magnetometer network in Abidjan, Ivory Coast is a ground-based facility located at Eboué, Aboisso, Sud-Comoé. It operates as part of the global MAGDAS system to monitor magnetic field variations on Earth's surface.
06f9dfbc-b826-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: MAGDAS magnetometer network at Eboué Observatory, Côte d'Ivoire

0705cc2c-b83b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Geneva Observatory 1.2m Leonhard Euler (Swiss EULER) Telescope is an optical telescope with a 1.2-meter aperture located at La Silla Observatory in South America, part of the facilities managed by the European Southern Observatory (ESO).
0705cc2c-b83b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Leonhard Euler Telescope at La Silla Observatory

072662a0-b7f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IGPP-LANL Teoloyucan Fluxgate Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure variations in the Earth's magnetic field at the Teoloyucan station, part of the IGPP-LANL Magnetometer Array.
072662a0-b7f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IGPP-LANL Teoloyucan Observatory

0730dc9e-b973-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The NEOWISE mission is a space telescope project that uses the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) to detect and study asteroids and comets, particularly those near Earth. It was launched in December 2009 and has significantly contributed to the discovery of minor planets and other celestial bodies.
0730dc9e-b973-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared NASA's 0.4m Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer part of NEOWISE

0733464e-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Observatory of Tacubaya is an astronomical observatory located in Mexico City, known for its ground-based facilities and historical significance. It was established to facilitate the study and observation of celestial bodies from Earth.
0733464e-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: National Observatory of Tacubaya, Mexico

073405e0-b61c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Miniature Integrated Camera Spectrometer (MICAS) is a compact, multi-channel instrument used on the Deep Space 1 mission, featuring two visible-wavelength imagers and two spectrometers for infrared and ultraviolet wavelengths, also supporting autonomous navigation.
073405e0-b61c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: The Miniature Integrated Camera Spectrometer on Deep Space 1

074a2ee4-bae8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mullard Radio Astronomy Observatory (MRAO) is a renowned ground-based observatory located near Cambridge, UK, known for its advanced radio telescopes used in astrophysical research. It is part of the University of Cambridge's Cavendish Laboratories and houses instruments like the One-Mile Telescope and the Arcminute Microkelvin Imager.
074a2ee4-bae8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mullard Radio Astronomy Observatory, United Kingdom

077876f2-b6f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: ASPOC (Active Space Potential Control) is an investigation on the Double Star 1 spacecraft designed to maintain its potential at a low voltage by neutralizing positive charges through the emission of indium ions. It continuously monitors the spacecraft's potential using the PEACE instrument.
077876f2-b6f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Active Space Potential Control part of Double Star 1

077e1dbe-b75d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Orion Astroview 120ST EQ** is a 12 cm refractor telescope located at the Goodricke-Pigott Observatory in Arizona, known for its high precision equatorial mount and advanced tracking capabilities.
077e1dbe-b75d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.12m Orion Astroview 120ST EQ at Goodricke-Pigott Observatory, United States

078c1500-b64e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hard X-ray Telescope (HXT) on Yohkoh is a Fourier-synthesis imager designed to capture high-resolution images of solar flares in the hard X-ray energy range, providing detailed observations above 30 keV with an angular resolution of approximately 5 arc seconds.
078c1500-b64e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hard X-Ray Telescope on Yohkoh

078f165c-b6d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kron Photometer is an astronomical instrument designed to measure the brightness or intensity of light from celestial objects, such as stars and galaxies, by performing photometric measurements across specific wavelength bands.
078f165c-b6d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kron Photometer at Lowell Observatory

07aa3384-baac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Climate Sounder (MCS) is an instrument onboard the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter designed to measure atmospheric conditions on Mars using optical spectrometry and limb viewing techniques.
07aa3384-baac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Spectrometer on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter

07b66262-b967-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition**:
OrbitJet Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Town of Boston, Erie County, New York. It operates as a ground-based facility for conducting various astronomical observations and research.
07b66262-b967-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: OrbitJet Observatory, United States

07bbe0b8-b91a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Moonedge Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Northport, New York, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
07bbe0b8-b91a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Moonedge Observatory, United States

07c2dfa8-bbd6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cassini Imaging Science Subsystem (ISS) is a dual-camera system on the Cassini spacecraft, featuring the Narrow Angle Camera (NAC) and the Wide Angle Camera (WAC), designed to capture high-resolution images of celestial bodies with varying thermal management strategies for optimal performance.
07c2dfa8-bbd6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Narrow Angle Camera and Wide Angle Camera on Cassini Spacecraft

07c8ad1a-b835-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Etyek Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Etyek, Fejér County, Hungary. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial bodies.
07c8ad1a-b835-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Etyek Observatory, Hungary

07ccde2e-b616-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Comet SL9-Jupiter Collision" mission refers to the historic event in which comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 impacted Jupiter between July 16 and 22, 1994. This was the first time humans predicted and observed a celestial body's collision with a planet well in advance, providing significant scientific insights and global observational efforts.
07ccde2e-b616-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 Jupiter Impact Investigation

07e190f0-b759-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Wind Ion Composition Spectrometer (SWICS) on the Advanced Composition Explorer (ACE) spacecraft is an instrument designed to measure the composition, temperatures, and speeds of solar wind ions, covering a wide range of elements from hydrogen to iron. It utilizes an electrostatic analyzer combined with time-of-flight and energy measurements to provide detailed data on solar wind characteristics.
07e190f0-b759-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer part of Solar Wind Ion Composition Spectrometer on Advanced Composition Explorer

07e75f54-ba5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 3 Fast Plasma Instrument (FPI) Suite's Dual Ion Spectrometers (DIS) is part of the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission and measures ion velocity-space distribution from 10 eV to 30 keV with a time resolution of 150 ms.
07e75f54-ba5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser on Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

07f343dc-bca8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISEE Magnetometer station at Lucky Lake, Canada is a ground-based facility located in North America that measures magnetic fields and has an induction instrument as part of its setup.
07f343dc-bca8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lucky Lake Observatory, Canada

0807415c-b6a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital instrument located in Pontianak, Indonesia, designed for measuring ionospheric total electron content using signals from Low Earth Orbit satellites. It employs GNU Radio software and USRP hardware to process 150 and 400 MHz beacon signals.
0807415c-b6a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU Radio Beacon Receiver at Pontianak Observatory

080aafd6-b64a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EMN Tamanrasset Station** is a ground-based facility located in Tafsit, Tamanghasset, Algeria, operating as part of the EMN magnetometer network to monitor magnetic field variations.
080aafd6-b64a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at EMN Tamanrasset Station, Algeria

08130d04-b855-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **DSS-33 34-m Radio Telescope** is a planned deep space communication antenna located at the Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex in Australia, expected to become operational in 2026. It utilizes a beam waveguide design for improved signal transmission and reception.
08130d04-b855-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Deep Space Station 33 at Canberra Observatory

0815efd0-b77c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Montevenere Observatory (also known as the Monzuno Observatory) is an astronomical observatory located in Monzuno, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial bodies.
0815efd0-b77c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Montevenere Observatory, Italy

0819ed40-b9db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lyon Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Genis-Laval near Lyon, France, founded in 1878 and listed as a historical site on May 9, 2007.
0819ed40-b9db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lyon Observatory, France

081a0d94-b9e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Conlin Hill Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at 43 Conlin Road in Buffumville, Oxford, Massachusetts. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
081a0d94-b9e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Conlin Hill Observatory

081c2794-b9a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Beijing geophysical observatory that measures the magnetic field of the Earth. This instrument has been operational since January 1957 and is part of the World Data Center for Geomagnetism (WDC_GDMC).
081c2794-b9a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Beijing Observatory

081d1278-bb60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Muntinlupa Ground Magnetic Field Instrument, operational since 1951, is part of the IUGONET observatory network and provides data for geomagnetic studies under the IAGA investigation.
081d1278-bb60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Muntinlupa Observatory

081e7664-b745-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at Eusebio (EUS) is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields as part of the IAGA investigation from 1975 to 1977.
081e7664-b745-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eusebio Observatory

081f1b6e-bbb4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The Hermanus Fluxgate Magnetometer, located in the World Data Centre in Kyoto with IAGA identifier HER, has been operational since January 1, 1941.
081f1b6e-bbb4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer at Hermanus Observatory

082063d0-bb31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Pear Tree Observatory is an astronomical ground-based facility located in Valparaiso, Florida, USA. It operates under the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code H23.
082063d0-bb31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pear Tree Observatory, United States

083cb18c-b5d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Montagut Observatory (K06) is an astronomical observatory located in Can Sola, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
083cb18c-b5d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Montagut Observatory, Spain

0846f282-b6a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Murchison Bay ground station, operational from 1957 to 1959, used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of the IAGA investigation.
0846f282-b6a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Murchison Bay Observatory

084b041c-ba2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Salluit Magnetometer is an instrument located at the Salluit Geophysical Observatory, operational since October 21, 2014, as part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG. It measures magnetic field variations to study geomagnetic activity and space weather phenomena.
084b041c-ba2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Salluit Geophysical Observatory

08620f8c-ba38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Descent Imager/Spectral Radiometer (DISR) on the Huygens probe was an optical instrument designed to measure solar radiation and capture images during its descent through Titan's atmosphere, providing critical data on the moon’s surface composition and atmospheric properties.
08620f8c-ba38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Descent Imager Spectral Radiometer on Huygens Probe

08665340-b8e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Yale-Columbia Station is an astronomical observatory located in Johannesburg, South Africa, which was established in 1925.
08665340-b8e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yale-Columbia Station Observatory, South Africa

0871bdc8-b769-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EPI-Hi/LET2** is an energetic particle instrument onboard the Parker Solar Probe mission. It measures high-energy protons, Helium nuclei, and electrons, contributing to understanding solar energetic particles' sources and behavior near the Sun.
0871bdc8-b769-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument part of Parker Solar Probe Mission

0886626c-bb4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Synoptic Optical Long-term Investigations of the Sun (SOLIS)** is a ground-based solar observatory located at Kitt Peak, funded by the NSF and operated by the National Solar Observatory. It is designed to gather long-term data on solar activity cycles, sudden energy releases, and solar irradiance changes using instruments like a vector spectromagnetograph (VSM), full disk patrol (FDP), and an Integrated Sunlight Spectrometer.
0886626c-bb4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Midi-Pyrénées Observatory, France

088e3b94-babe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Shumagin Geomagnetic Observatory (SHU)** is a ground-based facility located in the Aleutians East Borough, Alaska, United States, dedicated to geomagnetic research. It operates a magnetometer and has been active since 2005.
088e3b94-babe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Shumagin Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

0890552e-b63a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SESAME Magnetometer is an instrument designed to measure the H, D, and Z components of the Earth's magnetic field using fluxgate technology, with a sampling rate of once per second and a resolution of approximately 1 nT. It is part of the SESAME observatory.
0890552e-b63a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Satellite Experiments Simultaneous with Antarctic Measurements

08aaf86e-b95c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Energetic Electron and Proton Spectrometer DOK-S** is an instrument designed to measure the energetic spectrum and angular distribution of electrons (20-180 keV) and ions (20-1300 keV), featuring two detector units with silicon detectors, magnetic filters, and mylar foils for particle discrimination.
08aaf86e-b95c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Electron and Proton Spectrometer DOK-S on Magion 4

08b02eba-b8b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** LANL1991 is a geosynchronous spacecraft launched on January 1, 1991, equipped with instruments to monitor energetic electrons and ions in Earth's magnetosphere.
08b02eba-b8b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geosynchronous spacecraft carrying energetic electron and ion instruments part of Los Alamos National Laboratory Observatory

08bedc22-b95b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, particularly Earth's magnetic field. The ones referenced here are located at the Tananarive observatory in Kyoto, part of the IUGONET network.
08bedc22-b95b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tananarive Observatory

08c43904-b840-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at HLN is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Hualien, Taiwan, part of the MAGDAS observation network under the IUGONET observatory. It measures magnetic field variations with high precision.
08c43904-b840-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MAGDAS observation network

08d0dcc2-ba25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The one located in Lanzhou, China, has been operational since January 1959 as part of the IAGA investigation network.
08d0dcc2-ba25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lanzhou Observatory

08da01a0-bb95-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Skygems Namibia Remote Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at Hakos Astrofarm, Gamsberg Pass, Khomas, in Namibia. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
08da01a0-bb95-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Skygems Namibia Remote Observatory, Namibia

08da1830-b5b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tamanrasset Magnetic Observatory was a ground-based facility in Algeria dedicated to geophysical research, particularly magnetic observations, operating from 1932 until its closure at the end of 2015.
08da1830-b5b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tamanrasset Magnetic Observatory, Algeria

08db3be6-b74f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Roeser Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in Roeser, Luxembourg, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
08db3be6-b74f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Roeser Observatory, Luxembourg

08e267cc-b8c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MESSENGER Gamma Ray Spectrometer (GRS) was an instrument onboard the MESSENGER spacecraft that measured gamma-ray emissions from Mercury's surface to determine its elemental composition, aiding in understanding the planet's formation and evolution.
08e267cc-b8c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma Ray Spectrometer on MESSENGER

08e3cbcc-ba00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cosmic Ray Subsystem (CRS)** on Voyager 1 is an instrument designed to measure the intensity and composition of cosmic rays, offering valuable data on high-energy particles originating from the Sun, interstellar space, and other celestial sources.
08e3cbcc-ba00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cosmic Ray Subsystem part of Voyager 1

08e3fa82-b999-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The California Institute of Technology Cosmic Background Imager (CBI) is a millimeter-wave telescope located at the Chajnantor Observatory in South America. It is designed to study cosmic microwave background radiation.
08e3fa82-b999-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: millimeter California Institute of Technology Cosmic Background Imager at Chajnantor Observatory

08e4d61c-b793-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU radio beacon receiver (GRBR) station at Chumphon is an observatory in Thailand used to measure ionospheric disturbances and study middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes. It is part of the GRBR network and operates a GNU radio beacon receiver for these measurements.
08e4d61c-b793-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU Radio Beacon Receiver Station at Chumphon, Thailand

08e537b6-ba2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific magnetometer at Tihany (THY), part of the IUGONET Observatory, has been operational since January 1955 and provides valuable data for geomagnetic research as part of the IAGA investigation.
08e537b6-ba2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tihany Observatory

08f24ab0-b7af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Indian Hill North Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Huntsburg Township, Geauga County, Ohio, United States. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
08f24ab0-b7af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Huntsburg Observatory

08fbe9ca-b9b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Savissivik Magnetometer, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, has been operational since 2007-01-01 and is located at the Savissivik Geophysical Observatory in Greenland.
08fbe9ca-b9b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Savissivik Observatory

08ff21c4-b97e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Buckthorn, Thornton is a ground-based astronomical observatory located at Sandridge Street, Thornton, in New South Wales, Australia.
08ff21c4-b97e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Buckthorn Observatory, Australia

0907cd2a-b725-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pameungpeuk Observatory is a ground-based facility located in West Java, Indonesia, near the equator, equipped with an MF radar for measuring wind velocity in the equatorial mesosphere and lower thermosphere.
0907cd2a-b725-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: MF Radar at Pameungpeuk Observatory, Indonesia

091e0d88-b95f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Soroa station (identifier SOR), part of the IUGONET Observatory in Kyoto, operational from 1965 to 1967 as part of the IAGA investigation.
091e0d88-b95f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers part of IUGONET World Data Center

092225d4-b77b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The APS Beamline 13-ID-E is a hard X-ray microprobe facility at the Advanced Photon Source that supports high-resolution X-ray fluorescence, absorption spectroscopy, and diffraction analysis.
092225d4-b77b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hard X-ray microprobe on Advanced Photon Source

09233b2a-b809-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A "Spacecraft.V2" is a specific version of a spacecraft entity within NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS) context, identified by its unique urn and used to describe spacecraft details for various missions. It is part of a broader category defined by the VO Paris Observatory RDF schema for observational facilities.
09233b2a-b809-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: James Webb Telescope

09258348-b73d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1K Optical Photometer** is an instrument designed to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm, specifically during relativistic electron precipitation events, to determine the presence of protons and support studies on scattering by electromagnetic ion cyclotron (EMIC) waves.
09258348-b73d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

0927730e-b82f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vienna Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Vienna, Austria, operated by the University of Vienna since its establishment in 1753.
0927730e-b82f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vienna Observatory, Austria

0927e59c-baea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Bolzaneto Observatory** (code A88) is an astronomical observatory located in Genoa, Italy. It is a ground-based facility with the MPC ID A88 and focuses on astronomical research and observations.
0927e59c-baea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bolzaneto Observatory, Italy

092bfef2-b84c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ASC-Kislovodsk Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Karachay-Cherkessia, Russia, dedicated to the observation and study of small Solar System bodies. It operates under the Minor Planet Center's observatory codes system.
092bfef2-b84c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ASC-Kislovodsk Observatory, Russia

092c4f54-b65a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Mars Express is a European Space Agency (ESA) mission launched in 2003 to explore the planet Mars, consisting of an orbiter for studying the Martian atmosphere, surface, and subsurface, along with a lander named Beagle 2 designed to search for signs of life.
092c4f54-b65a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Express part of European Space Agency (ESA) Mission

092d725e-ba19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LAMP Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Maricopa County, Arizona, USA, dedicated to ground-based observations.
092d725e-ba19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: New River Observatory, United States

092e877c-bb07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Orange.Bay Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, located at the observatory with IAGA identifier ORB. It has been operational since January 1st, 1883.
092e877c-bb07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Orange Bay Observatory

092f640a-bace-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vinyols Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Vinyols i els Arcs, Tarragona, Catalonia, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
092f640a-bace-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vinyols Observatory, Spain

092f8d4e-b935-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Wien-Kobenzl Geomagnetic Observatory (WIK) was a ground-based facility in Vienna, Austria, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements from 1954 until its closure at the end of 2015.
092f8d4e-b935-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Wien-Kobenzl Geomagnetic Observatory

093b171e-ba74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity represents a telescope identified as "cebreros.dss83 35m," which is part of the Deep Space Network (DSN) and located at an observatory in Cebreros, Spain.
093b171e-ba74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 35m Telescope at Cebreros Observatory

093dc89c-b7f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Campo Imperatore Astronomical Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in the Apennine Mountains of Italy. It was established in 1965 and is situated at an altitude of approximately 2,130 meters within the Giardino botanico alpino di Campo Imperatore "Vincenzo Rivera."
093dc89c-b7f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Campo Imperatore Astronomical Observatory, Italy

094014e2-bafd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bucharest Astronomical Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Bucharest, Romania, founded in 1908. It is part of the Astronomical Institute of the Romanian Academy, which was established in 1990 by merging three observatories: Bucharest, Cluj, and Timișoara.
094014e2-bafd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Institute of the Romanian Academy at Bucharest Astronomical Observatory, Romania

09616128-bb71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ion Experiment (ION)** was an instrument built by Mullard Space Science Laboratory for the UKS mission. It consisted of two electrostatic analyzers designed to measure ions in the energy range of 10 eV to 20 keV, providing high-resolution data on ion distributions with all-sky coverage each spin.
09616128-bb71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser on AMPTE UKS

096eb2cc-b99d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Chengdu, part of the IAGA investigation and the Kyoto World Data Center network, operational since 1988.
096eb2cc-b99d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Chengdu Observatory

097357ec-b7fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Gaia is a European Space Agency (ESA) space telescope launched in 2013 to measure the positions and velocities of approximately one billion stars and create a precise three-dimensional map of the Milky Way galaxy.
097357ec-b7fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gaia part of European Space Agency

0976a13e-b863-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tennessee State University 2m Automatic Spectroscopic Telescope (AST) is located at the Fairborn Observatory in North America and specializes in optical waveband observations with a 2.0-meter aperture.

097aed14-b8bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Quanzhou Geomagnetic Observatory (QZH), located in Fengze District, Quanzhou, China, is a ground-based facility that operates a magnetometer to monitor and study geomagnetic activity. It has been operational since January 1995.

097dcdaa-b850-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Three-Axis Fluxgate Magnetometer on Prognoz 6 is an instrument designed to measure vector magnetic fields ranging from 1 to 60 nT with a resolution of 0.5 nT, capable of observing both interplanetary and geomagnetic tail fields.

097fd9f6-b670-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "In-Situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients (IMPACT)" on STEREO B is an investigation consisting of seven instruments designed to observe plasma electrons, magnetic fields, and energetic particles. This suite includes the Solar Wind Electron Analyzer (SWEA), Suprathermal Electron Telescope (STE), a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer (MAG), Solar Electron Proton Telescope (SEPT), Supratherman Ion Telescope (SIT), Low Energy Telescope (LET), and High Energy Telescope (HET).

098304cc-b65d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AGO P2 Antenna Instrument is a component of the ICESTAR observatory's AGO P2 ground station, designed for capturing and transmitting data. It is part of the broader observational facilities used in scientific investigations.
098304cc-b65d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna on ICESTAR part of AGO P2

09866d02-b77e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Majadahonda Observatory (L46) is an astronomical facility located in Majadahonda, Community of Madrid, Spain, dedicated to ground-based observations.
09866d02-b77e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Majadahonda Observatory, Spain

098b4bd2-b829-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tavolaia Astronomical Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Santa Maria a Monte, Pisa, Italy. It is known as the "Osservatorio astronomico di Tavolaia" and has been operational since January 1999.
098b4bd2-b829-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Astronómico de Tavolaia at Tavolaia Observatory, Italy

098c89d4-b702-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The North.Pole.13 Magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at the IAGA North Pole station numbered NPM.
098c89d4-b702-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole Observatory

098db238-b17f-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Energetic Particle Instrument (EPI) on Equator-S is part of the Three Dimensional Plasma Analyzer (3DA) and measures electrons and ions in specific energy ranges using solid-state telescopes, providing detailed data across a large fraction of the solid-angle sphere.

0994b3ce-b7d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lesedi Telescope-SAAO Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Sutherland, Northern Cape, South Africa. It is situated at coordinates -32.37979 latitude and 20.81064 longitude within the Karoo Hoogland Local Municipality.
0994b3ce-b7d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lesedi Telescope at Sutherland Observatory, South Africa

099b538e-b765-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Maunakea Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located on Maunakea, Hawaii, which includes multiple telescopes such as the 0.61m telescope used for various observational studies.
099b538e-b765-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Maunakea Observatory

099c2478-b961-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "MMS 3 Spacecraft Position" is a virtual instrument that provides the ephemeris data for the MMS 3 spacecraft, part of the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission, starting from March 13, 2015.
