099e6252-b686-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Magnetometers at Kodaikanal (KOD), established in 1902, are instruments used to measure the magnetic field at the Kodaikanal ground station, contributing to IAGA investigations and part of the WDC Kyoto network.
099e6252-b686-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kodaikanal Observatory

09a5fd9c-b716-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Paul Wild Observatory, also known as the Narrabri Observatory, is an astronomical research facility located near Narrabri, New South Wales, Australia. It houses the Australia Telescope Compact Array and the Culgoora Solar Observatory.
09a5fd9c-b716-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Australia Telescope Compact Array on Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation Astronomy and Space Science Australia Telescope Compact Array at the Paul Wild Observatory, Australia

09a8997c-b5fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is a ground-based ionospheric observatory located on Ascension Island, operated by Great Britain and known as the Digisonde station. It uses advanced technology to analyze various characteristics of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere.
09a8997c-b5fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde Ionospheric Station at Ascension Island Observatory

09bdb2e2-b636-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IRAS Focal Plane Array (FPA), also known as the Survey Array, was an instrument onboard the Infrared Astronomical Satellite (IRAS) that contained 62 infrared detectors sensitive to four wavelength bands centered at 12, 25, 60, and 100 microns.

09c4839c-b8ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nurmijarvi Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility in Finland dedicated to measuring and studying the Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since 1953 and is part of the global INTERMAGNET network, contributing crucial data for geomagnetic research.
09c4839c-b8ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nurmijärvi Geomagnetic Observatory, Finland

09c9e056-b6e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Jayapura station is a ground-based facility located in Jayapura, Malaysia, that operates as part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network to measure magnetic field data. It includes a fluxgate instrument and is situated at latitude 2.51 and longitude 140.7 on Earth's surface.
09c9e056-b6e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Jayapura Observatory, Malaysia

09df1b78-b648-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dikson Geophysical Observatory, located in Dikson, Russia, is a ground-based facility that includes instruments such as magnetometers for geophysical research.
09df1b78-b648-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dikson Geophysical Observatory, Russia

09ee8d88-b841-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Murou Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Murou-Ono, Uda, Nara Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
09ee8d88-b841-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nara National Astronomical Observatory at Nara Prefecture, Japan

09f54df0-b7c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the BOOTES-5 ground observatory located at Observatorio San Pedro Martir in Ensenada, Baja California, Mexico. It is situated at coordinates 31.04483° N latitude and 244.53556° longitude on the continent of North America.
09f54df0-b7c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Burst Optical Observer and Transient Exploring System at Observatorio San Pedro Martir, Mexico

09f8c2f4-b868-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Cluster II FM6 (Salsa) is one of four identical magnetospheric research satellites in the Cluster II constellation, launched to study small-scale plasma structures and dynamics in Earth's magnetic environment.
09f8c2f4-b868-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cluster II FM6 Salsa spacecraft part of Cluster II mission

09fd6820-b923-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Radisson (RADI) Geophysical Observatory, located in Radisson, Canada, is a ground-based facility established on October 21, 2014, for geophysical observations and research. It includes instruments such as a magnetometer to study Earth's surface dynamics.
09fd6820-b923-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Radisson Geophysical Observatory, Canada

0a0384de-b965-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** PolarLight is a CubeSat mission designed to detect and measure the polarization of X-rays in the few keV energy range, employing an innovative technique for X-ray astronomy.
0a0384de-b965-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: x-ray PolarLight CubeSat

0a076630-baf0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 91-cm Boller & Chivens Cassegrain reflector is a telescope with a 0.91-meter aperture located at the McDonald Observatory in Texas, USA, operational since February 1957.
0a076630-baf0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.91m Boller and Chivens Cassegrain Reflector Telescope at McDonald Observatory, United States

0a0966e0-ba02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Panameno Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in San Pedro de Atacama, Chile. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
0a0966e0-ba02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: San Pedro de Atacama Observatory, Chile

0a0aebcc-bb61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Large Probe Infrared Radiometer (LIR) was an instrument onboard the Pioneer Venus Large Probe designed to measure thermal flux in Venus's atmosphere, detect cloud layers, and estimate water vapor content using a six-channel calibrated radiometer operating in the 3 to 50 micron wavelength range.
0a0aebcc-bb61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Large Probe Infrared Radiometer on Pioneer Venus

0a0f00da-b9a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Entity Definition:** The **Hyderabad Magnetic Observatory** is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Hyderabad, India. It is operated by the National Geographical Research Institute and has been functional since 1965, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
0a0f00da-b9a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hyderabad Observatory, India

0a0f331c-b7ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The ST5-224 Fluxgate Magnetometer, developed at UCLA, is a low-power science-grade device employed on the ST5 spacecraft to investigate magnetic fields in space, featuring a dual-range capability and high linearity for accurate measurements.
0a0f331c-b7ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of Space Technology 5 Investigation

0a12a596-ba59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SuperDARN Hokkaido West HF radar is an observation site in Rikubetsu, Japan, part of the Super Dual Auroral Radar Network (SuperDARN) used for studying auroras and upper atmosphere phenomena. It operates as a ground-based facility with specific geographical coordinates: latitude 43.54 and longitude 143.61.

0a1bde3a-b9c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Thompson Geomagnetic Observatory (TMP):**
A ground-based facility in Thompson, Manitoba, Canada, operating since 1969 to monitor and study geomagnetic activities. It is part of the International Real-time Magnetic Observatory Network (INTERMAGNET).
0a1bde3a-b9c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Thompson Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

0a1d6b02-b95a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex (GDSCC) is a key facility of NASA's Deep Space Network, located near Barstow, California, providing continuous communication with spacecraft in deep space through its advanced antennas and signal processing capabilities.
0a1d6b02-b95a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 26m Antenna DSS-11 part of Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex, United States

0a1db000-bb6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Magnetometers at Poste-De-La-Baleine (PBQ), part of the IAGA investigation, have been operational since January 1985 and are located at the Poste de la Baleine ground station.
0a1db000-bb6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Poste de la Baleine Observatory

0a23cb92-b6cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Davey Lab Observatory is a ground-based observatory that features the Pennsylvania State University's 0.6m (24-inch) telescope, located at the Davey Laboratory.
0a23cb92-b6cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.6m Telescope at Davey Lab Observatory

0a30dc50-b96e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Athabasca Magnetometer is an instrument located at the Athabasca Geophysical Observatory in Canada, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG. It measures magnetic fields and has been operational since February 5, 2008.
0a30dc50-b96e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Athabasca Geophysical Observatory

0a48801e-b9f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EMN Hartland Station** is a ground-based facility located in Hartland, UK, that operates as part of the EMN magnetometer network, focusing on magnetic field measurements using instruments like fluxgate magnetometers.
0a48801e-b9f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hartland Observatory, United Kingdom

0a4d0a24-bc5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Voyager spacecraft, launched in 1977, are a pair of probes (Voyager 1 and 2) designed to explore the outer solar system, including investigating planetary atmospheres, satellites, magnetic fields, and interplanetary environment. They carry scientific instruments and famously bear a Golden Record with sounds and images from Earth.
0a4d0a24-bc5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Voyager 1 and 2 Spacecraft

0a53d20a-b7b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Modiim Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Mevo Modiim, Israel, that has been operating since 1975 and features a magnetometer for geophysical measurements. It is part of the IAGA observatories network.
0a53d20a-b7b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Modiim Observatory, Israel

0a54c86a-b741-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ny Alesund Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields and variations at the Ny-Ålesund geophysical observatory. It has been operational since January 18, 2009, as part of the THEMIS Mission GMAGs (Ground Magnetic and Electric Field Suite).
0a54c86a-b741-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission GMAG

0a5affae-b995-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The BARREL Balloon 2B Trajectory Positions is a virtual instrument that provides ephemeris data for the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) mission, detailing trajectory positions in various coordinate systems.
0a5affae-b995-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

0a65594a-bb9d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Digital Ion Drift Meter (DIDM) is an instrument designed to measure ion distributions and moments such as density, temperature, and drift velocity, aiding in the computation of V x B electric fields. It is part of the CHAMP mission and works alongside a Planar Langmuir Probe to differentiate between internal and external magnetic field variations.
0a65594a-bb9d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digital Ion Drift Meter on CHAMP

0a6af548-ba27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Organ Mesa Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Las Cruces, New Mexico. It operates as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
0a6af548-ba27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Las Cruces Observatory, United States

0a745c18-b8ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Big Delta Geophysical Observatory was a ground-based facility located in Unorganized Borough, Alaska, United States, primarily used for geomagnetic measurements from July 1957 to December 31, 1958.
0a745c18-b8ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Big Delta Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

0a801d44-b6c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AGO P5 Photometer Instrument is a photometric device located at the AGO P5 ground station, used for measuring light intensity and other optical properties as part of the ICESTAR project.
0a801d44-b6c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Photometer part of International Conjunction Exploration Satellites and Tether Research

0a80c04e-bb12-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IAGA:TIF Magnetometer** was a scientific instrument located at the Tiflis Observatory, operational from 1879 to 1905, used for measuring and recording magnetic field variations as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigations.
0a80c04e-bb12-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tiflis Observatory

0a8c44b0-b9b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Nampula Geomagnetic Observatory (NMP) is a ground-based facility in Mozambique that operated from 1982 to 1987, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity.
0a8c44b0-b9b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nampula Geomagnetic Observatory

0a8fc8c6-ba0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SBIG ST-6 UV camera is an astronomical instrument mounted in the Newtonian focus (f/4) of the 70 cm AZT-8 reflecting telescope at Chuguev Observatory, designed for ultraviolet imaging.
0a8fc8c6-ba0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: infrared SBIG ST-6 UV Camera on 0.70m AZT-8 Telescope at Chuguev Observatory

0a924e2c-baa4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MASCAM (MAScot CAMera) is an instrument onboard the MASCOT lander, part of the Hayabusa2 mission, featuring a wide-angle camera and LED illumination devices in four colors. It captures images during descent to the asteroid surface and provides ground data for various instruments.
0a924e2c-baa4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Multispectral Imager on Hayabusa2

0a944f42-b667-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The MMS 1 FIELDS Suite, Search Coil Magnetometer (SCM), specifically measures the three-axis AC magnetic field up to 6 kHz and contributes to studying plasma waves and turbulent dissipation in diffusion regions, having been operational since March 13, 2015.
0a944f42-b667-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Magnetometer part of MMS 1 FIELDS Suite

0a950e16-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The magnetometers at Hayriver (HRI) are instruments located at the IUGONET Observatory in Kyoto that measure magnetic fields as part of the IAGA network.
0a950e16-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

0a9b5ad2-bb29-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, particularly Earth's magnetic field. The specific instance referred to here are the magnetometers located at Arctic Village (AVI), part of a ground-based observatory, which have been operational since January 1979 and are associated with IAGA investigations.
0a9b5ad2-bb29-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Arctic Village Observatory

0a9ff2cc-ba70-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "LANL 2001 Positions" refers to the positional data of the Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) 2001 spacecraft, provided in various coordinate systems. This information is part of a broader observational dataset associated with the LANL Observatory and facilitates accurate tracking and analysis of the spacecraft's movements.
0a9ff2cc-ba70-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft Position part of LANL Observatory

0aa5ee1e-ba36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **MPO Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Florissant, Colorado, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
0aa5ee1e-ba36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Florissant Observatory, United States

0aac0cea-b7c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Piazzano Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Empoli, near Florence, Italy. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical research and observations.
0aac0cea-b7c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Piazzano Observatory, Italy

0ab4caac-b69d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Kaliningrad Geomagnetic Observatory (KNG)** is a ground-based facility in Ulyanovka, Kaliningrad, Russia, that has been operating since 1964 to monitor and study geomagnetic activities. It is notable for its magnetometer instrument and contributions to geophysical research.
0ab4caac-b69d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kaliningrad Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

0ab78624-b7ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fink Spectrograph, an astronomical instrument designed and built at the Lunar and Planetary Laboratory, utilized a transmission grating to cover a spectral range of 5700-11000 Angstroms with a resolution up to 11 Angstroms. It featured a Texas Instruments CCD array cooled to ~120°C for minimal dark noise and was part of a ground-based system developed at the California Institute of Technology.
0ab78624-b7ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Fink Spectrograph on Mount Bigelow 1.54m Telescope

0aca9c9e-b9de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 10.4m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) is a large optical telescope located at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory on La Palma, part of Spain's Canary Islands off the coast of Africa. It is one of the world’s largest single-aperture optical and infrared telescopes.
0aca9c9e-b9de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 10.4m Gran Telescopio Canarias Telescope at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory

0ad041f8-bafb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Celbridge Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located at Celbridge Community School in County Kildare, Ireland.
0ad041f8-bafb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Celbridge Observatory

0ad0cfbc-bba3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Entity Definition:**

The Mars Exploration Rover (MER) mission's second spacecraft, known as MER-2 or Spirit, was designed to explore the Martian surface after landing in Gusev Crater. It featured a robust design for entry, descent, and landing, and carried a suite of scientific instruments for data collection and analysis on Mars.
0ad0cfbc-bba3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Beam Waveguide Antenna at Goldstone Complex

0af7e456-b7f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Yanagida Observatory Mantenboshi is an astronomical observatory located in Kanmachi, Noto, Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan. Established on April 1, 1993, it serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
0af7e456-b7f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yanagida Astronomical Observatory, Japan

0afa42f2-b932-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Rockland Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Sierra Vista, Arizona. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
0afa42f2-b932-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rockland Observatory, United States

0aff3d2c-b5f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astroshot Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Monasterevin, County Kildare, Ireland. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to studying the night sky and celestial objects.
0aff3d2c-b5f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astroshot Observatory at Monasterevin, Ireland

0b00ab52-b9e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
La Giustiniana Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Rome, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
0b00ab52-b9e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: La Giustiniana Observatory, Italy

0b089e76-b61a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MEASURE Magnetometer Array at the University of South Carolina is a fluxgate magnetometer instrument used for geomagnetic observations. It is part of the broader MEASURE observatory network and operates under the University of South Carolina's supervision.
0b089e76-b61a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of MEASURE

0b0ee182-b688-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The magnetometer at the Shumagin Observatory is an instrument used to measure magnetic field variations as part of the IAGA investigation. It has been operational since January 1, 2005 and is integrated within the iugonet-observatory-wdc_kyoto-wdc-shu facility.
0b0ee182-b688-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Shumagin Observatory

0b11255e-b70b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The BiAnto Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Lauria, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting observations of celestial objects and phenomena.
0b11255e-b70b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: BiAnto Observatory, Italy

0b153232-ba55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Srobarova Geomagnetic Observatory (SRO), located in Marcelová, District of Komárno, Slovakia, is a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and measurement of Earth's geomagnetic field.
0b153232-ba55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Srobarova Geomagnetic Observatory, Slovakia

0b257108-b639-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Dal Es Salaam station is a magnetometer facility located in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, part of the global MAGDAS network for monitoring geomagnetic activity. It is situated at coordinates -6.47 latitude and 39.12 longitude on the African continent.
0b257108-b639-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dal Es Salaam Observatory, Tanzania

0b2f8ef2-bb04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Borok Geomagnetic Observatory (BOX):** A ground-based facility in Russia that monitors geomagnetic activity, part of the IUGONET instrument network and located in Yaroslavl Oblast.
0b2f8ef2-bb04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Borok Geomagnetic Observatory

0b347bde-b75c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Sonneberg Observatory** is an astronomical observatory in Sonneberg, Germany, founded in 1925, known for its long-term studies of variable stars and extensive archive of astronomical plates.
0b347bde-b75c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sonneberg Observatory, Germany

0b3ba1e8-ba4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located on Macquarie Island as part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network, used to measure magnetic fields for geophysical studies.
0b3ba1e8-ba4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observatory, Antarctica

0b43607e-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Mars crustal magnetic field analytical models" are a set of scientific tools used to analyze and understand the magnetic fields present in Mars's crust. These models are part of the CNES Observatory CDPP Archive Cluster 1 and provide valuable insights into the planet's geological history and internal structure through magnetic data analysis.
0b43607e-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Crustal Magnetic Field Analytical Model part of Cluster 1 Mission

0b4533d6-b97b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tashkent-2/Yangi-Bazar Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields at the IAGA observatory in Tashkent, operational since January 1883.
0b4533d6-b97b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tashkent Observatory

0b49367c-bad2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Salvador Astronomical Observatory (I20) is an astronomical facility located in Rio Cuarto, Argentina. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
0b49367c-bad2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Salvador Astronomical Observatory, Argentina

0b4b3074-b63d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Ourense, Galicia, Spain. It is known as the Miron del Cielo Observatory and operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
0b4b3074-b63d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Miron del Cielo Observatory, Spain

0b4e1870-b7cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Hakos Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in the Khomas Region of Namibia, situated at an altitude of 1852 meters. It was established in January 1999 and is part of the Gamsberg Pass area.
0b4e1870-b7cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hakos Observatory, Namibia

0b4e9e7a-bb6b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Shishikui Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. It is situated at the coordinates 33.551342° N, 134.3189° E and has the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 342.
0b4e9e7a-bb6b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Shishikui Observatory, Japan

0b509680-b5b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Saint-Felicien Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG since 2014.
0b509680-b5b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Saint-Felicien Observatory

0b53493e-bad0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **McDonald Observatory - LCO ELP Aqawan A #1:** An astronomical observatory located in Fort Davis, Texas, United States, known as part of the McDonald Observatory facilities.
0b53493e-bad0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: McDonald Observatory, United States

0b5d6db8-b717-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope (VLT), specifically Unit Telescope 1 (Antu or UT1), is an 8.2-meter Ritchey-Chretien Cassegrain telescope located at the Paranal Observatory in Chile, known for its advanced active optics system and a variety of instruments including FORS1, FORS2, NACO, and KMOS.
0b5d6db8-b717-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 8.2m Very Large Telescope Antu at Paranal Observatory, Chile

0b5e6f64-b86c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Neutral Atmosphere Temperature (NATE) experiment on the AE-D satellite measured the kinetic temperature of the neutral atmosphere by analyzing molecular nitrogen density variations within a spherical chamber, also providing data on neutral composition and zonal wind.
0b5e6f64-b86c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutral Atmosphere Temperature part of Explorer-54 Mission

0b67c1a2-ba08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Burlington Remote Site Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Woodland Township, Burlington County, New Jersey. It serves as part of the larger Burlington Observatory network and focuses on ground-based observations.
0b67c1a2-ba08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Burlington Remote Site Observatory, United States

0b6c707e-b6ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: NOTO, also known as the Nordic Optical Telescope Observatory, is a ground-based astronomical observatory located on the island of La Palma in the Canary Islands. It is operated collaboratively by institutions from Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden to conduct optical astronomy research.
0b6c707e-b6ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nordic Optical Telescope

0b6f02e2-b958-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The YGCO Hoshikawa and Nagano Stations is an astronomical observatory located in Gyoda, Saitama Prefecture, Japan. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research on Earth.
0b6f02e2-b958-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nagano Station at Hoshikawa Observatory, Japan

0b70527e-b623-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ion Mass Spectrometer** on Explorer 32 (AE-B) was an instrument designed to measure concentrations of ion species in the topside ionosphere, primarily hydrogen, helium, nitrogen, and oxygen. It operated for 10 months, providing real-time data to study diurnal variations and other atmospheric phenomena, using a spectrometer sensor with specific RF frequencies to cover the mass range of relevant ions.
0b70527e-b623-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer part of Atmosphere Explorer-B

0b7096a0-bb3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Deep Impact mission, launched in 2005, aimed to study the composition and structure of a comet by impacting it with a projectile. The mission successfully collided an impactor into Comet Tempel 1, revealing valuable data about the comet's interior through the resulting ejecta and crater formation.
0b7096a0-bb3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label:
Deep Impact space mission
part of Discovery Program

0b70d898-b628-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Prague Observatory was a ground-based facility located in the Historic Centre of Prague, operating from 1830 to 1926, primarily used for magnetic observations.
0b70d898-b628-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Prague Observatory, Czechia

0b792a18-b83d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Erfurt, Thuringia, Germany.
0b792a18-b83d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Erfurt Observatory

0b89624e-baf8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **THEMIS E Spacecraft Position** refers to the instrument aboard the THEMIS-D probe that provides data on its status and position as part of the THEMIS mission operated by the CNES Observatory.
0b89624e-baf8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: THEMIS E Ephemeris part of Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms

0b8cac38-bb93-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Woomera station was a ground-based observatory located in South Australia, operational from May 1961 to December 1969, primarily known for its ionosonde instrument used for studying the Earth's upper atmosphere.
0b8cac38-bb93-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionosonde at Woomera Observatory, Australia

0b9399fc-b6cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Saarbruecken Rastpfuhl Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Saarbrücken, Germany, known for its ground-based facilities.
0b9399fc-b6cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sternwarte Saarbruecken Rastpfuhl, Germany

0b94e370-b847-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Salvatore di Giacomo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in San Lazzaro, Agerola, near Naples, Italy. It is situated at the coordinates 40.623927 latitude and 14.56406 longitude on Earth.
0b94e370-b847-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Salvatore di Giacomo Observatory, Italy

0b9ced90-b6df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** OGO 4 (Orbiting Geophysical Observatory 4) was an American geophysical research satellite designed to study the interrelationships between various atmospheric and solar phenomena during periods of increased solar activity. It carried multiple experiments and was launched on July 28, 1967, from Vandenberg AFB, United States.
0b9ced90-b6df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Orbiting Geophysical Observatory part of Orbiting Geophysical Observatory Program

0ba44bf8-b94b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics (LASP) McPherson Vacuum Ultraviolet Analytical Spectrophotometer (VUVAS) is a high-performance Seya-Namioka scanning-grating monochromator designed for precise analysis in the ultraviolet spectrum, ranging from about 100 nm to 200 nm.
0ba44bf8-b94b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics McPherson Vacuum UltraViolet Analytical Spectrophotometer

0ba8e146-bbca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Merlette Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Hautes-Alpes, France, used for ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
0ba8e146-bbca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Merlette Observatory

0babc1de-ba4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Magadan fluxgate magnetometer** is part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) network, located at the IUGONET-Observatory in ISEE. It measures magnetic field variations using a fluxgate sensor type.
0babc1de-ba4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of Iugonet Observatory Isse Mm210 Mgd

0bb61bae-b742-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **NSF National Optical-Infrared Astronomy Research Laboratory (NOIRLab) NSF 2.1 Meter Telescope** is a 2.1-meter optical telescope located at the Kitt Peak National Observatory in North America, operated by NOIRLab and funded by the National Science Foundation (NSF).
0bb61bae-b742-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 2.1m Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory

0bb9b036-b646-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Magnetometer at Hartebeesthoek (HBK)** is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field, located at the Hartebeesthoek Radio Astronomy Observatory in South Africa. It has been operational since January 1973 and is part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
0bb9b036-b646-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hartebeesthoek Observatory

0bc053ea-b764-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Doyan Rose Observatory (code 744) is an astronomical observatory located in Indianapolis, Indiana, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
0bc053ea-b764-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Indianapolis Observatory

0bc6847e-b794-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sample Analysis at Mars (SAM) suite is a set of scientific instruments on the Curiosity rover designed to investigate the habitability of Mars by analyzing molecular and elemental chemistry relevant to life. It consists of a Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer, Gas Chromatograph, and Tunable Laser Spectrometer.
0bc6847e-b794-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sample Analysis at Mars on Curiosity rover

0bd06b56-b5c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Helium Abundance Detector (HAD)** is a specialized instrument on the Galileo Probe that measured the helium to hydrogen ratio in Jupiter's atmosphere using an interferometer, providing high-accuracy data on the planet's composition.
0bd06b56-b5c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Helium Abundance Detector for Galileo Probe on Galileo Spacecraft

0bdfdafe-bb64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mount Lemmon (Catalina) Station** is an observatory facility located on Mount Lemmon in Arizona. It is part of the Catalina Sky Survey and features a 1.54-meter telescope for astronomical observations.
0bdfdafe-bb64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.54m Telescope at Mount Lemmon Observatory

0be0efb2-b96a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Purple Mountain Observatory, located in Nanjing, China, is an astronomical observatory responsible for calculating the official Chinese calendar of mainland China. It was established in 1934 and is situated at an altitude of 267 meters on Purple Mountain.
0be0efb2-b96a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Purple Mountain Observatory, China

0be1ccc6-b946-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Chinese Culture University Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in the Shilin District of Taipei, Taiwan. It is situated at the Chinese Culture University and serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
0be1ccc6-b946-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Chinese Culture University

0c11039e-b93a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital receiver installed in Kwajalein, Micronesia, designed to measure ionospheric total electron content using LEO satellite signals. It employs GNU Radio software and USRP hardware for signal processing and acquisition at 150 and 400 MHz frequencies.
0c11039e-b93a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU Radio Beacon Receiver at Kwajalein Observatory, Micronesia

0c1ab024-ba1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The U.S. Naval Observatory's 1m (40 inch) telescope at the Naval Observatory Flagstaff Station (NOFS) is a ground-based observatory facility used for astronomical observations.
0c1ab024-ba1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.02m Telescope at Naval Observatory Flagstaff Station

0c20bb06-ba64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Pin Oak Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Fort Madison, Iowa, United States. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
0c20bb06-ba64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pin Oak Observatory

0c25af50-b75b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **MMS 3 FIELDS Suite, Axial Double Probe (ADP)** is an instrument on the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS), featuring two 10-meter antennas that measure three-dimensional electric fields from DC to 100 kHz. It was launched in March 2015 and is part of a suite led by the University of New Hampshire.
0c25af50-b75b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Axial Double Probe part of MMS 3 Fields Suite

0c2b38ac-bbd5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "GOES 8 Position" is an instrument on the GOES 8 spacecraft that provides ephemeris data, which includes information about the spacecraft's position and trajectory. It is part of the GOES 8 observatory system and facilitates accurate tracking and scientific observations from orbit.
0c2b38ac-bbd5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GOES 8 Ephemeris part of GOES 8

0c2c5eba-b93e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hoogeveen Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Hoogeveen, Drenthe, Netherlands. It operates as a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID B93.
0c2c5eba-b93e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hoogeveen Observatory, Netherlands

0c30da16-ba84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Flin Flon Vector Magnetic Field 0.5 s Data Geophysical Observatory, also known as the The Pas (TPAS) station, is located in The Pas, Manitoba, Canada, and is part of the UCLA GBO Network. It specializes in collecting magnetic field data with a magnetometer instrument.
0c30da16-ba84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Flin Flon Vector Magnetic Field 0.5 s Data Geophysical Observatory

0c323c8e-b66b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Mt. Bigelow is a ground-based observatory located at North General Hitchcock Highway, Soldier Camp, Pima County, Arizona, United States (latitude 32.41692° N, longitude 249.26736° E).
0c323c8e-b66b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mt. Bigelow Observatory, United States

0c338c42-b7c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) station at Kototabang, Indonesia is a ground-based facility developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research (ISEE), Nagoya University, to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions. It is located in Baringin, Agam, West Sumatra, and collaborates with RISH (Kyoto U.) and LAPAN.
0c338c42-b7c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Kototabang Observatory, Indonesia

0c33e20c-bb73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cégep de Trois-Rivières Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Champlain, Quebec, Canada. It is a ground-based facility used for educational and research purposes in astronomy.
0c33e20c-bb73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cégep de Trois-Rivières Observatory

0c36acb4-b68a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Christiania Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Oslo, Norway, known for its ground-based observations and contributions to astronomy.
0c36acb4-b68a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Christiania Observatory, Norway

0c3c66ae-b6e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Perth Observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Bickley, Western Australia, known for its ground-based observational research and public outreach programs. It is situated at coordinates -32.00874 latitude and 116.135 longitude within the continent of Oceania.
0c3c66ae-b6e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Perth Observatory

0c46ff24-b734-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Old Observatory of Geneva is an astronomical observatory located in Geneva, Switzerland, established in 1772. It served as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations until its operations were moved to a new location in 1967.
0c46ff24-b734-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Old Observatory of Geneva, Switzerland

0c4bb4f0-bba4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The BARREL Balloon 1R was a high-altitude balloon mission launched in January 2013 as part of NASA's Living with a Star program to study the loss of relativistic electrons from Earth’s radiation belts by measuring Bremsstrahlung X-rays and magnetic fields in the stratosphere.
0c4bb4f0-bba4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of NASA Living with a Star, Geospace Mission of Opportunity

0c4c84c8-bbc9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The NASA THEMIS EPO Petersburg Station (PTRS) is an educational public outreach magnetometer operated by UCLA, located in Petersburg, Alaska, USA. It is part of the THEMIS ground observatory network and provides magnetic field measurements subject to environmental noise.
0c4c84c8-bbc9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Petersburg Observatory, United States

0c4fedac-b737-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1D Ephemeris is a virtual instrument that provides trajectory positions of balloons in various coordinate systems, supporting the study of relativistic electron losses in space.
0c4fedac-b737-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses part of BARREL Observatory

0c53d5da-b916-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Maidbronn Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Rimpar, Bavaria, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to studying celestial objects and phenomena from its location on Earth.
0c53d5da-b916-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Maidbronn Observatory, Germany

0c54d6b2-baf4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Deep Space Climate Observatory (DSCOVR) is a space weather and Earth observation satellite operated by NOAA, launched in 2015 to monitor solar wind near the L1 point and provide early warnings of potential solar magnetic storms that could impact Earth's infrastructure.
0c54d6b2-baf4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep Space Climate Observatory

0c5748ee-bb0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LANL97A Energetic Spectrometer for Particles (ESP) is an instrument that measures high-energy particles using a bismuth germanate crystal and a plastic scintillator coupled to a photomultiplier tube, capable of detecting electrons from 0.7 to 26 MeV and protons from 11 to >20 MeV.
0c5748ee-bb0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energy Spectrometer for Particles part of LANL 97A Observatory

0c57d988-b14f-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2Q Optical Photometer is an instrument designed to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm during relativistic electron precipitation events, aiming to determine the presence of protons accompanying these electrons by observing emissions characteristic of precipitating protons.
0c57d988-b14f-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses BARREL Balloon 2Q Optical Photometer

0c57e612-bbe5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Málaga, Spain, known as the AGP GUAM 4 observatory.
0c57e612-bbe5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: AGP GUAM 4 Observatory, Spain

0c68a7ba-bb0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE)** was a NASA space mission launched on December 14, 2009, that completed two full scans of the sky in infrared light by early 2011, capturing data on hundreds of millions of celestial objects including galaxies, stars, and asteroids.
0c68a7ba-bb0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer

0c7690dc-badf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CS3-DanHenge Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Landers, California.
0c7690dc-badf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Landers Observatory

0c813190-b97c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Chinese Academy of Science 4m Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopy Telescope (LAMOST) is a large optical telescope located in Asia, known for its wide field of view and capability to conduct spectroscopic surveys. It is also referred to as the Guo Shoujing Telescope.
0c813190-b97c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopy Telescope

0c946670-bb20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LANL1994 is a geosynchronous spacecraft launched in 1994 that carries instruments to study energetic electrons and ions, primarily within Earth's magnetosphere and radiation belts.
0c946670-bb20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geosynchronous spacecraft carrying energetic electron and ion instruments

0c9cf8d6-b917-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Burnt Tree Hill Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Cle Elum, Washington, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility with the MPC code U63.
0c9cf8d6-b917-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Burnt Tree Hill Observatory, United States

0ca77bd6-bb87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
HEO-3 refers to a satellite in a Highly Elliptical Orbit (HEO), specifically one of three such satellites known as HEO-1, HEO-2, and HEO-3. These orbits have a period of about 12 hours, with a low perigee and high apogee, and are used primarily for non-science missions.
0ca77bd6-bb87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Highly Elliptical Orbit satellite 3

0caf18fe-b65b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Magnetometers at Annamalainagar (ANN)** were instruments used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at a ground-based observatory in Annamalainagar, operating from January 1957 until December 31, 1993.
0caf18fe-b65b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Annamalainagar Observatory

0cb47352-b6fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometers at Fredericksburg (FRD), operational since January 1956, are part of a ground-based observatory and contribute to the IAGA investigation, providing valuable data on Earth's magnetic field variations.
0cb47352-b6fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fredericksburg Observatory

0cc7c98a-b9d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Overberg Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bredasdorp, Western Cape, South Africa. It operates as a ground-based facility with the MPC (Minor Planet Center) ID 641.
0cc7c98a-b9d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Overberg Observatory, South Africa

0cd0fece-ba61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The MAGDAS observation network includes a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed at Rockhampton, Australia, part of the IUGONET observatory.
0cd0fece-ba61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MAGDAS observation network

0cd42562-bb25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Zlín Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Lesní čtvrť district of Zlín, Czechia. It operates as a ground-based facility at an altitude of 335 meters and is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code B41.
0cd42562-bb25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Zlín Observatory, Czechia

0cdcd5d0-b86f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific magnetometer at the Trelew ground station has been operational since January 1, 1957, and is part of the IAGA investigation network within the IUGONET Observatory (WDC Kyoto).
0cdcd5d0-b86f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

0ce091ca-b126-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RPA1 - EESA Electron Electrostatic Analyzer is an instrument aboard the Giotto spacecraft, designed to measure the three-dimensional distributions of electrons with energies between 10 eV and 30 keV.
0ce091ca-b126-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Electrostatic Analyzer part of Giotto

0ce203a0-bb0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MEX spacecraft ephemeris is a dataset providing the orbital positions and trajectories of the Mars Express (MEX) spacecraft. It is part of the CDPP-AMDA observatory managed by CNES and includes detailed positional data for scientific investigations.
0ce203a0-bb0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: MEX Ephemeris part of Mars Express

0ce32396-b959-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Skylab was the United States' first space station, launched by NASA in 1973. It served as an orbiting laboratory for approximately 24 weeks and supported various scientific experiments and observations before reentering Earth's atmosphere in 1979.
0ce32396-b959-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Skylab

0cf653aa-bb41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GOES (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites) series are NASA-developed and NOAA-operated spacecraft that orbit the Earth in a geosynchronous manner to provide continuous monitoring of weather patterns and environmental conditions.
0cf653aa-bb41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites

0d003e38-b8fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Pine Ridge Magnetometer is an instrument located at the Pine Ridge Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission's Ground-Based Observatories network. It has been operational since September 9, 2004, and measures magnetic field variations to study geomagnetic phenomena.
0d003e38-b8fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pine Ridge Observatory

0d0ad9e6-b86d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS) 1.52m Telescope at Observatoire de Haute-Provence (OHP) is a ground-based optical telescope located in France, used for astronomical research and observations.
0d0ad9e6-b86d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.52m Telescope at Observatoire de Haute-Provence

0d12b534-b7f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Koronas" is a series of Russian (Roskosmos) space missions designed to monitor solar activity using X-ray observations.
0d12b534-b7f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray Russian Roskosmos Koronas Solar Activity Monitor Satellite Mission

0d17a66a-bb2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nice Magnetometer is an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields, located at the IAGA-identified station NCE. It was operational from January 1, 1885, to December 31, 1901, and is part of the Nice observatory under the IAGA investigation.
0d17a66a-bb2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nice Observatory

0d18bc4c-bbd2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Plasma Wave Investigation (PWI)** on the Geotail spacecraft is an instrument designed to study wave-particle interactions and instabilities in various regions of Earth's magnetosphere. It consists of three sets of receivers—the Sweep Frequency Analyzer (SFA), Multi-Channel Analyzer (MCA), and Wave-Form Capture (WFC)—which measure electric and magnetic field spectra and waveforms in specific frequency ranges.
0d18bc4c-bbd2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Wave Investigation on Geotail

0d1ac2d8-b8af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Parker Solar Probe SWEAP Investigation's Electrostatic Analyzer (SPAN-Ai)** is an instrument aboard the Parker Solar Probe that uses electrostatic optics and time-of-flight measurements to determine the velocity, energy, and mass-to-charge ratio of incoming positively charged ions. It helps unambiguously measure the proportion of helium nuclei compared to protons in solar wind plasma.
0d1ac2d8-b8af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer part of Parker Solar Probe SWEAP Investigation

0d2bcd3c-b68c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Imaging Science Subsystem - Wide Angle for Voyager 2 is an instrument on the Voyager 2 spacecraft designed to capture wide-field images for planetary studies and space observations.
0d2bcd3c-b68c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imaging Science Subsystem - Wide Angle on Voyager 2

0d2ecddc-b7bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The BARREL Balloon 1D Engineering Data Interface is an instrument component of the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) mission, designed to convert analog signals (temperatures, voltages, and currents) into digital data with high precision.
0d2ecddc-b7bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

0d3bbaba-bba2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Temecula Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Rancho Palomar, Wolf Creek, California, known for ground-based observations.
0d3bbaba-bba2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Palomar Observatory, United States

0d42ca50-bb5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Soisy-sur-Seine Observatory (MPC ID: 614) is an astronomical observatory located in Évry, Essonne, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
0d42ca50-bb5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Soisy-sur-Seine Observatory, France

0d45e668-b619-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1L Data Processing Unit is an instrument controller board that collects data from various sensors, formats it for transmission via an Iridium Modem, and manages the command-cutdown system. It utilizes a flexible FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) to handle interface logic with other components through a backplane.
0d45e668-b619-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

0d46154a-b897-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the Deep Space Station 27 (DSS-27), a ground-based observatory primarily used for deep space communications and observations.
0d46154a-b897-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep Space Station 27, Antarctica

0d473f10-b766-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GROWTH India Telescope at the Indian Astronomical Observatory (IAO) is an astronomical observatory located in Leh district, Ladakh, India. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
0d473f10-b766-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m GROWTH India Telescope at Indian Astronomical Observatory, India

0d631f36-b8c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EMN magnetometer network** in Garoua, Cameroon, is a ground-based facility that monitors Earth's magnetic field variations at the specified coordinates (latitude 9.18, longitude 13.24) within the city of Djim on the African continent.
0d631f36-b8c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at EMN Garoua Observatory, Cameroon

0d645114-bbbb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "DSS-61" refers to a ground observatory, which is part of the Deep Space Network operated by NASA, used for radio and radar astronomy as well as spacecraft communications.
0d645114-bbbb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Madrid Observatory

0d7bbc2a-ba1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NEAR Laser Rangefinder (NLR) was an altimeter onboard the NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft that mapped the surface of asteroid 433 Eros with high precision using time-of-flight measurements.
0d7bbc2a-ba1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Laser Rangefinder on Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous

0d90fb38-b65c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ultraviolet Nitric-Oxide (UVNO) experiment on the AE-C satellite used a two-channel Ebert-Fastie spectrometer to measure nitric oxide density in the Earth's atmosphere by observing airglow in the ultraviolet spectrum. It operated by detecting resonance fluorescence of sunlight by nitric oxide molecules, providing altitude profiles of nitric oxide concentration along the satellite's path.
0d90fb38-b65c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Spectrometer on Atmosphere Explorer-C

0d979344-ba35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS Digital Fields Board Filter Bank is an instrument component designed to provide band-pass filtering for EFI and SCM spectra, as well as E12HF peak and average values, in a computationally efficient manner. It processes signals through a series of low-pass filters and decimation steps to reduce the sampling frequency while maintaining key data characteristics.
0d979344-ba35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Filter Bank on THEMIS

0da2eb22-b6c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Venera 10 Energetic Particles experiment was a suite of particle detectors used by the Soviet spacecraft Venera 10 to monitor charged particles in interplanetary space and Venus orbit, measuring protons and electrons within specific energy ranges.
0da2eb22-b6c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particles experiment on Venera 10

0dad077a-b705-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NICT Ionosonde at Okinawa is a Type 10C Ionosonde operated by the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT) in Japan, used for regular radar investigations.
0dad077a-b705-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Type 10C Ionosonde at Okinawa Observatory

0daed03e-b924-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The San Vittore Observatory was a private astronomical observatory located in Bologna, Italy, active from 1969 to 2004.
0daed03e-b924-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: San Vittore Observatory, Italy

0db9fbe8-b5b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kodiak Geophysical Observatory (KODK) is a ground-based facility located in Kodiak, Alaska, part of the THEMIS network. It houses instruments such as a magnetometer to conduct geophysical measurements and studies.
0db9fbe8-b5b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kodiak Geophysical Observatory

0dc0fcea-b92f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Bereznyaki ground station, operational since January 1965, which measures magnetic field variations as part of the WDC/GDMC investigation.
0dc0fcea-b92f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bereznyaki Observatory

0dc72a5a-b779-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pioneer Venus Small Probe (Day) Differential Long Base Line Interferometer was an experiment on the Pioneer Venus mission that used interferometry techniques to measure wind speeds and circulation patterns in Venus' lower atmosphere by tracking radio signals from descending probes.
0dc72a5a-b779-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Differential Long Baseline Interferometer part of Pioneer Venus Small Probe (Day)

0dd46134-b96d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kangerlussuaq Magnetometer is an instrument located at the Kangerlussuaq Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation since 2007. It measures magnetic field variations to study geomagnetic activity and space weather effects.
0dd46134-b96d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kangerlussuaq Observatory

0dd7c6ec-b7da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ARCAD-3 Ephemeris** is an instrument under the Platform investigation, providing data on the position and velocity of the ARCAD-3 spacecraft. It is part of the CNES Observatory CDPP Archive and offers ephemeris information for scientific research.
0dd7c6ec-b7da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ARCAD-3 part of CNES Observatory

0de109c8-b5ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Nihondaira Observatory (Obs. code: 385), also known as Oohira Station, is an astronomical observatory located in Shimizu, Japan, notable for its contributions to the discovery of minor planets by astronomer Takeshi Urata.
0de109c8-b5ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nihondaira Observatory, Japan

0de4bc26-b974-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Crolles Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Jean-de-Bournay, France. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
0de4bc26-b974-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Crolles Observatory, France

0de94476-bbb3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hinode X-Ray Telescope (XRT) is a high-resolution grazing incidence telescope on the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, designed to capture X-ray and visible light images with a 2k x 2k CCD camera over a bandwidth of 2 - 200 Angstrom.
0de94476-bbb3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray Telescope on Hinode

0df7b72e-b99a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF) 32m Noto VLBI Station is a 32-meter telescope located at the Noto Radio Observatory in Europe, designed for Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observations in the radio waveband.
0df7b72e-b99a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 32.0m radio National Institute for Astrophysics Noto Very Long Baseline Interferometry Station at Noto Radio Observatory

0e09a2b6-b5b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
DSS-26 is a 34-meter radio telescope located at the Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex in California, known for its innovative beam waveguide design and multi-band (S-, X-, Ka-) communication capabilities.
0e09a2b6-b5b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Beam Waveguide Antenna at Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex, United States

0e10754c-b71b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity represents the "Wind" spacecraft's ephemeris data, which includes its orbital positions and geomagnetic parameters. This information is part of the CNES Observatory CDPP Archive for Wind, accessible via the specified platform investigation name and codes.
0e10754c-b71b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wind part of CNES Observatory CDPP Archive

0e117d6c-b6f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Induction Magnetometer at Zhigansk, part of the ISEE Magnetometer Data initiative, measures variations in the 3-D vector geomagnetic field with a sampling rate of 64 Hz.
0e117d6c-b6f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Space Environment Service

0e140e2a-b8bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IPRT/AMATERAS** is a high-sensitivity radio spectropolarimeter installed at Tohoku University's Iitate observatory in Fukushima, Japan, designed for solar radio burst observations within the 150 to 500 MHz frequency range.
0e140e2a-b8bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna on Iitate Planetary Radio Telescope at Iitate Observatory, Japan

0e159c68-bad4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ) 0.5m Telescope at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory (OAO) is a small optical telescope located in Asia, specifically in Japan, used for astronomical observations and research.
0e159c68-bad4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.5m optical National Astronomical Observatory of Japan Telescope at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory, Japan

0e184df8-b978-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Shandong University 1m Telescope (WHO) is an optical telescope located at the Weihai Observatory in Asia. It has an aperture of 1 meter and is used for astronomical observations by Shandong University.
0e184df8-b978-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 1.0m Telescope at Weihai Observatory

0e27e150-bb85-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Entity Definition:**
RBSP-B, also known as Van Allen Probe B, is a space probe that was part of NASA's Radiation Belt Storm Probes mission to study Earth’s Van Allen radiation belts and their interaction with solar activity.
0e27e150-bb85-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radiation Belt Storm Probe B part of Van Allen Probes

0e2e8b48-b9fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Learmonth Solar Radio telescopes in Western Australia are instruments that monitor solar radio emissions across multiple frequencies to study both the quiet and active Sun, aiding in calibration, interference detection, and predicting space weather events.
0e2e8b48-b9fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Radio Telescope on Learmonth Observatory, Australia

0e2fb194-b65f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LFRTO (Low Frequency Radio Transmitter Observation) is a vertical electric monopole antenna designed to detect radio frequencies ranging from 20kHz to 100kHz and is part of the IUGONET observatory at Tohoku University, located in Pontianak station, Indonesia.
0e2fb194-b65f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low Frequency Radio Transmitter Observation Antenna part of IUGONET Observatory, Indonesia

0e391476-b819-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "IMAGE Positions" dataset provides the spatial coordinates of the IMAGE spacecraft in different reference frames, crucial for understanding its location and trajectory during scientific observations.
0e391476-b819-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Image on Spacecraft

0e3a3780-b7dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ion Composition 3D Spectrometer (PROMICS-3)** is a mass spectrometer aboard the Interball Tail Probe, designed to conduct three-dimensional measurements of ions and electrons within specified energy ranges, using toroidal electrostatic analyzers for mass separation.
0e3a3780-b7dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Composition 3D Spectrometer part of Interball Tail Probe

0e3cc35c-b718-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Ochiai Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Enzan-Ichinosetakahashi, Koshu, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan, known for its ground-based observations.
0e3cc35c-b718-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 368 Telescope at Ochiai Observatory, Japan

0e3d3784-b6e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kepler space telescope was a NASA mission launched in 2009 to discover Earth-sized planets orbiting other stars by detecting brightness variations in over 100,000 stars.
0e3d3784-b6e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.7m Kepler Space Telescope

0e3ddba4-bbc1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Elginfield Observatory was an astronomical observatory located in Middlesex Centre, Ontario, Canada, operated by the University of Western Ontario from 1969. It featured a 1.2 m Ritchey–Chrétien telescope used for spectroscopy and photometry, contributing to research on Cepheid variable stars, minor planets, and large Perseid meteoroids.
0e3ddba4-bbc1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.2m Ritchey–Chrétien Telescope at Elginfield Observatory, Canada

0e5119ae-b774-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The New Horizons Spacecraft Ephemeris Virtual Instrument provides the positional data and trajectory information for the New Horizons spacecraft during its flybys of Pluto and other Kuiper Belt objects. This virtual instrument is crucial for tracking and understanding the spacecraft's journey through the outer solar system.
0e5119ae-b774-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris part of New Horizons

0e6573fc-b659-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory (SAO) 10m Whipple Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope is a gamma-ray observing instrument located at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in North America. It has an aperture of 10 meters and is used for studying high-energy astrophysical phenomena through the detection of Cherenkov radiation.
0e6573fc-b659-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 10m Whipple Atmospheric Cherenkov Gamma-ray Telescope at Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory

0e69169e-b922-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS) 2m Bernard Lyot Telescope (TBL)" is a ground-based astronomical observatory located at Observatoire Midi-Pyrénées, used for scientific research and observations.
0e69169e-b922-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Bernard Lyot Telescope at Midi-Pyrénées Observatory

0e82428e-b6cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AUTH Astronomical Station is a ground-based observatory located in Prodromos, Limassol District, Cyprus. It is situated at coordinates 34.9321° N, 32.84016° E and serves as an astronomical research facility operated by Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (AUTH).
0e82428e-b6cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Station at Auth Observatory, Cyprus

0e8a2448-bb10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS)** onboard the DMSP-F18 satellite is a multi-channel microwave radiometer that provides imagery and sounding data for temperature, humidity, and precipitation measurements across 24 channels and 21 frequencies, covering the 54 and 183 GHz bands. It was launched on October 18, 2009 as part of the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP).
0e8a2448-bb10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Microwave Imager and Sounder on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

0e91e9d8-bbc6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Learmonth Solar Telescope** is part of the Learmonth Solar Observatory in Western Australia and includes a GONG instrument for helioseismological studies, an optical telescope for monitoring sunspots, and radio telescopes for tracking solar activity across various frequencies.
0e91e9d8-bbc6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spectrometer on Learmonth Solar Telescope at IUGONET Observatory, Australia

0e9ba6e6-b9b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IAGA Observatory in Budapest was a ground-based facility located at Tóth Árpád sétány in the Castle District of Budapest, Hungary. It operated from January 1, 1875, to December 31, 1889, and was part of a larger observatory network, primarily focusing on geomagnetic measurements with magnetometers.
0e9ba6e6-b9b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Budapest Observatory, Hungary

0eaede78-b78c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CNVL Observatory (also known as Colegiul Național Vasile Lucaciu Observatory) is an astronomical observatory located in Baia Mare, Romania. It operates as a ground-based facility and is situated within the premises of Colegiul Național Vasile Lucaciu at Strada George Coșbuc, Baia Mare.
0eaede78-b78c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Baia Mare Observatory, Romania

0eb26cde-b61d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dallas Geomagnetic Observatory (DAL), located in Richardson, Texas, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1964 to 1973, conducting geophysical measurements primarily with magnetometers.
0eb26cde-b61d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Dallas Observatory, United States

0eb6b338-bca9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The NASA Solar Maximum Mission (SolarMax) was a space mission launched to study solar flares and other phenomena using gamma-ray observations. It operated from 1980 to 1989, providing valuable data on the Sun's activities during its maximum phase of the solar cycle.
0eb6b338-bca9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: gamma-ray Solar Maximum Mission part of NASA Solar Maximum Mission

0ebdfc92-b948-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 0.6-m telescope is a 0.6 meter aperture telescope located at the Modra Astronomical and Geophysical Observatory in Modra, Slovakia, situated at coordinates 48.373273, 17.274021.
0ebdfc92-b948-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.6m Telescope at Modra Astronomical and Geophysical Observatory, Slovakia

0ec7a26a-b5ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Stanford Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS GBO Network, used for measuring magnetic fields.
0ec7a26a-b5ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Stanford Geophysical Observatory

0ed398fe-b6a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Chittagong (CHT) that is part of the WDC Kyoto observatory network and adheres to IAGA standards for magnetic field measurements.
0ed398fe-b6a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy

0ed66de4-bb65-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Spacewatch Drift Scan Camera is an astronomical instrument operated by the University of Arizona's Lunar and Planetary Laboratory as part of the Spacewatch Project. It is used to detect, track, and study small bodies in the solar system, particularly near-Earth objects (NEOs), asteroids, and comets.
0ed66de4-bb65-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.9m Spacewatch Drift Scan Camera at Kitt Peak Observatory

0ed6b8e2-b658-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Low Frequency Atmospheric Weather Electromagnetic System for Observation, Modeling, and Education (LF AWESOME) is a high-sensitivity radio receiver designed to capture electromagnetic signals in the 0.5-470 kHz frequency range, used for studying natural lightning emissions, transmitting beacons, and radio emissions from near-Earth space environments with improved sensitivity and timing accuracy compared to its predecessor, VLF AWESOME.
0ed6b8e2-b658-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low Frequency Atmospheric Weather Electromagnetic System for Observation, Modeling, and Education part of AWESOME Observatory

0ed76a82-b9e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Northwest Indiana Robotic Telescope is an astronomical observatory located in Cedar Creek Township, Lake County, Indiana. It operates as a ground-based observatory primarily used for robotic telescopic observations and studies of the night sky.
0ed76a82-b9e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Northwest Indiana Robotic Telescope at Lowell Observatory, United States

0ee1b2e4-b656-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Weipa Station is a ground-based magnetometer network facility located in Weipa, Australia, specifically at Tavern Road, Mission River, Napranum Aboriginal Shire, Queensland. It operates as part of the IUGONET Observatory and includes a fluxgate instrument for magnetic field measurements.
0ee1b2e4-b656-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at CPMN Weipa Station, Australia

0ee30bc8-b776-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The HISCALE Low-Energy Foil Spectrometer (LEFS) for Ulysses is an instrument designed to measure low-energy electron and ion fluxes with high sensitivity through pulse-height analysis and active anticoincidence, providing nearly complete 4π coverage during spins. It consists of silicon detectors and aluminized parylene foils to differentiate between particle types and energy ranges.
0ee30bc8-b776-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low-Energy Foil Spectrometer on Ulysses

0eea6e3e-b7e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the station with IAGA identifier "RAC," used for magnetic field measurements.
0eea6e3e-b7e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Raciborg Observatory

0eee93a0-b94f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **OCA–DLR Asteroid Survey (ODAS)** was an astronomical survey conducted in the late 1990s to search for small Solar System bodies, particularly near-Earth objects. It was a collaboration between the French Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur (OCA) and the German Aerospace Center (DLR), resulting in the discovery of one comet and over 1000 minor planets from 1996 to 1999.
0eee93a0-b94f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: OCA–DLR Asteroid Survey part of Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur and German Aerospace Center, France

0ef15858-b75e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Maria Mitchell Observatory in Nantucket, Massachusetts, USA, is an astronomical observatory founded in 1908 to honor Maria Mitchell, the first American woman astronomer. It consists of two sites and houses a valuable collection of photographic plates documenting sky observations from 1913 to 1995.
0ef15858-b75e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Maria Mitchell Observatory and Loines Observatory at Maria Mitchell Association, United States

0ef16452-b708-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sudbury Neutrino Observatory (SNO) was an underground neutrino detector located in Creighton Mine, Ontario, Canada, designed to detect solar neutrinos using a large tank of heavy water.
0ef16452-b708-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutrino Detector at Sudbury Neutrino Observatory, Canada

0ef4a046-b851-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 16 Command and Service Module (CSM) was a spacecraft used during the Apollo 16 mission in April 1972, which involved sending astronauts to walk on the lunar surface while the CSM remained in orbit. It housed the crew and essential systems for the journey to the Moon and back to Earth.
0ef4a046-b851-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Command and Service Module part of Apollo 16

0ef748b2-bb8c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Royal Observatory of Madrid is a historic ground-based observatory located in Madrid, Spain, founded in 1790, which serves as the headquarters for the Spanish National Observatory and conducts research in geophysics.
0ef748b2-bb8c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Deep Space Network Radio Astronomy Antenna at Royal Observatory of Madrid, Spain

0efd9070-bbad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Anderson Mesa Station is an astronomical observatory in Coconino County, Arizona, established in 1959 as a dark-sky site for Lowell Observatory. It is located about 12 miles southeast of Flagstaff on Mars Hill.
0efd9070-bbad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Anderson Mesa Station at Lowell Observatory, United States

0f017896-baab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **St. Petersburg University 16 inch Meade LX-200 telescope** is an optical telescope located in Europe, with a 41cm (16 inch) aperture, used for astronomical observations and research.
0f017896-baab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.41m Telescope

0f10b3d8-bbd7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located on Popov Island, Russia, specifically a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate instrument, part of the IUGONET observatory network.
0f10b3d8-bbd7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of Circum Pan Pacific Magnetic Network Investigation

0f12d67a-b5e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **HNRAO Terminated Folded Dipole and FSX-8S spectrograph system** is a ground-based radio astronomy instrument at the Hawk's Nest Radio Astronomy Observatory, featuring a 4-element square array aligned to true north and capable of simultaneous right circular polarization (RCP) and left circular polarization (LCP) measurements in the 15-30 MHz frequency range.
0f12d67a-b5e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terminated Folded Dipole and FSX-8S Spectrograph at Hawk's Nest Radio Astronomy Observatory

0f292576-b5ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IGPP-LANL Teoloyucan Magnetometer** is a ground facility located in Teoloyucan, Mexico, that measures magnetic field variations as part of the IGP Plan LANL Observatory.
0f292576-b5ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Teoloyucan Observatory, Mexico

0f34b038-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The International Space Station's Floating Potential Measurement Unit (FPMU) is an instrument used to monitor and correct the electrical charging of the station, ensuring a safe environment for astronauts during structural modifications.
0f34b038-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Floating Potential Measurement Unit on International Space Station

0f38eb5c-bb17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electric Field Double Probe (EDP) is an instrument onboard MMS4, part of NASA's Magnetospheric Multiscale mission. It measures 3-D electric fields using a combination of spin-plane and axial double probes with high accuracy and frequency range.
0f38eb5c-bb17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electric Field Double Probe part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

0f393cd6-bbaf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Near Infrared Spectrometer (NIS) was an instrument aboard the NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft, designed to analyze the composition of asteroid (433) Eros by measuring infrared spectra.
0f393cd6-bbaf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Infrared Spectrometer on NEAR Shoemaker

0f3b9026-b8f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Vega mission was a Soviet spacecraft project that conducted a Venus swingby and a Comet Halley flyby in the mid-1980s. It consisted of two identical spacecraft, Vega 1 and Vega 2, which carried out experiments to study both celestial bodies.
0f3b9026-b8f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Venera-Halley part of Vega 1 and Vega 2
