0f4581d6-b799-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Shigaraki Middle and Upper Atmosphere (MU) Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Shiga Prefecture, Japan, dedicated to studying the Earth's middle-latitude atmosphere from the troposphere up to the ionosphere using various radar systems and other instruments.
0f4581d6-b799-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Shigaraki Middle and Upper Atmosphere Observatory, Japan

0f51190a-b6af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1B magnetometer is a three-axis instrument used to measure magnetic field components with high resolution and sensitivity. It is part of the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) project and helps identify substorm activity and ULF oscillations, essential for studying precipitation modulations on ULF timescales.
0f51190a-b6af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

0f545044-b9b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tiksi Magnetometer Station, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) network, is a ground-based observatory located in Tiksi, Sakha Republic, Russia, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity.
0f545044-b9b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tiksi Observatory, Russia

0f600cbc-bb46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2X Magnetometer (TCM2) is a three-axis magnetometer used in the BARREL project to measure magnetic field components with high resolution and identify substorm activity and ULF oscillations. It includes tilt compensation for accurate readings and data transmission capabilities to support scientific investigations.
0f600cbc-bb46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

0f621e70-b615-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Checheng Elementary School Observatory is a ground-based observatory located in Pingtung County, Taiwan, at coordinates 22.07468° N, 120.71429° E.
0f621e70-b615-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Checheng Elementary School Observatory

0f6732ec-b92c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Michigan State University Observatory (MPC ID: 766) is an astronomical observatory operated by Michigan State University in East Lansing, Michigan. It houses a Cassegrain telescope and has been actively involved in astronomical research since its commission in 1969.
0f6732ec-b92c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: East Lansing Observatory

0f6cc238-b5c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Interball-Auroral spacecraft orbit and attitude" dataset provides information on the orbital path and orientation of the Interball-Auroral spacecraft, which is part of the CNES CDPP archive.
0f6cc238-b5c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Interball-Auroral

0f6f4148-b89c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Radio JOVE is a ground-based observatory project that engages students and the public in scientific discovery by making radio observations of Jupiter, the Sun, and the Galactic Background using standardized equipment.
0f6f4148-b89c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio JOVE Observatory

0f77c368-b8ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DAWEX (Darwin Area Wave Experiment) radiosonde balloon sounding system, located at the Katherine civilian airport in Australia during Oct-Dec 2001, was used to measure vertical profiles of pressure, temperature, humidity, and horizontal wind from the troposphere to lower stratosphere up to ~30 km.
0f77c368-b8ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radiosonde Sounding System part of Darwin Area Wave Experiment

0f9a7aa4-ba0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS) 0.8m Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Observatoire de Haute-Provence in Europe, used for astronomical research.
0f9a7aa4-ba0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 0.8m Telescope at Observatoire de Haute-Provence

0fa7c99e-b772-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Baranov Geophysical Observatory, used in the THEMIS Mission GMAG since February 10, 2017.
0fa7c99e-b772-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission

0fac8da6-b6c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Silver Spring Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in White Oak, Maryland, United States, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
0fac8da6-b6c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Silver Spring Observatory, United States

0fc4ebb2-b981-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Priddis (ROTH) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Priddis, Canada, primarily equipped with a magnetometer for geophysical studies. It has been operational since October 2005 and is part of the Autumn Observatory network.
0fc4ebb2-b981-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Priddis Geophysical Observatory, Canada

0fd26ee8-b0ff-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electric Field and Waves Suite (EFW) is an instrument on the Radiation Belt Storm Probe (RBSP) spacecraft designed to measure electric fields and plasma densities in Earth's inner magnetosphere, helping understand particle acceleration, transport, and loss processes.
0fd26ee8-b0ff-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Electric Field and Waves Suite on Radiation Belt Storm Probe

0fdbbdc0-b74b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Khurana model" is a scientific instrument used in the Galileo mission to calculate various magnetic parameters of Jupiter’s magnetic field, based on Khurana's modeling framework. It is part of the CNES Observatory CDPP Archive for Galileo data and provides detailed insights into the Jovian magnetosphere.
0fdbbdc0-b74b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Jovian Magnetic Field Models part of Galileo Mission

0fec769c-b728-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Indian Space Research Organization 0.5m Telescope at Mount Abu InfraRed Observatory (MIRO) is a telescopic facility located in Asia, specifically at the Mount Abu Infrared Observatory in India, designed for optical waveband observations with an aperture of 0.5 meters.
0fec769c-b728-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Indian Space Research Organization 0.5m Optical Telescope at Mount Abu Infrared Observatory

0ff5c260-b778-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tristan Da Cunha (TDC) Geophysical Observatory** was a ground-based facility in Edinburgh of the Seven Seas on Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha, operating from 2009 to 2016, primarily for geophysical observations including magnetometry.
0ff5c260-b778-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tristan Da Cunha Geophysical Observatory

0ffcd8ec-b945-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Yap Station is a ground-based magnetometer network facility located in Yap, Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), at coordinates 9.3° N latitude and 138.5° E longitude.
0ffcd8ec-b945-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Yap Observatory

0ffe1850-b8a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bear Island geophysical observatory is a ground-based facility located in Bjørnøya Heliport, Herwighamna, Svalbard, Norway. It includes a magnetometer and is part of the IUGONET observatory network, operational since 2011.
0ffe1850-b8a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bear Island Observatory, Norway

10010dec-baa1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 38.2MHz Imaging Riometer (IRIO) at Husafell, Iceland, is a scientific instrument used to study the Earth's ionosphere, featuring an 8x8-element dipole antenna array that produces independent beams covering an area of approximately 180km x 180km at D region altitude.
10010dec-baa1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imaging Riometer part of Conjugate Observation at Iceland

1004aa72-b5ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Centre for Radio Astrophysics Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT) is a radio telescope located in Asia, specifically designed to observe astronomical objects at meter wavelengths. It is one of the largest and most sensitive instruments of its kind in the world.
1004aa72-b5ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Giant Meter-wave Radio Telescope at National Centre for Radio Astrophysics

100f62b2-b645-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, and the entry describes a specific set of magnetometers located in Helsinki (HLS) that were operational from 1845 to 1909 as part of the IAGA investigation at the WDC Kyoto observatory.
100f62b2-b645-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Helsinki Observatory

101886a8-badc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Katuura Observatory was a ground-based facility in Katsuura, Wakayama Prefecture, Japan, operational from 1946 to 1953, focused on magnetometer observations as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
101886a8-badc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Katsuura Observatory, Japan

1037a1be-b7c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at HER is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed at Hermanus, South Africa, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
1037a1be-b7c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observatory Network, South Africa

10389af4-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Boambee Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Boambee East, New South Wales, Australia. It serves as a ground-based observatory for celestial observations and research.
10389af4-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Boambee Observatory, Australia

103c3428-bbbc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Electric Field and Waves (EFW)** instrument on Cluster-2 is a sophisticated device designed to measure electric fields and waves in space using four orthogonal spherical sensors deployed from 50 m cable booms, capable of providing high-resolution data across various frequency ranges.
103c3428-bbbc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electric Field and Waves on Cluster-2 part of CNES Observatory CDPP Archive

103e1e4c-b67a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Astronomical League Alpha Observatory**, located in Arizona Sky Village, Cochise County, Arizona, is a ground-based astronomical observatory known for its contributions to stargazing and research.
103e1e4c-b67a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical League Alpha Observatory, United States

104525d8-bc0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Slooh.com Canary Islands Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Teide National Park on the island of Tenerife, Spain, part of the Slooh.com network for remote astronomy.
104525d8-bc0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Canary Islands Observatory, Spain

10559d7c-bae6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Volkssternwarte Urania Jena is an observatory located in Jena, Thuringia, Germany, primarily functioning as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
10559d7c-bae6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Urania Observatory at Volkssternwarte Urania Jena, Germany

1055b0de-b701-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Lunar Polar Hydrogen Mapper (LunaH-Map) is a CubeSat designed to investigate the presence of water-ice on the Moon, launched as part of NASA's Artemis 1 mission in November 2022.
1055b0de-b701-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Polar Hydrogen Mapper part of NASA's SIMPLEx program

105f81ec-bad3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Salvia Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Saulges, Mayenne, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
105f81ec-bad3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Salvia Observatory, France

1062cd24-ba2f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Salluit (SALU) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in the Qikiqtaaluk Region, Nunavut, Canada, dedicated to geophysical research and equipped with instruments such as a magnetometer.
1062cd24-ba2f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Salluit Geophysical Observatory, Canada

1068a118-b70a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Kinguafjord is a ground-based observatory located in the Qikiqtaaluk Region, Nunavut, Canada. It has been operational since 1883 and includes a magnetometer instrument for geomagnetic measurements.
1068a118-b70a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kinguafjord Observatory, Canada

1068ab60-b78f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Seddin Geomagnetic Observatory (SED), located in Germany, was a ground-based facility operating from 1907 to 1931 that conducted geomagnetic measurements, including the use of magnetometers.
1068ab60-b78f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Seddin Geomagnetic Observatory, Germany

106a7082-ba7b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Kanzelhöhe Observatory:** A ground-based optical observatory located in Europe, specifically at Kanzelhöhe, dedicated to solar and environmental research.
106a7082-ba7b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Kanzelhohe Observatory for Solar and Environmental Research

107da20e-bb18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Geotail is an instrument used in the investigation of various magnetospheric analytical models, and it is part of the CNES Observatory CDPP AMDA Geotail.
107da20e-bb18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Different Magnetospheric Analytical Models part of Geotail

1087d440-ba14-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plomer Observatory (also known as Obs. Astronomico Plomer) is an astronomical observatory located in Buenos Aires, Argentina. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
1087d440-ba14-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Astronómico Plomer, Argentina

108a5168-bb34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2Q Ephemeris** is a virtual instrument that provides trajectory positions for the BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) mission in various coordinate systems.
108a5168-bb34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses part of BARREL Observatory

108b85b4-b68f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Washington 0.75m Telescope is located at the Manastash Ridge Observatory in North America and operates in the optical waveband.
108b85b4-b68f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.75m Telescope at Manastash Ridge Observatory

108ecc28-b8b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Panagjurishte geophysical observatory in Bulgaria, operational since 1964 and part of the IAGA network.
108ecc28-b8b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Panagjurishte Observatory

1091e212-b9cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Rutherford Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at Columbia University in New York City. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and education.
1091e212-b9cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rutherford Observatory

10984fbe-b9e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Pebek Geomagnetic Observatory (PBK)** is a ground-based facility in Pevek urban district, Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, Russia, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements and sponsored by Russia. It includes a magnetometer as part of its instrumentation and has been operational since 2001.
10984fbe-b9e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pebek Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

10a74466-bad1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMCCD station at Gakona, Alaska is a ground-based facility developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research (ISEE) at Nagoya University to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions. This observatory collaborates with the Institute of Cosmophysical Research and Aeronomy and operates within Alaska's Unorganized Borough.
10a74466-bad1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: EMCCD Camera at Gakona Station, United States

10b452fc-b773-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** DSS-56 is a 34-meter radio telescope operated by NASA's Deep Space Network, located near Madrid, Spain. It features an advanced beam waveguide design for enhanced signal transmission and reception.
10b452fc-b773-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Deep Space Station 56 Radio Telescope at Madrid Observatory, Spain

10b73ec4-b672-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Utsunomiya Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Utsunomiya, Tochigi Prefecture, Japan. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
10b73ec4-b672-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Utsunomiya Observatory, Japan

10be8cbc-b8e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kharasavey Geomagnetic Observatory (KHS) is a ground-based facility in Russia, located in Yamalsky Rayon, Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug. It operated from 1974 to 1980 and was part of the IUGONET network, contributing to geomagnetic data collection.
10be8cbc-b8e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kharasavey Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

10bf3c5a-b901-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The "RBSP B Positions" refers to the ephemeris data for the Radiation Belt Storm Probes (RBSP) spacecraft B, providing its positions in various coordinate systems.
10bf3c5a-b901-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris on RBSP B Spacecraft

10c9a92e-bb3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **Magnetometer** is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Helios Magnetometers, specifically E2 and E3, are part of the Helios spacecraft missions designed to study interplanetary magnetic fields, with E2 being a three-component vector magnetometer and E3 utilizing a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer.
10c9a92e-bb3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Helios Mission

10d3ef4a-ba11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fort McMurray Geomagnetic Observatory (FMM) is a ground facility located in Abasand, Alberta, Canada, operational since 1973, and focuses on geomagnetic measurements.
10d3ef4a-ba11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fort McMurray Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

10dc2b62-b695-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The pLIBS Z-300 is a portable, hand-held laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) instrument manufactured by SciAps, designed to collect spectral data under ambient conditions.
10dc2b62-b695-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: pLIBS Z-300

10df5bb4-bbd8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LLRI (Lunar Laser Ranging Instrument) is a pulsed laser instrument on the Chandrayaan-1 Orbiter designed for detailed study of the moon's surface topography.
10df5bb4-bbd8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Laser Ranging Instrument on Chandrayaan-1 Orbiter

10efb522-bbab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Onagawa station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Onagawa, Japan, part of the CPMN magnetometer network. It operates at coordinates 38.43° N, 141.47° E and is situated in Miyagi Prefecture on Honshu Island.
10efb522-bbab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at CPMN Onagawa Station, Japan

10f10e90-ba52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Petsamo Geomagnetic Observatory (PTS), located in Murmansk Oblast, Russia, is a ground-based facility established in 1933 for monitoring geomagnetic activities on Earth's surface.
10f10e90-ba52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Petsamo Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

10f7d256-b7fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
"Swift" is a spacecraft designed for the observation and study of gamma-ray bursts, facilitating rapid response to these high-energy cosmic events.
10f7d256-b7fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory

1100f6f0-b7e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS On Board Moments (MOM) system is part of the Instrument Data Processing Unit on the THEMIS-A spacecraft, designed to calculate electron and ion moments such as number density, flux, velocity, pressure, and temperature using data from ESA and SST instruments.
1100f6f0-b7e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: On Board Moments system part of THEMIS

11119ac0-b7b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Tokyo-Okayama Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Asakuchi, Okayama Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation of celestial bodies and phenomena.
11119ac0-b7b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Asakuchi Observatory, Japan

11181fe0-ba42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Ouna (VRAD Subsatellite)**: A small space probe deployed as part of Japan's Kaguya lunar mission in 2007, designed for Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) to enable differential observations from the ground.
11181fe0-ba42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Long Baseline Interferometry Radio Antenna on Ouna part of Kaguya

1123be60-bbb7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory (SAO) 1.2m Telescope at Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory (FLWO) is an optical telescope located in North America, specifically at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory, with a primary mirror diameter of 1.2 meters.
1123be60-bbb7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 1.2m Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory Telescope at Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory

112b88d2-b682-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **COMU Ulupinar Observatory** is an astronomical facility equipped with a 1.22m T122 telescope, located at Canakkale Onsekiz Mart University in Turkey.
112b88d2-b682-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.22m Telescope at Ulupinar Observatory

112bd1d6-b9b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity (MER 1) Moessbauer Spectrometer is an instrument designed to study the mineral composition of Martian rocks and soil by measuring gamma ray interactions with iron-bearing minerals, contributing significantly to understanding Mars' geological history.
112bd1d6-b9b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Moessbauer Spectrometer on Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity

112c8366-b643-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Magnetometers at Antipolo (ANO) were operational from January 1, 1910, to December 31, 1940, as part of the IAGA investigation at the WDC Kyoto observatory.
112c8366-b643-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Antipolo Observatory

112cc534-bbbf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tres Cantos Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Tres Cantos, Community of Madrid, Spain, operating as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
112cc534-bbbf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tres Cantos Observatory, Spain

1132a536-b768-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Warner and Swasey Nassau Station is an astronomical observatory located in Montville Township, Geauga County, Ohio, United States. It is designated as a ground-based facility used for conducting astronomical observations.
1132a536-b768-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Warner and Swasey Observatory at Chardon, United States

1139c8c0-b6b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: DSS 13 is a research and development antenna located at the Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex in North America. It operates as part of NASA's Deep Space Network for radio astronomy observations.
1139c8c0-b6b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Research and Development Antenna on Goldstone Complex

113f667c-b812-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sapporo Science Center is a science museum located in Atsubetsu Ward, Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan. It opened on October 4, 1981 and serves as both an educational facility and a ground-based observatory.
113f667c-b812-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sapporo Science Center

116291ee-b8dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISEE Magnetometer Istok (near Norilsk) station is a ground-based facility located in Dudinka, Russia. It operates as part of the International Ultraviolet Explorer Network (IUGONET) and specializes in magnetometry, particularly induction measurements at a latitude of 70.03° N and longitude of 88.01° E.
116291ee-b8dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Istok Observatory, Russia

1163a556-b622-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The MAGDAS observation network includes a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed at Cebu, Philippines, which is part of the IUGONET observatory infrastructure.
1163a556-b622-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System observation network

116ce284-b5f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Saint-Caprais Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Rabastens, France, known for its ground-based observations and designated by the Minor Planet Center with ID A04.
116ce284-b5f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Saint-Caprais Observatory, France

118504ee-baaf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Leiden Observatory is an astronomical institute of Leiden University in the Netherlands, established in 1633 and recognized as the oldest operating university observatory globally.
118504ee-baaf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Leiden Observatory, Netherlands

11855236-b808-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The International Service of Geomagnetic Indices (ISGI) is a ground facility responsible for creating and distributing geomagnetic indices and records of notable magnetic events, drawing on data from global magnetic observatories.
11855236-b808-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: International Service of Geomagnetic Indices

11896402-b5f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) Fabry-Perot Interferometer at Darwin, Australia is an instrument designed to measure thermospheric neutral wind through airglow emissions at 630.0 nm wavelengths, developed by Nagoya University to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere.
11896402-b5f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fabry-Perot Interferometer part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers

11918c92-b969-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Catalina Sky Survey 0.7-m Schmidt telescope** is a survey telescope with a 0.7-meter aperture, located on Mount Bigelow in Arizona, used for astronomical observations and research.
11918c92-b969-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.7m Schmidt Telescope on Mount Bigelow, United States

1194b87e-bc8c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The San Fernando Geomagnetic Observatory (SFS), located in Spain, is a ground-based facility that has been operational since 1957 and focuses on geomagnetic measurements.
1194b87e-bc8c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: San Fernando Geomagnetic Observatory, Spain

119ebe56-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fast Plasma Investigation (FPI) on the MMS3 spacecraft is an instrument that combines data from multiple spectrometers to measure the velocity-space distribution of electrons and ions with high time resolution. It includes four dual electron spectrometers (DES) and four dual ion spectrometers (DIS), providing detailed plasma measurements in the energy range from 10 eV to 30 keV.
119ebe56-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Fast Plasma Investigation on MMS

11a137de-b6c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Quinns Rock Observatory**, also known as the Gingin Observatory, is an astronomical observatory located in Jindalee, Western Australia. It operates as a ground-based facility for stargazing and astronomical research.
11a137de-b6c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gingin Observatory, Australia

11a4d76c-bb89-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fort St. John Geophysical Observatory, located in Canada, is a ground-based facility that includes a magnetometer for geophysical measurements, starting its operations on July 24, 1991.
11a4d76c-bb89-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fort St. John Geophysical Observatory, Canada

11aaf22c-b676-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 3.05-m Shane reflector is a telescope with a 3.05-meter aperture located at Lick Observatory in California, operational since 1959.
11aaf22c-b676-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.05m Shane Reflector at Lick Observatory, United States

11bcabc2-b8b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Kuyper observatory (KUY), operated from 1929 to 1962 as part of the IAGA investigation, used for measuring magnetic fields.
11bcabc2-b8b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy

11bcad6c-b79a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 210MM Adelaide station is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in MacDonald Park, Adelaide, South Australia, which operates as part of the ISEE Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network.
11bcad6c-b79a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Adelaide Observatory, Australia

11c45708-b608-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pitlekaya Magnetometer is an instrument located at the station with the IAGA identifier PTL, used to measure and record the Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since January 1, 1879.
11c45708-b608-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pitlekaya Observatory

11cc443c-bb39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Toledo 1m (42inch) Telescope at Ritter Observatory is an optical telescope with a 1.0-meter aperture, located in North America and part of the Ritter Observatory facilities.
11cc443c-bb39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.0m Optical Telescope at Ritter Observatory

11d14e50-b607-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Teheran Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Tehran, Iran, primarily known for its magnetometer instrument used to study geomagnetic fields. It has been operational since January 1, 1960.
11d14e50-b607-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tehran Observatory, Iran

11d26ed8-b6d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Nishi Kobe Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Nishi Ward, Kobe, Japan. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
11d26ed8-b6d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nishi Kobe Observatory, Japan

11e473ce-ba33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer situated at the IAGA-identified station ZHONG SHAN (alternatively known as ZHS), used for measuring magnetic fields.
11e473ce-ba33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Zhong Shan Observatory

11e4d7d8-b5e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at FYM** is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed in Fayum, Egypt. It is part of the MAGDAS observation network and provides magnetic field measurements for scientific research.
11e4d7d8-b5e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System observation network

11ebc156-b830-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Global Surveyor (MGS) Spacecraft Magnetometer (MAG) was an instrument designed to measure the magnetic field of Mars, providing data on localized magnetic anomalies and offering insights into the planet's geological history.
11ebc156-b830-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer on Mars Global Surveyor Spacecraft

11f32f6c-b930-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Aloushta station with the IAGA identifier ALU, operational from January 1957 to December 1961.
11f32f6c-b930-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Aloushta Observatory

11f4c186-bb80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "UARS Positions" dataset provides the spatial coordinates of the Upper Atmosphere Research Satellite (UARS) in different reference frames, supporting scientific investigations related to its orbital trajectory and mission data.
11f4c186-bb80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris on Upper Atmosphere Research Satellite

11fce46a-bac7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cerro Tololo-LCO Aqawan B #1 is an astronomical observatory located in the Gabriela Mistral International Dark Skies Sanctuary, Vicuña, Chile. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
11fce46a-bac7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Aqawan B #1 Observatory, Chile

120ee3e2-ba20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sydney Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field, located at the IAGA station in Sydney. It has been operational since January 1, 1892, and is part of the ASWS observatory ground facility in Camden.
120ee3e2-ba20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Camden Observatory

120fe61c-b6d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Hagen Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Ronkhausen, Germany. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
120fe61c-b6d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hagen Observatory, Germany

12143cfa-bb67-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1H Data Processing Unit (DPU)** is an instrument controller board designed for the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) project. It acquires data from various sensors, processes it, and transmits formatted data frames via an Iridium modem while also controlling the command-cutdown system.
12143cfa-bb67-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

1216b910-b11e-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AMPTE-CCE (Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers - Charge Composition Explorer) was a NASA satellite launched in 1984 as part of the Explorer program to study solar wind ion access to Earth's magnetosphere and magnetospheric particle transport and energization.
1216b910-b11e-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Charge Composition Explorer part of Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers

121b18e4-ba78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dust Impact Mass Analyzer (PUMA) for Vega 2 is a time-of-flight spectrometer aboard the Vega 2 spacecraft, designed to measure the size and spatial density of solid particles and determine specific isotopic ratios.
121b18e4-ba78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dust Impact Mass Analyzer on Vega 2

12400134-b791-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The CPMN Bac Lieu Station is a ground-based magnetometer observatory located in Bac Lieu, Vietnam, operating as part of the CPMN network to monitor geomagnetic activity.
12400134-b791-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bac Lieu Observatory, Vietnam

12403246-bab9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **DSS 13 (Deep Space Station 13)** is a radio telescope test facility located at the Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex in Fort Irwin, California. It has an aperture of 34 meters and is part of NASA's network for communicating with deep space missions.
12403246-bab9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34.0m Radio Telescope at Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex, United States

12407296-ba24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mount Bigelow Observatory, specifically the Catalina Station, is a ground-based observatory located at Mount Bigelow in Arizona. It features a 1.54-meter telescope used for astronomical research and observations.
12407296-ba24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.54m Telescope at Mount Bigelow Observatory

12498496-b70c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Viking Lander 1 Atmospheric Structure** experiment utilized various instruments to gather data on Martian atmospheric pressure and temperature profiles during the lander's descent, enabling calculations of atmospheric density and mean atomic mass below an altitude of 132 km.
12498496-b70c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Viking Lander 1 Atmospheric Structure part of Viking Lander

124a8fd6-b8b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fredericksburg Magnetic Observatory (FRD), located in Caroline County, Virginia, U.S.A., is a ground-based facility that operates magnetic field measurement instruments and has been active since 1956.
124a8fd6-b8b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fredericksburg Magnetic Observatory

124aa94a-b7a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Colorado Student Space Weather Experiment (CSSWE) is a 3U CubeSat funded by the National Science Foundation, designed to measure the directional differential flux of Solar Energetic Protons and Earth's radiation belt electrons. It was developed by students at the University of Colorado at Boulder and launched in 2012 aboard an Atlas V 401 rocket from Vandenberg AFB.
124aa94a-b7a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Telescope on Colorado Student Space Weather Experiment

124d946a-b9e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SBIG ST-8 is an astronomical CCD camera used for imaging celestial objects, known for its high sensitivity and resolution. It was part of the instrumentation at Palmer Divide's old 10-inch telescope setup.
124d946a-b9e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SBIG ST-8

1261e202-b59f-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Dilbert Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Forest Grove, Oregon, United States. It is designated with the MPC code G57 and known for its ground-based observations.
1261e202-b59f-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Forest Grove Observatory

1278e526-b6f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **OGO6 Positions** dataset provides the locations of the OGO6 spacecraft in different coordinate systems. It is part of the observations made by the OGO6 observatory and can also be referred to as OGO6 Ephemeris.
1278e526-b6f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Investigation part of OGO 6

12795740-bad9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The JMA Magnetometer at Kakioka Observatory consists of variometers (torsion magnetometers for H, D, and Z components) and absolute instruments such as a vector proton precession magnetometer and standard magnetometer for precise geomagnetic field measurements.
12795740-bad9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at World Data Center for Geomagnetism Observatory

1280f23c-b9fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Milagrito Telescope is a gamma-ray telescope located in North America and is part of the Milagro TeV All-Sky Gamma Ray Observatory. It operates within the gamma-ray waveband to observe high-energy astrophysical phenomena.
1280f23c-b9fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: gamma ray Milagrito Telescope at Milagro TeV All-Sky Gamma Ray Observatory

128579be-b7e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Hawkeye Positions" refers to the precise location data of the Hawkeye spacecraft within different coordinate systems, essential for tracking and navigating the spacecraft during its missions.
128579be-b7e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hawkeye Positions on Hawkeye Spacecraft

128b4de2-b7d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Apollo 17 Lunar Module (LM) Traverse Gravimeter (TG)** was a battery-powered lunar gravimeter used to survey the Moon's gravitational field and obtain geological substructure information during the Apollo 17 mission.
128b4de2-b7d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Traverse Gravimeter part of Apollo 17

12924624-b719-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Cheltenham Geomagnetic Observatory (CLH), located in Maryland, USA, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1901 to 1956, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
12924624-b719-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cheltenham Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

12958d3e-b8c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The ELF/VLF Receivers on Hawkeye 1 were instruments on the Hawkeye spacecraft designed to measure electric and magnetic fields using a 42.45-meter electric dipole antenna and a search coil antenna, covering frequencies from 1.78 Hz to 178 kHz for electric fields and 1.78 Hz to 5.62 kHz for magnetic fields with various sensitivities and dynamic ranges.
12958d3e-b8c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Magnetometer and Electric Antenna on Hawkeye 1

129cde7e-b929-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mendel Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Merrimack College in North Andover, Massachusetts, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and education.
129cde7e-b929-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mendel Observatory

12a34c0c-bb3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: MAGDAS Camden Station is a ground-based facility located in Grasmere, Sydney, Australia, part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network that monitors magnetic field variations. It is situated at coordinates -34.06 latitude and 150.67 longitude within the continent of Oceania.
12a34c0c-bb3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Camden Observatory, Australia

12a6f346-bb0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Lwiro Geophysical Observatory was a ground-based facility located in the Democratic Republic of Congo that operated from 1958 to 1965, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
12a6f346-bb0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lwiro Geomagnetic Observatory, Democratic Republic of the Congo

12a7184e-b8f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Galileo Plasma Wave Receiver is an advanced instrument onboard the Galileo spacecraft designed to study plasma waves and radio emissions within Jupiter's magnetosphere. It builds upon Voyager mission findings, offering comprehensive measurements of electric and magnetic fields with high resolution to explore regions like the magnetotail, plasma sheet, and interactions with Io’s volcanic activity.
12a7184e-b8f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Wave Receiver for Galileo Orbiter on Galileo

12a88182-bb24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: Les Barres Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Lamanon, France. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to studying the cosmos.
12a88182-bb24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Les Barres Observatory, France

12ab9b36-b784-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vienna Observatory (before 1879) is an astronomical observatory that was located at Georg-Coch-Platz in Vienna, Austria. It operated as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research before being relocated or closed after 1879.
12ab9b36-b784-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vienna Observatory, Austria

12b2bbe6-b6fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Ardore Marina Observatory, also known as "La Macchina del Tempo," is a ground-based observatory located in Ardore Marina, Reggio Calabria, Italy. It is situated at coordinates 38.16987° N, 16.2005° E on the European continent.
12b2bbe6-b6fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: La Macchina del Tempo at Ardore Marina Observatory, Italy

12c0a9ca-b6ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The one located in Abisko has been operational since 1921 as part of the IAGA investigation within the IUGONET observatory network.
12c0a9ca-b6ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Abisko Observatory

12cd4814-ba8e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Maputo Station is a ground-based facility located in Maputo, Mozambique, that operates as part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network to monitor geomagnetic activity on Earth's surface.
12cd4814-ba8e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Maputo Observatory, Mozambique

12cd5844-bada-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2.5m Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Telescope is located at the Apache Point Observatory in North America and specializes in optical astronomy with a 2.5-meter aperture.
12cd5844-bada-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.5m optical Sloan Digital Sky Survey Telescope at Apache Point Observatory

12d0df04-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Liverpool Observatory, established in 1867, is an astronomical facility located at 137 Brownlow Hill in Liverpool, England. It serves as a ground-based observatory for studying celestial bodies and phenomena from Earth.
12d0df04-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Liverpool Observatory, United Kingdom

12e133ac-b59c-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ahmedabad Geomagnetic Observatory (AHM) is a ground-based facility in Ahmedabad, India, established in 1973 to monitor geomagnetic activities.
12e133ac-b59c-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ahmedabad Geomagnetic Observatory, India

12ec2cd4-bbce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 210MM Macquarie Isl. station is a ground-based magnetic observatory located at Market Square, Huon Valley, Tasmania, Australia. It is part of the ISEE/MM210 magnetometer network and includes a fluxgate instrument for measuring magnetic fields.
12ec2cd4-bbce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Macquarie Island Observatory, Australia

12ef96be-b6a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Clinton Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Windbrook, Prince George's County, Maryland, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
12ef96be-b6a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Clinton Observatory, United States

12f4996e-b633-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Proton Telescope** on CRRES (Combined Release and Radiation Effects Satellite) is an instrument designed to measure protons in the energy range of 1 to 100 MeV. It consists of two sensor units—one for low-energy (1 - 9 MeV) and one for high-energy (6 - 100 MeV) measurements—and a data processing unit, capable of obtaining the entire energy spectrum each second.
12f4996e-b633-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument on CRRES

1306aaf6-b817-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ford Observatory, Wrightwood is a ground-based observatory located in Big Pines, California, USA. It is situated at coordinates 34.38219 latitude and -117.66395 longitude (converted from 242.33605).
1306aaf6-b817-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ford Observatory, Wrightwood

130f5f3e-bb05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LBT Consortium Large Binocular Telescope (LBT) is an optical telescope located at the Mount Graham International Observatory in North America. It is designed for high-resolution astronomical observations and operates within the visible light spectrum.
130f5f3e-bb05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Large Binocular Telescope at Mount Graham International Observatory

130fe8f6-bb90-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Escudero (ESC) Geomagnetic Observatory** is a ground facility located on Earth's surface, specifically at coordinates latitude -62.18 and longitude -58.92, primarily focused on geomagnetic measurements starting from 2004-01-01.
130fe8f6-bb90-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Escudero Observatory, Antarctica

131498f4-b8c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Deep Space Program Science Experiment (DSPSE), also known as Clementine, was a joint mission by the Ballistic Missile Defense Organization and NASA launched in 1994. It aimed to demonstrate lightweight technologies for future spacecraft and conduct systematic lunar mapping, though a software error led to its premature end before it could flyby asteroid Geographos.
131498f4-b8c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep Space Program Science Experiment part of Clementine

131e7dca-bb6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Norderstedt Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Norderstedt, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany. It is a ground-based facility situated at Breslauer Straße and is identified by the Minor Planet Center with the code 606.
131e7dca-bb6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sternwarte Norderstedt Observatory, Germany

13219ff2-b6b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Radio Science Investigation (RSI) on the Rosetta spacecraft utilized both onboard and ground-based instrumentation, including an ultra stable oscillator, to perform scientific studies using S-band and X-band telecommunications frequencies.
13219ff2-b6b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Investigation part of Rosetta

132a9cf2-ba30-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Italian Space Agency (ASI) Astro-rivelatore Gamma a Immagini LEggero (AGILE) satellite mission is a space-based gamma-ray observatory designed to study high-energy astrophysical phenomena. It operates in the gamma-ray waveband and aims to provide detailed images of cosmic gamma-ray sources.
132a9cf2-ba30-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: gamma-ray Italian Space Agency Astro-rivelatore Gamma a Immagini Leggero Satellite Mission

13346c2c-b9ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Huelva Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Huelva, Andalusia, Spain, used for ground-based observations of celestial objects.
13346c2c-b9ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Huelva Observatory, Spain

1338ca50-b613-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Skalnaté pleso Observatory is an astronomical and meteorological observatory located in the Tatra Mountains of Slovakia at an altitude of 1,786 meters. It is situated near a mountain lake called Skalnaté pleso and has been operational since 1943.
1338ca50-b613-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Skalnaté pleso Observatory, Slovakia

1339d282-b754-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Chula Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at 60 McGinty Drive in Tift County, Georgia, USA. It is a ground-based facility used for observing celestial objects.
1339d282-b754-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chula Observatory, United States

13457bf8-b6ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Pathfinder was a NASA mission that sent a lander and rover to the surface of Mars in 1997. The mission aimed to demonstrate innovative technologies for landing on Mars and conducting scientific investigations, including atmospheric entry techniques, airbag-mediated touchdown, and automated data collection from the Martian surface.
13457bf8-b6ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Instrument Host Overview - Spacecraft part of Mars Pathfinder

135be300-b9c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ISEE-3 Radio Receiver** was an instrument on the International Sun-Earth Explorer spacecraft, designed to detect and map Type III solar radio bursts at frequencies between 30 kHz and 2 MHz using two dipole antennas. It operated from August 1978 through the spacecraft's encounter with comet Giacobini-Zinner in September 1985, providing high-resolution data on solar wind disturbances.
135be300-b9c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Antenna part of International Sun-Earth Explorer Mission

135f6e7a-b5e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Equatorial Atmosphere Observatory at Kototabang is a ground-based research facility situated near the equator in West Sumatra, Indonesia. It houses various instruments to study atmospheric layers from the troposphere to the ionosphere.
135f6e7a-b5e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Equatorial Atmosphere Observatory, Indonesia

13644e4a-bab5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **FF051 Fairford, UK**: An advanced ionospheric research station located in Fairford, United Kingdom, equipped with a Digisonde to study various properties of signals reflected from the ionosphere.
13644e4a-bab5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Station at Fairford Observatory, United Kingdom

13672c54-ba07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Space Environment Monitor (SEM)** on GOES 6 is an instrument subsystem designed to measure in real-time the impact of solar activity on the near-Earth electromagnetic environment. It consists of four instruments: Energetic Particle Sensor, High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector, Solar X-Ray Sensor, and Magnetic Field Sensor, providing crucial data for space weather reports that support communication, navigation, power transmission systems, and satellites.
13672c54-ba07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Chamber part of Space Environment Monitor on GOES 6

13687f18-ba0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wayne State University's 20-inch Dan Zowada Memorial Observatory is a telescope facility located in North America with an optical waveband and an aperture of 0.51 meters, dedicated to astronomical observations.
13687f18-ba0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.51m Dan Zowada Memorial Telescope

1368d614-b1d1-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pioneer 8 Cosmic Dust Detector (CDD) is an instrument designed to measure the cosmic-dust flux density in the solar system and determine the distribution of cosmic dust concentrations in Earth's orbit, among other objectives.
1368d614-b1d1-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Cosmic Dust Detector on Pioneer 8

13767e76-b605-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is a fluxgate magnetometer located in Wewak, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network within the IUGONET observatory. This instrument measures magnetic fields and contributes to geophysical research.
13767e76-b605-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of ISEE/MM210/WEW Investigation

1378233a-b67c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometers at Kaliningrad (KNG), part of the IUGONET observatory network, specifically monitor geomagnetic activity in that region.
1378233a-b67c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kaliningrad Observatory

137a47c8-bb54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition**:
Minamitory Shima is a ground-based observatory located in Ogasawara Subprefecture, Tokyo, Japan, part of the IAGA network. It houses a magnetometer and has been operational since January 1941.
137a47c8-bb54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Minamitori Observatory, Japan

137de9f0-ba0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mars Exploration Rover (MER) Spirit Hazard Avoidance Camera (Hazcam)** is a set of four cameras on the Mars rover Spirit used to take images and help avoid obstacles during traversal. Each camera consists of a detector head with a lens assembly and CCD, along with an electronics box containing essential components for operation in extreme conditions.
137de9f0-ba0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hazard Avoidance Camera on Mars Exploration Rover Spirit

138d25fa-b5aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Energetic Particle Experiment (EPA) aboard the Giotto spacecraft was designed to measure the energy distribution of electrons, photons, and heavier nuclei during its mission. It consisted of three particle telescopes equipped with silicon detectors and background shielding.
138d25fa-b5aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: The Energetic Particle Experiment on Giotto

138f9a02-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Harvard College Observatory (HCO) is an astronomical research institution managed by the Harvard University Department of Astronomy, located in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Founded in 1839, it is part of the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian and features notable instruments like the Harvard Great Refractor.
138f9a02-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Harvard College Observatory, United States

13903b44-ba39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Perth Ionosonde is an instrument located in Perth, WA, Australia, used for radar investigation of the ionosphere. It features an IPS 5D digital ionosonde that operates within a frequency range of 1.0 to 21.5 MHz with a resolution of 5 kHz and up to 4095 steps.
13903b44-ba39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar Ionosonde part of Perth Observatory

13929894-b692-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU Radio Beacon Receiver (GRBR) is a digital instrument installed in Shiga Prefecture, Japan, designed to measure ionospheric total electron content using LEO satellite signals. It utilizes open-source software and hardware for signal acquisition and processing.
13929894-b692-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver at Shigaraki Middle and Upper Atmosphere Observatory, Japan

1397f666-b806-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to magnetometers located at Sachs Harbour (SAH), which are part of the IUGONET Observatory and contribute data to the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto.
1397f666-b806-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observatory

1398523e-b813-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Melezhy Astrophoto Observatory (L72) is an astronomical observatory located in the Kirzhachsky District of Vladimir Oblast, Russia. It specializes in astrophotography and ground-based observations.
1398523e-b813-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Melezhy Astrophoto Observatory, Russia

13a1dd00-bbf0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Colorado Ultraviolet Transit Experiment (CUTE) is a telescope designed to observe ultraviolet light, particularly focused on studying transiting exoplanets.
13a1dd00-bbf0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ultraviolet The Colorado Ultraviolet Transit Experiment

13af144e-b933-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tashkent-1 Magnetometer** was a magnetic field measurement device operational from 1883 to 1935 at the Tashkent Observatory as part of the IAGA investigation.
13af144e-b933-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tashkent Observatory

13bad896-bb78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The California Institute of Technology 10-inch Planet Search Telescope, also known as "Sherlock," is a telescope located at the Palomar Observatory in North America with an optical waveband and aperture of 0.25 meters.
13bad896-bb78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical California Institute of Technology 10inch Planet Search Telescope, Sherlock at Palomar Observatory

13bbae1a-ba83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **THEMIS Search Coil Magnetometer (SCM)** is an instrument on the THEMIS spacecraft that measures low-frequency magnetic field fluctuations and waves in three directions, covering frequencies from 0.1 Hz to 4 kHz. It complements fluxgate magnetometers by providing high sensitivity and broad frequency coverage, essential for studying electromagnetic phenomena in space.
13bbae1a-ba83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Magnetometer on THEMIS

13c8ac74-bae1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Yale Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bethany, Connecticut, known for its ground-based facilities.
13c8ac74-bae1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yale Observatory at Bethany, United States

13c9d122-b711-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2N X-ray Instrument (XRI)** is a scintillation detector used in the BARREL mission to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It employs a NaI crystal, photomultiplier tube, and pulse height analyzer to detect and analyze X-ray energies from 10 keV to 10 MeV.
13c9d122-b711-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

13cb3a18-babc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Spitzer Space Telescope** is a NASA infrared telescope with an aperture of 0.85 meters, designed to observe the universe in infrared wavelengths.
13cb3a18-babc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Spitzer Space Telescope

13dac218-ba34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. Specifically, the SAMBA Magnetometer Array at the Escudero geomagnetic observatory employs a fluxgate magnetometer to monitor variations in Earth's magnetic field.
13dac218-ba34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer at Escudero Observatory

13e87536-bab4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** A magnetometer located at the IAGA-identified station KTS in Korets, Ukraine, operational since January 1968, used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of the global IUGONET observatory network.
13e87536-bab4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Korets Observatory

13e98642-bb63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at Novolazarevskaya (NVL) is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, operational since 1961 as part of the IAGA investigation.
13e98642-bb63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Novolazarevskaya Station, Antarctica

13fb1712-b70e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1I Ephemeris** is a virtual instrument that provides trajectory positions in various coordinate systems, facilitating the study of relativistic electron losses as part of the Radiation Belt Storm Probes mission.
13fb1712-b70e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

13ff620c-ba76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetic Field Monitor on GOES 4 is a spinning twin-fluxgate magnetometer designed to measure the orthogonal components of Earth's magnetic field with high sensitivity and resolution.
13ff620c-ba76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetic Field Monitor on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite GOES 4

140496a0-b954-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dalian Geomagnetic Observatory (DLN) was a ground-based facility in Ganjingzi, Liaoning, China, operating from 1990 to 1992 to monitor geomagnetic activity.
140496a0-b954-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dalian Geomagnetic Observatory, China

14079b92-b5a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Cygnus Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in New Alresford, Hampshire, England, dedicated to ground-based observations of the night sky.
14079b92-b5a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cygnus Observatory, United Kingdom

14089114-b5a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Gothers Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Gothers, St. Dennis, Cornwall, United Kingdom, identified by the Minor Planet Center ID J03 and Wikidata identifier Q115607519.
14089114-b5a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gothers Observatory, United Kingdom

141b2586-b91e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LCROSS Mid-Infrared Camera 2 (MIR2) was a thermal imaging instrument on the Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite, designed to capture mid-infrared images of lunar impacts and ejecta clouds. It featured an uncooled microbolometer sensor and was used to study the morphology and thermal properties of impact events.
141b2586-b91e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mid-Infrared Camera 2 on Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite

142b143c-b92d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CFDT2 Cartesian Full-Disk Telescope Number 2 on SFO is an imaging instrument located at the IUGONET Observatory, part of the World Data Center for Solar-Terrestrial Physics in Kyoto. It captures full-disk images to study solar phenomena.
142b143c-b92d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cartesian Full-Disk Telescope Number 2 on Solar Flare Observatory part of WDC Kyoto

142c880c-b19a-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ultra-Low Energy Isotope Spectrometer (ULEIS) is a mass spectrometer on the Advanced Composition Explorer (ACE) spacecraft designed to measure energetic ion fluxes, identifying ions through time-of-flight and residual kinetic energy measurements.
142c880c-b19a-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultra-Low Energy Isotope Spectrometer on Advanced Composition Explorer

14342958-b5c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wind and Temperature Spectrometer (WATS) on Dynamics Explorer 2 was an instrument designed to measure in situ neutral winds, temperatures, and concentrations of selected gases to study their interrelationships with plasma drift and electric fields in the thermosphere.
14342958-b5c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wind and Temperature Spectrometer on Dynamics Explorer 2

143e9a3a-b6d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetic Data Acquisition System (MAGDAS) observation network includes a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed at Tirunelveli, India. This instrument is part of the IUGONET observatory and is used for measuring magnetic field variations in three dimensions.
143e9a3a-b6d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System observation network

1440dbf6-b6a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite (LCROSS) Mid-Infrared Camera 1 (MIR1)** was a thermal imaging instrument designed to capture mid-infrared images of the Centaur impact on the lunar surface, monitor ejecta cloud morphology, and measure thermal properties. It featured an uncooled microbolometer sensor with a specific field of view and bandpass filter.
1440dbf6-b6a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mid-Infrared Camera 1 on Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite

145db372-b7a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, specifically Earth's magnetic field. The magnetometers at Meanook (MEA) have been operational since 1916 and are part of the IUGONET observatory network managed by WDC Kyoto.

146f6c78-b675-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Institute of Astronomy of Nicolaus Copernicus University in Torun's 32m RT4 radio telescope is a large astronomical instrument located in Europe, specifically designed for radio waveband observations.

1476210e-bab1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: SWARM-B is one of three identical satellites in the European Space Agency's Swarm mission, launched on November 22, 2013, to study Earth’s geomagnetic field and its temporal changes.

14882ec2-b92a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Moana observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Puna'auia, French Polynesia. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.

148887ba-b938-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **LightBuckets Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Pingelly Heights, East Pingelly, Western Australia. It is recognized as a ground-based observatory with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID D24 and H11.

148f5d46-b94d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Les Planes de Son Observatory, Spain

149053c2-baba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RMS Observatory (W25) is an astronomical observatory located in Cincinnati, Ohio, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
149053c2-baba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: RMS Observatory, United States

14b00e5c-b712-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Los Cerrillos (CER) Geomagnetic Observatory is a ground facility located in Ñuñoa, Santiago Metropolitan Region, Chile, that began operations on May 1, 2003. 14c1b828-ba41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mark III Stellar Interferometer at Mount Wilson Observatory is an optical telescope located in North America that utilizes interferometry to study stars with high angular resolution. 14d60198-bac3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: El Teatrillo de Lyra Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Àger, Catalonia, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to celestial observations and research.

14d66202-ba53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1T Tilt Compensated Magnetometer (TCM2)** is a three-axis magnetometer used in the BARREL mission to measure magnetic field components with high resolution and accuracy, providing crucial data for studying substorm activity and ULF oscillations.

14ddf180-b9a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The San Emigdio Peak Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Pine Mountain Club, Kern County, California. It is a ground-based facility situated at coordinates 34.857391° N, 119.18° W on the continent of North America.
14ddf180-b9a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: San Emigdio Peak Observatory, United States

14eb49fe-b681-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Vysokaya Dubrava Observatory (also known as SVD) was a ground-based facility in Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia, operational from 1929 to 1980, primarily equipped with magnetometers for geophysical observations.
14eb49fe-b681-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Vysokaya Dubrava Observatory

14eded66-b6e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Auroral Observation at Syowa Station involves a Color Digital SLR Camera equipped with a fish-eye lens, located in Syowa Station, Antarctica, for capturing auroral phenomena.
14eded66-b6e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Color Digital SLR Camera part of Auroral Observation at Syowa Station, Antarctica

14f30e30-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Remus Magnetometer** is an instrument deployed at the Remus (RMUS) Geophysical Observatory as part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation. It measures variations in the Earth's magnetic field and has been operational since August 24, 2005.
14f30e30-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Remus Geophysical Observatory

15011686-b707-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Yap Island Station is a ground facility located at Yap International Airport in the Federated States of Micronesia, part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network that monitors magnetic field variations.
15011686-b707-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at MAGDAS Yap Island station, Federated States of Micronesia

150a8f0a-b7e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Beverly-Begg Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Dunedin, New Zealand, established by the Dunedin Astronomical Society in 1922.
150a8f0a-b7e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Beverly-Begg Observatory, New Zealand

1510214e-bb53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: "The STEREO-A Ephemeris is a dataset providing the position of the STEREO A spacecraft in Heliocentric Earth Ecliptic (HEE) coordinates with a resolution of 1 minute."
1510214e-bb53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stereo-A Ephemeris on STEREO A Spacecraft

151218ac-b61f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Star Cruiser Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Riverside County, California, United States (code: 444, MPC ID: 444).
151218ac-b61f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Star Cruiser Observatory, United States

15178b5a-b680-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Breitenweg Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Herkenrath, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility primarily for astronomical research and observations.
15178b5a-b680-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Breitenweg Observatory, Germany

151d9046-b8be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Jim Carrigan Observatory, operational since January 1, 2005, measures magnetic field variations as part of the WDC_GDMC investigation.
151d9046-b8be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Jim Carrigan Observatory

151f5ec8-b8d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Shawano Magnetometer is an instrument used in the THEMIS Mission to measure magnetic fields, located at the Shawano (SWNO) Geophysical Observatory and operational since October 17, 2005.
151f5ec8-b8d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Shawano Geophysical Observatory

15212fa6-b6e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 17 Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP) was a suite of scientific instruments deployed on the lunar surface during the Apollo 17 mission to collect data on various aspects of the Moon's environment and structure. It included experiments such as a heat flow experiment, lunar surface gravimeter, lunar mass spectrometer, lunar seismic profiling experiment, and lunar ejecta and meteorites experiment, powered by a radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG).
15212fa6-b6e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Surface Experiments Package part of Apollo 17

153ba80a-bb35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AGO P6 SearchCoil Instrument is a device used for geophysical investigations, specifically located at the AGO P6 ground station. It operates as part of the ICESTAR observatory network and utilizes search coils to conduct its measurements.
153ba80a-bb35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil on Automated Geophysical Observatory 6

154086be-b9cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: BARREL Balloon 3A was a high-altitude balloon mission launched on August 10, 2015, as part of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) project. It aimed to study particles escaping from Earth's radiation belts by measuring X-rays produced by precipitating relativistic electrons in the stratosphere.
154086be-b9cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of NASA Living with a Star, Geospace Mission of Opportunity

15517594-b64f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Connection Explorer (ICON) is a NASA satellite designed to study the interaction between Earth's weather systems and space weather in the ionosphere, aiming to understand how this dynamic affects communications and GPS signals.
15517594-b64f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Connection Explorer part of NASA's Explorers Program

1555172a-bb4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Bunia Geomagnetic Observatory (BNA) was a ground-based facility located in the Democratic Republic of the Congo that operated from 1959 to 1960, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
1555172a-bb4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bunia Geomagnetic Observatory, Democratic Republic of the Congo

155cdcac-babb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Volkssternwarte Dhaun Observatory (MPC ID: 515) is an astronomical observatory located in Hochstetten-Dhaun, Germany. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
155cdcac-babb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Volkssternwarte Dhaun Observatory, Germany

155f3cba-bc7b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Purgathofer-Sternwarte** is an astronomical observatory located in Klosterneuburg, Lower Austria. It operates as a ground-based facility for celestial observations and research.
155f3cba-bc7b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Purgathofer Observatory, Austria

157b674a-bb37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF Athabasca station (AUGSO) is a ground-based observatory located in Athabasca County, Alberta, Canada, established to study very low frequency and extremely low-frequency radio waves using a crossed loop antenna.
157b674a-bb37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VLF/ELF Crossed Loop Antenna at VLF/ELF Athabasca Station, Canada

157f9652-b5d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific instance referenced here was operational from 1965-01-01 to 1989-12-31, located in Berezniaki, and associated with observations conducted at Karaganda (KGD) as part of the IAGA investigation within the iugonet-observatory network.

1587cfd4-b723-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Montana Cabreja Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Vega de San Mateo on the Canary Islands, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
1587cfd4-b723-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Montaña Cabreja Observatory, Spain

1597eafe-b79b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IBEX-Hi instrument is a single-pixel imager designed to measure Energetic Neutral Atoms (ENAs) in six energy bands ranging from 0.38 keV to 6.0 keV, with a field of view of 6.5 x 6.5 degrees, capable of imaging a swath of the sky every 15-second spacecraft spin.

159b0228-b955-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Timberline Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Madison Township, Iowa, dedicated to ground-based astronomical observations.
159b0228-b955-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Timberline Observatory

159b6750-b90e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Cambridge Observatory is an astronomical observatory at the University of Cambridge in England. Established in 1823, it now operates as part of the Institute of Astronomy and houses a notable library collection of modern and historical astronomy books.
159b6750-b90e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cambridge Observatory

15a61df6-b654-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Lake Saint Louis Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Lake St. Louis, Missouri, United States, with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 751.
15a61df6-b654-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lake Saint Louis Observatory

15a7b1ac-bbcc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The White-light All-sky Watec Imager (AWI) at Tjautjas, Sweden is an automatic optical instrument used for capturing wide-field images of the sky using a CCD camera and fisheye lens.

**Definition:**
The Pelly Bay Geomagnetic Observatory (PEB), located in the Kitikmeot Region of Nunavut, Canada, was a ground facility operating from 1993 to 2002 that conducted geomagnetic measurements using magnetometers.

15b04f7a-b8b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ruhr University Bochum and Catholic University of the North (UCN) 1.5m Hexapod Telescope is an optical telescope with a 1.5-meter aperture located at the Cerro Armazones Observatory in South America. It is operated by the Ruhr University Bochum and the Catholic University of the North (UCN).
