15c3c546-ba13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RIT Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Henrietta, New York, operated by the Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT). It serves as a ground-based facility for research and educational purposes.
15c3c546-ba13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rochester Institute of Technology Observatory

15c73bee-b6c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Ojai Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located at Thacher School in Ojai, California. It is a ground-based facility used for stargazing and astronomical research.
15c73bee-b6c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Thacher School Observatory

15c804e4-b7b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The South Pole Geomagnetic Observatory (SPA) is a ground-based facility located at the Earth's surface, specifically at the geographic South Pole. It monitors geomagnetic activity and has been operational since January 1, 2005.
15c804e4-b7b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: South Pole Geomagnetic Observatory, Antarctica

15c84f72-bb7f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a group of ground-based observatory stations known as the "Chain of ground stations in the SAMBA Array," established on December 1, 2005. This network includes various locations across Earth's surface such as Antofagasta, Los Cerrillos, Conception, and others, collectively forming part of the SAMBA observatory infrastructure.
15c84f72-bb7f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SAMBA Ground Observatory Group

15d6b414-b872-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **OACT (VSO notation)** is an imaging instrument at the Catania Astrophysical Observatory (OAC), used for solar observations. It features a H-alpha Lyot filter and a 1360 x 1200 CCD array, capable of capturing full-disk images every 60 seconds with a 150 mm refractor.
15d6b414-b872-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hydrogen-Alpha Imager on 150mm Telescope at Catania Astrophysical Observatory

15d89d08-bb81-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer station located at the Whiteshell geophysical observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG since February 1979.
15d89d08-bb81-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Whiteshell Observatory

15e83740-ba05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gahberg Observatory is a private astronomical observatory located on the Gahberg near the Attersee in Upper Austria.
15e83740-ba05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gahberg Observatory, Austria

15f38c7e-bb1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Relativistic Proton Detector (RPD) on the Combined Release and Radiation Effects Satellite (CRRES) is an instrument designed to measure energetic electrons above 200 keV and higher energy electrons and protons in trapped radiation belts, utilizing Cerenkov and solid-state silicon sensors.
15f38c7e-bb1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument on Chemical Release and Radiation Effects Satellite

15ffa4fa-b980-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Mars Observer**: A NASA space probe launched in 1992 to study Mars' surface, atmosphere, climate, and magnetic field. Communication with the spacecraft was lost three days before its planned orbital insertion in August 1993.
15ffa4fa-b980-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Observer

160a7460-baee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The KMTNet is a network of three identical 1.6-meter optical telescopes operated by the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute, primarily used for microlensing observations to detect exoplanets and other astronomical phenomena.
160a7460-baee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: [optical] 1.6m Telescope part of Korea Microlensing Telescope Network

16194122-bb82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electro Optic Systems telescope is a 1.8-meter instrument located at the Mount Stromlo Observatory in Canberra, Australian Capital Territory, Australia. It is situated at an altitude of approximately 8130 meters with coordinates -35.316 latitude and 149.01 longitude.
16194122-bb82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.8m Electro Optic Systems Telescope at Mount Stromlo Observatory, Australia

161a3b44-b665-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS4 is one of four identically instrumented spacecraft in NASA's Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) mission, designed to study magnetic reconnection within Earth's magnetosphere.
161a3b44-b665-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetospheric Multiscale 4 part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

16285bbe-b72f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **LANL02A** is a geosynchronous spacecraft located in Earth's magnetosphere, specifically within the radiation belt, equipped with instruments to measure energetic electrons and ions.
16285bbe-b72f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Electron Spectrometer on Los Alamos National Laboratory Spacecraft

162b0218-bb5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific entity refers to the set of magnetometers operated at the Toolangi Observatory in Kyoto, Japan, from 1919 to 1980 as part of the IAGA investigation.
162b0218-bb5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Toolangi Observatory

16334dde-b703-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a magnetometer located in Minneapolis with the IAGA identifier MNN, which is part of the observatory network associated with WDC Kyoto and is used for magnetic field measurements.
16334dde-b703-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Minneapolis Observatory

163e10be-bb79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Juice: Jupiter magnetic field model" is a spherical harmonic representation of Jupiter's magnetic field, derived from data collected by the Juno spacecraft during its first nine polar orbits. This model combines a degree 20 spherical harmonic for the internal planetary field with a simple magnetodisc model for external magnetospheric currents, offering detailed insights into Jupiter's dynamo beyond Earth.
163e10be-bb79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: part of Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) Mission

16412dc0-b64d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Sandia View Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Rio Rancho, New Mexico, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility for observing celestial bodies and conducting astronomical research.
16412dc0-b64d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sandia View Observatory, United States

164579c2-b6f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Viking 2 Orbiter was a NASA spacecraft that orbited Mars as part of the Viking project. Launched on September 9, 1975, it played a crucial role in transporting the lander to Mars, performing reconnaissance for landing sites, and conducting scientific investigations while orbiting the planet.
164579c2-b6f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Viking 2 Orbiter part of Viking 2

1647226a-b7d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1U magnetometer is a three-axis instrument used to measure magnetic field components with high resolution, designed to detect substorm activity and ultra-low frequency oscillations for studying radiation belt dynamics.
1647226a-b7d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

1655e1d4-b738-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Fuente de los Matos Observatory**, also known as the **Observatorio Fuente de los Matos** in Muriedas, is an astronomical observatory located in Camargo, Cantabria, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.

165afca0-b8f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Galileo Plasma Wave Spectrometer (PWS)** is an instrument onboard the Galileo spacecraft designed to study plasma waves and radio emissions at Jupiter, featuring simultaneous electric and magnetic field measurements for enhanced accuracy and resolution.

1677873e-ba0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Southend Bradfield Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Tutts Clump, Bradfield Southend, West Berkshire, England. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to the study of celestial bodies and phenomena.

1679d134-bb48-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Electron Drift Instrument (EDI)** on the Cluster-3 spacecraft measures the drift of emitted electrons to determine electric and magnetic field properties. 167f0d76-bba1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Minsk/Pleshenitzi Ground Observatory is a geomagnetic monitoring facility located in Belarus. It has been operational since 1961 and focuses on measuring magnetic field variations from the Earth's surface.

1686361c-bb76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Near Infrared Spectrometer (NIRS3) was an instrument onboard the Hayabusa2 spacecraft designed to map hydrated minerals on asteroid Ryugu by analyzing spectral absorption lines around 3 micrometers.

16a9b772-b761-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Tzec Maun Observatory was an astronomical observatory located in Pingelly, Western Australia, operational until 2010.

16ab4f9a-bb7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **CPMN fluxgate magnetometer** is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument used to measure magnetic fields. It is installed in Adelaide, Australia and is part of the IUGONET observatory network.

16afd726-b610-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Husafell Geomagnetic Observatory (HUS)** is a ground-based facility located in Augastaðir, Borgarbyggð, Western Region, Iceland, which conducts geomagnetic observations as part of a collaborative study between the University of Iceland and NIPR.

16b8ddca-bb5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **LANL2002 Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer (MPA)** is an instrument designed to measure three-dimensional energy/charge distributions of ions and electrons in the magnetosphere using a single electrostatic analyzer coupled with channel electron multipliers, providing high sensitivity and moderate energy and angular resolutions at synchronous orbit.

16c2cccc-b5a3-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astronomical Observatory of La Hita is an astronomical facility located in La Puebla de Almoradiel, Spain, known for its research and dissemination activities under the management of the AstroHita Foundation.

16c3c02c-bb9e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Cape Zhelania Geomagnetic Observatory (CZA) is a ground-based facility located in Novaya Zemlya, Russia, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity as part of the IAGA observatories network.

16e17814-b9ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Equatorial Magnetometer Network's (EMN) fluxgate magnetometer at Mokolo, Cameroon is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument designed to measure magnetic field variations in the Earth's equatorial region.

173252f8-b824-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Capannoli Observatory, Italy

17444c96-b910-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GOLD (Global-scale Observations of the Limb and Disk) mission is a NASA heliophysics initiative that uses a far-ultraviolet imaging spectrograph to study Earth's thermosphere and ionosphere from geostationary orbit, focusing on atmospheric responses to geomagnetic storms and solar variability.

1754dbbc-bb16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The PANSY Radar at Syowa is a large Doppler radar located in the Antarctic, designed for continuous atmospheric observation from 1.5 km to 500 km altitude, utilizing an active phased array system with electronic beam control.

175d88fa-b6d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Jackvik Magnetometer, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, is an instrument located at the Jackvik Geophysical Observatory that measures magnetic fields and has been operational since September 1, 2010.

175e849c-b7e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Nayoro Municipal Observatory Kitasubaru is a public astronomical observatory located in Nayoro City, Hokkaido, Japan. It operates as a ground-based facility and features a reflecting telescope, primarily funded by the city of Nayoro.

1773f3e0-b5b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Quincampoix Observatory (code: A09) is an astronomical observatory located in Quincampoix, Rouen, France. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.

177b1af6-b81f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Castellaccio Geomagnetic Observatory (CAO) is a ground-based facility located in Genoa, Italy, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity from 1957 to 1969.

17818d36-b9ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Submillimeter Wave Astronomy Satellite (SWAS) was a space mission designed to study the composition and dynamics of interstellar clouds using millimeter-wave astronomy. 17818d36-b9ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Submillimeter NASA Submillimeter Wave Astronomy Satellite Mission

17890b80-b59e-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kislovodsk Mountain Astronomical Station is an astronomical observatory located in Karachay-Cherkessia, Russia, and has been operational since October 1948. 1795ba40-b762-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MEASURE investigation

181cd81a-b84b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF Kevo station in Finland is a ground-based facility equipped with a crossed loop antenna for Very Low Frequency (VLF) and Extremely Low Frequency (ELF) observations, established by Prof. Shiokawa of ISEE in collaboration with the Finnish Meteorological Institute.
181cd81a-b84b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Low Frequency / Extremely Low Frequency Crossed Loop Antenna at ISEE Observatory, Finland

181d1132-baf7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **RASC Observatory**, also known as the Alder Springs observatory, is an astronomical observatory located in Auberry, Fresno County, California. It is operated by Sierra Remote Observatories and is situated at coordinates 37.07039 N, -119.4131 W on the continent of North America.
181d1132-baf7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Alder Springs Observatory, United States

1822224e-b6ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Pionerskaya ground station, operational from January 1957 to December 1958, used for measuring magnetic field as part of the IAGA investigation.
1822224e-b6ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pionerskaya Observatory

18224ff6-b6b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pallerols Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Pallerols, Talavera, Segarra, Catalonia, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
18224ff6-b6b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pallerols Observatory, Spain

182b9870-ba3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: NASA's Uhuru, also known as the X-ray Small Astronomical Satellite 1 or Explorer 42, was a pioneering spacecraft designed to observe and study celestial objects in the X-ray waveband. Launched in 1970, it provided groundbreaking data on X-ray sources in space.
182b9870-ba3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: x-ray NASA Uhuru

183cbdc4-b85a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Apollo 17 Surface Electrical Properties (SEP) Experiment** involved a transmitting antenna near the Lunar Module and a receiving antenna on the Lunar Rover to study the electromagnetic properties of the lunar surface and subsurface.
183cbdc4-b85a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Surface Electrical Properties Experiment on Apollo 17 Lunar Module

183e43be-bb99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Calar Alto Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Almería province of Spain, situated on the 2,168-meter-high Calar Alto mountain. It is operated by the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy and the Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia (CSIC).
183e43be-bb99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Calar Alto Observatory, Spain

183ef3b2-b5d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Kwasan Observatory, part of Kyoto University, is an astronomical facility located in Yamashina, Kyoto, Japan, at an altitude of 221.0 meters.
183ef3b2-b5d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kwasan Observatory

18440448-b6a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 14** is an instrument designed to measure the magnitude and direction of Earth's geomagnetic field. It operates alongside a backup sensor to detect variations in magnetic fields, alert for solar wind shocks, and assess geomagnetic activity.
18440448-b6a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 14

1844901c-bae9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EISCAT Svalbard Radar is a research instrument operated by the EISCAT Scientific Association, using incoherent scatter techniques to measure electron and ion densities, temperatures, and velocities in the Earth's ionosphere. It is part of an international network with stations in Sodankylä, Finland, and Kiruna, Sweden, and is located near Longyearbyen, Svalbard.
1844901c-bae9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar at EISCAT Observatory

1850f182-b8f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Bradstreet Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Eastern University in St. Davids, Pennsylvania, USA. Named after astronomy professor David Bradstreet, it was built in 1996 and serves as a ground-based observatory for academic research and education.
1850f182-b8f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bradstreet Observatory, United States

1858bfd6-b5b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Small Carry-on Impactor (SCI) is an instrument deployed by the Hayabusa2 spacecraft to create artificial craters on asteroids by impacting a 2 kg copper liner, allowing access to subsurface materials unaffected by space weathering.
1858bfd6-b5b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Small Carry-on Impactor part of Hayabusa2

186a24ca-bbcb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 12 Lunar Surface Experiments Package Passive Seismic Experiment (PSE) was a set of four seismic stations deployed on the lunar near side during the Apollo missions, designed to monitor and record seismic activity on the Moon from 1969 until mid-1977.
186a24ca-bbcb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Passive Seismic Experiment part of Apollo 12 Lunar Surface Experiments Package

186bb2c8-b5b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Venera 2 Energetic Particles** experiment was a suite of particle detectors onboard the Soviet Venera 2 spacecraft, designed to measure medium-energy charged particles in interplanetary space and near Venus. It specifically monitored protons with energies greater than 30 MeV from the sunward direction and protons with energies between 1-5 MeV perpendicular to the sunward direction.
186bb2c8-b5b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particles experiment on Venera 2

186d1d48-bb02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISEE Magnetometer Nain Station is a ground-based observatory located in Labrador, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada. It is part of the International Ultraviolet Explorer (IUE) Observatory Network and specializes in magnetometer measurements for geomagnetic studies.
186d1d48-bb02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at ISEE Observatory, Canada

18714412-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lethbridge (LETH) Geophysical Observatory** is a ground-based facility in Lethbridge, Alberta, Canada, primarily known for its magnetometer instrument used to study geophysical phenomena.
18714412-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lethbridge Observatory, Canada

187b0402-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **West Skies Observatory**, also known as the **Mulvane Observatory**, is an astronomical observatory located in Mulvane, Kansas, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility for celestial observations and research.
187b0402-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: West Skies Observatory, United States

187e3df4-b9a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Qsaybeh Geomagnetic Observatory (QSB), located in Lebanon, operated from April 2000 to November 2007 and was equipped with a magnetometer for studying geomagnetic activity.
187e3df4-b9a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Qsaybeh Geomagnetic Observatory

18814f6a-b8ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kzil-Agach Geomagnetic Observatory (KZA) was a ground facility located in the Kerbulaq District of Kazakhstan that operated from 1974 to 1975, focusing on geomagnetic measurements as part of the IUGONET network.
18814f6a-b8ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kzil-Agach Geomagnetic Observatory, Kazakhstan

188a7586-bb1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Missouri City Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Missouri City, Texas, USA, designated with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID 722.
188a7586-bb1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Missouri City Observatory, United States

189b3b5c-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GOES 11, Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer is an instrument on the GOES 11 satellite designed to measure magnetic fields in space with high accuracy and sensitivity. It operates using a three-axis fluxgate sensor mounted on a boom to minimize interference from the spacecraft, providing crucial data for monitoring space weather and geomagnetic activity.
189b3b5c-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 11

18a1257c-b8d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Salida Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Socorro County, New Mexico, known for its ground-based observations.
18a1257c-b8d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Salida Observatory, United States

18a50376-b5ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Chicago Sunyaev-Zeldovich Array is an astronomical instrument located at the Owens Valley Radio Observatory in North America, operating in the millimeter waveband to study the cosmic microwave background radiation.
18a50376-b5ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sunyaev-Zeldovich Array millimeter at Owens Valley Radio Observatory

18a9b2d8-baf5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** CORONAS-F is a Russian solar observatory spacecraft launched in 2001 to conduct various observations of the Sun, including X-ray monitoring, radio measurements, and particle counting. It carries multiple instruments designed to study solar phenomena such as flares, coronal activity, and seismic oscillations.
18a9b2d8-baf5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label:
DIFOS instrument on CORONAS-F
SORS instrument on CORONAS-F
ZENIT coronograph on CORONAS-F
SUFR UV radiometer on CORONAS-F
VUSS instrument on CORONAS-F
DIAGENESS instrument on CORONAS-F
RESIK X-ray spectrometer on CORONAS-F
IRIS hard X-ray monitor on CORONAS-F
HELIKON high energy X-ray and Gamma ray detector on CORONAS-F
SKL instrument on CORONAS-F
RES-K X-ray spectroheliograph on CORONAS-F
RPS X-ray spectrometer on CORONAS-F
SPR-N X-ray polarimeter on CORONAS-F

18bacbb6-b674-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
PROBA2 is a small, 3-axis stabilized satellite operated by ESA in a sun-synchronous orbit, designed to demonstrate new technologies and conduct solar observation and space weather studies with instruments like SWAP, LYRA, TPMU, DSLP, and SGVM.
18bacbb6-b674-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label:
Sun Watcher using APS detectors and image Processing on PROBA2
Large Yield RAdiometer on PROBA2
Thermal Plasma Measurement Unit on PROBA2

18c84f78-baef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1.3-m Warsaw Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Las Campanas Observatory in Chile, primarily used for the Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment (OGLE) survey.
18c84f78-baef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 1.3m Warsaw Telescope at Las Campanas Observatory

18df5186-b870-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wide-field Imager for Solar Probe (WISPR) is an instrument on the Parker Solar Probe mission, consisting of two telescopes designed to capture images of the solar corona and inner heliosphere from behind a sunshield.
18df5186-b870-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide-field Imager for Solar Probe on Parker Solar Probe

18e1fb96-b9da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Siding Spring Survey (SSS) was a near-Earth object search program conducted at the Siding Spring Observatory in Australia, serving as the southern hemisphere counterpart to the Catalina Sky Survey.
18e1fb96-b9da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near-Earth Object Search Program at Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

18e377bc-b720-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sutherland-LCO** is an astronomical observatory located in Sutherland, Northern Cape, South Africa. It operates as part of the larger Sutherland Observatory complex and focuses on ground-based observations.
18e377bc-b720-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sutherland Observatory, South Africa

18e3ba8e-bab2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU radio beacon receiver (GRBR) station at Bandung is an observatory located in Indonesia, primarily used to measure ionospheric disturbances related to middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes.
18e3ba8e-bab2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU radio beacon receiver on GRBR Station, Indonesia

18e5cd34-b679-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operational from January 1957 to December 1962 located at the Hollandia station under IAGA, used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of the Kyoto World Data Center.
18e5cd34-b679-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at WDC Kyoto Observatory

18eeaf5e-bb19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The McDonald Observatory is an astronomical observatory located near Fort Davis in Jeff Davis County, Texas. It is operated by The University of Texas at Austin and includes facilities on Mount Locke and Mount Fowlkes.
18eeaf5e-bb19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Harlan J. Smith Telescope at McDonald Observatory, United States

18ef8156-b8c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Loysburg (LOYS) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility in Pennsylvania, USA, part of the NASA THEMIS EPO network, featuring a magnetometer for geophysical measurements.
18ef8156-b8c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Loysburg Observatory, United States

18f460ac-ba56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The North Ryde Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in North Ryde, Sydney, Australia. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
18f460ac-ba56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: North Ryde Observatory, Australia

1901dd32-ba32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Laurel (LREL) Geophysical Observatory** is a ground-based facility located in Laurel, Maryland, USA, primarily used for geophysical research and includes instruments such as the Laurel Magnetometer. It operates under the THEMIS Ground Observatory network since January 1, 2012.
1901dd32-ba32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Laurel Geophysical Observatory, United States

19058c70-ba82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The **CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at Canberra, Australia**, specifically, is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed as part of the IUGONET observatory network for geomagnetic research.
19058c70-ba82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Canadian Pacific Magnetic Network Observation Network

190aa8f0-b97d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Birdsville Station is a ground-based magnetometer observatory located in Birdsville, Australia, operated as part of the CPMN network.
190aa8f0-b97d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Birdsville Observatory, Australia

191122e6-bae2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Apollo 17 Lunar Module, named 'Challenger,' was the last crewed spacecraft to land on the Moon as part of NASA's Apollo program. It carried astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt, facilitated scientific experiments, and collected lunar samples during its mission in December 1972.
191122e6-bae2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Module Challenger part of Apollo 17 Mission

1915dcaa-b8a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Ultra Low Energy Charge Analyzer (ULECA) was a sensor on the International Sun-Earth Explorer 3/International Cometary Explorer spacecraft designed to analyze solar wind characteristics by measuring the charge composition of ions in the energy range of 2 - 560 keV/charge.
1915dcaa-b8a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultra Low Energy Charge Analyzer on International Sun-Earth Explorer 3

19205962-b5c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The DMSP/F18 SSUSI (Special Sensor Ultraviolet Spectrographic Imager) is a photometer launched in 2009 as part of the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program. It observes Extreme and Far UV radiation from the Earth's limb, specifically in the spectral range of 80-170 nm, to measure electron density vertical profiles and ion and neutral densities.
19205962-b5c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Ultraviolet Limb Imager on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program 5D-3 F18

19238738-baa6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Davis Imaging Riometer is an instrument located in Davis, Antarctica, designed to measure ionospheric absorption of cosmic radio noise using a 7x7 crossed dipole antenna array. It was deployed for studying space-time images of the cusp and auroral latitude ionosphere until around 2012.
19238738-baa6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imaging Riometer at Davis Observatory, Antarctica

192c5cb2-bb43-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Chandrayaan-3 Laser Retroreflector Array (LRA) is a passive optical instrument featuring eight corner cube retroreflectors mounted on an aluminum structure. It serves as a precision target for laser ranging from lunar orbit, enabling accurate geolocation of the lander and its instruments on the moon's surface.
192c5cb2-bb43-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Laser Retroreflector Array on Chandrayaan-3 Vikram

194146fc-b947-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Bohyeonsan Observatory**, also known as the OWL-Net observatory, is an astronomical observatory located at Mt. Bohyun in Cheongsong County, North Gyeongsang, South Korea. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
194146fc-b947-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Widefield Linker Network observatory on Mt. Bohyun, Korea

19600ce0-b7df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Deep Space Station 36 (DSS-36) is a 34-meter radio telescope located in Canberra, Australia, part of NASA's Deep Space Network. It operates using a beam waveguide design and supports communication with deep space missions at various frequencies.
19600ce0-b7df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Deep Space Station 36 Radio Telescope at Canberra Observatory, Australia

196c97b2-b6d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Ootake Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Otake-shi, Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
196c97b2-b6d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ootake Observatory, Japan

1970e5b0-b7f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Discovery Bay North** is a ground-based observatory located in Fort Conger, Nunavut, Canada, established in 1876, primarily for geomagnetic monitoring as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
1970e5b0-b7f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Discovery Bay North Observatory, Canada

197bf44a-bab0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The magnetometer at the Vassouras ground station is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field, part of the IAGA investigation and the IUGONET Observatory.
197bf44a-bab0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Vassouras Observatory

198fffe2-ba4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Voyager 1 Ephemeris refers to the precise positional data of the Voyager 1 spacecraft over time, crucial for tracking and understanding its trajectory through space.
198fffe2-ba4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris part of Voyager 1

1990970a-b647-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Australian National University (ANU) 1.3m Telescope at Mount Stromlo Observatory (MSO) is an optical telescope located in Australia with a 1.3-meter aperture, part of the Mount Stromlo Observatory.
1990970a-b647-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.3m Telescope at Mount Stromlo Observatory, Australia

1999477a-b84e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LANL1994 Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer (MPA) is an instrument consisting of a single electrostatic analyzer coupled to an array of channel electron multipliers, designed to measure three-dimensional energy/charge distributions of ions and electrons in the Earth's magnetosphere.
1999477a-b84e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer part of LANL 1994

19aca596-b5fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The H-alpha Imaging System (HIS) is an instrument located on the Domeless Solar Telescope (DST) at Hida Observatory, designed for imaging the Sun's chromosphere in the H-alpha spectral line.
19aca596-b5fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: H-alpha Imaging System on Domeless Solar Telescope at Hida Observatory

19b0340a-bae5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IAGA:WSW Magnetometer** is a scientific instrument located at the Warsaw observatory, used to measure magnetic fields starting from January 1, 1893. It is part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
19b0340a-bae5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Warsaw Observatory

19bf4a3a-bae0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is a ground-based observatory located in Pushchino, Mariinsko-Posadsky District, Chuvashia, Volga Federal District, Russia.
19bf4a3a-bae0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Puschino Observatory, Russia

19c21912-b898-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **THEMIS Electric Fields Instrument (EFI)** on the THEMIS spacecraft measures the three components of the ambient vector electric field using a combination of wire spin plane booms and rigid axial booms, covering frequencies from DC up to 4 kHz with additional spectral measurements.
19c21912-b898-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electric Field Instrument on THEMIS Spacecraft

19c73978-b1d2-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes magnetometers located at the Thule/Qanaq observatory, providing information about these instruments and their data.
19c73978-b1d2-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

19c73cf8-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISEE Magnetometer Gakona Station is a ground-based facility located in Unorganized Borough, Alaska, United States. It serves as an observatory for measuring magnetic fields and is part of the IUGONET network.
19c73cf8-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Gakona Observatory, United States

19d16b16-b892-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Extreme Ultraviolet Imager (EUVI) is an instrument aboard the NASA STEREO-B spacecraft, designed to observe coronal mass ejections and solar activity in extreme ultraviolet wavelengths with high resolution.
19d16b16-b892-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Extreme Ultraviolet Imager part of Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigations

19db9358-ba3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Tellnitz**: A former ground-based observatory in Knínice u Libouchce, Czechia, operational from 1933 to 1934, equipped with magnetometers for geomagnetic measurements.
19db9358-ba3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tellnitz Observatory

19e4782a-b9fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DSX Mission's SET-1 instrument is designed to measure space radiation effects, particularly ELDRS (Enhanced Low Dose Rate Sensitivity) and proton impacts on bipolar junction transistors (BJTs), to improve the understanding of these phenomena and validate ground test protocols.
19e4782a-b9fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument part of DSX Mission

19ee4b7a-b7f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Soft X-Ray Telescope (SXT) on Yohkoh is an instrument designed to capture high-resolution X-ray images and movies of solar flares and the solar corona, using a glancing incidence telescope and a CCD detector, with capabilities for energy separation and visible light imaging.
19ee4b7a-b7f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Soft X-Ray Telescope on Yohkoh

19f16e04-b903-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NEAS spacecraft is a 6U CubeSat equipped with a controllable solar sail, designed to encounter and study near-Earth asteroid 2020 GE using a monochromatic camera for optical navigation and scientific data collection.
19f16e04-b903-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Earth Asteroid Scout spacecraft part of Near Earth Asteroid Scout mission

19f39f00-ba28-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Bangui Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Zongo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, dedicated to monitoring and studying Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since 1952.
19f39f00-ba28-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bangui Magnetic Observatory, Congo, The Democratic Republic of the

19f5b82e-b7c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **New Horizons KBO Search-Magellan/Clay** is a telescope located at Las Campanas Observatory in Chile. It was used to search for Kuiper Belt Objects as part of the New Horizons mission.
19f5b82e-b7c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Magellan/Clay Telescope at Las Campanas Observatory, Chile

19f64fb6-bb68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Galileo Magnetometer (MAG) was an instrument onboard the Galileo spacecraft designed to study Jupiter's magnetosphere, its interaction with satellites, and other magnetic phenomena. It consisted of two triaxial fluxgate magnetometers mounted at different distances from the spacecraft spin axis to provide real-time estimates of magnetic fields and redundancy in measurements.
19f64fb6-bb68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Galileo

19f71586-bb86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Observatori de Santa Maria de Montmagastrell** is an astronomical observatory located in Santa Maria de Montmagastrell, Spain. It was established in 1991 and is situated at an altitude of approximately 319 meters.

1a27228e-b678-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **UCLA Global MHD model** is a computational tool developed by the University of California, Los Angeles, that simulates the interaction between the solar wind and Earth’s magnetosphere using magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) principles. It models various physical processes, including electric field dynamics, reconnection, and ionospheric conductance, on a non-uniform Cartesian grid to study space weather phenomena.

1a28cc58-b86a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Warnkenhagen Geomagnetic Observatory (WRH), located in Kalkhorst, Germany, is a ground-based facility that monitors and studies geomagnetic activity. 1da5397c-b85e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hamburg-Himmelsmoor Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Duvenstedt, Wandsbek, Hamburg, Germany. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
1da5397c-b85e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hamburg-Himmelsmoor Observatory, Germany

1da94a9e-baed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dettelbach Vineyard Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Dettelbach, Bavaria, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
1da94a9e-baed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dettelbach Vineyard Observatory, Germany

1daa46fa-b9ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Lund Observatory is an astronomical research facility in Lund, Sweden, originally established as the astronomy department at Lund University and now operating as a network of researchers within the Department of Physics.
1daa46fa-b9ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lund Observatory, Sweden

1db1f3f6-bafc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Gakona, Alaska (GA762) is an advanced ground facility that uses a Digisonde to analyze ionospheric reflections by evaluating the angle of arrival, polarization, Doppler frequency shift, and travel time of skywave signals.
1db1f3f6-bafc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Gakona Observatory, United States

1db299aa-b854-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Coral Harbour Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAGs since July 16, 2012.
1db299aa-b854-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Coral Harbour Geophysical Observatory

1db30916-b5f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a set of analytical models used in the MMS2 mission to study Earth's magnetosphere, part of the CDPP-AMDA observatory under CNES.
1db30916-b5f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetospheric Analytical Models part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

1dccc274-bbd0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **AGO P3 Antenna Instrument** is an antenna used for communication and data collection at the AGO P3 ground station, which is part of the ICESTAR observatory network. It plays a crucial role in facilitating scientific investigations and observations within this network.
1dccc274-bbd0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna on ICESTAR and Argentine Geophysical Observatory

1dd504e6-b7ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Digital Fields Board (DFB)** is an instrument aboard the Parker Solar Probe Mission that conditions, digitizes, and processes signals from voltage sensors and search coil magnetometers to produce various data streams used for time domain and spectral domain analysis.
1dd504e6-b7ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digital Fields Board part of Parker Solar Probe Mission

1dd66ace-b714-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a magnetometer instrument located at the observatory station identified by IAGA as CZA (Cape Zhelania). This magnetometer is part of the WDC Kyoto network and contributes to magnetic field measurements for geophysical studies.
1dd66ace-b714-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Cape Zhelania Observatory

1dda9878-bbac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Loomberah Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Loomberah, New South Wales, Australia.
1dda9878-bbac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Loomberah Observatory

1df71b58-b1b9-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Jekman Island Magnetometer** is a magnetometer located at the observatory on Jekman Island, identified by IAGA as JKI. It has been operational since January 1, 1939.
1df71b58-b1b9-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Jekman Island Observatory

1dfccb70-b957-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **North Pole 8 Magnetometer** is an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields at the IAGA North Pole 8 station, operational from January 1, 1959 to December 31, 1962.
1dfccb70-b957-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole Observatory

1dff736e-ba5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer used in the ISEE investigation to measure variations in the 3-D vector geomagnetic field with a sampling rate of 64 Hz, located at Magadan.
1dff736e-ba5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Induction Magnetometer part of International Monitor for Auroral Geomagnetic Effects

1e084e76-b7b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Abbey Ridge Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at 45 Abbey Road in Stillwater Lake, Nova Scotia, Canada. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
1e084e76-b7b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Abbey Ridge Observatory, Canada

1e08960c-b8a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **CANOPUS Magnetometer and Riometer Array (MARI)** was a ground-based instrument array used for remotely sensing the high latitude ionosphere during the International Solar-Terrestrial Physics/Global Geospace Science (ISTP/GGS) program. It has since been superseded by the Canadian Array for Realtime Investigations of Magnetic Activity (CARISMA).
1e08960c-b8a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Riometer part of Canadian Array for Realtime Investigations of Magnetic Activity

1e0d2724-b833-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Wind and Suprathermal Ion Composition Studies (SWICS) instrument is designed to measure the mass, charge, and energy of ions in the solar wind within an energy range of 0.5 to 30 keV/e, although its capabilities have been reduced due to a failure in its "stop" Micro Channel Plate (MCP).
1e0d2724-b833-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Wind and Suprathermal Ion Composition Studies on Wind Spacecraft

1e0d9244-b609-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mid-InfraRed Spectrometer and Imager (MIRSI) is a mid-infrared camera system with both spectroscopic and imaging capabilities, developed at Boston University and supported by the NASA Infrared Telescope Facility (IRTF) on Mauna Kea.
1e0d9244-b609-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mid-InfraRed Spectrometer and Imager on NASA Infrared Telescope Facility, USA

1e133f78-baff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Yunnan Astronomical Observatory (YNAO) is a ground-based astronomical facility located on Earth's surface, equipped with telescopes for observing celestial phenomena.
1e133f78-baff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1m Telescope at Yunnan Astronomical Observatory

1e162704-bac0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Archenhold Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Berlin-Treptow, Germany. It houses the Großer Refraktor (Great Refractor), which is known as the longest pointable telescope globally and is also referred to as Die Himmelskanone (Celestial Cannon).
1e162704-bac0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Archenhold Observatory, Germany

1e189d94-b7a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Viking Orbiter 1 Spacecraft (VO1) Radio Science Subsystem (RSS) was an instrument used to analyze radio signals from the spacecraft to study Mars' dynamics, surface properties, atmosphere, ionosphere, and other solar system characteristics. It utilized coherent Doppler and ranging measurements along with dual-frequency downlinks to gather precise data.
1e189d94-b7a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Subsystem on Viking Orbiter 1 Spacecraft

1e2ad9b0-bade-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **spectrometer** is an instrument used to measure properties of light over a specific portion of the electromagnetic spectrum. The **SOLIS Integrated Sunlight Spectrometer (ISS)** is designed to obtain high and moderate spectral resolution observations of the Sun as a star, providing disk-integrated sunlight measurements through a fiber optic feed system.
1e2ad9b0-bade-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Integrated Sunlight Spectrometer part of Synoptic Optical Long-term Investigations of the Sun

1e2dd87a-ba22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Remus Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Remus, Michigan, USA, operated by UCLA. It includes an Educational Public Outreach magnetometer and is part of the THEMIS ground observatory network, with specific magnetic coordinates calculated using IGRF models.
1e2dd87a-ba22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Remus Geophysical Observatory, United States

1e2dfade-b6ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Onsala Space Observatory (OSO)** is the Swedish National Facility for Radio Astronomy, located in Onsala, Sweden. It operates two radio telescopes and participates in international projects to study both Earth and the broader Universe.
1e2dfade-b6ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 20m Telescope at Onsala Space Observatory, Sweden

1e405410-bb2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **San Pablo-Toledo Magnetic Observatory** is a ground-based facility in San Pablo de los Montes, Toledo, Spain, dedicated to magnetic observations and funded by the Instituto Geográfico Nacional.
1e405410-bb2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at San Pablo de los Montes Observatory, Spain

1e4b62aa-b78e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "GEOS-1 Conjugated Points" refers to the footprints of the magnetic field line crossing the GEOS-1 spacecraft, modeled using Tsyganenko 1989's magnetic field data. It is part of the CDPP archive under the CNES Observatory.
1e4b62aa-b78e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Conjugated Points part of CNES Observatory CDPP Archive GEOS-1

1e505ff6-b7ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 14 Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP) Suprathermal Ion Detector Experiment (SIDE) was a scientific instrument deployed on the Moon during the Apollo 14 mission to measure the energies and masses of positive ions reaching the lunar surface, including those from the magnetosphere, solar wind, and interactions with the lunar atmosphere.
1e505ff6-b7ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Suprathermal Ion Detector on Apollo 14 Lunar Surface Experiments Package

1e52f9fe-bb7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Szamotuly-Gałowo Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Gałowo, Poland. It functions as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
1e52f9fe-bb7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Szamotuly-Galowo Observatory, Poland

1e61dcf0-bc58-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tri-axial Fluxgate Magnetometer FGM-I** is an instrument aboard the Interball Tail Probe designed to measure magnetic fields and waves. It features a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer and a Langmuir split probe plasma current sensor, with a measurement range of 0.3-37.5 nT and a frequency range of 0-2 Hz.
1e61dcf0-bc58-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tri-axial Fluxgate Magnetometer on Interball Tail Probe

1e65cedc-b91f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1.3GHz WPR (LQ4) at Koganei, Japan is a transportable wind profiler radar operating at 1.3 GHz frequency, used for atmospheric studies and weather monitoring.
1e65cedc-b91f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.3GHz Wind Profiler Radar at Koganei Observatory, Japan

1e6c9df8-b5f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Grasslands Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in Sonoita, Arizona, dedicated to ground-based observations of the night sky.
1e6c9df8-b5f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Grasslands Observatory, United States

1e72678e-b8ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **QOS Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Slobidka-Zalisetska, Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
1e72678e-b8ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Zalistsi Observatory, Ukraine

1e73ee2c-b8a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Leoncito Astronomical Complex (CASLEO) is an astronomical observatory located in the San Juan Province of Argentina, known for its favorable conditions with minimal cloud cover.
1e73ee2c-b8a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Complejo Astronómico El Leoncito

1e79666c-b6a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cereseto Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Cereseto, Alessandria, Piedmont, Italy. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center code K37 and focuses on ground-based observations of celestial bodies.
1e79666c-b6a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cereseto Observatory, Italy

1e79900e-b94a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lowell Discovery Telescope (LDT), previously known as the Discovery Channel Telescope (DCT), is a 4.3-meter Ritchey–Chrétien telescope located in Happy Jack, Arizona, operated by Lowell Observatory for advanced astronomical research.
1e79900e-b94a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 4.3m Lowell Discovery Telescope at Lowell Observatory, United States

1e7c808e-b869-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Cewanee Observatory at DSNM is an astronomical observatory located in Hidalgo County, New Mexico, United States. It is situated on Earth and functions as a ground-based observatory.
1e7c808e-b869-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cewanee Observatory, United States

1e843f0e-b805-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Lucy**: A NASA space mission and probe designed to conduct the first-ever exploration of Jupiter's Trojan asteroids, small bodies that share Jupiter’s orbit around the Sun. Lucy will perform flyby observations of eight asteroids—one main belt asteroid and seven Trojans—to study their composition, geology, and origins, aiming to shed light on early Solar System formation processes.
1e843f0e-b805-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terminal Tracking Camera on Lucy

1e8c8eca-b62f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 17 Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP) Heat Flow Experiment (HFE) was a scientific apparatus designed to measure the rate of heat loss from the lunar interior by taking temperature and thermal property measurements at the surface and subsurface of the Moon. This experiment was conducted during the Apollo 15, 16, and 17 missions using probes inserted into drilled holes on the lunar surface.
1e8c8eca-b62f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heat Flow Experiment part of Apollo 17 Lunar Surface Experiments Package

1e8de6d0-b6f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Helios-1 E5A Plasma Wave Experiment was an instrument onboard the Helios 1 spacecraft designed to measure electric field intensities in the solar wind, covering a frequency range from 31 Hz to 178 kHz, which includes key plasma frequencies.
1e8de6d0-b6f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Wave Antenna part of Helios 1

1eac5ac0-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Victoria ground station since 1956, part of the IAGA investigation and the IUGONET observatory network.
1eac5ac0-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

1eac9340-b9e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The CBA-NOVAC Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Front Royal, Virginia, United States. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
1eac9340-b9e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: CBA-NOVAC Observatory, United States

1eb11fd8-b706-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Natelli Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Lincoln Elementary School in Maplewood, Frederick, Maryland, USA. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
1eb11fd8-b706-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Natelli Observatory

1eb20650-bb70-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMN Guadalcanal station is a ground-based magnetometer network located in Lenggakiki, Honiara, Solomon Islands. It is situated at coordinates -9.43 latitude and 159.95 longitude on the continent of Oceania.
1eb20650-bb70-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Guadalcanal Observatory, Solomon Islands

1eba01be-b861-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tasiilaq Magnetometer is a ground-based instrument, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, used to measure magnetic fields at the Tasiilaq Geophysical Observatory since 2007.
1eba01be-b861-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tasiilaq Observatory

1ec3d042-b6ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2001 Mars Odyssey Spacecraft Accelerometer is an instrument aboard the 2001 Mars Odyssey spacecraft that measures forces acting on the vehicle to track its motion, orientation, and stability, crucial for maintaining its flight path and optimizing mission performance.
1ec3d042-b6ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: The 2001 Mars Odyssey Spacecraft Accelerometer on 2001 Mars Odyssey

1ed9d640-b6f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is the **Merak Observatory**, located in Wendeng District, Weihai, Shandong, China (coordinates: 37.19803° N, 121.786° E). It is a ground-based astronomical facility operated by the National Astronomical Observatories of China (NAOC).
1ed9d640-b6f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Merak Observatory, China

1ef5dc42-b97f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Time of Flight Energy Angle Mass Spectrograph (TEAMS)** is a high-sensitivity mass spectrometer designed to measure the 3-dimensional distribution function of major ion species, with capabilities for energy per charge selection, time-of-flight analysis, and detailed angular resolution.
1ef5dc42-b97f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer on FAST

1efd7f06-b97f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of California, Los Angeles 46m (150-foot) Solar Tower at Mount Wilson Observatory is a telescope facility located in North America, designed for observing the Sun in the optical waveband.
1efd7f06-b97f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 46m Solar Tower Telescope at Mount Wilson Observatory

1f0645a8-ba3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Sandvreten Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Testa, Skogs-Tibble, Enköpings kommun, Uppsala County, Sweden. It is a ground-based facility used for various astronomical observations and research.
1f0645a8-ba3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sandvreten Observatory, Sweden

1f0abdfc-b60e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Darwin of 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network** is a ground-based facility located at the Darwin Golf Course in Malak, Darwin, Australia. It operates as part of the ISEE/MM210 magnetometer network and includes a fluxgate instrument for magnetic field measurements.
1f0abdfc-b60e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at 210 Magnetic Meridian Observatory, Australia

1f0aec56-b74d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IR2, or 2-micron Camera, is an instrument onboard the Akatsuki spacecraft designed to study Venus' meteorology by observing near-infrared windows in its CO2 atmosphere. It captures images at specific wavelengths to detect cloud patterns and altitudes.
1f0aec56-b74d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Infrared 2-micron Camera on Akatsuki

1f0ec222-ba54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: H47 (Q116161190), also known as the Vicksburg Observatory, is an astronomical observatory located in Southhaven, Warren County, Mississippi. It operates under MPC ID H47 and conducts ground-based observations.
1f0ec222-ba54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vicksburg Observatory, United States

1f122112-b8d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The magnetometer located at the station with the IAGA identifier NAL in New Alesund has been operational since January 1966 as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
1f122112-b8d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ny-Ålesund Observatory

1f1843c6-b5a2-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Stazione Astronomica Le Pleiadi is an astronomical observatory located in Pantane, Taverna, Italy, with the MPC code L88.
1f1843c6-b5a2-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Stazione Astronomica Le Pleiadi, Italy

1f1c090a-b6d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Quito, comet astrograph station" (Q114662679) is an astronomical observatory located in Malchingui, Pedro Moncayo Canton, Pichincha, Ecuador. It specializes in the observation and study of comets.
1f1c090a-b6d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Comet Astrograph Station at Quito Observatory, Ecuador

1f1dd35a-baf1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SECS observatory is a virtual network comprising multiple ground magnetometer arrays, including CANMOS, CARISMA, DMI (in Greenland), GIMA, MACCS, THEMIS, and STEP, used to create the Spherical Elementary Current Systems datasets.
1f1dd35a-baf1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spherical Elementary Current Systems part of Spherical Elementary Current Systems Observatory

1f2d2490-bac9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Spectral Instruments 2K CCD is an astronomical instrument located at the Mount Lemmon Observatory, featuring an E2V_42-40_041831905 detector and iris shutter.
1f2d2490-bac9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spectral Instruments 2K CCD on 1m Telescope at Mount Lemmon Observatory

1f2d2578-bab8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The specific set of magnetometers mentioned here are located in Tsumeb (TSU) and have been operational since 1964 as part of the IAGA investigation under the World Data Center Kyoto.
1f2d2578-bab8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tsumeb Observatory

1f3091e6-b936-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** DMSP 5D-2/F10 is a meteorological satellite developed and operated by the U.S. Air Force as part of the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP), designed to provide global visual and infrared cloud cover data for weather analysis and forecasting.
1f3091e6-b936-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: visual and infrared Defense Meteorological Satellite Program part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

1f3a7ec4-bad8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
"BARREL Balloon 2Q" is a component of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) mission, designed to study electron precipitation from Earth's radiation belts using balloons equipped with scientific instruments in the stratosphere. It operated from February 2, 2014, to February 4, 2014.
1f3a7ec4-bad8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star Geospace Mission of Opportunity

1f4082ce-b5a1-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cassini Ion and Neutral Mass Spectrometer (INMS) is an instrument designed to analyze the mass composition and number densities of neutral species and low-energy ions in Saturn's system, with a focus on Titan's upper atmosphere and its interactions with Saturn's magnetosphere.
1f4082ce-b5a1-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Cassini Ion and Neutral Mass Spectrometer on Cassini Spacecraft

1f4dc74a-b98e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wuhan geophysical observatory is a ground facility located in Baoxie, East Lake High-tech Zone, Jiangxia District, Wuhan, Hubei, China. It specializes in geomagnetic measurements and has been operational since January 1, 1980.
1f4dc74a-b98e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Wuhan Observatory, China

1f52b6ac-baaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Westwood, Massachusetts, known as the Westwood Observatory.
1f52b6ac-baaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Westwood Observatory

1f67efca-b70f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Schonfeld Observatory**, also known as the Sternwarte Schonfeld or Dresden, is an astronomical observatory located in Dresden, Germany. It serves as a ground-based facility for observing celestial bodies and conducting astronomical research.
1f67efca-b70f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dresden Observatory, Germany

1f8356b4-b941-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The SupraThermal Ion Composition Spectrometer (STICS) is an instrument designed to measure the mass, mass per charge, and energy of ions within the energy range of 6-230 keV/e. It is part of the Wind spacecraft mission, contributing to studies of energetic particles in space.
1f8356b4-b941-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SupraThermal Ion Composition Spectrometer on Wind

1f8ae982-bbc7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2N Engineering Data Interface (EDI) is a component of the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL), responsible for converting analog signals to digital data, specifically monitoring temperatures, voltages, and currents with high precision.
1f8ae982-bbc7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

1f9801e4-b76c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**

1fe1a7c2-b889-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer installed in January 1964 at the Fort Rae 2 geophysical observatory, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the WDC_GDMC investigation.
1fe1a7c2-b889-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fort Rae Observatory

1fe393f6-b7d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **GSA Observatory in Gwangju** is a ground-based astronomical facility located at Gwangju Science High School in Buk-gu, Gwangju, South Korea. It serves as an educational and research observatory for students and the scientific community.
1fe393f6-b7d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gwangju Observatory, South Korea

1fe41066-b843-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Oberwiesenthal Observatory (C22) is an astronomical facility located in Oberwiesenthal, Germany. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting various astronomical observations and research.

1ffabbb2-b96b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital instrument installed in Majuro, United States, designed to measure ionospheric total electron content (TEC) using LEO satellite signals. It utilizes GNU Radio software and USRP hardware for signal processing and acquisition at 150 and 400 MHz frequencies.

20170284-b729-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Kandalaksha is a ground-based observatory in Russia, located at 67.133 latitude and 32.433 longitude on the Earth's surface, equipped with a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements as part of the IAGA network since 1933.
20170284-b729-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kandalaksha Observatory, Russia

201fc01c-b82e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nobeyama Radio Observatory (NRO) is a ground-based astronomical facility in Japan operated by the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ), featuring several radio instruments at an elevation of 1350 meters near Minamimaki, Nagano.
201fc01c-b82e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 45m Radio Telescope at Nobeyama Radio Observatory, Japan

202cb0ae-b9ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to magnetometers located at the IAGA-identified station UGT, operational from 1975 to 1979 as part of the Iugonet Observatory associated with WDC Kyoto.
202cb0ae-b9ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iugonet Observatory

202ebe4a-b690-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetometers at Ivigtut (IVI) were instruments used to measure the Earth's magnetic field from January 1, 1863, until December 31, 1960, as part of the IAGA investigation at the observatory in Ivigtut.
202ebe4a-b690-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ivigtut Observatory

203bacb0-b82d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Osservatorio Madonna di Dossobuono is an astronomical observatory located in Verona, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for celestial observations and research.
203bacb0-b82d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Madonna di Dossobuono Observatory, Italy

203ec140-b6f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mars Global Surveyor (MGS)** was a NASA spacecraft that orbited Mars from 1997 to 2006, collecting data on the planet's surface morphology, topography, composition, gravity, atmospheric dynamics, and magnetic field.
203ec140-b6f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Global Surveyor

20521de2-b8e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Dourbes Magnetic Observatory** is a magnetic observatory located in Belgium that has been operating since 1828, providing continuous monitoring and data collection of Earth's magnetic field.
20521de2-b8e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dourbes Magnetic Observatory, Belgium

2053226c-b6b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometers at Havana (HVN), part of the IAGA investigation since 1897, are located at a ground-based observatory in Havana.
2053226c-b6b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Havana Observatory

2053c4aa-b6be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: NEOSSat (Near Earth Object Surveillance Satellite) is a Canadian space telescope designed to detect and track asteroids, satellites, and space debris. It plays a crucial role in monitoring near-Earth objects and maintaining space situational awareness.
2053c4aa-b6be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Earth Object Surveillance Satellite

2053d3b0-b758-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Penwortham Observatory (D86) is an astronomical observatory located in Penwortham, South Australia. It is a ground-based facility situated at the coordinates 138.6407 longitude and -33.91894 latitude.
2053d3b0-b758-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Penwortham Observatory, Australia

2055b850-bbaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Express Orbiter SPICAM (SPectroscopie pour l’Investigation des Caractéristiques Atmosphériques de Mars) Light is an instrument on the Mars Express spacecraft designed to study the atmospheric characteristics of Mars using ultraviolet and near-infrared spectroscopy.
2055b850-bbaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet and near infrared Spectroscopy for the Investigation of the Characteristics of the Atmosphere of Mars on Mars Express Orbiter

2063adde-b9d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Instituto de Astrofisica de Andalucia (IAA-CSIC) 0.6m Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Observatorio de Sierra Nevada in Europe, operated by the Instituto de Astrofísica de Andalucía.
2063adde-b9d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.6m optical Telescope at Observatorio de Sierra Nevada

20667572-b926-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Thule/Camp Tuto Geomagnetic Observatory (THU), located in Avannaata, Greenland, was a ground-based facility sponsored by Denmark that operated from 1932 to 1952, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
20667572-b926-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Thule/Camp Tuto Geomagnetic Observatory

206e929e-b722-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **THEMIS C Spacecraft Position** is an ephemeris dataset that provides information on the position and status of the THEMIS-B probe within the NASA's THEMIS mission.
206e929e-b722-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft Position part of Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms

207d2846-b780-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Apollo 15 Command and Service Module Panoramic Camera** was a high-resolution camera designed to capture detailed panoramic images of the lunar surface from orbit during the Apollo 15 mission. It provided both stereoscopic and monoscopic coverage, supporting various scientific experiments by offering photographic data with resolutions of 1-2 meters from an altitude of 111 km.
207d2846-b780-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Itek Panoramic Camera on Apollo 15 Command and Service Module

2085b7f2-bb8d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISEE Magnetometer station at Magadan, Russia is a ground-based facility located in the Far Eastern Federal District of Russia that conducts magnetometer observations as part of the IUGONET network.
2085b7f2-bb8d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Magadan Observatory, Russia

208b59b8-b9c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: MMS_3 is a spacecraft in the Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) mission constellation, designed to study magnetic reconnection within Earth's magnetosphere.
208b59b8-b9c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetospheric Multiscale 3 part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

208d0534-b8b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AGO P6 Antenna Instrument is a component of the ICESTAR observatory, designed to facilitate communication and data collection at the AGO P6 ground station.
208d0534-b8b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna on ICESTAR part of Advanced Geospace Observatory

208d1526-bb59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cassegrain Spectrometer is a telescope-based instrument that analyzes light from distant celestial objects by dispersing it into its component wavelengths, providing spectral data essential for studying the composition and velocity of stars, galaxies, and nebulae.
208d1526-bb59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Cassegrain Spectrometer on 2.1m Otto Struve Telescope

208f003c-b9ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Jaén Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Jaén, Andalusia, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
208f003c-b9ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Jaen Observatory, Spain

209183d8-b6b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Klet Observatory-KLENOT, located in Křenov u Kájova, Czechia, is a ground-based astronomical observatory known for its contributions to astronomy and sky surveys.
209183d8-b6b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.57m Telescope at Klet Observatory, Czechia

209f7b52-bb1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **Spectrometer** is a scientific instrument designed to measure properties of light over a specific portion of the electromagnetic spectrum, particularly used in this context as part of the Electron Spectrometer investigation on the Freja spacecraft to detect and analyze electron energy and angular distributions.

20a1d552-b919-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field from 1956 to 1975, located at the World Data Center in Kyoto and identified as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA).
20a1d552-b919-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at WDC Kyoto Observatory

20aeb63c-b860-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: Church Stretton Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Church Stretton, Shropshire, England, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
20aeb63c-b860-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Church Stretton Observatory, United Kingdom

20b063e2-b8fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hollandia Geomagnetic Observatory (HNA) was a ground facility in Sentani, Indonesia, that operated from 1957 to 1962, sponsored by the Netherlands and known for its geomagnetic measurements.

20b77c04-b79d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GOES 14 spacecraft ephemeris is a dataset containing the positional data of the GOES 14 satellite, providing information on its location over time. 20b86876-b635-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Phoenix Lander Telltale was a mechanical wind indicator on the NASA Phoenix Mars lander that used a suspended cylinder to measure wind speed and direction through imaging with the Surface Stereo Imager.

20c0c238-b797-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **M57 Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Saltrio, Lombardy, Italy. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
20c0c238-b797-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: M57 Observatory, Italy

20c14a86-b7de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Deep Space Network (DSNR) Goldstone Solar System Radar is a radio telescope facility located in North America, primarily used for observing solar and planetary phenomena. 20c14a86-b7de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio The Deep Space Network Goldstone Solar System Radar

20c6ab82-ba10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IPS Sugadaira Station** is an antenna facility located in Ueda, Nagano Prefecture, Japan, dedicated to Interplanetary Scintillation (IPS) measurements. It includes a UHF radio telescope and contributes to ground-based astronomical observations.

20c97078-b81d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Explorer 40**, also known as **Injun 5**, was a NASA magnetically aligned research satellite launched in 1968 to study charged particles and VLF radio emissions in the ionosphere.

20ccd644-bb0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Osaka Prefecture University 1.85m millimeter-submillimeter Telescope is a telescope located in Asia with an aperture of 1.85 meters, designed for observing millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths. It is situated at Osaka Prefecture University.
20ccd644-bb0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.85m Telescope

20cdcf34-ba06-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Far Ultraviolet Space Telescope (FAUST), launched aboard the ATLAS 1 mission, is a space-based observatory designed to conduct astronomical observations in the ultraviolet waveband.
