20fb2ea0-b7f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Video camera imaging system on the Flare Monitoring Telescope (FMT) at Hida Observatory is an instrument used for capturing high-resolution images of the Sun's chromosphere to study solar flares and other dynamic phenomena.
20fb2ea0-b7f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager Video Camera Imaging System part of Sun.Chromosphere Investigation

2106eec4-b685-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometer at the Alibag ground station, part of the IAGA investigation and IUGONET Observatory, has been operational since 1904.
2106eec4-b685-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Alibag Observatory

21099f62-b9c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "Nizhnedevitsk" refers to a ground-based observatory located in Russia, specifically at Nizhnedevitsk, Voronezh Oblast. It operated from 1935 to 1940 and was equipped with magnetometers for geophysical observations.
21099f62-b9c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nizhnedevitsk Observatory, Russia

210b01fe-b5f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 0.41m Horacio Ghielmetti Telescope is an optical telescope located at the El Leoncito Astronomical Complex in South America, part of the Complejo Astronómico El Leoncito (CASLEO).
210b01fe-b5f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.41m optical Horacio Ghielmetti Telescope at El Leoncito Astronomical Complex

210e51ca-ba75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Eygalayes Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Eygalayes, France, dedicated to ground-based observations.
210e51ca-ba75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Eygalayes Observatory, France

210ebdde-b6f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The San Diego State University (SDSU) 1.25m (50-inch) Phillips Claud Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Mount Laguna Observatory in North America, operated by San Diego State University.
210ebdde-b6f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.25m Phillips Claud Telescope at Mount Laguna Observatory

21101ec8-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ESA Cebreros TBT Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Cebreros, Ávila, Castile and León, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations.
21101ec8-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: European Space Agency Tracking and Bistatic Telemetry Station at Cebreros Observatory, Spain

2131bda2-b9dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Voroshilov is a former ground-based magnetometer observatory located in Ussuriysk, Primorsky Krai, Russia, which operated from 1951 to 1957. It was part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network and contributed to geomagnetic field measurements.
2131bda2-b9dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Voroshilov Observatory, Russia

213aad36-b99b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Magadan station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in the Khasynsky Urban District, Magadan Oblast, Russia. It is part of the CPMN magnetometer network and specializes in monitoring geomagnetic activity using instruments like fluxgate magnetometers.
213aad36-b99b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Magadan Observatory, Russia

214a1b72-b8ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/F18, SESS Special Sensor Ionospheric Plasma Drift/Scintillation Monitor-3 (SESS/SSI/ES-3) is an instrument aboard the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program that measures electron density and temperatures, ion density, plasma drift, and scintillation at orbital altitudes.
214a1b72-b8ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Ionospheric Plasma Drift and Scintillation Monitor-3 on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

2159f1da-ba60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "NOAA 19 Positions" refers to the ephemerides data of the NOAA 19 spacecraft, detailing its positions in various coordinate systems. This data is part of the observational facilities managed by the NOAA-19 satellite.
2159f1da-ba60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: NOAA 19 Positions part of NOAA 19

21631388-b6b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Cometary Sampling and Composition Experiment (COSAC) is an instrument suite aboard the Rosetta Philae Lander, comprising a gas chromatograph and a time-of-flight mass spectrometer designed to analyze comet samples.
21631388-b6b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cometary Sampling and Composition Experiment on Rosetta Philae Lander

2171078a-b8cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Magnetic Ion-Mass Spectrometer (MIMS)** on the AE-C satellite is an instrument designed to measure in situ concentrations of ambient ion species within a mass range from 1 to 90 atomic mass units. It uses electric and magnetic fields to produce a mass spectrum, simultaneously collecting ions in three different mass ranges: 1 to 4, 4 to 16, and 16 to 90 u.
