It continuously monitors the spacecraft's potential using the PEACE instrument.
3adc5ace-bbbb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Active Space Potential Control part of Double Star 1

3ae02214-bb28-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **OLPH Observatory** is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, New York, associated with Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church.
3ae02214-bb28-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: OLPH Observatory at Brooklyn, United States

3af06e0e-b98d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fluxgate Magnetometer is an instrument designed to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. It consists of two tri-axial fluxgate sensors mounted on a spacecraft to study plasma regions and solar wind interactions with Venus's atmosphere.
3af06e0e-b98d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Venus Express

3af40ebe-b754-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Batavia Geomagnetic Observatory (BTV), located in Jakarta, Indonesia, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1884 to 1928, primarily focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
3af40ebe-b754-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Batavia Geomagnetic Observatory, Indonesia

3af9aa36-b7cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cape Dorset Magnetometer, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, is an instrument at the Cape Dorset Geophysical Observatory that measures magnetic field variations starting from January 14, 2007.
3af9aa36-b7cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cape Dorset Observatory

3b025732-b63f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover ChemCam instrument suite includes both the LIBS (Laser Induced Breakdown Spectrometer) and the RMI (Remote Micro-Imager), designed to analyze the chemical composition of rocks and soils on Mars. The LIBS component uses a laser to vaporize samples, enabling detailed spectral analysis for elemental identification within seven meters of the instrument.
3b025732-b63f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Laser Induced Breakdown Spectrometer part of Mars Science Laboratory

3b0bd6a0-bc38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cylindrical Electrostatic Probe (CEP)** on AE-D is a Langmuir probe instrument designed to measure electron temperatures, electron and ion concentrations, ion mass, and spacecraft potential using two identical retarding potential devices oriented differently relative to the spin axis of the spacecraft.
3b0bd6a0-bc38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Langmuir Probe part of AE-D Cylindrical Electrostatic Probe

3b176cce-bb5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Viking Lander 1 Spacecraft Labeled Release (LR) instrument was designed to detect microbial life on Mars by measuring the release of radioactive gas from martian soil samples inoculated with nutrients, using beta detectors and other sensors.
3b176cce-bb5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Labeled Release on Viking Lander 1 Spacecraft

3b17ffe0-bb91-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **AstroColauri Observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Chiaiano, Naples, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena. It operates under the MPC_ID L74 and provides valuable contributions to astronomical research from its strategic European location.
3b17ffe0-bb91-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: AstroColauri Observatory, Italy

3b18c524-b5e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** NASCam (Lowell Observatory's NASCam) is a specialized camera system developed through a collaboration between Lowell Observatory and NASA to study planetary systems and potential extraterrestrial life, particularly by imaging the atmospheres of planets like Mars.
3b18c524-b5e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Camera System at Lowell Observatory

3b1a9cea-b6c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "EMN fluxgate magnetometer at MMB" is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer located in Memanbetsu, Japan. It is part of the Equatorial Magnetometer Network and facilitates magnetic field measurements for scientific research.
3b1a9cea-b6c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of The Equatorial Magnetometer Network

3b1d7f26-bb35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Karaganda Geomagnetic Observatory (KGD), located in Karaganda, Kazakhstan, is a ground facility that operated from 1965 to 1989, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
3b1d7f26-bb35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Karaganda Geomagnetic Observatory, Kazakhstan

3b1ffcf0-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ESO Multi-Mode Instrument (EMMI) in its RILD mode is a versatile tool for low-resolution long-slit spectroscopy at the La Silla Observatory's New Technology Telescope, allowing observations across various visible wavelengths using grisms and fixed slits.
3b1ffcf0-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible ESO Multi-Mode Instrument on New Technology Telescope at La Silla Observatory

3b22ee2a-b81f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Akulivik Magnetometer is an instrument type used within the THEMIS Mission GMAGs, located at the Akulivik Geophysical Observatory. It measures magnetic field variations and has been operational since October 21, 2014.
3b22ee2a-b81f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Akulivik Observatory

3b2406d4-b996-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at Livingston Island, part of the IAGA network since 1997, used for measuring magnetic field variations.
3b2406d4-b996-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Livingston Island Observatory, Antarctica

3b258172-bb7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Cielo Profundo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bercianos del Páramo, León, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
3b258172-bb7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cielo Profundo Observatory, Spain

3b3acdf8-b930-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at AAB is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, designed to measure magnetic field variations as part of the MAGDAS observation network.
3b3acdf8-b930-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MAGDAS observation network

3b428d20-b806-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, particularly Earth's magnetic field. This specific magnetometer was operational at the IAGA station in Janow from January 1933 until December 1934.
3b428d20-b806-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy Investigation

3b4456b0-bc6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2.7m Telescope, also known as the Harlan J. Smith Telescope, is a 2.72-meter optical telescope located at McDonald Observatory in West Texas, administered by the University of Texas at Austin.
3b4456b0-bc6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.7m Harlan J. Smith Telescope at McDonald Observatory, United States

3b445980-ba3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Okutama Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in the Nishitama District of Tokyo, Japan. It is known for its ground-based observations and facilities.
3b445980-ba3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Okutama Observatory, Japan

3b482898-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Riometer is an instrument used to measure cosmic noise absorption, which is indicative of ionospheric disturbances. The AGO P4 Riometer Instrument is specifically located at the AGO P4 ground station as part of the ICESTAR observatory network.
3b482898-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Riometer at ICESTAR Observatory, Antarctica

3b530250-ba3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Richardson (RICH) Fluxgate Magnetometer is an instrument used at the McMAC Richardson station to measure magnetic fields. It operates as part of the Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain (McMAC).
3b530250-ba3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain

3b5c43de-b8ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Explorer 31 was an ionospheric observatory satellite launched by NASA in 1965 as part of the Explorer program. It carried seven experiments to make direct measurements of selected ionospheric parameters and operated until it was abandoned in 1971 due to lack of response from commands.
3b5c43de-b8ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Explorer 31

3b628f3c-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EISCAT Longyearbyen station is a ground-based observatory located near Longyearbyen on the island of Svalbard, Norway. It features a 32m steerable parabolic dish antenna, a 42m antenna aligned with the local magnetic field line, and other instruments like SPEAR radar and dynasonde for atmospheric and ionospheric research.
3b628f3c-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 32m Parabolic Dish Antenna at EISCAT Longyearbyen Station, Norway

3b66bc0e-bbbc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EISCAT Proton Imager is an instrument located at the EISCAT observatory in Tromsø, Norway, designed to capture images of protons in the upper atmosphere and ionosphere. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network and contributes to scientific investigations related to space weather and auroral phenomena.
3b66bc0e-bbbc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Proton Imager at EISCAT Tromsø Observatory

3b66c87e-bab9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Science Observatory is a solar research group based at the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ) in Mitaka, Tokyo. It operates ground-based instruments such as the Solar Flare Telescope and the New Sunspot Telescope for studying solar phenomena.
3b66c87e-bab9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: New Sunspot Telescope at Solar Science Observatory, National Astronomical Observatory of Japan, Japan

3b7172ca-b8bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tohoku University's 0.6m telescope at Haleakala Observatory is an optical telescope located in North America with a 0.6-meter aperture, part of the Haleakala Observatory on Maui, Hawaii.
3b7172ca-b8bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.6m Telescope at Haleakala Observatory

3b7d1196-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Mt. Wilson Geomagnetic Observatory (MWC), located in California, USA, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1926 to 1958, focusing on geomagnetic measurements and research.
3b7d1196-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mount Wilson Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

3b7e6328-b5fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cosmic Ray Subsystem (CRS)** on Voyager 2 is an instrument designed to detect and analyze cosmic rays and high-energy particles from the Sun and interstellar space, contributing to studies on their origin, acceleration processes, and behavior in various environments.
3b7e6328-b5fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cosmic Ray System part of Voyager 2

3b8428c4-ba64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pontianak Observatory is a ground-based facility located at the equator in West Kalimantan, Indonesia (0.00S, 109.36E), equipped with an MF radar to measure wind velocity in the equatorial mesosphere and lower thermosphere.
3b8428c4-ba64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Medium Frequency Radar at Pontianak Observatory, Indonesia

3b85df9c-b64b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) was a NASA space mission designed to test planetary defense by impacting the Dimorphos asteroid to alter its orbit. It successfully shortened Dimorphos's orbit by 32 minutes upon collision in September 2022.
3b85df9c-b64b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Didymos Reconnaissance and Asteroid Camera on Double Asteroid Redirection Test

3b8ebfd6-ba8d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2F magnetometer (TCM2) is a three-axis instrument designed to measure magnetic field components with high resolution for studying substorm activity and ULF oscillations during the investigation of relativistic electron losses.
3b8ebfd6-ba8d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL)

3b9d995e-b789-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Double Sphere" instrument on ISEE 1 was designed to measure quasi-static and low-frequency electric fields in various regions of space, including the plasmasphere, magnetosphere, magnetosheath, and solar wind. It utilized two vitreous carbon spheres separated by 73.5 meters to detect electric fields ranging from 0.1 to 200 mV/m with frequencies up to 1000 Hz.
3b9d995e-b789-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Double Sphere on International Sun-Earth Explorer 1

3bd57486-b5c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Nomad Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in Kochevanchik, Russia (L76), specifically at 12, Дорожная улица.
3bd57486-b5c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nomad Observatory, Russia

3bd73bd0-bb6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Gravelle Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Maurice, France, specifically at Pharmacie des Canadiens, Rue des Réservoirs, Joinville-le-Pont. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
3bd73bd0-bb6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatoire de Gravelle at Saint-Maurice Observatory, France

3bdaa080-bade-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: A magnetometer located at the IAGA station in Ebro, Spain, operational since 1905, used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of geomagnetic research and monitoring.
3bdaa080-bade-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ebro Observatory

3bdc7d5e-b743-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Munin is a Swedish nanosatellite designed for auroral research, launched on November 21, 2000, from Vandenberg Air Force Base. It was developed by the Swedish Institute of Space Physics in collaboration with students and carried instruments to study electron-ion spectra and high energy particles, as well as a camera to image auroras.
3bdc7d5e-b743-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Munin Earth observation satellite part of Munin Mission

3bdcc040-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Carpe-Noctem Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Navacerrada, Community of Madrid, Spain. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is situated at Paseo de la Maliciosa, Reajo del Roble, Collado Mediano.
3bdcc040-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Carpe-Noctem Observatory at Madrid Observatory, Spain

3be01f3c-b7b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2N was a high-altitude scientific payload launched on January 18, 2014, and operated until January 19, 2014, in the Earth's stratosphere to study the loss of relativistic electrons from the radiation belts. It was part of NASA's BARREL mission, which complemented observations from the Van Allen Probes spacecraft.
3be01f3c-b7b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of NASA Living with a Star, Geospace Mission of Opportunity

3beab07a-bae2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Drake University Observatory (Q114659341) is an astronomical observatory located at Waveland Golf Course in Des Moines, Iowa, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and education.
3beab07a-bae2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Des Moines Observatory

3bf037d4-b86c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Biaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 5 was a spinning twin-fluxgate magnetometer designed to measure the orthogonal components of Earth's magnetic field, with a range of +/- 400 nT and a resolution of 0.1 nT over a smaller range. It operated as part of the GOES 5 satellite observatory.
3bf037d4-b86c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Biaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 5

3c0ecd16-b97a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A "spacecraft" is an engineered vehicle designed for travel and operation in the vacuum of outer space, typically used for scientific research, exploration, or communication purposes. It serves as a host to various instruments and systems essential for its missions.
3c0ecd16-b97a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft

3c252c24-b5e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AE-E Backscatter Ultraviolet Spectrometer (BUV) was an instrument on the Atmospheric Explorer-E satellite that monitored atmospheric ozone by measuring UV radiation backscattered from Earth's atmosphere using a spectrometer and a photometer.
3c252c24-b5e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Backscatter Ultraviolet Spectrometer on Atmospheric Explorer E

3c252ef2-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Isafjordur station in Iceland was a ground-based geomagnetic observatory that operated from 1984 to 1989 as part of a collaborative study with Syowa Station, Antarctica.
3c252ef2-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Isafjordur Observatory, Iceland

3c262ed6-b75c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory (SAO) and Academia Sinica Institute of Astronomy and Astrophysics (ASIAA)'s 12m Greenland Radio Telescope is a radio telescope located in North America with an aperture of 12 meters, designed for astronomical observations.
3c262ed6-b75c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 12.0m radio Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory and Academia Sinica Institute of Astronomy and Astrophysics's Greenland Radio Telescope

3c2910c6-b796-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Omnidirectional Plasma Sensor Faraday Cups (VDP) on Interball Tail Probe is an instrument designed to measure the integral flux vector or energetic spectrum of ions and electrons in magnetospheric plasma within the energy range of 0.2 - 2.4 keV, utilizing six Faraday cups with a wide field of view for omnidirectional sensing.
3c2910c6-b796-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Omnidirectional Plasma Sensor Faraday Cups part of Interball Tail Probe

3c294694-bbb1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Euclid**: A space telescope developed by the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Euclid Consortium to map the geometry and expansion history of the universe, particularly focusing on understanding dark energy and dark matter.
3c294694-bbb1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Euclid

3c2b2866-bb88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Tsukioka-shin, Toyama Prefecture, Japan. It is known as the Toyama Observatory and has an MPC ID of 908.
3c2b2866-bb88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Toyama Observatory, Japan

3c2d80be-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Black Birch Astrometric Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Marlborough District of New Zealand, known for its ground-based observations and affiliation with Carter Observatory.
3c2d80be-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Carter Observatory, New Zealand

3c34fb02-b958-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Kap Tobin Geomagnetic Observatory (KTG) was a ground-based facility located in Uunarteq, Sermersooq, Greenland, that operated from 1959 to 1967 to monitor geomagnetic activity.
3c34fb02-b958-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kap Tobin Geomagnetic Observatory

3c40c59a-b778-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Bar Gyora Geomagnetic Observatory (BGY) was a ground-based facility in Israel dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity, operational from 1989 to 1996.
3c40c59a-b778-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bar Gyora Geomagnetic Observatory, Israel

3c531068-bb44-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Urania Observatory is a ground-based observatory located in Aalborg, Denmark. It was established on January 1, 1988 and is situated at 13 Borgmester Jørgensens Vej in the North Denmark Region.
3c531068-bb44-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Urania Observatory, Denmark

3c53f938-bb80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Vatican Advanced Technology Telescope (VATT)** is a 1.8-meter optical telescope operated by the Vatican Observatory Research Group, located at the Mount Graham International Observatory in North America.
3c53f938-bb80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.8m optical Vatican Observatory Research Group Alice P. Lennon Vatican Advanced Technology Telescope at Mount Graham International Observatory

3c66dd4a-b8cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Dynamics Explorer 2 Positions" is a dataset that provides the spatial coordinates of the Dynamics Explorer 2 spacecraft in different reference frames.
3c66dd4a-b8cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft Position Instrument part of Dynamics Explorer 2

3c6a611c-b79f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer that was operational from January 1974 to December 1979 at the Tevriz station, part of the IAGA investigation and the WDC Kyoto observatory.
3c6a611c-b79f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers part of World Data Centre for Geomagnetism Kyoto

3c6e7c70-b7d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: Kaguya (formerly SELENE) was a Japanese lunar orbiter spacecraft launched in 2007 to conduct comprehensive studies of the Moon's topography, mineralogy, gravity, and plasma environment.
3c6e7c70-b7d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Kaguya spacecraft

3c84f8cc-b65c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA-identified Gauss station, part of the observatory network since 1902, used for measuring magnetic fields and contributing to geomagnetic research within the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigations.
3c84f8cc-b65c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Gauss Station Observatory

3c85974c-ba75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Dynamics Explorer 1 Positions" dataset provides the spatial coordinates of the Dynamics Explorer 1 spacecraft in different reference frames.
3c85974c-ba75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dynamics Explorer 1 Positions part of Dynamics Explorer 1

3c874ff4-bb1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to magnetometers located at the Magallanes observatory, which are part of the IUGONET-Observatory network and contribute data to the World Data Centre (WDC) for Geomagnetism in Kyoto.
3c874ff4-bb1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Magallanes Observatory

3c923e18-bc9e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Opportunity (Mars Exploration Rover - B)** was a NASA robotic rover active on Mars from 2004 until 2018, launched to explore the planet's geology and search for signs of past water activity.
3c923e18-bc9e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Opportunity part of Mars Exploration Rover

3ca3a4b4-ba78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AGO P2 SearchCoil Instrument is a device located at the AGO P2 ground station, designed to conduct magnetic field measurements as part of the ICESTAR observatory.
3ca3a4b4-ba78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil on International Conjugate for Evening Surface TrougH And Relativistic Electron Currents Observational Regional-network ground station

3ca7cce8-b946-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF valley antenna is a triangular-shaped instrument located in Kagoshima, Japan, used for observing very low frequency (VLF) and extremely low frequency (ELF) signals from 1976 to 2001.
3ca7cce8-b946-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Low Frequency/Extremely Low Frequency valley antenna part of IUGONET Observatory

3caa92f2-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The European Southern Observatory Danish 1.54m Telescope is an optical telescope with a 1.54-meter aperture located at the La Silla Observatory in South America. It is operated by the European Southern Observatory and primarily used for optical astronomy observations.
3caa92f2-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.54m Telescope at La Silla Observatory

3cacc738-bb4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pioneer Venus Large Probe Differential Long Baseline Interferometer was an experiment that used interferometry techniques on radio signals from entry probes and a bus to measure wind speeds in Venus' lower atmosphere, aiding the modeling of its atmospheric circulation patterns.
3cacc738-bb4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Differential Long-Baseline Interferometer part of Pioneer Venus Probe

3cb0fed2-b8f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) Balloon 1I Data Processing Unit (DPU)** is a versatile instrument controller board designed to collect and process data from various sensors, including an X-ray spectrometer and magnetometer, and transmit this information via an Iridium modem. It utilizes an FPGA for flexible interface logic and has been successfully deployed on multiple sounding rocket experiments and balloon flights.
3cb0fed2-b8f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

3ccf3baa-ba83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Asiago Astrophysical Observatory is an Italian astronomical observatory operated by the University of Padua, located on the plateau of Asiago.
3ccf3baa-ba83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.82m Copernico Telescope at Asiago Astrophysical Observatory, Italy

3cd6fec6-b6f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Heavenly Owl Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Velykodolynske, Ukraine. It is a ground-based facility used for sky observations and research.
3cd6fec6-b6f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heavenly Owl Observatory, Ukraine

3cd987fc-b8b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Calern Observatory, also known as the "Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur" in France, is an astronomical facility equipped with a 0.25m TAROT telescope designed for rapid action and observation of transient objects.
3cd987fc-b8b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.25m Rapid Action Tarot Telescope for Transient Objects at Calern Observatory

3cdbeed8-baef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Navigation Camera (ONC) system onboard the Hayabusa2 spacecraft includes one telescopic camera and two wide-angle cameras, designed for multi-band imaging in visible and near-infrared ranges.
3cdbeed8-baef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Navigation Camera on Hayabusa2

3cde8cce-b91e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Fort Churchill Geophysical Observatory used in the THEMIS Mission GMAG to measure magnetic fields. It has been operational since January 1957 and is part of the ground-based observatory network.
3cde8cce-b91e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fort Churchill Observatory

3ceaada4-bac4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2.12-m Ritchey-Chretien reflector is a telescope located at the National Astronomical Observatory in Ensenada, Mexico, situated on the summit of the San Pedro Martir Sierra with an altitude of approximately 2800 meters and an aperture of 2.12 meters.
3ceaada4-bac4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.12m Ritchey-Chretien Reflector at Observatorio Astronomico Nacional - San Pedro Martir, Mexico

3ceb0936-b94b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The entity refers to magnetometers located at the Seykha observatory in Kyoto, which were operational from January 1, 1973, to December 31, 1980, as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigation.
3ceb0936-b94b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy

3cfc8a40-b76f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Small Astronomy Satellite 3 (SAS 3)** was a NASA X-ray astronomy space telescope operational from May 1975 to April 1979, designed to study celestial sources in the X-ray spectrum.
3cfc8a40-b76f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: x-ray Small Astronomy Satellite 3 part of Explorer Program

3cfe6722-bbaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Koksijde Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Koksijde, Belgium, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial bodies.
3cfe6722-bbaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Koksijde Observatory, Belgium

3d06a9e8-b8b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MASTER-IAC Observatory, located in Güímar, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain, is an astronomical observatory situated on the ground for conducting celestial observations.
3d06a9e8-b8b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: MASTER-IAC Observatory, Tenerife, Spain

3d079686-b62c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Electron Proton Telescope (SEPT) is a particle detector aboard STEREO-A that measures electrons and protons within specific energy ranges, providing anisotropy information through multiple fields of view. It consists of two dual telescopes positioned to observe different directions relative to the ecliptic plane.
3d079686-b62c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Electron Proton Telescope part of In-Situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients on STEREO A

3d102360-ba1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SAMBA Magnetometer Array's Fluxgate Magnetometer in Puerto Natales is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at this geomagnetic observatory.
3d102360-ba1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer at Puerto Natales Observatory

3d105d5e-bae9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Okina relay subsatellite (RSAT) was part of the Kaguya mission and served as a communication relay for studying the Moon's gravity field.
3d105d5e-bae9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Okina part of Kaguya mission

3d12db70-b5d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The White-light All-sky Watec Imager (AWI) at Tromso, Norway is an automated optical instrument featuring a CCD camera and fisheye lens used for all-sky imaging.
3d12db70-b5d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: White-light All-sky Watec Imager at Tromso Observatory, Norway

3d156674-b895-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Lwiro observatory used from 1958 to 1970 for geomagnetic field measurements.
3d156674-b895-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lwiro Observatory

3d1aafc6-bb79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tajimi Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Tajimi, Gifu Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID 901.
3d1aafc6-bb79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tajimi Observatory, Japan

3d2b7b26-b90d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lakeland Astronomical Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at Lakeland Community College in Kirtland, Ohio, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
3d2b7b26-b90d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lakeland Astronomical Observatory

3d33b45a-b8bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kouba Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Kouba, Algeria, known for its ground-based observations and contributions to astrophysics.
3d33b45a-b8bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kouba Observatory, Algeria

3d40349c-b810-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **La Palma-NEON Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Garafía, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility focused on astronomical research and observation.
3d40349c-b810-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: La Palma-NEON Observatory, Spain

3d4bf52a-b6d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MOMA Observatory (L94) is an astronomical observatory located in Oviedo, Spain, known for its ground-based observation facilities.
3d4bf52a-b6d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Oviedo Observatory, Spain

3d4c1b7e-ba11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Pitlekayah is a ground-based magnetometer observatory located in the Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, Far Eastern Federal District of Russia. It has been operational since 1879 and contributes to geomagnetic monitoring as part of the IAGA observatory network.
3d4c1b7e-ba11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pitlekaya Observatory, Russia

3d4e204a-b7dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Rosalind Franklin rover** is a planned robotic Mars rover developed as part of the international ExoMars programme led by the European Space Agency (ESA), named after British chemist and DNA research pioneer Rosalind Franklin.
3d4e204a-b7dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rosalind Franklin part of ExoMars

3d535268-bab6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Attu Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation since 2007.
3d535268-bab6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission

3d5934e4-b633-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Television System (TVS) on Vega 1 was an imaging instrument consisting of two telescopes designed for high-resolution and tracking purposes during the spacecraft's comet encounter.
3d5934e4-b633-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Television System on Vega 1

3d5d4c4a-b7e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DSCOVR Solar Wind Monitor is an instrument onboard the Deep Space Climate Observatory (DSCOVR) spacecraft that provides ephemeris data, including information about the spacecraft's position, orbit, and attitude.
3d5d4c4a-b7e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Instrument for Spacecraft Ephemeris, Orbit and Attitude on Deep Space Climate Observatory

3d6bfa40-b910-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Santiago-San Bernardo Observatory** is an astronomical facility located at Base Aérea El Bosque in the Santiago Metropolitan Region of Chile. It operates as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
3d6bfa40-b910-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Santiago-San Bernardo Observatory, Chile

3d73db0e-bca1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Changchun Geomagnetic Observatory (CNH)** is a ground-based facility located in Changchun City, Jilin, China, that operates a magnetometer to monitor geomagnetic activity. It has been operational since 1957 and is part of the IAGA observatory network.
3d73db0e-bca1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Changchun Geomagnetic Observatory

3d7a34da-ba18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cedar Drive Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Shawano County, Wisconsin, known for its ground-based observations.
3d7a34da-ba18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pulaski Observatory, United States

3d7df97c-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Energetic Particle Detectors from KS-18-M" on the Granat spacecraft are instruments designed to monitor fluxes of charged particles in interplanetary space and can also detect solar x-rays. They feature dual sensor blocks with various types of solid state detectors (SSDs) and gas-discharge counters, providing continuous measurements and different time resolutions for data collection.
3d7df97c-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Particle Detector part of Granat Mission

3d86121a-b945-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Güímar Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Santa Úrsula, Canary Islands, Spain. It is situated at Calle la Raya, La Raya, Guaza, Güímar, and focuses on ground-based observations of celestial objects.
3d86121a-b945-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Guimar Observatory, Spain

3d97f9c0-b5a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **GeoForschungsZentrum** (GFZ) operates the Adolf-Schmidt-Observatory for Geomagnetism in Niemegk, Germany, managing and supporting geomagnetic observatories globally through various national and international collaborations.
3d97f9c0-b5a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Adolf Schmidt Observatory for Geomagnetism at GeoForschungsZentrum

3da67980-b6b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2.6m Grigory Shajn Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Crimean Astrophysical Observatory in Europe, known for its aperture of 2.6 meters and used for astronomical research.
3da67980-b6b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.6m Grigory Shajn Telescope at Crimean Astrophysical Observatory

3da6f0bc-b985-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rosetta spacecraft is a complex mission designed to explore the comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko, originally intended for the comet Wirtanen. The design incorporates several sophisticated scientific instruments and subsystems tailored for long-term interplanetary travel and close observation of an irregular celestial body with a weak gravity field. The spacecraft is structured around a central box-type frame measuring 2.8m x 2.1m x 2.0m, featuring two solar panels with a combined area of 64 m² that can extend up to 32.7m tip to tip. It is divided into the Payload Support Module (PSM) for scientific equipment and the Bus Support Module (BSM) for platform and avionic components, with the Lander attached to the rear face. The spacecraft attitude allows continuous shading of specific panels during all mission phases to minimize cometary dust effects.
3da6f0bc-b985-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rosetta Spacecraft on International Rosetta Mission

3dabf7e6-b891-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover ChemCam Remote Micro-Imager (RMI) is an instrument suite on the rover that provides high-resolution context imaging at metric distances, complemented by a Laser Induced Breakdown Spectrometer (LIBS), to analyze Martian rock and soil composition.
3dabf7e6-b891-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Remote Micro-Imager on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

3db19c78-b6b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Case Western Reserve University Burrell Schmidt is an optical telescope located at the Warner and Swasey Observatory in North America.
3db19c78-b6b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Burrell Schmidt Telescope at Warner and Swasey Observatory

3db5af96-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NOAA 11 spacecraft was a third-generation operational meteorological satellite launched on September 24, 1988. It carried instruments like the AVHRR and TOVS for measuring atmospheric conditions, cloud cover, and ozone distributions, supporting both environmental monitoring and search and rescue missions.
3db5af96-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer and TIROS Operational Vertical Sounder and Solar Backscatter Ultraviolet Spectrometer on NOAA 11

3dbe7484-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bucharest Astronomical Institute is a ground observatory that includes the Big Data for Small Bodies 0.25m Telescope, used for astronomical research and observation.
3dbe7484-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.25m Telescope at Bucharest Astronomical Institute

3dcf9abe-ba73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **GTC OSIRIS Optical Imager and Spectrograph**: A versatile instrument on the Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) designed for optical imaging and spectroscopy, covering wavelengths from 0.365 to 1.05 microns with various modes including broad-band imaging, fast photometry, long-slit spectroscopy, and multi-object spectroscopy.
3dcf9abe-ba73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical System for Imaging and Low-Intermediate Resolution Integrated Spectroscopy on Gran Telescopio Canarias

3dd28282-bb37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Igloolik (IGLO) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based research facility located in the Qikiqtaaluk Region, Nunavut, Canada. It operates a magnetometer and began operations on October 9, 2008.
3dd28282-bb37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Igloolik Geophysical Observatory, Canada

3dd2d03e-b9e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: NOAA 15, also known as NOAA-K before launch, was an operational polar orbiting meteorological satellite operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), designed to monitor Earth's atmosphere, surface, and cloud cover.
3dd2d03e-b9e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Polar Operational Environmental Satellite NOAA 15

3dd5199c-bb92-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Neutral Particle Detector known as the Neutral Atom Detection Unit (NUADU) is an instrument onboard Double Star 2 designed to detect neutral atoms in space.
3dd5199c-bb92-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutral Particle Detector part of Double Star 2

3dd9dba2-b71a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Photoelectron Spectrometer (PES)** on AE-D was an instrument designed to measure the intensity, angular distribution, energy spectrum, and net flows of electrons in the thermosphere with energies between 1 and 500 eV. It featured two hemispherical electrostatic analyzers and offered multiple operating modes for detailed electron measurements.
3dd9dba2-b71a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer part of Photoelectron Spectrometer on AE-D

3ddd309a-b643-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Shed of Science South observatory (code: V61) is an astronomical observatory located in Pontotoc, San Saba County, Texas, United States. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
3ddd309a-b643-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Shed of Science South Observatory, United States

3de2999a-b67a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain (McMAC) San Antonio Station is a ground-based magnetometer observatory located in San Antonio, Texas. It is part of the McMAC network and operated by the Southwest Research Institute.
3de2999a-b67a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain San Antonio Station, United States

3dedc748-b832-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Bagdad Observatory (MPC ID: 714) is an astronomical observatory located in Bagdad, Yavapai County, Arizona. It functions as a ground-based observatory for astronomical research and observations.
3dedc748-b832-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bagdad Observatory, United States

3df25a4e-b8d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **El Maestrat Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Atzeneta del Maestrat, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial objects.
3df25a4e-b8d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: El Maestrat Observatory, Spain

3df2d56a-b870-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fluxgate Magnetometer (FGM) on Double Star 2 is an instrument designed to measure magnetic fields at a high sampling rate of 67 samples per second and is positioned at the end of a 3.5-meter boom for optimal data collection.
3df2d56a-b870-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Double Star 2

3dfdc92a-b613-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Coral Harbour Geophysical Observatory, located in the Kivalliq Region of Nunavut, Canada, is a ground-based facility that monitors geophysical phenomena and includes instruments such as a magnetometer.
3dfdc92a-b613-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Coral Harbour Geophysical Observatory, Canada

3e03f90c-b650-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CEASE (Compact Environment Anomaly Sensor) is an energetic particle instrument designed to measure radiation dose, surface and deep dielectric charging, and single event effects. It includes dosimeters and particle detectors capable of measuring electrons and protons within specific energy ranges, with flight heritage on the TSX-5 spacecraft.
3e03f90c-b650-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument Compact Environment Anomaly Sensor part of DSX

3e051292-b8c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LFRTO (Low Frequency Radio Transmitter Observation) is a vertical electric monopole antenna designed to detect radio frequencies ranging from 20 kHz to 100 kHz, operating as part of the IUGONET observatory at Saraburi station in Thailand.
3e051292-b8c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low Frequency Radio Transmitter Observation Antenna part of IUGONET Observatory, Thailand

3e165a32-bada-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Fluxgate Magnetometer for Average Fields (E3)** is a triaxial magnetometer onboard the Helios-B spacecraft, designed to measure magnetic fields with high precision and multiple ranges, featuring an automatic range switch system and periodic sensor calibration.
3e165a32-bada-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer for Average Fields part of Helios 2

3e18b2f2-bb14-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Interstellar Boundary EXplorer (IBEX) is a NASA research satellite designed to study the interaction between the solar wind and the interstellar medium using energetic neutral atoms.
3e18b2f2-bb14-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.95m Interstellar Boundary Explorer part of Small Explorer program

3e19bdb8-bbb0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 210MM Rikubetsu Station is a ground-based facility located in Rikubetsu, Japan, part of the ISEE/MM210 magnetometer network, designed for magnetic field observations.
3e19bdb8-bbb0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Rikubetsu Observatory, Japan

3e1bfbd6-bb4d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/F19, SESS Special Sensor Precipitating Electron and Ion Spectrometer 5 (SESS/SSJ5) is an instrument used to measure the transfer energy, mass, and momentum through the magnetosphere-ionosphere in Earth's magnetic field. It operates with four electrostatic analyzers that record the flux of precipitating ions or electrons at specific energy channels.
3e1bfbd6-bb4d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Precipitating Electron and Ion Spectrometer 5 part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

3e1d12be-b9b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: STPSat-1 is a Department of Defense (DoD) Space Test Program mission launched in 2007 to study the middle atmosphere and low latitude ionosphere, featuring two payloads: SHIMMER, an ultraviolet spectrometer, and CITRIS, for investigating irregularities affecting satellite communications.
3e1d12be-b9b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spatial Heterodyne Imager for Mesospheric Radicals on STPSat-1

3e1d4aa8-b860-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Santa Maria, Brazil, used for measuring the strength and direction of magnetic fields as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
3e1d4aa8-b860-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum-Pan Pacific Magnetometer Network investigation

3e25b4c2-b8c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ka-Dar Observatory** in Barybino is a ground-based observatory located in the Domodedovsky District of Moscow Oblast, Russia. It serves as an astronomical facility used for conducting various observations and research activities.
3e25b4c2-b8c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ka-Dar Observatory

3e294b36-b857-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The OWL-Net Observatory, located in Songino Khairkhan, Mongolia, is an astronomical facility dedicated to ground-based observations. It serves as a key site for studying the cosmos from Earth's surface.
3e294b36-b857-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: OWL-Net Observatory at Songino, Mongolia

3e43e186-b6b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DSS-12 34-m Radio Telescope, located at the Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex in California, was a key instrument for NASA's deep space communications and supported various missions from 1959 until its decommissioning in 2012.
3e43e186-b6b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Echo Station Radio Telescope at Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex, United States

3e4ce988-bbcc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Jovian Electrons and Ions (JEI) instrument is a sensor within the Particle Environment Package (PEP), designed to measure electrons and ions in Jupiter's magnetosphere. It was developed by the Max-Planck Institute for Solar System Research, Germany.
3e4ce988-bbcc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Particle Environment Package on Juice

3e4d830c-b5ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Port Foulke is a ground-based observatory facility in Avannaaata, Greenland, operated as part of the IAGA network. It has been functional since 1861 and includes a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements.
3e4d830c-b5ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Port Foulke Observatory

3e4f283c-bb32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at MUT is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument located in Muntinlupa, Philippines, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the MAGDAS observation network within the IUGONET observatory.
3e4f283c-bb32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MAGDAS Observation Network, Philippines

3e59604c-b95a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Siberian State Aerospace University Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at the Siberian State Aerospace University in Krasnoyarsk, Russia. It was established on April 10, 2009 and operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research.
3e59604c-b95a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Siberian State Aerospace University Observatory, Russia

3e6c987a-b6d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RPC magnetometer was a fluxgate instrument on the Rosetta Orbiter designed to measure magnetic fields with high precision and frequency. It featured dual sensors to capture three-dimensional B-field data at up to 20 Hz.
3e6c987a-b6d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: The Rosetta Plasma Consortium Magnetometer on Rosetta Orbiter

3e6d8f20-b7db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: ESA's Mars Express is a space mission launched on June 2, 2003, aimed at studying Mars from a polar orbit, focusing on high-resolution photo-geology and atmospheric composition mapping.
3e6d8f20-b7db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ValueSet(Value@MEX, Value@Mars Express)

40589180-b615-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Purcell Magnetometer Station (PCEL) is a ground-based facility located in Purcell, Oklahoma, USA. It is part of the Mid-continent MAgnetoseismic Chain (McMAC) and operates as one of its nine magnetometers to monitor geomagnetic activity.
40589180-b615-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain Purcell Station, United States

405fcbe4-b6ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The micro-indentation system (MCT^3) is a precision instrument used to measure hardness, elastic modulus, and deformation behavior of materials at the micrometer scale, suitable for testing diverse materials like meteorites, ceramics, and cement paste with various indenter tips.
405fcbe4-b6ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Micro Combi Tester

406867c0-bad1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **NOAA 8**: An advanced meteorological satellite launched in 1983 by NOAA to monitor Earth's atmosphere and surface conditions, equipped with sensors like AVHRR and TOVS, but experienced a premature failure in June 1984.
406867c0-bad1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer on NOAA 8

406c498e-baf5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Grahamstown, South Africa (URSI-code: GR13L), is a ground-based facility equipped with a Digisonde, which evaluates various properties of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere to study its characteristics.
406c498e-baf5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Ionospheric Station at Grahamstown, South Africa

4071f130-ba6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Georg Von Neumayer station is a ground-based observatory located in Antarctica, operational since January 01, 1983, which includes instruments like the magnetometer for scientific observations.
4071f130-ba6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Georg Von Neumayer, Antarctica

407b0838-b885-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SOAR Telescope is a 4.1 meter aperture telescope located on Cerro Pachón in Chile, known for its high-quality imaging capabilities across visible and near-infrared wavelengths.
407b0838-b885-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 4.1m Southern Astrophysical Research Telescope at Cerro Tololo Observatory, Chile

407c80aa-b894-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The PROBA-2 Thermal Plasma Measurement Unit (TPMU) is an instrument developed to study the ionosphere by measuring parameters such as total ion density, electron temperature, and ion composition. It operates using radio frequency probe techniques for electron measurements and Retarding Potential Analyzer (RPA) techniques for ion measurements, providing time-stamped data that can be correlated with satellite orbital position.
407c80aa-b894-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Thermal Plasma Measurement Unit on PROBA-2

40808d66-b7e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The North Pole 6 Geomagnetic Observatory (NPF), located in the Arctic at coordinates 83.6° N, 9.5° E, was a Russian ground facility that operated from 1957 to 1959, equipped with a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements.
40808d66-b7e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole 6 Geomagnetic Observatory

408c6a92-b94d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Zaria Geomagnetic Observatory (ZAR), located in Kaduna State, Nigeria, was an operational ground facility from 1964 to 1965 that monitored geomagnetic data as part of the IAGA observatory network.
408c6a92-b94d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Zaria Geomagnetic Observatory

40989afe-baee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Weizmann Astrophysical Observatory is a ground-based observatory located in Neot Smadar, Israel. It is situated at approximately 30.05297° N latitude and 35.04073° E longitude within the Beersheba Subdistrict of the South District.
40989afe-baee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Weizmann Astrophysical Observatory, Israel

409a0b20-ba06-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Suntopia Marina Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Orodani, Sumoto, Hyogo Prefecture, Japan. It operates as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
409a0b20-ba06-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Suntopia Marina Observatory

409aa4ce-b67b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SpectralPowerReceiver IGOR is a sophisticated instrument launched in 2006 as part of the COSMIC/Formosa Satellite Mission 3. It utilizes GNSS signals to measure atmospheric temperature and humidity through GPS radio occultation, offering high vertical resolution and precise spatial observations from low Earth orbit (LEO).
409aa4ce-b67b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Integrated GPS Occultation Receiver part of The joint Taiwan - U.S. Constellation Observing System for Meteorology, Ionosphere, and Climate Formosa Satellite Mission 3

409b4c44-b8e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Ørsted** is a Danish Earth science satellite launched in 1999 to study the Earth's geomagnetic field and perform global monitoring of high energy charged particle environments.
409b4c44-b8e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Ørsted

40a18432-b82f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CLPS Task Order 19D SCALPSS North East Short Focal Length Camera is an imaging device with a 5.4mm lens and narrow field of view, designed to capture video during lunar descent and landing to study plume-surface interactions.
40a18432-b82f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stereo CAmeras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies (SCALPSS) North East Short Focal Length Camera on CLPS Task Order 19D

40a22e52-b715-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT) 1.6m Big Bear Solar Observatory (BBSO), located in North America, is a telescope facility with an aperture of 1.6 meters, designed for optical observations of the Sun.
40a22e52-b715-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical New Jersey Institute of Technology Big Bear Solar Observatory Telescope at Big Bear Observatory

40b3b194-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wingst Observatory, also known as the Wingst Geomagnetic Observatory (WNG), was a ground-based facility in Germany that operated from 1939 to 2016, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
40b3b194-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Wingst Observatory, Germany

40b63a54-b987-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Rezman Observatory (MPC code A41) is an astronomical observatory located in Tunjiška Mlaka, Kamnik, Slovenia. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
40b63a54-b987-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rezman Observatory, Slovenia

40baba8e-b81a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tondano Geomagnetic Observatory (TND), located in Papakelan, North Sulawesi, Indonesia, is a ground-based facility sponsored by Indonesia for monitoring geomagnetic activity. It has been operational since January 1, 2001.
40baba8e-b81a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tondano Geomagnetic Observatory, Indonesia

40bd68d6-b95c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Heliospheric Imager-2 (HI-2) telescope is part of the SECCHI instrument suite on NASA's STEREO-B mission, designed to observe coronal mass ejections in the inner heliosphere from 66 to 318 solar radii.
40bd68d6-b95c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heliospheric Imager-2 Telescope part of Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigations

40be6812-b745-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
"BARREL Balloon 2A is a component of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) mission, designed to study electron losses from Earth's radiation belts using balloons equipped with scientific instruments in the stratosphere."
40be6812-b745-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star, Geospace Mission of Opportunity

40bf10a6-ba46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the Ionospheric Station at Tromsø, Norway (URSI-code: TR169), a ground facility equipped with a Digisonde that evaluates various properties of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere.
40bf10a6-ba46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Station at Tromsø Observatory, Norway

40c1cd62-b9a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 0.61m Helen Sawyer Hogg Telescope is an optical telescope located at the El Leoncito Astronomical Complex (CASLEO) in South America.
40c1cd62-b9a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.61m optical The 0.61m Helen Sawyer Hogg Telescope at El Leoncito Astronomical Complex

40d7474c-b65f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IAGA:MOH Magnetometer** is a magnetic field measurement device situated at the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) station in Mohe, China. It operates as part of the Space Mission Working Group Observatory to monitor geomagnetic activity.
40d7474c-b65f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy

40e0cb06-bbdb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Siding Spring-LCO A is an astronomical observatory located at the Coonabarabran Airport in New South Wales, Australia. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
40e0cb06-bbdb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

40e1d7c0-b71d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Observatorio ESTELIA in Ladines is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Sobrescobio, Asturias, Spain. It is situated at coordinates 43.20349° N and 5.81761° W (354.5553° longitude).
40e1d7c0-b71d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio ESTELIA, Spain

40e90c8a-b820-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "MMS3 Ephemeris" is a virtual instrument providing the positional data (ephemeris) of the MMS 3 spacecraft, part of the CDPP-AMDA observatory managed by CNES.
40e90c8a-b820-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Value Set on Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission Spacecraft part of CNES Observatory

40f53bc6-b6ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Dalat Observatory was a ground-based facility located in Da Lat, Lâm Đồng Province, Vietnam, operating from January 1, 1978, to December 31, 1992. It was part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network and focused on geomagnetic observations using magnetometers.
40f53bc6-b6ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dalat Observatory, Vietnam

40f99524-b991-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Heliospheric Imager-1 (HI-1) telescope is part of NASA's STEREO mission, specifically designed to observe coronal mass ejections and the inner heliosphere from 12 to 84 solar radii with a band-pass wavelength of 450-750 nm. It is one of the instruments in the Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigations (SECCHI) suite aboard the STEREO-B spacecraft.
40f99524-b991-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heliospheric Imager-1 Telescope part of Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigations

40fdbf5e-bac3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Vize Island Geophysical Observatory:** A ground-based research facility located on Vize Island in the Taymyrsky Dolgano-Nenetsky District of Russia, established in 2007 to conduct geophysical observations, including magnetometer readings.
40fdbf5e-bac3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Vize Island Geophysical Observatory, Russia

41082f7e-bba5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Purple Mountain Observatory, Yao'an Station is an astronomical observatory located in Yao’an County, Chuxiong, Yunnan, China, known for its ground-based observational facilities.
41082f7e-bba5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.8m Telescope at Purple Mountain Observatory, China

410e9610-b6d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Manila Geomagnetic Observatory (MAN)** was a ground-based facility in Manila, Philippines, that operated from 1889 to 1904, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements and research.
410e9610-b6d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Manila Geomagnetic Observatory

4128693c-b764-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Photoelectron Spectrometer (PES) on AE-E was an instrument featuring two hemispherical electrostatic analyzers designed to measure the intensity, angular distribution, energy spectrum, and net flow of electrons in the thermosphere within the 1 to 500 eV range.
4128693c-b764-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Photoelectron Spectrometer on AE-E

412d439c-b76b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Naval Observatory Flagstaff Station (NOFS)/Naval Research Laboratory (NRL)/Lowell Observatory Navy Prototype Optical Interferometer (NPOI) is an optical telescope located in North America, specifically at the Lowell Observatory's Anderson Mesa site. It is used for high-precision astronomical observations and research.
412d439c-b76b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical Naval Observatory Flagstaff Station and Naval Research Laboratory and Lowell Observatory Navy Prototype Optical Interferometer at Lowell Observatory, Anderson Mesa

412ff470-b61c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Nicosia, Cyprus (NI135) is a ground-based observatory equipped with an advanced ionosonde known as Digisonde. It evaluates angle of arrival, polarization, and Doppler frequency shift of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere, in addition to their travel time, providing comprehensive data for ionospheric studies.
412ff470-b61c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Nicosia Observatory, Cyprus

41343360-b931-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Umba Geomagnetic Observatory (UMA), located in Umba, Russia, is a ground-based facility dedicated to monitoring and studying geomagnetic phenomena.
41343360-b931-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Umba Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

41486060-b936-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Narssarssuaq station (NAQ), part of the IAGA network, operational since 1983.
41486060-b936-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Narssarssuaq Observatory

414ac08a-b66b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lunar Exploration Neutron Detector (LEND)** is a neutron telescope on the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) designed to map the Moon's neutron albedo, improving spatial resolution with collimated detectors.
414ac08a-b66b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Exploration Neutron Detector on Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter

4155f9a8-b712-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The magnetometer on Pioneer 11 was a triaxial helium instrument designed to measure magnetic fields with high precision and sensitivity, featuring seven dynamic ranges from ±2.5 nT to ±0.001 T and an accuracy of 0.5% of the full scale range.
4155f9a8-b712-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Pioneer 11

415783c2-bad2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Wave Detector (LFEW) on Double Star 2 is an instrument designed to measure and analyze low-frequency electromagnetic waves in space. It is part of the CNES Observatory CDPP Archive for the Double Star mission, contributing to the study of plasma physics and space weather phenomena.
415783c2-bad2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Wave Detector part of Double Star 2

4166815a-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Generic NICMOS IR Camera is an infrared imaging device used primarily for scientific and astronomical applications, featuring a Near-Infrared Camera and Multi-Object Spectrometer (NICMOS) to capture detailed images of celestial objects.
4166815a-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: infrared Generic Near-Infrared Camera and Multi-Object Spectrometer

4169aab2-b6d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1Q Ephemeris is a virtual instrument that provides trajectory positions of the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) in various coordinate systems. It is part of the BARREL observatory mission and focuses on studying relativistic electron losses in the Earth's radiation belts.
4169aab2-b6d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

416f3646-b9a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CCAT Trieste Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Trieste region of Italy. It is situated at La Fonte - Comunità Famiglia Onlus / Izvir - Skupnost družina Onlus, SP1, Altipiano Ovest, Campo Sacro / Božje Polje, and serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research.
416f3646-b9a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Trieste Observatory

416fc900-b7cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Texas A&M Physics Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in College Station, Texas. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial phenomena and conducting astronomical research.
416fc900-b7cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Texas A&M Physics Observatory, United States

41873ed8-b7de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Hermsdorf Magnetometer was an instrument located at the Hermsdorf Observatory, operational from 1901 to 1929, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IAGA investigation.
41873ed8-b7de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hermsdorf Observatory

418cf18c-bbd2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital receiver installed in Bangkok, Thailand, designed to measure ionospheric total electron content (TEC) using LEO satellite signals at 150 and 400 MHz. It utilizes GNU Radio software for signal processing and USRP hardware as the front-end.
418cf18c-bbd2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver GNU Radio Beacon Receiver part of Bangkok Observatory

4195e17c-b7e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometer at Dalian (DLN) was operational from 1990-01-01 to 1992-12-31 as part of the IAGA investigation and the IUGONET Observatory network.
4195e17c-b7e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dalian Observatory

41a19ac6-b608-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS FMCW observation network is a frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar installed at Sasaguri, Japan, used for atmospheric and ionospheric research. It operates under the IUGONET observatory within the framework of space physics and aeronomy.
41a19ac6-b608-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave Radar at Sasaguri Observatory, Japan

41aa011a-b901-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Americus Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Lyon County, Kansas, United States, equipped with a magnetometer for geophysical research. It has been operational since March 8, 2006 and is part of the McMAC observatory network.
41aa011a-b901-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Americus Geophysical Observatory, United States

41b01ee0-bb9c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA station identified as ARS in Arti, Kyoto, which has been operational since January 1973 and is part of the IUGONET observatory network.
41b01ee0-bb9c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Arti Observatory

41be51c8-bb73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Research Council (NRC) Herzberg Institute of Astrophysics 26m John A. Galt Telescope is a radio telescope located at the Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory in North America, featuring a 26-meter aperture and used for astronomical observations.
41be51c8-bb73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio National Research Council (NRC) Herzberg Institute of Astrophysics 26m John A. Galt Telescope at Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory

41d0eb52-ba5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ultraviolet Coronagraph Spectrometer (UVCS) on SOHO is a scientific instrument designed to study the solar corona and the acceleration processes of the solar wind. It measures key plasma parameters and spectroscopic data to understand the heating mechanisms and physical properties of the coronal regions that influence the solar wind.
41d0eb52-ba5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Coronagraph Spectrometer on Solar and Heliospheric Observatory

41d74768-b7c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Ayabe Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Satocho, Ayabe, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility used for observing celestial objects and phenomena.
41d74768-b7c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ayabe Observatory, Japan

41dbaf0e-b90f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 210MM Ewa Beach Station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Ewa Beach, Honolulu County, Hawaii, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) network.
41dbaf0e-b90f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ewa Beach Observatory, United States

41de0bea-b5fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sagastyr Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields and has been operational since 1883. It is located at the station with the IAGA identifier SAG as part of the IAGA investigation.
41de0bea-b5fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sagastyr Observatory

41e0042a-ba39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Doppler Wind Experiment (DWE) on the Galileo Probe was an instrument designed to measure the east-west winds of Jupiter's atmosphere by tracking the probe's radio signal frequency during its descent.
41e0042a-ba39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Doppler Wind Experiment part of Galileo Probe

41e8403e-b7a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The San Juan Observatory (San.Juan.1.2.3) is a ground-based facility in Bayamón, Puerto Rico, established in 1903 for geomagnetic research and includes a magnetometer as part of the IAGA observatory network.
41e8403e-b7a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at San Juan Observatory

41fa1be6-b8de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: AEROS (Aeronomy Satellite) was a German scientific satellite launched in 1972 to study the upper atmosphere and ionospheric F region, particularly focusing on the influence of solar ultraviolet radiation. It carried five experiments to gather data on particle temperatures, densities, compositions, and solar flux.
41fa1be6-b8de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: AEROS A

41ff0a88-b96b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Island Lake Canadian ground station, part of the CARISMA (Canadian Array for Real-time Investigations of Magnetic Activity) network.
41ff0a88-b96b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Island Lake Observatory

420273fa-b9dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The PS Observatory in Pârjol, Bacău, Romania, is a ground-based astronomical facility located at coordinates 46.57538° N, 26.61669° E.
420273fa-b9dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: PS Observatory, Parjol, Romania

420ba4b2-ba35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bradford Robotic Telescope (BRT) is an autonomous astronomical telescope situated at Teide Observatory in Tenerife, Canary Islands, owned by the University of Bradford and designed for remote use by schools and individuals globally.
420ba4b2-ba35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.35m Bradford Robotic Telescope at Teide Observatory, Spain

4216f280-b5b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Darwin Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor** is a specialized GPS receiver system located near Darwin, NT, Australia, designed to monitor and collect real-time ionospheric scintillation data for up to eleven visible satellites. It uses wide-bandwidth tracking loops to maintain signal lock during strong scintillation events and records detailed statistics for post-processing analysis.
4216f280-b5b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor part of Darwin Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor, Australia

42171338-b837-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Viking spacecraft were a pair of NASA probes, each consisting of an orbiter and a lander, designed to explore Mars. The orbiters carried instruments for imaging and atmospheric studies, while the landers conducted experiments on Martian soil and atmosphere, including searches for signs of life.
42171338-b837-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Viking Orbiter 2

421ee74c-bb53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 16 Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP) Lunar Surface Magnetometer (LSM) was an experiment featuring a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer deployed on the Moon during the Apollo 16 mission to study the electromagnetic properties of the lunar interior.
421ee74c-bb53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Surface Magnetometer on Apollo 16 Spacecraft

4222a11e-bb55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Emirates Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.
4222a11e-bb55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Emirates Observatory, United Arab Emirates

422c2c14-b5b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Back Geomagnetic Observatory (BKC) is a ground-based facility located in Manitoba, Canada, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity since 1978. It operates as part of the IAGA network and includes instruments such as magnetometers provided by Kyoto World Data Center.
422c2c14-b5b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Back Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

422ea2ae-b941-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** A magnetometer located at the IAGA station in Lazarev, operational from January 1960 to December 1961.
422ea2ae-b941-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Lazarev

424406b6-b780-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gretz-Armainvilliers Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Gretz-Armainvilliers, France, dedicated to ground-based observations.
424406b6-b780-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gretz-Armainvilliers Observatory, France

4264eab4-bb6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Carroll Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at Westmont College in Montecito, California. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
4264eab4-bb6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Carroll Observatory

426b7c2e-b905-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lajoux Observatory** is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Lajoux, District des Franches-Montagnes, Jura, Switzerland. It operates at coordinates 47.28111° N latitude and 7.13417° E longitude within Europe.
426b7c2e-b905-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lajoux Observatory, Switzerland

426c3eba-b74e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Washington Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field, operational from 1841 to 1894 at the IAGA observatory in Washington.
426c3eba-b74e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Washington Observatory

426fd31e-b626-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Spin-plane Double Probe (SDP)** is an instrument onboard the MMS 3 spacecraft, part of the FIELDS suite, designed to measure three-dimensional electric fields with high accuracy using four 48-meter wire booms equipped with spherical sensors.
426fd31e-b626-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spin-plane Double Probe part of MMS 3 FIELDS Suite

4271d372-b93b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Faint Object Camera (FOC)** was an optical and ultraviolet camera aboard the Hubble Space Telescope that operated at various resolutions to capture images in wavelengths from 122 to 550 nm. It was replaced by the Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS) in 2002.
4271d372-b93b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet and Optical Faint Object Camera on Hubble Space Telescope

4276a3d4-b7b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pierre Auger Observatory is an international cosmic ray observatory located in Argentina, designed to detect and study ultra-high-energy cosmic rays by utilizing a vast detection area of 3,000 km².
4276a3d4-b7b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pierre Auger Observatory, Argentina

4278332e-b84c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The STA-1600, 10.5x10.5k CCD is a high-resolution charge-coupled device with 10560x10560 9 µm pixels, designed for astronomical imaging and enhanced by the Imaging Technology Laboratories of the University of Arizona through thinning, passivation, and anti-reflective coating.
4278332e-b84c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: STA-1600 10.5x10.5k CCD

427b8400-baf1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory (STEREO) is a pair of spacecraft designed to study the Sun and its influence on the solar system, particularly focusing on Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) and their impact on Earth.
427b8400-baf1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ultraviolet NASA Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory

42a23362-bae6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Port-aux-Français geophysical observatory** is a ground facility located at Héliport Lapérouse in the Kerguelen Archipelago, French Southern and Antarctic Lands. It includes instruments such as the magnetometer part of the IUGONET network and has been operational since January 1957.
42a23362-bae6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Port-aux-Français Observatory, Antarctica

42a4454e-ba41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The PTF-100 Friability Tester is a precision mechanical device used to measure the resistance of particulate or granular materials to abrasion and fragmentation under controlled impact conditions. It features a rotating drum that simulates natural collisional disaggregation, conforming to USP standards but adapted for geological materials like meteorites.
42a4454e-ba41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: PTF 100 Friability Tester

42b6f540-ba82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at PTK is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed at St. Paratunka, Russia, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
42b6f540-ba82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum-Pan Pacific Magnetometer Network observation network
