42bded34-b9c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Beato Ermanno Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Impruneta, Florence, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility and is associated with the annual fair at Santa Maria Dell'Impruneta.
42bded34-b9c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Beato Ermanno Observatory, Italy

42c33b58-b685-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operational from 1960 to 1962 at the IAGA Norway Station, used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of ground-based observatory activities.
42c33b58-b685-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Norway Station Observatory

42c5f820-bb08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tesla Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Valdemorillo, Community of Madrid, Spain. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting various astronomical observations and research activities.
42c5f820-bb08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tesla Observatory, Spain

42d79fda-b68f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Deep Space Station 14 (DSS 14) is a radio telescope located at the Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex in Fort Irwin, California. It has an aperture of 70 meters and is used for both astronomical observations and communications with spacecraft as part of NASA's Deep Space Network.
42d79fda-b68f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 70m Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex Telescope at Goldstone Observatory, United States

42d92e30-bb3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ion Velocity Investigation** is an instrument on the San Marco-D/L satellite that measures relative thermal-ion velocity, plasma density, and ion temperature using a planar retarding potential analyzer. It determines ion angle of arrival and computes three-dimensional thermal-ion motion along the orbital path, with measurements taken once each spacecraft spin period (10 seconds).
42d92e30-bb3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Drift Instrument part of San Marco-D/L Mission

42da11aa-bab0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Osservatorio Astronomico Orciatico is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Via Mulini a vento, Orciatico, Lajatico, Pisa, Tuscany, Italy. It serves as a facility for astronomical research and observations within Europe.
42da11aa-bab0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Osservatorio Astronomico Orciatico, Italy

42e17c64-bab1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Maputo Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Maputo, Mozambique, on the Earth's surface, primarily known for its magnetometer instrument. It has been operational since January 1, 1980, and is part of the World Data Center (WDC) network.
42e17c64-bab1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Maputo Observatory, Mozambique

42e63c76-b7bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 12 Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP) Suprathermal Ion Detector Experiment (SIDE) was a scientific instrument deployed on the lunar surface during the Apollo 12 mission to measure the energies and masses of positive ions, including those from the magnetosphere, solar wind, and lunar atmosphere.
42e63c76-b7bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Suprathermal Ion Detector part of Apollo 12 Lunar Surface Experiments Package

42e83eb4-b6b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Gottolengo Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Gottolengo, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations.
42e83eb4-b6b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gottolengo Observatory, Italy

42ed5828-ba5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Apollo 12 Command and Service Module (CSM) was the spacecraft that orbited the Moon during the Apollo 12 mission in November 1969. It housed astronaut Richard F. Gordon while Charles P. "Pete" Conrad and Alan L. Bean landed on the lunar surface.
42ed5828-ba5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Command and Service Module on Apollo 12

42f07fbe-b79d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "IAGA:TAH Magnetometer" was an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at a ground observatory in Tahiti from January 1958 to December 31, 1972.
42f07fbe-b79d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tahiti Observatory

42f8a738-b8ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astrophysical Research Consortium (ARC) 3.5-meter telescope is situated at the Apache Point Observatory in Sunspot, New Mexico, featuring an altitude-azimuth mount and designed to host multiple instruments simultaneously for optical astronomical observations.
42f8a738-b8ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.5m Astrophysical Research Consortium Telescope at Apache Point Observatory, United States

4313f0e6-b182-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ussuriysk Astrophysical Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Gorno-Tajozhnoe, Russia, established on November 15, 1953. It specializes in ground-based observations and is part of the Institute of Applied Astronomy.
4313f0e6-b182-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Ussuriysk Astrophysical Observatory, Russia

43188332-ba00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Ksara station identified by IAGA as KSA, operational from 1930 to 1970.
43188332-ba00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory WDC Kyoto

4322187e-b628-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Orion-Colesanti Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Mairinque, São Paulo, Brazil. It is situated at the address Rua Orides Gemente, Sítio Kawazoe, with coordinates -23.56949 latitude and 312.78881 longitude.
4322187e-b628-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Orion-Colesanti Observatory at Mairinque, Brazil

4325d160-b83c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Juno Waves instrument, part of the Juno mission to Jupiter, is a waveform receiver designed to measure electric and magnetic spectral densities ranging from 50Hz to 41MHz and 50Hz to 20kHz respectively, capturing data in various intervals depending on its operational mode.
4325d160-b83c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: WaveformReceiver part of Juno

432b8e8e-b909-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Perth Observatory, located in Bickley, Western Australia, is a ground-based astronomical facility dedicated to studying the night sky and conducting various celestial observations.
432b8e8e-b909-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Perth Observatory

432f89e8-b653-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cerro Armazones Observatory is a ground-based observatory in Chile that includes the 1.5m Hexapod Telescope, operated jointly by Ruhr University Bochum and Catholic University of the North (UCN).
432f89e8-b653-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.5m Hexapod Telescope at Cerro Armazones Observatory

43423e20-bba9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Shandong University Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Weihai, China. It operates as a ground-based facility and is affiliated with Shandong University.
43423e20-bba9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Weihai Observatory, China

434df0e4-bc26-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Zeds Astronomical Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Lahore, Pakistan.
434df0e4-bc26-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Zeds Astronomical Observatory, Pakistan

434f6d54-b9ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Abbeydale Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Gloucestershire, England, used for ground-based observations of celestial bodies.
434f6d54-b9ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Abbeydale Observatory, United Kingdom

435447e8-bacb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kaliningrad-2 Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Ulyanovka, Kaliningrad, Russia. It has been operational since January 1964 and specializes in magnetometer measurements as part of the IAGA observatory network.
435447e8-bacb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kaliningrad Observatory, Russia

435ddc1c-bbad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ion Mass Spectrometer (BIMS) on the Pioneer Venus Probe Bus was an instrument designed to measure ion concentrations in Venus' upper atmosphere, providing data on solar wind interaction, photochemistry, and atmospheric transport characteristics. It operated using a Bennett ion spectrometer capable of measuring ions within a mass range from 1 to 60 atomic mass units (u).
435ddc1c-bbad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Mass Spectrometer on Pioneer Venus Probe Bus

435f34fc-bbdc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **NJIT Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located at the New Jersey Institute of Technology in Newark, New Jersey, dedicated to ground-based observations.
435f34fc-bbdc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Newark Observatory

4361d7e4-b7e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** LANL-97 is a classified geosynchronous spacecraft operated by the Department of Defense (United States) for surveillance and military purposes. It carries a Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer (MPA) to study energetic electrons and ions in Earth's magnetosphere.
4361d7e4-b7e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer on LANL 97A

4372ab30-b6ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Soroa Geomagnetic Observatory (SOR) was a ground-based facility in Candito, Cuba, operational from 1965 to 1967, dedicated to geomagnetic research.
4372ab30-b6ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Candito

437cca14-b5c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Magnetometers at Urumqi (WMQ) are located at an observatory identified by the IAGA code WMQ and have been operational since January 1, 1978.
437cca14-b5c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

43808806-bcad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Rio de Janeiro, operational from 1837 to 1910, part of the IAGA investigation and associated with the WDC Kyoto Observatory.
43808806-bcad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Rio de Janeiro Observatory

43858b96-b8eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument designed to measure magnetic fields with high precision and versatility. The MESSENGER mission's magnetometer utilizes a three-axis ring core fluxgate sensor mounted on a boom, capable of capturing data at various sampling rates and averaging intervals, while the Venus Express orbiter features two tri-axial fluxgate sensors to study magnetic interactions between Venus’ atmosphere and solar wind.
43858b96-b8eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Venus Express

438a2a3a-b8a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hydrogen Epoch of Reionization Array (HERA) is a radio telescope located in Africa, designed to study the epoch of reionization by observing hydrogen emissions from the early universe.
438a2a3a-b8a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio The Hydrogen Epoch of Reionization Array radio telescope

438be326-b8f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ESA TBT La Silla Observatory** is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in the Coquimbo Region of Chile, known for its contributions to European Southern Observatory (ESO) projects.
438be326-b8f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at La Silla Observatory, Chile

4393327e-b728-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Emmy Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in New Paltz, Ulster County, New York, United States.
4393327e-b728-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Emmy Observatory

4395c790-b7a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nephelometer for Pioneer Venus Small Probe (Night) was an instrument on the Pioneer Venus mission designed to measure energy backscattered from cloud particles using a solid-state pulsed laser and photodiodes, providing data on cloud presence and vertical extent along the spacecraft's trajectory.
4395c790-b7a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Small Probe Night Nephelometer on Pioneer Venus

43b121de-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 15 Lunar Surface Experiments Package Passive Seismic Experiment (PSE) was a component of the ALSEP deployed during the Apollo missions, featuring seismometers to monitor lunar seismic activity from 1969 to 1977.
43b121de-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Passive Seismic Experiment part of Apollo 15 Lunar Surface Experiments Package

43b4e410-b1be-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "OmegaLab observatory" (also known as OmegaLab Observatory or G16) is an astronomical observatory located in Palermo, Italy. It operates under the IAU Minor Planet Center and Wikidata listings, situated at the coordinates 38.10031 latitude and 13.34869 longitude.
43b4e410-b1be-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: OmegaLab Observatory, Italy

43bd03fe-b7b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Scott Base Magnetic Observatory is a magnetic observatory located in Antarctica that monitors and records the Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since July 1957 and is situated at an altitude of 10 meters on Williams Field Road, Scott Base, McMurdo Station.
43bd03fe-b7b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scott Base Magnetic Observatory, Antarctica

43c3a35a-bb01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Impactor Targeting Sensor (ITS) was a navigational instrument on the Deep Impact spacecraft's impactor, designed to guide it towards the comet. It was essentially a duplicate of the Medium Resolution Imager but without a filter wheel.
43c3a35a-bb01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Impactor Targeting Sensor on Deep Impact

43c5ab96-b6d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mount Abu InfraRed Observatory (MIRO)** is an astronomical facility located in India that includes a 0.5m telescope operated by the Indian Space Research Organization, designed for infrared observations.
43c5ab96-b6d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.5m Telescope at Mount Abu Infrared Observatory

43ce3aca-b720-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Johnstone Plasma Analyzer (JPA)** is a spectrometer instrument on the Giotto spacecraft designed to measure the three-dimensional energy distribution of positive ions to study interactions between the solar wind and ionized cometary particles.
43ce3aca-b720-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Johnstone Plasma Analyser Spectrometer on Giotto

43d0f26a-bb49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS magnetometer network at Tohno, Japan, is a ground-based facility located in Iwate Prefecture that monitors magnetic field variations on Earth's surface. It includes a fluxgate instrument and is situated at latitude 39.37 and longitude 141.6.
43d0f26a-bb49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at ICSWSE Observatory, Japan

43e1e422-baf3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at Cape Kamenniy (CKA), operational from 1973 to 1976, was an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IAGA investigation.
43e1e422-baf3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cape Kamenniy Observatory

43eb9098-b5f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** NASA's Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS) is a space mission designed to observe the Sun in ultraviolet wavelengths, specifically focusing on the interface region between the photosphere and corona. It aims to study how solar material and energy propagate through this crucial area of the Sun’s atmosphere.
43eb9098-b5f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph on NASA's Small Explorer Mission

43f5a3d4-bb90-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Inukjuak (INUK) Geophysical Observatory** is a ground-based facility located in Inukjuak, Quebec, Canada, primarily dedicated to geophysical research and equipped with instruments such as magnetometers. It has been operational since October 11, 2014.
43f5a3d4-bb90-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Inukjuak Geophysical Observatory, Canada

43fb8372-bc75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Entity Definition:** Explorer 43, also known as IMP-I and IMP-6, was a NASA satellite launched in 1971 to study interplanetary space and the outer magnetosphere by measuring energetic particles, plasma, and electric and magnetic fields.
43fb8372-bc75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Interplanetary Monitoring Platform I part of Explorers program

43fe0ebe-b953-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes the LANL1990, a geosynchronous spacecraft launched on January 1, 1990, designed to carry instruments for measuring energetic electrons and ions in Earth's magnetosphere and radiation belt.
43fe0ebe-b953-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geosynchronous spacecraft carrying energetic electron and ion instruments part of Los Alamos National Laboratory Observatory

440161c4-b9b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Energetic Particle Sensor (EPS) on GOES 13** is an instrument designed to measure energetic particles, including protons, electrons, and alpha particles, at geosynchronous orbit. It provides data crucial for operational alerts of hazardous conditions, assessing risks to satellites and astronauts, and improving radiation environment models.
440161c4-b9b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Sensor part of GOES 13

44070eb8-b8dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Honolulu Geomagnetic Observatory (HON) is a ground-based facility located in Ewa Beach, Hawaii, that has been operating since 1961 to monitor geomagnetic activity. It is part of the global INTERMAGNET network and is sponsored by the United States.
44070eb8-b8dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Honolulu Geophysical Observatory, United States

440da4ea-bb34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tevriz Geomagnetic Observatory (TEV), located in Tevriz, Omsk Oblast, Russia, was an Earth-surface ground facility that operated from January 1, 1974, to December 31, 1979. It was part of the IAGA observatory network and used magnetometers for geomagnetic measurements.
440da4ea-bb34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tevriz Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

440df9ca-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Neutral Atom Detection Unit (NUADU) on Double Star 2 is an instrument designed to measure energetic neutral atoms produced by the collision of energetic ions with cold neutral atoms, particularly focusing on those originating from the "Ring Current" belt in the magnetosphere.
440df9ca-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutral Particle Detector on Double Star 2

44124f6a-ba74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vector Electric Field Instrument (VEFI) on the Communication/Navigation Outage Forecasting System (C/NOFS) satellite is a multi-sensor experiment designed to measure AC and DC electric fields related to plasma shifts and irregularity development in the ionosphere. It includes three orthogonal electric field double probe antennas, a Langmuir probe, a fluxgate magnetometer, and an optical lightning detector.
44124f6a-ba74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vector Electric Field Instrument on Communication/Navigation Outage Forecasting System

441e1f28-b5cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Velikiye Luki Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Velikiye Luki, Pskov Oblast, Russia. It operates as a ground-based facility with the MPC ID C00.
441e1f28-b5cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Velikiye Luki Observatory, Russia

44388d8a-ba4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Hinotori**, also known as ASTRO-A, was a Japanese X-ray astronomy satellite developed by the Institute of Space and Astronautical Science (ISAS) to study solar flares during the solar maximum. Launched on February 21, 1981, its primary mission involved detailed imaging and spectroscopy of solar flare X-rays using rotating modulation collimators and a Bragg spectrometer.
44388d8a-ba4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: gamma-ray Hinotori

444e2f3e-ba7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Wind Electron Analyzer (SWEA) is an electrostatic analyzer onboard the MAVEN spacecraft designed to measure the energy and angular distributions of solar wind electrons and ionospheric photoelectrons in Mars' environment. It operates in two modes, providing detailed measurements with a 360° × 130° field of view and varying energy resolutions depending on altitude.
444e2f3e-ba7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Wind Electron Analyzer on MAVEN

4453420c-b972-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Equatorial Magnetometer Network's (EMN) 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer is an instrument located at the IUGONET Observatory in Eusebio, Brazil, designed to measure magnetic field variations.
4453420c-b972-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer at Eusebio Observatory

4455c932-bb3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "Krakau" refers to a ground-based observatory located in Świętego Wawrzyńca, Krakow, Poland, that operated from January 1, 1895, until December 31, 1936. It was equipped with magnetometers and was part of the IAGA observatory network.
4455c932-bb3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Krakau Observatory, Poland

44580650-b933-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Jovian Infrared Auroral Mapper (JIRAM) is an instrument on the Juno spacecraft designed to capture visual and thermal infrared images of Jupiter's auroras, featuring both imaging and spectroscopy capabilities in specific spectral ranges.
44580650-b933-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: infrared Jovian Infrared Auroral Mapper on Juno spacecraft

4466bd4e-ba96-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **DoubleStar2 (TC-2)** is a satellite launched on July 25, 2004 into a polar orbit to study the Earth's magnetosphere, focusing on energy flow from the Sun and physical processes over the magnetic poles.
4466bd4e-ba96-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: TC-2 Satellite part of Double Star Mission

447a29de-b761-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1-m Grubb reflector is a telescope located at the Crimean Astrophysical Observatory in Simeiz, Ukraine. It has an aperture of 1 meter and was operational from approximately May 1926 to around 1943.
447a29de-b761-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1m Telescope at Crimean Astrophysical Observatory, Ukraine

447fc560-ba36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wide Band Spectrometer (WBS)** on Yohkoh is an instrument consisting of three sub-instruments—the soft X-ray spectrometer (SXS), the hard X-ray spectrometer (HXS), and the gamma-ray spectrometer (GRS)—that collectively measure solar radiation from 2 keV to 100 MeV, providing detailed spectral data for studying solar flares.
447fc560-ba36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide Band Spectrometer on Yohkoh

447fecec-b9f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Zyryanka station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Zyryanka, Russia (latitude 65.75° N, longitude 150.78° E), part of the Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometer Network (CPMN).
447fecec-b9f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at CPMN Zyryanka Station, Russia

4484796a-bb18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **High Resolution Instrument (HRI) Infrared Spectrometer** was a component of the Deep Impact spacecraft, featuring a 30.0 cm classical Cassegrain telescope and a two-prism spectrometer designed to analyze near-infrared wavelengths between 1-5 microns with varying spectral resolution.
4484796a-bb18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared The High Resolution Instrument Spectrometer on Deep Impact

449691ba-bb84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The specific entity refers to the set of magnetometers operated at the White Shell observatory in Kyoto from 1977 to 1980 as part of the IAGA investigation, labeled as "Magnetometers at White Shell (WHS)."
449691ba-bb84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at White Shell Observatory

44a0743e-b7ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wyrick Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Haymarket, Virginia, United States. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with the code 935 and operates as a ground-based facility.
44a0743e-b7ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wyrick Observatory, United States

44a9c7ac-bae5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: GIRO (Global Ionospheric Radio Observatory) is a network of ground-based facilities equipped with Digisonde instruments that monitor and provide real-time data on the electron density in the Earth's ionosphere from over 60 locations worldwide. It offers open access to its data through dedicated web portals and software tools for analysis.
44a9c7ac-bae5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Global Ionospheric Radio Observatory Group

44c8dcca-bb8d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Trumbull Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in Trumbull, Connecticut, United States, identified by MPC code W72.
44c8dcca-bb8d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Trumbull Observatory

44c9c3ac-b9e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Solar Radiation and Climate Experiment (SORCE) is a space mission designed to observe solar radiation in the X-ray waveband. It aims to study how solar energy affects Earth's climate and atmosphere.
44c9c3ac-b9e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray NASA Solar Radiation and Climate Experiment satellite mission

44d3d7e0-b8ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Carbuncle Hill 0.35-meter telescope is a 35 cm Schmidt–Cassegrain telescope located at Carbuncle Hill Observatory in Coventry, Rhode Island, United States.
44d3d7e0-b8ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.35m Telescope at Carbuncle Hill Observatory, United States

44d79de4-b7ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A NASA PDS (Planetary Data System) context entity representing a spacecraft, identified within the VOParis-NS schema for observational facilities and instruments. It denotes a specific version (v7) of the spacecraft data model and is associated with related instrument entities also defined in the same schema.
44d79de4-b7ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft

44da0238-b6ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Kwasan and Hida Observatories of Kyoto University are astronomical research facilities located in Gifu, Japan, with the Hida Observatory situated at an altitude of 1275.0 meters.
44da0238-b6ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hida Observatory

44deee12-baa6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Canadian Space Agency (CSA) Microvariability and Oscillations of STars (MOST) satellite mission is an optical space-based telescope designed to study the oscillations and microvariability of stars.
44deee12-baa6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Canadian Space Agency Microvariability and Oscillations of Stars Satellite part of Canadian Space Agency Microvariability and Oscillations of Stars Satellite Mission

44e30ed4-b78b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The "ISEE2 Positions" dataset contains the recorded locations of the ISEE2 spacecraft in different coordinate systems, providing essential ephemeris data for scientific analysis and mission tracking.
44e30ed4-b78b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform on International Sun/Earth Explorer 2

44eb4406-b7a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Descent Imager Camera (MARDI) is a fixed-focus color camera on the Curiosity Rover designed to document its landing site and provide geological context for early operations.
44eb4406-b7a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Descent Imager Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

44f389de-ba2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Open-Source Neutral Mass Spectrometer** on AE-D was a double-focusing Mattauch-Herzog magnetic deflection mass spectrometer designed to study the thermosphere by providing in situ measurements of neutral atmospheric constituents with masses ranging from 1 to 48 atomic mass units (u). It operated using an impact ion source and featured multiple modes, including peak stepping and fly-through, to gather detailed data on chemical, dynamic, and energetic processes.
44f389de-ba2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Open-Source Neutral Mass Spectrometer on AE-D

44f4ab52-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The AJ4CO Dual Dipole Array and RadioJOVE receiver system is a ground-based instrument located at the AJ4CO Radio Astronomy Observatory in High Springs, Florida, designed for radio astronomy observations. It consists of two 25-foot long antenna elements separated by 20 feet, aligned to magnetic north, with a linear polarization and operates at 20.1 MHz with a 7 KHz RF bandwidth.
44f4ab52-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Dual Dipole Array and RadioJOVE Receiver System at AJ4CO Observatory

44f4fbce-b8ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA station in Tixie Bay (TIK), operational since 1957 and part of the WDC Kyoto observatory network.
44f4fbce-b8ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Tixie Bay Observatory

44fb39f2-b784-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Kilpisjärvi (KIL) Geophysical Observatory** is a ground-based observational facility located in Gálggonjárga, Storfjord, Troms, Norway. It has been operational since June 1983 and includes instruments such as an all-sky camera for monitoring geophysical phenomena.
44fb39f2-b784-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: All Sky Camera at Kilpisjarvi Geophysical Observatory, Norway

45031ede-bb98-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Visible Airglow Photometer (VAE) on the AE-D satellite was an instrument designed to measure volume emission rates of various dayglow, nightglow, and auroral optical emissions using two separate optical channels with different fields of view for high sensitivity and spatial resolution.
45031ede-bb98-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible Airglow Photometer part of AE-D

4506bf5e-b845-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The magnetometer at Nurmijarvi (NUR), operational since 1953, is part of the IUGONET Observatory and contributes data to the World Data Center in Kyoto.
4506bf5e-b845-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nurmijarvi Observatory

450cf57c-b14c-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "NOAA 12 Positions" refers to the positional data of the NOAA-12 spacecraft in various coordinate systems, part of the observatory's ephemeris dataset.
450cf57c-b14c-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of NOAA-12

4510296e-b731-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Deep Impact flyby spacecraft was a NASA probe used for the Deep Impact mission in 2005 and the extended EPOXI mission until 2013. It carried three scientific instruments and was notable for its encounter with comet Tempel 1, where it successfully delivered an impactor to study the comet's composition.
4510296e-b731-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Resolution Infrared Imaging Spectrometer on Deep Impact Flyby Spacecraft

45106f06-b73a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The New Horizons Kuiper Belt Extended Mission (KEM) is an exploration of the Kuiper Belt, featuring a close flyby of KBO Arrokoth and extensive surveys of other Kuiper Belt Objects to enhance understanding of this distant region of the solar system.
45106f06-b73a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: part of New Horizons Kuiper Belt Extended Mission

452b7ce8-bb6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Patacamaya Magnetometer is an instrument located at the IAGA-identified PTY station in Patacamaya, operational since 1983, used for measuring magnetic field variations.
452b7ce8-bb6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Patacamaya Observatory

45474d58-b7a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Dourbes, Belgium (URSI-code: DB049) is a ground facility equipped with an advanced Digisonde ionosonde that measures various characteristics of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere. Located in Wallonia, this observatory evaluates data such as angle of arrival, polarization, Doppler frequency shift, and travel time to study ionospheric conditions.
45474d58-b7a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Station at Dourbes Observatory, Belgium

454a298e-bb19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sydney Observatory** is a heritage-listed astronomical observatory and science museum located in Millers Point, Sydney, Australia. It was built between 1857 and 1859 and serves as an educational facility and function venue.
454a298e-bb19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sydney Observatory, Australia

4555bc7e-bb58-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wide Field Camera 3 (WFC3) is an astronomical camera on the Hubble Space Telescope designed to cover a wide field of view and a broad range of wavelengths from ultraviolet to near-infrared.
4555bc7e-bb58-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide Field Camera 3 on Hubble Space Telescope

4557fdb8-b919-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Old Orchard Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Fiddington, Somerset, England. It is a ground-based facility used for stargazing and celestial research.
4557fdb8-b919-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Old Orchard Observatory, United Kingdom

45603af8-b7e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Starkenburg Observatory Heppenheim Asteroid Survey (SOHAS) is an astronomical observatory located in Heppenheim, Germany, dedicated to the survey and study of asteroids.
45603af8-b7e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Starkenburg Observatory Heppenheim, Germany

45618b54-bb25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: SCALPSS is an imaging system designed to capture video during the descent and landing on the lunar surface, specifically used to reconstruct the effects of plume-surface interaction (PSI) through stereo photogrammetry. The East Short Focal Length Camera (SFL0), with a 3.37mm lens and wide field of view, is part of this system and pairs with SFL1 for comprehensive imaging.
45618b54-bb25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stereo CAmeras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies (SCALPSS) on CLPS Task Order 19D

4567626a-b9ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at EWA is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed at Ewa Beach, United States, used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of the MAGDAS observation network.
4567626a-b9ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System observation network

456a5cf6-b77a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Zephyrhills Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Pasco County, Florida, United States. It is a ground-based observatory used for stargazing and astronomical research.
456a5cf6-b77a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Quail Hollow Observatory, United States

456aef5a-b79c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Gnangara station with the IAGA identifier GNA, which is part of the IUGONET Observatory under WDC Kyoto.
456aef5a-b79c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

45783604-b618-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1T** is part of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) mission, designed to study electron precipitation from Earth's radiation belts using high-altitude balloons equipped with scientific instruments.
45783604-b618-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star Geospace Mission of Opportunity

4578f88c-b60e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gilgit Geomagnetic Observatory (GIT), located in Gilgit, Pakistan, is a ground-based facility that has been monitoring geomagnetic activity since 1967.
4578f88c-b60e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Gilgit Geomagnetic Observatory, Pakistan

4583db32-b6f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Microwave Instrument for the Rosetta Orbiter (MIRO) is a scientific instrument featuring two heterodyne radiometers operating at 1.3mm and 0.5mm wavelengths, designed to perform spectroscopic observations with high resolution and bandwidth capabilities.
4583db32-b6f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Microwave Instrument for the Rosetta Orbiter on Rosetta

458401c4-b89c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Gas-Plasma Environment-Dual Frequency Experiment (OGPE)** on the Pioneer Venus Orbiter was an instrument that used S-band and X-band radio signals to study lateral variations in Venus's atmosphere and ionosphere, analyze solar wind microscopic flow, and investigate solar wind scintillations.
458401c4-b89c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gas-Plasma Environment-Dual Frequency Experiment on Pioneer Venus Orbiter

45851f00-b699-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **1st Moscow Gymnasium Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Lipki, Moscow Oblast, Russia, established in 2004. It operates as a ground-based facility for scientific observation and education.
45851f00-b699-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1st Moscow Gymnasium Observatory

4594744a-ba32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wide-Angle Polarimetric Camera (PolCam)** is an instrument designed to capture polarimetric images of the entire lunar surface, except for the polar regions, at a spatial resolution of 80 meters from an altitude of 100 kilometers. It aims to study the detailed characteristics of lunar regolith.
4594744a-ba32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide-Angle Polarimetric Camera on Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter

4594789e-b8d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Osorno (OSO) Geomagnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Río Bueno, Los Ríos, Chile, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity since April 2002.
4594789e-b8d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Osorno, Chile

45952ed2-b639-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. This specific device, labeled "CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at MUT," is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed in Muntinlupa, Philippines, as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
45952ed2-b639-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum Pan Pacific Magnetic Network investigation at IUGONET Observatory

45ae23d8-b8fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Hisaki, also known as SPRINT-A, was a Japanese ultraviolet astronomy satellite operated by JAXA, designed to observe planets like Venus, Mars, and Jupiter in the extreme ultraviolet spectrum to study their atmospheres and plasma interactions.
45ae23d8-b8fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: extreme ultraviolet Spectroscopic Planet Observatory for Recognition of Interaction of Atmosphere

45aea4fe-b5b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Southern Auroral Electrojet (SAE) Index Instrument is a virtual instrument that aggregates data from multiple ground magnetometer arrays to measure the southern auroral electrojet index at 60-second intervals. It comprises contributions from various stations and arrays, such as SAMBA, RAM (Russia), UAPM (Japan), South Africa, Geosciences Australia, and BAS (British Antarctic Survey).
45aea4fe-b5b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Southern Auroral Electrojet Index Magnetometer part of Southern Auroral Electrojet Observatory

45b12a66-ba34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electron Proton and Alpha Monitor (EPAM) on the Advanced Composition Explorer (ACE) is an energetic particle instrument launched in 1997. It consists of five telescope apertures designed to measure the flux, direction, and composition of electrons and ions in space.
45b12a66-ba34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Proton and Alpha Monitor on Advanced Composition Explorer

45bd6b40-b954-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Davis Geomagnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Antarctica that conducts geophysical research and includes instruments such as ionosondes. It was established on February 1, 1985, and is situated at Davis Station with coordinates (77.967° E, -68.583° S).
45bd6b40-b954-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Davis Geomagnetic Observatory, Antarctica

45f24cec-b793-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Shenton Park Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Shenton Park, Western Australia. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting various astronomical observations and research.
45f24cec-b793-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Shenton Park Observatory, Australia

45f3a972-b5ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Energetic Particles Investigation (EPI)** instrument was part of the Galileo Probe mission, designed to study energetic particle populations in Jupiter's magnetosphere using a two-element telescope and multiple sensors.
45f3a972-b5ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particles Investigation part of Lightning and Radio Emission Detector on Galileo Probe

45f5b4c4-b606-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Heliosphere Instrument for Spectra, Composition, and Anisotropy at Low Energies (HISCALE) is an instrument on the Ulysses spacecraft designed to measure interplanetary ions and electrons, investigate solar flare processes, study solar elemental abundances, and analyze the propagation and acceleration of energetic particles in the heliosphere.
45f5b4c4-b606-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heliosphere Instrument for Spectra, Composition and Anisotropy at Low Energies on Ulysses

45f6e46e-ba09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **KANZ** instrument at the Kanzelhoehe Solar Observatory (KSO) in Austria produces H-alpha solar imagery, focusing on high precision full disk imaging of the photosphere to study sunspots, faculae, and chromospheric flares.
45f6e46e-ba09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: H-alpha Imager at Kanzelhoehe Solar Observatory, Austria

4600d756-bbc8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: GOES 6 was a geosynchronous operational spacecraft developed by NASA and operated by NOAA, primarily designed to provide high-quality day/night cloud cover data and monitor atmospheric conditions using various onboard instruments. It launched in April 1983 and remained active until November 1994, contributing significantly to weather forecasting and environmental monitoring.
4600d756-bbc8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible Infrared Spin-Scan Radiometer on GOES 6

460f9b48-ba05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is an open-source digital receiver installed in Nairobi, Kenya, designed to measure ionospheric total electron content (TEC) using LEO satellite signals, utilizing GNU Radio software and USRP hardware for signal processing.
460f9b48-ba05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver part of Research Institute for Sustainable Humanosphere and Ionospheric Ground Observation Network, Kenya

4618f1cc-b9b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Sant Celoni Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Sant Celoni, Catalonia, Spain, used for ground-based observations of celestial objects.
4618f1cc-b9b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sant Celoni Observatory

462a5280-b6c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Automatic Weather Station (AWS)** at the Biak observatory is a meteorological instrument operated by Kyoto University's Research Institute for Sustainable Humanosphere since 2008, measuring surface precipitation, temperature, humidity, pressure, and wind direction/speed.
462a5280-b6c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Automatic Weather Station part of Hydrometeorological ARray for Isv-Monsoon AUtomonitoring

462ab4de-b71f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The F. Schiller-Gymnasium Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Weimar, Germany, situated at 2, Thomas-Mann-Straße.
462ab4de-b71f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Weimar Observatory, Germany

462fd472-b955-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Science Foundation's (NSF) Daniel K. Inouye 4m Solar Telescope, operated by the National Solar Observatory (NSO), is a state-of-the-art optical telescope located in North America, designed for observing solar phenomena with an aperture of 4.0 meters.
462fd472-b955-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 4m optical Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope

4642c4f8-b69c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Generic GaAs High-Speed Photometer is a specialized light-measuring instrument using Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) photodiodes for rapid and efficient detection of light intensity, ideal for time-sensitive scientific applications.
4642c4f8-b69c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Generic GaAs High Speed Photometer

464435ce-bb9f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Equatorial Magnetometer Network's (IUGONET) fluxgate magnetometer at Maroua (MAR), Cameroon, is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument designed to measure magnetic field variations near the equator.
464435ce-bb9f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of The Equatorial Magnetometer Network

46447474-b8a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **South Wonston Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in South Wonston, Winchester, Hampshire, England, dedicated to ground-based observations.
46447474-b8a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: South Wonston Observatory, United Kingdom

46482936-b7a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Neutron Monitor observatory chain is a network of ground-based facilities on Earth's surface designed to measure neutron fluxes, which provide insights into cosmic ray intensities and solar activity.
46482936-b7a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutron Monitor at Huancayo Observatory

465d6582-b760-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Clavier Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Lora del Río, Sevilla, Andalusia, Spain. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial objects and phenomena from Earth.
465d6582-b760-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Clavier Observatory, Spain

4661bd4e-bb48-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Heavy Ion Telescope (HIT) on CRRES was an energetic particle instrument designed to measure the energy loss, incident ion energy, and time of flight of ions using a three-element solid state detector, providing unique determination of ion mass, elemental identification, and incident energy for H-Ar within the range of 100 keV to 15 MeV per ion.
4661bd4e-bb48-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heavy Ion Telescope on CRRES

46844240-b80c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Orbiter Atmospheric Drag (OAD) experiment was part of the Pioneer Venus mission, utilizing radio signals to study the Venusian atmosphere's thermospheric density variations and dynamics influenced by solar wind and UV radiation.
46844240-b80c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Orbiter Atmospheric Drag on Pioneer Venus

4687e3ae-b727-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: King Point is a ground-based observatory located in the Inuvialuit Settlement Region of Northwest Territories, Canada, primarily known for its magnetometer instrument used to monitor geomagnetic activity.
4687e3ae-b727-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at King Point Observatory, Canada

46922578-ba22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA/Johns Hopkins University (JHU) Far Ultraviolet Spectroscopic Explorer (FUSE) was a space mission designed to conduct high-resolution spectroscopy in the far ultraviolet waveband.
46922578-ba22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ultraviolet NASA Johns Hopkins University Far Ultraviolet Spectroscopic Explorer Satellite

469ae6b0-b7af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Space Environment Monitor-2 (SEM-2)** on NOAA 17 is an instrument designed to measure the population of Earth's radiation belts and detect charged particle precipitation in the upper atmosphere due to solar activity. It consists of two sensors: the Total Energy Detector (TED) for particles with energies from 50 eV to 20 keV, and the Medium Energy Proton/Electron Detector (MEPED) for higher energy particles up to several tens of MeV.
469ae6b0-b7af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Environment Monitor-2 on NOAA 17

469ef5be-b96e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite (LCROSS) Visible Spectrometer** was an instrument designed to measure visible light emission and reflectance spectrometry of the vapor plume and ejecta cloud resulting from a spacecraft impact on the Moon, focusing particularly on water vapor dissociation.
469ef5be-b96e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite Spectrometer on LCROSS

46a7bc00-b93f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Guam Station is a ground-based magnetometer network located in Dededo Municipality, Guam, United States, designed to measure magnetic field variations as part of the ICSWSE observatory.
46a7bc00-b93f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer Network at Guam Observatory, United States

46ab2bc2-b7e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko (C-G; P67) - Ephemeris is a platform used for the investigation of comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko, providing ephemerides data as part of the CNES observatory CDPP AMDA.
46ab2bc2-b7e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Comets part of CDPP AMDA Comet C-G Investigation

46af5078-b9e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Helios-2 E5A Plasma Wave Experiment** was an instrument aboard the Helios-2 spacecraft designed to measure electric field intensities in the solar wind plasma, with a frequency range from 31 Hz to 178 kHz. It utilized a 32-meter tip-to-tip electric antenna and a spectrum analyzer to capture key plasma frequencies between 0.3 to 1.0 AU.
46af5078-b9e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Wind Plasma Wave on Helios-2

46b5da5a-bc65-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ATLAS-MLO Auxiliary Camera (T07) is an astronomical observatory located at Mauna Loa Observatory in Hawaiʻi County, Hawaii, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility focused on astronomical observations and research.
46b5da5a-bc65-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ATLAS-MLO Auxiliary Camera at Mauna Loa Observatory, United States

46c042c4-b120-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at ONW is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed in Onagawa, Japan as part of the MAGDAS observation network.
46c042c4-b120-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MAGDAS Observation Network

46d2aa58-b667-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Yangi Bazar Geophysical Observatory**: Also known as Tashkent Geomagnetic Observatory, it was a ground-based facility in Uzbekistan that operated from 1957 to 2015, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
46d2aa58-b667-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tashkent Geomagnetic Observatory, Uzbekistan

46d3f4d2-b714-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The InSight Mars Lander Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL) instrument is a device on the InSight spacecraft that measured accelerations and decelerations during its entry into the Martian atmosphere and subsequent descent and landing.
46d3f4d2-b714-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Entry, Descent, and Landing Instrument on InSight Mars Lander

46d7e43c-bc9d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Yonsei Survey Telescopes for Astronomical Research (YSTAR)** is a former astronomical observatory located in Sutherland, South Africa. It was part of the larger Sutherland Observatory complex and specialized in ground-based observations.
46d7e43c-bc9d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yonsei Survey Telescopes for Astronomical Research at Sutherland Observatory, South Africa

46dc895c-bbd9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Taurus Australis Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Taguatinga, Brazil. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
46dc895c-bbd9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Taurus Australis Observatory at Taguatinga, Brazil

46e08262-bb6d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Arcangel Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Las Zocas, San Miguel de Abona, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to studying the night sky and conducting astronomical research.
46e08262-bb6d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Arcangel Observatory, Spain

46f4e510-b8b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Oaxaca Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in San Agustín Etla, Oaxaca, Mexico. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
46f4e510-b8b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Oaxaca Observatory, Mexico

46f9c60c-b6e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lyford (LYFD) Fluxgate Magnetometer** is an instrument at the McMAC Lyford station designed to measure magnetic field variations as part of the Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain investigation.
46f9c60c-b6e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain

46fd0464-b77b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electric Field and Waves Suite (EFW) on the Radiation Belt Storm Probe (RBSP) spacecraft is an instrument designed to measure three-dimensional electric fields and plasma densities in Earth's inner magnetosphere. It aims to understand the role of electric fields and waves in the acceleration, transport, and loss of energetic particles within this region.
46fd0464-b77b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electric Field and Waves Suite part of Radiation Belt Storm Probe

46ff68f2-b74a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 0.25m TAROT (Télescope à Action Rapide pour les Objets Transitoires) telescope is an optical instrument located at the Calern Observatory in Europe, designed for rapid response to observe transient astronomical events.
46ff68f2-b74a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rapid Action Telescope for transient objects and 0.25m Telescope at Calern Observatory

471b0266-b7c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Spin-Scan Auroral Imager (SAI)** onboard the Dynamics Explorer 1 satellite was an instrument designed to capture global images of auroras at visible and ultraviolet wavelengths, providing valuable data for studying auroral dynamics, magnetospheric plasmas, and energy deposition in the ionosphere.
471b0266-b7c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spin-Scan Auroral Imager on Dynamics Explorer 1

4723810a-bb4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The OMNI instrument is a virtual tool that consolidates data from various spacecraft magnetometers, electrostatic analyzers, and energetic particle instruments to create comprehensive datasets for studying the Sun and solar wind. It selects the best available data for each time period, acting as a proxy for multiple contributing instruments.
4723810a-bb4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument part of OMNI

47299426-b77f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Lowell Observatory, Happy Jack" refers to a ground-based observatory located in Arizona, USA. It includes the 4.3m Lowell Discovery Telescope (LDT), which is used for astronomical research and observations.
47299426-b77f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lowell Discovery Telescope at Lowell Observatory

472f4d4c-b641-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover's Front Hazard Avoidance Camera Left String B is one of the rover's navigation cameras used for obstacle detection and avoidance, as well as supporting science operations. It is part of a stereo camera system mounted on the front panel of the rover.
472f4d4c-b641-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hazard Avoidance Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

47364ccc-b7e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fluxgate Magnetometer onboard the ROSETTA spacecraft is an instrument designed to measure magnetic fields in the interaction region of solar wind plasma with comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko. It features two triaxial sensors with a high measurement range and resolution, capable of studying both cometary magnetic field variations and potential remnant magnetic fields of the nucleus.
47364ccc-b7e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of Rosetta Investigation

4737067c-b867-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Principia Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Málaga, Spain. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical observations and research.
4737067c-b867-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Principia Observatory, Spain

47469b56-bb1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF Kapuskasing station in Canada is a ground-based observatory equipped with a crossed loop antenna for monitoring very low frequency (VLF) and extremely low frequency (ELF) signals. It was established by Prof. Shiokawa of ISEE, with collaborations from Virginia Tech, and is located in Northeastern Ontario.
47469b56-bb1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VLF/ELF Kapuskasing Station, Canada

476283b6-bb68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) station at Resolute Bay, Canada, is a ground facility designed to study the upper atmosphere's dynamics through nighttime airglow emissions, developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research (ISEE), Nagoya University, in collaboration with SRI Ins. and U. Calgary.
476283b6-bb68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Resolute Bay Observatory, Canada

4762df36-bb0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Riometer (Relative Ionospheric Opacity Meter) is a scientific instrument used to measure the absorption of cosmic radio noise by the Earth's ionosphere. The Broad-beam riometer at Husafell, Iceland, specifically monitors these absorptions as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
4762df36-bb0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Riometer part of Conjugate Observation at Iceland

47645cb8-b726-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument that measures the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Purcell Magnetometer, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG, has been operational since January 1, 2007, at the Purcell Geophysical Observatory.
47645cb8-b726-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Purcell Geophysical Observatory

4767b920-b691-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1M** is a scientific investigation utilizing multiple balloons to study the escape of particles from Earth's radiation belts, focusing on measuring Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating relativistic electrons. It operates in conjunction with NASA's Van Allen Probes to enhance understanding through simultaneous observations in space and the stratosphere.
4767b920-b691-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star Geospace Mission of Opportunity

476fa96a-bb40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity represents a structured identifier for instruments and their associated products within the JAXA DARTS context, utilizing specific labels and value sets to ensure consistent categorization.
476fa96a-bb40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency instrument

477180c8-b8a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **St. George Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Cocoșești, Prahova, Romania (MPC ID: L15). It operates as a ground-based facility on Earth for conducting astronomical observations and research.
477180c8-b8a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: St. George Observatory

478b95c2-b6ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2A Ephemeris instrument provides trajectory positions in various coordinate systems, supporting investigations into relativistic electron losses as part of the RBSP mission.
478b95c2-b6ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform for Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

478f0a22-b9b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tokyo-Norikura Observatory (MPC ID: 382) is an astronomical observatory located in Katanokoya, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. It operates as a ground-based facility and is situated at coordinates 137.5553 longitude and 36.11377 latitude on the continent of Asia.
478f0a22-b9b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tokyo-Norikura Observatory, Japan

4797dfea-b8d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Special Sensor Microwave Imager (SSM/I)** onboard the DMSP-F15 satellite is a passive microwave radiometric system designed to measure atmospheric, ocean, and terrain brightness temperatures at multiple frequencies.
4797dfea-b8d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Microwave Imager part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

479fe23a-b887-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Elena Remote Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in San Pedro de Atacama, Chile. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial bodies and phenomena.
479fe23a-b887-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Elena Remote Observatory, Chile

47a36ff0-b59d-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lviv Polytechnic Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Lviv, Ukraine. It is associated with the Lviv Polytechnic National University and focuses on astronomical research and education.
47a36ff0-b59d-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Lviv Polytechnic Observatory, Ukraine

47aa117e-b733-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer (HPCA) is a mass spectrometer on the MMS4 spacecraft designed to measure the velocity-space distribution of ions with energies from 1 eV to 40 keV, providing detailed compositional data with high time resolution.
47aa117e-b733-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer part of Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer on Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

47ab5d2c-b6ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **CPMN fluxgate magnetometer** is a three-axis ring-core type instrument used to measure magnetic fields, specifically installed at Pontianak, Indonesia. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network and operates within the CPMN observation framework.
47ab5d2c-b6ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometers Network Investigation

47ad4758-b6b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Faraday Cup on the Parker Solar Probe's SWEAP investigation is a scientific instrument designed to measure ion and electron fluxes and flow angles from the Sun. It is part of the Solar Wind Electrons Alphas and Protons (SWEAP) investigation, which studies solar wind properties and their impact on space weather.
47ad4758-b6b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Faraday Cup on Parker Solar Probe

47b6d1b8-b18c-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: Yangwang-1 is a space observatory and telescope launched on June 11, 2021, designed for astronomical observations.
47b6d1b8-b18c-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Yangwang-1

47b8af52-b6db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Environment Monitor on GOES 11** is a Space Environment Monitor (SEM) System designed to provide real-time measurements of solar activity and magnetic fields from geostationary orbit. It includes sensors for detecting magnetic fields, solar X-rays, and energetic particles such as protons and alpha particles.
47b8af52-b6db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Environment Monitor System on GOES 11

47bf8b16-bb0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) All-Sky Imager at Gakona, Alaska, is a multi-wavelength instrument designed to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere by observing nocturnal airglow emissions.
47bf8b16-bb0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Multi-wavelength All-Sky Imager part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Investigation

47bfacd8-b8d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Elizabethville Geomagnetic Observatory (ELI) was a ground-based facility located in Lubumbashi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, operating from 1932 to 1957 for geomagnetic measurements.
47bfacd8-b8d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Elizabethville Geomagnetic Observatory, Democratic Republic of the Congo

47c13eec-baaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The BAS A84 Search Coil Instrument is a geomagnetic measurement tool located at the Augsburg observatory, designed to record low-frequency (<10 Hz) micropulsations in the Earth's magnetic field.
47c13eec-baaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil at Augsburg Magnetometer Array

47c4d226-b9c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Ion Velocity Meter**: A space instrument consisting of two planar thermal ion sensors, a retarding potential analyzer (RPA), and an ion drift meter (IDM). It is part of the ICON observatory and is used to measure ion velocity in space.
47c4d226-b9c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Velocity Meter on ICON

47d71928-b8fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: San Pedro de Atacama Ground Observatory (BOOTES-7) is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Orilla Solor, San Pedro de Atacama, Chile. It operates under the BOOTES network and is situated at latitude -22.95307 and longitude 291.82051.
47d71928-b8fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bursts Optical ObserVations and Transient Explorer System-7 at San Pedro Atacama Observatory, Chile

47da8fd4-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Wustrow observatory, operational from 1891 to 1903 as part of IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) investigations.
47da8fd4-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Wustrow Observatory

47ed8fa2-b739-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Fort Smith (FSMI) Station is a ground-based observatory located in Fort Smith, Northwest Territories, Canada, and it is part of the University of Alberta CARISMA network. It operates as a magnetic observation facility with specific magnetic coordinates calculated using the IGRF 2008 model.
47ed8fa2-b739-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutron Monitor on Bartol Neutron Monitor at Fort Smith Observatory

480b8a10-b7d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fort Reliance Geomagnetic Observatory (FRL), located in the Kitikmeot Region of Nunavut, Canada, is a ground-based facility dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity.
480b8a10-b7d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fort Reliance Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

480c0e88-b7dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Trevinca Skies-Amalthea is a ground observatory located in Ourense, Galicia, Spain. It serves as an astronomical facility for observing and studying celestial bodies and phenomena.
480c0e88-b7dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Trevinca Skies-Amalthea Observatory, Spain

48159ffc-b607-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Magnetic Field Fluctuations) instrument on Cluster-1 is a triaxial search-coil magnetometer designed to measure the magnetic components of electromagnetic fluctuations and compute spectral matrix coefficients using three magnetic and two electric wave components.
48159ffc-b607-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SearchCoil on Cluster-1 part of Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Magnetic Field Fluctuations

48255500-b855-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The UNHT Nanoindenter is a sophisticated instrument used in materials science to measure mechanical properties such as hardness and elastic modulus at the nanometer scale through precise indentation processes.
48255500-b855-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nanoindenter

482ce39c-b9f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pleiade Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Verona, Italy. It has been operational since January 1994 and specializes in ground-based observations from its location at an altitude of 90 meters.
482ce39c-b9f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pleiade Observatory, Italy

48338698-b7fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Radiation Belt Storm Probe (RBSP) EMFISIS is an instrument suite designed to measure electric and magnetic fields in the Earth's radiation belts. It includes a tri-axial fluxgate magnetometer and a search coil magnetometer with a sweep frequency receiver, aimed at understanding plasma wave interactions and their role in particle acceleration and loss processes.
48338698-b7fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: WaveformReceiver part of Radiation Belt Storm Probe

4834aa1e-b9bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Siding Spring Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Siding Spring, Australia, known for its ground-based telescopes and facilities. It houses the iTelescope Observatory, which provides remote access to astronomical equipment.
4834aa1e-b9bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: iTelescope Observatory at Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

48367a66-bacf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISON-Uzhhorod Observatory, also known as Derenivka Observatory, is an astronomical observatory located in Baranyntsi Rural Hromada, Uzhhorod Raion, Zakarpattia Oblast, Ukraine. It functions as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
48367a66-bacf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ISON-Uzhhorod Observatory, Ukraine

4838d9ce-b853-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Hov Faroe Islands Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, used to measure magnetic field variations.
4838d9ce-b853-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hov Faroe Islands Observatory

483ac210-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The THEMIS-E Search Coil Magnetometer (SCM) is an instrument designed to measure three-dimensional changes in magnetic flux within a frequency range of 0.1 Hz to 4 kHz, extendable up to 8 kHz under certain conditions, mounted on a retractable boom on the THEMIS spacecraft for studying magnetic field variations in space.
483ac210-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Magnetometer part of Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms

483e7cce-b198-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF crossed loop antenna at Moshiri, Japan is an instrument designed to detect very low frequency (VLF) and extremely low frequency (ELF) electromagnetic waves. It features a 43-meter tower and has been operational since August 28, 2009.
483e7cce-b198-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Low Frequency/Extremely Low Frequency Crossed Loop Antenna part of IUGONET Investigation, Japan

484887b0-b647-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Burjassot Observatory (MPC ID: J99) is an astronomical observatory located in Burjassot, Valencia, Spain. It is situated at coordinates 359.57808 longitude and 39.508013 latitude on the ground-based facility type.
484887b0-b647-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Burjassot Observatory, Spain

4848e09a-b942-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pangnirtung (PANG) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Pangnirtung, Canada, dedicated to geophysical measurements including magnetometry. It has been operational since October 4, 2008.
4848e09a-b942-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pangnirtung Geophysical Observatory, Canada

48512504-b8c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Net Flux Radiometer for Pioneer Venus Small Probe (Night) (SNFR) was an instrument onboard the Pioneer Venus mission designed to measure radiative convergence and divergence in Venus's atmosphere, specifically targeting the nightside of the planet within the spectral range of 1 to 25 microns. It weighed about 0.4 kg and consumed 2.2 W of power, utilizing different measurement periods based on altitude.
48512504-b8c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Net Flux Radiometer for Pioneer Venus Small Probe part of Pioneer Venus Multiprobe

48535c9e-b755-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Kupang Station is a ground-based facility in the MAGDAS magnetometer network, located in Kupang, Indonesia. It features a fluxgate instrument for magnetic field measurements and contributes to geomagnetic research within Asia.
48535c9e-b755-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kupang Observatory, Indonesia

48548a22-b9eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Schuelerlabor Astronomie St. 7 Observatory (code: G04) is an astronomical facility located in Wuppertal, Germany, situated at the Carl-Fuhlrott-Gymnasium school.
48548a22-b9eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Schuelerlabor Astronomie St. 7 Observatory at Carl-Fuhlrott-Gymnasium, Germany

4858b396-b8cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Observatory of Atmospheric Environment in Moshiri, located in Hokkaido, Japan, is a ground facility dedicated to monitoring and studying atmospheric conditions.
4858b396-b8cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatory of Atmospheric Environment in Moshiri, Japan

4860dbe0-b957-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **JCPM Oi Station** (code: 882) is an astronomical observatory located in Toyota, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
4860dbe0-b957-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Oi Astronomical Observatory, Japan

4860ec82-b5a3-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IMP 8 Magnetic Field Experiment** is an instrument aboard the IMP-8 spacecraft that uses a tri-axial fluxgate magnetometer to measure magnetic fields in space.
4860ec82-b5a3-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Interplanetary Monitoring Platform-8 spacecraft

48617186-b91b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Palazzo Bindi Sergardi Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Siena, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations.
48617186-b91b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Palazzo Bindi Sergardi Observatory, Italy

486276ca-bc69-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) All-sky imager at Ithaca, U.S.A., is a multi-wavelength instrument developed to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere through observations of nocturnal airglow emissions.
486276ca-bc69-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: All-sky Imager part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Investigation

4862db52-b7b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The BARREL Balloon 1K magnetometer (TCM2) is a three-axis instrument onboard the BARREL payload, designed to measure magnetic field components with high resolution and accuracy. It aids in identifying substorm activity and ultra-low frequency oscillations, crucial for studying electron precipitation modulations.
4862db52-b7b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

486635ca-b7a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU Radio Beacon Receiver (GRBR) at the Yogyakarta observatory is a digital receiver designed to measure ionospheric total electron content (TEC) using Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite signals, employing GNU Radio software and Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) hardware.
486635ca-b7a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver GRBR at Yogyakarta Observatory, Indonesia

4867ddc4-b7d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The WIND spacecraft is a NASA geomagnetic research satellite launched in 1994 to study the solar wind and its interactions with Earth's magnetosphere as part of the Global Geospace Science initiative.
4867ddc4-b7d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wind part of Global Geospace Science initiative

48683202-b59f-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Osservatorio Astronomico is an astronomical observatory located in Piobbico, Italy. It is known by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID L47 and is situated at coordinates 43.58589 latitude and 12.50711 longitude.
48683202-b59f-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Piobbico Observatory, Italy

487c75b6-b8c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Long Wire Stop (COWBOY) is an instrument used in the Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2 (RENU2) NASA mission to measure DC electric fields and high frequency (HF) and very low frequency (VLF) electric field wave data.
487c75b6-b8c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cornell Wire Boom Yo-yo part of Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2

488e4b52-b619-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2001 Mars Odyssey Spacecraft Mars Radiation Environment Experiment (MARIE) was an instrument designed to measure the radiation environment on Mars, primarily to assess the radiation levels future astronauts might encounter. It provided valuable data on cosmic rays and solar energetic particles near Mars, aiding in understanding the planet's shielding capabilities against harmful radiation.
488e4b52-b619-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Radiation Environment Experiment on 2001 Mars Odyssey Spacecraft

489073c4-bb0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Isotope Spectrometer (SIS) on the Advanced Composition Explorer (ACE) is an instrument designed to measure at isotopic resolution elements from helium through zinc at energies of 10 - 100 MeV/nucleon, focusing on energetic ions accelerated by solar flares and other space phenomena.
489073c4-bb0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Isotope Spectrometer part of Advanced Composition Explorer

48946b92-ba04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Corner Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Durmersheim, Germany. It is a ground-based observatory used for various astronomical studies and observations.
48946b92-ba04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Durmersheim Observatory

4899fbf8-b981-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Mariner 6 & 7 were a pair of NASA spacecraft designed to conduct flyby missions to Mars in 1969. Their primary goal was to capture TV images and collect scientific data during their close encounters with the planet within a short timeframe, enhancing our understanding of Mars' surface and atmosphere.
4899fbf8-b981-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mariner 6 and Mariner 7 part of Mariner Mars

48acd6fc-b890-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Solar X-ray Sensor (XRS)** on GOES 13 is an x-ray telescope designed to observe and measure solar x-ray emissions in specific ranges, providing real-time alerts of solar flares that can disrupt communications and GPS signals.
48acd6fc-b890-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar X-ray Sensor on GOES 13

48b4af76-b5de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
JASON3 is a satellite mission designed to measure sea level and ocean surface topography. It provides ephemeris data and orbital information as part of the CNES observatory CDPP-AMDA program.
48b4af76-b5de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Jason 3 Mission

48b6cfb6-b7fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **HANET Observatory Network** is a ground-based facility located on Earth's surface, comprising multiple observatories, including the Kiso Observatory.
48b6cfb6-b7fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: HANET Observatory Network

48c5ccd8-b738-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Culgoora Solar Observatory, located near Narrabri, New South Wales, Australia, continuously monitors solar activity through optical and radio observations, providing real-time data on solar flares, sunspots, and other phenomena to international space forecast centers.
48c5ccd8-b738-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Solar Radiospectrograph on 12 cm Solar Telescope at Culgoora Solar Observatory, Australia

48ca569c-b5d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) station at Rikubetsu, Japan, is a ground-based facility operated by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research (ISEE), Nagoya University, designed to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions.
48ca569c-b5d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research Observatory, Japan
