48d997de-b9dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kyoto University Astronomical Observatory's Seimei Telescope is a 3.8-meter optical telescope located in Asia, specifically designed for astronomical observations by the university’s Department of Astronomy.
48d997de-b9dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 3.8m Seimei Telescope at Kyoto University Astronomical Observatory

48ddf680-bc35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Finlaystone Observatory** is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Angel Fire, New Mexico, at 1 Vail Overlook. It offers facilities for stargazing and astronomical research in the United States.
48ddf680-bc35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Finlaystone Observatory, Angel Fire, United States

48f62ee2-bb33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RAS (Remote Astronomical Society) Observatory of New Mexico, also known as the New Mexico Skies Observatory, is a remotely controlled astronomical observatory located in Mayhill, New Mexico. It is hosted by the New Mexico Skies astronomy hosting company and is designated with the Minor Planet Center code H06.
48f62ee2-bb33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Remote Astronomical Society Observatory at Mayhill Observatory

48f727f8-bc36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Probe Experiment (OPE) on the Giotto Spacecraft was designed to measure the polarized emissivity of dust and gas in cometary comae using a photometer-polarimeter with seven interference filters, providing insights into the composition and behavior of comets.
48f727f8-bc36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Probe Experiment on Giotto Spacecraft

490836dc-b70a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Sodankylä Geophysical Observatory, established in 1913, is a ground-based research facility located in Finnish Lapland that conducts continuous measurements of geophysical phenomena such as Earth's magnetic field, seismic activities, and cosmic rays. It is operated by the University of Oulu and contributes to various scientific research projects.
490836dc-b70a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sodankylä Geophysical Observatory, Finland

490fc710-b9be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Crow Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Crow Hall within the Physics Department on the Danforth Campus of Washington University in St. Louis, known for its historic telescope that remains operational and open to public visitors.
490fc710-b9be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Crow Observatory at Washington University in St. Louis

4911ddac-ba45-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Entity Definition:**
NOAA 10 (also known as NOAA-G) was a third-generation operational meteorological satellite launched in 1986 to monitor Earth's atmosphere and environment for the National Operational Environmental Satellite System (NOESS). It carried advanced instruments for measuring cloud cover, temperature profiles, energy exchange, ozone distribution, and space environment conditions.
4911ddac-ba45-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer on NOAA 10

49162696-bb12-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Koschny Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Noordwijkerhout, Netherlands. It is a ground-based facility used for conducting astronomical observations and research.
49162696-bb12-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Koschny Observatory

49209012-bbc7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Carson City Magnetometer is an instrument located at the Carson City Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation. It measures magnetic field variations and has been operational since July 23, 2004.
49209012-bbc7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Carson City Geophysical Observatory

4922ca7c-b612-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Juno Stellar Reference Unit (SRU) is a star sensor on the Juno spacecraft that provides inertial attitude information and operates as a visible-light science imager for studying Jupiter's system, including its faint rings, auroral emissions, and low-light phenomena.
4922ca7c-b612-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible Juno Stellar Reference Unit on Juno spacecraft

492a736a-bb1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: North Pole 6 was a ground facility located on Earth's surface, operating from January 1, 1957, to December 31, 1959, as part of the IAGA Observatory network.
492a736a-bb1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole 6

492d8d30-baf0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Squirrel Valley Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Polk County, North Carolina. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical research and observations.
492d8d30-baf0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Squirrel Valley Observatory, United States

492ee620-b97f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, and the Linares Magnetometer, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation since 2007, operates at the Linares Geophysical Observatory.
492ee620-b97f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms Mission

492fcd2e-b722-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Tate’s Cairn was a ground-based observatory in Hong Kong that operated from 1972 to 1978, primarily known for its magnetometer instruments used for geophysical measurements.
492fcd2e-b722-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tate's Cairn Observatory, China

4946a260-bc68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Contwoyto magnetometer is a ground-based observatory located at Lupin Mine, Nunavut, Canada (65.754°N, 248.750°E), and is part of the CARISMA magnetometer array.
4946a260-bc68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Contwoyto Observatory, Canada

49519d76-b747-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Very Small Array (VSA) is an astronomical instrument located at the Observatorio del Teide in Africa, operating in the millimeter waveband.
49519d76-b747-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter Very Small Array at Observatorio del Teide

495c49b2-ba29-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Craigie Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Mullaloo Exchange, Coral Street, Craigie, City of Joondalup, Western Australia. It operates as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
495c49b2-ba29-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Craigie Observatory, Australia

49630392-b77c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Telescope Live Observatory (code: X02) is an astronomical observatory located in El Sauce, Chile. It is a ground-based facility operated by the Observatorio Mancomunado de Astrofísica (OMA).
49630392-b77c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Telescope Live Observatory at El Sauce Observatory, Chile

49667306-b713-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Grafton Test Facility Geomagnetic Observatory was a ground-based facility in Orange, New Hampshire, USA, operational from 1999 to 2003, dedicated to measuring geomagnetic activity.
49667306-b713-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Grafton Test Facility, United States

49686384-b8fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Falmouth Observatory was a ground-based facility in Falmouth, Cornwall, England, operational from 1891 to 1912, equipped with magnetometers for geomagnetic measurements.
49686384-b8fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Falmouth Observatory, United Kingdom

49695e86-bad8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Gamma Ray Spectrometer (GRS) was an instrument on the NEAR Shoemaker mission designed to detect gamma rays emitted from elements in asteroid surfaces, using a NaI scintillator detector to measure abundances of key elements.
49695e86-bad8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma Ray Spectrometer on Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous - Shoemaker

496b6772-b6b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **FIELDS instrument's V2 voltage probe**, part of the Parker Solar Probe mission launched in 2018, is designed to measure electric fields and radio/plasma waves as a capacitively-coupled antenna, contributing to a comprehensive study of the solar environment.
496b6772-b6b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: FIELDS instrument part of Parker Solar Probe Mission

49774d22-ba59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Smith College Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Smith College in Northampton, Massachusetts, used for ground-based observations.
49774d22-ba59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Smith College Observatory, United States

49816188-b96c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: DTU Space is a ground facility run by the Technical University of Denmark that monitors Earth's magnetic field using a network of stations located in Greenland, Faroe Islands, and Denmark. These stations provide high-resolution geomagnetic data, with some calibrated to INTERMAGNET standards.
49816188-b96c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetic Field Monitoring Network at DTU Space

4981b774-b75e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 2 Energetic Particle Detector (EPD) Suite, Energetic Ion Spectrometer (EIS) is an instrument aboard the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission that uses a time-of-flight/pulse-height sensor to measure ion composition and angular distributions in the energy range of ~45 keV to 500 keV, with a temporal resolution of 30 seconds.
4981b774-b75e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Ion Spectrometer on MMS 2 part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

4994de92-b59e-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2 (RENU2) Fluxgate Science Magnetometer (FGM) instrument was used in a NASA sounding rocket mission to measure vector magnetic fields in the Dayside Cusp Region on December 13, 2015.
4994de92-b59e-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Science Magnetometer on Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2

49975778-b844-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Karl Schwarzschild Observatory, officially known as the Thuringia State Observatory Tautenburg, is a German astronomical observatory located in Tautenburg near Jena, Thuringia. It operates under public law by the State of Thuringia and houses notable instruments such as the Alfred Jensch telescope.
49975778-b844-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2m Alfred Jensch Telescope at Thuringia State Observatory Tautenburg, Germany

49a4a3c2-b661-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Dragonfly is a NASA mission planned to send a robotic quadcopter drone to explore Titan, Saturn's largest moon, with the goal of studying prebiotic chemistry and extraterrestrial habitability through multiple flights and landings.
49a4a3c2-b661-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dragonfly part of New Frontiers Program

49a9af38-baea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Plasma Wave Investigation (RPW) is an instrument suite aboard Solar Orbiter designed to measure electric and magnetic fields, radio waves, and plasma properties in the inner heliosphere. It aims to address key scientific questions related to solar wind origin, solar transients' impact on heliospheric variability, and energetic particle radiation from solar eruptions.
49a9af38-baea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna part of Solar Orbiter

49aaaff6-b8d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Long-Range Reconnaissance Imager (LORRI) is a high-resolution telescope aboard the New Horizons spacecraft designed for detailed imaging of Pluto, Charon, and other celestial bodies encountered during its missions.
49aaaff6-b8d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Long Range Reconnaissance Imager on New Horizons

49b7040a-b70f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The TWINS 1 Positions dataset provides the spatial coordinates and trajectory information for the TWINS 1 spacecraft, which is part of the Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers (TWINS) mission.
49b7040a-b70f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers instrument on TWINS 1 Spacecraft

49bcaa0e-bb0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Chabot Space and Science Center** is a science museum, planetarium, and observatory located in Oakland, California, offering interactive exhibits and powerful telescopes for learning about Earth and space sciences.
49bcaa0e-bb0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chabot Space and Science Center, United States

49c54746-ba42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope (CFHT) is a 3.58-meter telescope located near the summit of Mauna Kea on Hawaii's Big Island, known for its Prime Focus/Cassegrain configuration and operational since 1979.
49c54746-ba42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.58m Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatory, United States

49c8ba0e-b6bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Iqaluit Ground Magnetic Field Instrument, operational since 1995-01-01 as part of the IAGA investigation at the IUGONET Observatory, specifically measures these properties in Iqaluit (IQA).
49c8ba0e-b6bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ground Magnetic Field Instrument at Iqaluit Observatory

49db3566-b947-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Khabarovsk Geomagnetic Observatory (KHB), located in Russia, is a ground facility that operated from 1975 to 1976, specializing in geomagnetic measurements with instruments like magnetometers.
49db3566-b947-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Khabarovsk Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

49dfdd7e-ba77-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Korets Geomagnetic Observatory (KTS), located in the Aqtöbe region of Kazakhstan, is a ground-based facility established in 1968 for monitoring and studying geomagnetic activity.
49dfdd7e-ba77-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Korets Geomagnetic Observatory, Kazakhstan

49e69faa-b8c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Kingsland Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in County Sligo, Ireland, situated at coordinates 53.923156 latitude and -8.3655 longitude.
49e69faa-b8c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kingsland Observatory, Ireland

49f4ce30-b989-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ISEE 3 Vector Helium Magnetometer** is a triaxial magnetometer installed on the ISEE-3 spacecraft, designed to measure steady magnetic fields and their low-frequency variations across multiple amplitude ranges. It features automatic ranging capabilities and provides high-precision data with minimal noise interference in its operational frequency bands.
49f4ce30-b989-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vector Helium Magnetometer on International Sun-Earth Explorer 3

4a06bbec-b6e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Apollo 14 Lunar Module, named "Antares," was the third crewed spacecraft to land on the Moon. It carried astronauts Alan B. Shepard Jr. and Edgar D. Mitchell, along with scientific equipment for experiments on the lunar surface.
4a06bbec-b6e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Apollo 14 Lunar Module Antares part of Apollo 14 Mission

4a08ee24-b858-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at CMD is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Camden, Australia, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
4a08ee24-b858-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System observation network

4a18c612-bb2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Thermal-Region Camera Spectrograph (T-ReCS) is a mid-infrared imager and long-slit spectrograph used with the Gemini South telescope, designed for high image quality and low thermal background in both imaging and spectroscopy modes.
4a18c612-bb2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mid-infrared Thermal-Region Camera Spectrograph on Gemini South Telescope

4a1e13fa-baa9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Siding Spring-Janess-G** is an astronomical observatory located at Siding Spring Observatory in Coonabarabran, New South Wales, Australia, operated by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA).
4a1e13fa-baa9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

4a38425c-b9b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wither Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at 9 Kendon Street in Witherlea, Blenheim, New Zealand.
4a38425c-b9b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wither Observatory, New Zealand

4a3baab4-b8ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Madrid Magnetometer was an instrument used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field, operational from January 1, 1879, to December 31, 1901, at the IAGA observatory in Madrid.
4a3baab4-b8ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Madrid Observatory

4a445c96-b5e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar EUV Experiment (SEE) on the TIMED mission is a photometer designed to measure the daily full-disk solar vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) irradiance, specifically in the wavelength range of 0 to 200 nm, to understand its impact on the Earth's upper atmosphere.
4a445c96-b5e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar EUV Experiment part of TIMED

4a450346-b6d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/F18, SESS Special Sensor Precipitating Electron and Ion Spectrometer 5 (SESS/SSJ5) is an instrument onboard the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program that measures the energy transfer, mass, and momentum through the magnetosphere-ionosphere within Earth's magnetic field.
4a450346-b6d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Precipitating Electron and Ion Spectrometer 5 on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

4a482714-b642-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **e-CALLISTO:** A global network of CALLISTO spectrometers designed for continuous monitoring of solar radio bursts, primarily used for astronomical research, education, and citizen science.
4a482714-b642-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Compound Astronomical Low frequency Low cost Instrument for Spectroscopy and Transportable Observatory at ETH Zurich

4a551cea-bc6d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Mauguio Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Pérols, near Montpellier, France. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the study of celestial objects and phenomena.
4a551cea-bc6d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mauguio Observatory

4a5a2a18-b98f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The WHISPER instrument is a scientific tool on the Cluster 2/FM7 (Samba) spacecraft designed to measure electron density in plasma via active sounding and record natural wave emissions in the high-frequency range from 4–80 KHz. It is part of the Wave Experiment Consortium (WEC) and began operations on December 1, 2000.
4a5a2a18-b98f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waves of High Frequency and Sounder for Probing Electron Density by Relaxation part of Cluster

4a5f3576-b679-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IGPP-LANL Table Mountain Fluxgate Magnetometer is a scientific instrument located at the Table Mountain station of the Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics (IGPP) and Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL), designed to measure magnetic field variations. It is part of the broader IGPP-LANL Magnetometer Array, contributing to geomagnetic research and monitoring.
4a5f3576-b679-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of IGPP-LANL Magnetometer Array

4a680916-b797-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Observatoire de Haute-Provence (OHP) 1.2m CCD is a telescope located in France that was operational from 1996 to 2014, equipped with a Charge-Coupled Device detector for astronomical observations.
4a680916-b797-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.2m Telescope at Observatoire de Haute-Provence, France

4a6a800e-b7f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Lowell Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Flagstaff, Arizona, United States. Established in 1894 by Percival Lowell, it is one of the oldest observatories in the U.S. and is notable for being the site where Pluto was discovered in 1930.
4a6a800e-b7f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lowell Observatory, United States

4a742858-b6f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2P Engineering Data Interface is a component of the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) project that converts analog measurements of temperatures, voltages, and currents into digital data with high precision.
4a742858-b6f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Engineering Data Interface part of Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Relativistic Electron Losses

4a7e3440-b83a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN magnetometer network at Cachoeira Paulista, Brazil, is a ground-based facility dedicated to measuring magnetic fields, located in the Southeast Region of Brazil.
4a7e3440-b83a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer network at Cachoeira Paulista Observatory, Brazil

4a801cba-b6aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The magnetometers at the Dallas observatory were operational from 1964 to 1974 and were part of an investigation by IAGA.
4a801cba-b6aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at WDC Kyoto Observatory

4a84a55c-ba54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetometer at Warnkenhagen (WRH) is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of Earth's magnetic field, located at a station with the IAGA identifier WRH. It is part of the iugonet-observatory network, specifically associated with the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto.
4a84a55c-ba54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Warnkenhagen Observatory

4a976bf0-ba23-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Molėtai Astronomical Observatory (MAO) is an astronomical research facility operated by Vilnius University Institute of Theoretical Physics and Astronomy, situated on Kaldiniai Hill near Kulionys, Lithuania. It was established in 1969 and serves as a ground-based observatory for various astronomical studies.
4a976bf0-ba23-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Molėtai Astronomical Observatory, Lithuania

4a9de19e-b6bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Universidad de Monterrey Observatory is an astronomical facility located in San Pedro Garza García, Nuevo León, Mexico. It is used for ground-based observations of celestial objects.
4a9de19e-b6bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Monterrey Observatory, Mexico

4aa57840-bb30-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer (MAG) is part of the FIELDS instrument suite on the Parker Solar Probe Mission, designed to measure magnetic fields and electric field antenna voltages in the Sun's atmosphere.
4aa57840-bb30-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer on Parker Solar Probe Mission

4ab40bce-bc86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "MMS 1 Spacecraft Position" is a virtual instrument that provides the ephemeris data for the MMS 1 spacecraft, part of the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS), which began operations on March 13, 2015.
4ab40bce-bc86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft Position part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

4ab681fc-b956-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The MMS 4 Spacecraft Position is a virtual instrument that provides ephemeris data for the MMS 4 spacecraft, part of the CNES-CDPP archive. It offers positional information essential for tracking and analyzing the spacecraft's trajectory.
4ab681fc-b956-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: MMS 4 Spacecraft Position part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

4abfe9d6-b8e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DSX Wave Particle Interaction eXperiment (WPIx) Loss Cone Imager (LCI) is an instrument designed to measure three-dimensional energetic particle distributions, particularly focusing on the fluxes of energetic electrons along and against the local geomagnetic field vector. It consists of rotating sensor heads and a high sensitivity telescope for detailed measurements in the loss cone region.
4abfe9d6-b8e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Loss Cone Imager part of Demonstration and Science Experiments

4ac8a408-b65a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SpectralPowerReceiver, specifically the LOFAR FR606 HBA Standalone Receiver, is a component of the LOFAR (Low Frequency Array) telescope, operating within the 120 to 240 MHz spectral range and located at the Nançay station in France. It contributes to various astronomical studies, including deep sky surveys and the study of high-energy cosmic phenomena.
4ac8a408-b65a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spectral Power Receiver on LOFAR FR606

4ae34340-b816-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Fayetteville Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Washington County, Arkansas, United States. It operates as a ground-based observatory with the MPC code V81 and serves the purpose of celestial observations from Earth.
4ae34340-b816-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fayetteville Observatory

4ae6c77a-b94e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Aorangi Iti Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Lake Tekapo, New Zealand. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID R57 and is situated at coordinates 170.47278 longitude and -44.008206 latitude.
4ae6c77a-b94e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Aorangi Iti Observatory, New Zealand

4af65348-b8db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Brisbane Geomagnetic Observatory (BRS) is a ground-based facility located in Pinjarra Hills, Greater Brisbane, Australia, dedicated to monitoring and studying geomagnetic activity since 1943.
4af65348-b8db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Brisbane Geomagnetic Observatory, Australia

4afee9ca-b9e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Colegio Cristo Rey astronomical observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Rosario, Santa Fe, Argentina. It is situated at coordinates 299.3649 longitude and -32.95368 latitude on the South American continent.
4afee9ca-b9e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Astronomico del Colegio Cristo Rey at Rosario Observatory, Argentina

4b05faf6-b6be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A "spacecraft.v13" refers to a specific version or designation of a spacecraft within NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS), indicating its role as an instrument host and its inclusion in the Virtual Observatory Paris-Meudon (VOParis) database, which catalogs observational facilities and instruments.
4b05faf6-b6be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: James Webb Telescope

4b079e92-bb64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "LANL 1991 Positions" refers to the ephemeris data of the LANL (Los Alamos National Laboratory) spacecraft from 1991, detailing its positions in various coordinate systems.
4b079e92-bb64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Los Alamos National Laboratory 1991

4b0aba6a-b843-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dynamic Albedo of Neutrons (DAN) is a neutron spectrometer on the Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover designed to measure the abundance and depth distribution of hydrogen- and oxygen-bearing materials in Mars' subsurface.
4b0aba6a-b843-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dynamic Albedo of Neutrons on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

4b1150fc-b963-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EMN Cachoeira Paulista Station** is a ground-based magnetometer network located in Cachoeira Paulista, Brazil. It operates as part of the IUGONET observatory and monitors Earth's magnetic field variations.
4b1150fc-b963-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cachoeira Paulista Observatory, Brazil

4b1ea8ce-b990-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tangerang Geomagnetic Observatory (TNG), located in Kiara Payung, Pakuhaji, Tangerang Regency, Indonesia, was a ground-based facility operated from 1957 to 1969 for monitoring and studying geomagnetic activity.
4b1ea8ce-b990-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tangerang Observatory, Indonesia

4b2054c8-b6eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ST5-155 Fluxgate Magnetometer** is a low-power science-grade instrument used on the ST5 spacecraft to measure magnetic fields, featuring a boom-mounted design with no active components and dual commandable ranges of 64,000 nT and 1000 nT.
4b2054c8-b6eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Space Technology 5 Mission

4b219b8a-ba10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Magnetometers at Freetown (FTN) were operational from January 1, 1961, to December 31, 1967, as part of the IAGA investigation at the Freetown ground station.
4b219b8a-ba10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Freetown Observatory

4b284912-b7d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Podkammenaya Tung. Geomagnetic Observatory (POD) is a ground-based facility in the Turukhansky District of Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia, established in 1968 to monitor geomagnetic activity and includes instruments such as magnetometers.
4b284912-b7d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Podkammenaya Tung. Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

4b3b06fe-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Magnetometers at Mauritius (MRI)" is a historical instrument used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field. It was operational from January 1, 1892, to December 31, 1965, and is part of the IAGA investigation at the WDC Kyoto observatory in Mauritius.
4b3b06fe-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at WDC Kyoto Observatory

4b46c2f0-b85a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) All-sky imager at Resolute Bay, Canada is a multi-wavelength instrument designed to study the upper atmosphere by capturing nocturnal airglow emissions. It was developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research at Nagoya University and operates as part of the IUGONET Observatory in Resolute Bay.
4b46c2f0-b85a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: All-Sky Imager part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research Observatory

4b46c9ae-ba1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **HNRAO Terminated Folded Dipole and RadioJOVE receiver system** is an array of four 24-foot antennas configured in a square pattern, operating within the 15-30 MHz bandwidth at the Hawk's Nest Radio Astronomy Observatory. It features simultaneous right-circular polarization (RCP) and left-circular polarization (LCP), with a direct conversion receiver functioning at 20.1 MHz and a 7 KHz RF bandwidth.
4b46c9ae-ba1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terminated Folded Dipole and RadioJOVE Receiver System at Hawk's Nest Radio Astronomy Observatory

4b49b01a-b76e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wien-Auhof Geomagnetic Observatory (WIA) was a ground facility in Vienna, Austria, operational from 1929 to 1944, primarily used for geomagnetic research and instrumentation.
4b49b01a-b76e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Wien-Auhof Observatory, Austria

4b4cbccc-bb2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Schaerding Observatory is an astronomical facility located in St. Florian am Inn, Upper Austria. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
4b4cbccc-bb2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Schaerding Observatory, Austria

4b55927a-b86a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sonnenborgh Observatory in Utrecht, Netherlands, is a public astronomical observatory and museum housed in a historic fort, known for its rich history including being the site of one of the world's earliest chemical laboratories.
4b55927a-b86a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Museum Sterrenwacht Sonnenborgh Observatory, Netherlands

4b5901e6-b9fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The HARIMAU instrument is a transportable wind profiler radar located in West Kalimantan, Indonesia. It operates using active-phased array technology with seven Luneberg lens antennas to monitor wind velocity and atmospheric turbulence in the lower troposphere.
4b5901e6-b9fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar at Pontianak Observatory

4b7b686a-ba40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Talcott Mountain Science Center for Student Involvement (TMSC) is a non-profit organization in Avon, Connecticut, dedicated to enhancing science education through direct engagement with students, teachers, and the public.
4b7b686a-ba40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Talcott Mountain Science Center Observatory, United States

4b9286de-b834-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Gissar Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in the Rudaki District of Tajikistan, established in 1956. It is situated at an altitude of 743 meters and focuses on ground-based observations.
4b9286de-b834-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gissar Observatory, Tajikistan

4b970502-ba81-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Electrostatic Fields** instrument onboard the IMP-J (IMP 8) spacecraft was designed to measure ambient electric fields in the solar wind and Earth's magnetosheath with frequencies up to 1 kHz, utilizing a pair of 70-m wire antennas spun at approximately 24 rpm.
4b970502-ba81-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Long Wire on Interplanetary Monitoring Platform part of IMP-8

4b97623c-b751-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific entity refers to a historical magnetometer located in Manila, operational from 1889 to 1904 as part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) investigation.
4b97623c-b751-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Manila Observatory

4b986f44-b63c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Montcabrer Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Cabrils, Maresme, Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. It has a Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID of 213 and operates as a ground-based facility at an altitude of 120 meters.
4b986f44-b63c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Montcabrer Observatory, Spain

4b9af194-b6df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Camden station in Sydney, NSW, is a ground-based observatory operating since November 1980, known as part of the IAGA network and featuring an ionosonde instrument.
4b9af194-b6df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ASWS Instrument on Camden Station at Sydney Observatory, Australia

4ba37f70-b8b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The THEMIS Electric Fields Instrument (EFI) is a device onboard the THEMIS spacecraft designed to measure the three components of the ambient vector electric field using wire and rigid booms, covering frequencies from DC up to 4 kHz for waveform measurements.
4ba37f70-b8b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electric Field Instrument on Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms

4bc34e02-b651-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **210MM Lunping Station** is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Taoyuan City, Taiwan, part of the ISEE (International Space Environment Explorer) Magnetometer Network. It focuses on monitoring and studying geomagnetic activity along the 210th magnetic meridian.
4bc34e02-b651-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lunping Station, Taiwan

4bc57e90-b609-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Cracow-Fort Skala Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Krakow, Poland. It is a ground-based facility situated at the coordinates 50.05424° N, 19.8263° E.
4bc57e90-b609-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cracow-Fort Skala Observatory, Poland

4bc639ae-bb02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Goldstone Solar System Radar (GSSR) Transmitter** is a high-powered radar system located at the Deep Space Station 14 in Goldstone, California. It operates at an 8560 MHz frequency with a maximum transmission power of 450 kW and can achieve a range resolution as fine as 3.75 meters.
4bc639ae-bb02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-band Goldstone Solar System Radar Transmitter on Deep Space Station 14, United States

4bcabf54-b7da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LANL02A Energetic Sensor for Particles (ESP) is an instrument onboard the Los Alamos National Laboratory satellite that measures high-energy particles using a bismuth germanate crystal and plastic scintillator. It has been operational since 1989 and can detect electrons with energies from 0.7 to 26 MeV and protons with energies from 11 to over 20 MeV.
4bcabf54-b7da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Spectrometer for Particles part of LANL02A Observatory

4bceb064-b960-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bilbao Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bilbao, Spain, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
4bceb064-b960-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bilbao Observatory, Spain

4bd8cbb4-bba7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **MAGDAS Abuja Station** is a ground-based magnetometer facility located at the National Space Research and Development Agency in Abuja, Nigeria. It is part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network and operates under IUGONET's Observatory ICSWSE.
4bd8cbb4-bba7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Abuja Observatory, Nigeria

4bf31842-bafe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cosmic Ray Telescope for the Effects of Radiation (CRaTER) is an instrument aboard the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) designed to measure the radiation environment on the Moon and its biological impacts by detecting galactic and solar cosmic rays.
4bf31842-bafe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cosmic Ray Telescope for the Effects of Radiation on Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter

4c05e046-bb60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, often employed in geophysical observatories like PENGUIn-1 (PG1) for studying Earth's magnetic field.
4c05e046-bb60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at PENGUIn-1 Observatory, Antarctica

4c091486-bab7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Terre Adélie**: A ground-based observatory located at Dumont d'Urville Station in Antarctica, established in 1957, which includes a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements.
4c091486-bab7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Terre Adelie Observatory, Antarctica

4c0d9a48-b6f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Neumayer Station III**: A ground-based geophysical observatory located on Earth's surface at an altitude of 46.0 meters and coordinates -70.693 latitude, 351.25 longitude. It has been operational since January 1, 1999, and includes a magnetometer as part of its instrumentation.
4c0d9a48-b6f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neumayer Station III Observatory, Antarctica

4c162980-bb59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 12 Cold Cathode Gage Experiment (CCGE) was part of the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments package (ALSEP), designed to measure the density of neutral particles and determine the amount of gas present at the lunar surface, aiding in understanding the tenuous lunar atmosphere.
4c162980-bb59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cold Cathode Ionization Gage on Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package

4c1dc73a-b645-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Northern Auroral Electrojet (NAE) Index Instrument is a virtual tool that aggregates data from various ground magnetometer arrays to compute the auroral electrojet index in the northern hemisphere at 60-second intervals. It utilizes data from multiple observatories, including GIME, THEMIS GBO, INTERMAGNET, DTU, University of Iceland, and NIPR, with contributing magnetometers varying daily.
4c1dc73a-b645-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Northern Auroral Electrojet Index Magnetometer at Northern Auroral Electrojet Observatory

4c386060-b68e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Marana Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Crespadoro, Vicenza, Veneto, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility for stargazing and research purposes.
4c386060-b68e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Marana Observatory, Italy

4c442d4e-b663-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Kagiya Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Tokai, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 878 and focuses on ground-based observations.
4c442d4e-b663-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kagiya Observatory, Japan

4c4bdfa8-b974-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The International Astrophysical Observatory "GRANAT" was a Soviet/Russian space observatory launched in 1989 to study high energy emissions from galactic and extra-galactic sources using X-ray and gamma-ray telescopes.
4c4bdfa8-b974-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X- and gamma-ray International Astrophysical Observatory Granat

4c528920-bb9a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **AGO P1 Antenna Instrument** is an antenna located at the AGO P1 ground station, part of the ICESTAR observatory, designed for astronomical observations. It functions as a critical component in facilitating communication and data collection for space missions.
4c528920-bb9a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna on ICESTAR AGO P1

4c564736-bb5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Chiclayo Geomagnetic Observatory (CCL)** was a ground-based facility in Chiclayo, Peru that operated from 1957 to 1960 for geomagnetic observations.
4c564736-bb5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Chiclayo Geomagnetic Observatory, Peru

4c631302-b6e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Chiricahua Skies Observatory is a ground-based observatory located in East Bumble Bee, Cochise County, Arizona, United States. It is situated at coordinates 31.86683° N and 250.4842° E, offering astronomical observations from North America.
4c631302-b6e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chiricahua Skies Observatory, United States

4c66dcfe-ba87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Felliscopio Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Fellicarolo, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations.
4c66dcfe-ba87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Felliscopio Observatory, Italy

4c6f4d6e-b6a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Equatorial Magnetometer Network (EMN) fluxgate magnetometer at Guam is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field, installed as part of the IUGONET Observatory in Guam, USA.
4c6f4d6e-b6a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of The Equatorial Magnetometer Network

4c739412-b6c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The FM-3I is a fluxgate DC magnetometer on the Interball Tail Probe, designed to measure magnetic fields in two ranges (+/-200 nT and +/-1000 nT) using two independent magnetometers (M1 and M2) with different sampling rates.
4c739412-b6c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Interball Tail Probe

4c7c1ae4-b62f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IGPP-LANL Jicamarca Fluxgate Magnetometer** is a scientific instrument located at the IGPP-LANL observatory in Jicamarca, designed to measure and monitor magnetic field variations as part of geophysical investigations.
4c7c1ae4-b62f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IGPP-LANL Jicamarca Observatory

4c7f14a0-ba2c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The CBA-MM Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Hardy County, West Virginia, dedicated to ground-based astronomical observations.
4c7f14a0-ba2c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mountain Meadows Observatory, United States

4c86863a-b5eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hartung–Boothroyd Observatory (HBO) is an astronomical observatory located atop Mount Pleasant near Cornell University in Ithaca, New York, primarily used as a teaching facility for upper-level undergraduate astronomy classes.
4c86863a-b5eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hartung–Boothroyd Observatory

4c8c7344-ba21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Village-Neuf Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Village-Neuf, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
4c8c7344-ba21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Village-neuf Observatory, France

4c99d5de-b61b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Huancayo Magnetic Observatory:** A ground-based magnetic observatory located in Huancayo, Peru, operational since 1922, dedicated to monitoring and studying the Earth's magnetic field.
4c99d5de-b61b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Huancayo Observatory, Peru

4c9e7970-bb54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer deployed in 1957 at the Lourenço Marques observatory as part of the IAGA investigation to measure magnetic fields.
4c9e7970-bb54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lourenco-Marques Observatory

4c9ef522-b752-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: San Polo a Mosciano Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Casignano, Scandicci, Florence, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
4c9ef522-b752-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: San Polo a Mosciano Observatory, Italy

4ca44382-b69a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Durban station is a ground-based facility in the MAGDAS magnetometer network, located at Windy Hill, uMshwathi Ward 12, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. It includes a fluxgate instrument for measuring magnetic field variations.
4ca44382-b69a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Durban Observatory, South Africa

4ca98dde-ba7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kuujjuaq (KUUJ) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Kuujjuaq, Quebec, Canada, that houses instruments such as a magnetometer and is part of the NASA THEMIS Ground-Based Observatory network.
4ca98dde-ba7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kuujjuaq Geophysical Observatory, Canada

4caa3478-b74d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2I Trajectory Positions is a virtual instrument providing ephemeris data for the BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) project, offering trajectory positions in various coordinate systems.
4caa3478-b74d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses part of BARREL

4caacefe-b81c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Liverpool John Moores University 2m Telescope is a 2-meter optical telescope located at the Observatorio del Roque de Los Muchachos in Africa.
4caacefe-b81c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.0m Liverpool John Moores University Telescope at Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos

4cb3e0da-b131-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Ionospheric Station at Norilsk (NO369), located in the Russian Federation, is a ground facility equipped with an advanced ionosonde called Digisonde. It measures angle of arrival, polarization, Doppler frequency shift, and travel time of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere to determine reflection points.
4cb3e0da-b131-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Ionospheric Station, Russia

4cb517e8-b730-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Sternwarte Davidschlag is a private ground-based observatory located in Kirchschlag bei Linz, Upper Austria, known for its observations of small Solar System bodies.
4cb517e8-b730-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Davidschlag Observatory, Austria

4cbb1458-babf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tromsø VHF is an EISCAT incoherent scatter radar located in Tromsø, Norway, featuring a steerable antenna with dimensions of 120x40m.
4cbb1458-babf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VHF Radar part of EISCAT incoherent scatter radar in Tromso

4cbc917a-b9c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AVON (Asia VLF Observation Network) Hanoi station, located in Phường Trung Hưng, Sơn Tây, Hà Nội, Vietnam, is a ground-based facility dedicated to observing very low frequency (VLF) radio signals as part of the broader Asia VLF Observation Network.
4cbc917a-b9c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Asia VLF Observation Network Hanoi station, Vietnam

4cc1da0a-b6bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Daneborg Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAGs project since 2007.
4cc1da0a-b6bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Daneborg Observatory, Greenland

4cc2d5e0-b848-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Boston University's 1.8m telescope** is located at the Lowell Observatory in North America and operates within the optical waveband. It is situated specifically at Anderson Mesa and has an aperture of 72 inches (1.8 meters).
4cc2d5e0-b848-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 1.8m Telescope at Lowell Observatory and Anderson Mesa

4cc83af0-bb39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: "**Cluster** is a European Space Agency (ESA) mission comprising four spacecraft orbiting Earth to study the solar wind's effects on the planet's magnetosphere in three dimensions."
4cc83af0-bb39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cluster, ESA Magnetospheric Mission

4cced9fc-badd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Spacecraft Ephemeris is a virtual instrument that provides the positions and trajectory data for the Curiosity rover as it explores Mars. It's part of the MSL observatory and offers essential information for tracking and planning the mission.
4cced9fc-badd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft Ephemeris part of Mars Science Laboratory

4cd9d476-bc98-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Paul Robinson Observatory is an astronomical observatory operated by the New Jersey Astronomical Association, situated in Voorhees State Park, Lebanon Township, New Jersey.
4cd9d476-bc98-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Paul Robinson Observatory, United States

4ce06cb0-b8aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometers at Coimbra (COI) are part of the IAGA investigation and have been operational since January 1, 1866.
4ce06cb0-b8aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at WDC Kyoto Observatory

4cea1ec2-bc0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Mount Cuba Astronomical Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Greenville, Delaware, United States. It houses a 0.6-meter telescope used for research and public outreach by the Delaware Astronomical Society and academic institutions.
4cea1ec2-bc0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mount Cuba Astronomical Observatory

4cef8c6c-b8ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NOAA 9 Solar Backscatter Ultraviolet Radiometer (SBUV/2) is a spectrometer designed to measure the vertical distribution of ozone in Earth's atmosphere by analyzing backscattered solar radiation at specific wavelength bands and providing continuous spectral scans from 160 nm to 400 nm.
4cef8c6c-b8ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Backscatter Ultraviolet Radiometer part of NOAA 9

4cf1073e-bb3c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Magnetometer at Jayapura (JYP), part of the MAGDAS observation network, is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate instrument used for measuring magnetic fields in Malaysia.
4cf1073e-bb3c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System observation network

4cf663ea-b8b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes the Mizuho Observatory, a ground-based facility located on Earth's surface at an altitude of 2230 meters with coordinates (latitude -70.7, longitude 44.333), which operated from January 1, 1970, to December 31, 1987, and included a magnetometer as part of its instrumentation.
4cf663ea-b8b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mizuho Observatory

4cf76ac8-ba26-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Watheroo Ionosonde** was an ionospheric research station located near Watheroo, WA, Australia. Operating from May 1938 to March 1959, it used nitrate film (1938-1946) and later 35 mm film (1950-1959) for its studies.
4cf76ac8-ba26-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar Ionosonde at Watheroo Observatory, Australia

4d06f0f6-ba6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Woomera Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Woomera, South Australia, known for its ground-based observations.
4d06f0f6-ba6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Woomera Observatory, Australia

4d075fec-b980-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTIs) All-Sky Imager at Yonaguni, Japan is a multi-wavelength instrument designed to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere through nocturnal airglow emissions. It was developed by Nagoya University and is operated by the Electronic Navigation Research Institute (ENRI).
4d075fec-b980-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: All-Sky Imager part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers, Japan

4d2d8df4-bc17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mariner 5 Magnetometer (MAG) was an instrument aboard the Mariner 5 spacecraft designed to measure interplanetary and Venusian magnetic fields using helium absorptivity to circularly polarized infrared light. It operated with high precision and provided excellent data throughout most of its mission duration from June to October 1967.
4d2d8df4-bc17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Low Field Helium Magnetometer on Mariner 5

4d507bb0-bbbe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Waterlooville Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Waterlooville, Hampshire, England. It operates as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
4d507bb0-bbbe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waterlooville Observatory, United Kingdom

4d53b194-bb1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1J Optical Photometer** is an instrument designed to detect the flux of visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm during relativistic electron precipitation events, aiming to determine the presence of protons accompanying the precipitating electrons and support research on scattering by electromagnetic ion cyclotron (EMIC) waves as a precipitation mechanism.
4d53b194-bb1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

4d56ec4c-b787-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1.0m Telescope is a 1-meter aperture telescope situated at Mount Canopus Observatory in Hobart, Tasmania, Australia. It operates from the Grote Reber memorial and is part of the larger observatory facility on Earth.
4d56ec4c-b787-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.0m Telescope at Mount Canopus Observatory, Australia

4d5bf4e2-b7f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at MGD is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Magadan, Russia, used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
4d5bf4e2-b7f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MAGDAS observation network

4d63f4c6-b630-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vesqueville Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Vesqueville, Belgium, with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 231.
4d63f4c6-b630-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vesqueville Observatory, Belgium

4d65a2e6-b791-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: MAGDAS Magadan Station is a ground-based magnetometer network located in the Khasynsky Urban District, Magadan Oblast, Russia, part of the MAGDAS (Magnetic Data Acquisition System) project.
4d65a2e6-b791-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at MAGDAS Magadan Station, Russia

4d703d12-b8b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Roburent Geomagnetic Observatory (ROB), located in Italy, is a ground-based facility that has been operating since 1964 to conduct geomagnetic measurements.
4d703d12-b8b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Roburent Geomagnetic Observatory, Italy

4d70fbde-b992-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SPECULOOS-South Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Paranal, Chile, dedicated to searching for habitable planets eclipsing ultra-cool stars.
4d70fbde-b992-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SPECULOOS-South Observatory, Chile

4d92b822-bc7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NSO Observatory Group is a ground-based astronomical facility located on Earth's surface, specifically at Kitt Peak.
4d92b822-bc7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Mayall Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory

4d95b486-b827-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA-designated station AIA on Argentine Island, operational since 1957. It is part of the ground observatory network for geomagnetic field measurements.
4d95b486-b827-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Faraday Station Observatory

4da4cbee-b866-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Maisach-1:** An observatory in Bavaria, Germany (longitude: 11.093° E, latitude: 48.213° N) that operated a ground magnetometer from January 1, 1927, to December 31, 1932.
4da4cbee-b866-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Maisach Observatory, Germany

4db6c63a-b71e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital receiver located in Jorge Town, Thailand, designed to measure ionospheric total electron content (TEC) by detecting signals from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. It uses GNU Radio software and Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) hardware for signal acquisition and processing.
4db6c63a-b71e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver at Jorge Town Observatory

4db808e2-b6ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF Moshiri Station in Japan is a ground-based observatory located in Hokkaido Prefecture that houses specialized antennas for measuring Very Low Frequency (VLF) and Extremely Low Frequency (ELF) electromagnetic waves.
4db808e2-b6ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Low Frequency and Extremely Low Frequency Moshiri Station, Japan

4dc21312-b5d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The W. M. Keck Observatory is a ground-based observatory located atop Mauna Kea on the island of Hawai'i in the United States. It features the Keck I telescope and is renowned for its advanced astronomical research capabilities.
4dc21312-b5d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 10m W. M. Keck Telescope at W. M. Keck Observatory, United States

4dc34a0c-bb71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Red Fox Observatory in Pendleton, Indiana is a ground-based astronomical facility located at 40.00844 latitude and -85.75038 longitude (274.24962), offering observational services from North America.
4dc34a0c-bb71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 14" Telescope at Red Fox Observatory, United States

4dce7e66-bb00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU Radio Beacon Receiver (GRBR) Station at Nairobi-KP is a ground facility located in Kenya that measures ionospheric disturbances related to middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes.
4dce7e66-bb00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNURadio Beacon Receiver on GNU Radio Beacon Receiver Station at Nairobi-KP, Kenya

4dda3746-b60b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **CARISMA Magnetometer at Taloyoak** is a scientific instrument located in Taloyoak, Canada, designed to measure magnetic field variations as part of the THEMIS ground-based observatory network.
4dda3746-b60b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of THEMIS Ground-Based Observatory

4de2544e-b67e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nançay Radio Astronomy Facility is a ground-based observatory located on Earth's surface, jointly operated by the Paris Observatory, the National Research Council for Scientific Research (CNRS), and the University of Orléans. It was established on October 21, 1956, and became part of the Observatoire des sciences de l’Univers de la région centre (OSUC) in 2009.
4de2544e-b67e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Astronomy Facility at Nançay Radioastronomy Observatory

4dec2566-ba19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Moorook is a location in South Australia, situated at Battams Road within the District Council of Loxton Waikerie. It hosts an astronomical observatory known as SNX-NET, Moorook.
4dec2566-ba19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Moorook Observatory, Australia

4df332b6-ba5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Fort Nelson Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG since 2007.
4df332b6-ba5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission GMAG

4df8a09e-b7d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Xinjiang Astronomical Observatory's Nanshan Station is an astronomical observatory located in Ürümqi County, China, dedicated to ground-based observations.
4df8a09e-b7d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Xinjiang Observatory at Nanshan Station, China

4e0c066e-b7f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
DSS-17 is a ground observatory, part of the Deep Space Network (DSN), operated by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory for tracking and communicating with interplanetary spacecraft. It is equipped with facilities to support deep-space missions and astronomical observations.
4e0c066e-b7f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep Space Station 17

4e100626-b5b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plateau Astronomique de La Couronne (PALC) is a ground-based observatory located in Cordes-sur-Ciel, Albi, Tarn, Occitania, France. It is situated at latitude 44.083 and longitude 1.94844 on the European continent.
4e100626-b5b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plateau Astronomique La Couronne, France

4e13eeb4-bb5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Americus (AMER) Fluxgate Magnetometer is a type of magnetometer located at the Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain (McMAC) Americus station. It measures magnetic field variations as part of broader geophysical research initiatives.
4e13eeb4-bb5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain

4e1600a4-b95e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Casellina Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Scandicci, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations.
4e1600a4-b95e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Casellina Observatory, Italy

4e294d96-b6a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Energetic Particle Monitor (EPM)** on GOES 8 is an instrument designed to detect and analyze high-energy particles, specifically protons, alpha particles, and electrons. It consists of three main components: the EP8 Telescope, Dome Assembly, and High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector (HEPAD), which together provide measurements across various energy channels.
4e294d96-b6a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Monitor on GOES 8

4e2c5718-b757-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in the Gabriela Mistral International Dark Skies Sanctuary, Vicuña, Chile.
4e2c5718-b757-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cerro Tololo Observatory, Chile

4e338852-b6ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Low-Energy Ion Detector (LEID)** is an instrument on the Double Star 2 spacecraft designed to measure and analyze low-energy ions in Earth's magnetosphere. It utilizes electrostatic analysis to characterize ion populations, contributing valuable data for understanding solar wind interactions with Earth’s magnetic field.
4e338852-b6ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low-Energy Ion Detector on Double Star 2

4e54f556-b5e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Ashibetu Station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located at the Seisa University Asahikawa Campus in Ashibetsu, Hokkaido Prefecture, Japan. It is part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network and monitors geomagnetic activity for scientific research.
4e54f556-b5e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer network at Ashibetsu, Japan

4e61cf6e-b8e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ingenio Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Ingenio, Las Palmas, on the Canary Islands of Spain. It operates as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
4e61cf6e-b8e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ingenio Observatory, Spain

4e682cd2-ba60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Heavy Ion Counter (HIC) aboard the Galileo spacecraft is an instrument designed to monitor energetic heavy nuclei from carbon to nickel within the Jovian magnetosphere, enhancing our understanding of trapped heavy ions and their impact on spacecraft electronics. It is a modified version of the Voyager Cosmic-Ray Science instrument with improved measurement capabilities.
4e682cd2-ba60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heavy Ion Counter on Galileo

4e6ca228-b716-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Beaconsfield Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Knotty Green, Buckinghamshire, England, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
4e6ca228-b716-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Beaconsfield Observatory, United Kingdom

4e723446-ba03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF crossed loop antenna at Gakona, Alaska, is a specialized instrument designed to measure very low frequency (VLF) and extremely low frequency (ELF) magnetic field variations, featuring a 5-meter height and a sensitivity peak at 8kHz.
4e723446-ba03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Low Frequency / Extremely Low Frequency crossed loop antenna at IUGONET Observatory

4e778a66-b86b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "DMSP_5D3-F15 Positions" dataset provides the spacecraft positions of the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) 5D-3 F15 satellite in various coordinate systems. This information is crucial for tracking and analyzing the satellite's orbit and movements.
4e778a66-b86b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: DMSP 5D3-F15 on DMSP 5D3-F15 spacecraft

4e785038-b5f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument that measures the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Magnetometer at Huancayo, identified by IAGA code HUA, has been operational since 1922 as part of a ground-based observatory for studying Earth's magnetic field.
4e785038-b5f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Huancayo Observatory

4e85eb4e-b7ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: Mill Creek Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Wasco County, Oregon, United States. It is situated at 7030 Mill Creek Road and operates as a ground-based observatory.
4e85eb4e-b7ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mill Creek Observatory, United States

4e8c5a10-b73d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plonsk Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Płońsk, Masovian Voivodeship, Poland. It is a ground-based facility used for observing celestial objects and phenomena.
4e8c5a10-b73d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Płońsk Observatory, Poland

4e8d52cc-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Katanning of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network is a ground facility located in Katanning, Australia. It measures magnetic field variations and contributes to the global IUGONET monitoring system.
4e8d52cc-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Katanning Observatory, Australia

4e941922-ba7f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The IAGA:DEK Magnetometer was an instrument located at the Dekelia observatory that measured magnetic fields from 1935 to 1939 as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigations.
4e941922-ba7f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dekelia Observatory

4ea0843c-b73c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Eglin AFB, Florida, USA (URSI-code: EG931) is a ground facility equipped with a Digisonde that measures the angle of arrival, polarization, and Doppler frequency shift of signals reflected from the ionosphere to study its characteristics.
4ea0843c-b73c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Station at Eglin Air Force Base Observatory, United States

4ea208dc-ba27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** An Carraig Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Loughinisland, Northern Ireland, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects.
4ea208dc-ba27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: An Carraig Observatory, United Kingdom

4ea3d456-b5da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Little Moose Observatory (code: V13) is an astronomical observatory located in Timber Lakes, Wasatch County, Utah, United States. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to celestial observations and research.
4ea3d456-b5da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Timber Lake Observatory, United States

4ea7c2e0-b97d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Energetic Particle Sensor (EPS) on GOES 15 is an instrument designed to measure energetic particles, including protons, electrons, and alpha particles, at geosynchronous orbit. It provides continuous monitoring of the radiation environment for operational alerts, satellite design guidelines, and research purposes.
4ea7c2e0-b97d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Sensor on GOES 15

4eafd97e-b5e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mercator Telescope is a 1.2 m optical telescope located at the Observatorio del Roque de Los Muchachos on La Palma, Canary Islands, operated by Katholieke Universiteit Leuven in collaboration with the University of Geneva and primarily focused on exoplanet research.
4eafd97e-b5e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.2m Mercator Telescope at Roque de Los Muchachos Observatory, Spain

4eb1651e-b76d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pueblo Magnetometer is an instrument located at the Pueblo (PBLO) Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS GBO Network, used for measuring magnetic fields since May 13, 2009.
4eb1651e-b76d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pueblo Geophysical Observatory

4eb42480-b690-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The S-300 Search Coil Magnetometer is an instrument on the GEOS-1 spacecraft that measures AC magnetic fields up to 30 kHz, DC/AC electric fields, plasma resonances up to 80 kHz, and mutual and self-impedance using a combination of sensors mounted on radial and axial booms.
4eb42480-b690-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Magnetometer on GEOS-1

4eb6cbc0-bb47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Petit Jean Mountain Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located on Petit Jean Mountain in Conway County, Arkansas, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
4eb6cbc0-bb47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Petit Jean Mountain Observatory, United States

4eba9b2a-b76d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes a magnetometer instrument located at the Arctic Ice Flo station with the IAGA identifier AIF, operational from January 1957 to December 1958 as part of the IUGONET observatory.
4eba9b2a-b76d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observatory WDC Kyoto WDC AIF

4ec679b4-b73f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Newcastle-upon-Tyne Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Coxlodge, Newcastle upon Tyne, England. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial objects and phenomena.
4ec679b4-b73f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Newcastle-upon-Tyne Observatory, United Kingdom

4ec869f8-b67d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The JMA electrometer is a magnetometer instrument deployed at the Kyoto WDC Observatory, designed to measure geoelectric fields using perpendicularly aligned carbon rods in N-S and E-W directions.
4ec869f8-b67d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of WDC Kyoto Observatory

4ecdf660-bb97-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Narama Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Odole, Narama, in the Lesser Poland Voivodeship of Poland. It operates as a ground-based facility and has been assigned MPC ID B45.
4ecdf660-bb97-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Narama Observatory, Poland

4edeac04-b6cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Pioneer 10 is a NASA space probe launched in March 1972. It was the first mission to explore the outer solar system and investigate Jupiter, subsequently following an escape trajectory from the solar system.
4edeac04-b6cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pioneer 10 part of Pioneer Program

4efc359e-bb23-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bucharest Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bucharest, Romania, notable for being the city's only observatory open to the public.
4efc359e-bb23-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bucharest Observatory, Romania

4efd5b70-b5e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: XRISM is a collaborative space mission between JAXA, NASA, and ESA designed for advanced X-ray imaging and spectroscopy in space.
4efd5b70-b5e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency/NASA/European Space Agency X-Ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission

4f01d410-b914-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Vallauris Observatory (code: B51) is an astronomical observatory located in Golfe-Juan, Vallauris, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
4f01d410-b914-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Vallauris Observatory, France

4f026012-b854-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IAGA:KVA Magnetometer was a ground-based instrument located at the Karavia observatory, operational from January 1958 to December 31, 1961, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigations.
4f026012-b854-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Karavia Observatory

4f0aabb6-baff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Electrostatic Analyzer** on the ISEE 1 spacecraft was part of an experiment to study electron and proton fluxes in the outer magnetosphere. It measured electrons and protons at specific energy levels using a combination of semiconductor-detector telescopes and fixed-voltage electrostatic analyzers to understand particle phenomena in space.
4f0aabb6-baff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of International Sun Earth Explorer Mission

4f0b625e-b61d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **PHOBOS-1 Plasma Wave System (PWS)** is an instrument onboard the PHOBOS-1 spacecraft designed to study electric field fluctuations in the interplanetary medium and Martian magnetosphere, measure plasma density, assess spacecraft potential, and investigate wave activity resulting from solar wind interactions with Phobos.
4f0b625e-b61d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Wave System part of Phobos 1

4f11dcc8-b7a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High Energy Electron Detector (HEED) is an instrument on the Double Star 1 spacecraft designed to measure the flux of energetic electrons within Earth's magnetosphere.
4f11dcc8-b7a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Energy Electron Detector on Double Star 1

4f165fe6-b6a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/S20, SESS Special Sensor Ultraviolet Spectrographic Imager (SESS/SSULI) is an imaging spectrometer onboard the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program that observes Extreme and Far UV radiation from Earth's limb to measure electron density vertical profiles as well as ion and neutral densities.
4f165fe6-b6a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Ultraviolet Spectrographic Imager on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program 5D-3/S20

4f1c834a-b7ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Chilbolton station with the IAGA identifier CLB. It is part of the WDC Kyoto observatory network and was previously identified as spase://SMWG/Instrument/IAGA/Chilbolton/Magnetometer.
4f1c834a-b7ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Chilbolton Observatory

4f1d7fec-b6c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Bruno Zugna Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Basovizza, Trieste, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
4f1d7fec-b6c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bruno Zugna Observatory, Italy

4f23244a-ba08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The UAS-ISON Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Cosalá, Sinaloa, Mexico. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
4f23244a-ba08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: UAS-ISON Observatory, Mexico

4f244426-bb69-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AGO P2 Photometer Instrument is a photometric device located at the AGO P2 ground station, used for measuring light intensity and related properties as part of the ICESTAR observatory.
4f244426-bb69-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Photometer part of ICESTAR investigation

4f25bda4-b64d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mass Spectrum Analyzer** is a key sensor within the Mercury Plasma Particle Experiment (MPPE) suite onboard Mio, designed to measure mass-resolved 3D distribution functions of ions from 1 eV/q up to 38 keV/q, providing insights into magnetospheric plasma dynamics and characterizing planetary ions like Na+ or K+.
4f25bda4-b64d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrum Analyzer part of Mercury Plasma Particle Experiment

4f33ce08-ba2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Island Lake is a ground observatory located on Earth’s surface, part of the CARISMA network. It features a magnetometer for monitoring geomagnetic activity.
4f33ce08-ba2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Island Lake Magnetometer at Island Lake Observatory

4f3acc40-b926-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **OBSTECH's Observatorio El Sauce 0.6m telescope** is an optical telescope located in South America with a 0.6-meter aperture, used for astronomical observations and research.
4f3acc40-b926-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 0.6m Telescope at Observatorio El Sauce

4f44a980-bba2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Julianehaab Geomagnetic Observatory (JUL) was a ground-based facility located in Qaqortoq, Greenland, that operated from 1932 to 1965, primarily for geomagnetic measurements.
4f44a980-bba2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Julianehaab Geomagnetic Observatory

4f474dc8-b677-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lovell Telescope is a 76.2-meter diameter radio telescope located at the Jodrell Bank Observatory in Europe, operated by the Jodrell Bank Centre for Astrophysics.
4f474dc8-b677-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 76.2m Lovell Telescope at Jodrell Bank Observatory

4f4a16b0-b6c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Daneborg (DNB) Geophysical Observatory, located in Daneborg, Greenland, is a ground-based facility that began operations on January 1, 2007, and includes instruments such as magnetometers for geophysical research.
4f4a16b0-b6c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Daneborg Geophysical Observatory, Greenland

4f4ac588-b952-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes the ground-observatory known as "Metzerlen," located at Riedmattweg in Metzerlen, Switzerland (latitude: 47.46273° N, longitude: 7.46° E), situated on the continent of Europe.
4f4ac588-b952-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Metzerlen Observatory, Switzerland

4f59b8e0-b5a1-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: Helwan Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Helwan district of Cairo, Egypt, which began operations on January 1, 1903.
4f59b8e0-b5a1-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Helwan Observatory, Egypt

4f6d5226-b9c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Göttingen-1 Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field, located at the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) station in Göttingen. It has been operational since January 1957.
4f6d5226-b9c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Göttingen Observatory
