59e32090-b767-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kitt Peak Vacuum Telescope (KPVT) was an instrument used for solar imaging at the Kitt Peak National Observatory. It operated from 1973 to 2002 and provided various types of data from daily full-disk observations of the sun, including magnetic fields, HeI 1083 nm equivalent width, CaII K line intensity, and continuum intensity.
59e32090-b767-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager on Kitt Peak Vacuum Telescope at Kitt Peak Observatory

59f527f6-bbca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the ephemeris data for the DMSP_5D2-F11 spacecraft, detailing its positions in various coordinate systems as part of the DMSP 5D-2 F11 observatory.
59f527f6-bbca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Positions part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

59f7d026-bbb8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VERA project, operated by the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ), is a space mission focused on radio astrometry using Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI).
59f7d026-bbb8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio National Astronomical Observatory of Japan VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry project

5a0669ec-b8fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Athabasca University THEMIS UCLA Magnetometer Network (AUTUMN) is a ground-based facility consisting of a magnetometer array primarily situated in Quebec, Canada. It operates from the Earth's surface and began functioning on November 1, 2014.
5a0669ec-b8fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Inukjuak Observatory, Canada

5a12728e-baad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GONG instrument at Learmonth Observatory is part of the Global Oscillation Network Group, a network dedicated to studying solar internal structure and dynamics using helioseismology through continuous observations of the Sun's oscillations.
5a12728e-baad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Interferometer part of Global Oscillation Network Group on Learmonth Observatory

5a1ba4d0-b8e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at Wake Island (WKE) used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IAGA observatory network.
5a1ba4d0-b8e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers part of IUGONET Observatory

5a1f757a-b7cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2D Data Processing Unit (DPU)** is a versatile instrument controller board designed for the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) mission, responsible for acquiring data from various onboard sensors and managing communications and control functions.
5a1f757a-b7cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

5a296b9e-b60a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Van Rensselaer Observatory** is a ground-based facility in Avannaata, Greenland, that has been operational since January 1854. It primarily hosts a magnetometer and contributes to the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network.
5a296b9e-b60a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Van Rensselaer, Greenland

5a320a42-bb7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1Q X-ray Instrument (XRI) is a scintillation detector used in the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) project to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays, helping study precipitating electrons with an energy response from 10 keV to 10 MeV.
5a320a42-bb7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

5a425cb2-bb87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Biosphere 2 Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at the Biosphere 2 Research Center in Pinal County, Arizona, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observation.
5a425cb2-bb87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Biosphere 2 Observatory, United States

5a465962-b6f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Ursa Havaintokeskus, Artjärvi**: An observatory located in Kimonkyläntie, Suurikylä, Orimattila, Finland. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
5a465962-b6f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Artjärvi Observatory, Finland

5a48a63a-b9de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Hermsdorf Observatory:** A ground-based facility in Sobięcin, Poland that operated from 1901 to 1929, housing magnetometers for geomagnetic measurements as part of the IAGA observatory network.
5a48a63a-b9de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hermsdorf Observatory, Poland

5a4bfdba-b9c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS Digital Fields Board Filter Bank is an instrument component that provides band-pass filtering for various spectra and signals onboard the THEMIS spacecraft, designed to be less computationally intensive than traditional methods like Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). It processes and averages data through a series of low-pass filters and decimation steps, ultimately compressing the output for efficient data management.
5a4bfdba-b9c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digital Fields Board and Filter Bank part of Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms

5a5457aa-b736-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Oak Ridge Observatory (ORO), also known as the George R. Agassiz Station, is an astronomical observatory located in Harvard, Massachusetts, operated by the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian from 1933 until 2005.
5a5457aa-b736-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.5m Wyeth Telescope at Oak Ridge Observatory, United States

5a54737a-ba1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is the ground-based observatory located in Opicina, Trieste, Italy, specifically at 81/1, Via di Monrupino. It is situated at coordinates 45.69388° N latitude and 13.79647° E longitude in the Friuli – Venezia Giulia region of Europe.
5a54737a-ba1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triestecode Observatory, Italy

5a71979c-b656-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mount Lemmon Observing Facility (MLOF) is an astronomical observatory located at Mount Lemmon, operated by the University of Minnesota, featuring a 1.52-meter telescope for research and observation purposes.
5a71979c-b656-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.52m Telescope at Mount Lemmon Observing Facility

5a7536dc-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU Radio Beacon Receiver (GRBR) at Manado, Indonesia is a digital receiver designed for measuring ionospheric total electron content (TEC) using signals from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. It employs open-source software and hardware, specifically GNU Radio and the Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP), to process beacon signals at 150 and 400 MHz.
5a7536dc-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver GNU Radio Beacon Receiver at Manado Observatory, Indonesia

5a761340-b5b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The TWINS1 Lyman-alpha Detector (LAD) is an instrument on the TWINS mission, consisting of two sensors designed to measure Lyman-alpha radiation from neutral hydrogen atoms, providing full azimuthal coverage with a time resolution of 60 seconds.
5a761340-b5b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lyman-alpha Detector on Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometer

5a81e1b2-b6cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Bayfordbury Observatory**: An astronomical and atmospheric physics remote sensing observatory owned by the University of Hertfordshire, located in Bayfordbury, England. It is one of the largest teaching observatories in the UK, used for academic research and public outreach.
5a81e1b2-b6cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bayfordbury Observatory

5a84e440-b96d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Compton Gamma Ray Observatory (CGRO) was a space observatory designed to detect gamma rays, the most energetic form of light. It operated from 1991 to 2000, providing groundbreaking insights into high-energy phenomena in the universe.
5a84e440-b96d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Compton Gamma Ray Observatory

5a8fcf9a-ba3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tomsk State University Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Tomsk, Russia. Established in 1923, it is a ground-based facility situated at an altitude of 137 meters.
5a8fcf9a-ba3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tomsk State University Observatory, Russia

5a95550a-bb4d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Palo Alto Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Palo Alto, California, USA, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects.
5a95550a-bb4d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Palo Alto Observatory, United States

5a985d16-ba4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: San Pedro de Atacama Ground Observatory (ABYO) is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Orilla Solor, San Pedro de Atacama, Chile. It operates at an altitude conducive to high-quality observations due to its clear skies and low light pollution.
5a985d16-ba4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Atacama Bio-Optics Observatory, Chile

5aad702e-b5ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Etah Magnetometer is a ground-based instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at the ETAP station as part of the IAGA investigation, operational from 1908 to 1947.
5aad702e-b5ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eskdalemuir Observatory

5ab2208c-b665-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Planetario di Anzi is an astronomical observatory located in Anzi, Italy, specifically designed for planetary observations.
5ab2208c-b665-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Planetary Astronomical Observatory of Anzi at Potenza Observatory, Italy

5ab7b3ce-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hadano Observatory (MPC ID: 355) is an astronomical institution located in Hino, Tokyo, Japan, dedicated to ground-based observations.
5ab7b3ce-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hadano Observatory

5ab8850c-ba53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Koeditz Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Köditz, Bavaria, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial bodies.
5ab8850c-ba53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Köditz Observatory, Germany

5abc77f8-b7f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Solar Wind Plasma Analyzer (OPA)** on the Pioneer Venus Orbiter is an electrostatic analyzer designed to measure solar wind conditions and study the ionopause structure of Venus, featuring a quadrispherical design with five current collectors and electrometers.
5abc77f8-b7f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Pioneer Venus Orbiter

5ac0d8e4-bba0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: La Quiaca Geomagnetic Observatory (LQA) was a ground-based facility in Argentina that operated from 1920 to 1992, specializing in geomagnetic measurements.
5ac0d8e4-bba0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at La Quiaca Geomagnetic Observatory, Argentina

5acb2b18-b912-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Spain's National Geographic Institute (IGN) Yebes Observatory 13.2 m radio telescope is a facility located in Europe, specifically in Yebes, Spain, designed for radio astronomy with an aperture of 13.2 meters.
5acb2b18-b912-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 13.2m Radio Telescope at Spain's National Geographic Institute Yebes Observatory

5acf0d58-b69e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High-Energy Cosmic Rays (HECR) instrument on the ISEE-3 observatory is designed to measure the isotopic abundance of primary cosmic rays from hydrogen through nickel, utilizing a 10-element solid-state particle telescope and a six-plane drift chamber for directional data.
5acf0d58-b69e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High-Energy Cosmic Rays part of International Sun-Earth Explorer 3

5adb081a-ba3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ALPHA-3 experiment's **Ion Trap** is an instrument aboard the Interball Tail Probe designed to study cold magnetospheric plasma using planar electrostatic analyzers, capable of measuring particle energies up to 25.5 eV and proton densities as low as 1 per cc.
5adb081a-ba3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Interball Mission

5aebab2c-b732-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gjoahavn Geomagnetic Observatory (GJO) was a ground-based facility located in Gjoa Haven, Canada, that operated from 1903 to 1905. It was part of the IUGONET network and focused on geomagnetic measurements using instruments like magnetometers.
5aebab2c-b732-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Gjoahavn Geomagnetic Observatory

5b1fe5d6-ba16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Bohyunsan Optical Astronomy Observatory (BOAO) is an astronomical observatory located in South Korea, known for its 1.8-meter telescope and ground-based observation facilities.
5b1fe5d6-ba16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.8m Telescope at Bohyunsan Optical Astronomy Observatory, South Korea

5b233710-b717-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Thompson, part of the IAGA investigation, used for measuring magnetic fields since 1969.
5b233710-b717-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at IUGONET Observatory

5b2432b2-ba39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Esashi ground station that measures magnetic field data and is part of the IUGONET-observatory network.
5b2432b2-ba39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Esashi Observatory

5b30e6de-b7db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Olmen Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Olmen, Belgium. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
5b30e6de-b7db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Olmen Observatory, Belgium

5b312942-ba5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Marina di Cerveteri Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Marina di Cerveteri, Italy. It is situated at Via Umberto Cetra, Cerenova Costantica, Cerveteri, Roma Capitale, Lazio, and operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research.
5b312942-ba5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Marina di Cerveteri Observatory, Italy

5b342564-b95d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Max Planck Institute for Astronomy and Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia (CSIC) 2.2m Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Calar Alto Observatory in Europe, used for astronomical research.
5b342564-b95d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.2m optical Max Planck Institute for Astronomy and Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia Telescope at Calar Alto Observatory

5b363770-b839-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectrometer (NGIMS) was a quadrupole mass spectrometer onboard the CONTOUR spacecraft, designed to measure both neutral gases and ambient ions during comet encounters using two optimized sources.
5b363770-b839-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectrometer part of Contour

5b3f53c8-b5a0-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1U Data Processing Unit (DPU)** is a general-purpose instrument controller board designed for the BARREL balloon missions, which acquires data from various scientific instruments and controls communication systems.
5b3f53c8-b5a0-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL)

5b4cd5b2-b7c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IAGA:LUB Magnetometer was an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields, operational from January 1, 1885 to December 31, 1893 at the Lübeck observatory as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
5b4cd5b2-b7c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lübeck Observatory

5b51be2a-bad5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ) 0.91m Telescope at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory (OAO) is an optical telescope located in Asia, specifically at the Okayama Astrophysical Observatory in Japan. It has an aperture of 0.91 meters and is used for astronomical observations.
5b51be2a-bad5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 0.91m National Astronomical Observatory of Japan Telescope at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory

5b54f038-bb05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bologna University Northern Cross Radio Telescope Array is a radio telescope facility located in Medicina Radio Astronomical Station, Italy, dedicated to astronomical observations in the radio waveband.
5b54f038-bb05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Northern Cross Radio Telescope Array at Medicina Radio Astronomical Station

5b556e90-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The "Electrostatic Waves and Radio Noise" instrument on IMP-8 was a set of receivers and antenna systems designed to observe the magnetic and electric field intensities, frequency spectra, polarization, and direction of arrival of naturally occurring radio noise in the magnetosphere. It studied phenomena related to the distribution, origin, propagation, and characteristics of radio noise across the magnetospheric boundary region, with a frequency range of 0.3 Hz to 200 kHz for electric fields and 20 Hz to 200 kHz for magnetic fields.
5b556e90-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Waves and Radio Noise on IMP-8

5b57d4b0-b72c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Americus Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation since March 8, 2006.
5b57d4b0-b72c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Americus Observatory

5b66937c-b832-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The TechDome Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Mayhill, New Mexico, USA. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
5b66937c-b832-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: TechDome Observatory, United States

5b79ee24-bae2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) Accelerometer is an instrument aboard the MRO spacecraft that measures changes in velocity due to aerodynamic forces during aerobraking, providing data at 1-second intervals.
5b79ee24-bae2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Accelerometer on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter

5b7f8d58-b7ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Abinger Geomagnetic Observatory**: A ground-based facility in Surrey, England that operated from 1925 to 1957, dedicated to measuring and recording geomagnetic data.
5b7f8d58-b7ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Abinger Geomagnetic Observatory, United Kingdom

5b86990c-bb6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The CLPS Task Order 2-AB NIRVSS is an instrument system on the Peregrine lunar lander designed to measure and analyze lunar surface materials, capturing millimeter-scale morphology, spectral signatures, and temperature using its imaging module, near infrared spectrometer, and calibration sensor.
5b86990c-bb6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Infrared Volatiles Spectrometer System on Peregrine Lunar Lander

5b87b13e-b83b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Katori Observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Katori, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. It focuses on ground-based observations of celestial phenomena and is recognized with the MPC ID Q24.
5b87b13e-b83b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Katori Observatory, Japan

5b88607a-b5f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cancelada Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Estepona, Malaga, Andalusia, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility for observing celestial objects.
5b88607a-b5f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cancelada Observatory, Spain

5bafffde-b851-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Pla D'Arguines Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Algímia d'Alfara, Valencia, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility with an altitude of 126 meters and has been active since January 2000.
5bafffde-b851-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Pla D'Arguines Observatory, Spain

5bb678c6-b9a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ion Mass Spectrometer (OIMS)** on the **Pioneer Venus Orbiter** was an instrument designed to measure and analyze thermal positive ions in Venus's ionosphere, providing insights into solar wind interactions, atmospheric photochemistry, and mass/heat transport.
5bb678c6-b9a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Mass Spectrometer on Pioneer Venus Orbiter

5bebb890-b7c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Interball-1 different magnetospheric analytical models" refer to a set of analytical tools used for studying the Earth's magnetosphere based on data from the Interball-1 spacecraft. These models are part of the CDPP (Centre de Données de la Physique des Plasmas) archive and provide insights into various magnetic phenomena observed during the mission.
5bebb890-b7c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetospheric Analytical Models part of Interball-1

5bf3c5ce-b7df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Andenes Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, which began operation on December 30, 2006.
5bf3c5ce-b7df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Andenes Observatory

5bf45cf0-bb4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Radcliffe Observatory was the astronomical observatory of the University of Oxford from 1773 until 1934 and is now part of Green Templeton College. It is a Grade I listed building located in Oxford, United Kingdom.
5bf45cf0-bb4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radcliffe Observatory

5bf498fe-b696-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Ad Astra Sangos Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Alhendín, Granada, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility for celestial observations and research.
5bf498fe-b696-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ad Astra Sangos Observatory, Spain

5bfa8590-b6f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Utsunomiya-Imaizumi Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Utsunomiya, Tochigi Prefecture, Japan, known for its ground-based observations.
5bfa8590-b6f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Utsunomiya-Imaizumi Observatory, Japan

5c02b282-bb63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific MAGDAS (Magnetic Data Acquisition System) magnetometer installed at Ancon, Peru, is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer that operates as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
5c02b282-bb63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observatory

5c09a0ca-b789-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Kazan Observatory (identified as KZN by IAGA), operational from 1892 to 1992.
5c09a0ca-b789-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kazan Observatory

5c0ada46-bb56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Deep Space Network's DSS-23 is a 34-meter radio telescope located at the Goldstone Observatory in North America, used for radio astronomy observations.
5c0ada46-bb56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34.0m Radio Telescope part of The Deep Space Network

5c120338-bb5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ephemeris: Saturn Moons** is a dataset that provides the positional data and specific coordinate systems for the moons of Saturn, part of the Cassini mission under the CNES observatory.
5c120338-bb5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Saturn Moons Ephemeris part of Cassini Mission

5c12bf74-ba55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Haagaar Observatory**: A ground-based astronomical observatory located in Eina, Norway, dedicated to studying celestial objects and phenomena.
5c12bf74-ba55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Eina Observatory, Norway

5c1abb4e-b153-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Gaisberg Observatory, Schärding** is a ground-based observatory located in Schärding, Upper Austria. It is informed by the IAU-MPC list and situated at coordinates 48.54304° N, 13.4744° E.
5c1abb4e-b153-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Gaisberg Observatory, Austria

5c214838-bc7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Marl Observatory (MPC ID: 605) is an astronomical observatory located in Marl, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It functions as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
5c214838-bc7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Marl Observatory, Germany

5c3e2706-b710-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Sounding of the Atmosphere using Broadband Emission Radiometry (SABER) instrument is an infrared radiometer onboard the TIMED satellite, designed to measure Earth limb emissions and vertical distributions of atmospheric constituents and temperature. It operates within a wavelength range of 1.27 to 16.9 micrometers, providing high-resolution data from the Earth's surface up to an altitude of approximately 180 kilometers.
5c3e2706-b710-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sounding of the Atmosphere using Broadband Emission Radiometry on TIMED

5c449dec-b775-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MESSENGER X-Ray Spectrometer (XRS) was an instrument aboard the MESSENGER spacecraft designed to measure X-rays emitted from Mercury's surface in the energy range of 1 to 10 keV, using three identical gas proportional counters with various filters to identify specific elements.
5c449dec-b775-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-Ray Spectrometer on MESSENGER spacecraft

5c4b21f4-b670-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1V Data Processing Unit (DPU) is an instrument controller board that collects data from various sensors, formats it, and transmits it via an Iridium modem. It is designed to be flexible and has been used in multiple sounding rocket experiments and balloon flights.
5c4b21f4-b670-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for Radiation Belts Relativistic Electron Losses

5c557aaa-ba35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Belgrade Observatory is an astronomical observatory situated in the Zvezdara Forest in eastern Belgrade, Serbia.
5c557aaa-ba35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Belgrade Observatory, Serbia

5c5fd066-b604-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cosmic Ray Particles Experiment on Helios-B (E6)** was an investigation conducted to study high-energy charged cosmic-ray particles from solar, planetary, and galactic origins in interplanetary space using a sophisticated particle telescope.
5c5fd066-b604-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cosmic Ray Particles Experiment on Helios-B

5c60332e-bb65-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Stardreams Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Vălenii de Munte, Prahova, Romania. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
5c60332e-bb65-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stardreams Observatory at Vălenii de Munte, Romania

5c6847d4-b99a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Haleakala Neutron Monitor is a ground-based scientific facility located at the Haleakala Observatory in Maui County, Hawaii. It operates as part of Tohoku University and is situated at an altitude of 3030 meters on Earth's surface, primarily used for monitoring neutrons.
5c6847d4-b99a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutron Monitor at Haleakala Observatory

5c6d9568-b850-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/F16 Operational Linescan System (OLS) is an imaging instrument onboard the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program's F16 satellite, launched in 2003, which measures visible and infrared wavelengths to provide global cloud cover imagery at varying resolutions.
5c6d9568-b850-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Operational Linescan System part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

5c6ed58a-ba72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The 9-channel ELF/VLF (Extremely Low Frequency/Very Low Frequency) receiver at Isafjordur, Iceland is an instrument used for atmospheric and ionospheric research as part of the IUGONET observatory. It captures electromagnetic signals in the ELF/VLF range to study phenomena such as lightning discharges and auroral activity.
5c6ed58a-ba72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna part of Conjugate Observation at Iceland

5c7c2c26-b923-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Roving Observer** is a spacecraft within the Unistellar Network, dedicated to astronomical observations and data collection. It operates under the code 270 and is identified by its unique type in the VOParis namespace.
5c7c2c26-b923-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Unistellar Network

5c8e9bd2-b91d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** A magnetometer situated at the IAGA-identified station "ASC" on Ascension Island, operational since January 1, 1993.
5c8e9bd2-b91d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Ascension Island Observatory

5c91fdba-b7cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Siding Spring-LCO Clamshell #2**: An astronomical observatory located at Coonabarabran Airport in New South Wales, Australia.
5c91fdba-b7cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: [Entity Not Clearly Identified] at Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

5ca3f136-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Terrassa Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Terrassa, Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. It is used for ground-based observations and research in astronomy.
5ca3f136-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terrassa Observatory, Spain

5ca9481c-bab5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **1.9m Telescope** is an astronomical telescope located at Mount Stromlo Observatory in Canberra, Australia, with a primary mirror diameter of 1.9 meters and situated at an altitude of 760 meters above sea level.
5ca9481c-bab5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.9m Telescope at Mount Stromlo Observatory, Australia

5cafb082-b725-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Colchester Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Heathlands Church of England Voluntary Controlled Primary School in West Bergholt, Colchester, Essex, United Kingdom. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
5cafb082-b725-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Colchester Observatory, United Kingdom

5cb1cb54-ba01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NOAA 9 spacecraft, launched in December 1984, was a satellite in a sun-synchronous orbit equipped with instruments like the AVHRR and TOVS for Earth observation and environmental monitoring.
5cb1cb54-ba01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Backscatter UV Radiometer on NOAA 9

5cb24dde-b67f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Baguio Geomagnetic Observatory (BAG)** is a ground-based facility located in Baguio, Philippines, operated from 1964 to 1983, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements.
5cb24dde-b67f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Baguio Geomagnetic Observatory, Philippines

5cc04bee-b929-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Josef Bresser Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Borken, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is a ground-based facility used for observing celestial bodies and conducting astronomical research.
5cc04bee-b929-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Josef Bresser Observatory, Germany

5cc2f6c4-b676-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Space Tracking and Communications Center (JAXA)** is an astronomical observatory located in Biseicho-Okura, Ibara, Okayama Prefecture, Japan. It serves as a ground-based facility for tracking space missions and communicating with satellites operated by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA).
5cc2f6c4-b676-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Tracking and Communications Center at Biseicho-Okura Observatory, Japan

5cc70496-bac5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gamma Ray Burst Detector (OGBD) on the Pioneer Venus Orbiter was an omnidirectional instrument designed to detect and study high-energy gamma-ray bursts from astronomical sources using two Phoswich scintillation spectrometers sensitive to photons ranging from 0.1 to 2.0 MeV.
5cc70496-bac5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma Ray Burst Detector on Pioneer Venus Orbiter

5ccdf796-bb57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 90Prime Mosaic Camera is a large-format astronomical camera used for wide-field imaging at the Kitt Peak National Observatory. It is primarily utilized for conducting surveys and scientific research, particularly in areas such as galaxy and star formation, stellar evolution, and cosmic structure.
5ccdf796-bb57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.3m Bok Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory

5cd36a1c-b9ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sterni Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Kempten, Bavaria, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observation.
5cd36a1c-b9ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sterni Observatory, Germany

5cd485a4-b876-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Kurashiki Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Kurashiki, Okayama Prefecture, Japan. It was established on November 1, 1926 and is designated as a ground-based observatory.
5cd485a4-b876-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kurashiki Observatory, Japan

5cdad732-b5e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tashkent-1 Observatory was a ground facility located in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, operating from 1883 to 1935, primarily for magnetic observations.
5cdad732-b5e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tashkent Observatory, Uzbekistan

5ce96e2e-bc8b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wilfred Hall Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Preston, England. It operates as a ground-based facility and is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with the code 989.
5ce96e2e-bc8b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Alston Lane Observatory, United Kingdom

5cef00c6-b701-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Goodsell Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Carleton College in Northfield, Minnesota, United States. It was constructed in 1887 and initially served as a significant timekeeping station, bringing national prominence to the college during its early years.
5cef00c6-b701-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Goodsell Observatory

5cef5cd8-b715-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Guido Ruggieri Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in San Carlo, Padua, Italy. It functions as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
5cef5cd8-b715-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Guido Ruggieri Observatory, Italy

5cf04db2-ba1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "ISEE Magnetometer" is an induction magnetometer located in Sata, Japan, designed to measure three-dimensional variations in the geomagnetic field with a sampling rate of 64 Hz, controlled by GPS clock signals. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network and provides high-resolution data for geomagnetic studies.
5cf04db2-ba1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Induction Magnetometer part of International Solar-Terrestrial Physics Mission

5cf71b48-b702-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at Ilorin (ILR) is a 3-axis ring-core type device installed in Nigeria, part of the MAGDAS observation network under IUGONET Observatory.
5cf71b48-b702-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System observation network

5d035032-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Antares Observatory is an astronomical facility located in San Eduardo, Villa Rosa, Partido del Pilar, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
5d035032-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antares Observatory, Argentina

5d07c9c6-b689-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Dikson Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, used to measure magnetic field variations since 2011.
5d07c9c6-b689-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dikson Geophysical Observatory

5d0cc692-bc8d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The UKS Electron Instrument (ELX) is an electrostatic analyzer onboard the AMPTE-UKS satellite designed to measure the three-dimensional velocity distribution of electrons in Earth's ionosphere. It uses two hemispherical analyzers with microchannel plate detectors to count incoming electrons in eight directional sectors, covering energy ranges from 6 eV to 25 keV.
5d0cc692-bc8d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer part of AMPTE-UKS

5d12a6da-b6a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Iqaluit Geomagnetic Observatory (IQA) is a ground-based facility located in Iqaluit, Nunavut, Canada, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity. It operates as part of the INTERMAGNET network and features instruments such as magnetometers from institutions like WDC Kyoto.
5d12a6da-b6a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iqaluit Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

5d166fa8-bbcf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Dutch Open Telescope** is an optical solar facility located at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory in Africa. It is part of a network for astronomical observations focused on studying the Sun.
5d166fa8-bbcf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Dutch Open Telescope at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory

5d23e47c-b7c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a simulation related to the Mars Global Surveyor (MGS) spacecraft, categorized under the Observatoire Virtuel - Paris seamless access data center's ontology for observational facilities.
5d23e47c-b7c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Global Surveyor Simulation

5d32c08a-b83d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The DSS-34 is a 34-meter radio telescope located in Canberra, Australia, part of NASA's Deep Space Network, used for radio astronomy observations and spacecraft communication.
5d32c08a-b83d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio The Deep Space Network Telescope at Canberra Observatory, Australia

5d36d21a-b860-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Whipple Observatory on Mt. Hopkins is a ground-based observatory located in Santa Cruz County, Arizona, United States, primarily used for astronomical research and observations. It is operated by the Smithsonian Institution.
5d36d21a-b860-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Whipple Observatory

5d40dcb6-bb16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Canada Foundation for Innovation Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) is a radio telescope located in North America, designed to map the intensity of hydrogen throughout the universe.
5d40dcb6-bb16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio The Canada Foundation for Innovation Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment

5d4411be-b6ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/F16 SESS Special Sensor Ionospheric Plasma Drift/Scintillation Monitor-3 (SESS/SSI/ES-3) is an instrument on the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program's F16 satellite that measures electron density, ion density, plasma drift, and scintillation at orbital altitudes. It has been operational since October 18, 2003.
5d4411be-b6ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Ionospheric Plasma Drift and Scintillation Monitor on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program 5D-3 F16

5d499840-b84d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tuntungan Observatory is a ground-based geomagnetic observatory located in North Sumatra, Indonesia. It has been operational since January 1999 and is part of the global network of magnetic observatories under the INTERMAGNET program.
5d499840-b84d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tuntungan Geomagnetic Observatory, Indonesia

5d4b5394-b620-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specified entity refers to magnetometers located at the Raciborz observatory, part of the WDC Kyoto network, which monitor geomagnetic activity.
5d4b5394-b620-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Raciborz Observatory

5d588f72-b6d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A riometer station located at Istok near Norilsk, Russia, developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research to study upper atmosphere dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions.
5d588f72-b6d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Riometer at Istok Observatory, Russia

5d745a58-bb95-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EISCAT Kiruna UHF receiver is a radar instrument used for atmospheric and ionospheric research, located at the Kiruna observatory in Sweden as part of the EISCAT scientific association. It operates in the ultra-high frequency (UHF) band to investigate the upper atmosphere and ionosphere.
5d745a58-bb95-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: UHF Receiver on EISCAT Radar Observation

5d8af8e4-b708-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The IAGA:FAL Magnetometer was an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at the Falmouth observatory from 1891 to 1912. It was part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
5d8af8e4-b708-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Falmouth Observatory

5d925746-b9fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located on Popov Island, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) network, used for measuring magnetic fields and is associated with ISEE/MM210 within the IUGONET observatory.
5d925746-b9fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observatory

5d9354da-bb31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a magnetometer located in Fort Simpson (identifier FSP), operational from 1990-01-01 to 1994-12-31, part of the IAGA investigation and associated with the THEMIS Ground CANMAG Observatory.
5d9354da-bb31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IAGA

5d99f68c-b71c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Consell Observatory (Observatori Astronòmic de Consell) is an astronomical observatory located in Consell on Majorca island, Spain. It is owned and operated by the Latin American League of Astronomy and situated at an altitude of 130 meters.
5d99f68c-b71c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Astronómico de Consell, Spain

5d9e8e08-bb8c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Atmospheric Structure Instrument (ASI) for the Galileo Probe was designed to measure atmospheric conditions during its descent into Jupiter's atmosphere, operating in two modes to accommodate high-speed entry and parachute descent, collecting data on temperature, pressure, and acceleration.
5d9e8e08-bb8c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Atmospheric Structure Instrument on Galileo Probe

5da09b7c-bba4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Magellan Spacecraft Radio Science Subsystem** was an instrument suite on the Magellan spacecraft that used radio signals to investigate Venus' atmosphere, surface, and gravity field, providing key data on the planet’s internal structure and topography.
5da09b7c-bba4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Subsystem on Magellan Spacecraft

5da98576-bbc1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL)**, specifically the BARREL Balloon 2N Ephemeris instrument, provides trajectory positions in various coordinate systems to study relativistic electron losses within Earth's radiation belts. This virtual instrument is part of the broader BARREL observatory mission.
5da98576-bbc1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses part of BARREL Observatory

5dab7806-b72d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Corona Experiment (SCE) on the Ulysses spacecraft was a radio science instrument designed to investigate the solar corona, focusing on measuring plasma density and properties during solar conjunctions. It utilized dual-frequency ranging and Doppler data in collaboration with the Deep Space Network (DSN).
5dab7806-b72d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Coronal Sounding part of Ulysses

5db23d50-b5c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Istanbul-Kandilli Geomagnetic Observatory (ISK), located in Turkey, is a ground-based facility dedicated to geomagnetic measurements and research. It operated from 1946 until at least 1998 and was part of the global network of World Data Centers for geomagnetism.
5db23d50-b5c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Istanbul Kandilli Geomagnetic Observatory, Turkey

5db47ee8-bc40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover Engineering Camera Suite (ECAM) is a set of nine cameras on the Perseverance Rover designed to assist in navigating Martian terrain and verifying sample collection. It includes Hazard Avoidance Cameras (HazCams), Navigation Cameras (NavCams), and a Sample Caching System Camera (CacheCam).
5db47ee8-bc40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Engineering Camera Suite part of Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover

5db4b780-ba49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Nozomi was a Japanese space probe intended to study the martian upper atmosphere and its interaction with the solar wind. It failed to enter Mars orbit due to electrical issues and subsequently remained in heliocentric orbit.
5db4b780-ba49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hope part of Nozomi Mission

5dba5d72-b5c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is an infrared space observatory launched on December 25, 2021, designed to study the early universe, galaxy formation, and exoplanets.
5dba5d72-b5c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: infrared 6.5m James Webb Space Telescope

5dbbecee-b666-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Peverell Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at 12 Peverell Park Road, Mutley, in Plymouth, England. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
5dbbecee-b666-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Peverell Observatory, United Kingdom

5dcc3ed8-b6f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Bouzareah Magnetometer was an instrument located at the IAGA-identified BZR station, operational from January 1888 to December 31, 1950, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IAGA investigation.
5dcc3ed8-b6f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bouzareah Observatory

5dccda66-b6d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Psyche Magnetometer (MAG) is an instrument onboard the Psyche spacecraft designed to detect and measure the remanent magnetic field of asteroid (16) Psyche using two high-sensitivity sensors positioned along a boom.
5dccda66-b6d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Psyche Magnetometer on Psyche Spacecraft

5dd2690e-b7e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ASPERA4_ELS (Electron Spectrometer) is an instrument on the Venus Express spacecraft that measures electrons in the energy range of 0.01-20 keV using a compact top-hat electrostatic analyzer with a field of view of 4 deg x 360 deg, divided into 16 sectors.
5dd2690e-b7e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Retarding Potential Analyser on Venus Express

5dd3f1b0-bafb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Global Oscillation Network Group (GONG) instrument at El Teide Observatory in the Canary Islands is part of a six-station network using interferometers for helioseismology to study solar internal structure and dynamics through continuous observations of the Sun's oscillations.
5dd3f1b0-bafb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Interferometer Global Oscillation Network Group part of El Teide Observatory, Canary Islands

5dd778d2-b6a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The CLPS TO 2-IM ROLSES is an instrument on the Nova-C lunar lander designed to measure charged lunar dust density using a low-frequency radio receiver, capturing signals between 10 kHz and 10 MHz near the Moon's surface.
5dd778d2-b6a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio wave The CLPS Task Order 2-IM Nova-C Lunar Lander Radio Wave Observation at the Lunar Surface of the Photoelectron Sheath on Nova-C Lunar Lander

5de0f932-bb9b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Minami-Oda Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Hyogo Prefecture, Japan. It operates as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
5de0f932-bb9b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Minami-Oda Observatory, Japan

5dee2736-b78d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bodo Geomagnetic Observatory (BOD) was a ground-based facility located in Bodø, Norway, operational from 1932 to 1934, specializing in magnetometer measurements as part of the IAGA observatory network.
5dee2736-b78d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bodo Geomagnetic Observatory

5df31ffa-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Ca del Monte Observatory (Code B14) is an astronomical facility located in Cecima, Pavia, Italy. It operates as a ground-based observatory for various astronomical studies and observations.
5df31ffa-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ca del Monte Observatory, Italy

5e07aad8-b7b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Interball-Tail spacecraft orbit and attitude** pertains to the trajectory and orientation data of the Interball-Tail satellite, part of the CDPP archive managed by CNES. This information is crucial for understanding the spacecraft's positioning and directional aspects during its mission.
5e07aad8-b7b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Interball-Tail spacecraft orbit and attitude part of Interball-Tail

5e0dbde0-b5d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Eastport Magnetometer, operational from 1860 to 1864, was an instrument used at the IAGA Eastport Observatory for measuring magnetic fields.
5e0dbde0-b5d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eastport Observatory

5e481532-bc2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Flower and Cook Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
5e481532-bc2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Flower and Cook Observatory

5e612aae-b703-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Touch-and-Go Camera Suite (TAGCAMS) aboard the OSIRIS-REx spacecraft is a system of three cameras designed for optical navigation, sample acquisition aid, and documentation of sample stowage during asteroid exploration.
5e612aae-b703-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: The Touch-and-Go Camera Suite on OSIRIS-REx

5e63a340-b77d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Jan Mayen (JAN) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Jan Mayen, Norway, established to conduct geophysical observations and studies. It is part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy's network.
5e63a340-b77d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Jan Mayen Geophysical Observatory, Norway

5e708108-b7a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **The Cottage Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Altoona, Pennsylvania, operated as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
5e708108-b7a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Altoona Observatory, United States

5e772148-bb80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rocca Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Jardim Botânico de Brasília, Brazil. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
5e772148-bb80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rocca Observatory at Jardim Botânico de Brasília, Brazil

5e797568-b8cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Energetic Electron and Proton Spectrometers (MPS and SPS)** are instruments on the Interball S2-X spacecraft designed to monitor solar wind parameters, register ion fluxes in the bow-shock region, and measure energy distributions of ions and electrons within the terrestrial magnetosphere.
5e797568-b8cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Electron and Proton Spectrometers on Interball

5e8cc372-b73e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Evelyn L. Egan Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Florida Gulf Coast University in Fort Myers, Florida. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and education.
5e8cc372-b73e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Evelyn L. Egan Observatory

5e8d46dc-b61a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Canvas View New Mexico Skies observatory (code: V32) is an astronomical observatory located in Mayhill, New Mexico, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
5e8d46dc-b61a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Canvas View New Mexico Skies Observatory

5e94a7da-b6ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **JICAMAG (JIC)** Magnetometer Station, situated at the Jicamarca Radio Observatory in Peru, is a ground-based facility dedicated to measuring magnetic fields.
5e94a7da-b6ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Jicamarca Observatory, Peru

5e9707d4-b7e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The SPECULOOS Southern Observatory is an astronomical facility located at the Paranal Observatory in South America, consisting of four 1-meter telescopes designed to search for habitable planets around ultra-cool stars in the infrared waveband.
5e9707d4-b7e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Search for habitable Planets Eclipsing Ultra-cool Stars Southern Observatory four 1 meter telescopes at Paranal Observatory

5ea4e610-ba0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Jimginny Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at 1001 Huntleigh Drive in Naperville, Illinois, United States. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial objects.
5ea4e610-ba0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Naperville Observatory, United States

5eac2672-b897-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Jaluit Observatory was a ground-based facility in Jabor, Marshall Islands, operating from 1938 to 1942 as part of the IAGA network, primarily known for its magnetometer instrument.
5eac2672-b897-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Jaluit Observatory, Marshall Islands

5eb42ea2-b81b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Double Star 2 is a joint European-Chinese satellite launched in 2004 to study Earth's magnetosphere. It operates as a polar orbiter and carries instruments for geomagnetic research, complementing its equatorial counterpart, Double Star 1.
5eb42ea2-b81b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Double Star 2 part of Double Star mission

5eb9089e-b967-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High Energy Proton Detector (HEPD) on Double Star 1 is an instrument designed to detect energetic protons in the magnetosphere and solar wind. It is part of the CNES observatory CDPP archive for the Double Star mission.
5eb9089e-b967-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Energy Proton Detector on Double Star 1

5ecfcb78-b602-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plasma Energy Analyzer (PM1) for Vega 2 was an instrument designed to study the energy distribution of solar and cometary particles using six detectors including ion and electron analyzers.
5ecfcb78-b602-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Energy Analyzer on Vega 2

5eda1584-babb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Jackvik (JCK) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Jäkkvik, Sweden, primarily known for its magnetometer and contributing to the IUGONET observatory network.
5eda1584-babb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Jackvik Geophysical Observatory, Sweden

5ee1ebb0-b6a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2A Engineering Data Interface** is an instrument that performs analog to digital conversion of key temperatures, voltages, and currents for the BARREL balloon array, part of NASA's RBSP mission. It has multiple inputs for monitoring various parameters with a 16-bit precision ADC.
5ee1ebb0-b6a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

5ee2a3f2-b7d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The O'Higgins Fluxgate Magnetometer is an instrument within the SAMBA Magnetometer Array, located at the O'Higgins geomagnetic observatory, used for measuring magnetic field variations.
5ee2a3f2-b7d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer at O'Higgins Observatory, Antarctica

5ee8645e-b5fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EISCAT Longyearbyen ESR 32m radar is an instrument operated by the EISCAT Scientific Association in Longyearbyen, Spitsbergen. It features a fixed 42 m dish antenna aligned with the magnetic field for UHF band (~500 MHz) observations and operates with peak powers of approximately 1 MW.
5ee8645e-b5fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: UHF Radar on EISCAT Svalbard Radar at Longyearbyen Observatory

5efab584-b9c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The DS932 Dyess AFB, Texas, USA, was an ionospheric observatory equipped with a Digisonde, operational from 1999 to 2009, which studied the ionosphere by evaluating skywave signal characteristics.
5efab584-b9c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Station at Dyess Air Force Base Observatory, United States

5efd18a6-b753-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **HEED** (High Energy Electron Detector) is an instrument on the Double Star 1 spacecraft designed to measure the flux of energetic electrons in Earth's magnetosphere. It is part of the CNES observatory CDPP/AMDA Double Star 1 mission, contributing to our understanding of high-energy particle dynamics in space.
5efd18a6-b753-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Energy Electron Detector on Double Star 1

5f0f5b86-bb6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: El Far Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in El Far d'Empordà, Catalonia, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility for studying celestial bodies and phenomena.
5f0f5b86-bb6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: El Far Observatory, Spain

5f1036de-b898-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Bay St. Louis ground station, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG, which measures magnetic field data and has been operational since January 1986.
5f1036de-b898-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetic Field Instrument part of THEMIS Mission

5f146854-b9c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Tumanny observatory is an instrument used to measure variations in Earth's magnetic field, which is part of the World Data Center for Geomagnetism at Kyoto.
5f146854-b9c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at WDC Kyoto Observatory

5f153ae8-b9f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Pioneer Venus Orbiter Radio Science Experiment** was a mission component designed to study Venus’s atmosphere, ionosphere, gravity field, and surface properties using radio signals from the spacecraft. It provided valuable data on temperature, pressure, density profiles, and gravitational shifts, also studying the solar corona during specific alignments with the Sun.
5f153ae8-b9f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Experiment on Pioneer Venus Orbiter

5f28617e-b9a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The V. P. Engel'gardt Astronomical Observatory, also known as the Engelhardt Observatory, is an astronomical observatory located 20 kilometers west of Kazan, Russia. It was established in 1901 and is part of the astronomical observatories of Kazan Federal University.
5f28617e-b9a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: V. P. Engel'gardt Astronomical Observatory, Russia

5f2bf050-bacc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Sable Island is a ground-based observatory located on Earth's surface in North America, specifically in Canada, equipped with a magnetometer for scientific observations since 1999.
5f2bf050-bacc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sable Island Observatory, Canada

5f30f274-b6b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Barrackpore Magnetometer was an instrument used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field, operational from January 1, 1904, to December 31, 1914, at the IAGA-identified station BAP in Barrackpore.
5f30f274-b6b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Barrackpore Observatory

5f3201fa-b772-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The "Ion Spectra and Anisotropy" (ION) instrument on the Interball Auroral Probe is a set of mass spectrometers designed to measure ion composition, energy spectra, and anisotropy, complemented by electron spectrometers for comprehensive charged particle analysis in space.
5f3201fa-b772-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer part of Interball Auroral Probe

5f3fbb3e-bb45-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Helios 2 was a solar probe launched in 1976 as part of a joint mission between the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and NASA to study solar processes from heliocentric orbit.
5f3fbb3e-bb45-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Helios 2

5f4883aa-b77a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Mazagon is a ground observatory located in Moguer, Huelva, Andalusia, Spain, known as BOOTES-1.
5f4883aa-b77a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: BOOTES-1 at Mazagón Observatory, Spain

5f59d09e-b6e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Durham Geomagnetic Observatory (DUR) is a ground facility in Newington, New Hampshire, United States, that houses a magnetometer as part of the IAGA observatories and contributes to global geomagnetic data collection.
5f59d09e-b6e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Durham Geomagnetic Observatory

5f73115e-b916-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Cluster Joint Science Operations Centre (JSOC) Virtual Instrument" is an unspecified instrument that catalogs identified scientific events related to the Cluster spacecraft mission. It serves as a virtual tool within the CDPP-Archive at CNES for accessing and analyzing Cluster model data.
5f73115e-b916-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cluster Joint Science Operations Centre Virtual Instrument for Cluster Model Data part of Cluster

5f76122e-ba0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Atacama Submillimeter Telescope Experiment (ASTE)** is a 10-meter radio telescope located in the Atacama Desert of Chile, built by Mitsubishi Electric as a prototype for ALMA to conduct submillimeter astronomy.
5f76122e-ba0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 10m Atacama Submillimeter Telescope Experiment at Llano de Chajnantor Observatory, Chile

5f783260-b8ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ibadan Geomagnetic Observatory (IBD), located in Samonda, Ibadan North, Oyo State, Nigeria, is a ground facility established in 1956 to monitor geomagnetic activities and operated until December 31, 1975.
5f783260-b8ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ibadan Geomagnetic Observatory, Nigeria

5f846fe4-b9cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Zao Observatory** at Tohoku University is a ground-based radio wave observatory located in Togatta Onsen, Zao, Katta County, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan. It operates at an altitude of 500 meters and is situated on the Earth's surface within Asia.
5f846fe4-b9cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Wave Observatory at Zao Observatory, Japan

5f86b262-b610-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetometers at Alma Ata (AAA), operational since 1963, are instruments used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at the Alma Ata ground station.
5f86b262-b610-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Alma Ata Observatory

5f876bf6-b662-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cordell–Lorenz Observatory is an astronomical observatory owned and operated by Sewanee: The University of the South, located in Sewanee, Tennessee.
5f876bf6-b662-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cordell–Lorenz Observatory, United States

5f8d1f7e-b6d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Valdicerro Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Costabianca, Loreto, Ancona, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
5f8d1f7e-b6d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Valdicerro Observatory, Italy

5f98a2e8-b79f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS Ground Magnetometers are a network of ground-based instruments associated with the THEMIS spaceflight mission, designed to measure magnetic field variations as part of NASA's exploration of geomagnetic activity and substorms.
5f98a2e8-b79f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of THEMIS Ground Magnetometers

5fa8f11e-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Mackay Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in San Cristóbal de La Laguna on the island of Tenerife in the Canary Islands, Spain.
5fa8f11e-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mackay Observatory, Spain

5fbaa66c-b5b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Extreme UltraViolet Explorer (EUVE) Satellite Mission was a space mission dedicated to conducting astronomical observations in the extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and X-ray wavebands. It operated from 1992 to 2001, providing valuable data on various celestial objects.
5fbaa66c-b5b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Extreme Ultraviolet NASA Extreme UltraViolet Explorer Satellite Mission

5fbc851c-b97c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISEE Magnetometer Sata station is a ground-based observatory located in Otomari, Minamiosumi, Kimotsuki County, Kagoshima Prefecture, Japan. It operates under the IUGONET network to monitor magnetic field variations and contribute to geophysical research.
5fbc851c-b97c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sata Observatory, Japan

5fc3cbd4-bad9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Warren & Beverly Observatory (MPC ID: 709) is an astronomical observatory located in Cloudcroft, New Mexico, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
5fc3cbd4-bad9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Warren and Beverly Observatory, United States

5fc5f714-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Al Sadeem Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
5fc5f714-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Al Sadeem Observatory, United Arab Emirates

5fcb67b8-b944-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "NOAA 15 Positions" dataset provides the spatial coordinates of the NOAA 15 spacecraft in different reference frames. It is part of the NOAA-15 observatory and includes ephemeris data for tracking the spacecraft's location.
5fcb67b8-b944-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris on NOAA 15 Spacecraft

5fcce3e0-ba57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **LANL1994 Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer (SOPA)** is an instrument designed to measure the energetic particle environment in synchronous orbit, featuring three silicon solid state detector telescopes that detect and differentiate various particles including protons, electrons, alpha particles, and heavier ions.
5fcce3e0-ba57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer part of Los Alamos National Laboratory 1994

5fcd7352-b92e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The **CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at LMT**, specifically, is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed at Learmonth, Australia, as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
5fcd7352-b92e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometer Network

5fce407e-b64b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Kielce Observatory is an astronomical facility located at the University of Jan Kochanowski in Kielce, Poland, dedicated to ground-based observations.
5fce407e-b64b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kielce Observatory, Poland

5fd1bb7e-b915-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Chinese Academy of Sciences and the City of Shanghai Tianma Radio 65m Telescope at Sheshan" is a large radio telescope located in Sheshan, China. It is part of a ground observatory operated by the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the city of Shanghai.
5fd1bb7e-b915-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 65m Tianma Radio Telescope at Sheshan

5fdb0ca4-b75f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cape Dorset Geophysical Observatory, located in the Qikiqtaaluk Region of Nunavut, Canada, is a ground-based facility established on January 14, 2007, that includes instruments such as magnetometers for geophysical research.
5fdb0ca4-b75f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cape Dorset Geophysical Observatory, Canada

5fdcb662-b16f-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Max Planck Institute for Astronomy and Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia (CSIC) 3.5m Telescope at Calar Alto Observatory is an optical telescope with a 3.5-meter aperture located in Europe, specifically at the Calar Alto Observatory.
5fdcb662-b16f-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.5m optical Max Planck Institute for Astronomy and Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia Telescope at Calar Alto Observatory

5fde4e26-b644-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tahiti Ground Observatory** was a geophysical observatory located in Faʻaʻā, French Polynesia, operating from 1958 to 1970, known for its magnetometer instruments.
5fde4e26-b644-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tahiti Observatory

5fdefb78-b5db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Preston Hills Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Celina, Texas, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for celestial observation and research.
5fdefb78-b5db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Preston Hills Observatory, United States

5ff2afd8-b784-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Stammersdorf Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Vienna, Austria, dedicated to ground-based observations and research.
5ff2afd8-b784-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stammersdorf Observatory, Austria

5ff56524-bab4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Photopolarimeter Subsystem (PPS) for Voyager 2 is an instrument designed to measure the intensity and polarization of light, offering valuable data on planetary atmospheres and ring systems.
5ff56524-bab4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Photopolarimeter Subsystem on Voyager 2

5ff66e92-b951-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The ISRO Astrosat is a multi-wavelength space telescope operated by the Indian Space Research Organization, designed to observe celestial sources in various wavelengths, including gamma rays.
5ff66e92-b951-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma-ray The Indian Space Research Organization's Astrosat Multi-Wavelength Space Telescope

5ff70fe4-b9b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 2 Fast Plasma Instrument (FPI) Suite's Dual Electron Spectrometer (DES) is a component of the FPI onboard the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission, designed to measure electron velocity-space distribution from 10 eV to 30 keV with high time resolution.
5ff70fe4-b9b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dual Electron Spectrometer part of MMS

5ff8b304-b7bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Intermediate Dispersion Spectrograph (IDS) is a long-slit spectrograph used with the 2.5m Isaac Newton Telescope, featuring two CCD detectors and multiple gratings to allow for various dispersions and spatial scales.
5ff8b304-b7bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Intermediate Dispersion Spectrograph on 2.5m Isaac Newton Telescope

5ffd1718-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Trapped Radiation Detector for P11** is a specialized instrument designed to measure and characterize trapped radiation particles in space, contributing to the study of radiation levels and assessing their impact on the P11 mission's spacecraft and instruments.
5ffd1718-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Trapped Radiation Detector part of P11

60086c38-b5ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Qianling Ground Magnetic Field Instrument is a magnetometer located at the Qianling ground station and part of the IAGA investigation. It measures magnetic field data starting from January 1, 1984.
60086c38-b5ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Qianling Observatory

600b4bfe-b993-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **VLF AWESOME** is a Spectral Power Receiver instrument designed to provide high-sensitivity broadband radio measurements of natural lightning emissions, transmitting beacons, and radio emissions from the near-Earth space environment within the frequency band of 0.8-50 kHz. It has been operational since its completion in 2004.
600b4bfe-b993-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spectral Power Receiver part of Awesome Investigation

601565ea-b622-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Mickleover Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Derby, England. It is designated as a ground-based observatory and operates under the code 492 recognized by the Minor Planet Center (MPC).
601565ea-b622-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mickleover Observatory, United Kingdom

60160fba-bada-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The magnetometers at Da Lat (DLT) are part of the observatory facilities managed by the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto, Japan.
60160fba-bada-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Da Lat Observatory

601c5396-bb09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The one specified here has been operational since January 1933 and is part of the WDC Kyoto observatory, with the IAGA identifier PTS.
601c5396-bb09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Petsamo Observatory

602bb26a-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IMSC Magnetic Field Instrument on DEMETER is a search coil magnetometer consisting of three orthogonal antennae designed to measure magnetic fields in space. It features a high-permeability permalloy core wound with copper wire, enabling precise detection and amplification of magnetic signals.
602bb26a-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetic Field Experiment on DEMETER

6034d57a-b5ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Magnetic Field Observations (MAG-A) on Dynamics Explorer 1 was an investigation using a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer to measure vector magnetic field data, primarily to study field-aligned currents in the auroral oval and polar cap at different altitudes.
6034d57a-b5ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Field Observations on Dynamics Explorer 1

6034d996-b68d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operated from 1974 to 1980 at the WDC Kyoto Observatory in Grahamstown, used for measuring and studying the Earth's magnetic field as part of the IAGA investigation.
6034d996-b68d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ground Magnetic Field Instrument at Grahamstown Observatory

603c20d0-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lunar Cafe Observatory (MPC ID: 847) is an astronomical observatory located in Flint, Michigan, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
603c20d0-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Cafe Observatory, United States

60428b04-b872-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "VEX spacecraft ephemeris" is a platform investigation tool that provides orbital data and position information for the Venus Express (VEX) spacecraft. It is part of the CNES CDPP-AMDA observatory archive and serves to document the spacecraft's trajectory over time.
60428b04-b872-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Orbital Ephemeris on Venus Express Spacecraft

604786b8-b746-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Search Coil Magnetometer (SCM) on THEMIS A is an instrument designed to measure low-frequency magnetic field fluctuations and waves in three directions, covering a frequency range from 0.1 Hz to 4 kHz. It complements the measurements of fluxgate magnetometers with high sensitivity and precision, providing essential data for studying space weather and magnetic phenomena.
604786b8-b746-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Magnetometer on THEMIS A

604f1be4-bbbf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "GOES 4 Position" refers to the spatial coordinates and trajectory data of the GOES 4 satellite, which is part of the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite (GOES) series operated by NOAA for environmental monitoring.
604f1be4-bbbf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 4 Position on Spacecraft

605e4788-bb36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hawk's Nest Radio Astronomy Observatory (HNRAO) hosts the Terminated Folded Dipole and SDRPlay Spectrograph System, a radio astronomy instrument featuring a 4-element square array aligned to true north with each antenna element being 24 feet long. This system operates in the 15-30 MHz bandwidth and can simultaneously detect both right circular polarization (RCP) and left circular polarization (LCP).
605e4788-bb36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terminated Folded Dipole and SDRPlay Spectrometer at Hawk's Nest Radio Astronomy Observatory

6063c980-b5df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Deep Space Station 35 (DSS-35) is a 34-meter radio telescope located in Canberra, Australia, part of NASA's Deep Space Network, designed to support deep space missions with advanced communication capabilities.
6063c980-b5df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Radio Telescope at Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex, Australia

60670fee-b69f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: DMSP F15 (USA 147) is an artificial satellite launched by the U.S. Defense Meteorological Satellite Program to monitor meteorological, oceanographic, and solar-terrestrial physics environments from a sun-synchronous near-polar orbit at an altitude of 840km.
60670fee-b69f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible and Infrared Sensors on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

6067e38a-b828-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Chilbolton Geomagnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Wiltshire, England, dedicated to monitoring and studying geomagnetic activity. It operates as part of the World Data Centre for Geomagnetism, Kyoto (WDC), and houses instruments such as magnetometers for precise measurements.
6067e38a-b828-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Chilbolton Geomagnetic Observatory, United Kingdom

606a878a-bc87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2W Optical Photometer** is an instrument designed to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm during relativistic electron precipitation events, with the objective of determining the presence of protons accompanying these electrons by measuring specific optical emissions indicative of proton precipitation.
606a878a-bc87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

606b4a82-b5d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fairborn Observatory is a ground observatory that includes the Tennessee State University 2M Automatic Spectroscopic Telescope, located at Fairborn.
606b4a82-b5d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2m Automatic Spectroscopic Telescope at Fairborn Observatory

607019a2-b7dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The TRT-NEO Observatory is an astronomical facility located in the Mae Chaem District of Chiang Mai Province, Thailand. It specializes in tracking near-Earth objects (NEOs) from its ground-based observatory on Earth.
607019a2-b7dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: TRT-NEO Observatory, Thailand
