6073d9f4-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The JMA magnetometer at Kakioka Observatory (KNY), part of the IUGONET observatory network, includes high-sensitivity triaxial fluxgate and Overhauser magnetometers for measuring magnetic field components and scalar field, respectively, with historical use of torsion magnetometers and current absolute instruments like a magnetometer theodolite and proton precession magnetometer.
6073d9f4-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kyoto Observatory

6083f92e-b9e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 3.5-m Galileo Zeiss Ritchey-Chretien altazimuth reflector is a telescope located at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory in Garafía, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain, operational since 1995 and known for its 3.5-meter aperture.
6083f92e-b9e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.5m Telescope at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory, Spain

60862224-b9a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tinsley photometer is a single-channel, dry-ice cooled photomultiplier instrument used at the Mauna Kea Observatory for astronomical observations.
60862224-b9a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tinsley Photometer at Mauna Kea Observatory

60881bd4-b8e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Korea Microlensing Telescope Network-CTIO (KMTNet-CTIO) is an astronomical observatory located in Vicuña, Chile. It specializes in ground-based observations and is part of the global network dedicated to studying microlensing events.
60881bd4-b8e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Korea Microlensing Telescope Network-CTIO Observatory, Chile

60890c20-b72b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **University of Tartu Old Observatory**, also known as the Tartu Old Observatory (Estonian: Tartu Tähetorn), is a former astronomical observatory in Tartu, Estonia, that operated from 1810 to 1964 and now functions as a museum.
60890c20-b72b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Old Observatory at Tartu, Estonia

6089747a-b8a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **AJ4CO Terminated Folded Dipole and FS-200B Radio Spectrograph system** is a ground-based instrument located at the AJ4CO Radio Astronomy Observatory in High Springs, Florida. It consists of a Terminated Folded Dipole (TFD) array and an FS-200B Radio Spectrograph operating in the 16 - 26 MHz frequency range for simultaneous right circular polarization (RCP) and left circular polarization (LCP).
6089747a-b8a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terminated Folded Dipole and FS-200B Radio Spectrograph at AJ4CO Observatory

6089fb8c-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DreamSky Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Lisnyky, Ukraine. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
6089fb8c-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: DreamSky Observatory, Ukraine

609deaea-b961-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Craven E. Williams Observatory is an astronomical observatory operated by Gardner-Webb University in Boiling Springs, North Carolina, featuring a 16-inch Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope and hosting community events.
609deaea-b961-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Craven E. Williams Observatory

60a77bd6-b8f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: GOES 7 was a geosynchronous environmental satellite developed by NASA and operated by NOAA, designed to provide high-quality cloud cover data, atmospheric temperature readings, and space environment monitoring.
60a77bd6-b8f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible Infrared Spin-Scan Radiometer on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite

60a7b3a0-bbd1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Byrd Station 1 was a ground-based observatory located on Earth's surface at an altitude of 1515 meters, operational from January 1957 to December 31, 1968, primarily used for scientific observations including magnetometer readings.
60a7b3a0-bbd1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Byrd Station Observatory, Antarctica

60a7c78e-b945-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 7300 Observatory is an astronomical facility located at 47 Serenity Street in Otero County, New Mexico, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
60a7c78e-b945-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cloudcroft Observatory, United States

60ae9cde-baf4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Murchison Radio-astronomy Observatory (MRO) is a research facility established by CSIRO in 2009, located in a radio quiet zone near Boolardy Station in Western Australia. It houses major astronomical instruments like the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder and the Murchison Widefield Array.
60ae9cde-baf4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Inyarrimanha Ilgari Bundara the CSIRO Murchison Radio-astronomy Observatory, Australia

60b53da2-b6c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Kahoku Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Kahoku, Nishimurayama County, Yamagata Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the study and observation of celestial bodies.
60b53da2-b6c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kahoku Observatory, Japan

60cc0a1c-bb1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the ground observatory located in Cariati, Cosenza, Calabria, Italy, with coordinates at approximately 39.48877 latitude and 16.95608 longitude.
60cc0a1c-bb1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cariati Observatory, Italy

60d705f6-b8a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** InSight (Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport) was a NASA robotic lander mission that studied Mars' deep interior from November 2018 to December 2022. The mission aimed to understand the formation and evolution of terrestrial planets by measuring seismic activity, heat flow, and other geological properties.
60d705f6-b8a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport

60d8ef96-bbaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the Modra Observatory, an astronomical facility located in Modra, Slovakia, which is equipped with a telescope identified as "urn-nasa-pds-context-telescope-modra.0m6."
60d8ef96-bbaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Modra Observatory, Slovakia

60de3616-b648-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Macquarie Island station is a ground-based observatory located on Macquarie Island in the Southern Ocean, which has been operational since June 1950. It primarily monitors ionospheric scintillation and contributes to scientific research related to space weather and geophysics.
60de3616-b648-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor at Macquarie Island Station, Australia

60de8a8c-b6e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GOES 13 Spacecraft Position is an instrument that provides the ephemeris data for the GOES 13 satellite, detailing its position and trajectory over time as part of the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite (GOES) system.
60de8a8c-b6e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris on GOES 13

60e27888-b9d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Deep Space Station Media Calibration Subsystem (DMD) provides GPS data, weather statistics, and water vapor emissions using advanced instrumentation like the AWVR to measure tropospheric frequency shifts accurately.
60e27888-b9d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Advanced Water Vapor Radiometer on Deep Space Network

60eda5e0-baeb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Las Cumbres 1m Telescopes with the Network of Robotic Echelle Spectrographs (NRES) are part of the Las Cumbres Observatory Global Telescope Network, offering continuous access to telescopes for professional astronomy and educational purposes.
60eda5e0-baeb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1m Las Cumbres Telescope and Network of Robotic Echelle Spectrograph at Las Cumbres Observatory

60ef2bfe-bbc2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mapping Imaging Spectrometer for Europa (MISE) is a near-infrared spectrometer on the Europa Clipper spacecraft designed to map the composition and distribution of ices, salts, organics, and hotspots on Jupiter's moon Europa, helping scientists understand its geologic history and assess habitability.
60ef2bfe-bbc2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Mapping Imaging Spectrometer for Europa on Europa Clipper

60f56218-b1a8-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lunar Terrain Imager (LUTI) is an instrument designed to capture high-resolution images of potential landing sites and special target areas on the lunar surface, with a spatial resolution of 2.5 meters per pixel from an altitude of 100 kilometers.
60f56218-b1a8-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Terrain Imager on Korean Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter

61066918-b85c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Middle and Upper atmosphere (MU) radar** is a large Doppler radar located at Shigaraki MU Observatory in Japan, used for atmospheric observation by transmitting radio waves to detect winds and turbulence from the troposphere up to the ionosphere.
61066918-b85c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Middle and Upper Atmosphere Radar at Shigaraki Observatory, Japan

610cab3c-b8ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Girardville station, part of the IAGA investigation, used for measuring magnetic field variations since 1973.
610cab3c-b8ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Girardville Observatory

61210a5a-b9b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ultraviolet/Visible Camera (UVVIS) is an advanced imaging instrument designed for lunar mineral mapping, featuring a catadioptic telescope and capable of capturing high-resolution images across various spectral bands.
61210a5a-b9b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet/Visible Camera on Clementine Spacecraft

6126e658-b68a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tenerife Observatory-LCO A is an astronomical observatory located in Teide National Park on the island of Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain. It is situated at coordinates 28.300417° N, -16.51165° W and operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research.
6126e658-b68a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tenerife Observatory-LCO A, Spain

6129b7b0-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The UWA Observatory (D22) is an astronomical observatory located in Crawley, Western Australia. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial objects and phenomena.
6129b7b0-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: UWA Observatory

613a6a5a-bbc3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Digisonde ionospheric station at Bundoora, Australia (URSI-code: BV53Q) is an advanced facility that analyzes skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere to determine their angle of arrival, polarization, Doppler frequency shift, and travel time.
613a6a5a-bbc3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Bundoora Observatory, Australia

61488e0a-b925-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**

Zhong Shan is a ground-based observatory located on Earth's surface at coordinates -69.4 latitude and 76.4 longitude, with an altitude of 10 meters, primarily functioning as part of the IAGA Observatory network for geomagnetic measurements.
61488e0a-b925-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Zhong Shan Observatory, Antarctica

614d99cc-bb14-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO)** is an astronomical observatory located in the Coquimbo Region of Chile, known for its ground-based facilities and contributions to astronomical research.
614d99cc-bb14-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cerro Tololo Observatory, Chile

614e3d10-bc85-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VHF radar at Kototabang, Indonesia is a Very High Frequency Doppler radar used for atmospheric and ionospheric studies, operating at 30.8 MHz with a peak transmitting power of 20 kW and capable of steering its beam in multiple directions.
614e3d10-bc85-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very High Frequency Radar at IUGONET Observatory

615393ee-bba6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Green Bank Telescope (GBT) 4mm Receiver is a dual-beam instrument designed to operate within the low-frequency range of the 3mm atmospheric window, specifically between 67 and 93 GHz. It is used for astronomical observations at these frequencies.
615393ee-bba6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 4mm Green Bank Telescope

6157cdb8-ba13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Highly Elliptical Orbit (HEO) satellites are a series of spacecraft, including HEO-1, that orbit Earth in highly elliptical paths known as Molniya orbits. These orbits have a period of approximately 12 hours, with a low perigee and high apogee, primarily used for purposes other than scientific research.
6157cdb8-ba13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Highly Elliptical Orbit-1

6159db38-b7c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
ChemLIBS is an instrument used for laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy, featuring three Ocean Optics HR2000+ spectrometers and a Quantel Ultra100 laser with adjustable power density. It operates under various atmospheric conditions to simulate environments such as Earth's atmosphere, vacuum, and Mars-like conditions within a 12-inch cube vacuum chamber.
6159db38-b7c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ChemLIBS

615b6668-b918-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Phobos-2 Plasma Wave System (PWS) is an instrument aboard the PHOBOS-2 spacecraft designed to study electric field fluctuations in the interplanetary medium and Martian magnetosphere, measure plasma density, and assess spacecraft potential during its encounter with Mars' moon Phobos.
615b6668-b918-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Wave System part of Phobos-2

6160ad08-bb89-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tartu Geophysical Observatory** is a ground-based facility located in Tartu County, Estonia, primarily known for its magnetometer instrument and contributions to geophysical research.
6160ad08-bb89-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tartu Geophysical Observatory, Estonia

6179bd76-b78c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mauna Kea Observatories (MKO)** are a group of independent astronomical research facilities located at the summit of Mauna Kea on Hawaiʻi, United States, known for their significant contributions to astronomy and ongoing cultural and environmental controversies.
6179bd76-b78c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mauna Kea Observatories

618aba22-ba84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Lucca Observatory (also known as the Lucca Astronomical Observatory) is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Maggiano, Lucca, Italy. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center with the code A93 and is situated at coordinates 43.8623° N, 10.5362° E.
618aba22-ba84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Maggiano Observatory, Italy

618b7d1e-b948-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Harvard and Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics' MicroObservatory Robotic Telescope Network (MRTN) is a series of robotic telescopes located in North America, primarily used for optical astronomy observations.
618b7d1e-b948-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical MicroObservatory Robotic Telescope Network at Harvard and Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics

6191cf88-b917-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Solar Wind Analyzer (MONITOR-3) on the Interball Tail Probe is an instrument designed to measure solar wind ion fluxes and energy-angular distributions of H+ and He++ around the Sun direction with high time resolution. It is part of the Interball-1 observatory mission.
6191cf88-b917-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Wind Analyzer on Interball Tail Probe

619685f6-b6f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Uppsala Astronomical Observatory (UAO) is the oldest astronomical observatory in Sweden, founded in 1741 and located at the University of Uppsala.
619685f6-b6f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Uppsala Astronomical Observatory, Sweden

6198a7f2-b6e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Extreme Ultraviolet Imager (EUV)** on the IMAGE mission is an instrument designed to observe the distribution of He+ in Earth's plasmasphere by detecting its resonantly-scattered emission at 30.4 nm, providing global snapshots of the cold plasma structure and dynamics within the plasmasphere.
6198a7f2-b6e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Extreme Ultraviolet Imager part of IMAGE mission

6199526e-b820-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Heavy Ion Detector (HID) on Double Star 2 is an instrument designed to detect heavy ions with atomic mass units greater than 4. It is part of the CNES observatory CDPP archive for the Double Star mission.
6199526e-b820-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heavy Ion Detector on Double Star 2

619f5b36-ba5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Deep Space Station 25 (DSS-25) is a ground observatory designed for tracking and communicating with spacecraft, typically part of NASA's Deep Space Network.
619f5b36-ba5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: DSS-25 Observatory

61afe570-b64e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The White-light All-sky Watec Imager (AWI) at Kiruna, Sweden is an automatic optical instrument consisting of a CCD camera and a fisheye lens used for capturing all-sky images.
61afe570-b64e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: White-light All-sky Watec Imager at IUGONET Observatory

61b3acc8-b9fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Space Environment Monitor (SEM) on GOES 7 is an instrument suite designed to measure the real-time effects of solar activity on the near-Earth electromagnetic environment, providing crucial data for space weather reports that are essential for communication, navigation, and satellite operations.
61b3acc8-b9fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Chamber part of Space Environment Monitor on GOES 7

61b93f4c-b682-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The AJ4CO Observatory in High Springs, Florida is a participant in the Radio JOVE project, dedicated to observing radio emissions from Jupiter, the Sun, and the Galactic Background using various receiver systems fed by TFD and dipole arrays.
61b93f4c-b682-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio JOVE AJ4CO TFD and Tunable Wideband Receiver on RadioJOVE, Nepal

61ba1168-ba44-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CLPS Task Order 2IM Laser Retroreflector Array (LRA) is a small, passive optical instrument used for precision laser ranging from lunar orbit, aiding in the geolocation of landers and establishing fiducial markers on the Moon's surface.
61ba1168-ba44-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Laser Retroreflector Array on CLPS Task Order 2IM

61c80a82-b794-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ottawa Observatory, also known as the Ottawa Geomagnetic Observatory, is an astronomical and geomagnetic research facility located in Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. Established in 1968, it focuses on ground-based observations and measurements of Earth's magnetic field.
61c80a82-b794-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Ottawa Observatory, Canada

61c87c50-b8da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "code: urn:nasa:pds:context:instrument_host:spacecraft.clps_to_prime1_athenatype" refers to a spacecraft in NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS) context, specifically the CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) TO Prime 1 Athena mission, which is part of a broader set of observational facilities.
61c87c50-b8da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: CLPS to Prime1 Athena Spacecraft

61cff7ea-b840-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IGPP LANL magnetometer chain** is a ground-based facility located on Earth's surface that operates as part of the Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics (IGPP) at Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL). It consists of multiple magnetometers, including one at the Air Force Academy, used for monitoring geomagnetic activity.
61cff7ea-b840-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Air Force Academy

61d58d24-bb72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1Q Data Processing Unit (DPU)** is an instrument controller board designed for the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses mission. It acquires data from various sensors, formats it for downlink via an Iridium modem, and controls command-cutdown operations, utilizing a flexible FPGA for backplane signal interfacing.
61d58d24-bb72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

61dce2d6-b90b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The NEAR magnetometer, part of the Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous (NEAR) Shoemaker spacecraft, was designed to detect and map the magnetic fields of asteroid 433 Eros using highly sensitive ring core sensors.
61dce2d6-b90b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous Shoemaker

61e588f2-b896-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mirny Geomagnetic Observatory (MIR), located in Antarctica and sponsored by Russia, has been operational since 1956. It is a ground facility specializing in geomagnetic measurements as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy's observatory network.
61e588f2-b896-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mirny Geomagnetic Observatory, Antarctica

61ef42ba-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dust Impact Detection System (DIDSY) on the Giotto spacecraft was a system designed to record and analyze impacts of particles of significant mass, providing data on their mass spectrum through six subsystems mounted on Giotto's dust shield.
61ef42ba-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dust Impact Detection System on Giotto spacecraft

621487d2-b950-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Attu (ATU) Geophysical Observatory, established in 2007 and located on the Earth's surface in Qeqertalik, Greenland, is a ground facility dedicated to geophysical observations. It includes a magnetometer as part of its instrumentation and is affiliated with the IUGONET observatory network.
621487d2-b950-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Attu Geophysical Observatory, Greenland

62159938-ba95-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Caraquiz Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Uceda, Guadalajara, Spain. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial objects and phenomena.
62159938-ba95-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Caraquiz Observatory, Spain

6219aea4-b803-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Southern African Large Telescope (SALT)** is a 9.2-metre optical telescope primarily designed for spectroscopy, located near Sutherland in the Karoo region of South Africa. It consists of 91 hexagonal mirror segments and is operated by the South African Astronomical Observatory.
6219aea4-b803-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 9.2m Southern African Large Telescope at Sutherland Observatory, South Africa

621cd52c-b60d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ISIS 2 Ion Mass Spectrometer** was an instrument aboard the ISIS 2 satellite designed to measure the distribution of positive ion species, particularly focusing on polar wind particles. It featured two ion detector systems and mass scanning capabilities from 1 to 64 atomic mass units (u), with modes for peak detection and analog output to optimize telemetry bandwidth.
621cd52c-b60d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Mass Spectrometer on International Satellites for Ionospheric Studies 2

621ce3be-babd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1K Ephemeris is a virtual instrument that provides trajectory positions in various coordinate systems, supporting the investigation of relativistic electron losses as part of the Radiation Belt Storm Probes (RBSP) mission.
621ce3be-babd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

622047d2-b178-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes the Kerguelen ground facility, part of the IAGA observatory network, located in the Kerguelen Archipelago, France. It operated from January 1, 1875 to December 31, 1988 and includes a magnetometer instrument.
622047d2-b178-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kerguelen Observatory, Antarctica

6227bc0c-b906-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Arroyo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Arroyo Hurtado, Spain. It is a ground-based facility used for celestial observations and research.
6227bc0c-b906-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Arroyo Observatory, Spain

62317e40-b659-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Go-Chome and Kobe-Suma Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Suma Ward, Kobe, Hyogo Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID 904.
62317e40-b659-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Go-Chome and Kobe-Suma Observatory, Japan

623c6d9a-b5bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Darwish Wind Tunnel at Texas Tech University's Agricultural Engineering Department is a research facility designed for investigating wind flow dynamics, aerodynamics, and the environmental effects on agricultural and structural systems.
623c6d9a-b5bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Darwish Wind Tunnel at Texas Tech University

623c6f92-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Paratunka magnetometer, operational since 1969, is part of the IAGA investigation and located at the Petropavlovsk observatory, contributing to geomagnetic data collection.
623c6f92-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Paratunka Observatory

623d379a-b91e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Gravesend Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at St John's Catholic Comprehensive School in Gravesend, Kent, United Kingdom. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and educational purposes.
623d379a-b91e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gravesend Observatory

6242fa3e-b637-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/F16 SSJ5 is a spectrometer onboard the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program's F16 satellite, designed to measure the energy, mass, and momentum transfer within Earth's magnetosphere-ionosphere system. It uses electrostatic analyzers to record particle flux in specific energy ranges.
6242fa3e-b637-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Precipitating Electron and Ion Spectrometer 5 part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

6246db1a-bb6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Oslo observatory, operational from 1843 to 1930, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IAGA investigation.
6246db1a-bb6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Oslo Observatory

62488bd6-bbd5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nuevos Horizontes Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Camas, Sevilla, Andalusia, Spain. It is situated at coordinates 37.403179°N, -6.03269°W and serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
62488bd6-bbd5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nuevos Horizontes Observatory, Spain

625c218c-b7c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES) 3.6-m Devasthal Optical Telescope is a large optical telescope located in Asia, specifically in Devasthal, India, designed for observing the universe in the visible light spectrum.
625c218c-b7c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences Devastal Optical Telescope at Devasthal

6265f6dc-b7b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the 60cm Cassegrain telescope located at the Institute of Astronomy of Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, Europe. This optical telescope has an aperture of 0.6 meters and is used for astronomical observations within the optical waveband.
6265f6dc-b7b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 0.6m Cassegrain Telescope at The Institute of Astronomy of Nicolaus Copernicus University

626d339e-b934-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The magnetometers at Orcades del Sur (ORC), part of the IUGONET observatory network managed by WDC Kyoto, provide data on geomagnetic activity in that region.
626d339e-b934-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Orcades del Sur Observatory, Antarctica

62821f4e-babe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kitt Peak Mosaic Camera is an astronomical imaging instrument featuring eight 2048 x 4096 pixel CCDs arranged as an 8192 x 8192 pixel detector, providing a field of view of 36 arcminutes on the KPNO 4-meter telescope.
62821f4e-babe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mosaic Imager on 4m Mayall Telescope at Kitt Peak Observatory

6282b360-bca7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The STEREO-A (STEREO Ahead) spacecraft is part of NASA's Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory mission, designed to study coronal mass ejections and solar energetic particles from a heliocentric orbit around the Sun.
6282b360-bca7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation part of Solar-Terrestrial Relations Observatory

628c3dbe-b6c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Port Stanley Geomagnetic Observatory (PST)** is a ground-based geophysical facility located in the Falkland Islands that conducts geomagnetic measurements, with an altitude of 135 meters and operational since January 01, 1994. It includes a magnetometer instrument provided by WDC Kyoto.
628c3dbe-b6c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Port Stanley Geomagnetic Observatory

628f3054-b969-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope (FGST), formerly known as the Gamma-ray Large Area Space Telescope (GLAST), is a space observatory designed for gamma-ray astronomy, launched in 2008 to study high-energy astrophysical phenomena from low Earth orbit.
628f3054-b969-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: gamma-ray Fermi Space Telescope

628fcb4c-ba4d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The European Southern Observatory (ESO) Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) at Cerro Paranal is an astronomical facility located in South America, designed to operate in the infrared waveband.
