It consists of two sensors with ring-core fluxgate magnetometers, providing detailed measurements across three dynamic ranges.
7f43a0c2-b8d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MAVEN Magnetometer Investigation

7f46e584-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Research Foundation of South Africa 1.0m Elizabeth Telescope is an optical telescope with a 1.0-meter aperture located at the South African Astronomical Observatory in Africa.
7f46e584-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.0m Elizabeth Telescope at South African Astronomical Observatory, South Africa

7f57e53e-b9fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Neutral Atmosphere Composition Experiment (NACE) on the AE-D satellite was an in situ investigation using a mass spectrometer to measure spatial and temporal changes in neutral atmospheric species concentrations. It provided insights into measurement techniques by comparing data with other onboard experiments.
7f57e53e-b9fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer part of Neutral Atmosphere Composition

7f5d74ce-ba5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Astrophysical Multimessenger Observatory Network (AMON)** is a network of astrophysical observatories in North America that uses multiple messengers like gravitational waves and gamma rays to detect and study cosmic phenomena.
7f5d74ce-ba5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astrophysical Multimessenger Observatory Network

7f643986-b8c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cosmic Ray Isotope Spectrometer (CRIS) on ACE is a particle detector designed to measure galactic cosmic ray nuclei from He to Zn at energies of 100 to 600 MeV/nucleon and explore ultra-heavy nuclei, using a combination of scintillating optical fibers and silicon solid-state detectors.
7f643986-b8c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cosmic Ray Isotope Spectrometer on Advanced Composition Explorer

7f65fbfc-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Norba Caesarina Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Cáceres, Spain. Known by its MPC ID Z71, it is situated at 6 Avenida Río Tíber and operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
7f65fbfc-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Aldea Moret Observatory, Spain

7f69feaa-bb0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ray Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Toyoura, Abuta County, Iburi Subprefecture, Hokkaido Prefecture, Japan. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 362 and specializes in ground-based observations.
7f69feaa-bb0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ray Observatory, Japan

7f7538f4-b800-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Waves instrument** is a complex device on the Juno spacecraft designed to detect and analyze wave electric and magnetic fields in various frequency ranges. It consists of antennas, pre-amplifiers, receivers, and a digital processing unit to capture and process signals from 50 Hz to 45.25 MHz, providing detailed spectral data and waveforms for studying plasma waves and other phenomena.
7f7538f4-b800-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Astronomy Instrument on Juno

7f7cedee-bb00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Fluxgate Magnetometer on Juno (FGM)** is a scientific instrument aboard the Juno spacecraft designed to measure Jupiter's magnetic field in three dimensions using miniature ring-core fluxgate sensors. It aims to map the planet's magnetic dynamo and interior, as well as explore its polar magnetosphere.
7f7cedee-bb00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer on Juno

7f7e861a-b8ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The MINiature Exoplanet Radial Velocity Array (MINERVA) is a 0.7-meter robotic observatory in North America designed for optical waveband observations, primarily focused on detecting and studying exoplanets through radial velocity measurements.
7f7e861a-b8ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical The Miniature Exoplanet Radial Velocity Array 0.7m robotic observatory

7f7fd764-b986-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTIs) All-Sky Imager at Kototabang, Indonesia is a multi-wavelength instrument designed to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere by observing nocturnal airglow emissions. Developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research at Nagoya University, it operates as part of the IUGONET Observatory network to provide comprehensive data on atmospheric phenomena.
7f7fd764-b986-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Multi-wavelength All-sky Imager part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers, Indonesia

7f85660c-bb52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Institute of Astronomy of Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń's 15m RT3 radio telescope is a facility located in Europe, featuring a 15-meter aperture and operating in the radio waveband for astronomical research.
7f85660c-bb52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 15.0m Radio Telescope at The Institute of Astronomy of Nicolaus Copernicus University

7f9325b8-b98a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Chinese VLBI Network (CVN) is a ground-based radio observatory located in China. It operates within the radio waveband and is designed for Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observations.
7f9325b8-b98a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chinese Very Long Baseline Interferometry Network

7f947ff4-b5f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Large Probe Nephelometer** (LN) of the Pioneer Venus mission was an instrument designed to measure cloud particle backscatter using a gallium arsenide laser LED and photodiodes, providing insights into Venus's cloud structure.
7f947ff4-b5f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Large Probe Nephelometer on Pioneer Venus

7fa12794-b769-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Alibag Magnetic Observatory** is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Alibag, Maharashtra, India, operated by the Indian Institute of Geomagnetism since 1923.
7fa12794-b769-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Alibag Magnetic Observatory, India

7fa3532c-ba0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer, specifically a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate model, that is part of the MAGDAS observation network and installed in Tohno, Japan.
7fa3532c-ba0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System Observation Network

7fb5fd10-b758-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gemini North is an astronomical observatory located on Mauna Kea in Hawaii. It serves as the northern hemisphere facility of the Gemini Observatory.
7fb5fd10-b758-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gemini North Observatory on Mauna Kea, United States

7fbe57ba-b8bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** POLAR was a NASA geomagnetic research satellite launched in 1996 as part of the Global Geospace Science (GGS) program to study the polar magnetosphere and aurorae. It operated until 2008, providing multi-wavelength imaging of the aurora and measuring plasma interactions within Earth's magnetic field.
7fbe57ba-b8bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Global Geospace Science (GGS) Polar satellite

7fc7157c-b687-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **iTelescope Observatory, Beryl Junction** is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in West 1800 North, Iron County, Utah, United States. It facilitates remote telescopic observations and research activities.
7fc7157c-b687-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: iTelescope Observatory, Beryl Junction

7fc823aa-b776-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The magnetometer on Pioneer 11 was a triaxial helium instrument designed to measure magnetic fields with high precision and sensitivity, capable of detecting fields from ±2.5 nT to ±1.0E-3 T in seven dynamic ranges.
7fc823aa-b776-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Pioneer 11

7fca8c60-b6ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory (DRAO) is a renowned research facility in Kaleden, British Columbia, Canada, dedicated to radio astronomy, housing multiple telescopes and supporting advanced instrumentation development.
7fca8c60-b6ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory, Canada

7fd685aa-b751-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Uummannaq Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG.
7fd685aa-b751-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Uummannaq Observatory

7fd8366a-b9c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Air Force Maui Optical and Supercomputing Site (AMOS)** is a ground-based observatory in Maui, Hawaii, managed by the U.S. Air Force for space surveillance and astronomical research.
7fd8366a-b9c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Air Force Maui Optical and Supercomputing Site

7fdd2c18-b745-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mid-Infrared Array Camera 2 (MIRAC2)** was an infrared instrument used for astronomical observations, operating at wavelengths from 2 to 28 microns and equipped with a high-performance arsenic-doped silicon array cooled by liquid helium. It was deployed on the UKIRT and IRTF telescopes to study various celestial objects including galaxies, nebulae, and Solar System bodies.
7fdd2c18-b745-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mid-Infrared Array Camera 2 on IRTF 3.0m Telescope

7fe053f0-bc42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The JCPM Hamatonbetsu Station is an astronomical observatory located in Hamatonbetsu, Esashi County, Soya Subprefecture, Hokkaido Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based observatory with the MPC ID 394.
7fe053f0-bc42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hamatonbetsu Observatory, Japan

7fe51816-b686-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition**:
Orange Bay is a ground-based observatory located in Cape Horn, Chile, part of the IAGA network, primarily known for its magnetometer instrument. It has been operational since 1883 and is situated at an altitude of 580 meters on the Earth's surface.
7fe51816-b686-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Orange Bay Observatory, Chile

7fef58ae-b789-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) 37m Haystack Radio Telescope is a large telescope located in North America with a 37-meter aperture designed for radio astronomy, operated by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
7fef58ae-b789-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 37.0m Haystack Radio Telescope at Haystack Observatory

7ff3a85a-bb03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Easter Island Observatory was a ground-based facility in Hanga Roa, Easter Island, Chile, that operated from 1959 to 1968, focusing on geomagnetic measurements as part of the IAGA observatory network.
7ff3a85a-bb03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Easter Island Observatory, Chile

7ffdad68-bba4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer, specifically a fluxgate type, located at the Valdivia geomagnetic observatory as part of the SAMBA Magnetometer Array.
7ffdad68-bba4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer at Valdivia Observatory

800973bc-b89a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Suprathermal Electron Telescope (STE) on STEREO A is an instrument designed to measure electrons in the energy range of ~2 keV to 20 keV, which are present as a superhalo on solar wind electrons and associated with Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs). It uses silicon semiconductor devices to trace heliospheric magnetic field lines and probe the structure of interplanetary CMEs and the inner heliosphere.
800973bc-b89a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Suprathermal Electron Telescope on Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory A

800b25ae-b854-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **Riometer** is a scientific instrument used to measure radio wave absorption in the Earth's ionosphere. The 60MHz Riometer at Nyrola, Finland, specifically features an 8x8-element dipole antenna array and produces independent beams covering an area of about 180km x 180km at D region altitude to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere.
800b25ae-b854-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Riometer at IUGONET Observatory

8011f6ca-b847-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 30MHz Imaging Riometer (IRIO) at Tjornes, Iceland, is an instrument used for studying the ionosphere's D region. It features an 8x8-element dipole antenna array and generates 8x8 independent beams covering approximately 180km x 180km in area.
8011f6ca-b847-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 30 MHz Imaging Riometer on Conjugate Observation at Iceland

8018776c-b909-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Retarding Potential Analyzer (ORPA)** on the Pioneer Venus Orbiter was a Langmuir-probe instrument designed to measure electron and ion concentrations, temperatures, drift velocities, and photoelectron energy distributions in the Venusian ionosphere. It aimed to study plasma transport processes, polar wind presence, and solar wind-ionosphere boundary interactions on Venus.
8018776c-b909-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Retarding Potential Analyzer part of Pioneer Venus Orbiter

801bd114-b670-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Europa Imaging System (EIS) Narrow-Angle Camera (NAC) is an eight-megapixel camera designed to capture high-resolution color and stereoscopic images of Europa, studying geologic activity and providing context for other instruments.
801bd114-b670-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Europa Imaging System Narrow-Angle Camera on Clipper

801ee9e8-babd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Mazariegos Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Mazariegos, Palencia, Spain, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
801ee9e8-babd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mazariegos Observatory, Spain

8023b06c-ba4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU Radio Beacon Receiver (GRBR) Station at Yogyakarta is an observatory in Indonesia, located near the equator. It measures ionospheric disturbances related to middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes using a specialized radio beacon receiver.
8023b06c-ba4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU Radio Beacon Receiver Station at Yogyakarta, Indonesia

802764f0-bb09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wendelstein Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Brannenburg, Bavaria, Germany, known for its 2-meter telescope and ground-based observational facilities.
802764f0-bb09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2m Telescope at Wendelstein Observatory, Germany

80472282-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: HALCA, or Highly Advanced Laboratory for Communications and Astronomy, was a Japanese radio telescope satellite used for Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI), launched in 1997 to study distant celestial objects with high resolution.
80472282-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 8m Highly Advanced Laboratory for Communications and Astronomy on VLBI Space Observatory Programme

804de622-ba30-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment (MOXIE) is an instrument onboard the Perseverance rover designed to produce oxygen from carbon dioxide in the Martian atmosphere using solid state electrolysis.
804de622-ba30-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Oxygen In-Situ Resource Utilization Experiment part of Perseverance Rover

804e4878-b68a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Rikubetsu, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network.
804e4878-b68a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of 210 Magnetic Meridian Magnetometer Network

80519dfa-b80d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Muntinlupa, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network, designed to measure magnetic fields.
80519dfa-b80d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of 210 Magnetic Meridian Magnetometer Network

807dc44e-b91f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cape Kamenniy Geomagnetic Observatory (CKA) is a ground-based facility located in Yamalsky Rayon, Russia, that operated from 1973 to 1976 for geomagnetic measurements.
807dc44e-b91f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cape Kamenniy Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

8080a158-b971-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at Andrews Air Force Base (AWS), operational since January 1972, is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network within the IUGONET observatory.
8080a158-b971-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Andrews Observatory

808fbfd4-b5c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a set of three single-frequency GPS receivers installed at Kototabang, Indonesia, designed to measure signal intensity and amplitude scintillation index S4 for studying ionospheric irregularities.
808fbfd4-b5c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GPS Scintillation Antenna part of IUGONET Observatory

8090c4a0-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Onagawa, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network under IUGONET Observatory.
8090c4a0-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of 210 Magnetic Meridian Network

809be2d4-bb8c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Zen Observatory in Scandicci is a ground-based astronomical facility located at 28d Via Ilio Barontini, Florence, Italy. It is situated at coordinates 43.77458 latitude and 11.13494 longitude within the continent of Europe.
809be2d4-bb8c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Zen Observatory, Italy

80aca53c-b737-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Rude Skov Geomagnetic Observatory (RSV)** was a ground-based facility located in Rudersdal Municipality, Denmark, operational from 1927 to 1981, primarily used for geomagnetic measurements.
80aca53c-b737-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Rude Skov Geomagnetic Observatory, Denmark

80ace3c2-b83a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EPIC (Energetic Particles and Ion Composition) investigation is an instrument designed to study the outer magnetosphere and distant magnetotail region by measuring the charge state, mass, and energy of ions and electrons using two main sensor assemblies: STICS for suprathermal ions and ICS for energetic ions.
80ace3c2-b83a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particles and Ion Composition part of Geotail

80b3243c-b770-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Yatsugatake-Kobuchizawa Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Hokuto, Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting various astronomical observations and research.
80b3243c-b770-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Yatsugatake-Kobuchizawa Observatory, Japan

80b9dd64-bbd4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Mayhill is a ground-based observatory located in Otero County, New Mexico, United States. Known as Dimension Point, it is situated at coordinates 32.91304° N, 254.47472° E within the Milky Way region.
80b9dd64-bbd4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dimension Point Observatory, United States

80c09980-b862-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GINOP-KHK Observatory (also known as the Piszkesteto Observatory) is an astronomical observatory located in Mátraszentimre, Hungary. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to studying celestial phenomena and events.
80c09980-b862-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Piszkesteto Observatory, Hungary

80c5b554-b629-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **IAGA:PAT Magnetometer**, operational from 1954 to 1956 at the Patrick observatory, was a ground-based instrument used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigations.
80c5b554-b629-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Patrick Observatory

80d2e8b6-b8fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Miwa Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Tsumagoi, Agatsuma County, Gunma Prefecture, Japan, known for its ground-based facilities.
80d2e8b6-b8fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 377-1613 Miwa Observatory, Japan

80d33dbe-bb3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Culgoora Radio Spectrograph is an instrument located at the Culgoora Solar Observatory in New South Wales, Australia, used for monitoring solar radio bursts by sweeping through a frequency range of 18-1800 MHz every 3 seconds.
80d33dbe-bb3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Spectrometer part of Culgoora Observatory, Australia

80d793c2-b9ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Umbrella Observatory** (also known as the Fredenbeck Observatory) is an astronomical observatory located in Fredenbeck, Germany. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 243 and focuses on ground-based observations.
80d793c2-b9ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Umbrella Observatory, Germany

80da096a-b772-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ultraviolet Photometer for P11 is a specialized instrument designed to detect and measure ultraviolet radiation, providing crucial data on atmospheric properties, space weather, and celestial bodies during the P11 mission.
80da096a-b772-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Photometer on Pioneer 11

80dcb460-b7d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EMN Peradenia Station** is a ground-based magnetometer network located in Kandy, Sri Lanka, dedicated to monitoring and studying the Earth's magnetic field. It operates under IUGONET (Inter-university Upper atmosphere Global Observation NETwork) and includes a fluxgate instrument for precise measurements.
80dcb460-b7d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at EMN Peradenia Observatory, Sri Lanka

80de17f0-b775-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Longwave Infrared Camera (LIR)** is an instrument onboard the Akatsuki spacecraft that detects thermal emissions from cloud tops over a wavelength region of 8-12 um to map cloud-top temperatures, providing valuable data for studying Venus' atmospheric conditions.
80de17f0-b775-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Longwave Infrared Camera on Akatsuki Spacecraft

80e7b05a-b99e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2O Optical Photometer** is an instrument designed to detect visible light flux at wavelengths near 486.1 nm during relativistic electron precipitation events, specifically to determine the presence of accompanying protons and support theories on scattering mechanisms involving EMIC waves.
80e7b05a-b99e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible Light Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

80e954ea-ba21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2L Data Processing Unit (DPU)** is a versatile instrument controller for the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) project. It collects data from various sensors, formats it, and sends it via an Iridium modem while managing system commands and operations using a flexible FPGA-based design.
80e954ea-ba21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

80ea47ac-b7cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Loring AFB Geomagnetic Observatory (LOB), located in Limestone, Maine, USA, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1966 to 1972, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
80ea47ac-b7cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Loring AFB Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

80eadf22-b846-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Quito Astronomical Observatory (OAQ) is a research institute of the National Polytechnic School in Quito, Ecuador, focusing on astronomy and atmospheric physics. It was established in 1873 and is located at an altitude of 2823 meters.
80eadf22-b846-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Astronómico de Quito, Ecuador

80f005fc-b8e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Willis Island station is an observatory located on Willis Island in the Coral Sea Islands, Australia. It has been operational since December 2010 and includes instruments for monitoring ionospheric scintillation.
80f005fc-b8e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor on Willis Island, Australia

8100825e-bc1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Burlington Geomagnetic Observatory (BRT), located in Kit Carson County, Colorado, was a ground-based facility operational from 1957 to 1959 that conducted geomagnetic measurements using magnetometers.
8100825e-bc1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Burlington Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

810866c4-b7dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, and the ones at North Pole 13 (NPM) specifically monitor geomagnetic activity in that region.
810866c4-b7dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of World Data Center for Geomagnetism, Kyoto

81195006-ba20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AMPTE/CCE Charge-Energy-Mass experiment (CHEM) is an energetic particle instrument designed to measure the energy and composition of charged particles in space. It operates within an energy range of 1 to 300 keV/q, providing detailed data on various species including hydrogen, helium, oxygen, and other elements up to iron.
81195006-ba20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Charge-Energy-Mass experiment part of AMPTE CCE

811df7c6-b63f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
BARREL Balloon 1Q is a scientific payload launched as part of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) mission, designed to study the escape of particles from Earth's radiation belts by measuring Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating relativistic electrons in the stratosphere.
811df7c6-b63f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star Geospace Mission of Opportunity

811f7214-b918-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Mount Tuffley Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Gloucester, England, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial bodies.
811f7214-b918-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mount Tuffley Observatory, United Kingdom

81390782-b85b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 2 FIELDS Suite, Electron Drift Instrument (EDI) measures electric and magnetic fields by tracking the drift of ~1 keV electrons emitted from its Gun Detector Unit, contributing to the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission's study of Earth's magnetosphere.
81390782-b85b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Drift Instrument part of MMS 2 FIELDS Suite

8143a4c4-b8bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU radio beacon receiver (GRBR) station at Kuala Lumpur is an observatory in Malaysia, part of the GRBR network, used to study ionospheric disturbances and atmospheric coupling processes.
8143a4c4-b8bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU radio beacon receiver station at Kuala Lumpur

814c7e8a-b684-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1.3-m Boller & Chivens Cassegrain reflector is a 1.3 meter telescope situated at the Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona, USA. It was constructed around 1965 and is used for astronomical observations.
814c7e8a-b684-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.3m Boller & Chivens Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory, United States

814f03fe-b7d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the station with the IAGA identifier AED, part of the iugonet-observatory-wdc_kyoto network.
814f03fe-b7d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

8159d0d4-b946-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Lycksele Geomagnetic Observatory (LYC), located in Sweden, was a ground facility operating from 2008 to 2016 that conducted geomagnetic measurements as part of the global INTERMAGNET network.
8159d0d4-b946-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lycksele Geomagnetic Observatory, Sweden

8160617e-b856-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1V Tilt Compensated Magnetometer (TCM2)** is a three-axis magnetometer used in the BARREL project to measure magnetic field components with high resolution, identifying substorm activity and ULF oscillations. It includes tilt sensors for separating horizontal and vertical components of the magnetic field, enhancing its precision in investigating relativistic electron losses.
8160617e-b856-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

816a7c92-bba1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** DMSP 5D-2/F13, also known as USA 109, is a meteorological satellite developed and operated by the U.S. Air Force under the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) to provide global visual and infrared cloud cover data for weather analysis and forecasting requirements of the Department of Defense.
816a7c92-bba1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: infrared Defense Meteorological Satellite Program part of DMSP

816b7d76-b616-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kiel Magnetometer was an instrument used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field at the IAGA station in Kiel, operational from 1856 to 1890.
816b7d76-b616-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy

8173e90c-bb11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tucson Geomagnetic Observatory (TUC) is a ground-based facility located in Pima County, Arizona, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity. It operates under the INTERMAGNET network and has been active since January 1, 2007.
8173e90c-bb11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tucson Geomagnetic Observatory

817ceef4-bb2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CLPS Task Order PRIME-1 Laser Retro-Reflector Array (LRA) is a small, passive optical instrument designed for precision laser ranging from lunar orbit, enabling geolocation of the lander and establishing a fiducial marker on the moon's surface.
817ceef4-bb2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Laser Retroreflector Array on CLPS Task Order PRIME-1 Athena

8180bbda-bb81-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "210MM Chichijima station" is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Ogasawara, Japan. It is part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network and features a fluxgate instrument for measuring magnetic fields.
8180bbda-bb81-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Chichijima Observatory, Japan

818393a0-b78a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Shillong Geomagnetic Observatory (SHL), located in Shillong, India, was a ground facility dedicated to geophysical observations and operated until December 31, 2014. It featured magnetometers from the WDC Kyoto as part of its instrumentation.
818393a0-b78a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Shillong Geomagnetic Observatory, India

81877690-b61e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is a **3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer** located in College, United States. It is part of the IUGONET observatory and is used to measure magnetic fields as part of the CPMN observation network.
81877690-b61e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometer Network

818c0dd2-b753-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Microscopic Imager (MI) was a fixed-focus camera on the rover's extendable arm, designed to capture high-resolution images of Martian rocks and soils for geological analysis.
818c0dd2-b753-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Microscopic Imager part of Mars Exploration Rover Spirit

8190c03a-b8c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AGO P2 Magnetometer Instrument is a device located at the ICESTAR observatory's AGO P2 ground station, designed to measure magnetic fields and variations in the Earth's magnetosphere.
8190c03a-b8c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Conjugate Point for Exploration, Science, Technology And Research Investigation

81a2903e-bc6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA station Gibilmanna, operational from January 1, 1954 to December 31, 1957.
81a2903e-bc6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iugonet Observatory

81a8fe0e-b79b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Charged Particle Instrument for P11** was a space-based experiment that used two telescopes to measure the composition and energy spectra of solar and galactic particles above 0.5 MeV/nucleon, providing data on particle arrival direction and interplanetary regions.
81a8fe0e-b79b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Charged Particle Instrument for P11 on Spacecraft

81b1546a-b678-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Roquetes, Spain (URSI-code: EB040) is a ground facility that uses advanced ionosondes to analyze skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere, evaluating parameters like angle of arrival, polarization, and Doppler frequency shift.
81b1546a-b678-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Station at Roquetes Observatory, Spain

81cf2636-b69e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Langmuir Probe** is a type of electric field instrument launched on December 2, 2013, as part of the SWARM-C mission. It features two probes operating in a harmonic mode to measure currents and admittances, marking a novel approach for orbital measurements.
81cf2636-b69e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Langmuir Probe on Swarm-C Spacecraft

81d25b46-b91c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **GOES 10 (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite)** is a geosynchronous spacecraft launched in 1997 as part of the GOES-NEXT series, designed to monitor weather systems over the United States and provide meteorological data, environmental monitoring, and solar disturbance warnings. It carries various instruments for Earth imaging, atmospheric sounding, space environment monitoring, search and rescue, and data collection.
81d25b46-b91c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 10

81dcd9f4-b90d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The HARIMAU transportable wind profiler (LQ7) is an active-phased array radar located in Manado, Indonesia, designed to observe wind velocity and atmospheric turbulence profiles throughout the lower troposphere. It operates at a frequency of 1357.5 MHz with a peak transmitted power of 2800 W and features electronically steerable antennas for comprehensive wind component estimation.
81dcd9f4-b90d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar part of Hydrometeorological Array for Isv-Monsoon Automonitoring

81debc1a-b75f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Autonomous University of Mexico's 2.12m Telescope at the OAN Sierra San Pedro Martir is a ground-based observatory located in Baja California, Mexico, dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
81debc1a-b75f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.12m Telescope at El Observatorio Astronomico Nacional Sierra San Pedro Martir

81dfca74-b976-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kitab Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Kitab, Uzbekistan. It has been operational since June 20, 1928, and is situated at an altitude of 650 meters.
81dfca74-b976-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kitab Observatory, Uzbekistan

81e22ba2-b912-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Centro Astronómico Hispano-Alemán is a ground-based observatory located at Calar Alto in Spain.
81e22ba2-b912-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.23m Telescope at Centro Astrónomico Hispano-Alemán

81eb656a-b6f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Palominas Observatory, located in Cochise County, Arizona, USA, is an astronomical observatory situated on Earth and identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID 925.
81eb656a-b6f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Palominas Observatory, United States

81eedfe0-bbb1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pico dos Dias Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Minas Gerais, Brazil, operated by the National Astrophysical Laboratory of Brazil. It features a 1.6m Perkin-Elmer telescope and a 0.6m Boller and Chivens telescope for ground observations.
81eedfe0-bbb1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.6m Perkin-Elmer Telescope at Pico dos Dias Observatory, Brazil and 0.6m Boller and Chivens Telescope at Pico dos Dias Observatory, Brazil

81efad3c-b731-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS Flux Gate Magnetometer (FGM) is an instrument onboard the THEMIS spacecraft that measures background magnetic fields and low-frequency fluctuations with high precision, utilizing advanced digital technology for improved robustness and reduced mass. It was developed by the Technical University of Braunschweig in Germany and led by K. H. Glassmeier.
81efad3c-b731-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tri-axial Fluxgate Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission

81fa3cd6-b73e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISON-Castelgrande Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Castelgrande, Potenza, Basilicata, Italy. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
81fa3cd6-b73e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ISON-Castelgrande Observatory, Italy

81ffb7f4-b902-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1J was part of a NASA mission to study the escape of particles from Earth's radiation belts, conducted in the stratosphere from January 1, 2013, to January 15, 2013. This specific balloon carried instruments to measure X-rays and magnetic fields, contributing to the broader BARREL campaign that aimed to understand electron loss mechanisms in coordination with NASA's Van Allen Probes.
81ffb7f4-b902-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star Mission of Opportunity

820c369e-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operated in Anchorage from 1957 to 1959 as part of the IAGA investigation.
820c369e-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Anchorage Observatory

820ef64e-bbb2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Voyager 2 is a space probe launched by NASA in 1977 to study the outer Solar System. It is currently the second furthest spacecraft from Earth after Voyager 1 and has explored Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and interstellar space beyond the heliosphere.
820ef64e-bbb2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Voyager 2

82150810-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Digisonde ionospheric station at Anyang, Korea (URSI-code: AN438) is an advanced facility that measures various properties of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere to evaluate its characteristics. It operated from 1998 to 2009 and was located in South Korea.
82150810-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde Ionospheric Station at Anyang Observatory, South Korea

821f8a58-ba64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High Resolution Stereo Camera (HRSC) is a sophisticated imaging instrument aboard the European Space Agency's Mars Express mission, designed to capture high-resolution stereoscopic and multispectral images of the Martian surface for geological and atmospheric studies.
821f8a58-ba64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Multispectral Camera on Mars Express

82278c26-b825-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at BJI** is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed in Beijing, China, as part of the IUGONET observatory network. It measures magnetic field variations to study geomagnetic phenomena and related space weather events.
82278c26-b825-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of China Permanent Magnetic Network Observation Network

822a1832-bb9b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cormons Observatory (MPC ID: A94) is an astronomical observatory located in Cormons, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility and is situated at coordinates 13.4577 longitude and 45.95736 latitude.
822a1832-bb9b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cormons Observatory, Italy

8230a684-b696-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Sasaguri FM-CW radar station, located in Kanzaki, Saga Prefecture, Japan, is a ground facility part of the MAGDAS FM-CW radar network used for observing and studying Earth's surface.
8230a684-b696-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: FM-CW Radar Station at MAGDAS Observatory, Japan

824ccac6-b916-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lunar Prospector Spacecraft Radio Science Subsystem was a communication and scientific data link between the Lunar Prospector satellite and ground stations, facilitating radio tracking experiments to study the Moon's gravity field.
824ccac6-b916-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Subsystem on Lunar Prospector

8259086a-bad1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Chante-Perdrix Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Dauban, Banon, France, dedicated to ground-based observations.
8259086a-bad1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chante-Perdrix Observatory, France

82642f02-b6c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The PASTIS Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Banon, France. It is situated at coordinates 5.64731 longitude and 43.999461 latitude within the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence region of Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur.
82642f02-b6c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Banon Observatory, France

82698ed0-b7d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, particularly those associated with Earth's geomagnetic field. The specific instance referred to here includes magnetometers deployed at the North Pole 12 (NPL) observatory as part of the IUGONET network, contributing to geophysical research and monitoring.
82698ed0-b7d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole 12

826a6886-b6d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Penn Heights Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Rickmansworth, Hertfordshire, England. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
826a6886-b6d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Penn Heights Observatory, United Kingdom

82703964-bb7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Topside Plasma Sounder on Ohzora is an instrument designed to measure ionospheric electron density profiles, detect radio waves emanating from planets, and observe higher harmonic emissions from terrestrial electric power lines.
82703964-bb7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Topside Plasma Sounder on Ohzora

827ec48c-bbcc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Warrumbungle Observatory, located in Coonabarabran, Australia, is an astronomical observatory known for its ground-based facilities and contributions to astrophysics research.
827ec48c-bbcc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Warrumbungle Observatory, Australia

82951ad6-b602-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Bülach Observatory (German: Sternwarte Bülach) is a public astronomical observatory located near Bülach in the canton of Zürich, Switzerland.
82951ad6-b602-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bülach Observatory, Switzerland

82972ffe-ba37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kogota Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Wakuya, Toda County, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan. It has the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 356 and is situated at coordinates 141.0867 longitude and 38.540262 latitude on Earth.
82972ffe-ba37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kogota Observatory, Japan

829ad418-b863-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ISEE Magnetometer** is an induction magnetometer located at the Kevo observatory, designed to measure variations in the 3-D vector geomagnetic field with a sampling rate of 64 Hz. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network and operates under the control of a PC clock signal.
829ad418-b863-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Solar-Terrestrial Physics Investigation

82a0d9d4-b783-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tsingtao Field Station is an astronomical observatory located on the Xisha Islands in China.
82a0d9d4-b783-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Tsingtao Field Station Observatory, China

82ac4206-b99f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** INTEGRAL (International Gamma-Ray Astrophysics Laboratory) is a European Space Agency (ESA) space telescope launched in 2002 to study celestial gamma-ray sources in the energy range of 15 keV to 10 MeV. It features instruments like SPI, IBIS, JEM-X, and OMC for detailed gamma ray imaging and spectroscopy.
82ac4206-b99f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: gamma ray International Gamma-Ray Astrophysics Laboratory

82ad28a0-bbad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **PUNCH-NFI (Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere – Narrow Field Imager)** is a NASA space telescope designed to observe the inner heliosphere using an externally occulted visible-light coronagraph, focusing on understanding how coronal structures become the solar wind and tracking transient phenomena like coronal mass ejections.
82ad28a0-bbad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible-light Narrow Field Imager on Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere

82b11bac-b9a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hallett Geomagnetic Observatory (HLL), located in Antarctica at coordinates -72.32 latitude and 170.22 longitude, was a ground facility operated by New Zealand from 1957 to 1963 for geomagnetic measurements.
82b11bac-b9a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hallett Geomagnetic Observatory

82b1ead8-b690-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Center for Astrophysical Research in Antarctica (CARA) 2.1m Viper Submillimeter Telescope is a research facility located in Antarctica, designed to observe the universe in the millimeter waveband using a telescope with an aperture of 2.1 meters.
82b1ead8-b690-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter 2.1m Center for Astrophysical Research in Antarctica Viper submillimeter Telescope, Antarctica

82c23e10-ba5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Byrd Station 2 is a geophysical observatory established on August 1, 1957, located in Antarctica (-80.017 latitude and 240.483 longitude) that includes instruments such as a magnetometer for monitoring Earth's magnetic field and other geophysical phenomena.
82c23e10-ba5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Byrd Station 2 Observatory, Antarctica

82c25f60-b70a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Jiama'erdeng Station of the Purple Mountain Observatory** is a ground-based astronomical observatory located at China National Highway 219, Günsa Township, Gar County, Ngari Prefecture, Tibet, China. It is situated at approximately 32.32494° N latitude and 80.02674° E longitude on the Asian continent.
82c25f60-b70a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Purple Mountain Observatory at Jiama'erdeng, China

82c76704-b72c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Exploration Rover Spirit (MER 2) Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT) was a sophisticated instrument on the Spirit rover designed to expose fresh surfaces of Martian rocks by brushing away dust and debris, acting as both a geologic hammer and a tool for studying rock physical properties.
82c76704-b72c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rock Abrasion Tool on Mars Exploration Rover Spirit

82d0fd42-b6f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Hibiscus Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Puna'auia, French Polynesia. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the study of celestial phenomena from its Earth-bound location at specific geographic coordinates (-149.6158 longitude and -17.634072 latitude).
82d0fd42-b6f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hibiscus Observatory, French Polynesia

82e3bc40-ba12-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Binza Geomagnetic Observatory (BIN) was a ground-based facility located in Lissanga, Congo-Brazzaville, operational from 1953 to 1973, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity.
82e3bc40-ba12-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Binza Geomagnetic Observatory

82fba11a-b649-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
AstroKoT in Port-Sainte-Marie is a ground observatory located at Église Saint-Julien in France. It serves as an astronomical facility for observations and research.
82fba11a-b649-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: AstroKoT Observatory, France

831094ea-b805-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sirius Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Las Lomas, León, Spain. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID Z75.
831094ea-b805-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sirius Observatory, Spain

831654ae-bab5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Waizenreuth Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Weidenberg, Bavaria, Germany. It is a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center code K64.
831654ae-bab5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Waizenreuth Observatory, Germany

831cbb3c-bb69-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) All-Sky Imager at Nyrola, Finland is a multi-wavelength instrument designed to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere by observing nocturnal airglow emissions. It was developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research at Nagoya University and is part of the IUGONET Observatory.
831cbb3c-bb69-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: All-Sky Imager part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers

83226178-ba2d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Youndegin observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Western Australia at coordinates -31.82052 latitude and 117.28146 longitude. It operates under the designation 6R-AUS1 within the Shire of Cunderdin, situated on Mills Road in Youndegin.
83226178-ba2d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: [Entity Name Unknown] at Youndegin Observatory, Australia

832360a6-b75c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
El Guijo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Galapagar, Community of Madrid, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
832360a6-b75c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: El Guijo Observatory, Spain

83253f00-bb4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at Wien-Kobenzl observatory, operational from 1954 to 1898, used for measuring and studying the Earth's magnetic field as part of the IAGA investigation.
83253f00-bb4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Wien Kobenzl Observatory

83288bec-b91b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Resolute Bay Magnetic Observatory** is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Resolute, Nunavut, Canada, operated by the Geological Survey of Canada since 1957. It is part of the global INTERMAGNET network and contributes to monitoring Earth's magnetic field.
83288bec-b91b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Resolute Bay Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

833350e2-b7cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Colville National Forest (NEW) Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation since 2007.
833350e2-b7cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Colville National Forest Observatory

833418b6-b689-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MF radar at Syowa Station, Antarctica is an instrument that measures horizontal wind profiles in the mesosphere and lower thermosphere using full-correlation analysis and meteor echo measurement. It operates within the IUGONET observatory network based in Kyoto.
833418b6-b689-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: MF Radar at Syowa Observatory, Antarctica

83363bee-bbbd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Comet Nucleus Tour (CONTOUR) was a NASA Discovery-class space probe launched in 2002 to study comets, but it failed shortly after launch and was presumed lost.
83363bee-bbbd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Comet Nucleus Tour spacecraft part of Comet Nucleus Tour mission

8338fd3e-bb95-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **210MM Magnetometer Network** is a fluxgate magnetometer located in Moshiri, operated by the IUGONET-Observatory. It measures magnetic field variations along the 210th meridian as part of a broader network to monitor geomagnetic activity.
8338fd3e-bb95-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observatory

835e6ba6-b748-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nagycenk Magnetic Observatory, located in Fertőboz, Hungary, is a ground-based facility dedicated to monitoring and studying the Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since 1993 and is funded by the Geodéziai és Geofizikai Kutatóintézet.
835e6ba6-b748-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nagycenk Magnetic Observatory, Hungary

835eb818-b5b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 12 Solar Wind Spectrometer (SWS) was an instrument deployed on the Moon during the Apollo 12 mission to measure protons and electrons in the solar wind and magnetotail plasma, helping study lunar surface properties and general solar wind characteristics.
835eb818-b5b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Wind Spectrometer part of Apollo 12

8365568e-bc7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lazarev Geomagnetic Observatory (LZV) is a ground-based facility located on Earth's surface at an altitude of 430.0 meters and coordinates -69.97 latitude, 12.9 longitude, which operated from January 1, 1960, to December 31, 1961.
8365568e-bc7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lazarev Geomagnetic Observatory

836990c4-bc31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Innhovde (IHD) is a ground-based observatory located in Antarctica, part of the automated magnetometer network near Syowa Station, equipped with instruments to measure magnetic fields.
836990c4-bc31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Innhovde, Antarctica

836bea7c-bb37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sternwarte Metzerlen is an astronomical observatory located in Metzerlen-Mariastein, Solothurn, Switzerland. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
836bea7c-bb37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Metzerlen Observatory, Switzerland

836d005e-bb43-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Redondo Beach Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Redondo Beach, California, dedicated to ground-based observations.
836d005e-bb43-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Redondo Beach Observatory, United States

83745740-b8e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Thule Neutron Monitor** is a ground-based scientific facility located in Thule, Greenland, part of the Intermagnet network. It has been operational since January 1947 and is situated at an altitude of 57 meters on Earth's surface.
83745740-b8e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutron Monitor at Thule Ground Observatory, Greenland

83780424-b9cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Leningradskaya geophysical observatory used for measuring magnetic field variations. It was first operational starting January 1, 1977.
83780424-b9cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Leningradskaya Observatory

838ea846-b5b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of California 2.4m Automated Planet Finder (APF) Telescope is a robotic optical telescope located at Lick Observatory in North America, designed for the detection and characterization of exoplanets.
838ea846-b5b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 2.4m Automated Planet Finder Telescope at Lick Observatory

83900340-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Zaymishche Observatory was a ground-based facility in Kazan, Russia, operational from July 1957 to December 31, 1989, known for its magnetometer instruments.
83900340-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Zaymishche Ground Observatory

8395d6a0-b7ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Aravaca Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Madrid, Spain, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial bodies.
8395d6a0-b7ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Aravaca Observatory, Spain

83b4862c-ba5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **Magnetometer** is a scientific instrument that measures the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Equatorial Magnetometer Network (EMN) includes a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed at Chambon la Foret, France, as part of its observatory infrastructure.
83b4862c-ba5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of Equatorial Magnetometer Network

83b683f6-bbc4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Artemis Observatory (MPC ID: Z25) is an astronomical observatory located in Teide National Park, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain. It is a ground-based facility situated at coordinates 343.49031 longitude and 28.300012 latitude.
83b683f6-bbc4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Teide Observatory, Spain

83bfac2c-ba2c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sanglok Observatory Photometer-Polarimeter** is a single-channel instrument developed at the Institute of Astrophysics of Tadjik Academy of Sciences, capable of performing quasi-simultaneous photometric and polarimetric observations within a wavelength range of 0.35-0.75 microns using a rapidly rotating polarizer.
83bfac2c-ba2c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Single-channel Photometer-Polarimeter at Sanglok Observatory

83d82b88-b736-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Springbok Observatory (code L80) is an astronomical observatory located at the Tivoli Landing Site in Khomas Region, Namibia. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
83d82b88-b736-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tivoli Observatory, Namibia

83de0b84-b73b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SAMBA Magnetometer Array, specifically the Fluxgate Magnetometer instrument at the Antofagasta geomagnetic observatory, is a ground-based tool used to measure and monitor variations in the Earth's magnetic field. It is part of the broader SAMBA (South American Meridional B-field Array) network designed for detailed geomagnetic observations.
83de0b84-b73b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer at Antofagasta Observatory

83e8c694-baf3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cat's Eye Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Manciano, Grosseto, Tuscany, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for stargazing and astronomical research.
83e8c694-baf3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cat's Eye Observatory, Italy

83e972a8-b88f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **NEO Surveyor**: A spacecraft designed for surveying Near-Earth Objects (NEOs), aimed at identifying and studying asteroids that pose potential hazards to Earth.
83e972a8-b88f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared NEO Surveyor

83e9efc0-b804-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Deep Sky West Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in San Miguel County, New Mexico. It is situated at the coordinates 35.33108 latitude and -104.65353 longitude (254.34647 converted to a negative value for western hemisphere), serving as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
83e9efc0-b804-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep Sky West Observatory, United States

83ec63a0-ba3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AGO P6 Ground Observatory, located on Earth's surface at coordinates latitude -71.07 and longitude 127.87 with an altitude of 2343 meters, is part of the ICESTAR observatory network and includes a specific instrument designated for search coil operations.
83ec63a0-ba3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Instrument at AGO P6 Ground Observatory

83f0848c-b702-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Purple Mountain Observatory; Qinhai Observation Station is a ground-based observatory located in China, known for its 13.7m Delingha telescope operated by the National Astronomical Observatories of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (NAOC).
83f0848c-b702-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 13.7m Telescope at Purple Mountain Observatory, China

83f62602-b636-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dusheti geophysical observatory is a ground-based facility located in Aragvispiri, Dusheti Municipality, Georgia, that operates a magnetometer and contributes to the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA).
83f62602-b636-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dusheti Observatory, Georgia

8405d4e0-b9cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Terahertz Far-Infrared Beamline at the Australian Synchrotron Facility provides edge and bending magnet radiation, offering high-resolution infrared spectroscopy with energy coverage from 0.4 to 100 µm and beam sizes ranging from 8 x 8 µm to 3 x 3 µm.
8405d4e0-b9cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terahertz and Far Infrared Beamline at Australian Synchrotron

8413f9f2-b89d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Equatorial Magnetometer Network (EMN) operates a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer located in Ariquemes, Brazil. This instrument is part of the IUGONET Observatory and measures magnetic field variations to study geomagnetic phenomena.
8413f9f2-b89d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of The Equatorial Magnetometer Network

84141846-b6c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Double Star 1 (TC-1) was a joint Chinese-European geomagnetic satellite launched in 2003 to study Earth's magnetosphere, carrying instruments from both the European Space Agency (ESA) and China National Space Administration (CNSA).
84141846-b6c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Double Star 1 part of Double Star Mission

8422b0be-bb4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetometer at Apia is an instrument located in the IUGONET Observatory network, specifically identified by IAGA as API, and has been operational since 1905. It measures magnetic field variations to contribute to global geomagnetic studies under the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA).
8422b0be-bb4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iugonet Observatory

8424c3f2-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Student Nitric Oxide Explorer (SNOE) Ultraviolet Spectrometer (UVS) is an instrument designed to measure nitric oxide density in Earth's upper atmosphere by observing specific gamma bands. It utilizes an Ebert-Fastie spectrometer, a telescope, and phototube detectors mounted on the SNOE spacecraft.
8424c3f2-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Spectrometer part of Student Nitric Oxide Explorer

842b2f52-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Venera 3 Energetic Particles** experiment was a suite of Soviet particle detectors designed to monitor the flux of charged particles in interplanetary space and near Venus, measuring protons and electrons at various energy levels and directions.
842b2f52-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particles experiment on Venera 3

843b92fa-b762-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Pianoro Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Pianoro, Italy. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
843b92fa-b762-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pianoro Observatory, Italy

843f4f24-b83b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hinode EUV Imaging Spectrometer (EIS) is an instrument onboard the Hinode observatory that simultaneously measures ultraviolet radiation in the 170-210 and 250-290 Angstrom ranges using two large back-illuminated CCDs, designed to study solar phenomena.
843f4f24-b83b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: EUV Imaging Spectrometer on Hinode

844e927c-b7a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Gières Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Gières, France, with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code B83.
844e927c-b7a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gières Observatory, France

84500c7c-b194-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at PON" is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed at Pohnpei, Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), which is part of the CPMN observation network under the IUGONET observatory.
84500c7c-b194-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of CPMN observation network

8459fcce-b9fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ashkhabad Geomagnetic Observatory (ASH) is a ground-based facility located in Ashgabat City, Turkmenistan, that has been operating since 1959 to monitor geomagnetic activity on Earth's surface. It is part of the International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics network and includes instruments such as magnetometers for data collection.
8459fcce-b9fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Vannovskaya Ground Observatory, Turkmenistan

845bdaa6-baf5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bommes Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Le Tachon, Bommes, within the Gironde region of France. It serves as an observational site for studying celestial phenomena and conducting astronomical research.
845bdaa6-baf5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bommes Observatory, France

8460961c-b7fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nairobi Geomagnetic Observatory (NAI), located in Kenya, is a ground-based facility that operated from 1964 to 1980, focusing on geomagnetic measurements and contributing data to the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto.
8460961c-b7fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nairobi Geomagnetic Observatory, Kenya

84618738-bc0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences (NAOC) 1m New Vacuum Solar Telescope (NVST) is a solar observatory located in Yunnan, China, designed for infrared observations with a telescope aperture of 1.0 meters.
84618738-bc0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared National Astronomical Observatories 1m New Vacuum Solar Telescope at Yunnan Astronomical Observatory

8480c172-b81b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vatican Observatory is an astronomical research and educational institution supported by the Holy See, currently headquartered in Castel Gandolfo, Italy.
8480c172-b81b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vatican Observatory at Castel Gandolfo, Italy

8487ba74-bad0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Tasmania (UTAS) 1m Telescope at Mount Canopus is an optical telescope located in Australia with a 1.0-meter aperture, primarily used for astronomical research and observations.
8487ba74-bad0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.0m Optical Telescope at Mount Canopus Observatory, Australia

84a5689e-bb75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition**:
ESA-GEOS 2 (European Space Agency - Geostationary Orbit Scientific Satellite 2) was a spacecraft dedicated to scientific measurements in an equatorial geostationary orbit. It served as a core reference for the International Magnetospheric Study (IMS), carrying instruments to measure electric and magnetic fields, plasma, and energetic particles.
84a5689e-bb75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: European Space Agency GEOS 2 part of International Magnetospheric Study

84a77334-b8d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bocholt Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bocholt, Germany, known for its ground-based observations and research activities. It is situated at 7 Holtwicker Straße and plays a crucial role in the field of astronomy within Europe.
84a77334-b8d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bocholt Observatory, Germany

84b59f1e-babe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **SATINO Remote Observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Saint-Michel-l'Observatoire, France. It operates as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
84b59f1e-babe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Haute-Provence Observatory, France

84b8aab6-b851-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 0.45m Astrograph for the Southern Hemisphere is a telescope located at the El Leoncito Astronomical Complex (CASLEO) in South America, designed for optical observations.
84b8aab6-b851-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.45m optical Astrograph for the Southern Hemisphere at El Leoncito Astronomical Complex

84b958b4-b8b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Russian Arctic and Antarctic Magnetometer (RAM) network, established on March 3, 1920, is a ground-based observatory system operated by the Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute to monitor magnetic field variations in polar regions. It includes facilities like the IUGONET Observatory and contributes data to the World Data Center in Kyoto.
84b958b4-b8b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Arctic and Antarctic Research Institute

84c4be36-b6a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, particularly Earth's magnetic field. The Kandalaksha Magnetometer, located at the IAGA-identified station KND, has been operational since January 1933 as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
84c4be36-b6a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kandalaksha Observatory

84c682e8-b7fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Deep Space 1 (DS1) was a NASA technology demonstration spacecraft that flew by an asteroid and a comet as part of the New Millennium Program. It was designed to validate advanced technologies for future space missions while also conducting scientific observations.
84c682e8-b7fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep Space 1 part of New Millennium Program

84c804bc-b6a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Kwasan Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at Kyoto University in Japan, founded in 1929.
84c804bc-b6a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kwasan Observatory

84ca1158-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Isachsen station with the IAGA identifier ISC, used for geomagnetic field measurements. It is part of the IUGONET Observatory under the World Data Centers in Kyoto and the International Service of Geomagnetic Indices (ISC).
84ca1158-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Isachsen Observatory

84d1f192-b97d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sanae Geomagnetic Observatory** was a ground-based facility located on Earth's surface, specifically at coordinates 357.59° longitude and -70.312° latitude, operational from January 1, 1961, to December 31, 1989, primarily known for its geomagnetic measurements including those using a magnetometer instrument.
84d1f192-b97d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sanae Geomagnetic Observatory

84dd9e6c-b85f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the IRT observatory in Irkutsk is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, particularly the Earth's magnetic field.
84dd9e6c-b85f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Irkutsk Observatory

84eb7aba-b5e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Casal Lumbroso Observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Rome, Italy. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is situated at Via Carlo Tincani, Massimina, Castel di Guido.
84eb7aba-b5e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Casal Lumbroso Observatory, Italy

84edfd5e-ba24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The STA-1600, 10.5x10.5k CCD is a high-resolution imaging sensor developed by the University of Arizona's Imaging Technology Laboratories, featuring a monolithic array with 10560x10560 pixels, each measuring 9 µm.
84edfd5e-ba24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: STA-1600, 10.5x10.5k CCD

84eed42c-bbb4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CMF astronomical observatory, also known as Polo Astronómico CMF, is a ground-based observatory located in Foz do Iguaçu, Paraná, Brazil. It is situated at the Parque Tecnológico Itaipu and operates under MPC_ID X57.
84eed42c-bbb4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Foz do Iguaçu, Brazil

84f79778-b732-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISEE Muon Telescope is a multi-directional cosmic-ray muon detector constructed in Sakashita, Gifu prefecture, Japan, as part of the International Magnetospheric Study (IMS) program from 1975 to 1977.
84f79778-b732-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Muon Telescope part of International Magnetospheric Study, Japan

84fc712c-baf6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) all-sky imager at Nain, Canada is a multi-wavelength instrument developed by Nagoya University to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions.
84fc712c-baf6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Multi-wavelength All-Sky Imager part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Nain Observatory

8503cb36-b801-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
HIBOU (Highly Intelligent Bouncing Observation Unit) is a small rover, specifically Rover-1a, part of the MINERVA-II1 system onboard the Hayabusa2 spacecraft, designed to explore asteroid Ryugu by hopping autonomously due to its internal swing-arm mechanism. It is equipped with various sensors and cameras for data collection.
8503cb36-b801-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Highly Intelligent Bouncing Observation Unit on MINERVA-II1 part of Hayabusa2

850b30e6-b861-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Extreme Ultraviolet Imager (EUVI) is an instrument aboard NASA's STEREO-A spacecraft designed to observe coronal mass ejections and solar activity by measuring specific emission lines in the extreme ultraviolet range.
850b30e6-b861-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Extreme Ultraviolet Imager part of Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigations instrument suite on NASA Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory-A Mission

85100d86-b6af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Loparskoe ground station that measures the Earth's magnetic field. It is part of the IUGONET Observatory and WDC Kyoto's network for monitoring geomagnetic activity.
85100d86-b6af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Loparskoe Observatory

851652e4-b5ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: Neufahrwasser was a ground-based observatory in Gdansk, Poland, operational from 1891 to 1903, equipped with magnetometers for geomagnetic measurements.
851652e4-b5ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Neufahrwasser Observatory, Poland

852a76ec-b945-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Picard Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in St. Veit im Mühlkreis, Upper Austria, known for its ground-based observations and contributions to astronomy.
852a76ec-b945-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: St. Veit Observatory, Austria

852f88fc-b784-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition**:
Alger Island is a ground-based observatory located in the Primorsky District, Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia. It has been operational since 1905 and includes a magnetometer as part of its facilities.
852f88fc-b784-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Alger Island Observatory, Russia

853b9726-bb1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SuperDARN King Salmon HF radar is an observation site located at King Salmon Airport, Alaska, part of the Super Dual Auroral Radar Network (SuperDARN).
853b9726-bb1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: King Salmon High Frequency Radar at King Salmon Observatory, United States

8542777c-bb77-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DEMETER micro-satellite was a French spacecraft launched in 2004 to study ionospheric disturbances related to seismic and volcanic activity, as well as human-induced electromagnetic changes.
8542777c-bb77-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Detection of ElectroMagnetic Emissions Transmitted from Earthquake Regions part of DEMETER Mission

8544ce4c-b8f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The RAPID (Research with Adaptive Particle Image Detectors) instrument on the Cluster-1 spacecraft is a sophisticated particle detector designed to analyze suprathermal plasma distributions. It measures particles in specific energy ranges for electrons, hydrogen, and heavier ions using two sub-instruments: the Imaging Ion Mass Spectrometer (IIMS) and the Imaging Electron Spectrometer (IES).
8544ce4c-b8f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors part of Cluster-1

85473f3c-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Le Couvent de Lentin Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Lédergues, France. It serves as a ground-based observatory for studying celestial phenomena from Earth's surface.
85473f3c-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Le Couvent de Lentin Observatory, France

8547a87c-bb05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **SpectralPowerReceiver, LOFAR FR606 LBA**: A low-frequency radio telescope receiver operating in the 10 to 80 MHz range, part of the LOFAR interferometer network, used for various astronomical observations and studies.
8547a87c-bb05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spectral Power Receiver on Nançay LOFAR Station, France

8548f0c4-b6cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2Y Engineering Data Interface** is a component of the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) mission. It performs analog to digital conversion of key temperatures, voltages, and currents, featuring multiple inputs for voltage, current, and temperature sensors with high precision scaling and conversion capabilities.
8548f0c4-b6cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

85522ae8-bb34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Prescott Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Prescott, Arizona, known for its contributions to the discovery of minor planets.
85522ae8-bb34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Prescott Observatory

8554d158-b74c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1H Optical Photometer** is an instrument designed to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm during relativistic electron precipitation events, aiming to determine the presence of protons accompanying these electrons and support the theory of scattering by electromagnetic ion cyclotron waves as the precipitation mechanism.
8554d158-b74c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible Light Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

855a8ade-b991-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The STEREO-A SECCHI is a suite of remote sensing instruments on the STEREO-A spacecraft designed to observe coronal mass ejections (CMEs) from the Sun, tracking their journey towards Earth and studying their potential impacts on Earth's magnetosphere and ionosphere. It includes coronagraphs, an extreme ultraviolet imager, and heliospheric imagers to capture various aspects of solar activity.
855a8ade-b991-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation part of Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory A

8568ec62-bb46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DSS-45 is a ground-based observatory, part of the Deep Space Network (DSN), used for tracking and communicating with spacecraft in deep space missions.
8568ec62-bb46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: DSS-45

8576b2b6-b7b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **NAOJ Solar Flare Telescope (SFT)/T2** is an imaging spectrometer used to obtain full-Stokes maps of the Sun, specifically focusing on the magnetic field information at various heights from the photosphere to the chromosphere. It operates in the infrared spectrum, particularly in the lines of He-I 10830, Si-I 10827, and Fe-I 15648.
8576b2b6-b7b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Solar Flare Telescope and Full-Disk Infrared Full-Stokes Spectro-Polarimeter part of National Astronomical Observatory of Japan

857d22f2-b710-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Tasmania (UTAS) 0.4m (16-inch) Telescope at Mount Canopus is an optical telescope located in Australia, operated by the University of Tasmania and situated on Mount Canopus in Oceania.
857d22f2-b710-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 0.4m Telescope at Mount Canopus Observatory, Australia
