857ef7fa-ba5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Spectromagnetograph at Kitt Peak National Observatory** (KPNO) was an instrument operational from 1992 to 2002 that measured various solar parameters, including magnetic field strength and Doppler shifts in specific spectral lines.
857ef7fa-ba5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetograph at Kitt Peak Observatory

858b7ec6-b6b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Worthington Geophysical Observatory, located in Worthington Township, Minnesota, is a ground-based facility dedicated to geophysical research and measurements. It includes instruments such as the Worthington Magnetometer for monitoring Earth's magnetic field.
858b7ec6-b6b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Worthington Geophysical Observatory, United States

858ea07e-b9ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Global Geospace Science (GGS) Wind Satellite Mission is a space-based observatory designed to study high-energy phenomena, focusing on gamma rays and the observation of neutrinos, particles, and gravitational waves.
858ea07e-b9ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma-ray NASA Global Geospace Science Wind Satellite Mission

85969db8-b7a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Desert Moon Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Las Cruces, New Mexico, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects.
85969db8-b7a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Desert Moon Observatory, United States

85a95c46-bbbb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nyenheim Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Culemborg, Gelderland, Netherlands. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
85a95c46-bbbb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nyenheim Observatory, Netherlands

85b26d58-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Grosshabersdorf Observatory (code: A34) is an astronomical observatory located in Aurachtal, Bavaria, Germany. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center with MPC_ID A34 and operates as a ground-based facility.
85b26d58-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Grosshabersdorf Observatory, Germany

85b62688-bb20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 16 is an instrument designed to measure the space environment magnetic field, crucial for monitoring charged particle dynamics in the outer magnetosphere and providing alerts for geomagnetic activity. It is a key component of NOAA's Space Weather Operations, essential for satellite operators and power utilities.
85b62688-bb20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 16

85bcc4cc-bbbe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The IMP 4 Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer was an instrument onboard the Interplanetary Monitoring Platform (IMP) 4 spacecraft, designed to measure magnetic fields in space with high precision and multiple ranges. It operated from May 1967 to February 1969, providing valuable data despite a late malfunction in the spacecraft's optical aspect system.
85bcc4cc-bbbe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Interplanetary Monitoring Platform 4

85be9c1c-b721-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The COSMO K-Coronagraph (K-Cor) at Mauna Loa Solar Observatory (MLSO) is a ground-based instrument designed to study coronal mass ejections and the density structure of the low solar corona by recording polarization brightness.
85be9c1c-b721-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 20 cm Coronograph on Mauna Loa Solar Observatory, Hawaii

85beba1c-b7ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Navigation Camera (NavCam) was a crucial component of the Rosetta Orbiter's Attitude and Orbital Control System, consisting of two identical CCD cameras to ensure redundancy. It provided imaging capabilities, autonomous star-field acquisition and tracking, and supported autonomous navigation for the orbiter.
85beba1c-b7ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Navigation Camera on Rosetta Orbiter

85c80688-b61a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the Digisonde ionospheric station located in Beijing, China (URSI-code: BP440), which is an advanced ground facility used to study the ionosphere by analyzing skywave signals reflected from it.
85c80688-b61a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Beijing Observatory, China

85ca3a34-bac5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: Apollo 11 was the historic NASA mission that successfully landed astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon on July 20, 1969, while Michael Collins orbited overhead in the Command Module, culminating in the first human moonwalk.
85ca3a34-bac5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Module part of Apollo 11 Mission

85caa950-b83c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
JANUS is a spacecraft equipped with the instruments Balt and Janus_B.
85caa950-b83c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: JANUS and JNSB

85d1626c-b9ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The TWINS2 Lyman-alpha Detector (LAD) is an instrument on the TWINS observatory designed to measure Lyman-alpha radiation emitted by neutral hydrogen atoms, featuring two sensors with a 4° field of view and providing full azimuthal coverage.
85d1626c-b9ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lyman-alpha Detector on Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometer

85d66f94-b8ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Hormersdorf Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Hormersdorf, Bavaria, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
85d66f94-b8ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hormersdorf Observatory, Germany

85e1af88-b8cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1H magnetometer, specifically the TCM2-20 Axis model by PNI Sensor Corporation, is a three-axis instrument designed to measure magnetic field components with high resolution. It is used on balloons to detect substorm activity and ULF oscillations, which are crucial for studying the modulation of electron precipitation in space.
85e1af88-b8cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

85e409be-b773-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/F16 SESS Special Sensor Magnetometer-Boom (SSM-Boom) is a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer launched in 2003 as part of the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program, designed to measure geomagnetic fluctuations associated with geophysical phenomena.
85e409be-b773-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Magnetometer-Boom on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

85e4bffe-b934-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Magellan Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located near Goulburn in New South Wales, Australia. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
85e4bffe-b934-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magellan Observatory

85efbfa0-b7d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Polar Plasma Waves Investigation (PWI) is an instrument on the POLAR spacecraft designed to measure electromagnetic and electrostatic plasma waves along its trajectory, capable of capturing waveforms for six fields simultaneously. It operated from March 25, 1996, until it encountered a power supply issue on September 16, 1997.
85efbfa0-b7d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver part of Plasma Waves Investigation on Polar

85f30084-b720-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Everstar Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Olathe, Kansas, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility for celestial observations.
85f30084-b720-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Everstar Observatory

85f5b27c-ba02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Val-des-Bois Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Val-des-Bois, Quebec, Canada. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
85f5b27c-ba02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Val-des-Bois Observatory, Canada

85f9d53c-bbb0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gwen Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in San Francesco al Campo, Italy. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation of celestial bodies and phenomena.
85f9d53c-bbb0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gwen Observatory

85faa4f0-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Union Observatory Annex is an astronomical observatory located in Madibeng Ward 29, Meerhof, South Africa. It is known by the label Johannesburg-Hartbeespoort and has the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID of 076.
85faa4f0-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Union Observatory Annex, South Africa

8608de82-b7bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EISCAT observation site at Bjørnøya, Norway is a ground-based facility dedicated to atmospheric research, featuring a meteor radar and located in Svalbard.
8608de82-b7bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Meteor Radar at EISCAT Bjornoya Station, Norway

860e37d6-b5e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DSS-15 34-m Radio Telescope was a fully steerable, dual-shaped reflector antenna part of NASA's Deep Space Network at the Goldstone Complex near Barstow, California. It operated from the mid-1980s until its decommissioning in May 2018, capable of receiving signals between 2.0-8.6 GHz and transmitting up to 250 W at 2.1 GHz or 20 kW at 7.1 GHz.
860e37d6-b5e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Radio Telescope part of Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex, United States

8619f7f6-bbb8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Southern Astrophysical Research (SOAR) Telescope is a 4.1-meter aperture telescope located on Cerro Pachón, Chile, designed for high-quality imaging across various wavelengths from the ultraviolet to near infrared.
8619f7f6-bbb8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 4.1m Southern Astrophysical Research Telescope at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory, Chile

861e3ac4-bb4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
A magnetometer at the Eilat observatory (ELT) is a scientific instrument used to measure magnetic fields, specifically as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network since 1998. It contributes data to global geomagnetic studies under the IUGONET Observatory and WDC Kyoto frameworks.
861e3ac4-bb4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eilat Observatory

8626bf3c-b694-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LFRTO (Low Frequency Radio Transmitter Observation) instrument is a standard radio signals receiver located at the Zao observatory in Miyagi, Japan, operated by Tohoku University. It measures amplitude and phase time series of standard radio signals at frequencies 40.0 kHz (JJY), 60.0 kHz (JJY), and 67.5 kHz (BPC).
8626bf3c-b694-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low Frequency Radio Transmitter Observation part of IUGONET Observatory

8629ea12-bb36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Baffin Island Observatory was a ground-based facility located in the Qikiqtaaluk Region, Nunavut, Canada, operational from 1921 to 1922, primarily used for magnetometer observations.
8629ea12-bb36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Baffin Island Observatory, Canada

862f2246-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **IMAGE (International Monitor for Auroral Geomagnetic Effects)** is a network of 41 magnetometer stations across Northern Europe, dedicated to studying auroral electrojets and moving two-dimensional current systems, contributing to high-latitude magnetospheric-ionospheric physics research.
862f2246-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: International Monitor for Auroral Geomagnetic Effects

8630a432-b795-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Observatory Robert A. Naef** is an astronomical observatory located in Épendes, Canton of Fribourg, Switzerland. Established on May 19, 1984, it is situated at coordinates 7.13938 degrees east and 46.76236 degrees north, with an altitude of 680 meters above sea level.
8630a432-b795-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatory Robert A. Naef at Épendes Observatory, Switzerland

8640a1a4-bb99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ohio State University Observatory (H57) is an astronomical observatory located in Bath Township, Allen County, Ohio, United States. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
8640a1a4-bb99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lima Observatory

86437004-b6ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gravitational Waves (Radio Science) (GWE) on Ulysses is an investigation designed to detect low-frequency gravitational waves using Doppler tracking of the Ulysses spacecraft, leveraging its interplanetary trajectory for optimal sensitivity in the mHz frequency band.
86437004-b6ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gravitational Wave Experiment for Ulysses part of Ulysses

86467616-b873-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Two-Meter Twin Telescope (TTT1)**, also known as the Teide Observatory, is a ground-based astronomical observatory located at TF-514, Güímar, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain. It is situated at coordinates 28.29873° N latitude and 343.49042° E longitude on the continent of Europe.
86467616-b873-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2m Twin Telescope at Teide Observatory, Spain

8650aff2-ba4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 2 FIELDS Suite, Fluxgate Magnetometer (FGM) is an instrument on the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS) that measures magnetic fields and current structures in space using both Analog and Digital Fluxgate magnetometers. It is part of the FIELDS suite and has been operational since March 13, 2015.
8650aff2-ba4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MMS 2 FIELDS Suite

86552382-b7c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA 0.9m Gerard P. Kuiper Airborne Observatory (KAO) was an infrared telescope with a 0.9-meter aperture, designed to conduct astronomical observations from high altitudes aboard an aircraft.
86552382-b7c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared NASA 0.9m Gerard P. Kuiper Airborne Observatory

865597ae-bc83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Nyrölä Observatory is an amateur astronomical observatory located in the countryside village of Nyrölä near Jyväskylä, Finland, owned and operated by the astronomical association Jyväskylän Sirius ry.
865597ae-bc83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nyrölä Observatory, Finland

8661015e-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mariner 7 Spacecraft Wide Angle Camera (WAC) was an instrument on the Mariner 7 spacecraft featuring Zeiss refractor optics and a vidicon detector, designed to capture detailed images of Mars with spectral filters for color imaging.
8661015e-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide Angle Camera on Mariner 7 Spacecraft

8667ca60-ba16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the White-water Fiber Scintillation Telescope (WFST) located at the Lenghu ground observatory in Qinghai, China. It is situated at approximately 38.6076° N latitude and 93.89522° E longitude.
8667ca60-ba16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide Field Survey Telescope at Saishiteng Observatory, China

866963ae-b870-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Altenburg Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Altenburg, Thuringia, Germany. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical observations and research.
866963ae-b870-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Altenburg Observatory, Germany

86708da4-ba83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Munhoz Observatory, located in Munhoz, Minas Gerais, Brazil, is a ground-based astronomical facility situated at approximately latitude -22.62891 and longitude 313.6047 in South America.
86708da4-ba83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Munhoz Observatory, Brazil

8684d304-b76d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The WIYN Consortium 3.5m Wisconsin-Indiana-Yale-NOIRLab (WIYN) Telescope is an optical telescope with a 3.5-meter aperture located at the Kitt Peak National Observatory in North America. It is operated by a consortium including the University of Wisconsin, Indiana University, Yale University, and NOIRLab.
8684d304-b76d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 3.5m Wisconsin-Indiana-Yale-NOIRLab Telescope at NSF Kitt Peak National Observatory

868c5fa0-bb70-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Russian Academy of Sciences 576m Radio Telescope, also known as RATAN-600, is a large radio telescope located in Russia that operates within the radio waveband and is primarily used for solar observations. It is part of the Special Astrophysical Observatory in Asia.
868c5fa0-bb70-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio Russian Academy of Sciences 576m Radio Telescope at Special Astrophysical Observatory

86a11618-b7f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: AVON is an antenna located in Pontianak, Indonesia, designed to receive Very Low Frequency (VLF) magnetic signals originating from lightning discharges. It measures the North-South and East-West components of these signals as part of the IUGONET Observatory network managed by Tohoku University's radio observatory.
86a11618-b7f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VLF Antenna part of AVON

86a41072-ba04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Express Orbiter (MEX) Observatoire Minéralogie, Eau, Glaces, et Activité (OMEGA) is a dual-channel mapping spectrometer aboard the Mars Express spacecraft designed to analyze the mineralogy and water content of Mars by capturing visible and infrared spectral data.
86a41072-ba04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible and Infrared Mars Express Orbiter Observatoire Mineralogie, Eau, Glaces, Activite on Mars Express

86aed69e-bb83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Magnetometers at Enköping (ENK)" is a magnetometer instrument located in Enköping and operated as part of the IAGA investigation from 1965 to 1980.
86aed69e-bb83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Enköping Observatory

86af6292-b8b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Wind Analyser - Heavy Ion Sensor (SWA-HIS) is an instrument developed by the Southwest Research Institute that determines the charge states of oxygen and iron, maps the three-dimensional velocity distribution of minor species, and measures pick-up ions from various origins. It is part of the Solar Orbiter mission and operates while pointing towards the sun.
86af6292-b8b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heavy Ion Sensor part of Solar Wind Analyser

86b2d468-b978-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The OAVdA is a 1-meter telescope situated at the Osservatorio Astronomico della Regione Autonoma Valle d'Aosta in Lignan, Italy. It is used for astronomical observations and is located at an altitude of 1600 meters above sea level.
86b2d468-b978-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1m Telescope at Osservatorio Astronomico della Valle d'Aosta, Italy

86b6f1c4-b932-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Cielos de Banfield is a ground-based observatory located in Banfield, Partido de Lomas de Zamora, Buenos Aires, Argentina. It serves as an astronomical facility for observations and research.
86b6f1c4-b932-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cielos de Banfield Observatory, Argentina

86bff862-b803-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: THEMIS C Spacecraft Modes refers to the operational states of the THEMIS C spacecraft, which include slow survey, fast survey, particle burst, and wave burst modes. These modes dictate how data is collected and processed during different phases of its mission.
86bff862-b803-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: THEMIS C spacecraft modes part of Cluster

86cc249c-bb7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Augsburg College Search Coil Ground Observatory Group** is a network of ground-based observatories located in Antarctica, equipped with search coil magnetometers from Augsburg College. This group includes stations operated by the British Antarctic Survey and other locations like Halley Bay and the South Pole.
86cc249c-bb7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Magnetometer at British Antarctic Survey A80, Antarctica

86d0118c-ba0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Tixie Bay Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Tiksi, Sakha Republic, Russia, established in 1957 to monitor and study geomagnetic activities.
86d0118c-ba0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tixie Bay Magnetic Observatory

86d0507e-b5db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Bosscha Observatory is Indonesia's oldest modern observatory and one of Asia's earliest, situated in Lembang, West Java.
86d0507e-b5db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bosscha Observatory, Indonesia

86d97408-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer on Pioneer 10 designed to measure magnetic fields in space, capable of detecting ranges from ±2.5 nT to ±10 gauss with high linearity and accuracy, operational until November 1975.
86d97408-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Pioneer 10

86dcf238-b7e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **TRAPPIST-North Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in Oukaïmeden, Morocco, dedicated to ground-based observations and part of the TRAPPIST (Transiting Planets and Planetesimals Small Telescope) project.
86dcf238-b7e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: TRAPPIST-North Observatory at Oukaïmeden, Morocco

86f0024a-ba84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Shatsk Geomagnetic Observatory (SHT):** A ground-based facility located in Russia, operational from 1957 to 1960, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements as part of the IAGA observatory network.
86f0024a-ba84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Shatsk Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

86f36490-b5e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Nariño Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Pasto, Colombia. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
86f36490-b5e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pasto Observatory, Colombia

86f51dd2-b6e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Tasmania 1.27m Harlingten Telescope (H127) is an optical telescope located at Greenhill Observatory in Australia, operated by the University of Tasmania.
86f51dd2-b6e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.27m Harlingten Telescope at Greenhill Observatory, Australia

87052aa0-b703-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Bomem DA 3.02 FT-IR Spectrometer** is a Fourier Transform Infrared (FT-IR) spectrometer developed by Bomem Inc., designed for accurate spectral analysis within the infrared range.
87052aa0-b703-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Bomem DA 3.02 Fourier Transform Infrared Spectrometer

871366b2-b666-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Insight-HXMT is a telescope operated by the China National Space Administration (CNSA) and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, designed to observe high-energy astrophysical phenomena in the X-ray waveband.
871366b2-b666-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray China National Space Administration and the Chinese Academy of Sciences Hard X-ray Modulation Telescope

8713d3fe-b6c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMN fluxgate magnetometer at PRM is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument located in Presidente Medici, Brazil, and it is part of the Equatorial Magnetometer Network (IUGONET) observatory.
8713d3fe-b6c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Equatorial Magnetometer Network

871d9b8a-b6f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Three-Axis Fluxgate Magnetometers on Prognoz 7 are instruments designed to measure vector magnetic fields ranging from 1 to 1,200 nT with an intensity resolution of 0.5 nT, capable of measuring both interplanetary and geomagnetic tail fields.
871d9b8a-b6f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Three-Axis Fluxgate Magnetometers on Prognoz 7

871dd2b2-ba50-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **THEMIS Ground Gakona All Sky Imager** is an instrument located in Gakona, Alaska, designed to monitor the auroral oval with a 170-degree field of view at kilometer resolution. It features a fisheye lens and CCD within a protective enclosure, capturing images typically every three seconds.
871dd2b2-ba50-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ground All Sky Imager at Gakona Observatory, Alaska

871f4184-b996-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Wisconsin, Madison Wisconsin H-Alpha Mapper (WHAM) is an optical telescope located in North America, designed for studying the distribution and dynamics of ionized gas in the interstellar medium through observations of the H-alpha spectral line.
871f4184-b996-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical Wisconsin H-Alpha Mapper

8724aea8-bc4d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Texas at San Antonio Kleberg Advanced Microscopy Center Bruker Quantax XFlash 4010 SSD Energy-Dispersive X-Ray Detector is an instrument used for chemical analysis via energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, attached to a Hitachi S5500 Field-Emission SEM. It enables elemental identification and quantification of both thin and bulk samples through interactive software processing.
8724aea8-bc4d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bruker Quantax XFlash 4010 SSD Energy-Dispersive X-Ray Detector at University of Texas at San Antonio Kleberg Advanced Microscopy Center

872500ee-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 16 lunar module (LM) spacecraft, also known as the APOLLO 16 LUNAR MODULE, was the fifth crewed vehicle to land on the Moon. It carried astronauts John W. Young and Charles M. Duke, Jr., along with scientific instruments and a Lunar Roving Vehicle for surface exploration during its mission in April 1972.
872500ee-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Apollo 16 Lunar Module on Apollo 16

872d1cfc-b9a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Santiago Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Providencia, Santiago Metropolitan Region, Chile, that operated from 1850 to 1909 and was part of the IAGA observatory network.
872d1cfc-b9a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Santiago Observatory, Chile

87307e78-bb5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Geotail Electric Field Detector (EFD)** is an instrument onboard the Geotail spacecraft designed to study electric field configurations and variations in different regions of Earth's magnetosphere. It consists of two orthogonal double probes with variable separation distances, capable of measuring electric fields and plasma density with high time resolution.
87307e78-bb5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Double Sphere part of Geotail

8734588a-b6cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The McGrath Magnetometer is an instrument used in the THEMIS Mission to measure magnetic fields, located at the McGrath Geophysical Observatory since 2005.
8734588a-b6cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at McGrath Geophysical Observatory

87363f9c-b806-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hartland Magnetic Observatory, located in Hartland, United Kingdom, is a ground-based facility dedicated to the continuous measurement of Earth's magnetic field.
87363f9c-b806-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hartland Magnetic Observatory, United Kingdom

87514694-b675-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Karrenkneul Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Ehrsten, Calden, Germany, identified by the Minor Planet Center code A45.
87514694-b675-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Karrenkneul Observatory, Germany

8752aab6-b88c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Dark Side Observatory in Weatherly is a ground-based astronomical facility located at 349 Wallace Way in Packer Township, Carbon County, Pennsylvania, United States. It operates at coordinates 40.89796° N and 284.10758° E.
8752aab6-b88c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dark Side Observatory at Weatherly, United States

875857ac-b604-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Lovö Observatory in Kyoto, operational from 1928 to 2004, used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of the IAGA investigation.
875857ac-b604-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy

87666376-b62a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Inge Lehmann Magnetometer** is a scientific instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field. It was operational from January 1, 1966, to December 31, 1967, and was part of the IAGA investigation at the Inge Lehmann observatory.
87666376-b62a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Inge Lehmann Observatory

876c418e-b656-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **SuperMAG:** A global collaboration of over 200 ground geomagnetic observatories, coordinated by Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory (JHU/APL), that standardizes and processes data for studying ionospheric and magnetospheric current systems.
876c418e-b656-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at SuperMAG

876d242c-b96d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) Monitor of All-sky X-ray Image (MAXI) is an experiment aboard the International Space Station that monitors and images X-rays from across the sky.
876d242c-b96d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: x-ray Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency Monitor of All-sky X-ray Image experiment part of International Space Station

878058cc-b93a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LANL1990 Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer (SOPA) is an instrument designed to measure the fluxes of energetic particles, including protons, electrons, and various ions, in synchronous orbit around Earth. It features three silicon detector telescopes with precise angular cutoffs and extensive shielding to ensure accurate particle detection across specific energy ranges.
878058cc-b93a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer part of Los Alamos National Laboratory 1990

8782e712-b927-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fast Plasma Investigation (FPI) on the MMS4 spacecraft consists of four dual electron spectrometers (DES) and four dual ion spectrometers (DIS), designed to measure the velocity-space distribution of electrons and ions within a specific energy range with high time resolution.
8782e712-b927-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Fast Plasma Investigation on MMS4

87886964-b79f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific magnetometer at the Fuquene ground station, part of the IAGA investigation, has been operational since January 1954 and is a component of the WDC Kyoto observatory network.
87886964-b79f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fuquene Observatory

8788d592-b9cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Phoenix mission was a NASA space exploration project that sent a lander to the northern plains of Mars to study its water history and assess local habitability. Launched on August 4, 2007, it operated from May 25, 2008, until November 2, 2008.
8788d592-b9cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Phoenix on National Aeronautics and Space Administration (United States)

878dde6c-b6a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Shizuoka Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Aoi Ward, Shizuoka, Japan. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
878dde6c-b6a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Shizuoka Observatory, Japan

87935894-b617-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Félix Aguilar Observatory (also known as El Leoncito) is an astronomical observatory located in San Juan Province, Argentina. Established in 1953 and later renamed the Carlos Ulrrico Cesco Astronomical Station in 1974, it is situated at an altitude of 2,348 meters on Earth.
87935894-b617-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Félix Aguilar Observatory, Argentina

8797bbc6-b68c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Infrared Telescope Facility (IRTF) is a 3.2-meter telescope located at Mauna Kea Observatories on the Big Island of Hawai'i, optimized for infrared observations and operated by the University of Hawai`i Institute for Astronomy for NASA.
8797bbc6-b68c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.2m Infrared Telescope at Maunakea Observatories, United States

879e077a-b6ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is the **Ionospheric Station at Wuhan, China (WU430)**, a ground-based observatory that uses advanced ionosondes to analyze skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere, providing data on angle of arrival, polarization, and Doppler frequency shift.
879e077a-b6ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Ionospheric Station in Wuhan, China

879f8908-b8e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Yerkes Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Williams Bay, Wisconsin, United States. It was established in 1897 and is notable for its historic significance and ongoing public tours and programming.
879f8908-b8e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yerkes Observatory

87a0c0c0-b9db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A spacecraft, as defined in this context, is a vehicle or device designed for travel or operation beyond Earth's atmosphere, often used for scientific exploration and observation missions by organizations like NASA.
87a0c0c0-b9db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: James Webb Telescope

87b1b06a-bb16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DSS-14 X-band Goldstone Solar System Radar Receiver is a cryogenically-cooled, dual-channel HEMT low noise amplifier designed to receive radio signals at 8560 MHz or 3.5 cm wavelength for solar system observations.
87b1b06a-bb16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-band Goldstone Solar System Radar Receiver on Deep Space Station 14, United States

87c1e50e-b8ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Maiaky Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Ukraine, known for its ground-based observations. It has been operational since January 1957 and is situated at an altitude of 27 meters above sea level.
87c1e50e-b8ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Maiaky Observatory, Ukraine

87cc4370-b6f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The meteor wind radar at the Kototabang observatory in Indonesia is a VHF radar system designed to measure wind velocities by tracking the drift of ionized meteor trails in the upper atmosphere, providing valuable data on atmospheric dynamics.
87cc4370-b6f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar part of Coupling Processes in the Equatorial Atmosphere at Kototabang Observatory

87cd0572-bb39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Okinawa, Japan (URSI-code: OK426) was a ground facility equipped with a Digisonde for advanced ionospheric measurements. It operated from December 31, 2001, to April 5, 2003, and was located in Ogimi, Kunigami, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan.
87cd0572-bb39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Okinawa Ionospheric Station, Japan

87ce7fa2-b7b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dudley Observatory is an astronomical education non-profit located in Loudonville, New York, and it is the oldest non-academic institution of astronomical research in America. It was formerly a working observatory with previous locations in Albany and Schenectady.
87ce7fa2-b7b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dudley Observatory

87d09864-b8cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The MAGDAS Fayum station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Faiyum, Egypt (29.17° N, 30.53° E), part of the international MAGDAS magnetometer network under IUGONET, designed to monitor and study geomagnetic field variations.
87d09864-b8cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Faiyum Observatory, Egypt

87d96130-bb72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Space Environment Monitor (SEM)** on NOAA 6 was an instrument designed to measure proton and electron fluxes, as well as their energy spectra in the upper atmosphere using three detector systems.
87d96130-bb72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Environment Monitor on NOAA 6

87e40e14-b66d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Puchenstuben Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Puchenstuben, Lower Austria. It is a ground-based facility situated at 10 Schulgasse, Buchberg, dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
87e40e14-b66d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Puchenstuben Observatory, Austria

87f3f5fc-ba07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EMN magnetometer network** at **Santa Maria, Brazil**, operated by the Universidade Federal de Santa Maria, is a ground-based facility that includes instruments like the ICSWSE EMN SMA fluxgate for measuring magnetic fields.
87f3f5fc-ba07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Santa Maria Observatory, Brazil

87f9365a-b9f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite (LCROSS) Near Infrared Camera 2 (NIR2) was an instrument on the LCROSS spacecraft designed to capture near-infrared imagery of lunar impacts, specifically to study the Centaur impact plume, monitor ejecta cloud morphology, and determine grain properties and water concentration maps.
87f9365a-b9f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Infrared Camera 2 on Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite

87fd6380-b7b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Observatory of Atmospheric Environment in the National Institute for Environmental Studies (NIES), located in Tsukuba, Japan, is a ground-based facility focused on atmospheric research, equipped with instruments such as a millimeter wave spectroscopic radiometer.
87fd6380-b7b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter Wave Spectroscopic Radiometer at Observatory of Atmospheric Environment in National Institute for Environmental Studies, Japan

87fe80e8-bb57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CLIO imager and spectrograph is an astronomical instrument that features a 256 x 320 array of InSb pixels for capturing images and low-resolution spectra in the near-infrared range, from approximately 2.5 to 4.5 microns.
87fe80e8-bb57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Clio Imager and Spectrograph on Single Mirror 6m5 Telescope

88077ac8-b5cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kamihoriguchi Observatory (code: 405) is an astronomical observatory located in Besshochō, Ota, Gunma Prefecture, Japan. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center with MPC ID 405 and operates as a ground-based facility.
88077ac8-b5cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kamihoriguchi Observatory, Japan

8815703a-b717-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute (PARI) is a non-profit astronomical observatory located in the Pisgah National Forest near Balsam Grove, North Carolina, operating radio and optical telescopes for research and educational purposes. It is affiliated with the University of North Carolina system through PARSEC.
8815703a-b717-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 26m Radio Telescope at Pisgah Astronomical Research Institute, United States

881998d6-b910-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GiaGa Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Pogliano Milanese, Italy. It has the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 203 and focuses on ground-based observations.
881998d6-b910-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GiaGa Observatory, Italy

881f07ee-b93d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Linceo Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Santander, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
881f07ee-b93d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Santander Observatory, Spain

88209266-b759-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Digital CCD Imagers on the Flare Monitoring Telescope (FMT) at Hida Observatory are specialized instruments designed to capture high-resolution images of the Sun's chromosphere, particularly for monitoring solar flares.
88209266-b759-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Digital Charge Coupled Device Imagers on Flare Monitoring Telescope at Kwasan and Hida Observatory

88268666-b615-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Gillam Canadian ground station operated from 1974 to 1976 as part of the IAGA investigation and the THEMIS Ground CANMAG Observatory.
88268666-b615-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Gillam

882a60da-b807-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Toyokawa Observatory is an astronomical ground observatory located in Toyokawa, Aichi Prefecture, Japan, dedicated to scientific research and observations of celestial bodies.
882a60da-b807-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Toyokawa Observatory, Japan

882b6c40-bba0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Keck Echelle Spectrograph and Imager (ESI) at Keck Observatory is a versatile instrument that operates in echelle, low-resolution, and direct imaging modes, offering high spectral resolution and various slit widths for detailed astronomical observations.
882b6c40-bba0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Echelle Spectrograph and Imager on 10m Keck II Telescope

8835af1e-b882-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astronomical Observatory of Kyiv University is an astronomical observatory located in Kyiv, Ukraine, operated by the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine since 1944.
8835af1e-b882-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory of Kyiv University, Ukraine

8837b9c6-b7ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Space Environment Monitor-2 (SEM-2) on NOAA 15 is an instrument designed to measure the Earth's radiation belts and charged particle precipitation in the upper atmosphere due to solar activity. It consists of two sensors—the Total Energy Detector (TED) and the Medium Energy Proton/Electron Detector (MEPED)—and a common Data Processing Unit (DPU).
8837b9c6-b7ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Environment Monitor-2 on NOAA 15

883b845a-b5c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Darwin Geomagnetic Observatory (DAR), situated in Darwin, Northern Territory, Australia, is a ground-based facility that has been monitoring geomagnetic activity since January 1957.
883b845a-b5c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Darwin Observatory, Australia

883f0644-bbd5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MASTER-OAGH Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Cananea, Sonora, Mexico. It is situated at coordinates 31.05603° N and 249.6181° W (equivalent to 109.6181° E).
883f0644-bbd5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: MASTER-OAGH Observatory, Mexico

884b00c2-bad9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Asuka Station Geomagnetic Observatory (ASK) is a ground-based facility located on Earth's surface at an altitude of 930 meters, which operated from January 1, 1987, to December 31, 1991, primarily for geomagnetic observations.
884b00c2-bad9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Asuka Station

8859d282-b796-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nedlands Observatory in Perth is a ground-based astronomical facility located at Bruce Street, Nedlands, Western Australia. It serves as an observational site for astronomy research and education.
8859d282-b796-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nedlands Observatory, Australia

885a7c24-bad3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **NASA WB-57 High-Altitude Research Program** is an airborne observatory that conducts optical observations of the Sun from high altitudes using specialized aircraft. It operates under NASA to gather data and support solar research initiatives.
885a7c24-bad3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical NASA WB-57 High-Altitude Research Program

885efc1a-b60d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Hopen Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, used for measuring magnetic fields since September 1, 2008.
885efc1a-b60d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hopen Geophysical Observatory

8888b442-bacc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Beloit Geophysical Observatory was a ground-based facility located in Mitchell County, Kansas, United States, which operated from July 1957 to December 31, 1959, primarily for geomagnetic measurements.
8888b442-bacc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Beloit Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

88a1315c-b6ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS) onboard the DMSP/F19 satellite is a microwave radiometer that provides multi-purpose imagery and temperature/humidity sounding channels for improved precipitation measurements across 21 frequencies and 24 channels.
88a1315c-b6ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program F19

88aa4888-bb0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hermanus (HER) Geomagnetic Observatory is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Hermanus, South Africa, operating since 1941 and funded by the South African National Space Agency.
88aa4888-bb0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hermanus Magnetic Observatory, South Africa

88ac31f0-b77b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Pioneer 11**: A NASA space probe launched in 1973 to explore Jupiter and Saturn, becoming the first to encounter Saturn and its rings. It carried various instruments for studying interplanetary and planetary magnetic fields, cosmic rays, and more, and contains a plaque depicting human figures and Earth's location.
88ac31f0-b77b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pioneer 11 part of CNES Observatory

88bf3f36-bab2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 17** is a scientific instrument designed to measure the magnetic field in space around Earth, providing crucial data for monitoring geomagnetic activity and ensuring safety for satellites and human spaceflight. It plays a vital role in NOAA's Space Weather Operations by detecting magnetic storms and validating large-scale space environment models.
88bf3f36-bab2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 17

88d2d4e0-bb13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kevo Geophysical Observatory (KEV) is a ground-based facility located in Utsjoki, Northern Lapland, Finland, specializing in geophysical measurements including magnetometry.
88d2d4e0-bb13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kevo Geophysical Observatory, Finland

88dc4522-b792-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) station at Darwin, Australia is a ground-based facility developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nighttime airglow emissions.
88dc4522-b792-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Darwin Observatory, Australia

88e73dfe-b7b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Osservatorio Aldebaran is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Rivalba, Corniglio, within the Parma province of Emilia-Romagna, Italy. It serves as a facility for conducting various astronomical observations and research.
88e73dfe-b7b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Aldebaran Observatory, Italy

88e97f86-b81d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Oslo Observatory, identified as "IAGA:OSL," is a ground-based scientific facility located in Oslo, Norway, which operated from 1843 to 1930 and was part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
88e97f86-b81d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Oslo Observatory, Norway

88e9ef14-b5f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Astronomical Research Westfield Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Westfield, Coles County, Illinois, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observation.
88e9ef14-b5f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Research Observatory

88edd84c-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Jovian Energetic Neutrals and Ions (JENI)** instrument is part of the Particle Environment Package (PEP) onboard the European Space Agency’s JUICE mission, designed to study neutral and charged particles within Jupiter's magnetosphere using six sensors.
88edd84c-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Jovian Energetic Neutrals and Ions part of Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer

88f59358-b650-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Large Angle Spectrometric Coronagraph (LASCO) is an instrument on the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO) satellite designed to observe the solar corona with a wide-field white light and spectrometric coronagraph consisting of three optical systems having nested fields of view.
88f59358-b650-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph on Solar and Heliospheric Observatory

8905cf3a-b85c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lompoc Geomagnetic Observatory (LOC)** is a ground-based facility in California dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity. It operates under the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) and contributes data to the World Data Center for Geomagnetism, Kyoto.
8905cf3a-b85c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lompoc Geomagnetic Observatory

89077e34-b6fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Glenlee Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in Glenlee, Queensland, Australia.
89077e34-b6fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Glenlee Observatory, Australia

890c2934-bb63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Grocka Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility in Serbia dedicated to monitoring and studying the Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since 1958 and is part of the global network of geomagnetic observatories.
890c2934-bb63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Grocka Geophysical Observatory, Serbia

8912823e-ba0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Karmoy Geophysical Observatory** is a ground-based facility located in Dyrland, Sandve, Karmøy, Rogaland, Norway. It operates at an altitude of 40 meters and includes a magnetometer as part of its instrumentation, primarily focusing on geophysical observations.
8912823e-ba0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geophysical Observatory at Karmoy, Norway

89173b46-b67a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
LUNAR-A was a planned Japanese space probe intended to study the Moon's interior structure and thermal properties using seismometers and heat flow devices on surface penetrators. The mission was cancelled in 2007 after multiple delays.
89173b46-b67a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar-A space probe

892a3ab2-b77d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Trivandrum Geomagnetic Observatory (TRD)** is a ground-based facility located in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India, which operated from 1957 to 1999 and was part of the IAGA observatories network.
892a3ab2-b77d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Trivandrum Geomagnetic Observatory, India

892f6ffc-b5f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Watec All-sky TV camera** is an automatic optical instrument featuring a white-light all-sky CCD camera used for observing auroral phenomena, operated at both Syowa Station in Antarctica and two stations in Iceland as part of the IUGONET Observatory.
892f6ffc-b5f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Watec All-sky TV Camera part of Syowa-Iceland Conjugate Observation of Auroral Phenomena

89392610-b5ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Space Environment Monitor (SEM)** on the GOES 13 spacecraft is a multi-instrument package designed to monitor solar activity and its effects on Earth's geomagnetic environment. It includes sensors for energetic particles, X-rays, magnetic fields, and extreme ultraviolet radiation.
89392610-b5ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Environment Monitor on GOES 13 spacecraft

893a7204-ba1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mount Canopus Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Hobart, Tasmania, Australia, known for housing the 1m0 telescope.
893a7204-ba1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1m Telescope at Mount Canopus Observatory, Australia

8949cac4-bbc1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The C/NOFS Planar Langmuir Probe (PLP) is a dual-disk instrument designed to measure plasma density and fluctuations in situ, providing both low time-resolution data for background ionosphere models and high time-resolution data for monitoring disturbance conditions and spacecraft surface potential.
8949cac4-bbc1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Planar Langmuir Probe on C/NOFS

894af2e4-b9d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1A Ephemeris is a virtual instrument providing trajectory positions in various coordinate systems, used to study the dynamics and losses of relativistic electrons. It is part of the broader BARREL observatory project associated with NASA's Radiation Belt Storm Probes (RBSP) mission.
894af2e4-b9d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

895068d2-b925-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astro Dolomites Observatory (K75) is an astronomical facility located in Santa Cristina Valgardena, Italy. It is a ground-based observatory primarily used for stargazing and educational purposes.
895068d2-b925-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astro Dolomites Observatory, Italy

895089d4-b97f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vatican Advanced Technology Telescope (VATT), also known as the Alice P. Lennon Telescope and its Thomas J. Bannan Astrophysics Facility, is a 1.83-meter Gregorian telescope located at Mount Graham International Observatory in Arizona, United States, used for optical and infrared observations.
895089d4-b97f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Alice P. Lennon Telescope and Thomas J. Bannan Astrophysics Facility at Mount Graham International Observatory, United States

895aeaaa-b899-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Measurement of Low-Energy Protons and Electrons** experiment used the LEPEDEA electrostatic analyzer on the IMP-H spacecraft to measure energy spectra of low-energy electrons and protons in geocentric ranges, studying magnetospheric phenomena such as geomagnetic storms and auroras.
895aeaaa-b899-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low Energy Proton and Electron Differential Energy Analyzer part of IMP-H

896b73ce-b647-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Retarding Potential Analyser/Drift Meter (RPA)** on the AE-C satellite is an instrument designed to measure vector ion drift velocities, ion concentration and temperature, spacecraft potential, and provide an ionospheric irregularity index. It features four planar sensor heads, with three used for general measurements and one specialized for ion-drift velocity assessments.
896b73ce-b647-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Retarding Potential Analyser and Drift Meter on AE-C

89a251c4-bb5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific magnetometers mentioned are part of the IUGONET observatory in Kyoto, Japan, located at the SLU station, and their information is accessible through the VO Paris-NS database.
89a251c4-bb5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sloutzk Observatory

89a29b8a-b8c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wide Field Imager (WFI)** is a heliospheric imager designed to capture wide-field images from 18 to 180 solar radii on the sky. It is part of NASA's PUNCH mission and utilizes advanced optics based on the Nagler eyepiece in reverse geometry to attenuate direct sunlight by over 16 orders of magnitude.
89a29b8a-b8c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide Field Imager part of PUNCH

89a42ca4-b742-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Tokyo-Asahikawa Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Takasu, Kamikawa County, Hokkaido Prefecture, Japan, known for its ground-based observations.
89a42ca4-b742-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tokyo-Asahikawa Observatory, Japan

89a68514-b970-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Langkawi station is a ground-based facility in Langkawi, Malaysia, that operates as part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network to monitor geomagnetic activity.
89a68514-b970-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Langkawi Observatory, Malaysia

89a81732-b838-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Interball Tail" spacecraft's ephemeris data provides the orbital and attitude information necessary for tracking its position and orientation in space. This dataset is part of the CNES Observatory CDPP Archive Interball-Tail collection, managed by the French Space Agency (CNES).
89a81732-b838-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft Position Instrument part of Interball Tail Mission

89af8d0e-b681-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2MASS 1.3m Telescope is a 1.3-meter telescope situated at the Fred L. Whipple Observatory in Arizona, known for its role in the Two Micron All Sky Survey (2MASS) project using an open-tube, equatorial fork-mount design with Cassegrain focus and articulated secondary mirror.
89af8d0e-b681-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.3m Two Micron All-Sky Survey Telescope at Fred L. Whipple Observatory, United States

89bed168-bb6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Frederick C. Gillett Gemini North Telescope is an 8.1-meter optical telescope located at the Mauna Kea Observatory in North America, operated by the Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy (AURA).
89bed168-bb6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 8.1m optical Frederick C. Gillett Gemini North Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatory

89c62270-b768-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Pula Observatory** was an astronomical observatory located in Pula, Croatia, operational from 1881 to 1922.
89c62270-b768-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pula Observatory, Croatia

89c7de2c-b811-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 16 Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP) is a suite of scientific instruments deployed on the moon during the Apollo 16 mission to conduct various experiments and gather data about the lunar environment.
89c7de2c-b811-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Surface Experiments Package part of Apollo 16

89d44ac6-b5c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes magnetometers located at the Las Acacias observatory, operational from 1964 to 1996, as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigations.
89d44ac6-b5c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy

89da3140-b734-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Akashina Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Azumino, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
89da3140-b734-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Akashina Observatory, Japan

89ecdf6e-b5f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Thermal Infrared Imager (TIR)** on the Hayabusa2 spacecraft is a bolometric imager designed to capture thermal images of asteroid Ryugu, providing insights into its thermophysical properties such as surface temperature and roughness.
89ecdf6e-b5f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: infrared Thermal Infrared Imager on Hayabusa2

89ee0134-bad6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer installed at the Norman Wells Observatory, part of the IUGONET network, used for measuring magnetic field variations and contributing data to the World Data Center in Kyoto.
89ee0134-bad6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers part of International Real-time Magnetic Observatory Network

89f4930c-b78c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to magnetometers located in Leadville (LDV) that were operational from January 1, 1957, to December 31, 1959, as part of the IAGA investigation at the WDC Kyoto observatory.
89f4930c-b78c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Leadville Observatory

89f744da-b6ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Torus Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Buckley, Pierce County, Washington, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility with the MPC (Minor Planet Center) ID 653.
89f744da-b6ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Torus Observatory, United States

8a1e76c0-b7c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes a fluxgate magnetometer located in Dalby, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network within the IUGONET observatory. This instrument measures magnetic field variations and is identified by its unique code and type classification.
8a1e76c0-b7c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of 210 Magnetic Meridian Magnetometer Network

8a210bda-bbb5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High Energy Telescope (HET) is an instrument within the COSPIN suite on the Ulysses spacecraft, designed to measure high-energy particles, specifically protons in the range of ~0.3-7 MeV and helium ions from 0.4-4 MeV/n. It was built by the National Research Council in Ottawa, Canada.
8a210bda-bbb5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument part of Ulysses

8a34409c-b97b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Hawkeye Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Durand, Illinois, known for its ground-based facilities used for sky observation.
8a34409c-b97b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hawkeye Observatory at Durand, United States

8a563e1a-b8a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Uecht Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Niedermuhlern, Canton of Bern, Switzerland.
8a563e1a-b8a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sternwarte Uecht Observatory, Switzerland

8a64b824-ba0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Scott Observatory (also known as Fitchburg Observatory) is an astronomical observatory located at 777 Scott Road in Fitchburg, Worcester County, Massachusetts. It is a ground-based facility with the MPC ID of 823.
8a64b824-ba0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scott Observatory, United States

8a6db5fe-bab4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Isachsen Geomagnetic Observatory (ISC), located in the Qikiqtaaluk Region of Nunavut, Canada, is a ground facility dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity on Earth's surface. It is part of the IAGA observatory network and sponsored by the U.S.A.
8a6db5fe-bab4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Isachsen Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

8a6f8baa-b897-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dededo Geophysical Observatory, located in Yigo Municipality, Guam, is a ground-based facility operated by the USGS that includes instruments such as magnetometers for geophysical monitoring.
8a6f8baa-b897-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dededo Geophysical Observatory, United States

8a884b20-bb5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Loiano's Virgil Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located at 20 Via Nazionale in Bologna, Emilia-Romagna, Italy. It serves as an observational site for celestial studies and research.
8a884b20-bb5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Virgil Observatory, Loiano, Italy

8a927782-bb9e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS-A Digital Fields Board Filter Bank is an instrument component that provides band-pass filtering for EFI and SCM spectra as well as E12HF peak and average values. It reduces computational and power demands compared to using FFT by employing a cascade of filters and decimation processes.
8a927782-bb9e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digital Fields Board and Filter Bank part of Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms mission

8aa8a136-b59c-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Greiner Research Observatory (MPC code H51) is an astronomical observatory located in Verona, Wisconsin, United States. It is primarily involved in astrometric observations of minor planets and comets.
8aa8a136-b59c-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Greiner Research Observatory, United States

8ab09f02-b6ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at DAV is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Davao, Philippines, used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of the MAGDAS observation network.
8ab09f02-b6ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System observation network

8ab5e8c0-b6a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Far Ultraviolet Imager (FUV) on the IMAGE satellite is a suite of instruments designed to capture ultraviolet images of Earth's aurora and geocoronal emissions, optimized for high photon collection efficiency and real-time data processing.
8ab5e8c0-b6a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Far Ultraviolet Imager on IMAGE

8ab7bd20-bac8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Orwell Park Observatory is an astronomical facility located at Orwell Park School in Nacton, Suffolk, England. It operates as a ground-based observatory dedicated to the study of celestial bodies and phenomena.
8ab7bd20-bac8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Orwell Park Observatory, United Kingdom

8abff3d8-b680-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SP-2 (Dust Particle Detector) on Vega 1 was an acoustic detector used to measure the mass of dust particles, with a range from 3x10^-13 to ~2x10^-6 g, divided into 16 logarithmically distributed channels.
8abff3d8-b680-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dust Particle Detector on Vega 1

8ac3b292-b960-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Madimbo, South Africa (URSI-code: MU12K) is a ground-based observatory equipped with an advanced ionosonde that measures various properties of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere to study its characteristics. It is located in Mutale Ward 12, Limpopo Province, and operates as part of the GIRO (Global Ionospheric Radio Observatory) network under ISWI (International Space Weather Initiative).
8ac3b292-b960-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Ionospheric Station at Madimbo, South Africa

8ac90a40-b5bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **SCATHA High Energy Particle Spectrometer (SC3)** is an instrument onboard the Spacecraft Charging At High Altitudes (SCATHA) mission that measures the fluxes, spectra, and pitch-angle distribution of energetic particles, particularly electrons in the range 47 to 10,000 keV, protons from 1 to 200 MeV, and alpha particles from 6 to 60 MeV.
8ac90a40-b5bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Energy Particle Spectrometer on Spacecraft Charging At High Altitudes

8ac928c8-b9e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 1 Fast Plasma Instrument (FPI) Suite, Dual Electron Spectrometer (DES), is a component of the Fast Plasma Investigation onboard the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS 1). It measures the velocity-space distribution of electrons from 10 eV to 30 keV with high time resolution.
8ac928c8-b9e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dual Electron Spectrometer part of MMS 1 Fast Plasma Investigation

8ad2c8f4-b695-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cosmic Dust (GRU/DUST) instrument on the Ulysses spacecraft is designed to study particulate matter in the heliosphere, measuring properties like mass, speed, and charge of individual dust particles to understand their interaction with other interplanetary phenomena.
8ad2c8f4-b695-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dust Detector part of Ulysses

8ad54e30-b1a4-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics (CfA) 1.5m Tillinghast Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in North America, with a 1.5m aperture.
8ad54e30-b1a4-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 1.5m Tillinghast Telescope at Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory

8ad86076-b86a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Siegen Observatory is an astronomical facility located at the University of Siegen in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is a ground-based observatory dedicated to studying celestial objects and phenomena.
8ad86076-b86a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Siegen Observatory, Germany

8ad94450-b9fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **AFOSC Polarimeter** is an astronomical instrument featuring a double Wollaston prism that splits light into four polarized beams, enabling the simultaneous determination of Stokes parameters I, Q, and U with minimal instrumental polarization.
8ad94450-b9fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Asiago Faint Object Spectrographic Camera Polarimeter on Copernico Telescope

8ae956c6-b809-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Golmud Geomagnetic Observatory (GLM) is a ground-based geophysical facility located in Kunlunlu Subdistrict, Golmud, China. It specializes in magnetic observations and is part of the IUGONET network, with an altitude of 2802 meters above sea level.
8ae956c6-b809-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Golmud Geomagnetic Observatory, China

8afb8916-b9aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operated in Palau from 1926 to 1941, part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network, used for measuring magnetic fields.
8afb8916-b9aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy Investigation

8b053e58-b5f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO) is an astronomical observatory situated in the Coquimbo Region of northern Chile, known for its principal telescopes including the 4 m Víctor M. Blanco Telescope and various other research facilities.
8b053e58-b5f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 4.0m Víctor M. Blanco Telescope at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory, Chile

8b0879fc-b64c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTIs) station at Kapusukasing, Canada is a ground-based observatory developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions, collaborating with Virginia Tech.
8b0879fc-b64c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Kapuskasing Station, Canada

8b0def12-bae4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Málaga Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Carranque, Cruz de Humilladero, Málaga, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
8b0def12-bae4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Málaga Observatory, Spain

8b1b6fb2-b69c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Redshed Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Kallham, Upper Austria. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
8b1b6fb2-b69c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Redshed Observatory

8b1c25da-b843-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1O X-Ray Instrument (XRI) is a scintillation detector used to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It operates within an energy range from 10 keV to 10 MeV, utilizing a NaI crystal scintillator and a photomultiplier tube for detection.
8b1c25da-b843-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

8b20a038-b645-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Roque de los Muchachos Observatory (ORM)** is an astronomical observatory located on the island of La Palma in the Canary Islands, Spain, operated by the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias. 8b244dbc-ba39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **David Dunlap Observatory (DDO)** is an astronomical observatory located in Richmond Hill, Ontario, Canada, known for its 74-inch reflector telescope, which was once the second-largest in the world and remains the largest in Canada.

8b7af640-bac9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Indian Institute of Geomagnetism (IIG) is a premier research institute in India focused on geomagnetism and related fields such as geophysics, atmospheric science, space physics, and plasma physics. 8b7feff4-b648-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IMP 8 Spacecraft Position refers to the ephemeris data detailing the location of the IMP 8 spacecraft in various coordinate systems. 8b861220-b9dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Moose Springs Observatory (V14)** is an astronomical observatory located in Timber Lakes, Utah, United States, known for its ground-based observations.

8b94a288-baed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Area 52 Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Howard County, Arkansas, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility for stargazing and celestial observations.

8baa4586-b7df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sternwarte Düsseldorf, also known as the Bilk Observatory, was a private observatory founded in 1843 by Johann Friedrich Benzenberg in Düsseldorf-Bilk and destroyed by bombing in 1943.

8bce02d2-b6db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pacific Sky Observatory (E04) is an astronomical observatory located in San Vicente, Saipan Municipality, Northern Mariana Islands. It operates as a ground-based facility with the MPC ID E04.

8bd0c444-ba38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Ramonville Saint Agne Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Toulouse, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
8bd0c444-ba38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ramonville Saint Agne Observatory, France

8bdf1c36-b6d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Kototabang, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network, used for measuring magnetic field variations.

8c03b720-b77a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ObservaSTYRium at Stainz bei Straden, Austria

8c08d1f0-bb90-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Jaluit Magnetometer** was an instrument located at the IAGA-identified station JAL, operational from January 1938 to December 1942, used for measuring magnetic fields.

8c2f55d8-b829-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Kotel'nyy, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) network under IUGONET Observatory, used for measuring magnetic field variations.

8c4d189e-b9a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cardiff Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Cardiff, Wales, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects.
8c4d189e-b9a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cardiff Observatory, United Kingdom

8c4f368a-b8df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Valmeca Observatory (also known as the Valmeca Observatory, Puimichel) is an astronomical observatory located in Puimichel, France. It is situated at coordinates 43.981430555556° N, 6.0361° E and has the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 184.

8c718762-b7ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity represents the Hallett geomagnetic observatory in Antarctica, operational from January 1957 to December 31, 1962, equipped with a ground-based magnetometer.
8c718762-b7ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hallett Observatory

8c7f563c-bb0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Schefferville Geophysical Observatory** is a ground-based facility located in Quebec, Canada, focused on geophysical measurements and part of the larger Autumn observatory network.
8c7f563c-bb0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Schefferville Geophysical Observatory, Canada

8c873608-bb18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Sakigake**, also known as MS-T5 and "Pioneer," was Japan's first interplanetary spacecraft, launched to study the solar wind plasma and observe Comet P/Halley from a distance. 8c873608-bb18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sakigake

8c89164a-b9b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Isle of Man Observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Foxdale on the Isle of Man, Europe. It is a ground-based observatory used for stargazing and astronomical research.
8c89164a-b9b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Isle of Man Observatory, Isle of Man

8c98d208-babb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nephelometer for Pioneer Venus Small Probe (North) was an instrument designed to measure the energy backscattered from cloud particles on Venus using a pulsed laser LED and photodiode detectors, providing insights into cloud structure and vertical extent along the probe's trajectory.

8ca84012-bbab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "EMN Yap Station" is a ground-based magnetometer network located in Garim, Gilmaan, Yap, Federated States of Micronesia. It includes a fluxgate instrument and operates as part of the EMN (Equatorial Magnetometer Network).

8cab1782-b6bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wobblesock Observatory** is an astronomical facility located at Coonabarabran Airport in New South Wales, Australia. It functions as a ground-based observatory dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
8cab1782-b6bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wobblesock Observatory, Australia

8cacf5d4-b995-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ponte Uso Observatory** (MPC code: L41) is an astronomical observatory located in Sogliano al Rubicone, Emilia-Romagna, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility for studying celestial bodies and phenomena.
8cacf5d4-b995-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ponte Uso Observatory, Italy

8cb0def2-b9b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Speranza Observatory** is a ground-based astronomical observatory located at 5, Speranza Avenue in the Kāpiti Coast District of Wellington, New Zealand. It functions as a facility for observing and studying celestial phenomena from its coordinates at approximately -40.76181 latitude and 175.16936 longitude.

**Definition:**
The **Table Mountain Observatory, Wrightwood-PHMC**, located in Big Pines, Los Angeles County, California, is a ground-based observatory situated at coordinates 34.38182° N, 242.31841° E (approximately 117.68159° W), used for astronomical observations and research.
8cb5580a-b92c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Table Mountain Observatory

8cc1a1de-b83f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Begues Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Begues, Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 170 and operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
8cc1a1de-b83f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Begues Observatory, Spain

8cc37694-b79a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The BARREL Balloon 2N Tilt Compensated Magnetometer (TCM2) is an instrument carried by the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses mission to measure magnetic field components with a resolution of 10 nT, helping identify substorm activity and ULF oscillations. It features three orthogonal magneto-inductive sensors and provides pitch and roll information.
8cc37694-b79a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

8cd11aae-bb02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Muxagata Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Muxagata, Portugal, known for its ground-based observations.
8cd11aae-bb02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Muxagata Observatory, Portugal

8cd34d94-b6ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Hackney Wick 1 was a ground-based observatory located in London, England, operational from 1813 to 1815, equipped with a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements.
8cd34d94-b6ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hackney Wick Observatory, United Kingdom

8cd5bb7a-bb40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nobeyama Radioheliograph (NoRH) is a radio telescope specifically designed for solar observations, featuring 84 parabolic antennas arranged in east-west and north-south directions to capture detailed images of the Sun at frequencies of 17GHz and 34GHz.
