929b4374-b99a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The ROSA Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Verclause, France, dedicated to ground-based observations.
929b4374-b99a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Verclause Observatory, France

929e08ae-b6e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cloud Imaging and Particle Size Experiment (CIPS)** is a UV panoramic imager on the AIM spacecraft that uses intensified CCD cameras to image Polar Mesospheric Clouds, providing detailed data on their distribution, morphology, and particle sizes.
929e08ae-b6e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Cloud Imaging and Particle Size Experiment on Aeronomy of Ice in the Mesosphere

92a52f48-b7fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Operational Linescan System (OLS)** onboard the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program's S20 satellite is an imager that captures visible and infrared wavelengths to provide global cloud cover imagery at varying resolutions.
92a52f48-b7fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Operational Linescan System part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

92a9324a-b779-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The International Ultraviolet Explorer (IUE) was a collaborative space mission between NASA, ESA, and the UK's SERC, launched in 1978 to observe ultraviolet spectra of astronomical sources. It operated successfully until its termination in 1996.
92a9324a-b779-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet International Ultraviolet Explorer part of NASA/European Space Agency (ESA)/Science and Engineering Research Council (SERC) International Ultraviolet Explorer (IUE) Satellite Mission

92b70836-b7bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Paramaribo that operated from 1957 to 1974 as part of the IAGA investigation, measuring ground magnetic field data.
92b70836-b7bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Paramaribo Observatory

92b893d4-b91d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Canberra Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility in Australia that monitors magnetic fields and geophysical data. It operates under the funding of Geoscience Australia and has been active since 1979.
92b893d4-b91d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Canberra Magnetic Observatory, Australia

92c3f130-b9e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Deep Space Station 34 (DSS-34) is a 34-meter radio telescope located at the Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex in Australia, designed with a beam waveguide system to transmit and receive signals for deep space communication.
92c3f130-b9e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Radio Telescope at Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex, Australia

92c7b712-bb32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Calarreona Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Águilas, Murcia, Spain. It is a ground-based observatory used for stargazing and astronomical research.
92c7b712-bb32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Calarreona Observatory, Spain

92c8f6ae-b7cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) station at Sata, Japan, is a ground-based facility developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research at Nagoya University to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions. It is located in Minamiosumi, Japan, with coordinates 31.0 degrees latitude and 130.7 degrees longitude.
92c8f6ae-b7cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at ISEE Observatory, Japan

92d3ce9a-bae1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electron Temperature Probe (OETP) on the Pioneer Venus Orbiter is an instrument designed to measure electron temperature and plasma density in Venus' ionosphere using cylindrical Langmuir probes. It provides high-resolution data to study Venus' upper atmosphere and its interaction with the solar wind.
92d3ce9a-bae1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Temperature Probe part of Pioneer Venus Orbiter

92f25b20-b66e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Millstone Hill (MSH) Geomagnetic Observatory was a ground-based facility located in Westford, Massachusetts, operated by Boston University from 1999 to 2001 for the purpose of geomagnetic measurements.
92f25b20-b66e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Millstone Hill Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

92ffb48e-b982-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Brixiis Astronomical Observatory** is a ground-based observatory located in Kruibeke, Belgium. It is dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
92ffb48e-b982-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Brixiis Astronomical Observatory, Belgium

93044634-b608-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** ISIS 2 (International Satellites for Ionospheric Studies) was a Canadian ionosphere research satellite launched in 1971. It carried various instruments to study the Earth's ionosphere and was operational until its deactivation in 1990.
93044634-b608-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Observatory on ISIS-2

93065234-bb68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Boulder Geomagnetic Observatory (BOU), located in Colorado, USA, is a ground-based facility that has been operating since 1961 to monitor and study geomagnetic activity.
93065234-bb68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Boulder Geomagnetic Observatory

930ac3b0-b900-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Podkamennaya Tunguska Magnetometer is an instrument located at the Podkamennaya Tunguska geophysical observatory that has been operational since January 1, 1969, used for measuring and studying Earth's magnetic field.
930ac3b0-b900-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Podkamennaya Tunguska Observatory

930ee53e-bbc7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Agincourt Geomagnetic Observatory (AGN) was a ground-based facility in Toronto, Canada, that operated from 1932 to 1969, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
930ee53e-bbc7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Agincourt Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

93160966-bc78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The specified magnetometer is part of the observatory facilities at the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto, focusing on monitoring magnetic activity in the North West Pacific region.
93160966-bc78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at World Data Center Kyoto Observatory

932646ac-b9f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Arkansas Sky Observatory, Petit Jean Mountain South is an astronomical observatory located at 9 Bratcher Road, Conway County, Arkansas. It serves as a ground-based facility for observing celestial objects and phenomena.
932646ac-b9f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Arkansas Sky Observatory on Petit Jean Mountain South, United States

932e7572-b8b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Kumasi station with the IAGA identifier KUM, operational since January 1972.
932e7572-b8b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kumasi Observatory

933eb838-b738-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Northview Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Mendon, New York, known for its ground-based observations.
933eb838-b738-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Northview Observatory

933f4dfe-bae7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Marion Island geophysical observatory was a ground-based facility located in the city of Marion Base, South Africa, operating from 1973 to 1980 and primarily involved in magnetic measurements with magnetometers.
933f4dfe-bae7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Marion Island Observatory, South Africa

9341b9ee-b8db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Thomas More College Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Thomas More University in Crestview Hills, Kentucky. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and education.
9341b9ee-b8db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Thomas More College Observatory

9348143c-b968-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Global Ionospheric Radio Observatory (GIRO), specifically the Cosmos-1809 satellite (also known as COSMOS_1809 and NORAD ID 17241), is an Earth observation satellite launched by the USSR in 1986 to study ionospheric characteristics. Equipped with various instruments such as a topside sounder, impedance probe, and mass spectrometer, it aimed to measure plasma density profiles, electron temperatures, and other ionospheric parameters until its deactivation, though it remains re-activatable if funding is secured.
9348143c-b968-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Global Ionospheric Radio Observatory part of Cosmos 1809

934a64fe-b985-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sinsen Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Marl, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It has the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID 142 and focuses on ground-based observations.
934a64fe-b985-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sinsen Observatory, Germany

934fed30-ba51-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MIMI Ion Neutral Camera for the Cassini Orbiter is an instrument designed to detect ions and neutral particles in Saturn’s magnetosphere, aiding in mapping their distribution and characteristics to better understand Saturn's atmospheric dynamics and magnetospheric processes.
934fed30-ba51-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Neutral Camera on Cassini Orbiter

93500cd8-b9a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Galactic and Solar Cosmic Ray Experiment on Helios-A (E7)** is an energetic particle instrument designed to measure cosmic rays, including electrons, protons, and alpha particles within specific energy ranges. It features multiple telescopes with varying geometric factors to detect these particles and monitor solar X-rays between 2-8 keV.
93500cd8-b9a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument part of Helios Mission

9354daac-b830-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **BARREL Balloon 1A:** A high-altitude balloon, part of NASA's BARREL mission, designed to study relativistic electron losses from Earth's radiation belts using a NaI scintillator and a DC magnetometer. It operated in the stratosphere from January 28 to February 14, 2013.
9354daac-b830-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star, Geospace Mission of Opportunity

9355f66c-b786-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Hoher List Observatory is an astronomical observatory located on the Hoher List mountain in the Eifel region of Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. It has been operational since 1954 and is situated approximately 60 km southwest of Bonn.
9355f66c-b786-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hoher List Observatory, Germany

935d00e2-b75e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nagoya University 4m Radio Telescope is a millimeter-wave telescope located at the Las Campanas Observatory in South America. It has an aperture of 4 meters and is operated by Nagoya University for astronomical observations.
935d00e2-b75e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 4.0m Radio Telescope at Las Campanas Observatory

93623902-b9e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) Fabry-Perot Interferometer at Shigaraki, Japan is an instrument used to measure neutral winds in the mesosphere and thermosphere through airglow emissions. It operates at wavelengths of 630.0 nm and 557.7 nm and was developed by Nagoya University to study upper atmospheric dynamics.
93623902-b9e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fabry-Perot Interferometer part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Shigaraki Observatory

9366a4d8-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MIMI Low Energy Magnetospheric Measurement Sensor (LEMMS) for the Cassini Orbiter is an instrument designed to measure low-energy charged particles within Saturn's magnetosphere, providing crucial data on plasma environments and magnetic field interactions.
9366a4d8-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: MIMI Charge/Energy Mass Spectrometer on Cassini Orbiter

9366f5e4-b99c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Submillimeter Telescope Observatory, also known as the Heinrich Hertz 10-meter Telescope, is a ground-based observatory specializing in submillimeter astronomy.
9366f5e4-b99c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Submillimeter Heinrich Hertz 10m Telescope at Submillimeter Telescope Observatory

93707e18-bb6b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "STV51" is a spacecraft identified by the code -212, as defined within the Virtual Observatory Paris (VOParis) namespace for observing facilities.
93707e18-bb6b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: STV51

93795038-b68e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Atmosphere Explorer (AE) spacecraft series were designed to investigate Earth's atmosphere, thermosphere, and ionosphere.
93795038-b68e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Atmosphere Explorer Spacecraft

937a0e42-b69d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dixon Geomagnetic Observatory (DIK), located in Russia, is a ground-based facility that has been operating since 1957 to monitor geomagnetic activity.
937a0e42-b69d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dixon Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

938010ac-b8ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Snap Lake (SNAP) Station is a ground-based observatory located in Snap Lake, Northwest Territories, Canada. It is part of the UCLA Ground Based Observatories Network and primarily focuses on magnetic field measurements for space weather research as part of NASA's THEMIS mission.
938010ac-b8ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Snap Lake Station, Canada

938b9a76-b743-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Voyager 1 Spacecraft Sensors refer to the suite of instruments onboard the Voyager 1 spacecraft, including magnetometers, plasma detectors, charged particle instruments, and imaging systems, designed to study planetary environments and interstellar space.
938b9a76-b743-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Voyager 1 Spacecraft Sensors on Voyager 1 Spacecraft

938baf9a-ba34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lunar Prospector Spacecraft Magnetometer and Electron Reflectometer (MAGER) was an instrument on the Lunar Prospector spacecraft designed to investigate lunar crustal magnetic fields and estimate the size of a metallic core, utilizing a 3-axis fluxgate magnetometer and an electrostatic analyzer.
938baf9a-ba34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer and Electron Reflectometer on Lunar Prospector

939053b2-b84d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Saint Barthelemy Observatory (OAVdA) is an astronomical facility located in the Aosta Valley region of Italy. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is situated at 43 Strada Regionale n. 36 di Saint-Barthélemy, Lignan, Nus, with coordinates 7.478780296733483 longitude and 45.790854471000884 latitude.
939053b2-b84d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Saint Barthelemy Observatory, Italy

93af751e-bb07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Vykhodnoy**: A former ground-based observatory in Russia, operational from 1949 to 1955, equipped with a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements.
93af751e-bb07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Vykhodnoy Observatory, Russia

93b2d386-b827-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Borga Geomagnetic Observatory (BGA), located on Earth's surface and sponsored by South Africa, is a ground-based facility operating since 1975 that specializes in geomagnetic measurements.
93b2d386-b827-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Borga Geomagnetic Observatory

93bb4334-b90a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2O Data Processing Unit (DPU) is a versatile instrument controller board used in the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) project. It collects data from various sensors, formats it for transmission via an Iridium modem, and manages system commands, utilizing an FPGA for flexible interface logic.
93bb4334-b90a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

93bfa03c-bb62-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Seveso Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in the Province of Monza and Brianza, Italy. It is situated at Villa Dho, Via Cacciatori delle Alpi, Altopiano di Seveso, Seveso, and operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
93bfa03c-bb62-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Seveso Observatory, Italy

93d60fc6-b9b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Orbiting Solar Observatory 7 (OSO-7) was a satellite mission launched to observe the Sun in the gamma-ray waveband, contributing valuable data on solar processes and phenomena.
93d60fc6-b9b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma-ray Orbiting Solar Observatory 7 Satellite Mission

93d63ecc-b69f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cassini Orbiter Ultraviolet Imaging Spectrograph (UVIS)** is a set of telescopes on the Cassini spacecraft designed to measure ultraviolet light from Saturn's atmospheres, rings, and surfaces, and perform occultation measurements.
93d63ecc-b69f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Imaging Spectrograph on Cassini Orbiter

93d7c130-bb35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Sukagawa Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Sukagawa, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical research and observations.
93d7c130-bb35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sukagawa Observatory, Japan

93dcd52a-bbb3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: El Catalejo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Santa Rosa, La Pampa, Argentina. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
93dcd52a-bbb3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: El Catalejo Observatory, Argentina

93dd1e68-b72b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Urdinegi, Italy, known as the Mount Matajur Observatory.
93dd1e68-b72b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mount Matajur Observatory, Italy

93e2dff4-bb33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The La Seyne sur Mer Observatory is an astronomical facility located in La Seyne-sur-Mer, France. It operates as a ground-based observatory dedicated to the study of celestial objects and phenomena from its site on Earth.
93e2dff4-bb33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: La Seyne sur Mer Observatory, France

93e518da-b64e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Instituto de Astrofisica de Canarias 0.8m Telescope (IAC-80) is an optical telescope located at the Observatorio del Teide in Africa, with an aperture of 0.8 meters.
93e518da-b64e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical Instituto de Astrofisica de Canarias 0.8m Telescope at Observatorio del Teide

93e73f1c-baee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ASPERA-4 Electron Spectrometer (ELS) is an instrument aboard the Venus Express spacecraft designed to study the interaction between the solar wind and Venus' atmosphere by measuring plasma and neutral gas environments, with a focus on energetic electron populations.
93e73f1c-baee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Spectrometer on ASPERA-4

93fb6222-bc41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 1 Energetic Particle Detector (EPD) Suite, Fly's Eye Energetic Particle Sensor (FEEPS) is an instrument on the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission that measures three-dimensional energetic ion and electron flux distributions over specific energy ranges with a time resolution of 10 seconds.
93fb6222-bc41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fly's Eye Energetic Particle Sensor part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

941cc52c-ba05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Hot Plasma Analyzer (Hydra)** is an electrostatic analyzer instrument on the Polar spacecraft designed to observe and quantify magnetic reconnection in the cusp region, study field-aligned currents in the auroral zone, and provide high time resolution definitions of regions associated with the cusp and entry layer.
941cc52c-ba05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser on Polar part of Hot Plasma Analyzer

94236b36-b81e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Warner and Swasey Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in East Cleveland, Ohio, part of Case Western Reserve University. It houses the Burrell Schmidt telescope and is used for ground-based observations.
94236b36-b81e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Warner and Swasey Observatory, United States

9425420e-bbce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Eyrewell Magnetic Observatory:** A ground-based magnetic observatory located in Christchurch, New Zealand, operated by GNS Science since 1978. It is part of the global INTERMAGNET network and contributes to monitoring and studying the Earth's magnetic field.
9425420e-bbce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eyrewell Magnetic Observatory, New Zealand

942eb2b6-bc79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gornotayezhnaya geophysical observatory is a ground-based facility located in Ussuriysk, Primorsky Krai, Russia. It operated from 1957 to 1997 and was part of the World Data Center (WDC) system.
942eb2b6-bc79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Gornotayezhnaya Observatory, Russia

943bccec-b749-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Kumamoto Astronomical Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Minami Ward, Kumamoto, Japan. It operates under the MPC ID 864 and is situated within the Kumamoto Prefecture on Kyushu Expressway.
943bccec-b749-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kumamoto Observatory, Japan

9448511a-b654-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "GOES 6 Position" is an instrument on the GOES 6 satellite that provides ephemeris data, detailing the spacecraft's positional information over time. It is part of the broader GOES observatory system used for environmental monitoring and weather forecasting.
9448511a-b654-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris on GOES 6 Spacecraft

945628aa-bb2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Fluxgate Magnetometer at Kagoshima** is a part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) network, located in Kagoshima and used for measuring magnetic fields.
945628aa-bb2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at ISEE-210 Magnetic Meridian Observatory

94645756-b6eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SLIM Navigation Cameras consist of two small cameras, CAM-PX and CAM-MZ, used for vision-based navigation with field views aligned along the +X axis and -Z axes respectively.
94645756-b6eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Navigation Camera on SLIM Lander

9466f050-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Bellavista Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in San Cipriano, L'Aquila, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
9466f050-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bellavista Observatory

946807be-bb89-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cassini Orbiter Composite Infrared Spectrometer (CIRS)** is an instrument on the Cassini spacecraft designed to detect and analyze infrared light to measure the temperature and composition of celestial objects. It uses a combination of optics, interferometers, and detectors to cover both mid-infrared and far-infrared spectral regions.
946807be-bb89-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Composite Infrared Spectrometer on Cassini Orbiter

946969ea-b64a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram is a lander that was part of India's Chandrayaan-3 mission, designed to explore the lunar surface and carry scientific instruments like LRA (Laser Retroreflector Array) for precise measurement.
946969ea-b64a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Rover and Lander on Chandrayaan 3

946a397a-b77f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Calar Alto TNO Survey** is an astronomical observatory located at the Centro Astronómico Hispano en Andalucía in Gérgal, Spain. It specializes in trans-Neptunian object (TNO) surveys and operates as a ground-based facility.
946a397a-b77f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Calar Alto TNO Survey at Calar Alto Observatory, Spain

947221aa-b683-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Taunton Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Taunton, Massachusetts, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
947221aa-b683-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Taunton Observatory, United States

947abd0a-b733-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Chesterfield Inlet is a ground-based observatory located in the Kivalliq Region of Nunavut, Canada, which operated briefly from 1932 to 1933 and included a magnetometer as part of its instrumentation.
947abd0a-b733-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Chesterfield Inlet Observatory, Canada

94823830-badc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Hoyerswerda Observatory (code: C43) is an astronomical observatory located in Hoyerswerda - Wojerecy, Bautzen - Budyšin, Saxony, Germany. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial objects and phenomena.
94823830-badc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hoyerswerda Observatory, Germany

9484833c-bab0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Observatory Moers Kapellen** is a ground-based observatory located at 8, James-Krüss-Straße in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It operates as an astronomical facility for observation and research purposes.
9484833c-bab0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatory Moers Kapellen, Germany

94894baa-bb97-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Whitehorse (WHS) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility in Whitehorse that operated from 1992 to 2017, primarily equipped with magnetometers for geophysical measurements.
94894baa-bb97-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Whitehorse Observatory

948b6982-b60e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Asterion Observatory is an astronomical observatory and astronomy club located in Petrozavodsk, Russia. It was established on October 1, 2008, and operates as part of Petrozavodsk State University.
948b6982-b60e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Asterion Observatory, Russia

948d15b4-b700-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lüscherz Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Lüscherz, Switzerland. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial objects and phenomena from Earth.
948d15b4-b700-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lüscherz Observatory

94929346-b727-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wu-Han Geomagnetic Observatory (WHN)** is a ground-based facility located in Wuhan, China, that specializes in geomagnetic observations and is part of the global network for monitoring Earth's magnetic field.
94929346-b727-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Wu-Han Geomagnetic Observatory, China

94a1827a-bc4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NOAK Observatory (L02) is an astronomical observatory located in Stavraki, Greece. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
94a1827a-bc4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stavraki Observatory, Greece

94a1ac1a-b9ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rapid City Geomagnetic Observatory (RPC) is a ground-based facility located in Castle, Meade County, South Dakota, United States. It is part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) observatory network and monitors geomagnetic activity using instruments such as magnetometers.
94a1ac1a-b9ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Rapid City Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

94a941cc-b7c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High Energy Telescope (HET) on STEREO B is a particle detector within the IMPACT investigation, designed to measure protons, helium ions up to 100 MeV/n, and electrons up to 5 MeV using a linear array of six solid-state detectors.
94a941cc-b7c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Energy Telescope part of In-Situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients Investigation on STEREO B

94b2a44c-b669-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) 1.52m Harold Johnson Telescope at El Observatorio Astronómico Nacional/Sierra San Pedro Mártir (OAN/SPM) is an optical telescope located in North America, specifically in Sierra San Pedro Mártir, Mexico. It has a 1.52-meter aperture and is used for astronomical research and observations.
94b2a44c-b669-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Harold Johnson Telescope at El Observatorio Astronómico Nacional Sierra San Pedro Mártir, Mexico

94b85112-b6d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Budkov, used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field, which has been operational since January 1967.
94b85112-b6d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Budkov Observatory

94bb5522-ba99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Red Barn Observatory** (MPC code H68) is an astronomical observatory in Ty Ty, Georgia, dedicated to the follow-up observations and detections of asteroids, comets, and Near-Earth objects. It was established in 2006 and is located at 1148 West B Parks Road, Tift County, Georgia, United States.
94bb5522-ba99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Red Barn Observatory, United States

94bf7dbc-b609-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Dridri Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Passirano, Brescia, Lombardy, Italy. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to celestial observation and research.
94bf7dbc-b609-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dridri Observatory, Italy

94c4f092-b665-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **InSight Mars Lander Auxiliary Payload Sensor Subsystem (APSS) Pressure Sensor** was a component of the InSight Mars Lander, designed to collect environmental data to support the SEIS instrument and facilitate safe hardware deployment on the Martian surface. It specifically helped in reducing atmospheric effects from seismic signals detected by SEIS.
94c4f092-b665-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pressure Sensor part of InSight Mars Lander Auxiliary Payload Sensor Subsystem

94c71e68-ba74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Siding Spring Observatory is an astronomical observatory located near Coonabarabran, New South Wales, Australia, known for housing several telescopes including the Anglo-Australian Telescope and being part of the Australian National University's Research School of Astronomy & Astrophysics.
94c71e68-ba74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Siding Spring Observatory

94c73494-b6b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AVON (Asia VLF Observation Network) Saraburi station, located in Khao Phraya Doen Thong, Lop Buri Province, Thailand, is a ground-based facility dedicated to very low frequency radio observations as part of the Asia VLF Observation Network.
94c73494-b6b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VLF Asia VLF Observation Network Saraburi station, Thailand

94c7c8a0-ba00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nagoya University 4m Radio Telescope at Atacama is a millimeter-wave telescope with a 4.0-meter aperture located in Antofagasta, Chile. It is operated by Nagoya University and is situated in the Atacama Desert for optimal astronomical observations.
94c7c8a0-ba00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 4.0m Nagoya University Radio Telescope at Atacama, Chile

94ceab2e-b7d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **Langmuir Probe** is an instrument featuring two cylindrical electrostatic probes designed to measure electron density and temperature. It operates by sweeping a 2-Hz sawtooth voltage across the probes, analyzing current profiles to determine these properties, and was operational from launch until August 1968 on Explorer 22 (BE-B).
94ceab2e-b7d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Langmuir Probe on Explorer 22

94db21e6-b8c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a spacecraft with the label "Geocentric" and is associated with a value set containing "Geocentric." It falls under the type defined by the VO-Paris namespace for observational facilities, specifically indicating its status as a spacecraft.
94db21e6-b8c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Value Set on Geocentric

94e7dc34-ba42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Global Surveyor Spacecraft (MGS) Radio Science Subsystem was an instrument suite that utilized both spacecraft and ground-based equipment to conduct radio science experiments. It studied Mars' gravity field, atmosphere, and ionosphere by analyzing Doppler shifts in the spacecraft’s radio signals, providing insights into the planet's internal structure and atmospheric dynamics.
94e7dc34-ba42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Subsystem on Mars Global Surveyor Spacecraft

94f5cfb2-bbe4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SBIG ST-6 is an astronomical instrument, specifically a type of CCD camera used for imaging in astronomy. It is designed to capture detailed images of celestial objects and is recognized within the context of NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS).
94f5cfb2-bbe4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SBIG ST-6 on 1m Grubb Telescope

9506685c-b808-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Vermillion Cliffs Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in Kanab, Utah, United States, primarily functioning as a ground-based facility.
9506685c-b808-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vermillion Cliffs Observatory at Kanab

9510eaaa-b760-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Ramey AFB in Puerto Rico (PRJ18) is a ground-based facility equipped with a Digisonde for evaluating the properties of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere, providing advanced data on angle of arrival, polarization, Doppler frequency shift, and travel time.
9510eaaa-b760-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Ionospheric Station on Ramey Air Force Base

95156972-b698-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Television System (TVS) on Vega 2 was an imaging instrument consisting of two telescopes—a narrow-angle and a large-angle—designed for high-resolution observations and tracking of the comet nucleus during the spacecraft's flyby.
95156972-b698-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Television System on Vega 2

95241c70-b7e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specified magnetometer is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate model installed at Chokurdakh, Russia, as part of the CPMN observation network within the IUGONET observatory.
95241c70-b7e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometer Network observation network

952e33aa-b646-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Urumqi Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility in Ürümqi, Xinjiang, China, dedicated to monitoring the Earth's magnetic field since 1978.
952e33aa-b646-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Urumqi Observatory, China

954733f0-b7b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Marseille Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Marseille, France, notable for its discovery of Stephan's Quintet and its long history dating back to the early 18th century.
954733f0-b7b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Marseille Observatory, France

954859b0-ba15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Mass Ejection Imager (SMEI) is an instrument on the U.S. Air Force's Coriolis satellite designed to photograph and monitor coronal mass ejections (CMEs) from the Sun using three optical cameras. It provides advanced warnings of Earth-directed CMEs by capturing Thompson-scattered light, employing differential photometry to distinguish the variable light from CMEs against the stronger Zodiacal light background.
954859b0-ba15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Mass Ejection Imager on Coriolis

954f7ffc-b857-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure magnetic fields. At the Hallett (HLL) observatory, part of the IUGONET WDC Kyoto network, these instruments are utilized for geomagnetic monitoring and research purposes.
954f7ffc-b857-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hallett Observatory

955545d6-b8d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tataka Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Mt. Yu-Shan National Park, Xinyi Township, Nantou County, Taiwan. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observation.
955545d6-b8d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tataka Observatory, Taiwan

95570c14-b6fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fire in the Sky Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at 20464 Madson Avenue in West Crow Wing, Crow Wing County, Minnesota. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
95570c14-b6fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fire in the Sky Observatory, United States

95593f02-b9e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Magnetometer named "MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at LSK" is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate instrument installed at Lusaka, Zambia, part of the MAGDAS observation network.
95593f02-b9e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System observation network

9567b926-b755-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sabadell Astronomical Society (also known as Agrupació Astronòmica de Sabadell) is an astronomical observatory located in Sabadell, Catalonia, Spain. It was established on April 14, 1960, and focuses on ground-based observations.
9567b926-b755-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sabadell Observatory, Spain

956e2906-b7a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Chamberlin Observatory is an astronomical observatory owned and operated by the University of Denver, located in Denver, Colorado. It was funded by Humphrey B. Chamberlin and opened in 1894.
956e2906-b7a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chamberlin Observatory

95772930-bb5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **GOES-9 (1995-025A)** is the second satellite in the GOES-NEXT series, a joint effort by NASA and NOAA to monitor weather systems over the United States, distribute meteorological data, support search and rescue programs, and improve atmospheric process understanding for better forecasting.
95772930-bb5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 9

9583da5c-b741-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Paranal Observatory is an astronomical observatory operated by the European Southern Observatory (ESO), located in the Atacama Desert of Northern Chile on Cerro Paranal at 2,635 meters altitude. It houses the Very Large Telescope (VLT) and is notable for being one of the largest optical-infrared observatories globally.
9583da5c-b741-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Antu Telescope on European Southern Observatory Very Large Telescope at Paranal Observatory, Chile

95969086-b631-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Casper Geomagnetic Observatory (CSR) is a ground-based facility located in Midwest Heights, Natrona County, Wyoming, United States, established in 1958 for geomagnetic research and monitoring.
95969086-b631-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Casper Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

95985ac8-b673-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The HillTopTop Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Edgewood, New Mexico, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
95985ac8-b673-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hill Top Observatory

95b1d70e-ba2f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: Tumamoc Hill Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Tucson, Arizona, used for ground-based observations.
95b1d70e-ba2f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tumamoc Hill Observatory, United States

95b65c10-b963-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **ISEE1 Resonance Sounder** is an instrument on the ISEE-1 spacecraft designed to measure electron density in various regions of space, such as the solar wind and magnetosheath, by emitting radio pulses and detecting plasma resonances. It was part of a larger experiment aimed at studying key plasma parameters essential for understanding both large-scale MHD processes and microscopic kinetic processes.
95b65c10-b963-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna part of Radio Mapping of Solar Wind Disturbances (Type III bursts) in 3-D

95b7050e-ba7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The magnetometers at Fort Reliance (FRL) are part of the IUGONET observatory network and provide data on geomagnetic activity in that region.
95b7050e-ba7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fort Reliance Observatory

95b7bbf2-bb0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment (HiRISE) is a powerful remote sensing instrument on the MRO spacecraft that captures high-resolution images and topographic data of the Martian surface, with capabilities to provide detailed observations in three colors.
95b7bbf2-bb0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter

95be12bc-b59d-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: This entity represents a magnetometer instrument located at the Tjornes (TJO) observatory in Kyoto, providing information and data related to its operation and measurements.
95be12bc-b59d-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tjornes Observatory

95c20906-bbd0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Mizusawa Ground Magnetic Field Instrument, operational since 1960, is a specific type of magnetometer located at the IUGONET Observatory in Kyoto, Japan, under the auspices of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA).
95c20906-bbd0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mizusawa Observatory

95ca6792-bba6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar X-ray Monitor on GOES 6 was an instrument designed to monitor solar X-rays in two wavelength bands (5-30 nm and 10-80 nm) using ion chambers filled with specific gas mixtures, mounted behind a lead-lined aluminum collimator. It had high sensitivity thresholds and dynamic ranges but ceased providing usable data from August 1994 onwards.
95ca6792-bba6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar X-ray Monitor on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 6

95e7b4b6-bac3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Jack C. Davis Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Western Nevada College in Carson City, Nevada, equipped with multiple telescopes for studying celestial bodies and sunspots. The facility includes internet-connected cameras allowing remote access to images.
95e7b4b6-bac3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Jack C. Davis Observatory, United States

95eaf16c-bb31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wide Field Imager (WFI)** is a space instrument designed for heliospheric imaging, capable of capturing images from 18 to 180 solar radii and attenuating direct sunlight by over 16 orders of magnitude. It is part of the PUNCH mission and utilizes wide-field achromatic optics based on the Nagler eyepiece in reverse geometry.
95eaf16c-bb31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide Field Imager part of PUNCH-WFI 3

95ebb6d6-ba2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at TIK** is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed at Tixie, Russia, used for measuring magnetic field variations. It is part of the IUGONET observatory's CPMN observation network.
95ebb6d6-ba2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometer Network observation network

95f4f384-b888-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Amberley Geomagnetic Observatory (AML) was a ground-based facility located in Amberley, New Zealand, operational from July 1957 to December 31, 1977, dedicated to measuring and recording geomagnetic data.
95f4f384-b888-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Amberley Geomagnetic Observatory, New Zealand

961f0046-b5a1-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes an EMN fluxgate magnetometer installed at Moshiri, Japan (MSR), which is part of the Equatorial Magnetometer Network and the IUGONET observatory.
961f0046-b5a1-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Moshiri Observatory, Japan

9637b926-b662-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IBEX Background Monitor** is an instrument onboard the Interstellar Boundary Explorer (IBEX) spacecraft that measures the flux of protons with energies greater than approximately 14 keV, providing data at a time resolution of 0.24 seconds within a 7-degree conical viewing angle.
9637b926-b662-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument on Interstellar Boundary Explorer part of IBEX

963f1bfa-b67e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Interball-2 Ephemeris" is an instrument onboard the Spacecraft "Interball Aurora," providing data related to orbital modeling and position for the Interball-2 observatory. It includes information sets labeled as "Value@Interball-2 Ephemeris" and "Value@Interball-2 Orbit."
963f1bfa-b67e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris part of Interball 2 Mission

963fb7e6-b63c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Homer Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission's Ground Based Observatories (GBO), which began operations on January 1, 2007.
963fb7e6-b63c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Homer Observatory

964ada5c-b7fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 3 FIELDS Suite's Fluxgate Magnetometer is an instrument on the Magnetospheric Multiscale mission that combines Analog and Digital Fluxgate magnetometers to provide precise measurements of magnetic fields in space.
964ada5c-b7fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MMS FIELDS Suite

964bb1e6-b6ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Eurac Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Bolzano, Italy, operated by the European Academy of Bozen/Bolzano.
964bb1e6-b6ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: European Academy of Bozen/Bolzano Observatory

964e0a6a-b832-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Bergen-Enkheim Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Frankfurt, Germany, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects.
964e0a6a-b832-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bergen-Enkheim Observatory, Germany

96590660-bca4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ELFIN Mission's ELFIN A is a 3U+ CubeSat designed to investigate the loss of relativistic electrons from Earth’s radiation belts using energetic particle detectors and a fluxgate magnetometer.
96590660-bca4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Detector for Electrons part of Electron Losses and Fields Investigation Mission

965ae7ce-b7ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Karmoy Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG since December 30, 2006.
965ae7ce-b7ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Karmoy Geophysical Observatory

965fb640-b5fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operated on Marion Island from 1973 to 1980 as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy's (IAGA) investigations.
965fb640-b5fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Marion Island Observatory, Antarctica

96691882-b79c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Yuzhny Shar Geomagnetic Observatory (YSH) is a ground-based facility in Zapolyarny District, Russia, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements and has been operational since 1980.
96691882-b79c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Yuzhny Shar Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

966bd844-ba88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Stereo/Waves (Swaves) on STEREO B is an instrument designed to measure radio bursts and plasma waves associated with solar activity and coronal mass ejections (CMEs), providing detailed observations in the frequency range of 16 MHz to 40 kHz.
966bd844-ba88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stereo/Waves on STEREO B

966e8f78-b9e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure magnetic fields, and the "Magnetometers at Hel (HLP)" specifically refers to such instruments located at the Hel observatory in Kyoto, Japan, as part of the IAGA investigation.
966e8f78-b9e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Hel Observatory

9679a30c-ba33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BSH Byulsem Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at the Busan Science High School in Busan, South Korea. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
9679a30c-ba33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Busan Science High School Byulsem Observatory, South Korea

967a2ce8-ba86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Santiago-Quinta Normal was a ground observatory located in Santiago, Chile, that operated from 1862 to 1920. It was situated at the coordinates -33.44514 latitude and 289.3083 longitude.
967a2ce8-ba86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Santiago-Quinta Normal Observatory, Chile

967f42fe-ba7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Palomar High Angular Resolution Observer (PHARO)** is an instrument designed for the 5 m Hale telescope at Palomar Observatory, featuring adaptive optics and capabilities in spectroscopy, imaging, and coronagraphy.
967f42fe-ba7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 5m Hale Telescope at Palomar Observatory

96839f42-bbb9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Digital Stargate Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Manciano, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation of celestial objects and phenomena.
96839f42-bbb9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digital Stargate Observatory at Manciano, Italy

Foggy Bottom Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Hamilton, New York, owned and operated by Colgate University. Built in 1951, it serves as a ground-based facility for studying celestial objects.

96d1d3ea-b60c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole 6 Observatory

96d96740-ba17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: St. Mellons Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in St. Mellons, Cardiff, Wales, United Kingdom. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial objects.

96e489de-b9e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RAPID (Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors) instrument on the Cluster 2/FM6 spacecraft is a dual-sensor spectrometer designed to analyze suprathermal plasma distributions, measuring electrons and ions within specific energy ranges and providing detailed angular distributions for scientific research.

9779defe-b621-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Dumont d'Urville ground station used to measure magnetic field data since April 1957.

97a36c94-b9b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: SCALPSS is an imaging system designed to capture video during the descent and landing on the lunar surface, specifically aimed at reconstructing the effects of plume-surface interaction using stereo photogrammetry techniques. 97a582cc-bc5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Melbourne Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Melbourne, Australia. It operated officially from 1863 to 1945 and remains open to the public today, situated adjacent to the Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria.

97a7bc10-b9c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The R.A. Bagnold Wooden Wind Tunnel (c. 1935) is an early experimental wind tunnel designed by Ralph Alger Bagnold to study sand transport and desert dynamics.
97a7bc10-b9c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: R.A. Bagnold Wooden Wind Tunnel

97aa07bc-bbcd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Electric Field Instrument: Langmuir Probe** is a space-based instrument introduced in 2013 that utilizes two probes to measure electric fields and admittances using a sinusoidally varying bias mode. 97ae10d4-b6e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The "Double Star 1 Spacecraft Position" refers to the dataset providing the geocentric solar ecliptic (GSE) coordinates of the Double Star 1 spacecraft at a resolution of one minute, archived by the Centre National d'Études Spatiales (CNES).

97b5ea46-b8cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pulsating Aurora Project's All-sky EMCCD Imager with an RG665 filter located in Sodankyla, Finland is part of the ISEE observatory and utilizes an ImagEM X2 EMCCD camera by Hamamatsu Photonics for capturing comprehensive images of pulsating auroras.

97bd472a-b1ad-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Van Vleck Observatory (IAU code 298) is an astronomical observatory located at Wesleyan University in Middletown, Connecticut.

9806b79a-b8a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ukhta Observatory

980791f2-bc63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Monte Deva Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Gijón, Asturias, Spain. It is a ground-based observatory used for studying celestial bodies and phenomena from Earth's surface.
980791f2-bc63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Monte Deva Observatory, Spain

981e98a2-b740-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Thermal Electron Energy Distribution part of Akebono

98239850-b5b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Energetic Proton/Electron Spectrometer DOK-2** is an instrument on the Interball Tail Probe spacecraft designed to study energetic particle acceleration and transport within Earth's magnetosphere. 98240c78-b926-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Sanglok Observatory (Q4329992) is an astronomical observatory located in Kaltok, Tajikistan, with the Minor Planet Center code 193.

9828e09c-bad7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Khovd station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Khovd, Mongolia, part of the larger MAGDAS network that monitors geomagnetic activity.
9828e09c-bad7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Khovd Observatory, Mongolia

9831d9a2-b624-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Uppsala-Angström Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Uppsala, Sweden. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.

98513c70-b85e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low-Energy Ion Detector on Double Star 2

9a061674-bab3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Magnetometers at Christchurch (CHR)" were scientific instruments used to measure the Earth's magnetic field in Christchurch as part of the IAGA investigation from 1902 to 1930.

9a19fe3e-b73c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Trześń is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in the village of Trześń within Mielec County, Subcarpathian Voivodeship, Poland. It operates at coordinates 50.33454° N, 21.49325° E and is known as Kamyk, Trześń.

9a249e0c-b7e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Seykha Geomagnetic Observatory (SEY) was a ground-based facility in Russia that operated from 1973 to 1980, located in the Yamalsky Rayon of the Ural Federal District.
9a249e0c-b7e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Seykha Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

9a2551f4-b65f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Chinon Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Chinon, France, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects.
9a2551f4-b65f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chinon Observatory, France

9a2b8c04-b6a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA/Goddard Space Sciences Laboratory FAST (Fast Auroral SnapshoT explorer) Satellite Mission is a space mission designed to observe neutrinos, particles, and gravitational waves. 9a2b8c04-b6a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fast Auroral Snapshot Explorer part of NASA/Goddard Space Sciences Laboratory

9a2fc662-bb45-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the **Ionospheric Station at Zhongshan station, Antarctica**, identified by URSI-code ZS36R. It is a ground facility equipped with an advanced Digisonde that analyzes angle of arrival, polarization, Doppler frequency shift, and travel time of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere, located at latitude -69.4 and longitude 76.4.

9a34035e-b99b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1.4m Infrared Survey Facility (IRSF) is a telescope located at the South African Astronomical Observatory's Sutherland site, designed for infrared observations. It operates within the infrared waveband and is situated on the continent of Africa.

9a38144a-bacb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover Radar Imager for Mars Subsurface Experiment (RIMFAX) is a ground-penetrating radar on the Perseverance rover, designed to transmit and receive electromagnetic waves to map subsurface geologic structures on Mars.

9a3f4cc6-b7db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole 13 Geomagnetic Observatory

9a49d93e-bb50-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, and the "Magnetometers at North Pole 7 (NPG)" refers specifically to those installed at the observatory located in the northern polar region.

**Definition:**
The Simosato Geomagnetic Observatory (SSO), located in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1957 to 1978, dedicated to monitoring and studying geomagnetic activities.
9a4ccc7c-b8b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Simosato Geomagnetic Observatory, Japan

9a527082-badb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SWF Observatory (G09) is an astronomical facility located in South Woodham Ferrers, England. It is a ground-based observatory used for stargazing and astronomical research.
9a527082-badb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: South Woodham Ferrers Observatory, United Kingdom

9a583016-b7b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The INAOE 2.12m Telescope at Observatorio Astrofisico Guillermo Haro (OAGH) is an optical telescope located in North America, operated by the Instituto Nacional de Astrofisica, Optica y Electronica (INAOE). It is part of the OAGH facility and has an aperture of 2.12 meters.
9a583016-b7b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 2.12m Telescope at Observatorio Astrofisico Guillermo Haro

9a58f886-ba03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Solar Wind Analyzer (SWA)** is a quadrispherical plasma analyzer within the Comprehensive Plasma Instrumentation on Geotail, designed to measure three-dimensional fluxes of ions in the energy range of 150-7,000 eV/Q.
9a58f886-ba03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Quadrispherical Plasma Analyzer part of Comprehensive Plasma Instrumentation on Geotail

9a64b87c-b924-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Plasma Waves Instrument (PWI)** on the Dynamics Explorer 1 spacecraft was designed to measure electric and magnetic fields in various frequency ranges to study wave phenomena, particularly those associated with auroral processes and particle acceleration. It utilized multiple antennas and receivers to capture wideband and low-frequency signals for detailed analysis.
9a64b87c-b924-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Dynamics Explorer 1 Plasma Waves Investigation

9a65bad0-b7ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Equatorial Magnetometer Network's (IUGONET) fluxgate magnetometer at Porto Velho is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument designed to measure magnetic field variations, installed at the observatory in Porto Velho, Brazil.
9a65bad0-b7ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of The Equatorial Magnetometer Network

9a71a7f8-bb86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Houston Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Colorado County, Texas, United States. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
9a71a7f8-bb86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Houston Observatory, United States

9a79701c-bbc9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CFDT1 (Cartesian Full-Disk Telescope Number 1) is an imager used for observing the full disk of the Sun. It is part of the IUGONET Observatory at the World Data Center in Kyoto, Japan.
9a79701c-bbc9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager on Solar Flare Observatory

9a7aaea0-b72d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AMPTE (Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers) mission was an international space mission launched in 1984 to study the interaction of solar-wind ions with Earth's magnetosphere, focusing on particle transport and energization. 9a89b284-ba10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Karmakuly Observatory

9a8ab70e-bba7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ISEE 1 Vector Electron Spectrometer (VES)** was an instrument aboard the ISEE-1 satellite, featuring two triaxial systems of cylindrical electrostatic analyzers to measure three-dimensional electron distribution functions across various energy ranges, with specific modes for solar wind, magnetosheath, and magnetotail observations.
9a8ab70e-bba7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer part of International Sun-Earth Explorer 1

9a96af50-b837-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Beuthen Observatory was a ground-based facility in Bytom, Poland, operational from 1899 to 1932, known for its magnetometer instruments as part of the IAGA observatory network.
9a96af50-b837-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Beuthen Observatory, Poland

9a9db92e-b9e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Interball Auroral Probe is a spacecraft launched as part of the multi-national Interball Project to study the physical mechanisms of solar wind energy transmission and dissipation in the magnetosphere during substorms. It was specifically designed to observe auroral phenomena and electric currents connecting the magnetospheric tail with the ionosphere.
9a9db92e-b9e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Interball Auroral Probe part of Interball

9aa8f4a2-ba5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The **South Observatory**, also known as the Clanfield Observatory, is an astronomical observatory located in Clanfield, East Hampshire, England. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
9aa8f4a2-ba5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: South Observatory, United Kingdom

9aae409e-b8c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Longyearbyen (LYR) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based research facility located in Svalbard, Norway, which includes a magnetometer and is part of the IUGONET observatory network. It has been operational since December 30, 2006.
9aae409e-b8c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Longyearbyen Geophysical Observatory, Norway

9abc35d0-b7e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 61-cm Astro Mechanics Cassegrain/Coude reflector is a telescope with a 0.61-meter aperture located at the Table Mountain Observatory in California, operational since 1965.
9abc35d0-b7e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.61m Astro Mechanics Cassegrain/Coude Reflector Telescope at Table Mountain Observatory, United States

9abc39a2-ba1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The San Pere Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Mataró, Catalonia, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
9abc39a2-ba1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatori Astronòmic Sant Pere at Mataró Observatory, Spain

9abd0334-b7b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electric field Double Probe (EDP) is an instrument suite on the Magnetospheric Multiscale mission (MMS), comprising Spin-plane Double Probe (SDP) and Axial Double Probe (ADP) to measure 3-D electric fields with high accuracy over a wide frequency range.
9abd0334-b7b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electric Field Double Probe part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

9ac12886-b993-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) All-Sky Imager at Haleakala, Hawaii, is a multi-wavelength instrument designed to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere by capturing nocturnal airglow emissions. It was developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research at Nagoya University and operates from the ISEE Observatory in Hawaii.
9ac12886-b993-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Multi-wavelength All-Sky Imager part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers

9acf7978-b8c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ion Propulsion System (IPS) Diagnostic Subsystem (IDS) is a set of sensors integrated into the Deep Space 1 spacecraft's propulsion system, designed to collect data on electric and magnetic fields during encounters like that with Comet Borrelly.
9acf7978-b8c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: The Ion Propulsion System Diagnostic Subsystem part of Deep Space 1

9ae12a98-b919-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sudbury Geomagnetic Observatory (SUB)** is a ground-based facility located in Medfield, Massachusetts, USA, that monitors geomagnetic activity as part of the IAGA network.
9ae12a98-b919-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sudbury Geomagnetic Observatory

9b02f9c0-b7de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS Electrostatic Analyzers (ESAs) are instruments on the THEMIS spacecraft that measure the flux of thermal particles over a 360° field of view and energy range from ~3 eV to 30 keV, providing full 3-D distributions, density, velocity, and temperature data for both electrons and ions.
9b02f9c0-b7de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer part of Dual Full Distribution Electrostatic Analyzers

9b06bb60-b76f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: EPI-Lo is an instrument aboard the Parker Solar Probe Mission designed to measure energetic electrons and ions in a specific energy range. It is a time-of-flight mass spectrometer that provides comprehensive observations of particle spectra and resolves major heavy ion species, contributing to understanding solar energetic particles close to the Sun.
9b06bb60-b76f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument Low Energy on Parker Solar Probe

9b08ae98-b797-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Imaging Science Subsystem - Narrow Angle for Voyager 1 is a high-resolution camera on the Voyager 1 spacecraft designed to capture detailed images of planets and other celestial objects.
9b08ae98-b797-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Narrow Angle Camera on Imaging Science Subsystem part of Voyager 1

9b1f1ba4-b9b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Sura Gardens is an astronomical observatory located in Rakshivka, Ukraine. It operates as a ground-based facility and is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with the code L55.
9b1f1ba4-b9b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sura Gardens Observatory, Ukraine

9b277fd2-b92a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The EVE (Extreme Ultraviolet Variability Experiment) is an instrument aboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) that measures solar extreme ultraviolet irradiance variations to understand the Sun's influence on Earth's outer atmosphere. It operates in the 0.1-105 nm range with high spectral resolution and temporal cadence, utilizing multiple channels and grating spectrographs.
9b277fd2-b92a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Extreme Ultraviolet Variability Experiment part of Solar Dynamics Observatory

9b5563c2-ba18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Vilnius University Astronomical Observatory** is one of the oldest astronomical observatories in Europe, founded in 1753 and located in Vilnius, Lithuania. Although it no longer conducts direct observations due to light pollution, it remains active in scientific research.
9b5563c2-ba18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vilniaus universiteto astronomijos observatorija at Vilnius

9b71df3a-b8a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2001 Mars Odyssey Spacecraft Thermal Emission Imaging System (THEMIS) is an instrument on the Mars Odyssey spacecraft designed to capture high-resolution images of Mars using infrared and visible light, providing data on surface features, mineral composition, and thermal properties.
9b71df3a-b8a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Thermal Emission Imaging System on 2001 Mars Odyssey Spacecraft

9b767ff0-bb42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Stonehenge Observatory** is a ground-based observatory located in Coleman County, Texas, United States. It is situated at coordinates 31.93738° N, 260.30403° W.
9b767ff0-bb42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stonehenge Observatory, Novice

9b7f681e-b7ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operated in Budakeszi (BUZ) from 1949 to 1955 as part of the IAGA investigation to study geomagnetic fields.
9b7f681e-b7ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Budapest Observatory

9b86379e-b91a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Southern Stars Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Pamatai, Faʻaʻā, French Polynesia. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
9b86379e-b91a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Southern Stars Observatory, French Polynesia

9b867598-b6f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Akebono Auroral Television (ATV)** was an imaging instrument aboard the Akebono satellite that captured downward-looking images of auroras in 1989-1990, with data accessible through DARTS.
9b867598-b6f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Auroral Television Imager on Akebono

9b8d79c6-b5fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 3 Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer (HPCA) is a scientific instrument aboard the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS), designed to measure ion fluxes and composition in space plasma environments, particularly near magnetopause reconnection regions. 9b8d79c6-b5fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

9b93598a-b89b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Llano del Hato National Astronomical Observatory is Venezuela's principal astronomical observatory, located 3600 meters above sea level in the Venezuelan Andes near Mérida.
9b93598a-b89b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Llano del Hato National Astronomical Observatory, Venezuela

9ba8af96-bb17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The British Geological Survey (BGS), established on July 11, 1935, is a ground-based observatory that specializes in geomagnetism, measuring and interpreting variations in Earth's magnetic fields to advance scientific understanding and provide services to industry and academia.
9ba8af96-bb17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetism Team at British Geological Survey

9bb0d9da-b826-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Canterbury Mount John Observatory (UCMJO) is New Zealand's premier astronomical research observatory, located atop Mount John in the Mackenzie Basin, South Island, and established in 1965.
9bb0d9da-b826-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mount John Observatory, New Zealand

9bb15d58-bab8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Ukiah Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission Ground-based observations (GMAG), operational since October 1, 2004.
9bb15d58-bab8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ukiah Geophysical Observatory

9bb25ba4-b766-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) Monitor is a photometric instrument aboard the MAVEN spacecraft, designed to measure solar irradiance in three broad bands within the soft x-ray and extreme ultraviolet wavelength range, contributing to studies of solar EUV input and its impact on the Martian upper atmosphere.
9bb25ba4-b766-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Extreme Ultraviolet Monitor on MAVEN spacecraft

9bb6aed6-b84f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kourou Geomagnetic Observatory (KOU), located in Kourou, France, is a ground-based facility that monitors geomagnetic activity and has been operational since 1995.
9bb6aed6-b84f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kourou Geomagnetic Observatory, France

9bcab58a-b74a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sodium Lidar at Tromsø, Norway** is an instrument that measures sodium density, temperature, and wind in the mesosphere at altitudes of 80-110 km.
9bcab58a-b74a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sodium Lidar at EISCAT Tromsø Observatory, Norway

9bd51ffc-b6be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The "Pioneer10 Positions" refers to the dataset containing the positional data of the Pioneer 10 spacecraft, which is part of the CDPP/AMDA observatory under CNES.

9bd7607c-b750-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Astrodomi Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Tigre, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina, designated with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code I37.
9bd7607c-b750-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astrodomi Observatory, Argentina

9be0b1e4-b706-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Achternholt Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Wardenburg, Lower Saxony, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility for stargazing and scientific research.
9be0b1e4-b706-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Achternholt Observatory, Germany

9be221ec-bb47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The San Antonio Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility in Texas, USA, that includes instruments like the magnetometer and is part of the McMac observatory network.
9be221ec-bb47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at San Antonio Geophysical Observatory, United States

9be232f2-b75c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the Deep Space Station 12 (DSS-12), a ground-based observatory facility used for astronomical observations and space communications.
9be232f2-b75c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep Space Station 12

9be2ebca-b6bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A high-resolution Fourier transform infrared spectrometer (FTIR) installed at the Rikubetsu observatory, used to monitor the vertical distribution of atmospheric molecules like O3, HCl, HNO3, and HF.
9be2ebca-b6bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High-resolution Fourier Transform Infrared Spectrometer part of ISEE

9be6c92c-b994-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Honolulu Magnetic Observatory**: A ground-based magnetic observatory located in Ewa Beach, Hawaii, operated by the USGS since 1902. It is part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.

NOAA 5 was a meteorological satellite launched in 1976 as part of the NOAA series to provide global cloud cover data and atmospheric temperature soundings. It featured advanced sensors such as the Very High Resolution Radiometer (VHRR) and Vertical Temperature Profile Radiometer (VTPR).

9bf1593c-b7f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Saturn Ring Plane Crossing 1995" was an astronomical event where Earth and the Sun crossed Saturn's ring plane multiple times between 1994 and 1997, providing unique opportunities for studying Saturn's rings and moons.

9bfc89ac-b754-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Geiger Tube Telescope on Pioneer 10 is an instrument designed to measure proton and electron fluxes in interplanetary space and near Jupiter using seven miniature Geiger tubes arranged in specific configurations.
