9c172b8a-bb4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Martigues Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Martigues, France, known for its ground-based observations and research in astronomy.
9c172b8a-bb4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Martigues Observatory, France

9c19061c-bad4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Quadrispherical Plasma Analyzer on Pioneer 11 is a scientific instrument featuring dual electrostatic analyzers designed to measure plasma distribution parameters, including energy ranges from 0.1 to 18 keV for protons and 1 to 500 eV for electrons, and particle fluxes ranging from 1.0E+2 to 3.0E+9/(sq cm-s).
9c19061c-bad4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Quadrispherical Plasma Analyzer on Pioneer 11

9c1f2202-ba3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Ametlla del Vallès Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Can Reixac (Sant Gregori), near l'Ametlla del Vallès, Barcelona, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
9c1f2202-ba3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ametlla del Valles Observatory, Spain

9c2435f4-b611-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 17 Lunar Atmospheric Composition Experiment (LACE) was a miniature mass spectrometer deployed on the lunar surface to analyze the composition and flux of gases in the Moon's atmosphere as part of the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP).
9c2435f4-b611-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Miniature Magnetic Deflection Mass Spectrometer on Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package

9c2b5474-bc33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Suno Astronomical Observatory** is a public ground-based observatory located in Suno, Novara, Piedmont, Italy. It focuses on astronomical observations and research from its Earth-bound facility.
9c2b5474-bc33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Suno Observatory, Italy

9c2c2554-b858-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Bassano Bresciano Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Bassano Bresciano, Brescia, Lombardy, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to studying celestial phenomena.
9c2c2554-b858-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bassano Bresciano Observatory, Italy

9c2e5b3e-ba1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "LANL 1994 Positions" dataset provides spacecraft position data for the LANL 1994 mission in various coordinate systems, offering detailed ephemerides for scientific analysis.
9c2e5b3e-ba1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: LANL 1994 Positions on Spacecraft

9c300f56-baf2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **GNU Radio Beacon Receiver (GRBR) Station at Bac Lieu** is an observatory located in Vietnam, designed to measure ionospheric disturbances related to middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes. It operates as part of the GRBR network and utilizes a GNU radio beacon receiver for its measurements.
9c300f56-baf2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU radio beacon receiver on GRBR station at Bac Lieu, Vietnam

9c3437a0-b699-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The G. C. Gloriosi Astronomical Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in San Filippo, Montecorvino Rovella, Salerno, Italy. It is designated by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with the ID 229 and focuses on astronomical research and observations.
9c3437a0-b699-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: G. C. Gloriosi Astronomical Observatory, Italy

9c3d1024-ba08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The European Space Agency (ESA) XMM-Newton X-Ray Multi-Mirror Mission Satellite is a spacecraft designed for conducting detailed studies of celestial objects in the x-ray waveband.
9c3d1024-ba08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray European Space Agency XMM-Newton X-Ray Multi-Mirror Mission Satellite

9c3e2b9c-b8de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Williams College 0.6m (24-inch) Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Hopkins Observatory in North America, used for astronomical observations and research.
9c3e2b9c-b8de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 0.6m Telescope at Hopkins Observatory

9c4c1bc6-bca3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Taurus-1 Observatory (also known as the Mazzarot-1 Observatory) is an astronomical observatory located in Baran', Belarus, with the Minor Planet Center code A98.
9c4c1bc6-bca3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Taurus-1 Observatory, Belarus

9c4dcb4a-bbd8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Allahabad (ALH), operational since January 1, 2011, that is part of the IAGA investigation and the iugonet-observatory-wdc_kyoto-wdc-alh observatory.
9c4dcb4a-bbd8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Allahabad Observatory

9c4f82ce-b7e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wave-form Analyzer ULF, Electric & Magnetic** is an instrument aboard the Interball S2 spacecraft designed to collect and process data on three components of the magnetic field and one component of the electric field. It operates in two modes, transmitting all four components at high bit rates or a selected component at lower bit rates, with specific digitizer frequencies for each mode.
9c4f82ce-b7e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver Wave-form Analyzer ULF, Electric and Magnetic part of Interball S2

9c543458-b944-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Davis Ionosonde is a ground-based instrument located in Davis, Antarctica, used for studying the Earth's ionosphere. It operates by transmitting radio waves vertically and measuring the reflected signals to determine electron density and other parameters, with current equipment including a Lowell Digisonde sweeping frequencies from 0.5 to 30 MHz.
9c543458-b944-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar Ionosonde part of World Data Center for Geomagnetism, Kyoto and Davis, Antarctica

9c54c2b6-b939-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "NOAA 11 Positions" dataset provides the spatial coordinates of the NOAA 11 spacecraft in multiple reference frames.
9c54c2b6-b939-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: NOAA 11 part of Spacecraft

9c56bbc6-bb1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Paratunka geophysical observatory, also known as the Petropavlovsk Geomagnetic Observatory (PET), is a ground-based facility located in Kamchatka Krai, Russia, dedicated to studying geomagnetism since 1969.
9c56bbc6-bb1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Petropavlovsk Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

9c585702-bb80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Space Environment Monitor-2 (SEM-2)** on NOAA 18 is an instrument designed to measure the population of Earth's radiation belts and charged particle precipitation in the upper atmosphere, utilizing two sensors: the Total Energy Detector (TED) and the Medium Energy Proton/Electron Detector (MEPED).
9c585702-bb80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument part of Space Environment Monitor-2 on NOAA 18

9c5b9750-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISIS ionospheric observatories consist of the ISIS satellites, which are space facilities designed to study Earth's near-surface ionosphere.
9c5b9750-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionosphere Observatory

9c68df0a-bae0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Ancon Geomagnetic Observatory (ANC), located in Ancón, Lima, Peru, is a ground-based facility that monitors geomagnetic activity and has been operational since January 1990.
9c68df0a-bae0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ancon Geomagnetic Observatory, Peru

9c7b77b4-ba40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU radio beacon receiver (GRBR) station at Chiang Mai is an observatory located in Thailand that measures ionospheric disturbances related to middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes. It is situated at an altitude of 865 meters above sea level and is part of the GRBR network.
9c7b77b4-ba40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU Radio Beacon Receiver Station at Chiang Mai Observatory, Thailand

9c818b08-ba78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI) is a camera on the Mars Science Laboratory's Curiosity rover designed to capture high-resolution images of Martian geological materials, featuring a 2-megapixel color camera with a focusable macro lens.
9c818b08-ba78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Hand Lens Imager Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

9c8adc86-b9c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Galileo Probe Nephelometer (NEP)** was an instrument aboard the Galileo spacecraft designed to measure light scattering properties of Jupiter's atmospheric particles at various angles, providing insights into cloud structures and particle characteristics along the probe's descent trajectory.
9c8adc86-b9c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nephelometer on Galileo Probe

9c8d7bca-b8e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Scott Base Ionosonde is an instrument located in Scott Base, Antarctica, used since 1958 to study the Earth's ionosphere by transmitting radio waves vertically and recording the reflected signals.
9c8d7bca-b8e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionosonde at Scott Base Observatory, Antarctica

9c944ef2-b93b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Embry–Riddle Observatory is an astronomical observatory operated by Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University in Daytona Beach, Florida, featuring a 1m telescope and various optical instruments.
9c944ef2-b93b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1m Telescope at Embry-Riddle Observatory, United States

9c9e44b2-b5ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) instrument, specifically the Balloon 2C Ephemeris (EPHM), is a virtual instrument that provides trajectory positions in various coordinate systems. It is part of the BARREL observatory and supports investigations related to relativistic electron losses in space.
9c9e44b2-b5ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses part of BARREL Observatory

9ca5510e-b9a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Valldoreix Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Sant Cugat del Vallès, Spain, dedicated to ground-based observations.
9ca5510e-b9a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Valldoreix Observatory, Spain

9cad5f34-b5b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kingston station in Hobart, Tasmania, operated a Cosmic Ray monitor from June 30, 2004, to November 7, 2016, as part of its ground-based observatory facilities.
9cad5f34-b5b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cosmic Ray Monitor at Kingston Observatory, Australia

9cbba548-b9c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IGPP-LANL San Gabriel Dam Fluxgate Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, located at the San Gabriel Dam station as part of the IGPP-LANL Magnetometer Array.
9cbba548-b9c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IGPP-LANL San Gabriel Dam Observatory

9cbf9ec8-b5de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO)** is a NASA mission launched in 2010 to study the Sun's magnetic field and its impact on Earth's environment. It operates from an inclined geosynchronous orbit, carrying instruments like AIA, EVE, and HMI to gather data on solar activity and variations.
9cbf9ec8-b5de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Atmospheric Imaging Assembly on Solar Dynamics Observatory part of Living With a Star

9cc41b84-b8c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Hartebeesthoek Magnetic Observatory**, located in Gauteng, South Africa, is a ground-based facility dedicated to magnetic observations and is part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
9cc41b84-b8c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hartebeesthoek Observatory, South Africa

9cc47516-b961-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1K Data Processing Unit (DPU)** is an instrument controller board used in the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) project. It collects data from various sensors, formats it, and transmits it via an Iridium modem while also managing the command-cutdown system.
9cc47516-b961-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

9ceb5ffa-b713-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vallemare di Borbona Astronomical Observatory is a ground-based observatory located in Colle Marcone, Borbona, Rieti, Lazio, Italy. It operates at an altitude of 1,170 meters and is situated within Europe with specific geographical coordinates (latitude: 42.485925, longitude: 13.1181).
9ceb5ffa-b713-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vallemare di Borbona Astronomical Observatory, Italy

9cf80bbe-b60b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 8** is an instrument used to monitor magnetic fields from the GOES 8 satellite as part of space weather monitoring efforts. It consists of a three-axis fluxgate magnetometer with high sensitivity and accuracy, mounted on a boom away from the main spacecraft to minimize interference from stray magnetic fields.
9cf80bbe-b60b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 8

9d0951a8-b12e-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Birch Forest Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Huairou District, with coordinates provided for a location in Australia.
9d0951a8-b12e-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Birch Forest Observatory

9d1a6432-b85b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Tucson observatory used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of the IAGA investigation since 1909.
9d1a6432-b85b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

9d1b4220-ba0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **GSHS Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Suwon, South Korea. It is situated at Gyeonggi Science High School and operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
9d1b4220-ba0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Suwon Observatory, South Korea

9d28a93c-b6f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Daventry Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Daventry, West Northamptonshire, England, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial bodies.
9d28a93c-b6f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Daventry Observatory, United Kingdom

9d2adfe6-b753-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Sheshan geophysical observatory used for magnetic field measurements from June 1932 to December 1974.
9d2adfe6-b753-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sheshan Observatory

9d3ff340-b690-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Armilla Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Granada, Spain, known for its armillary sphere and ground-based observations.
9d3ff340-b690-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Armilla Observatory, Spain

9d432db4-bc1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The VERITAS Collaboration Very Energetic Radiation Imaging Telescope Array System, located at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in North America, is a ground-based gamma-ray observatory designed to detect and study very high energy gamma rays.
9d432db4-bc1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Energetic Radiation Imaging Telescope Array System gamma-ray at Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory

9d541bd8-b5e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Southern Hemisphere Spherical Elementary Current Systems (SECS) Instrument** is a virtual instrument that aggregates data from various ground magnetometer arrays to derive spherical elementary currents over Antarctica at 10-second resolution, providing insights into geomagnetic activity.
9d541bd8-b5e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Southern Hemisphere Spherical Elementary Current Systems Investigation

9d607a76-b7a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Davis Station is a ground facility located in Antarctica, specifically at coordinates -74.49 latitude and 99.62 longitude, which operates as part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network to monitor magnetic field variations.
9d607a76-b7a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Davis Observatory, Antarctica

9d647136-b715-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Talara, operational from 1957 to 1960, used for geomagnetic measurements as part of the IAGA investigation.
9d647136-b715-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Talara Observatory

9d8c2f7a-b844-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hyper Spectral Imager (HySI) is an instrument onboard the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft designed to map the lunar surface in 64 contiguous bands within the visible and near-infrared spectral region for mineralogical studies of the Moon.
9d8c2f7a-b844-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hyper Spectral Imager on Chandrayaan-1

9d982204-bbf9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Uppsala.1 Magnetometer is an instrument located at the Uppsala observatory, identified by the IAGA code UPP, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of geophysical investigations.
9d982204-bbf9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Uppsala Observatory

9da87172-b6d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Girardville Geomagnetic Observatory (GIR), located in Quebec, Canada, is a ground-based facility that has been operating since 1973 to monitor geomagnetic activity on Earth's surface.
9da87172-b6d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Girardville Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

9db3d540-b752-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: NOAA-16 was a defunct American weather satellite operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) as part of its polar orbiting meteorological satellite series. It was launched in 2000 and decommissioned in 2014 after an anomaly, eventually breaking up in orbit.
9db3d540-b752-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer/3 on NOAA-16

9db88f62-bbd6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MF radar at Poker Flat, Alaska is an instrument that measures the height profile of horizontal wind in the mesosphere and lower thermosphere using full-correlation analysis and meteor echo measurements. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network and operated by NICT/SALMON.
9db88f62-bbd6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar part of Mesosphere and Lower Thermosphere Wind Profiler at Poker Flat Observatory

9dbab5f2-b5e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Townsville Magnetometer** is a Fluxgate Magnetometer situated in Townsville, Queensland, Australia, operational since October 1998 as part of the ASWS Observatory.
9dbab5f2-b5e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Townsville Observatory, Australia

9dbc025e-bb28-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nobeyama Radio Observatory 1.2m Submillimeter Wave Telescope, located at Mount Fuji, is a ground-based observational facility used for studying celestial objects through submillimeter wavelengths.
9dbc025e-bb28-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.2m Submillimeter Wave Telescope at Nobeyama Radio Observatory on Mount Fuji

9dbce98c-b79d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Sternwarte Wetzikon (Observatory Wetzikon) is an astronomical observatory located in Wetzikon, Switzerland. It operates as a ground-based facility for observing celestial objects and conducting astronomical research.
9dbce98c-b79d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sternwarte Wetzikon Observatory

9dc1501a-b763-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Termoskan was an optical mechanical scanning radiometer onboard the Phobos 2 spacecraft designed to study Mars' surface temperature dynamics, thermal inertia of soil, and detect humidified regions and subsurface ice formations.
9dc1501a-b763-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Termoskan on Phobos 2

9dd3f13c-bafd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** La Romaneta Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Monòver / Monóvar, Alicante, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation of celestial objects and phenomena.
9dd3f13c-bafd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: La Romaneta Observatory, Spain

9dd603a0-b7c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Makroskooppi, Fregenal de la Sierra is a ground-based observatory located in Camino de los Molinos, Fregenal de la Sierra, Spain. It serves as an astronomical facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial objects from the ground level.
9dd603a0-b7c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Makroskooppi at Fregenal de la Sierra Observatory, Spain

9ddb0cda-b82b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 15 Command and Service Module (CSM) was a spacecraft used during the Apollo 15 mission to orbit the Moon while astronauts explored the lunar surface. It consisted of two units: the Command Module, which housed the crew and re-entry equipment, and the Service Module, which carried consumables and the main propulsion system.
9ddb0cda-b82b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Infrared Camera and Multi-Object Spectrometer on Apollo 15 Command and Service Module

9de6ba1e-b7ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Valencia Observatory** is a ground-based astronomical facility located at 3, Carrer del Poeta Eduard Buïl, Camí de Vera, Benimaclet, Valencia, Spain. It operates at coordinates approximately 39.4915° N latitude and -0.35786° E longitude in Europe.
9de6ba1e-b7ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Valencia Observatory, Spain

9dfadd92-ba7b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Geotail Hot Plasma Analyzer** is a quadrispherical plasma analyzer that measures three-dimensional fluxes of electrons and ions within the energy range of 1 to 50,000 eV/Q.
9dfadd92-ba7b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hot Plasma Analyzer on Comprehensive Plasma Instrumentation part of Geotail

9dfb860c-babc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 61-cm Boller & Chivens Cassegrain reflector #1 is a 61 cm telescope situated at the Mauna Kea Observatory, operational since November 1969 and managed by NASA and the University of Hawaii.
9dfb860c-babc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.61m Boller and Chivens Cassegrain Reflector Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatory, United States

9e01a7f0-b9c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cape Evans Geomagnetic Observatory (CEV), located in Antarctica and sponsored by New Zealand, was a ground facility that operated from 1912 to 1958 for geomagnetic observations.
9e01a7f0-b9c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cape Evans Geomagnetic Observatory

9e07b0c2-bbd3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sao Miguel Geophysical Observatory was a ground-based facility located in Ponta Delgada, Azores, Portugal, that operated from October 1965 to November 30, 1965. It housed magnetometers and contributed to geomagnetic data collection as part of the global observatory network.
9e07b0c2-bbd3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sao Miguel Geomagnetic Observatory, Portugal

9e0eaa08-b65b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pinawa (PINA) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in the Rural Municipality of Lac du Bonnet, Manitoba, Canada, and is part of the NASA THEMIS Ground-Based Observatory network. It specializes in geophysical measurements, including magnetometer readings, to study Earth's magnetic field and space weather phenomena.
9e0eaa08-b65b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pinawa Geophysical Observatory, Canada

9e1571f8-b6ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2.15-m Boller & Chivens reflector is a telescope with an aperture of 2.15 meters, located at the El Leoncito Astronomical Complex in Calingasta, San Juan, Argentina. It has been operational since February 1986 and is situated at coordinates -31.799166 latitude and 290.699997 longitude.
9e1571f8-b6ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.15m Boller and Chivens Reflector at El Leoncito Astronomical Complex, Argentina

9e15bd92-b7e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Apollo 14**: A NASA space mission, launched on January 31, 1971, that landed astronauts Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell on the Moon while Stuart Roosa orbited overhead in the Command Module, returning to Earth on February 9, 1971.
9e15bd92-b7e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package part of Apollo 14

9e2935de-bb61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The InSight Mars Lander Radiometer (RAD) is an instrument on the InSight lander designed to measure surface temperature in support of determining the subsurface temperature profile of Mars. It operates in three infrared bands and is part of the Heat Flow and Physical Properties Package (HP3).
9e2935de-bb61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: infrared Radiometer on InSight Mars Lander

9e3ace8c-b5dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 13.7m Telescope at Metsahovi Radio Observatory

9e3cbe00-b658-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A spectrometer instrument used for the ISEE atmospheric CO2 isotope observation project in Nagoya, Japan, utilizing infrared laser absorption spectroscopy to measure CO2 isotopes.

9e42ca4a-b840-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mars Science Laboratory (MSL)**, nicknamed Curiosity, is a large rover designed to explore Mars' environment for signs of past or present habitability for life. 9e4c2c80-b948-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tri-axial Fluxgate Magnetometer (FGM)** is a scientific instrument launched in 2007 as part of the THEMIS mission. It measures background magnetic fields and low-frequency fluctuations with high precision, using advanced digital technology for improved robustness and reduced mass.
9e4c2c80-b948-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tri-axial Fluxgate Magnetometer part of Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms

9e4dc61c-b6dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Swope 4K CCD is a visible-wavelength, direct-imaging camera used with the Swope 1m Telescope at Las Campanas Observatory, capable of capturing detailed images over a specific field of view and utilizing various filters.

9e8d0914-bb53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bootes Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Boecillo, Valladolid, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility and is situated at coordinates 355.29639 longitude and 41.54555 latitude.

9ea445fa-ba0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **SENSU SuperDARN Syowa South HF Radar** is a high-frequency coherent radar located at Syowa Station, Antarctica, functioning as part of the Super Dual Auroral Radar Network (SuperDARN) operated by the National Institute of Polar Research, Japan. 9eb4224a-ba6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The La Chaux-de-Fonds Observatory (Q114456619) is an astronomical observatory located in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland. It is situated at 38, Rue de la Fiaz, Les Éplatures, and has been assigned the Minor Planet Center code 575.

Starfront Observatories, Rockwood is a ground-based observatory located in Coleman County, Texas, United States. It is situated at the coordinates 31.5471° N latitude and 260.61773° E longitude.

9eeff274-b61f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bruker IFS 125HR is a high-resolution Fourier-Transform Infrared (FT-IR) spectrometer capable of resolving complex spectra into discrete lines for detailed spectral analysis, offering a broad spectral range from the far-infrared to the ultraviolet.

9ef9a756-bb3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astrognosis Observatory, United Kingdom

9efcdcf4-ba62-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Barton Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Canberra, Australia. It operates as a ground-based facility and can be found at the address Hotel Realm, 18 National Circuit, Barton.
9efcdcf4-ba62-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Barton Observatory

9f2b8a58-bb08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Flux Telescope on Ulysses

9f42b188-ba4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The "Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) Balloon 1L Ephemeris" is a virtual instrument that provides trajectory positions in various coordinate systems, contributing to the study of relativistic electron losses as part of the BARREL mission.

9f47693c-bb56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dust Flux Monitor Instrument (DFMI) is a spacecraft instrument designed to detect dust particles of varying masses using a polyvinylidene fluoride sensor and dual acoustic sensors.
9f47693c-bb56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dust Flux Monitor Instrument on Stardust

9f4dbc82-b99f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Antelope Hills Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Bennett, Colorado, United States. It operates as a ground-based observatory for stargazing and scientific research.
9f4dbc82-b99f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antelope Hills Observatory at Bennett

9f504b00-baa8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Galileo mission was an American robotic space probe designed to explore the planet Jupiter and its moons. Named after Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei, it consisted of both an orbiter and an atmospheric entry probe. Launched by Space Shuttle Atlantis in 1989, Galileo's trajectory included flybys of Venus and Earth to gain the necessary energy for its journey to Jupiter. The mission significantly contributed to our understanding of Jupiter's atmosphere, moons (especially Europa), and magnetosphere through a series of close encounters and data collection from 1995 until its intentional impact into Jupiter in 2003 to prevent contamination of the planet's moons.
9f504b00-baa8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Galileo

9f53492c-ba71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Wishing Star Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Barrington, Rhode Island. It is a ground-based facility used for stargazing and scientific research.
9f53492c-ba71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wishing Star Observatory, United States

9f5c515a-b6c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Asiago-DLR Asteroid Survey (ADAS) was an astronomical survey conducted in the early 2000s focused on discovering comets and asteroids, particularly near-Earth objects. It is credited with identifying over 200 minor planets after 2001.
9f5c515a-b6c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Asiago-DLR Asteroid Survey at Asiago Observatory, Italy

9f647d2e-b6c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Suisei Spacecraft Ephemeris is a virtual instrument that provides the positional data (ephemerides) of the Suisei spacecraft and Planet-A during its mission to study Halley's Comet.
9f647d2e-b6c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris part of Suisei Spacecraft

9f6d6f90-b8a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IAGA

9f787a46-b907-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bollwiller Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bollwiller, France. It is situated at coordinates 47.86497° N, 7.25544° E and has the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code B91.
9f787a46-b907-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bollwiller Observatory, France

9f787d6e-ba4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Cerro Tololo-LCO A**: An astronomical observatory located at the Gabriela Mistral International Dark Skies Sanctuary in Vicuña, Coquimbo Region, Chile.

9f7d0d80-bb06-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Fast Auroral SnapshoT (FAST) Explorer** is a NASA plasma physics satellite designed to investigate the plasma physics of auroral phenomena with high temporal and spatial resolution. Launched on August 21, 1996, it was part of the Small Explorer program (SMEX).
9f7d0d80-bb06-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fast Auroral SnapshoT Explorer part of Small Explorer program

9f7ef57c-b959-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AMPTE/UKS 3-D Plasma Analyzer, launched in 1984, was an instrument designed to study the three-dimensional ion distributions in various plasma environments such as plasma clouds, solar wind, and magnetosphere with high time and angular resolutions. It utilized spherical electrostatic energy analyzers to measure positive ion energy/charge distribution over a wide range of polar angles.
9f7ef57c-b959-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3-D Plasma Analyzer on UK Satellite part of AMPTE mission

9f82f814-b622-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Córdoba Observatory (CODE), also known as the Code Astronomical Observatory - Santa Fe Space Observations Center, is a museum and ground-based observatory located in Santa Fe, Argentina. 9f82f814-b622-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 35.64021N 254.026E Telescope at Code Astronomical Observatory - Santa Fe Space Observations Center

9f830ade-bc44-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **MTSU Terminated Folded Dipole and FSX-6S spectrograph** is a ground-based instrument at Middle Tennessee State University, featuring a 4-element square array of 24-foot antennas operating in the 15-30 MHz frequency range with dual polarization capabilities. It is used for radio astronomy observations and data collection.
9f830ade-bc44-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terminated Folded Dipole and FSX-6S Spectrograph at Radio Jove Observatory

9f8b5d04-bb6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fresno Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based geophysical facility in Madera County, California, dedicated to measuring and monitoring the Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since 1982 and is funded by the United States Geological Survey.
9f8b5d04-bb6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fresno Magnetic Observatory, United States

**Definition:**
"BARREL Balloon 5A was a specific high-altitude balloon mission within the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) project, designed to study electron losses from Earth's radiation belts. It operated in the stratosphere from June 25 to June 26, 2018."

9f9427b6-ba59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Energetic Proton/Electron Spectrometer DOK-2** is an instrument on the Interball Tail Probe designed to measure energetic electron and ion spectra in the Earth's magnetosphere, featuring two pairs of particle telescopes with adjustable viewing angles.
9f9427b6-ba59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Proton/Electron Spectrometer DOK-2 on Interball Tail Probe

9f94dcec-bb8f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: HALCA is a space mission by the Institute of Space and Astronautical Science (ISAS), featuring an 8-meter aperture radio telescope designed for Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) observations.
9f94dcec-bb8f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio Institute of Space and Astronautical Science 8m Highly Advanced Laboratory for Communications and Astronomy Very Long Baseline Interferometry Space Observatory Program Satellite Mission

9f988a76-b672-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) Two-Channel Tilting Photometer at Athabasca is an instrument located in Canada that measures airglow emissions at specific wavelengths every 10 minutes to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere.

9f98f154-b6f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Regensberg Observatory was a ground-based facility in Zurich, Switzerland, operational from 1931 to 1975, focused on geomagnetic measurements as part of the IAGA network.
9f98f154-b6f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Regensberg Observatory, Switzerland

9f99e07e-ba46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The V. P. Engel'gardt Astronomical Observatory, also known as the Engelhardt Observatory, is an astronomical observatory located about 20 kilometers west of Kazan, Russia. It utilizes three sets of cylindrical electrostatic analyzers with a specific angular field of view and energy resolution capabilities to study particles within an energy range from 0.2 to 15 keV/q.
9fbaa1e6-b975-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Interball Auroral Probe

9fbbd1b4-b778-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Valentia Magnetic Observatory was a ground-based magnetic observatory located in County Kerry, Ireland, operational from July 1957 to December 2016.
9fbbd1b4-b778-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Valentia Magnetic Observatory, Ireland

9fbf2eec-baeb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission Satellite 2 (MMS_2) is a spacecraft within NASA's MMS mission, designed to study magnetic reconnection in Earth’s magnetosphere using high-resolution plasma and field measurements.
9fbf2eec-baeb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft Magnetospheric Multiscale 2 part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

9fc05a56-b94c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **STEREO-B IMPACT Solar Wind Plasma Electron Analyzer (SWEA)** is an instrument on the STEREO B spacecraft designed to measure the distribution function of solar wind electrons with high spectral and angular resolution. It utilizes a hemispherical top-hat electrostatic analyzer to provide nearly full spherical coverage, allowing detailed observations during both quiet periods and Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) disturbances.
9fc05a56-b94c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: In-Situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients, Solar Wind Plasma Electron Analyzer on STEREO B part of In-Situ Measurement of Particles and CME Transients

9fcd190a-b8be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometer at the Sodankyla ground station has been operational since January 1, 1883, as part of the IAGA investigation under the WDC Kyoto observatory.
9fcd190a-b8be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sodankyla Observatory

9fcdb800-b8f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mount Cuba Astronomical Observatory's 0.6m telescope, located in North America, is an optical telescope with a 0.6-meter aperture used for astronomical observations.
9fcdb800-b8f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.6m Telescope at Mount Cuba Astronomical Observatory

9fdaf258-bb3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The TWINS-1 Energetic Neutral Atom Imager (ENA) is an instrument on the TWINS-1 spacecraft designed to capture and image energetic neutral atoms, produced by charge exchange, over a wide energy range to study magnetospheric ion fluxes.
9fdaf258-bb3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Neutral Atom Imager on TWINS-1

9fdddd2c-b83b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Brownstown Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in County Meath, Ireland. It serves as a ground-based facility for celestial observations and research.
9fdddd2c-b83b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Brownstown Observatory, Ireland

9fe17ef6-b6e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Helwan Geomagnetic Observatory (HLW), located in Cairo, Egypt, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1903 to 1960, dedicated to measuring and recording geomagnetic data.
9fe17ef6-b6e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Helwan Geomagnetic Observatory, Egypt

9feb29b8-ba76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Stanford (STFD) Geophysical Observatory, located in Ladera, San Mateo County, California, is a ground-based facility dedicated to geophysical research and observations. Established in 2009, it includes instruments such as the Stanford magnetometer and conducts studies on Earth's surface.
9feb29b8-ba76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Stanford Geophysical Observatory, United States

9fef25f6-bb6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Energetic Particle Sensor (EPS)** on GOES 14 is an instrument designed to measure energetic particles, including protons, electrons, and alpha particles, at geosynchronous orbit. It provides critical data for operational alerts, satellite design guidelines, and research into the radiation environment, helping to assess risks to satellites and astronauts as well as disruptions in navigation and communication systems.
9fef25f6-bb6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Sensor on GOES 14

9ff8b260-babf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes a magnetometer located at the station identified by IAGA as CPS, situated at the observatory in Kyoto (WDC_Kyoto) and part of the IUGONET network.
9ff8b260-babf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers part of International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics Observatory Network

9ff8c3b0-bbbc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Boundary Layer Radar (BLR)-1 at the Serpong observatory is a high-frequency radar system designed to measure wind velocity components within the atmospheric boundary layer. Operating since 1992, it features three fixed parabolic antennas and has been instrumental in various tropical atmosphere research projects like TOGA/COARE.
9ff8c3b0-bbbc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Boundary Layer Radar at Serpong Observatory

a006c99c-b6da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sutherland-LCO Aqawan A #1 observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Sutherland, Northern Cape, South Africa. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is part of the broader Sutherland Observatory complex.
a006c99c-b6da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Sutherland Observatory, South Africa

a00b62c4-b8ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pulsating Aurora Project's All-sky EMCCD Imager is an instrument located in Tromso, Norway, equipped with a 428nm monochromatic filter and the ImagEM X2 EMCCD camera (C9100-23B) produced by Hamamatsu Photonics.
a00b62c4-b8ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: All-sky Imager on Pulsating Aurora Project part of IUGONET Observatory, Norway

a00be7e8-b9c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Sozzago Astronomical Station is an astronomical observatory located in Sozzago, Novara, Piedmont, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID A12.
a00be7e8-b9c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Sozzago, Italy

a00e888a-b757-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NOT Council 2.56m Nordic Optical Telescope (NOT) is an optical telescope with a 2.56-meter aperture located at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory, situated on La Palma in the Canary Islands.
a00e888a-b757-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.56m Nordic Optical Telescope at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory

a011e77c-ba3c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Zi-Ka-Wei station, operational from 1875 to 1907, used for magnetic field measurements as part of the IAGA investigation.
a011e77c-ba3c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Zi-Ka-Wei Observatory

a0120144-ba82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Visakhapatnam Ground Observatory was a ground-based facility located in Visakhapatnam, India, operational from 1996 to 2014, and part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) observatory network. It housed magnetometer instruments from the Kyoto World Data Center for geophysical measurements until its closure on October 31, 2014.
a0120144-ba82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Visakhapatnam Observatory, India

a014e5da-b127-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The entity refers to the Roi Baudouin Observatory, a ground facility located on Earth's surface in Antarctica (latitude -70.43, longitude 24.308), which operated from January 1, 1958, to December 31, 1966. It was part of the IAGA observatory network and included instruments such as a magnetometer, with data contributions informed by specific lists and descriptions available via linked resources.
a014e5da-b127-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Roi Baudouin Observatory

a0192c78-b6ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, particularly Earth's geomagnetic field. The Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 13 specifically monitors variations in the magnetic field near the spacecraft, providing alerts for solar wind shocks or sudden impulses that impact the magnetosphere.
a0192c78-b6ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 13

a01b8f2e-b777-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plasma Science Experiment (PLS) for Galileo Orbiter is an instrument designed to study the Jovian magnetosphere by analyzing positive ions and electrons using electrostatic analyzers and magnetic mass spectrometers, providing detailed plasma dynamics data with high temporal resolution.
a01b8f2e-b777-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Science Experiment for Galileo Orbiter part of Galileo Mission

a02513f0-b94d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Thermal Ion Dynamics Experiment (TIDE)** on the Polar spacecraft is an instrument designed to study low-energy ions in Earth's magnetosphere by measuring their distribution functions within specific energy and mass ranges, contributing to our understanding of ion dynamics.
a02513f0-b94d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Thermal Ion Dynamics Experiment part of Polar

a025f554-bc1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Faraday Islands geophysical observatory is a ground-based facility located on Earth's surface at an altitude of 10 meters, situated at latitude -65.25 and longitude 295.73. It has been operational since January 1, 1957, and includes instruments such as magnetometers for geophysical observations.
a025f554-bc1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Faraday Islands Observatory

a0281b24-b6d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The SGT Observatory (L03) is an astronomical observatory located in Gaflenz, Austria. It is a ground-based facility used for celestial observations and research.
a0281b24-b6d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SGT Observatory at Gaflenz, Austria

a034a990-b854-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Giuseppe Piazzi Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Ponte in Valtellina, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
a034a990-b854-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Giuseppe Piazzi Observatory, Italy

a042b26a-b68d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operated at the IAGA station in Nizhnedevitsk from January 1, 1935, to December 31, 1940.
a042b26a-b68d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nizhnedevitsk Observatory

a046c014-b726-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Subaru Telescope** is an 8.2-meter optical-infrared telescope located at the Mauna Kea Observatory in Hawaii, operated by the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ). It features multiple focal points and a wide field of view for deep astronomical surveys.
a046c014-b726-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 8.2m Subaru Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatory

a046c6c0-ba48-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the ground observatory located at 45b, Hauptstraße, Siek, in Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, with coordinates latitude 53.6369 and longitude 10.29447.
a046c6c0-ba48-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Siek Observatory, Germany

a04cacce-b7a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition**:
Concordia Station's ASTEP (Antarctic Search for Transiting ExoPlanets) is an astronomical observatory located at Concordia Station in Antarctica. It specializes in the search and study of exoplanets using ground-based observation techniques.
a04cacce-b7a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatory at Concordia Station, Antarctica

a06c4d56-bb00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Polonia Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in San Pedro de Atacama, Chile. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
a06c4d56-bb00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Polonia Observatory, Chile

a08c19aa-baac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Angra do Heroísmo was a ground-based observatory in Portugal, operational from 1957 to 1970, equipped with magnetometers for geomagnetic measurements.
a08c19aa-baac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Angra do Heroísmo Observatory, Portugal

a0a3555c-bb38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Christchurch Ionosonde** is a ground-based radar instrument located near Christchurch, New Zealand, used for investigating the ionosphere with a frequency range typically between 1.0 and 22.0 MHz.
a0a3555c-bb38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar part of World Data Centre for Solar-Terrestrial Science, Kyoto - Christchurch

a0ae153a-b5a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Medium Electron Sensor (MEA)** on the CRRES satellite is an instrument designed to measure temporal, spectral, and directional variations of electron fluxes in the energy range of 100-2000 KeV. It is part of the Medium Energy Electron Spectrometer and features a magnet assembly, collimators, and solid-state detectors to ensure precise measurements with varying acceptance angles based on energy levels.
a0ae153a-b5a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Medium Electron Sensor on CRRES

a0bf82d4-b72f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **OSIRIS-REx Propulsion Subsystem (PROP):** The propulsion system onboard the OSIRIS-REx spacecraft, consisting of 28 thrusters designed for various maneuvers, including precise operations like the touch-and-go sample acquisition at asteroid Bennu.
a0bf82d4-b72f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: OSIRIS-REx Propulsion Subsystem on OSIRIS-REx

a0c35ed8-bb74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The "Spirit" rover (Mars Exploration Rover A or MER-2) was one of two rovers launched by NASA to Mars in 2003. It operated on the Martian surface from 2004 to 2010, conducting scientific investigations to determine if life ever arose on Mars and characterize its climate and geology.
a0c35ed8-bb74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Exploration Rover - Spirit

a0c4501a-b9a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ellinogermaniki Agogi Observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Pallini, Greece. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with the code C68.
a0c4501a-b9a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ellinogermaniki Agogi Observatory, Greece

a0ea7dae-b707-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 0.65m telescope at the Ondřejov Observatory is an optical telescope with a 65 cm aperture, located in Europe and operated by the Astronomical Institute of the Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic.
a0ea7dae-b707-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 0.65m Telescope at Ondřejov Observatory

a0f0a02a-ba37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Toby Point Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Narragansett, Rhode Island. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
a0f0a02a-ba37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Toby Point Observatory, United States

a0f0c72e-b62e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Exploration Rover Spirit (MER 2) Mössbauer Spectrometer was an instrument used to analyze iron-bearing minerals in Martian rocks and soil, providing insights into their chemical composition and oxidation states through the measurement of the Mössbauer effect. This helped scientists understand Mars' geological history and assess its past habitability for microbial life.
a0f0c72e-b62e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Moessbauer Spectrometer on Mars Exploration Rover Spirit

a0fb4fae-b8ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High Altitude Water Cherenkov (HAWC) Gamma-Ray Observatory is a ground-based observatory located in North America that specializes in detecting high-energy gamma rays through the use of water Cherenkov detectors.
a0fb4fae-b8ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Altitude Water Cherenkov Gamma-Ray Observatory

a0fe401e-b770-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Capricornus Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Csókakő, Hungary. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
a0fe401e-b770-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Capricornus Observatory, Hungary

a101bc1e-b769-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Po Leung Kuk Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Tuen Mun District, Hong Kong. It operates as a ground-based facility at the PLK Leung Chow Shun Kan Primary School and focuses on astronomical research and education.
a101bc1e-b769-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Po Leung Kuk Observatory, China

a10cffc4-b64d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition**:
The Vector Magnetometer on Magsat (VMAG) was an instrument consisting of three orthogonally aligned fluxgate sensors that measured magnetic field vectors at a rate of 16 times per second, with a resolution better than 1 nT and an absolute accuracy of better than 6 nT rms.
a10cffc4-b64d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vector Magnetometer on Magsat

a11387d2-ba61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pioneer Venus Orbiter Turbulence Experiment (OTUR) was an instrument on the Pioneer Venus Orbiter spacecraft that used radio signals to measure turbulence and ionospheric electron density variations in the Venus atmosphere.
a11387d2-ba61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Turbulence Experiment on Pioneer Venus Orbiter

a12068ee-bab6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Hinode is a Japanese space telescope launched in 2006 to conduct high-resolution observations of the Sun at optical, EUV, and X-ray wavelengths, focusing on solar magnetic fields and coronal heating.
a12068ee-bab6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: x-ray and optical and EUV Hinode on Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency Solar Mission

a121d58e-b80a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The magnetometers at Fürstenfeldbruck (FUR) are part of the IAGA investigation and have been operational since January 1, 1939.
a121d58e-b80a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fürstenfeldbruck Observatory

a121e7a6-b8bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Badalona Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Badalona, Catalonia, Spain, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
a121e7a6-b8bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Badalona Observatory, Spain

a126ca66-b81f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The specific instance described here was operational from January 1, 1957, to December 31, 1959, and located at the Espanola observatory as part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) investigation.
a126ca66-b81f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Espanola Observatory

a12825e0-b8b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/F17 Operational Linescan System (OLS) is an instrument onboard the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program's F17 satellite that measures visible and infrared wavelengths to provide global cloud cover imagery at resolutions of 2.7 km and 0.56 km since its start date on November 4, 2006.
a12825e0-b8b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Operational Linescan System part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

a12a8d40-bac2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing of the Electron density by Relaxation) instrument on Cluster 2/FM8 (Tango) is designed to measure electron density through active sounding and record natural wave emissions in the high-frequency range from 4--80 KHz. It is part of the Wave Experiment Consortium (WEC) on Cluster and operates with a sensitive double-sphere antenna, transmitter, receiver, and digital spectrum analyzer.
a12a8d40-bac2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waves of High Frequency and Sounder for Probing Electron Density by Relaxation part of Cluster Mission

a1339f88-b7f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A photometer aboard the DMSP-F19 satellite, the SSUSI (Special Sensor Ultraviolet Spectrographic Imager) is designed to observe vertical profiles of Extreme and Far UV radiation from Earth's limb, particularly in the spectral range of 80-170 nm.
a1339f88-b7f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Ultraviolet Spectrographic Imager part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

a135e656-b71e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Moquegua Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Cambrune, Carumas District, Province of Mariscal Nieto, Moquegua, Peru. It is a ground-based facility situated at coordinates -70.67844 longitude and -16.828157 latitude.
a135e656-b71e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Astronomico de Moquegua, Peru

a1457398-b6ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Van Allen Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Riverside, Washington County, Iowa. It is a ground-based facility primarily used for astronomical observations and research.
a1457398-b6ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Van Allen Observatory

a161f602-b7c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Washington Observatory was a ground-based facility in the District of Columbia, USA, that operated from January 1, 1841, to December 31, 1894. It primarily housed magnetometers and contributed to IAGA's global magnetic field measurements.
a161f602-b7c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Washington Observatory

a172783e-b8b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the Cerro Armazones Observatory (CAO) in San Pedro de Atacama, Chile, a ground-based observatory that operated until January 1, 2012. It was located at specific coordinates in the Antofagasta Region of South America.
a172783e-b8b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: San Pedro de Atacama Observatory, Chile

a1752b6c-bb93-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetic Field Instrument (MAM) on Equator-S is a magnetometer consisting of two three-axis flux-gate sensors, designed to measure magnetic fields with high precision and reduce spacecraft interference. It operates at sampling rates of 128 or 64 vectors per second, with a resolution of 16 bits and adjustable measurement ranges from 250 to 64000 nT.
a1752b6c-bb93-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetic Field Instrument on Equator-S

a178a51e-b718-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SuperDARN King Salmon HF radar is a high-frequency coherent radar located in King Salmon, Alaska, part of the Super Dual Auroral Radar Network (SuperDARN). It is operated by the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT) and is used for studying ionospheric plasma convection as well as thermospheric and mesospheric research.
a178a51e-b718-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: HF Radar at Super Dual Auroral Radar Network Observatory

a17cefa4-b7e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Ion Mass Spectrometer (IMS) on the Giotto spacecraft was an instrument designed to measure ion abundances and velocity distributions in different energy ranges during its mission. It consisted of two main subsystems: the High Energy Range Spectrometer (HERS) for hot, turbulent ions outside the contact surface, and the High Intensity Spectrometer (HIS) for low-energy ions inside the contact surface.
a17cefa4-b7e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Mass Spectrometer on Giotto Spacecraft

a182304c-b679-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Meudon SID is an antenna located at the Observatoire de Paris, designed to detect Sudden Ionospheric Disturbances (SID). It has been operational since January 1, 2017.
a182304c-b679-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sudden Ionospheric Disturbances Antenna at Meudon Observatory

a184119c-b768-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: "El Condor Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Córdoba, Argentina."
a184119c-b768-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: El Condor Observatory, Argentina

a188b2b6-b992-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT) is a precision-controlled device used to expose and clean fresh surfaces of Martian rocks for scientific analysis. It acts as both a geologic hammer and a brush, enabling other instruments to study the physical properties of the rock samples.
a188b2b6-b992-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rock Abrasion Tool on Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity

a18e7292-b865-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Huygens was an atmospheric entry probe that successfully landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005 as part of the Cassini-Huygens mission. Built and operated by the European Space Agency (ESA) and launched by NASA, it conducted detailed observations of Titan’s atmosphere and surface during its descent.
a18e7292-b865-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Atmospheric Entry Probe on Cassini–Huygens Mission

a19401e4-bb2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Hurbanovo Magnetic Observatory**: A ground-based magnetic observatory located in Hurbanovo, Slovakia, established in 1900. It is known for its geomagnetic measurements and contributions to scientific research.
a19401e4-bb2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hurbanovo Magnetic Observatory, Slovakia

a19faeca-b5b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Bacau Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Bacau, Romania, with the Minor Planet Center code L57.
a19faeca-b5b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bacau Observatory, Romania

a1ad5aa6-b895-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RCC Richey-Chretien Telescope is a 1-meter telescope situated at the Institute of Astrophysics in Dushanbe, Tajikistan. It is located on Mt. Sanglok and operated by the Institute of Astrophysics of Tadzhikistan.
a1ad5aa6-b895-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1m Richey-Chretien Telescope at Dushanbe Observatory, Tajikistan

a1b5d1b2-b7e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **GOES 9 Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer** is a scientific instrument onboard the GOES 9 satellite designed to measure magnetic fields with high precision and sensitivity, using three-axis stabilization for accurate data collection.
a1b5d1b2-b7e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 9

a1be9fbc-b87e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **ARCAD-3 Project:** A Franco-Soviet space mission launched aboard the AUREOL-3 satellite on September 21, 1981, designed to study ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling through detailed measurements of particles, waves, and fields in a quasi-polar orbit.
a1be9fbc-b87e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ARCAD-3 part of AUREOL-3

a1bf0780-b677-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The All-sky TV camera (ATV) at Syowa Station, Antarctica, is a high-sensitivity panchromatic imager used for recording all-sky auroral images at 30 frames per second. It employs advanced light-receiving elements like a night viewer and CCD analog camera to capture detailed auroral activity from an optical dark room.
a1bf0780-b677-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: All-sky Television Camera part of Auroral Observation at Syowa Station

a1c1bffa-b967-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Galați Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Galați, Romania, part of the "Razvan Angheluta" Natural Sciences Museum Complex. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and public outreach.
a1c1bffa-b967-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Galați Observatory, Romania

a1cd8eb8-b83e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Turin Astrophysical Observatory (also known as Pino Torinese) is an astronomical observatory located in the town of Pino Torinese near Turin, Italy. It was founded in 1759 and has been a significant site for asteroid discoveries.
a1cd8eb8-b83e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Turin Astrophysical Observatory, Italy

a1ce5738-b949-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA station in Chesterfield Inlet (CFI) since 1933, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of geophysical research and monitoring.
a1ce5738-b949-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Chesterfield Inlet Observatory

a1da1198-b5c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The millimeter-wave spectroscopic radiometer at Rio Gallegos is an instrument equipped with a superconducting receiver, located in Argentina. It monitors variations of the vertical ozone distribution in the stratosphere and mesosphere.
a1da1198-b5c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter-Wave Spectroscopic Radiometer at Rio Gallegos Observatory, Argentina

a1f74708-ba55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **NOB_RH** observatory is a space facility located in the Heliosphere near Earth, primarily designed for astronomical and solar observations. It includes the NORH instrument as part of its equipment.
a1f74708-ba55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Northern Observatory for IDAR (Ionospheric and Atmospheric Remote sounding) on Heliosphere.NearEarth

a1f9de2a-b5e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **CPMN fluxgate magnetometer** is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument used to measure magnetic fields, installed at the Onagawa Observatory in Japan.
a1f9de2a-b5e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Canada-France Magnetic Observing Network

a1fe897e-ba7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Zyryanka of 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network** is a ground facility located in Verkhnekolymsky Ulus, Sakha Republic, Russia. It is part of the ISEE magnetometer network and includes a fluxgate instrument for measuring magnetic fields on Earth's surface.
a1fe897e-ba7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Zyryanka Observatory, Russia

a21b6484-b77c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Summit (SUM) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Greenland, specifically at the coordinates 72.3°N and 321.7°W, dedicated to geophysical research and observations since May 2016.
a21b6484-b77c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Summit Geophysical Observatory, Greenland

a224016a-b5c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Nonndorf Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Nonndorf, Lower Austria. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
a224016a-b5c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nonndorf Observatory

a226b1e2-ba1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ibis Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Manhattan, Kansas, USA, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
a226b1e2-ba1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ibis Observatory

a22db630-b8d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Induction Magnetometer at Istok (near Norilsk) is part of the ISEE Magnetometer Data project and measures variations in the 3-D vector geomagnetic field with a sampling rate of 64 Hz.
a22db630-b8d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Induction Magnetometer part of International Synthetic Expertise Platform for Observing Systems

a233e998-b89c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at Piura (PIU) is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, specifically located at the Piura observatory within the WDC Kyoto network.
a233e998-b89c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Piura Observatory

a2348024-b8ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ken-Ting Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Hengchun, Pingtung County, Taiwan, established in 2000. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
a2348024-b8ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ken-Ting Observatory

a2384c20-bb87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An **Electrostatic Analyzer**, specifically the Solar Wind Electron, Proton, and Alpha Monitor (SWEPAM) on ACE, is an instrument that measures solar wind plasma electron and ion fluxes as functions of direction and energy, providing detailed real-time data for space weather monitoring. It utilizes separate sensors with electrostatic analyzers to measure particle energies from 0.26 KeV to 36 KeV for ions and 1 eV to 1350 eV for electrons.
a2384c20-bb87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser Solar Wind Electron, Proton and Alpha Monitor on Advanced Composition Explorer

a23cbcf6-b9c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter (KPLO), also known as Danuri, is South Korea's first lunar mission, launched to conduct scientific investigations and demonstrate technologies for future space exploration.
a23cbcf6-b9c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter

a24adbdc-b6e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Cherkizovo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Cherkizovo, Pushkinsky District, Moscow Oblast, Russia. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
a24adbdc-b6e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cherkizovo Observatory

a25c66a4-b6d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dededo Magnetometer, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, is an instrument at the Dededo (GUA) Geophysical Observatory that measures magnetic fields, operational since January 1, 2007.
a25c66a4-b6d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dededo Observatory

a26ef360-b835-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Brorfelde Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Brorfelde near Holbæk, Denmark. It was formerly run by the Copenhagen University and is known for housing the Brorfelde Schmidt Telescope.
a26ef360-b835-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Brorfelde Observatory, Denmark

a27086cc-b8bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **MOTH (Magneto Optical filters at Two Heights)** instrument was a multispectral imager operational only in 2003, used at the JSPO observatory for magneto optical imaging.
a27086cc-b8bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Multispectral Imager part of MOTH Magneto Optical filters at Two Heights

a273cbcc-bbd4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Asociación Astronómica de Cartagena is an astronomical observatory located in Canteras, Cartagena, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and public outreach.
a273cbcc-bbd4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Canteras, Spain

a284cfb2-b896-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Arecibo Observatory was an astronomical observatory in Puerto Rico known for its large radio telescope, which from 1963 to 2016 was the world's largest single-aperture antenna.
a284cfb2-b896-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: National Astronomy and Ionosphere Center 305m Radio Telescope at Arecibo Observatory, Puerto Rico

a28faeda-b8f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU radio beacon receiver (GRBR) station at Manado is an observatory located in Indonesia that measures ionospheric disturbances related to middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes.
a28faeda-b8f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU Radio Beacon Receiver on GRBR Station at Manado Observatory, Indonesia

a29096b4-bb14-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Astrocamp Manciano Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Manciano, Italy. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the study and observation of celestial bodies and phenomena.
a29096b4-bb14-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astrocamp Manciano Observatory

a2964d34-bb0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer** is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Lagos, Nigeria, designed to measure the Earth's magnetic field as part of the MAGDAS observation network.
a2964d34-bb0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System Observation Network

a299618c-b933-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Observatorio de Vega del Codorno is a ground-based observatory located in Cuenca, Castile-La Mancha, Spain. It operates at coordinates 40.41729° N, 358.08932° E and serves as an astronomical research facility.
a299618c-b933-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatory at Vega del Codorno, Spain

a29cfe2c-baf1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Henrietta Swope Telescope is a 1-meter optical telescope located at the Las Campanas Observatory in South America, operated by the Carnegie Institution for Science.
a29cfe2c-baf1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Henrietta Swope Telescope at Las Campanas Observatory

a2a4fe5c-b73f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA)/NASA Suzaku (ASTRO-EII) X-ray Satellite Mission was a collaborative space mission focused on observing the universe in gamma rays.
a2a4fe5c-b73f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Suzaku X-ray Satellite part of Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency/NASA Suzaku (ASTRO-EII) X-ray Satellite Mission

a2a50536-bb41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission Satellite 1 (MMS-1) is a NASA spacecraft designed to study magnetic reconnection in Earth's magnetosphere using highly sensitive instruments. It is part of a constellation of four identical satellites launched in 2015.
a2a50536-bb41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.5m Magnetospheric Multiscale 1 part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

a2ae4132-b628-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Kerguelen Magnetometer** is an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields, located at the Kerguelen observatory. It was operational from January 1, 1875, to December 31, 1988, as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
a2ae4132-b628-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kerguelen Observatory, Antarctica

a2b0a912-b6c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Perpignan Magnetometer was an instrument used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field, operational from January 1, 1885, to December 31, 1910, located at the IAGA observatory in Perpignan.
a2b0a912-b6c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Perpignan Observatory

a2b5711c-bbca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Reynolds Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at the Potsdam Municipal Airport in Potsdam, New York. It is recognized by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with the ID H91 and primarily operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
a2b5711c-bbca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Reynolds Observatory at Potsdam

a2b99888-b6f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Magnetometers at Charcot (CTX) were instruments used to measure Earth's magnetic field at a station identified by the IAGA code CTX, operational from January 1, 1957, to December 31, 1958.
a2b99888-b6f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iugonet Observatory

a2c3617c-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
LiShan Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Lintong District of Xi'an, Shaanxi, China. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
a2c3617c-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lintong Observatory, China

a2c40b94-b8ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Double Star 1 Ephemeris refers to the positional data of the Double Star 1 spacecraft, providing essential information for tracking and analyzing its orbit as part of scientific investigations.
a2c40b94-b8ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris part of Double Star 1

a2c9eb04-b776-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Joan Roget Observatory (C17) is an astronomical observatory located in Ager, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility and is part of the Parc Astronòmic Montsec.
a2c9eb04-b776-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Joan Roget Observatory at Parc Astronòmic Montsec, Spain

a2ca8684-bbba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Okinawa ionospheric radar facility is a ground-based observatory located in Ogimi, Kunigami, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan, operated by the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT) for studying the Earth's ionosphere.
a2ca8684-bbba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Okinawa ionospheric radar facility at Okinawa Observatory, Japan

a2de13c2-b668-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Voyager 1** is a space probe launched by NASA in 1977 to study the outer Solar System and is currently the furthest spacecraft from Earth.
a2de13c2-b668-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Camera and Multi-Object Spectrometer on Hubble Space Telescope

a2e1869a-b6b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP_5D3-F18 Positions refer to the precise locations of the DMSP_5D3-F18 spacecraft recorded in different coordinate systems. This data set includes ephemeris information, which details the orbital positions of the spacecraft over time for scientific and operational use.
a2e1869a-b6b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: DMSP 5D-3 F18 Positions part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program Observatory

a2e20970-b855-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Texas at San Antonio Kleberg Advanced Microscopy Center's Hitachi S 5500 is a high-resolution, dual Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) and Scanning Transmission Electron Microscope (STEM) capable of achieving sub-nanometer resolution for detailed surface and bulk material analysis.
a2e20970-b855-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Field-Emission Scanning Electron Microscope at University of Texas at San Antonio Kleberg Advanced Microscopy Center

a2e5285c-ba72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The ROMAP (Rosetta Magnetometer and Plasma Monitor) was an instrument onboard the Rosetta Philae Lander designed to measure magnetic fields, ions, and electrons in its environment. It included a fluxgate magnetometer, electrostatic analyzer, Faraday cup, and pressure sensors.
a2e5285c-ba72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer and Plasma Monitor on Rosetta Philae Lander

a2e583be-bb59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Solar Wind Experiment (ESP) onboard the Suisei spacecraft was an instrument designed to study solar wind particles. It featured two sensors—one for electrons and one for positive ions—each equipped with a collimator, electrostatic analyzer, and micro-channel plate detector, covering an energy range from 30 eV to about 15.8 keV.
a2e583be-bb59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Wind Experiment on Suisei

a2ec842e-b97a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The World Data Center for Sunspot Index (SDIC) is a ground-based observatory located in Sanhe, Tianjia'an District, Huainan, Anhui, China. It specializes in monitoring and cataloging data related to sunspots.
a2ec842e-b97a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: World Data Center for Sunspot Index at Sanhe, China

a2f2f1c2-ba12-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **AGO P3 Photometer** is an instrument used to measure light intensity and other optical properties, located at the AGO P3 ground station. It is part of the ICESTAR observatory network.
a2f2f1c2-ba12-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Photometer part of ICESTAR Investigation

a30fac52-b6e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The European Space Agency (ESA) 3.5m Herschel Space Observatory Mission is an infrared space telescope with a 3.5-meter aperture, designed to explore the universe's far-infrared and submillimeter wavelengths.
a30fac52-b6e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared European Space Agency 3.5m Herschel Space Observatory Mission

a3127374-b870-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Woolston Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in North Cadbury, Somerset, England, used for ground-based observations.
a3127374-b870-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Woolston Observatory, United Kingdom

a32620ec-b7a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Libbiano Astronomical Observatory is a ground-based observatory located in Peccioli, Italy. It is used for astronomical research and observations.
a32620ec-b7a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Libbiano Astronomical Observatory, Italy

a3328d50-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Osuna, Sevilla, Andalusia, Spain known as the Osuna Observatory or Osuna.
a3328d50-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Osuna Observatory, Spain

a332dd40-b798-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/F17 SSULI is an imaging spectrometer onboard the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program's F17 satellite that observes Extreme and Far UV radiation from Earth’s limb to measure electron density, ion, and neutral densities.
