a332dd40-b798-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Ultraviolet Spectrographic Imager on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

a3364d1e-b977-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ulysses Energetic Particle Composition (EPAC) Experiment on the Ulysses spacecraft is an investigation aimed at studying the composition, energy spectra, and spatial distribution of energetic particles in interplanetary space using four identical telescopes.
a3364d1e-b977-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument part of Ulysses Energetic Particle Composition Experiment on Ulysses

a33fc134-b81c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 17 Command and Service Module Metric (Mapping) Camera was used to capture high-quality black and white photographs of the lunar surface with precise geometric accuracy from lunar orbit, aiding in selenodetic/cartographic control and supporting other photographic experiments.
a33fc134-b81c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Metric Camera on Apollo 17 Command and Service Module

a3400ee0-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Green Island Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Geçitkale, Northern Cyprus, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
a3400ee0-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Green Island Observatory, Northern Cyprus

a3439992-b6de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 3 FIELDS Suite, Digital Signal Processor (DSP) is a component of the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission that processes signals from various instruments on the spacecraft, performing analog conditioning, A/D conversion, and digital processing to maximize scientific data collection under limited telemetry.
a3439992-b6de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digital Signal Processor part of MMS 3 Fields Suite

a346e79c-b70a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AVON instrument is a type of antenna located in Thailand that measures magnetic components in the Very Low Frequency (VLF) range, originating from lightning discharges.
a346e79c-b70a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VLF Antenna at Tohoku University Radio Observatory

a35468ec-b730-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Olive Farm Observatory (J83) is an astronomical observatory located in Coupe Green, South Ribble, Lancashire, England. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
a35468ec-b730-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Olive Farm Observatory at Coupe Green, South Ribble, Lancashire, United Kingdom

a35e6726-b711-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific magnetometer mentioned operated from 1907 to 1931 at the Seddin observatory, part of the IAGA investigation, collecting data on geomagnetic activity.
a35e6726-b711-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy

a362bb06-b7f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Giotto was a European Space Agency (ESA) robotic spacecraft mission designed to study Halley's Comet during its 1986 perihelion passage, becoming the first spacecraft to make close-up observations of a comet.
a362bb06-b7f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Giotto Comet Probe

a366d490-b9cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Boca Raton Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Florida Atlantic University in Boca Raton, Florida. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and education.
a366d490-b9cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Boca Raton Observatory, United States

a3683178-b8f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Active Spacecraft Potential Control (ASPOC)** on Cluster 2/FM5 is an instrument that regulates the electric potential of a spacecraft relative to its surrounding plasma by emitting positively charged indium ions, thereby minimizing disturbances in measurements caused by high floating potentials. It operates using liquid metal ion emitters and has various modes for controlling emission current and maintaining optimal performance.
a3683178-b8f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Active Spacecraft Potential Control part of Cluster 2

a36d7eaa-b5ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Contern Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Contern, Luxembourg, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial bodies.
a36d7eaa-b5ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Contern Observatory

a36f9d9e-b8a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lake of the Woods Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Lake of the Woods, Orange County, Virginia, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
a36f9d9e-b8a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lake of the Woods Observatory

a379dae2-b8d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Near-Earth Asteroid Tracking (NEAT) facility at Palomar Observatory is an astronomical observatory located on Palomar Mountain in California, dedicated to discovering and tracking near-Earth asteroids.
a379dae2-b8d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near-Earth Asteroid Tracking on Samuel Oschin Telescope at Palomar Observatory, United States

a37ea4be-b76b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory is a space mission dedicated to observing gamma-ray bursts and other high-energy phenomena in the universe. It provides valuable data for astrophysical research, particularly in understanding the origins and properties of these energetic events.
a37ea4be-b76b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma-ray NASA Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory

a3842dc6-b90f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Remoto Bosque Alegre Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in the Santa María Department of Córdoba, Argentina. It is a ground-based facility situated at specific coordinates (-64.5502 longitude, -31.598171 latitude) within South America.
a3842dc6-b90f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bosque Alegre Observatory, Argentina

a388382c-ba35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The magnetometer at Arequipa is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field and has been operational since January 1958. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network and is identified by the IAGA code ARE.
a388382c-ba35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at IUGONET Observatory

a38a75f8-bc22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AMPTE_IRM Ephemeris is a dataset providing the spacecraft positions of the AMPTE (Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers) IRM (Ion Release Module) in various coordinate systems.
a38a75f8-bc22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: AMPTE IRM Ephemeris part of CDPP-AMDA Observatory

a39da842-b931-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Promiod Observatory (Osservatorio Dalai Lama di Promiod)**: An astronomical observatory located in Noussan, Aosta Valley, Italy. It is situated at coordinates 45.78553° N, 7.6033° E and is known for its ground-based observations.
a39da842-b931-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Osservatorio Dalai Lama di Promiod at Promiod Observatory, Italy

a3afd48e-bc8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Beine-Nauroy Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Beine-Nauroy, France. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial bodies.
a3afd48e-bc8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Beine-Nauroy Observatory, France

a3b54a20-b66a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Osservatorio Rivalta is an astronomical observatory located in Gazzola, Piacenza, Emilia-Romagna, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
a3b54a20-b66a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rivalta Observatory, Italy

a3c27810-b630-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Terre Haute Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Vigo County, Indiana, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
a3c27810-b630-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terre Haute Observatory, United States

a3c87678-bb55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Parker Solar Probe FIELDS instrument's V4 voltage probe is a component of the FIELDS suite that measures electric fields and radio/plasma waves as part of the mission to study the Sun's outer atmosphere. It operates in extreme heat conditions, reaching over 1300°C at closest approach to the Sun.
a3c87678-bb55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: FIELDS instrument on Parker Solar Probe

a3cfde82-bb09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Espanola Geomagnetic Observatory (EPN) is a ground facility in New Mexico, United States, that operated from 1957 to 1959 for monitoring geomagnetic activity.
a3cfde82-bb09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Espanola Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

a3db45b0-b942-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plasma Electron and Current Experiment (PEACE) on Double Star 1 is an electrostatic analyzer that measures the number and speed of thermal electrons to infer the positive potential of the spacecraft. This data is used as input for the operation of ASPOC, aiding in understanding plasma electron behavior around Earth's magnetosphere.
a3db45b0-b942-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer part of Double Star 1

a3e3a0ee-b928-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Fort Chipewyan Geomagnetic Observatory (FCP), located in Alberta, Canada, is a ground-based facility that monitors and studies geomagnetic activity on Earth's surface.
a3e3a0ee-b928-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Fort Chipewyan, Canada

a3e7ca74-bb9f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "DSS-42" is a ground-based observatory, also known as the Deep Space Station 42.
a3e7ca74-bb9f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep Space Station 42

a3ecdffc-b70b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The MMS 2 FIELDS Suite, Search Coil Magnetometer (SCM), specifically measures 3-axis AC magnetic fields up to 6 kHz and is employed to study plasma waves and turbulent dissipation in space environments.
a3ecdffc-b70b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Magnetometer part of MMS 2 FIELDS Suite

a3f16f18-b701-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: "Janus A (also known as JNSA) is a spacecraft facility involved in astronomical observations and data collection."
a3f16f18-b701-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: JANUS A

a3f35e42-bb96-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pulsating Aurora Project's All-sky EMCCD imager is an instrument located at Tromsø, Norway, designed to capture all-sky images using a 777nm monochromatic filter and features the ImagEM X2 EMCCD camera (C9100-23B) produced by Hamamatsu Photonics.
a3f35e42-bb96-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 777nm All-sky EMCCD Imager part of Pulsating Aurora Project

a40ae8b2-b805-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RoSaMund Observatory - DSC in Rio Hurtado is a ground-based observatory located in the Coquimbo Region of Chile, specifically at Camino del Observatorio, Río Hurtado.
a40ae8b2-b805-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: RoSaMund Observatory - DSC, Rio Hurtado, Chile

a41468a4-baaf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IRTF RC2 Photometer ("RC2") is an infrared instrument used for astronomical observations, featuring a single-element InSb detector sensitive to wavelengths from 1 to 5 microns. It utilizes discrete filters and a circular variable filter (CVF) segment, with cooling systems using solid nitrogen for the detector and liquid nitrogen for the filters.
a41468a4-baaf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3m2 RC2 on Infrared Telescope Facility at Maunakea Observatory

a4223aa6-b8e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Akulivik (AKUL) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in the Qikiqtaaluk Region, Nunavut, Canada. It started operations on October 21, 2014, and includes instruments such as a magnetometer for geophysical measurements.
a4223aa6-b8e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Akulivik Geophysical Observatory, Canada

a425bb84-b6bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Solar Wind Analyser - Electron Analyser System (SWA-EAS) is an instrument designed to measure solar wind electrons in the heliocentric distance range between approximately 0.3 AU and 1 AU, enabling the study of electron velocity distribution functions to understand solar wind dynamics.
a425bb84-b6bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Wind Analyser - Electron Analyser System on Solar Orbiter

a425e7c4-b84c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Magnetometers at Port Moresby (PMG)" is a magnetic field instrument that operated from 1957 to 1999 as part of the IAGA investigation at the WDC Kyoto Observatory.
a425e7c4-b84c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy

a42b5584-b7d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dar Es Salaam Geomagnetic Observatory (DRS) was a ground-based facility located in Tanzania, Africa, operational from 1896 to 1903. It focused on geomagnetic observations and was part of the International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics' network.
a42b5584-b7d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dar Es Salaam Geomagnetic Observatory

a42bfad0-b872-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Plessisville Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Plessisville, Quebec, Canada.
a42bfad0-b872-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plessisville Observatory, Canada

a440acc6-b7c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Valle del Sol Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in the Region of Murcia, Spain. It is situated at coordinates 37.84982° N, -1.0335999° W and has been assigned the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code J72.
a440acc6-b7c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Valle del Sol Observatory, Spain

a448287a-b68a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Glyndon Geophysical Observatory**, located in Stockwood, Minnesota, USA, is a ground-based facility known for its magnetometer and geophysical research activities.
a448287a-b68a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Glyndon Geophysical Observatory, United States

a44fc8e4-b8c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover's Hazard Avoidance Cameras (Hazcams) are stereo camera pairs mounted on the front and rear of the rover, designed to detect obstacles in its path and support navigation by providing near-field imaging.
a44fc8e4-b8c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hazard Avoidance Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

a465d3e8-b70c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SKA-3 instrument on the Interball Auroral Probe is a set of particle detectors designed to measure the distribution functions of electrons and ions (H+, He+, O+) within an energy range of 30 - 500 keV. It includes two electrostatic toroidal analyzers for low-energy particles and two time-of-flight spectrometers for high-energy measurements.
a465d3e8-b70c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: part of Interball Auroral Probe

a46b889a-b803-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cotos de Monterrey, Venturada** is a ground-based observatory located in Venturada, Community of Madrid, Spain. It serves as an astronomical facility for observations and research.
a46b889a-b803-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cotos de Monterrey Observatory, Spain

a479f2bc-b791-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astronomical Observatory of Capodimonte is a ground-based observatory in Naples, Italy, dedicated to research in astronomy, astrophysics, and space science. It is part of the National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF) and includes a museum of astronomical instruments.
a479f2bc-b791-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory of Capodimonte, Italy

a48fc1ce-bbb4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operational from 1925 to 1932 at the Mikolow observatory, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IAGA investigation.
a48fc1ce-bbb4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mikolow Observatory

a493b276-bacd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Göttingen-1 observatory is a ground facility located in Herberhausen, Lower Saxony, Germany, operating since January 1957, and equipped with a magnetometer to monitor geomagnetic activity. It is part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network.
a493b276-bacd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Göttingen Observatory, Germany

a497e1d0-ba45-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Observatory Hurtado** is an astronomical observatory located in El Sauce, Río Hurtado, within the Coquimbo Region of Chile. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
a497e1d0-ba45-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatory Hurtado at El Sauce, Chile

a4a0fbb6-b67c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lunar Prospector Spacecraft Engineering Instrument encompasses key subsystems—attitude control (ACS), command and data handling (CDH), and communications (COM)—that supported the science missions of the Lunar Prospector by ensuring accurate operation, without directly acquiring scientific data.
a4a0fbb6-b67c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Prospector Spacecraft Engineering Instrument on Lunar Prospector

a4b4e618-bb67-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tsingtao/Qingdao Magnetometer** was a magnetometer located at the Tsingtao observatory in China, operational from January 1906 to December 31, 1936. It was part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network for magnetic field measurements.
a4b4e618-bb67-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tsingtao Observatory

a4b69990-ba27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ROP KKN Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Ubolratana, Khon Kaen Province, Thailand (16.76068° N, 102.63094° E). It is situated on the Asian continent and serves as an observation point for various celestial studies.
a4b69990-ba27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: KKU Optical and Radio Observatories at Nong Rua, Khon Kaen University (ROPKKNU)

a4be2c1c-b6aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The King Edward Point Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, operated by the British Geological Survey since 1906. It houses a magnetometer identified by the IAGA code KPT.
a4be2c1c-b6aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at King Edward Point Magnetic Observatory

a4c0f024-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Apollo 15 Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP) was a suite of scientific instruments deployed on the Moon's surface during the Apollo 15 mission. It included various experiments such as a seismometer, magnetometer, and solar wind spectrometer, powered by a radioisotope thermoelectric generator, to collect and transmit data about the lunar environment back to Earth.
a4c0f024-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Apollo 15 Lunar Surface Experiments Package on Apollo 15

a4c13eb4-b756-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 4.5cm aperture solar full-disk H-alpha imaging telescope at Mitaka, NAOJ is an instrument used for continuous observation of the Sun's chromosphere in full disk view, located at the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ) in Mitaka.
a4c13eb4-b756-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: H-alpha Imager part of National Astronomical Observatory of Japan Solar Chromosphere Investigation

a4caddce-bb3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CLPS Task Order 19D Lunar PlanetVac (LPV) is a pneumatic sampling system designed for lunar surface missions, consisting of a sampling head, transfer tubes, and a capture system to collect regolith samples. It can be integrated into lander footpads or deployed via a boom, with flexible routing for sample transfer.
a4caddce-bb3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar PlanetVac on CLPS Task Order 19D

a4d624e6-b78d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Lyford (LYFD) Magnetometer Station is a ground facility located in Lyford, Texas, USA, that functions as part of the Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain (McMAC), used for geomagnetic research.
a4d624e6-b78d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain Lyford Station, United States

a4d94efc-b87b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration's (NASA) Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER) is a spacecraft designed to study the interior composition of neutron stars by observing their X-ray emissions.
a4d94efc-b87b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray National Aeronautics and Space Administration's Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer on International Space Station

a4db99ae-b92b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Hamburg Observatory** was an astronomical facility located in Hamburg, Germany, operational from 1885 until the end of 1896.
a4db99ae-b92b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hamburg Observatory, Germany

a4ddf036-bbc0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Reflectance Experiment Laboratory (RELAB) Nicolet 740 Fourier-Transform infrared spectrometer is a specialized instrument used for measuring reflectance in the near and mid-infrared ranges, equipped with various detectors and an environmental chamber to simulate Mars-like conditions. It has been decommissioned.
a4ddf036-bbc0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared NASA Reflectance Experiment Laboratory Nicolet 740 Fourier-Transform Spectrometer

a4e2b88c-b954-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Kitt Peak-Bok Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Schuk Toak District of Pima County, Arizona, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
a4e2b88c-b954-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kitt Peak-Bok Observatory, United States

a4e59648-bb24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes magnetometers located at the Rostov On Don (ROD) observatory in Kyoto, part of the IUGONET network, which are used for magnetic field measurements and adhere to IAGA standards.
a4e59648-bb24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at World Data Center for Geomagnetism Kyoto Observatory

a4eeb32c-b74b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Plasma Wave System (PWS)** on Voyager 1 is an instrument designed to measure electron-density profiles and wave-particle interactions in the magnetospheres of Jupiter and Saturn. It includes a step-frequency receiver and a low-frequency waveform receiver, operating within a frequency range from 10 Hz to 56 kHz.
a4eeb32c-b74b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver part of Voyager 1

a4ef0514-b838-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Glyn Marsh Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Douglas, on the Isle of Man, dedicated to ground-based observations.
a4ef0514-b838-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Glyn Marsh Observatory

a4ef2202-bb84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Bisei Spaceguard Center (BSGC)** is an astronomical observatory in Bisei-chō, Ibara, Okayama Prefecture, Japan, dedicated to tracking asteroids and space debris through its Bisei Asteroid Tracking Telescope for Rapid Survey (BATTeRS) program.
a4ef2202-bb84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bisei Astronomical Observatory, Japan

a4f23afa-b71a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is the **Ionospheric Station at Jeju Island, South Korea**, identified by URSI-code JJ433. It is a ground facility equipped with an advanced Digisonde that evaluates various properties of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere, located in Gwideok-ri, Hallim, Jeju, South Korea.
a4f23afa-b71a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at GIRO Observatory, South Korea

a50a8dfe-bafc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU radio beacon receiver (GRBR) station at Kosrae is an observatory located in the Federated States of Micronesia, designed to measure ionospheric disturbances related to middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes.
a50a8dfe-bafc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU radio beacon receiver on GRBR station at Kosrae, Federated States of Micronesia

a50afd64-b6a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Alouette1 Positions" dataset provides the spatial coordinates of the Alouette 1 spacecraft, recorded in multiple reference frames.
a50afd64-b6a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Alouette1 Positions part of Alouette1

a5109522-b9a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ny-Ålesund NIPR Observatory, also known as the Rabben station, is a ground-based research facility in Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard, Norway, operated by the National Institute of Polar Research (NIPR) since 1991. It focuses on polar studies and includes instruments for various observations.
a5109522-b9a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ny-Ålesund National Institute of Polar Research Observatory, Norway

a510b342-b772-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Healy Geomagnetic Observatory (HEA) was a ground-based facility located in Healy, Alaska, operational from 1957 to 1958, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements.
a510b342-b772-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Healy Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

a51485ea-b767-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital receiver used for measuring ionospheric total electron content (TEC) from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite signals, utilizing GNU Radio software and Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) hardware.
a51485ea-b767-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver at Bahir Dar Observatory, Ethiopia

a51fd218-b818-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS MacQuarie Island station is a ground-based facility located in Huon Valley, Australia (Oceania) at coordinates -54.5 latitude and 158.96 longitude, part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network that monitors geomagnetic activity.
a51fd218-b818-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at MacQuarie Island Observatory, Australia

a527dde4-b6df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Isaac Roberts' Observatory was a private astronomical observatory established by British astronomer Isaac Roberts in Crowborough, Sussex. It operated from 1890 until his death in 1904 and is notable for its inclusion in the Minor Planet Center's list of observatory codes with the designation 001.
a527dde4-b6df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Isaac Roberts' Observatory at Crowborough, United Kingdom

a534e4ee-b6b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **LANL1997 Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer** is an instrument designed to measure the three-dimensional energy/charge distributions of ions and electrons in Earth's magnetosphere, utilizing a single electrostatic analyzer coupled with channel electron multipliers for high sensitivity and moderate resolution.
a534e4ee-b6b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Los Alamos National Laboratory Observatory

a5485f2c-b69b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Budakeszi Geomagnetic Observatory (BUZ)** is a ground-based facility located in Budakeszi, Hungary. It operated from 1949 to 1955 and was dedicated to geomagnetic measurements using magnetometers.
a5485f2c-b69b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Budakeszi Geomagnetic Observatory, Hungary

a548b2d6-b8eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sunflower Observatory in Santa Fe is a ground-based astronomical facility located at 4, Sunflower Drive, Santa Fe County, New Mexico. It operates from the coordinates 35.70918° N, 253.98617° E in North America.
a548b2d6-b8eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sunflower Observatory at Santa Fe, United States

a565ea4e-ba54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Electric Field Double Probe (EDP)** on MMS3 is an instrument combining the Spin-plane Double Probe (SDP) and Axial Double Probe (ADP), designed to measure three-dimensional electric fields with high accuracy over a wide frequency range. It is part of the Magnetospheric Multiscale mission's FIELDS instrument suite, utilizing biased spherical probes on wire booms in the spin plane and cylindrical probes on stiff booms along the spacecraft axis.
a565ea4e-ba54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electric Field Double Probe part of Magnetospheric Multiscale mission

a56654c8-bb1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mataro Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Mataró, Catalonia, Spain. It is designated by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with the code A06 and is used for ground-based astronomical observations.
a56654c8-bb1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mataro Observatory, Spain

a569d66a-b7eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Solar Orbiter Ephemeris" is a calculated dataset providing the precise position and trajectory information for the Solar Orbiter spacecraft, derived from SPICE kernels at IRAP (Institut de Recherche en Astrophysique et Planétologie).
a569d66a-b7eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Orbiter Ephemeris part of Solar Orbiter Mission

a56e2516-b5c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Monte Argentario Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Grosseto, Tuscany, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
a56e2516-b5c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Monte Argentario Observatory

a56e5436-bb1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1A X-ray Instrument (XRI)** is a scintillation detector designed to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It operates with an energy response from 10 keV to 10 MeV, utilizing a NaI crystal scintillator and photomultiplier tube to detect and analyze X-ray signals, providing insights into electron energies within the Earth's radiation belts.
a56e5436-bb1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

a56e8a56-b643-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Ulugh Beg Astronomical Institute (UBAI) 1.5m telescope AZT-22 at Maidanak Astronomical Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Uzbekistan, featuring a 1.5-meter Cassegrain reflector telescope used for various astrophysical observations and research.
a56e8a56-b643-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.5m Telescope at Maidanak Astronomical Observatory

a581e9fc-b8f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Štefánik's Observatory**, located in Prague, Czech Republic, is an astronomical observatory founded in 1928 and named after Slovak astronomer Milan Rastislav Štefánik. It specializes in the popularization of astronomy and related natural sciences.
a581e9fc-b8f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Štefánik's Observatory, Czechia

a5862d6c-b95b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Research Foundation of South Africa 1.9m Radcliffe Telescope is an optical telescope located at the South African Astronomical Observatory (SAAO) in Sutherland, Northern Cape Province, South Africa. It has a primary mirror diameter of 1.9 meters and operates within the visible light spectrum for astronomical observations.
a5862d6c-b95b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.9m Radcliffe Telescope at South African Astronomical Observatory

a58736e2-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Herchmer Geomagnetic Observatory (HCR), located in Manitoba, Canada, is a ground-based facility that has been operating since 1973 to monitor geomagnetic activity on Earth's surface.
a58736e2-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Herchmer Geomagnetic Observatory

a5898e2c-baa9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **NAOC-Korla (LW-1)** is a ground observatory located in Shinigha, Korla City, Bayingolin, Xinjiang, China. It operates under the National Astronomical Observatories of China (NAOC) and is situated at approximately 41.55266° N latitude and 86.23504° E longitude on the continent of Asia.
a5898e2c-baa9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: LAMOST Wide field Survey Telescope at National Astronomical Observatories of China Observatory, Xinglong, China

a58c9a02-b6cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Darwin Station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located at the Darwin Golf Course in Malak, Darwin, Australia, operating as part of the ICSWSE/CPMN network to monitor geomagnetic activity.
a58c9a02-b6cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Darwin Observatory, Australia

a58deb6c-b670-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Einarin Observatory** is a ground-based observatory located in Uusikylä, Tampere, Finland. It is situated at coordinates 61.49452° N, 23.8283° E and serves as an astronomical facility within Europe.
a58deb6c-b670-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Einarin Observatory, Tampere, Finland

a5903ffc-b8f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Entity:**
Quantum Computing

**Definition:**
Quantum computing is a type of computation that uses quantum-mechanical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement, to potentially solve certain problems much more efficiently than classical computers. It operates on the principles of quantum bits, or qubits, which can represent both 0 and 1 simultaneously, unlike classical bits.
a5903ffc-b8f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.term:
Entity:
aperture: 8.1m
is part of: Gemini Observatory South

a5944402-b8ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Tivoli Observatory (MPC code 194) is an astronomical observatory located in Namibia, Africa. It is situated at coordinates 18.0094° E longitude and -23.46159° S latitude, specifically in the Khomas region near Tivoli Gardens.
a5944402-b8ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tivoli Observatory, Namibia

a59b8334-b7a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tennant Creek Ionosonde was an instrument located near Tennant Creek, Northern Territory, Australia, operational from May to November 1985. It utilized 16 mm film to record data and was part of the ground observatory facilities in Tennant Creek.
a59b8334-b7a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar at Tennant Creek Observatory, Australia

a5b4cd4e-b9cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IAA-AI Atacama Observatory is an astronomical facility located in San Pedro de Atacama, Chile. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
a5b4cd4e-b9cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Atacama Observatory, Chile

a5baeb6c-b63e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, particularly Earth's magnetic field. The Honolulu.1-2-3 Magnetometer, part of the IAGA observatory in Honolulu, has been operational since 1902 and contributes to geomagnetic research and monitoring.
a5baeb6c-b63e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Honolulu Observatory

a5c6f442-b8ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Oukaimeden Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in the Atlas Mountains near Marrakech, Morocco. It is situated at an altitude that provides optimal conditions for celestial observations.
a5c6f442-b8ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Oukaimeden Observatory, Morocco

a5d2a29e-b836-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RISH Radiosonde and Rawinsonde system at Bandung, Indonesia, measures vertical atmospheric profiles including pressure, temperature, humidity, and wind from the troposphere to lower stratosphere using Vaisala radiosondes and TOTEX balloons.
a5d2a29e-b836-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radiosonde and Rawinsonde part of RISH Observatory, Indonesia

a5e52640-b5d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Breslau Observatory was an astronomical observatory located in Wrocław, Poland, operational from 1852 until its closure at the end of 1895.
a5e52640-b5d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Breslau Observatory

a5f19d8a-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EMN Mokolo Station** is a ground-based magnetometer facility in Za-Gabaca, Nigeria, part of the EMN magnetometer network, located at 10.44 latitude and 13.48 longitude on Earth's surface.
a5f19d8a-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mokolo Observatory, Nigeria

a5f55c44-b7ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rosetta Plasma Consortium (RPC) Ion and Electron Sensor (IES) is an instrument aboard the Rosetta Orbiter that measured the flux of ions and electrons as a function of energy and direction, primarily for studying the solar wind and the environment around comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko.
a5f55c44-b7ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion and Electron Sensor on Rosetta Orbiter

a613f6de-b676-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apatity Geomagnetic Observatory (APA) is a ground-based facility located in Apatity Urban Okrug, Murmansk Oblast, Russia, dedicated to geomagnetic observations and has been operational since 1973.
a613f6de-b676-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Apatity Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

a6142494-b863-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Swarthmore Newark Neutron Monitor is a ground facility located on Earth's surface, specifically in the Bartol Research Institute at Swarthmore College and Newark. It is part of a broader network of neutron monitors used for observing and studying cosmic rays.
a6142494-b863-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutron Monitor at Bartol Observatory

a6170c22-b8f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Entity Definition:**
The **International GNSS Service (IGS)** is a global network of satellite tracking stations, data centers, and analysis centers that collects, archives, and distributes high-quality GPS data to support Earth science research, multidisciplinary applications, and education. It provides standardized data products for monitoring Earth's surface deformations, rotation, and atmospheric changes, among other scientific endeavors.
a6170c22-b8f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: International Global Navigation Satellite System Service

a6173a1c-b6a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IAGA: BEU Magnetometer was a scientific instrument used to measure magnetic fields at the Beuthen observatory from 1899 to 1932 as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigations.
a6173a1c-b6a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Beuthen Observatory

a61c898e-b9b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Halstead Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Princeton, New Jersey, operated as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations.
a61c898e-b9b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Princeton Observatory

a620f8fe-bb65-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Otto Observatory, located in Tatuí, Brazil, is a ground-based astronomical facility dedicated to celestial observation and research. It is situated at coordinates -23.39303 latitude and 312.21833 longitude in the Southeast Region of Brazil.
a620f8fe-bb65-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Otto Observatory at Tatuí, Brazil

a6259a92-b8e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) Kevo station in Finland is a ground-based facility operated by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research (ISEE), Nagoya University, designed to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions. It collaborates with the Finnish Meteorological Institute and features an all-sky imager as part of its instrumentation.
a6259a92-b8e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Kevo Station, Finland

a627689a-b5f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Portable High-Speed Occultation Telescope GJON Camera," also known as the Photdoc Camera, is a high-speed photometric camera featuring a 512x1024 frame-transfer CCD, with only half of the device receptive to light. It is a standard PhotonMax camera manufactured by Princeton Instruments.
a627689a-b5f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Portable High-Speed Occultation Telescope GJON Camera on 2.4m Magdalena Ridge Observatory

a62eebb4-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Conway Observatory (code: H43) is an astronomical observatory located in Conway, Arkansas, USA, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial bodies.
a62eebb4-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Conway Observatory, United States

a6336aae-bbd1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Angmakssalik is a ground-based observatory located in Tasiilaq, Sermersooq, Greenland, established in 1933 for conducting geomagnetic measurements as part of the IAGA network.
a6336aae-bbd1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IAGA Observatory

a637bf18-b759-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetic Electron Spectrometers were an instrument onboard the OV1-19 satellite, designed to measure the energy and distribution of electrons in space.
a637bf18-b759-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetic Electron Spectrometer part of OV1-19

a63ee3d4-bbcc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: La Specola is a historic astronomical observatory in Padua, Italy, established in 1767 within a 14th-century tower that was once part of a medieval castle.
a63ee3d4-bbcc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 14th-century tower Telescope at Astronomical Observatory of Padova, Italy

a643707c-b7b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMN magnetometer network in Okinawa, Japan is a ground-based facility located at Matsuda, Ginoza, Kunigami, dedicated to measuring magnetic fields. It includes instruments such as fluxgate magnetometers and is situated at coordinates 26.5° N latitude and 128.0° E longitude on the continent of Asia.
a643707c-b7b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Earth.Surfacecode Observatory, Japan

a6463b8c-b859-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Mars 96**: A failed Russian Mars mission launched in 1996 to study the planet's evolution and physics, which crashed back to Earth due to a launch vehicle failure.
a6463b8c-b859-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars 96 part of failed Russian Mars mission

a64758ae-b751-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISON-Blagoveschensk observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Plodopitomnik, Blagoveshchensk, Amur Oblast, Russia. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
a64758ae-b751-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ISON-Blagoveschensk Observatory, Russia

a6553c96-b72c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Regensberg Magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at the IAGA observatory in Regensberg, operational from 1931-01-01 until 1975-12-31.
a6553c96-b72c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Regensberg Observatory

a65a6b14-b63f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Toolik Lake Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAGs, used for measuring magnetic fields starting from April 23, 2015.
a65a6b14-b63f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Toolik Lake Observatory

a6681e54-b67f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kvistaberg Observatory was a Swedish astronomical observatory operated by Uppsala University, now serving as a museum since 2009. It is located between the cities of Uppsala and Stockholm in Upplands-Bro Municipality.
a6681e54-b67f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kvistaberg Observatory, Sweden

a675f852-ba09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Mass Spectrometer for Planetary Exploration (MASPEX) is a mass spectrometer on the Europa Clipper spacecraft designed to analyze gases in Europa's atmosphere and possible plumes, studying the moon's subsurface ocean chemistry and surface interactions.
a675f852-ba09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer for Planetary Exploration on Europa Clipper

a679403e-b5db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer used in the IUGONET observation network located at Weipa, Australia.
a679403e-b5db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometer Network

a68981fe-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Iowa State University Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel is a research facility operated by the Department of Aerospace Engineering at Iowa State University, historically used for studying boundary layer conditions on various planetary bodies. It is known for its contributions to understanding wind processes and has been directed by notable researchers such as James D. Iversen and Ronald Greeley.
a68981fe-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel at Iowa State University

a691beae-b6d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Sumoto, Hyogo Prefecture, Japan, known as the Sumoto Observatory.
a691beae-b6d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sumoto Observatory, Japan

a6938100-b712-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The RPC-ICA is an instrument aboard the Rosetta spacecraft that measured the three-dimensional distribution of positive ions using electrostatic and magnetic filters, with an energy range of 25 - 40 keV and a wide angular field of view.
a6938100-b712-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rosetta Plasma Consortium Ion Composition Analyser on Rosetta Orbiter

a69a9986-bb4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Tirunelveli station with the IAGA identifier TIR, part of the WDC Kyoto observatory network, used for magnetic field measurements.
a69a9986-bb4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Tirunelveli

a6a0a596-b867-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF antenna is a Very Low Frequency / Extremely Low Frequency crossed loop antenna with a 13.9m tower located in Kagoshima, Japan, designed to detect electromagnetic signals primarily between 2-8 kHz.
a6a0a596-b867-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Low Frequency/Extremely Low Frequency crossed loop antenna with a 13.9m tower at Iugonet Observatory, Japan

a6a2aaa6-b972-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex (CDSCC) is one of three facilities in NASA's Deep Space Network (DSN), providing continuous communication with spacecraft exploring the solar system. Located in Tidbinbilla, Australia, it includes several antennas and a Signal Processing Center to handle various types of data for uplink and downlink operations.
a6a2aaa6-b972-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep Space Station on Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex, Australia

a6baba1a-b5da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fabry-Perot Interferometer (FPI) on Dynamics Explorer 2 was a high-resolution remote sensing instrument designed to measure thermospheric temperature, meridional wind, and density of specific metastable atoms by performing wavelength analysis on light detected from thermospheric emissions.
a6baba1a-b5da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fabry-Perot Interferometer on Dynamics Explorer 2

a6c36c68-b671-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Spatial Infrared Imaging Telescope (SPIRIT III) was an instrument aboard the Midcourse Space Experiment, featuring a 33cm clear-aperture off-axis telescope with both high spatial resolution radiometer and Fourier transform spectrometer for infrared observations.
a6c36c68-b671-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spatial Infrared Imaging Telescope on Midcourse Space Experiment

a6c4629e-bb5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Eusebio Geomagnetic Observatory (EUS), located in Brazil, was a ground-based facility operational from 1975 to 1977 that conducted geomagnetic measurements using magnetometers.
a6c4629e-bb5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eusebio Geomagnetic Observatory, Brazil

a6c8d1a8-b680-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA station MID (Midway), operational until December 31, 2002.
a6c8d1a8-b680-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Midway Observatory

a6d530c6-b8b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the IAGA Observatory in Singapore, a ground-based facility that operated from January 1, 1840, to December 31, 1847. It was located at Prudential Tower, Cecil Street, and included magnetometers for scientific observations.
a6d530c6-b8b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Singapore Observatory, Singapore

a6d6ba52-b856-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Arizona's Spacewatch project, also known as LPL/Spacewatch II, is an astronomical survey focused on the study of minor planets and comets. It operates from a ground observatory located in Pima County, Arizona.
a6d6ba52-b856-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: LPL Spacewatch II at University of Arizona Observatory, United States

a6d896fa-bbae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ULU Observatory in Caselle Landi is a ground-based astronomical facility located at Via Po, Gerre alte, in Lodi, Italy. It provides valuable observational data and is situated at coordinates 45.09803° N, 9.7975° E.
a6d896fa-bbae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ULU Observatory, Caselle Landi, Italy

a6dbbe2c-b710-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High Energy Proton Detector (HEPD) is an instrument onboard the Double Star 2 spacecraft designed to detect energetic protons in both the Earth's magnetosphere and solar wind.
a6dbbe2c-b710-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Energy Proton Detector on Double Star 2

a6dddec0-ba3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a magnetometer instrument located at the Camp Douglas station with the IAGA identifier CDS, which is part of the WDC Kyoto observatory and used for magnetic field measurements.
a6dddec0-ba3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of World Data Center for Geomagnetism Kyoto investigation

a6deec5a-b61b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The North.Pole.7 Magnetometer was an instrument used to measure magnetic field variations at the IAGA observatory in the North Pole from January 1, 1957, to December 31, 1959.
a6deec5a-b61b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole 7 Observatory

a6e989b6-b6e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Hemingford Abbots Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Cambridgeshire, England, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
a6e989b6-b6e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hemingford Abbots Observatory, United Kingdom

a6fdab12-b95f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Whole Earth Blazar Telescope (WEBT)** is a collaborative global network of telescopes designed for continuous monitoring and study of blazars in the optical waveband. It aims to provide comprehensive data on these highly variable active galactic nuclei by coordinating observations from multiple locations around the world.
a6fdab12-b95f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Whole Earth Blazar Telescope

a703cba2-b93f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nordic Optical Telescope (NOT) is an astronomical observatory located at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory on La Palma in the Canary Islands, Spain. It is known for its ground-based telescopes and facilities dedicated to astronomy research.
a703cba2-b93f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Roque de los Muchachos Observatory, Spain

a703d6c8-b94a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BAS A84 Geomagnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Augsburg, operational since January 1999, which monitors geomagnetic activity at approximately 84.0 degrees Geographic Latitude and 336.13 degrees East Longitude.
a703d6c8-b94a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Augsburg Observatory

a7089be0-ba85-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **PENGUIn**: A collaborative research project led by Virginia Tech, University of Michigan, and the National Institute of Aerospace, operating low-powered magnetometers in Antarctica to study geospace and upper atmosphere dynamics along the 40-degree magnetic meridian.
a7089be0-ba85-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at PENGUIn Observatory, Antarctica

a7096bde-b7af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The YALO consortium 1m Yale-AURA-Lisbon-Ohio State (YALO) Telescope is an optical telescope with a 1.0m aperture located at the Cerro Tololo International Observatory (CTIO) in South America. It is operated by a consortium of institutions including Yale University, AURA, Lisbon, and Ohio State.
a7096bde-b7af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.0m optical YALO consortium Yale-AURA-Lisbon-Ohio State Telescope at Cerro Tololo International Observatory

a7097d6c-b9fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The HIA (Hot Ion Analyzer) on Double Star 1 is an instrument designed to measure the distribution function of ions in the magnetosphere and solar wind, providing data every four seconds during each spin period.
a7097d6c-b9fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hot Ion Analyzer on Double Star 1

a71bdda6-b73b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Toyoharanew Magnetometer** was an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields at the IAGA-identified station TOH, operational from January 1, 1932, to December 31, 1944.
a71bdda6-b73b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Toyohara Observatory

a7336078-b639-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA/Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) Galaxy Evolution Explorer (GALEX) satellite mission was a space-based observatory designed to study the evolution of galaxies by detecting ultraviolet light.
a7336078-b639-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Galaxy Evolution Explorer part of NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory Galaxy Evolution Explorer Satellite Mission

a736a204-baf5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Texas, Austin 0.8m Telescope is an optical telescope located at the McDonald Observatory in North America, with an aperture of 0.8 meters.
a736a204-baf5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.8m optical Telescope at McDonald Observatory

a736ff3a-b936-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: SAC-C is an international Earth observation satellite launched in 2000 to remotely sense vegetation, wetlands, and ecosystems with a spatial resolution of 1 km.
a736ff3a-b936-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible and near-infrared Satellite of Scientific Applications-C

a7381d12-b7cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CARISMA Magnetometer at the Contwoyto Canadian ground station is an instrument used for measuring magnetic field variations, contributing to geomagnetic research and monitoring as part of the Canadian Array for Realtime Investigations of Magnetic Activity (CARISMA) network.
a7381d12-b7cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of CARISMA investigation

a7383e3c-b714-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ceilometer CT25K at Kototabang, Indonesia, is an instrument operated since April 6, 2002, designed to measure cloud heights and vertical visibilities using pulsed diode laser LIDAR technology. It detects up to three cloud layers simultaneously and provides continuous status information for internal monitoring.
a7383e3c-b714-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Light detection and ranging Ceilometer part of Coupling Processes in the Equatorial Atmosphere investigation

a740a3e4-b947-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Surlari Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility in Romania equipped with magnetometers to measure and monitor the Earth's magnetic field.
a740a3e4-b947-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Surlari Magnetic Observatory, Romania

a754d920-b6b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 9-channel ELF/VLF receiver at Syowa Station, Antarctica, is an instrument used for monitoring and studying the upper atmosphere's physics through observations of extremely low frequency (ELF) and very low frequency (VLF) radio waves. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network associated with WDC Kyoto.
a754d920-b6b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 9-channel Extremely Low Frequency and Very Low Frequency Receiver part of Upper Atmosphere Physics Monitoring Observation at Syowa Station, Antarctica

a7633bb0-ba24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Holsteinsborg, also known as Qeqqata in Greenland, was a ground-based observatory active from 1853 to 1965, focused on geomagnetic measurements.
a7633bb0-ba24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Holsteinsborg Observatory, Greenland

a7660006-b7aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hudson Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Hudson, New Hampshire, USA. It serves as a ground-based facility for studying celestial phenomena from Earth.
a7660006-b7aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hudson Observatory, United States

a76c2060-b8a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTIs) at Gakona, Alaska, is a ground-based observatory developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research to study upper atmospheric dynamics through airglow emissions. It collaborates with the Geophysical Institute of the University of Alaska Fairbanks and the University of Florida.
a76c2060-b8a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Gakona Observatory, United States

a7734a6c-b7d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Helios 1 Ephemeris** is an instrument used to calculate the spacecraft's position data for the Helios 1 mission using SPICE kernels provided by NASA. It provides detailed positional information and is part of the CNES Observatory CDPP-AMDA system.
a7734a6c-b7d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of CNES Observatory

a77f8c3e-bb9b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fast Plasma Investigation (FPI) on the MMS1 spacecraft is an instrument that measures the velocity-space distribution of electrons and ions within specific energy ranges using multiple spectrometers. It provides high time resolution data crucial for studying plasma dynamics in space.
a77f8c3e-bb9b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

a7802ee4-b6fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1.54-m Cassegrain/Coude reflector is a telescope with a 1.54-meter aperture, located at the Mount Bigelow (Catalina) Station in Arizona, United States, operational since October 1965.
a7802ee4-b6fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.54m Cassegrain/Coude Telescope at Mount Bigelow Observatory, United States

a7884f30-b822-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1T X-ray Instrument (XRI)** is a scintillation detector used to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It operates with an energy response from 10 keV to 10 MeV, featuring different data binning modes for varying time and energy resolutions.
a7884f30-b822-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

a78a53f6-ba5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Global Oscillation at Low Frequencies (GOLF)** instrument on the SOHO spacecraft performs continuous velocity oscillation and magnetic field measurements of the full solar disk with high sensitivity using resonant scattering and Zeeman effect techniques.
a78a53f6-ba5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Global Oscillation at Low Frequencies on SOHO

a7926ed8-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS-B Search Coil Magnetometer (SCM) is an instrument designed to measure three-dimensional changes in magnetic flux within a frequency range of 0.1 Hz to 4 kHz, extendable to 8 kHz under specific conditions, mounted on a retractable boom extending from the spacecraft.
a7926ed8-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission

a79ac334-b847-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Barentsburg Geomagnetic Observatory (BBG) was a ground-based facility in Norway that operated from 1957 to 1959, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements as part of the IAGA observatory network.
a79ac334-b847-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Barentsburg Geomagnetic Observatory, Norway

a79fbf9e-b86d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Osenbach Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Westhalten, France, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects. It operates under the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID 630 and is situated at coordinates 47.992991° N, 7.2367° E.
a79fbf9e-b86d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Osenbach Observatory, France

a7a0086e-b5f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ulugh Beg Astronomical Institute (UBAI) 1.5m Telescope, also known as AZT-22, is located at the Maidanak Astronomical Observatory in Asia and operates within the optical waveband.
a7a0086e-b5f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.5m Ulugh Beg Astronomical Institute Telescope at Maidanak Astronomical Observatory, Uzbekistan

a7a48d58-bae3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **South African Astronomical Observatory (SAAO) Sutherland site** is an astronomical research facility located in Sutherland, South Africa. It includes various telescopes and observational instruments, such as the 1.4m Infrared Survey Facility (IRSF), dedicated to studying celestial bodies through infrared technology.
a7a48d58-bae3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.4m Infrared Survey Facility at South African Astronomical Observatory, South Africa

a7a70b96-b79b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and/or direction of magnetic fields, particularly the Earth's magnetic field. The magnetometers at Lu-Kia-Pang (LUK) are part of the WDC Kyoto observatory network and provide data for geomagnetic studies.
a7a70b96-b79b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lu-Kia-Pang Observatory

a7aa1868-bb88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Variability of Solar Irradiance and Gravity Oscillations (VIRGO) on SOHO is an investigation focused on studying the variability and oscillations in solar irradiance, utilizing active cavity radiometers, sun photometers, and a high-precision luminosity oscillation imager.
a7aa1868-bb88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near ultraviolet, visible, and near infrared The Variability of Solar Irradiance and Gravity Oscillations on SOHO

a7adf2ba-b905-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Open-Source Neutral Mass Spectrometer on AE-E** was a double-focusing, Mattauch-Herzog magnetic deflection mass spectrometer designed to study the chemical, dynamic, and energetic processes in the thermosphere by measuring neutral atmospheric constituents with masses from 1 to 48 atomic mass units.
a7adf2ba-b905-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer part of AE-E

a7b0d318-bb6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: BARREL Balloon 3C was a component of the BARREL mission, launched on August 17, 2015, and concluded on August 18, 2015. It operated in Earth's stratosphere to study the precipitation of relativistic electrons from radiation belts using instruments like NaI scintillators and magnetometers.
a7b0d318-bb6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses on BARREL part of NASA Living with a Star Geospace Mission of Opportunity

a7ba48a4-b94f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Digital Wave Processor (DWP)** is a key component of the Wave Experiment Consortium onboard the Cluster-1 spacecraft, responsible for coordinating instrument operations, data compression, and implementing diagnostic techniques like particle correlation to study wave-particle interactions in various plasma environments.
a7ba48a4-b94f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digital Wave Processor part of Cluster-1

a7c8952c-b8a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **GNU radio beacon receiver (GRBR) station at Pohnpei** is an observatory in Micronesia designed to monitor ionospheric disturbances related to atmospheric coupling processes, equipped with a GNU radio beacon receiver.
a7c8952c-b8a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU Radio Beacon Receiver Station at Pohnpei, Federated States of Micronesia

a7e4aa9c-bbd7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lightning and Airglow Camera (LAC)** is an instrument onboard the Akatsuki spacecraft designed to detect lightning flashes and map airglow emissions on Venus's nightside, aiming to resolve debates about atmospheric lightning and study global circulation patterns.
a7e4aa9c-bbd7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lightning and Airglow Camera on Akatsuki

a7f3929e-bb02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Longyearbyen Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAGs, used to measure magnetic fields.
a7f3929e-bb02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Longyearbyen Observatory, Antarctica

a7f8200a-b901-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 17 Command and Service Module Far-Ultraviolet Spectrometer (FUVS) was an instrument on the Apollo 17 mission designed to measure radiation intensity in the far-ultraviolet range, primarily to study the lunar atmosphere's composition from orbit.
a7f8200a-b901-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Far-Ultraviolet Spectrometer on Apollo 17 Command and Service Module

a7fa96d2-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lübeck Observatory was a public ground-based facility in Germany, operational from 1885 to 1893, primarily known for its magnetometer instrument.
a7fa96d2-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lübeck Observatory, Germany

a8053196-b7bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Taipei/Taihoku Magnetometer** was an instrument used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field at a station in Taipei (identified as TAP by IAGA) from 1919 to 1967. It was part of the observatory associated with the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA).
a8053196-b7bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Taipei Observatory

a805a2e6-b63d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Energetic Particle and Plasma Spectrometer (EPPS): Fast Imaging Plasma Spectrometer (FIPS) is an imaging mass spectrometer that combines a wide-angle electrostatic deflection system with a linear time-of-flight system, designed to analyze ions within specific energy/charge bands.
a805a2e6-b63d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fast Imaging Plasma Spectrometer part of MESSENGER

a822882e-ba21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Virginia 40-inch Baker Schmidt Astrometric Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Fan Mountain Observatory in North America, with an aperture of 1.02 meters.
a822882e-ba21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.02m University of Virginia Baker Schmidt Astrometric Telescope at Fan Mountain Observatory

a822cd56-b964-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Seeberg Observatory, also known as the Gotha Observatory, was a German astronomical observatory located on Seeberg hill near Gotha, Thuringia, which operated from 1787 to 1857 and focused on astrometry, geodetic, meteorological observations, and time tracking.
a822cd56-b964-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Seeberg Observatory, Germany

a824c46a-b70e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF Istok (near Norilsk) station in Dudinka, Russia, is a ground-based observatory equipped with a crossed loop antenna for studying very low and extremely low frequency radio waves. It collaborates with the Institute of Solar-Terrestrial Physics to conduct research on these phenomena.
a824c46a-b70e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VLF/ELF crossed loop antenna at VLF/ELF Istok Station (near Norilsk), Russia

a8342318-b7dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kitt Peak National Observatory (KPNO) is a major astronomical observatory located on Kitt Peak in the Arizona-Sonoran Desert, housing over twenty optical and radio telescopes.
a8342318-b7dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.5m WIYN Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory, United States

a835068a-ba7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The SOLIS Vector Spectromagnetograph (VSM) is an advanced telescope designed for solar observation, capable of measuring magnetic fields and velocities in the Sun's photosphere and chromosphere using specific spectral lines. It provides full-disk magnetograms and other data products to study solar activity.
a835068a-ba7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.5m Vector Spectromagnetograph at SOLIS Observatory

a843e7e4-b66b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **HelioSwarm Observatory** is a space mission comprising nine spacecraft designed to study turbulence in the solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field through simultaneous multipoint measurements, set to launch on January 1, 2028.
a843e7e4-b66b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: HelioSwarm Observatory

a84b770e-b790-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is a VLF/ELF (Very Low Frequency/Extremely Low Frequency) crossed loop antenna located in Nyrola, Finland. It operates with 10 turns and has a height of 5 meters, capable of sampling up to 100kHz with peak sensitivity at 8kHz, designed to measure magnetic field variations along NS (North-South) and EW (East-West) directions.
a84b770e-b790-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VLF/ELF Crossed Loop Antenna at Nyrola Observatory

a8615356-b9ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS On Board Moments (MOM) system is an instrument used for calculating electron and ion moments, including number density, energy flux, and momentum flux tensor, from ESA and SST data on board the THEMIS spacecraft. It provides crucial plasma parameters such as velocity, pressure, and temperature in various coordinate systems, essential for studying space weather and magnetospheric dynamics.
a8615356-b9ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: On Board Moments part of THEMIS

a87525bc-bb7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Plasma Energy Analyzer (PM1)** was an instrument aboard the Vega 1 spacecraft designed to study the energy distribution of solar and cometary particles using six detectors, including ion and electron analyzers.
a87525bc-bb7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Energy Analyzer on Vega 1

a882913c-b74d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The KM-7 instrument on the Interball Auroral Probe is designed primarily to measure cold electron temperatures in the plasmasphere. It also measures potential differences between a floating spherical probe and the spacecraft, allowing for evaluations of the spacecraft's potential and determinations of ambient ion density under specific conditions.
a882913c-b74d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Thermal Plasma Measurements on Interball Auroral Probe

a883f930-b89e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The ISON-Terskol Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Elbrus District of Kabardino-Balkaria, Russia. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
a883f930-b89e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ISON-Terskol Observatory, Russia

a88ec07c-b678-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AKEBONO RDM (Radiation Monitor) instrument is part of the AKEBONO satellite and includes a High energy Particle Monitor (HPM) for measuring fluxes of electrons, protons, and alpha particles across specified energy ranges.
a88ec07c-b678-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radiation Dose Monitor part of AKEBONO

a89155a4-bb77-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Powell Observatory:** An astronomical observatory near Louisburg in Miami County, Kansas, featuring large telescopes and open for public viewing, private use by Astronomical Society of Kansas City members, and research projects.
a89155a4-bb77-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Powell Observatory

a89f003a-b8bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Mount Kent Observatory**: An astronomical observatory near Toowoomba, Queensland, Australia, owned by the University of Southern Queensland and equipped for exoplanet research and stellar astrophysics.
a89f003a-b8bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mount Kent Observatory, Australia

a8a84b46-b736-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The "Duo Ursi de Saltu" is a ground-based observatory located at 40 Montrose Road in the Village of Scarsdale, Westchester County, New York. It serves as an astronomical facility for observations and research.
a8a84b46-b736-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scarsdale Observatory, United States

a8b48334-badd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the **BARREL Balloon 2W**, a component of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) mission, which operated from December 31, 2013, to January 15, 2014, in the Earth's stratosphere to study particles escaping from the radiation belts.
a8b48334-badd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: part of Living with a Star Geospace Mission of Opportunity

a8bc108c-b5a0-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pioneer Venus Small Probe (North) Differential Long Baseline Interferometer was an experiment conducted during the Pioneer Venus mission to measure wind speeds in Venus' lower atmosphere using differential long-baseline interferometry techniques on radio signals from entry probes and a bus. The results helped model Venus' atmospheric circulation patterns, revealing wind velocities and shear at various altitudes.
a8bc108c-b5a0-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Differential Long Baseline Interferometer on Pioneer Venus Small Probe

a8bd4196-baf0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Halley Multicolor Camera (HMC) was an instrument aboard the Giotto spacecraft featuring a modified Ritchey-Chretien telescope and multiple detectors to capture images of Comet Halley and its surroundings during the 1986 flyby mission.
a8bd4196-baf0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Halley Multicolor Camera on Giotto

a8be6eea-b6a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Flint Observatory is an astronomical facility located in the Flint Cultural Center on Forest Street, East Village Neighborhood, Flint, Genesee County, Michigan. It operates as a ground-based observatory for studying celestial phenomena.
a8be6eea-b6a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Longway Observatory at Flint Observatory, United States

a8c522d8-b70f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Canadian Meteor Orbit Radar (CMOR), located at the University of Western Ontario meteor radar complex near Tavistock, Ontario, is a system of three interferometric radars used to detect and track meteors since 2001. It operates at multiple frequencies and uses sophisticated antenna arrays to measure velocity vectors and other characteristics of individual meteors.
a8c522d8-b70f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Canadian Meteor Orbit Radar at University of Western Ontario Observatory

a8d2fdb2-bb5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The "LANL 1990 Positions" dataset provides the spacecraft positions of the Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) 1990 mission in various coordinate systems.
a8d2fdb2-bb5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of LANL 1990

a8d58c9c-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer called "CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at CBI" is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed at Chichijima, Japan, used for measuring magnetic fields.
a8d58c9c-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometer Network observation network on Chichijima Island

a8d65082-b6e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Venera 15 and 16**: A dual-spacecraft mission launched in June 1983 by the Soviet Union to study Venus using radar mappers, primarily focusing on surface properties. Each spacecraft carried instruments like synthetic aperture radar and a radar altimeter.
a8d65082-b6e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Synthetic Aperture Radar and Radar Altimeter part of Venera 15 and 16

a8d74ec4-b951-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The CIS-CODIF is a mass spectrometer on the Cluster 2/FM7 (Samba) spacecraft, designed to measure full 3D ion distributions with high time and mass-per-charge resolution. It consists of two main instruments: the Hot Ion Analyzer (HIA) and the Ion Composition and Distribution Function analyzer (CODIF), which together provide comprehensive data on ion species and their energies.
a8d74ec4-b951-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cluster Ion Spectrometry on Cluster 2/FM7 (Samba)

a8d8acdc-b62d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Glyndon (GLYN) Fluxgate Magnetometer is an instrument located at the McMAC Glyndon station, designed to measure magnetic field variations as part of the Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain (McMAC).
a8d8acdc-b62d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain

a8dc568a-b6f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Trelew Magnetic Observatory, located in Argentina, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1957 to 2014, conducting magnetic observations.
a8dc568a-b6f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Trelew Observatory, Argentina

a8ddda56-b6cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astronomical Observatory of St. Petersburg State University, established in 1881, is a ground-based observatory located in Saint Petersburg, Russia, dedicated to astronomical research and education.
a8ddda56-b6cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory Saint Petersburg, Russia

a8def988-b78c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Puçol Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Puçol, Valencia, Spain, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects.
a8def988-b78c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Puçol Observatory, Spain

a8e0ed2e-bba1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The magnetometer at Saskatoon is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, located at the station identified by IAGA code SAS. It is part of the International Real-time Magnetic Observatory Network (INTERMAGNET) and affiliated with the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto.
a8e0ed2e-bba1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iugonet Observatory

a8f6b22a-bc1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Wormhout, France. Known as the Wormout Observatory or alternatively as the Wormhout Observatory.
a8f6b22a-bc1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wormout Observatory, France

a8f87454-bace-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Aeronomy of Ice in the Mesosphere (AIM) is a NASA satellite launched in 2007 to study noctilucent clouds (NLCs), also known as Polar Mesospheric Clouds, which form at high altitudes and latitudes during summer.
a8f87454-bace-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Bernard Lyot Telescope at Midi-Pyrénées Observatory, France

a8f8f152-ba67-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Las Cumbres Observatory is a global network of telescopes with various sizes and locations, designed to optimize astronomical observations by allocating scheduled observations to the most suitable telescope based on instrumentation needs and observing conditions.
a8f8f152-ba67-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2m Telescope at Las Cumbres Observatory

a8fecdc2-bafb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometers at Maliya Karmakul (MKL) are part of the IUGONET observatory network, specifically managed by the World Data Center in Kyoto, Japan.
a8fecdc2-bafb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Maliya Karmakul Observatory

a9018c6c-b801-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Deokheung Optical Astronomy Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Dongil, Goheung-gun, South Jeolla, South Korea. It is dedicated to optical astronomy and operates as a ground-based facility.
a9018c6c-b801-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deokheung Optical Astronomy Observatory, South Korea
