aefd08de-b1ae-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Wind Tunnel at High Plains Wind Erosion Laboratory

af02d776-ba16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SBIG ST-10XME is an advanced imaging camera equipped with a Kodak KAF-3200ME CCD detector, offering high quantum efficiency and resolution for astronomical observations.
af02d776-ba16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SBIG ST-10XME on Fremont Peak Observatory 0.32m Telescope

af0a69a4-b5c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Pioneer 9 Cosmic Dust Detector (CDD) was an instrument designed to measure cosmic dust flux density in the solar system, determine dust concentrations and properties in Earth's orbit, and evaluate the reliability of microphones as cosmic dust sensors.
af0a69a4-b5c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cosmic Dust Detector on Pioneer 9

af0dee24-b75d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) station at Paratunka, Russia is a ground-based facility developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research (ISEE), Nagoya University, to study upper atmospheric dynamics via nocturnal airglow emissions. It is located in Kamchatka Krai and collaborates with IKIR.
af0dee24-b75d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Paratunka Observatory, Russia

af17eb30-b61e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Eilat Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility in Israel that monitors geomagnetic activity using instruments like the WDC Kyoto magnetometer. It has been operational since 1998 and is located at an altitude of 250 meters above sea level.
af17eb30-b61e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eilat Geomagnetic Observatory, Israel

af1a7e36-bb46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GOES 3 Energetic Particle Monitor (EPM) is an instrument launched in 1978 that uses silicon solid-state detectors to measure the energy and types of particles, specifically protons, alpha particles, and electrons, within certain ranges.
af1a7e36-bb46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Monitor on GOES 3

af2d4c10-b6fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cape Dennison Geomagnetic Observatory (CDN) was a ground-based facility in Antarctica, operated by Australia primarily during 1912-1913, for geomagnetic research.
af2d4c10-b6fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cape Dennison Geomagnetic Observatory, Antarctica

af2e902a-b636-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mogadiscio Geomagnetic Observatory (MOG) is a ground-based facility in Mogadishu, Somalia, established in 1933 to monitor geomagnetic activity.
af2e902a-b636-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mogadiscio Geomagnetic Observatory, Somalia

af32d608-bba4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VIKING V4 experiment was an instrument onboard the VIKING spacecraft designed to measure electric and magnetic fields in space. It consisted of various sensors, including wire booms for electric field measurements and both loop and fluxgate antennas for magnetic field detection, covering a wide range of frequencies.
af32d608-bba4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electric and Magnetic Waves experiment on VIKING

af3743f4-b655-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Westport Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Westport, Bristol County, Massachusetts, United States. It facilitates scientific observations and research on celestial bodies from its North American location.
af3743f4-b655-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Westport Observatory, United States

af395d64-b638-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Livingston Island Geomagnetic Observatory (LIV), located in Antarctica and sponsored by Spain, is a ground-based facility established in 1995 to monitor geomagnetic activity. It includes a magnetometer instrument and operates out of the Juan Carlos I Antarctic Base.
af395d64-b638-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Juan Carlos I Antarctic Base, Antarctica

af586762-b67a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **VLT Survey Telescope (VST) at Paranal** is a ground-based observatory located in the Antofagasta Region of Chile. It is part of the European Southern Observatory's facilities and is situated at an elevation of 2,635 meters on Cerro Paranal.
af586762-b67a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VLT Survey Telescope at Paranal Observatory, Chile

af5d3f4e-bb7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wide Band Data (WBD) instrument on Cluster 2 is designed to measure high-resolution frequency/time spectra of plasma waves in the Earth's magnetosphere by capturing electric and magnetic field data within specific frequency bands.
af5d3f4e-bb7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide Band Data on Cluster 2 part of Wave Experiments Consortium

af625a84-b7b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Barrow Magnetic Observatory** is a ground-based facility in North Slope Borough, Alaska, dedicated to monitoring magnetic activity on Earth's surface. It is operated by the United States Geological Survey and has been active since January 1, 2007.
af625a84-b7b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Barrow Magnetic Observatory, United States

af641e64-bb5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Venus Express spacecraft position and velocity" dataset provides the spatial coordinates and movement details of the Venus Express spacecraft in different reference frames.
af641e64-bb5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Venus Express

af66e080-b9b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nancay Radio Telescope is a radio astronomy facility located in France, part of the Nancay Observatory.
af66e080-b9b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Nancay Radio Telescope at Nancay Observatory

af6926e4-bad8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Sørøya Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG since 2007, used to measure magnetic field variations.
af6926e4-bad8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Soroya Observatory

af820332-b7ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cosmosoz Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Tassin-la-Demi-Lune, France. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial phenomena.
af820332-b7ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cosmosoz Observatory, France

af8de052-b5e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Live Oak Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Pontotoc, San Saba County, Texas. It operates as a ground-based facility and is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code V62.
af8de052-b5e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Live Oak Observatory at Pontotoc, United States

afa1b066-b873-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **SESAME Riometer** is a radio receiver used to monitor the intensity of cosmic radio noise and measure the absorption of radio signals in the ionosphere. It operates as part of the SESAME observatory, sampling data once per second with high sensitivity.
afa1b066-b873-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Riometer part of Satellite Experiments Simultaneous with Antarctic MEasurements

afac4b42-baef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Star Ridge Observatory (H31) is an astronomical ground-based facility located in Weimar, Texas, United States. It is situated at coordinates 29.612413 latitude and -96.67 longitude.
afac4b42-baef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Weimar Observatory, United States

afafec80-ba1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1D Data Processing Unit (DPU) is a versatile instrument controller board that collects data from various sensors on the balloon array, formats it for transmission via an Iridium modem, and manages the command-cutdown system. It utilizes an FPGA for flexible interface logic and has been successfully deployed in multiple sounding rocket experiments and balloon flights.
afafec80-ba1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

afbf6292-b61a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vilnius Observatory, established in 1939, is an astronomical observatory located in Vilnius, Lithuania. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
afbf6292-b61a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vilnius Observatory, Lithuania

afc0ae64-b871-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Stony Ridge Observatory is an amateur astronomical observatory located in the mountains of Los Angeles County, California. Established in 1957, it is notable for its large telescope and contributions to asteroid discovery and lunar research.
afc0ae64-b871-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 760 mm Newtonian-Cassegrain Telescope at Stony Ridge Observatory, United States

afc8e906-b6bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Chorzow Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at the Silesian Planetarium in Park Śląski, Chorzów, Poland. It is part of the Silesian Planetarium and operates as a ground-based facility.
afc8e906-b6bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Silesian Planetarium Observatory, Poland

afe48f10-bbc2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Chichibu Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Yokoze, Saitama Prefecture, Japan, known for its contributions to asteroid discovery.
afe48f10-bbc2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chichibu Observatory, Japan

afe5479a-b9b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the 4.1m Southern Astrophysical Research (SOAR) Telescope located at Cerro Pachón, a ground-based observatory facility used for astrophysical research.
afe5479a-b9b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 4.1m Southern Astrophysical Research Telescope at Cerro Pachón

afe7037c-b851-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 25-cm Fecker refractor is a historic telescope with a 25 cm aperture that was operational from 1950 to 2004 at the University of Alabama Observatory in Tuscaloosa, Alabama.
afe7037c-b851-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.25m Fecker Refractor Telescope at University of Alabama Observatory, United States

afeb3e16-b6cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Patacamaya is a ground-based observatory located in Patacamaya, Provincia Aroma, La Paz, Bolivia. It operates as part of the IAGA network and specializes in geomagnetic measurements with its magnetometer instrument.
afeb3e16-b6cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Patacamaya Observatory, Bolivia

aff27388-bbc1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Norfolk State University 0.6m (24-inch) Rapid Response Robotic Telescope (RRRT) is an optical telescope located at the Fan Mountain Observatory in North America, designed for quick response and automated observations.
aff27388-bbc1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.6m optical Rapid Response Robotic Telescope at Fan Mountain Observatory

b000ab46-b71c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Langmuir probe instrument, the "Plasma Probes" on Ohzora, is designed to measure electron density and electron temperature. It was part of the Ohzora observatory's mission to study plasma properties in space.
b000ab46-b71c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Probes on Ohzora

b011565c-b8b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MASTER-SAAO Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Sutherland, South Africa. It is part of the Mobile Astronomical System of Telescope Robots (MASTER) network and utilizes optical telescopes for ground-based observations.
b011565c-b8b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Telescope at MASTER-SAAO Observatory, South Africa

b02a7050-b809-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Particulate Impact Analyzer (PIA) was a mass spectrometer on the Giotto spacecraft that used time-of-flight principles to analyze dust particles by detecting light pulses from particle impacts.
b02a7050-b809-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Particular Impact Analyser on Giotto spacecraft

b0306d0c-b629-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA High Energy Astronomy Observatory 1 (HEAO 1) was a satellite mission launched to study high-energy astronomical phenomena, particularly focusing on gamma-ray observations. It was part of the broader HEAO program aimed at advancing X-ray and gamma-ray astronomy.
b0306d0c-b629-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: gamma-ray NASA High Energy Astronomy Observatory 1 Satellite Mission

b03458d8-b820-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sdr Stromfjord Geomagnetic Observatory (STF), located in Kangerlussuaq, Greenland, is a ground-based facility operated by the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto since 1972, focusing on monitoring geomagnetic activity.
b03458d8-b820-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sdr Stromfjord Geomagnetic Observatory, Greenland

b0382fb4-bb20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Astronomical Observatory - Rozhen is an astronomical observatory located in the Smolyan Province of Bulgaria. It is operated by the Institute of Astronomy of the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences and serves as a principal center for astronomical research in the country.
b0382fb4-bb20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: National Astronomical Observatory - Rozhen, Bulgaria

b03a7882-b7ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Challenging Minisatellite Payload (CHAMP) was a German geomagnetic research satellite launched in 2000 for atmospheric and ionospheric studies, including gravity field determination and GPS radio occultation.
b03a7882-b7ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Challenging Minisatellite Payload

b041a1a8-b782-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mizusawa Geomagnetic Observatory (MIZ)** is a ground facility in Ichinoseki, Iwate Prefecture, Japan that has been monitoring geomagnetic data since 1980.
b041a1a8-b782-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mizusawa Geomagnetic Observatory, Japan

b04ee920-b6c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Electron Drift Instrument (EDI)** is a scientific instrument onboard the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS) that measures electric and magnetic fields by tracking the drift of approximately 1 keV electrons emitted from its Gun Detector Unit.
b04ee920-b6c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Drift Instrument part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

b059880e-b6fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Panoramic Camera (Pancam) is an instrument launched to Mars in 2003 as part of the Athena science payload. It was designed to capture high-resolution, color images to study the morphology, topography, and mineralogic properties of the Martian surface, as well as provide mission support for rover navigation and sampling target selection.
b059880e-b6fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Panoramic Camera on Mars Exploration Rover Spirit

b06079f2-b633-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Kingsgrove Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Kingsgrove, Sydney, Australia, used for ground-based observations of celestial objects.
b06079f2-b633-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kingsgrove Observatory, Australia

b06a1848-b937-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Coyote Watcher, Pie Town is a ground-based observatory located at Deer Run Trail in Catron County, New Mexico. It is situated at approximately 34.32186° N latitude and -108.17017° W longitude (251.82983° E) in North America.
b06a1848-b937-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Coyote Watcher at Pie Town Observatory, United States

b076517a-b627-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Wind Plasma Analyzer (OPA) is an instrument designed to measure solar wind conditions around Venus, including velocity, density, flow direction, and temperature. It operates using quadrispherical electrostatic analysis with varying voltages to detect charged particles over a wide energy range and angular coverage.
b076517a-b627-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Wind Plasma Analyzer on Pioneer Venus

b07a091c-b75a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Electron Drift Instrument (EDI)** is a scientific tool aboard the MMS 1 spacecraft designed to measure electric and magnetic fields by tracking the drift of ~1 keV electrons emitted from its Gun Detector Unit. It is part of the FIELDS Suite investigation led by the University of New Hampshire.
b07a091c-b75a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Drift Instrument part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission Fields Suite

b0806630-bb75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Kleť Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in the Czech Republic near České Budějovice. Situated at an altitude of 1,070 meters on Mount Kleť, it was constructed in 1957 and operates with around 150 clear nights per year.
b0806630-bb75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kleť Observatory, Czechia

b0828464-b59f-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Chinese Academy of Science 1.56m Telescope at Shanghai Astronomical Observatory (SHAO), Sheshan Station is an optical telescope located in Asia with a 1.56-meter aperture, used for astronomical observations.
b0828464-b59f-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.56m Chinese Academy of Science Telescope at Shanghai Astronomical Observatory Sheshan Station

b08c3c4c-b6c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bullcreek Observatory is a geomagnetic observatory located in Osceola County, Florida, operated by the Florida Institute of Technology from 1999 to 2004.
b08c3c4c-b6c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bullcreek Observatory, United States

b090e26e-b7f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) on the Mars Global Surveyor Spacecraft was an instrument designed to map Mars' topography using laser pulses, providing detailed 3D maps and crucial information about the planet's surface features and geological history.
b090e26e-b7f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter on Mars Global Surveyor Spacecraft

b0918fae-b92d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Kiruna, part of the WDC Kyoto observatory network under IAGA investigations, operational since January 1962.
b0918fae-b92d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Kiruna

b093dbba-b5ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NEAT-Maui camera was a high-resolution astronomical imaging device used by the Near Earth Asteroid Tracking (NEAT) survey at the Maui Space Surveillance Site, featuring a 4096 x 4096 pixel CCD and operating primarily with the MSSS 1.2m telescope from 2000 to 2007.
b093dbba-b5ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Earth Asteroid Tracking on Maui Space Surveillance Site

b0960bb0-b9e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: "STV53 is a spacecraft, identified by the code -214, which may be associated with various values or datasets represented as 'ValueSet({Value@STV53}).'"
b0960bb0-b9e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Value Set on Spacecraft

b09b35ca-b79f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetometers at Changchun (CNH) is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at the Changchun ground station since January 1957. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network and contributes to the World Data Centre for Geomagnetism in Kyoto and China.
b09b35ca-b79f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Changchun Observatory

b0a12596-b5b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Osservatorio Astrofisica di Catania (OAC) is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Ottawa, Canada, dedicated to astrophysics research and observations.
b0a12596-b5b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Osservatorio Astrofisica di Catania, Canada

b0a1c522-bb4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Gravity Science Instrument** of the **Juno mission** uses X and Ka-band transponders on the spacecraft along with Doppler tracking equipment at the Deep Space Network to study the gravitational field of celestial bodies.
b0a1c522-bb4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gravity Science Instrument for Juno part of Juno

b0a69bd6-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory is an astronomical observatory located on Mount Hopkins near Amado, Arizona, owned and operated by the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory (SAO).
b0a69bd6-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Bernard Lyot Telescope at Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory, United States

b0a86316-b7d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Rybachy Geomagnetic Observatory (RYB) is a ground-based facility located in the Murmansk Oblast, Russia, dedicated to monitoring and studying geomagnetic activity. It is part of the IAGA observatories network and includes instruments such as magnetometers for precise measurements.
b0a86316-b7d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Rybachy Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

b0b22f98-b766-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The San Marco Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Salerno, Campania, Italy.
b0b22f98-b766-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: San Marco Observatory, Italy

b0bb2bfc-ba0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Volkssternwarte Kempten** is a public observatory located in Kempten (Allgäu), Bavaria, Germany. It provides ground-based astronomical observations and is situated at an altitude of 725 meters.
b0bb2bfc-ba0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Volkssternwarte Kempten Observatory, Germany

b0c345ba-b600-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Casey Station Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Antarctica that operates magnetometers to monitor and study the Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since 1978 and is funded by Geoscience Australia.
b0c345ba-b600-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Casey Station Magnetic Observatory, Antarctica

b0c5e194-b92f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kakadu Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based geophysical facility in Kakadu, Northern Territory, Australia, operated by Geoscience Australia since 1995. It specializes in magnetic observations and data collection for scientific research.
b0c5e194-b92f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kakadu Magnetic Observatory, Australia

b0d086c2-bae1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Las Vaguadas Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Badajoz, Extremadura, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to celestial observation and research.
b0d086c2-bae1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Las Vaguadas Observatory, Spain

b0d3a008-b647-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Osservatorio Explorer, Pula" is a ground-based observatory located at Villa Nicole in Pula, Croatia. It serves as an astronomical facility for observations and research within the continent of Europe.
b0d3a008-b647-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical and Infrared Telescope at Osservatorio Explorer, Croatia

b0d8e2a2-b8b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Shasta Valley Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Siskiyou County, California, United States. It is situated at coordinates 41.57916° N, 237.451° E and is known for its ground-based observations.
b0d8e2a2-b8b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Shasta Valley Observatory, United States

b0dc74a8-b886-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Phoenix Lander Microscopy, Electrochemistry, and Conductivity Analyzer (MECA) Thermal and Electrical Conductivity Probe (TECP) was a tool designed to study the thermal properties of Martian soil by measuring how heat and electrical currents traveled through it. This probe provided essential data on the soil's ability to retain heat, moisture content, and interactions with the Martian environment, aiding in assessing the presence of water ice and potential for future human exploration.
b0dc74a8-b886-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Thermal and Electrical Conductivity Probe part of Phoenix Lander Microscopy, Electrochemistry, and Conductivity Analyzer

b0eb2bfc-b66e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Harris Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS GBO Network, used to measure magnetic field variations.
b0eb2bfc-b66e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Harris Geophysical Observatory

b0f01048-b7f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAVEN Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) instrument is a scientific tool onboard the MAVEN spacecraft designed to measure electrons and ions over specific energy ranges to study the impact of solar energetic particles on Mars' upper atmosphere. It consists of two sensors with double-ended solid-state telescopes, positioned to optimize the field of view for detecting these particles.
b0f01048-b7f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solid State Detector on MAVEN

b0f60802-bb54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AJ4CO Terminated Folded Dipole and Dual-Radio JOVE receiver system is a ground-based instrument located at the Radio Astronomy Observatory in High Springs, Florida, featuring two 4-element square arrays with each antenna element being 32 feet long, aligned to true north, and dual-radio receivers operating at 20.1 MHz for uncorrelated RCP and LCP signals.
b0f60802-bb54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terminated Folded Dipole and Dual-Radio JOVE receiver system at AJ4CO Radio Astronomy Observatory

b104017a-bae4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a magnetometer located at the Cape Evans observatory in Antarctica, operated from 1912 until 1958 as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy's (IAGA) network.
b104017a-bae4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cape Evans Observatory

b10ab490-b7cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Astreo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Mairena del Aljarafe, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to observing celestial bodies and phenomena.
b10ab490-b7cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astreo Observatory, Spain

b10e5e6a-b957-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Transition Region and Coronal Explorer (TRACE) was a NASA space telescope designed to study the Sun's magnetic fields and their impact on the solar atmosphere, focusing particularly on fine-scale structures and dynamics in the corona.
b10e5e6a-b957-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Transition Region and Coronal Explorer

b113c86e-b5ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An Electrostatic Analyzer (ESA) is an instrument used in space missions to measure the flux of thermal particles over a wide field of view and energy range. The Dual Full Distribution ESAs on ARTEMIS-P1 specifically capture the full 3-D distributions, density, velocity, and temperature of ambient electrons and ions.
b113c86e-b5ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer on Acceleration Reconnection Turbulence and Electrodynamics of Moon's Interaction with the Sun spacecraft

b1205e4a-b681-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bergisch Gladbach Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bergisch Gladbach, Germany. It has been operational since 1995 and is known for its work under the guidance of astronomer Wolf Bickel.
b1205e4a-b681-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bergisch Gladbach Observatory, Germany

b12208f2-b781-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **HNRAO Dual Dipole Array and RadioJOVE receiver system** is a radio astronomy instrument located at the Hawk's Nest Radio Astronomy Observatory. It consists of a 2-element array with each antenna element being 25 feet long, separated by 20 feet, aligned to magnetic north, and operates at 20.1 MHz with a 7 KHz RF bandwidth.
b12208f2-b781-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Waveband Riometer at Hawk's Nest Radio Astronomy Observatory

b125913e-b6b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Swilken Brae Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in St. Andrews, Fife, Scotland, United Kingdom. It is situated at Strathkinness High Road and operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
b125913e-b6b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Swilken Brae Observatory, United Kingdom

b12c94be-bad0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Ulysses Ephemeris" refers to the recorded positional data of the Ulysses spacecraft, providing detailed information about its location and trajectory over time. This dataset is part of the CNES Observatory CDPP Archive for Ulysses and serves as a critical resource for understanding the spacecraft's mission dynamics.
b12c94be-bad0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Instrument on Ulysses Spacecraft

b12ec144-b74c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The United States Space Surveillance Network (SSN) is a system that detects, tracks, catalogs, and identifies artificial objects orbiting Earth, such as satellites and space debris. It operates under the responsibility of the United States Space Command and utilizes facilities like the Haleakala Observatory in Maui County, Hawaii.
b12ec144-b74c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: United States Space Surveillance Network at Haleakala Observatory

b13202da-b7d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Griffin Hunter Observatory** (code 449) is an astronomical observatory located in Kershaw County, South Carolina, United States, operated by Bethune-Cookman University. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
b13202da-b7d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Griffin Hunter Observatory, United States

b1336680-b810-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Astronomical Observatory of Farra d'Isonzo is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Farra d'Isonzo, Italy.
b1336680-b810-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory of Farra d'Isonzo, Italy

b135f97c-b9af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Wykrota Observatory-CEAMIG is an astronomical observatory located in Penedia, Caeté, Minas Gerais, Brazil. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
b135f97c-b9af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wykrota Observatory

b1379f46-b691-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SBIG ST-8 is a high-sensitivity astronomical CCD camera used for astrophotography and scientific imaging, popular among both amateur and professional astronomers for capturing detailed images of celestial objects.
b1379f46-b691-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SBIG ST-8 at Carbuncle Hill Observatory

b1411332-bb7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Retarding Potential Analyzer/Drift Meter on AE-D is an instrument designed to measure vector ion drift velocities, ion concentration, and temperature, as well as spacecraft potential in the ionosphere. It consists of a retarding potential analyzer with multiple sensor heads that can observe along the spacecraft velocity vector.
b1411332-bb7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Retarding Potential Analyzer and Drift Meter on AE-D

b1457a58-b704-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dalat Magnetometer was an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields, operational from January 1, 1978, to December 31, 1992, as part of the IAGA investigation at the Dalat Observatory.
b1457a58-b704-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dalat Observatory

b1545432-b6ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Galileo Orbiter Ultraviolet Spectrometer (UVS)** was an instrument on the Galileo spacecraft designed to study the interstellar wind and its interaction with the solar system, featuring a Cassegrain telescope and Ebert-Fastie scanning spectrometer for detailed ultraviolet spectral analysis.
b1545432-b6ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Spectrometer on Galileo Orbiter

b158add6-ba4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** CARISMA (Canadian Array for Realtime Investigations of Magnetic Activity) is a network of magnetometers deployed across Canada and parts of the United States to measure and study disturbances in Earth's magnetic field caused by activity in the magnetosphere. It is an essential resource for magnetospheric physics, contributing to numerous scientific publications.
b158add6-ba4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Canadian Array for Realtime Investigations of Magnetic Activity

b15c07b8-ba02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **JADE (Jovian Auroral Distributions Experiment)** is an instrument suite on NASA's Juno spacecraft designed to measure electrons and ions, helping understand plasma energy particles and processes within Jupiter's magnetosphere that drive its powerful auroras.
b15c07b8-ba02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: The Jovian Auroral Plasma Distributions Experiment on Juno

b15e7394-bb9d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Plasma and Electrodynamics Instrument (IPEI) on ROCSAT-1 is a scientific instrument designed to measure ion density, temperature, and drift velocity in the low-latitude ionosphere, with a focus on studying large-scale electrodynamics and plasma distribution, particularly around the equatorial region above Taiwan.
b15e7394-bb9d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Plasma and Electrodynamics Instrument on ROCSAT-1

b16a91b8-b5c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Misallat Geophysical Observatory was a ground-based facility in Faiyum, Egypt, that operated from 1964 to 2003 and specialized in geomagnetic measurements.
b16a91b8-b5c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Misallat Geomagnetic Observatory, Egypt

b1724c8c-babe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The European Southern Observatory (ESO) 0.6m TRAPPIST is a telescope located at the La Silla Observatory in South America, designed to study transiting exoplanets and minor planets using optical wavebands.
b1724c8c-babe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.6m Transiting Planets and Planetesimals Small Telescope at La Silla Observatory

b1740afe-b7c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 (WFPC2) was a camera on the Hubble Space Telescope that operated from 1993 to 2009, capturing images across UV, visible, and infrared wavelengths with a field of view of 2.7 arcminutes square.
b1740afe-b7c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Visible Near-Infrared Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2 on Hubble Space Telescope

b174a5ca-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kapuskasing Magnetometer is an instrument located at the Kapuskasing (KAPU) Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation. It measures magnetic field variations and has been operational since May 17, 2006.
b174a5ca-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission, Antarctica

b177bb66-b7c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: El Leoncito (X19) is a ground-based observatory located in Calingasta, San Juan, Argentina. It operates under the label "Santel Observatory" and is situated at coordinates -31.80244 latitude and 290.67383 longitude in South America.
b177bb66-b7c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: El Leoncito Observatory, Argentina

b1851b72-b64b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Chinese Hα Solar Explorer (CHASE) is a ground-based telescope located in space. It operates in the optical waveband and is dedicated to observing solar phenomena such as hydrogen alpha emission lines.
b1851b72-b64b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Chinese Halpha Solar Explorer Telescope

b185b0e2-b825-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1R magnetometer (TCM2) is a three-axis instrument designed to measure magnetic field components with high resolution, primarily used for identifying substorm activity and ULF oscillations in support of the BARREL investigation.
b185b0e2-b825-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

b18ef506-bb9c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Canberra, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network, which measures magnetic field variations.
b18ef506-bb9c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observatory

b18fdeba-b9dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mount Terskol Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Elbrus District of Kabardino-Balkaria, Russia. It was established in 1980 and is funded by the International Center For Astronomical, Medical and Ecological Research.
b18fdeba-b9dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terskol Observatory

b198d3f4-ba3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The XPS (Extreme Ultraviolet Photometer System) on SORCE is a lightweight photometer designed to monitor the x-ray and UV band at 1-34 nm with a resolution of about seven nm and an irradiance accuracy of approximately 15%.
b198d3f4-ba3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Extreme Ultraviolet Photometer System on Solar Radiation and Climate Experiment

b1b60d50-b7ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **RadioJOVE Dual Dipole Array and RadioJOVE receiver system** is an instrument used for radio astronomy, consisting of a two-element antenna array with linear polarization and adjustable beam pattern, along with a direct conversion receiver operating at 20.1 MHz with a 7 KHz RF bandwidth.
b1b60d50-b7ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Riometer part of RadioJOVE

b1cc1bfe-b9e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operated from 1929 to 1977 at the WDC Kyoto AML observatory, used for measuring magnetic fields.
b1cc1bfe-b9e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Amberley Observatory

b1cdbfbc-bae7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Kakioka Observatory in Japan, part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network since 1913.
b1cdbfbc-bae7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kakioka Observatory

b1d92b4e-b96c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The **BARREL Balloon 2T Optical Photometer** is an instrument designed to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm, specifically to identify precipitating protons during relativistic electron precipitation events, thereby aiding in the study of electromagnetic ion cyclotron (EMIC) wave scattering as a potential mechanism for such events.
b1d92b4e-b96c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

b1df7de6-b6ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAVEN Accelerometer (ACC) is a high-precision instrument onboard the MAVEN spacecraft designed to measure atmospheric drag accelerations, which are used to recover atmospheric density and temperature profiles along the orbiter's path.
b1df7de6-b6ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Accelerometer on Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN Spacecraft

b1e043e4-bb5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Ulysses Dust Detection System (UDDS) was an instrument on the Ulysses spacecraft designed to detect and analyze dust particles in interplanetary and interstellar space, featuring a hemispherical gold foil target and advanced charge collection methods.
b1e043e4-bb5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ulysses Dust Detection System on Ulysses Spacecraft

b2023316-bb94-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magellan Spacecraft Radar System utilized synthetic aperture radar (SAR) to produce high-resolution maps of Venus' surface, revealing detailed features and contributing to the understanding of the planet's geology and tectonic activity.
b2023316-bb94-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar System on Magellan Spacecraft

b20492d2-b86f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Turin Observatory (before 1913), also known as the Turin Observatory, was an astronomical observatory located in Turin, Italy. It operated on Earth and functioned as a ground-based observatory.
b20492d2-b86f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Turin Observatory, Italy

b20a4f8c-ba28-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1R Ephemeris is a virtual instrument providing trajectory positions for the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) mission, offering data in various coordinate systems.
b20a4f8c-ba28-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

b20ec21a-bb90-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ksara Geomagnetic Observatory (KSA), located in Saadnayel, Lebanon, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1930 to 1970, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
b20ec21a-bb90-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ksara Geomagnetic Observatory, Lebanon

b211485e-b966-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **AJ4CO Terminated Folded Dipole and Dual-Polarization Spectrograph** is a specialized instrument at the AJ4CO Radio Astronomy Observatory in High Springs, Florida, designed for radio astronomy observations. It features a dual-polarization spectrograph operating between 16-32 MHz with simultaneous Right Circular Polarization (RCP) and Left Circular Polarization (LCP), providing high resolution and sensitivity for astronomical studies.
b211485e-b966-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terminated Folded Dipole and Dual-Polarization Spectrograph at AJ4CO Radio Astronomy Observatory, High Springs

b21249be-bb52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cylindrical Electrostatic Probes (CEP)** on AE-C were a pair of Langmuir probe instruments designed to measure electron temperatures, electron and ion concentrations, ion mass, and spacecraft potential. They consisted of two identical probes oriented differently on the spacecraft to provide comprehensive data collection.
b21249be-bb52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Retarding Potential Langmuir Probe part of Atmosphere Explorer-C Mission

b214fbb4-b779-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tashkent Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting various astronomical observations and research.
b214fbb4-b779-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mirzo Ulugbek Observatory, Uzbekistan

b215d784-bab5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The McDonald Observatory Linear Polarimeter is an instrument installed in 1978 at the McDonald Observatory, designed to measure polarization with high precision using a rotating Glan-Air prism. It achieves accuracy down to \(10^{-4}\), primarily limited by photon statistics rather than instrumental factors.
b215d784-bab5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Linear Polarimeter at McDonald Observatory

b218347a-b8e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the telescope located at the Narrabri Deep Space Station (DSS47) in 2008, which is part of NASA's Deep Space Network facility.
b218347a-b8e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: DSS-47 Telescope at Narrabri Observatory

b21a16aa-bb05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Magnetometers at Kanozan (KNZ)" are instruments used to measure the Earth's magnetic field and have been operational since January 1961 as part of the IUGONET Observatory in Kyoto, Japan. They are part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
b21a16aa-bb05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kanozan Observatory

b21b2b84-bbbf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tiflis Observatory was a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Tbilisi, Georgia, operating from 1879 to 1905. It was part of the IAGA network and contributed to geomagnetic research with its magnetometer instruments.
b21b2b84-bbbf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tbilisi Observatory

b21b32e8-b6db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Royal Observatory, Cape of Good Hope** is a former astronomical observatory in Cape Town, South Africa, established in 1820 and now serving as the headquarters for the South African Astronomical Observatory.
b21b32e8-b6db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Royal Observatory at Cape of Good Hope, South Africa

b21df782-b675-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Shawano Geophysical Observatory:** A ground-based facility located in Shawano, Wisconsin, USA, operated by UCLA as part of the THEMIS project, primarily for educational public outreach and featuring a magnetometer that may be subject to environmental noise.
b21df782-b675-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Shawano Geophysical Observatory, United States

b222a582-b5aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Combined Release and Radiation Effects Satellite (CRRES) was a research satellite launched in 1990 to study fields, plasmas, and energetic particles within Earth's magnetosphere. It conducted experiments on radiation effects on microelectronics and performed chemical releases to observe plasma behavior.
b222a582-b5aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Combined Release and Radiation Effects Satellite

b233f910-bc97-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Viking Lander 1 Spacecraft Camera 1 was a facsimile camera used on the Viking Lander 1 mission. It employed a single, stationary photosensor array and scanning mechanisms to capture images by focusing light from azimuth and elevation scans onto the sensor.
b233f910-bc97-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Viking Lander 1 Spacecraft Camera 1 on Viking Lander 1

b23456e6-bb3c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Leibniz-Institut für Astrophysik Potsdam operates two 1.2m STELLA (STELLar Activity) optical telescopes located at the Observatorio del Teide in Tenerife, Canary Islands. These telescopes are dedicated to studying stellar activity and are part of a broader astronomical research initiative based in Africa.
b23456e6-bb3c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical Leibniz Institute for Astrophysics Potsdam two 1.2m Stellar Activity (STELLA) telescopes at Observatorio del Teide

b2437b74-bbb6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bayerwald Observatory, also known as the Bayerwald Sternwarte in Spiegelau, is an astronomical observatory located in Neuhütte, Germany. It serves as a ground-based facility for stargazing and astronomical research.
b2437b74-bbb6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spiegelau Observatory, Germany

b2540aa0-b604-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes a magnetometer located at the IAGA station identified as VQS in Kyoto. Operational from 1903 to 1924, this instrument was part of the WDC Kyoto observatory and measured magnetic field data.
b2540aa0-b604-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy

b25cf518-bb2f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "North Pole 10" refers to a ground-based observatory located on Earth's surface at the coordinates 76.62 latitude and 166.38 longitude, operational from January 1, 1961, to December 31, 1962. It is part of an IAGA observatory network and includes a magnetometer as one of its instruments.
b25cf518-bb2f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ground Magnetometer at North Pole Observatory

b2689bb6-b5a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SBIG ST-9E is a camera developed by the Santa Barbara Instrument Group, featuring a Kodak KAF0261E CCD and a 5-position color filter wheel, designed for imaging with high quantum efficiency and thermoelectric cooling capabilities.
b2689bb6-b5a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Santa Barbara Instrument Group ST-9E

b26b7930-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **SOLIS FDP**: The SOLIS Full Disk Patrol (FDP) is a 14-cm telescope that captures full disk images of the Sun at several wavelengths in the 380-670 nm range and at 1083 nm, with high spectral and spatial resolution.
b26b7930-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Full Disk Patrol Telescope part of Solar Observing Optical Network

b2747bd6-bba5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISEE (International Sun-Earth Explorer) program was a collaborative mission between NASA and ESA that operated from 1977 to 1987, focused on studying the interaction of the solar wind with Earth's magnetosphere.
b2747bd6-bba5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ISEE

b278d820-b605-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Foligno Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Foligno, Italy, operated by the Club Alpino Italiano - Sezione Foligno. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
b278d820-b605-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Osservatorio di Foligno, Italy

b28865f6-b5bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vega Mission Plasma Energy Analyzer, also known as "Plazmag," was an instrument on the Vega 2 spacecraft designed to study solar wind interactions with comets. It featured five detectors to measure ion and electron energies, velocities, and compositions, helping to understand plasma conditions near comets.
b28865f6-b5bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Retarding Potential Analyser part of Vega Mission

b290c5fe-b694-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Mexico City Magnetometer" was an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields at the IAGA-identified station MEX in Mexico City from 1879 to 1887. It was part of the observatory network managed by the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA).
b290c5fe-b694-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mexico City Observatory

b2936a9c-bb2c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The magnetometers at Sukkertoppen (SKT), part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation and IUGONET Observatory, are instruments used to measure magnetic fields starting from February 5, 2007. These devices provide essential data for geophysical research and space weather monitoring.
b2936a9c-bb2c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

b29872bc-b974-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Imaging Riometer Observation at Husafell is a 60MHz riometer located in Husafell, Iceland, designed to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere by monitoring nocturnal airglow emissions. It features an 8x8-element dipole antenna array that produces independent beams covering an area of approximately 180km x 180km at D region altitude.
b29872bc-b974-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 60MHz Riometer at ISEE Observatory, Iceland

b2a167ca-bada-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Magnetometers at Stonyhurst (STO)" were instruments used from 1865 to 1967 for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IAGA investigation at the observatory in Stonyhurst.
b2a167ca-bada-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Stonyhurst Observatory

b2a65fa6-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Trapper Creek Geophysical Observatory, located in Matanuska-Susitna Borough, Alaska, is a ground facility established on October 4, 2013, dedicated to geophysical research and equipped with instruments such as magnetometers.
b2a65fa6-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Trapper Creek Geophysical Observatory, United States

b2a74e98-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute 1.8m Telescope at Bohyunsan Optical Astronomy Observatory (BOAO) is a telescopic facility located in Asia, specifically in South Korea, designed for optical astronomy with an aperture of 1.8 meters.
b2a74e98-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 1.8m Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute Telescope at Bohyunsan Optical Astronomy Observatory

b2b05ac6-bb8b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **George Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Needville, Texas, known for its ground-based facilities and operations starting from 1996.
b2b05ac6-bb8b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: George Observatory, United States

b2b4901a-b8c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Dome Concordia is a ground-based observatory located on Earth's surface at an altitude of 3233 meters and coordinates -75.102 latitude, 123.395 longitude. It has been operational since January 1, 2004, and includes instruments such as a magnetometer.
b2b4901a-b8c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dome Concordia Observatory, Antarctica

b2b51e52-bbb9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vulpecula Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Budapest, Hungary. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
b2b51e52-bbb9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vulpecula Observatory, Hungary

b2c0578c-b5e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The CLPS Task Order PRIME-1 Mass Spectrometer Observing Lunar Operations (MSolo) is a modified residual gas analyzer designed to measure the composition of gases on the lunar surface and monitor the release of lunar volatiles during drilling operations. It is part of NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program.
b2c0578c-b5e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer Observing Lunar Operation on Athena

b2c063e8-b17d-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTIs) station at Nain, Canada is an observatory developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research (ISEE), Nagoya University, to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions.
b2c063e8-b17d-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Nain Observatory, Canada

b2d701aa-b940-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bredenkamp Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bremen, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
b2d701aa-b940-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bredenkamp Observatory

b2e1a122-b806-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Astronomical Society of Tahiti** is a ground-based observatory located in Loulin, Piafau, Faʻaʻā, Windward Islands, French Polynesia. It operates under the jurisdiction of France and focuses on astronomical observations and research.
b2e1a122-b806-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Bernard Lyot Telescope at Midi-Pyrénées Observatory, France

b2ec4e06-b5f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The magnetometers at She-Shan Observatory are part of the IUGONET network and have been operational since 1930, contributing to geomagnetic studies and monitoring.
b2ec4e06-b5f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at She-Shan Observatory

b2f0a1ae-b93c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "GOES 17 Spacecraft Ephemeris" is an instrument that provides positional data for the GOES-17 satellite as part of the GOES observatory system. It helps track and predict the spacecraft's location over time, essential for geostationary weather monitoring missions.
b2f0a1ae-b93c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GOES 17 Position part of Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite

b2f24444-b8da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Campo Catino Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Guarcino, Italy, known for its ground-based facilities and contributions to astronomy.
b2f24444-b8da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Campo Catino Observatory, Italy

b2ff966c-b731-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wide-field Imager for Solar Probe (WISPR) Outer Telescope** is an instrument on the Parker Solar Probe mission that consists of two telescopes designed to capture images from the side of the spacecraft, with the Outer Telescope viewing areas offset from 98.5° to 156.5° from the Sun center.
b2ff966c-b731-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide-field Imager for Solar Probe on Parker Solar Probe

b302b652-bac5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 3 FIELDS Suite, Fluxgate Magnetometer (FGM) is an instrument on the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS) designed to measure magnetic fields and current structures in space, featuring both Analog and Digital Fluxgate magnetometers for redundant data collection.
b302b652-bac5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of MMS 3 FIELDS Suite

b3094f88-b761-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Prognoz spacecraft series were Soviet Earth research satellites designed to investigate solar activity, its impact on the interplanetary environment, and the Earth's magnetosphere.
b3094f88-b761-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Prognoz Spacecraft Series

b30953ca-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lunar Prospector Spacecraft Neutron Spectrometer (NS) was an instrument on the Lunar Prospector spacecraft designed to measure thermal, epithermal, and fast neutrons from the lunar surface to detect water ice in permanently shadowed polar regions. It consisted of two helium-3 filled gas proportional counters with different shielding materials to distinguish between various neutron energy levels.
b30953ca-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutron Spectrometer on Lunar Prospector

b309ed3a-ba04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Kunlun Station is a ground-based observatory located at Zhongshan - Dome A in Antarctica, specifically situated at coordinates -80.41742 latitude and 77.1167 longitude. It is also known as the Plateau Observatory for Dome A.
b309ed3a-ba04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plateau Observatory for Dome A at Kunlun Station, Antarctica

b30cb2ba-b737-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cosmic Dust Experiment (CDE) is an instrument on the AIM spacecraft designed to measure inflowing cosmic dust contributing to Polar Mesospheric Clouds. It utilizes thin Polyvinylidene Fluoride films to detect particles greater than 1 micron in radius, featuring twelve zenith-facing detectors and two downward-facing ones for background noise measurements.
b30cb2ba-b737-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dust Detector on Aeronomy of Ice in the Mesosphere

b318dba2-bb57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Beijing Astronomical Observatory (BAO) is a ground-based observatory located in Chaoyang District, Beijing, China. It was established in 1958 and is part of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, featuring multiple observing stations including its principal site at Xinglong Station.
b318dba2-bb57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Beijing Astronomical Observatory, China

b3226e68-ba50-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetometer at the Arkhangelsk ground station is an instrument used to measure the magnetic field and has been operational since January 1985. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network under WDC Kyoto and contributes to the IAGA investigation.
b3226e68-ba50-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Arkhangelsk Observatory

b3246252-b764-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Kaktovik (KAKO) Geophysical Observatory was a ground-based facility in Alaska, United States, operational from 1999 to 2014, equipped with magnetometers for geophysical measurements.
b3246252-b764-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kaktovik Geophysical Observatory

b32e3bf4-b897-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Auckland Island Observatory was a ground-based facility in New Zealand that operated from 1874 to 1875, equipped with magnetometers for scientific observations.
b32e3bf4-b897-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Auckland Island Observatory

b3427244-baaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The El Boalo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in El Boalo-Cerceda-Mataelpino, Community of Madrid, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
b3427244-baaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: El Boalo Observatory, Spain

b349076c-ba6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
DSS-25 is a 34-meter radio telescope located at the Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex in California, known for its beam waveguide design and capability to operate at both X-band and Ka-band frequencies.
b349076c-ba6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Radio Telescope at Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex, United States

b34f304c-bbe0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Grahamstown Geomagnetic Observatory (GRM) was a ground-based facility in South Africa that operated from 1974 to 1980, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
b34f304c-bbe0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Grahamstown Geomagnetic Observatory, South Africa

b351f3d4-b746-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1.54-m multipurpose reflector is a 1.54-meter telescope located at the Mount Lemmon (Catalina) Station in Arizona, operational since 1970. It is part of the Mount Lemmon Observatory and is used for various astronomical observations.
b351f3d4-b746-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.54m Telescope at Mount Lemmon Observatory, United States

b353a142-b6f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EISCAT Tromsø UHF Radar Observation** is an astronomical observatory located in Tromsø, Norway. It operates a high-power (1.7 MW peak) incoherent scatter radar system at approximately 931 MHz for studying the Earth's ionosphere and upper atmosphere.
b353a142-b6f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultra High Frequency Radar at EISCAT Observatory, Norway

b3546618-b8c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cape Chelyuskin geophysical observatory is a ground-based facility located in Russia, specifically on the Earth's surface at an altitude of 10 meters, and it has been operational since January 1935. It includes a magnetometer instrument and is part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) observatory network.
b3546618-b8c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cape Chelyuskin Observatory, Russia

b355d634-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Planetarium de Vaulx-en-Velin Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Vaulx-en-Velin, Lyon, France. It is situated at a latitude of 45.777818 and longitude of 4.92247 on the European continent.
b355d634-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Planetarium de Vaulx-en-Velin Observatory, France

b3654002-ba42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU Radio Beacon Receiver (GRBR) Station at Phuket is an observatory located in Thailand that monitors ionospheric disturbances using a specialized radio receiver.
b3654002-ba42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU radio beacon receiver on GRBR station at Phuket Technical College, Thailand

b365b4e8-bb13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Santa Coloma de Gramenet Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Àger, Noguera, Lleida, Catalonia, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
b365b4e8-bb13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Santa Coloma de Gramenet Observatory, Spain

b36695c0-bb68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Framing Camera 2 (FC2) was one of two multispectral CCD imagers used on the NASA Dawn mission to asteroids Vesta and Ceres, functioning both as a scientific instrument and an optical navigation tool.
b36695c0-bb68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Framing Camera 2 part of Dawn

b367f2b4-b62f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The TRACE (Transition Region and Coronal Explorer) Imaging Telescope is a Cassegrain-design telescope aboard the TRACE spacecraft, primarily tasked with studying magnetic field structures in the solar atmosphere, heating mechanisms of the outer solar atmosphere, and triggers for solar flares and mass ejections.
b367f2b4-b62f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager part of Transition Region and Coronal Explorer

b367f314-bbce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** "Cluster3 Magnetospheric Analytical Models" refers to a collection of data and tools used for analyzing magnetic field environments in space, specifically associated with the Cluster-II mission.
b367f314-bbce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetospheric Analytical Models part of Cluster Mission

b37223ec-b5ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Pulkovo Astronomical Observatory is the principal astronomical observatory of the Russian Academy of Sciences, located 19 km south of Saint Petersburg. It serves as a major center for astronomical research and observations in Russia.
b37223ec-b5ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pulkovo Astronomical Observatory at Central Astronomical Observatory of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Russia

b3810f44-b682-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Plasma Electron and Current Experiment (PEACE)** is an energetic particle instrument on the Cluster 2/FM6 (Salsa) spacecraft, designed to measure electron velocity distribution functions in three dimensions with high time, energy, and angular resolution. It consists of two sensors per spacecraft, each providing complete 4π solid angle coverage in one spin, with a dynamic range extended by combining data from both sensors.
b3810f44-b682-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Electron and Current Experiment on Cluster 2/FM6

b3887d0a-bb79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAGs, located at the Dead Horse (DED) Geophysical Observatory since March 2010.
b3887d0a-bb79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dead Horse Geophysical Observatory

b38d8354-ba84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory (SAO) 1.5m (61-inch) Wyeth Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Oak Ridge Observatory in North America, with a primary mirror diameter of 1.5 meters.
b38d8354-ba84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.5m optical Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory Wyeth Telescope at Oak Ridge Observatory

b392eca6-b9d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at RIK is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Rikubetsu, Japan, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
b392eca6-b9d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum Pan-Pacific Magnetic Network, Japan

b3981f96-b6ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) Radio Science Subsystem (RSS) is an instrument used to conduct radio science investigations on Mars, utilizing both spacecraft and ground station elements to study the planet's atmosphere, ionosphere, and gravity field through the analysis of radio signals.
b3981f96-b6ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Subsystem on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter

b39a2626-bc60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The WITec Alpha300R Raman Imaging Spectrometer, housed at the Center for Planetary Exploration at Stony Brook University, is an advanced instrument featuring dual laser excitation sources and capable of high-resolution spectral imaging with powerful multivariate analysis software.
b39a2626-bc60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: WITec Alpha300R Raman Imaging Spectrometer at Center for Planetary Exploration

b39c84fc-ba3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at EWA** is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed at Ewa Beach, United States, for measuring magnetic fields. It is part of the IUGONET observatory and the CPMN observation network.
b39c84fc-ba3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of CPMN Observation Network

b39eeeb6-ba00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Calgary Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Charleswood, Calgary, Alberta, Canada. It operates as a ground-based facility for studying celestial bodies and phenomena from Earth.
b39eeeb6-ba00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Calgary Observatory, Canada

b3a224b0-b9fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Catalina Station**: An astronomical observatory located on Mount Bigelow in the Santa Catalina Mountains near Tucson, Arizona, operated by Steward Observatory of the University of Arizona.
b3a224b0-b9fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.54m Kuiper Telescope at Catalina Station, United States

b3a2758c-b72a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gas Chromatograph Mass Spectrometer (GCMS) on the Huygens Probe was an instrument designed to measure the chemical composition and isotope ratios of Titan's atmosphere, as well as analyze gas samples from the Aerosol Collector Pyrolyser. It utilized a quadrupole mass filter with multiple ion sources and detection systems for continuous and batch sampling of atmospheric gases.
b3a2758c-b72a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gas Chromatograph Mass Spectrometer on Huygens Probe

b3a45de8-b720-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) Telescope was a 40 cm infrared telescope equipped with four detectors operating at different wavelengths, designed to survey the sky and provide detailed infrared images.
b3a45de8-b720-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer on The Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer

b3a5c3c8-bab7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Lunar IceCube**: A NASA nanosatellite orbiter mission designed to prospect and analyze water ice deposits on the Moon, launched as a secondary payload on Artemis 1 in November 2022.
b3a5c3c8-bab7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Broadband InfraRed Compact High-resolution Explorer Spectrometer on Lunar IceCube part of Artemis 1

b3a5d6b0-b828-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity represents the InSight instrument, part of a NASA mission, specifically designed for geophysical investigations and seismic monitoring on Mars. It is associated with the InSight spacecraft and provides valuable data about the planet's interior structure.
b3a5d6b0-b828-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: InSight Seismometer on Mars InSight Lander

b3a837f2-ba0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: RMI (Radar for Icy Moons Exploration) is an instrument designed to study the subsurface structures of Jupiter's icy moons, particularly focusing on detecting and characterizing potential liquid water oceans beneath their surfaces. It operates as part of the spacecraft's suite of scientific instruments.
b3a837f2-ba0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: [unknown waveband] Unknown Entity on Unknown Spacecraft

b3aa8530-bb8d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The magnetometer located in Hyderabad is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since January 1965 and is part of the IUGONET Observatory network, specifically the WDC Kyoto-WDC Hyb observatory.
b3aa8530-bb8d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hyderabad Observatory

b3baa36c-b76d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Mariner 10 Spacecraft" was an unmanned NASA space probe launched to study Mercury and Venus, making it the first spacecraft to use a gravitational slingshot maneuver and perform multiple planetary flybys. It is part of the CDPP-AMDA observatory managed by CNES, providing orbital data known as ephemeris.
b3baa36c-b76d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris part of Mariner 10 Spacecraft

b3d1ba30-b956-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Martin Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Blacksburg, Virginia, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
b3d1ba30-b956-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Martin Observatory, United States

b3eb8f8c-b6cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BCMT (Bureau Central de Magnétisme Terrestre) operates the French National Magnetic Observatory and a network of geomagnetic observatories globally to provide high-quality ground-based geomagnetic observations and data products.
b3eb8f8c-b6cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at French National Magnetic Observatory

b405debe-ba05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sonoran Desert Skies Observatory in Pearce is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in East Bumble Bee, Cochise County, Arizona.
b405debe-ba05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sonoran Desert Skies Observatory, United States

b4112458-b902-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Langmuir Probe (LAP)** was an instrument onboard the ESA Rosetta mission, designed to measure various plasma properties such as density, temperature, and electric fields around comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko using two spherical probes.
b4112458-b902-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Langmuir Probe part of Rosetta Plasma Consortium

b417a874-b857-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Orbit/Attitude Info" is an auxiliary platform investigation conducted as part of the Rosetta mission. It provides useful orbit and attitude data for the spacecraft, which was produced by the WIGNER Research Centre for Physics in Hungary.
b417a874-b857-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Part of Rosetta Mission

b42827e8-b97f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SIM (Spectral Irradiance Monitor) on the SORCE mission is a rotating Fery prism spectrometer designed to measure solar irradiance in the 200-2,000 nm wavelength range with high accuracy and resolution.
b42827e8-b97f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spectral Irradiance Monitor on SORCE

b42aada8-b9c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) station at Tromsø, Sweden is a ground-based facility designed to study the upper atmosphere through observations of nocturnal airglow emissions. It is operated by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research (ISEE), Nagoya University, in collaboration with the EISCAT team and UiT The Arctic University of Norway.
b42aada8-b9c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research, Norway

b43a452e-ba5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Brooklyn Park Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Brooklyn Park, South Australia, primarily used for ground-based observations.
b43a452e-ba5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Brooklyn Park Observatory, Australia

b4492a96-b90d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Crimean Astrophysical Observatory (CrAO) is an astronomical observatory located in Nauchnij, near Bakhchysarai on the Crimean peninsula, known for its prolific discovery of minor planets.
b4492a96-b90d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.7m Telescope AZT-8 at Crimean Astrophysical Observatory, Ukraine

b4547986-b8cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **AUTH Observatory** is an astronomical ground-based observatory located in the Jewish Cemetery Monument area of Thessaloniki, Greece. It operates under Aristotle University of Thessaloniki and facilitates scientific research and public outreach activities related to astronomy and astrophysics.
b4547986-b8cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Aristotle University of Thessaloniki Observatory

b45d2fc0-b9fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Observatory of San Vito a Montelupo is an astronomical observatory located in Montelupo Fiorentino, Italy. It was established in 1992 and operates as a ground-based facility.
b45d2fc0-b9fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Observatory of San Vito a Montelupo, Italy

b468ed8e-ba2c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tri-Axial Fluxgate and Search-coil Magnetometers on FAST are instruments designed to measure magnetic fields, including a DC fluxgate magnetometer for low frequencies (up to 100 Hz) and an AC search coil magnetometer for higher frequencies (10 Hz to 2.5 kHz).
b468ed8e-ba2c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tri-Axial Fluxgate and Search-coil Magnetometers on FAST

b46a4c88-b9ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Express Orbiter (MEX) Planetary Fourier Spectrometer (PFS) is an instrument on the Mars Express spacecraft designed to analyze Martian radiation in two wavelength ranges using a double pendulum interferometer. It accurately controls and measures displacements, enabling simultaneous sampling of both spectral channels and efficient computation of Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT).
b46a4c88-b9ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Planetary Fourier Spectrometer on Mars Express Orbiter

b471d470-b9c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Akebono (EXOS-D) spacecraft is a satellite launched by JAXA/ISAS to study Earth's magnetosphere. It includes instruments such as the VLF receiver for scientific observations.
b471d470-b9c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VLF and MC on Akebono

b47b3686-b9b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Portable High-Speed Occultation Telescope Doc Camera is a specialized astronomical instrument featuring a high-speed photometric camera with a 512x1024 frame-transfer CCD, where only half of the device is receptive to light.
b47b3686-b9b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Portable High-Speed Occultation Telescope Doc Camera

b48b0728-b7e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tooele Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Stansbury Park, Utah, United States, known for its ground-based facilities.
b48b0728-b7e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stansbury Park Observatory

b493e340-b68f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Phillips Academy Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Phillips Academy in Andover, Massachusetts. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and education.
b493e340-b68f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Andover Observatory, United States

b4995bee-b6a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1K** is a component of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) mission, which involves launching balloons to study the escape of relativistic electrons from Earth's radiation belts by measuring Bremsstrahlung X-rays in the stratosphere.
b4995bee-b6a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses 1K part of Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses

b49b5c1e-b866-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **El Berrueco Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Madrid, Spain. It is situated at Camino Canteras, Pradera del Amor, El Berrueco, Community of Madrid, and operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
b49b5c1e-b866-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: El Berrueco Observatory, Spain

b4a71efa-b81b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tasiilaq (AMK) Geophysical Observatory, located in Solos Pynt, Tasiilaq, Greenland, is a ground-based facility established on January 1, 2007, for geophysical research and includes instruments such as a magnetometer.
b4a71efa-b81b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tasiilaq Geophysical Observatory, Greenland

b4a9d53c-b93d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Kolobov Observatory** is an astronomical ground observatory located at 38 Gornolyzhnaya Ulitsa in Novoabzakovo, Bashkiria, Russia. It operates within the Volga Federal District and is known for its contributions to astronomical research.
b4a9d53c-b93d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kolobov Observatory, Russia

b4ad96f6-bafd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Gamma Ray Imaging Platform (GRIP)** is an airborne facility designed for gamma-ray observations, providing capabilities in the gamma-ray waveband.
b4ad96f6-bafd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma Ray Imaging Platform

b4add5a0-bb4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Climax Observatory** was a high-altitude solar research facility established in 1940 near Climax, Colorado. It played a crucial role in studying the solar corona and its impact on radio communications, particularly during World War II, and later became part of NCAR until its closure in 1972.
b4add5a0-bb4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Coronagraph at Climax Observatory

b4b059ba-b75e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Apollo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at the Boonshoft Museum of Discovery in Dayton, Ohio. It is owned by the museum and operated by the Miami Valley Astronomical Society.
b4b059ba-b75e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Apollo Observatory at Dayton

b4b1463e-b666-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Würzburg University Observatory (MPC code 028) is an astronomical observatory located in Würzburg, Bavaria, Germany. Established in 1937, it operates as a ground-based facility with an altitude of 186 meters above sea level.
b4b1463e-b666-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Würzburg Observatory, Germany

b4b970cc-b619-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DSS-16 is a 26-meter diameter radio telescope located in San Bernardino County, California, originally part of NASA's Manned Space Flight Network and later used for tracking Earth orbiting satellites and communicating with the Space Shuttle.
b4b970cc-b619-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 26m DSS-16 Radio Telescope at Goldstone Observatory, United States
