b4bbbe6e-b6ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Negara Observatory is an astronomical facility located at the Langkawi Cable Car in Langkawi, Kedah, Malaysia. It serves as a ground-based observatory for studying celestial phenomena.
b4bbbe6e-b6ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Langkawi Observatory, Malaysia

b4d400fc-ba03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Guadarrama Observatory**: A ground-based astronomical observatory located in Madrid, Spain.
b4d400fc-ba03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Guadarrama Observatory, Spain

b4d75da4-bb72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Observatory of Atmospheric Environment in Rio Gallegos is a ground-based facility located in Rio Gallegos, Argentina, dedicated to atmospheric research and equipped with instruments such as the Millimeter Wave Spectroscopic Radiometer.
b4d75da4-bb72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter Wave Spectroscopic Radiometer at Observatory of Atmospheric Environment in Rio Gallegos, Argentina

b4e7b3fe-bb7f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Boltwood Observatory (Q114662593) is an astronomical observatory located in Stittsville, Ottawa, Ontario, Canada. It operates as a ground-based facility and has the Minor Planet Center ID 772.
b4e7b3fe-bb7f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Boltwood Observatory, Canada

b4f35908-bb33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rio Cofio Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Robledo de Chavela, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to studying celestial objects and phenomena from Earth.
b4f35908-bb33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rio Cofio Observatory, Spain

b4f4f730-bbf2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA High Energy Astronomy Observatory 3 (HEAO 3) was a satellite mission designed to study gamma-ray sources and perform high-resolution spectroscopy in space. It operated as part of the HEAO program, contributing significantly to the field of high energy astronomy.
b4f4f730-bbf2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: gamma-ray NASA High Energy Astronomy Observatory 3 Satellite Mission

b4f53868-bbb0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Green Bank Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the National Radio Quiet Zone in Green Bank, West Virginia, U.S., known for operating the Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope, the world's largest fully steerable radio telescope.
b4f53868-bbb0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope on Green Bank Observatory, United States

b4fea2e2-b861-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Tirunelveli station is a ground-based facility in Krishnapuram, Palayamkottai, Tamil Nadu, India (latitude 8.7, longitude 77.8), part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network for studying geomagnetic activity and space weather.
b4fea2e2-b861-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at MAGDAS Tirunelveli Observatory, India

b5011138-bc82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Clarkson University Geomagnetic Observatory** was a ground-based facility located in Potsdam, NY, that operated from June 16, 1999, to July 28, 2003, primarily for geomagnetic measurements.
b5011138-bc82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Clarkson University Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

b50df132-ba07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Artjärvi Observatory (also known as Viestikallio) is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Kimonkyläntie, Suurikylä, Orimattila, within the Lahti sub-region of Päijät-Häme, Finland. It is situated at coordinates 60.73447° N, 26.21154° E.
b50df132-ba07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Artjärvi Observatory, Finland

b510e0ba-bac8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Derby (DRBY) station in Vermont, USA is an Educational Public Outreach magnetometer site operated by UCLA as part of the NASA THEMIS project. It is located at North Country Union Junior High School and provides magnetic field data, though it may be influenced by environmental noise.
b510e0ba-bac8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at NASA THEMIS EPO Derby Station, United States

b51913d2-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tulsa Geomagnetic Observatory (TUL), located in Leonard, Oklahoma, USA, is a ground-based facility that has been operating since 1961 to monitor geomagnetic activity.
b51913d2-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tulsa Geomagnetic Observatory

b523a6ea-ba4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Cometary Secondary Ion Mass Analyzer (COSIMA) was a time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometer on the Rosetta Orbiter, designed to collect and analyze dust samples from comets. It included components like a dust collector, microscope, primary ion source, and mass spectrometer for detailed particle inspection.
b523a6ea-ba4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: The Cometary Secondary Ion Mass Analyzer on Rosetta Orbiter

b52c8586-badc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Cor2 is a coronagraph on the STEREO-A spacecraft, part of the SECCHI instrument suite, designed to observe the off-limb solar corona between 2.5 and 15 solar radii in visible light.
b52c8586-badc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Coronograph on STEREO-A

b537bc9c-ba34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Philadelphia and operational from January 1840 to December 1845, part of the IAGA observatory network.
b537bc9c-ba34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IAGA Observatory

b53a8500-b89d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Dst Index Observatory Group** is a network of ground-based magnetic field stations (Hermanus, Honolulu, Kakioka, and San Juan) that collectively calculate the Dst Index, a measure of global geomagnetic activity.
b53a8500-b89d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatory Group created to represent the chain of magnetic field stations used to calculate the Dst Index

b53efa20-ba43-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Meudon Observatory is a French astrophysical and solar observatory located in Meudon, France, established in 1876. It serves as an important ground-based facility for astronomical research, particularly focusing on the Sun.
b53efa20-ba43-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Meudon Observatory, France

b54cc1f6-ba79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS Search Coil Magnetometer (SCM) is an instrument designed to measure low-frequency magnetic field fluctuations and waves in three directions aboard the THEMIS spacecraft, covering a frequency range from 0.1 Hz to 4 kHz.
b54cc1f6-ba79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission

b54d36f2-b652-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: BARREL Balloon 3G is a scientific payload launched as part of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) mission to study electrons escaping Earth's radiation belts. It operated in the stratosphere from August 25, 2015, to August 26, 2015, carrying instruments like a NaI scintillator and a DC magnetometer for its investigations.
b54d36f2-b652-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: part of NASA Living with a Star Geospace Mission of Opportunity

b54f9e80-b862-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital receiver located in Bandung, Indonesia, designed to measure ionospheric total electron content using signals from Low Earth Orbit satellites. It employs GNU Radio software and USRP hardware for signal processing and acquisition at 150 and 400 MHz frequencies.
b54f9e80-b862-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: WaveformReceiver on GNU Radio Beacon Receiver part of IUGONET-Bandung Observatory

b553ef0c-ba93-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Equatorial Magnetometer Network's (IUGONET) magnetometer located in Colibri, Brazil is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate instrument designed to measure magnetic field variations.
b553ef0c-ba93-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Equatorial Magnetometer Network

b5558dc6-b8db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMN Colibri station is a ground-based facility located in Comodoro, Brazil, that operates as part of the EMN magnetometer network to monitor geomagnetic activity.
b5558dc6-b8db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Colibri Observatory, Brazil

b55e9eea-ba41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Shinshiro Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located at Aichi Prefectural Xincheng East High School in Shinshiro, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility used for stargazing and astronomical research.
b55e9eea-ba41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Shinshiro Observatory, Japan

b560df26-b8bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cylindrical Electrostatic Probes on ISIS 1** were Langmuir probe instruments used to study global variations in electron temperature and concentration at satellite altitudes during solar maximum, as well as characteristics of the satellite ion sheath. They consisted of two probes—a boom probe and an axial probe—designed to collect measurements relatively undisturbed by satellite motion or wake effects.
b560df26-b8bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cylindrical Electrostatic Probes part of ISIS 1

b567d0b6-bbe3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gaomeigu Gemini Observatory in Lijiang is an astronomical facility located at Ruhanping, Yulong Nakhi Autonomous County, Lijiang City, Yunnan, China. It serves as a ground-based observatory for various astronomical studies and observations.
b567d0b6-bbe3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gemini Telescope at Gaomeigu Observatory, China

b569fe48-b82f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ondřejov Observatory is an astronomical facility in the Czech Republic, located at the Czech Academy of Sciences in Ondřejov. It houses a 0.65-meter telescope and serves as a ground observatory for various astronomical studies.
b569fe48-b82f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.65m Telescope at Ondřejov Observatory, Czechia

b575ae2c-b6d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The **BARREL Balloon 2E X-ray Instrument (XRI)** is a scintillation detector used in the BARREL mission to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It employs a NaI crystal, photomultiplier tube, and peak detect board to convert X-ray energies into charge pulses for spectral analysis.
b575ae2c-b6d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-Ray Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

b580c2d6-b889-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Helios Ontígola Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Ontígola, Toledo, Spain. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
b580c2d6-b889-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Helios Ontigola Observatory, Spain

b58ad7d4-b808-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Simeiz Observatory was an astronomy research observatory located on Mount Koshka in Crimea, operational until the mid-1950s.
b58ad7d4-b808-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 22m Radio Telescope at Simeiz Observatory, Ukraine

b58ae192-b8ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Zaymishche ground station used to measure magnetic field data since 1957.
b58ae192-b8ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Zaymishche Observatory

b58c7fb2-b6c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ONCH-TBF electric and magnetic field probes on Aureol 3 were designed to measure the three components of the magnetic field at frequencies between 10 Hz and 16 kHz, providing comprehensive data on both electric and magnetic wave fields in various modes.
b58c7fb2-b6c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: WaveformReceiver part of Aureol 3

b5a11ed0-b999-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Poker Flat Geomagnetic Observatory** is a ground-based facility located in Pilot Bluff, Fairbanks North Star Borough, Alaska, United States. It has been operational since 1997 and includes an IUGONET instrument for geophysical observations.
b5a11ed0-b999-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Poker Flat Geophysical Observatory, United States

b5ac14d6-b9c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MEASURE observatory group, active from January 1999 to April 2004, consisted of multiple ground-based facilities dedicated to monitoring and research activities on Earth's surface.
b5ac14d6-b9c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millstone Hill Observatory

b5ae98ba-b6f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Toulouse Observatory (French: Observatoire de Toulouse) is an astronomical observatory located in Toulouse, France, established in 1733. It was primarily operational from 1882 to 1905 and housed ground-based instruments including magnetometers.
b5ae98ba-b6f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Toulouse Observatory, France

b5b28f9e-b971-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Odysseus, also known as the IM-1 mission, was the first commercial lunar lander to successfully reach the Moon, developed by Intuitive Machines under NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services program. It delivered a mix of NASA and commercial payloads and returned data for over 160 hours post-landing.
b5b28f9e-b971-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Odysseus part of Intuitive Machines IM-1 Mission

b5b86bd6-b817-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hubble Space Telescope (HST) is a joint NASA and European Space Agency (ESA) mission featuring a 2.4-meter aperture telescope designed to observe the universe primarily in ultraviolet wavelengths from its orbit in space.
b5b86bd6-b817-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ultraviolet 2.4m Hubble Space Telescope

b5bd000a-b9b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cruz del Sur Observatory is an astronomical facility located in San Justo, Buenos Aires, Argentina. It is a ground-based observatory dedicated to the study of celestial objects and phenomena from its Earthbound location.
b5bd000a-b9b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cruz del Sur Observatory, Argentina

b5bdc90c-bae5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Heavy Ion Detector (HID) on Double Star 1 is an Energetic Particle Instrument designed to detect heavy ions with atomic mass units greater than 4.
b5bdc90c-bae5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heavy Ion Detector on Double Star 1

b5c3db2e-ba5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Serra da Piedade Observatory, also known as SONEAR Wykrota-CEAMIG, is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Caeté, Minas Gerais, Brazil. It is situated at coordinates -19.82425 latitude and 316.31 longitude, within the Southeast Region of South America.
b5c3db2e-ba5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Serra da Piedadecode Observatory, Brazil

b5c4a17e-bb11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Wake Island Geomagnetic Observatory (WKE)** is a ground-based facility located on Wake Island at an altitude of 5.0 meters and coordinates 19.3° N, 167.6° E, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity as part of the IAGA observatory network.
b5c4a17e-bb11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Wake Island Geomagnetic Observatory

b5ca4cac-ba51-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operated in Prague from 1830 to 1926, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigations.
b5ca4cac-ba51-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Prague Observatory

b5cfd974-b7f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Comprehensive Suprathermal and Energetic Particle Instrument (COSTEP) on SOHO is a space-based instrument designed to measure solar particle emissions, including electrons and various ion species, over a wide range of energies using its LION and EPHIN sensors. It is part of the CEPAC experiment on board the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO).
b5cfd974-b7f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Comprehensive Suprathermal and Energetic Particle Instrument on SOHO

b5d18734-b6b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Haystack Observatory is a multidisciplinary radio science center and astronomical microwave observatory located in Westford, Massachusetts, owned by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).
b5d18734-b6b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Haystack Observatory, United States

b5d1d4ce-b815-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Schela Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Schela, Galați, Romania, identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code L23.
b5d1d4ce-b815-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Schela Observatory, Romania

b5d9b696-baca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital receiver located in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, designed for measuring ionospheric total electron content (TEC) by detecting signals from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites using GNU Radio software and USRP hardware.
b5d9b696-baca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver part of IUGONET Observatory, Malaysia

b5db648a-b969-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Aurora Web Camera (AWC) at Poker Flat, Alaska** is a digital camera operated by NICT and GI/UAF to capture real-time images of the aurora borealis, with its data accessible via the "Aurora Live!" website.
b5db648a-b969-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager on Poker Flat Observatory

b5e094a6-bae9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Tasmania 30m Telescope is a radio telescope located at the Ceduna Radio Observatory in Australia. It has an aperture of 30 meters and operates within the radio waveband, primarily used for astronomical observations.
b5e094a6-bae9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 30.0m Telescope at Ceduna Radio Observatory, Australia

b5f35dde-b887-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Wallace Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Westford, Massachusetts, operated as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
b5f35dde-b887-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Westford Observatory, United States

b6050d66-bb27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ultraviolet Photometer on Pioneer 11 was an instrument designed to measure UV radiation between 200 and 800 Å, primarily used to study the solar wind transition region and Jupiter's atmosphere during the spacecraft's mission.
b6050d66-bb27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Photometer on Pioneer 11

b614e716-bba6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The McMurdo Antenna Instrument is part of the ICESTAR investigation, located at the McMurdo ground station in Antarctica, and is used for various scientific observations.
b614e716-bba6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna on McMurdo Observatory, Antarctica

b61fd5a0-bbc3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Meschede Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Meschede, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the study of celestial bodies and phenomena from Earth.
b61fd5a0-bbc3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Meschede Observatory, Germany

b623066c-bb73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Yunling Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Yao'an County, Chuxiong, Yunnan Province, China. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
b623066c-bb73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yunling Observatory

b627cb9a-b978-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA/European Space Agency (ESA) 6.5m James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is a space mission featuring an infrared telescope designed to study the universe with unprecedented sensitivity and resolution, operating primarily in the optical waveband.
b627cb9a-b978-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 6.5m optical James Webb Space Telescope

b6283738-b78e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The JMU Space-Observatory is a ground observatory located at the Mineralogisches Museum on Hubland Campus Süd in Würzburg, Germany. It is situated at latitude 49.78261 and longitude 9.97013 within Europe.
b6283738-b78e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Observatory at Mineralogisches Museum, Würzburg

b62e6a88-bb10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Peawanuck Neutron Monitor is a ground-based scientific facility located in Peawanuck, Canada, designed to detect and measure neutrons as part of Earth's surface observation efforts.
b62e6a88-bb10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutron Monitor at Bartol Peawanuck Observatory, Canada

b631f148-ba58-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Phoenix Lander Robotic Arm Camera (RAC) was a color camera on the Mars Phoenix lander's robotic arm, designed to capture close-up and microscopic images of Martian surface materials and features not easily visible to other cameras.
b631f148-ba58-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Robotic Arm Camera on Phoenix Lander

b6375f9c-bbb2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Jicamarca, Peru (URSI-code: JI91J), established on July 20, 1993, is a ground facility that utilizes advanced ionosondes to analyze skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere, providing valuable data on angle of arrival, polarization, and Doppler frequency shift.
b6375f9c-bbb2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Ionospheric Station at Jicamarca, Peru

b63c6d7e-b898-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The East Asia VLBI Network (EAVN) is a ground-based observatory in Asia focused on millimeter waveband astronomy, utilizing Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) techniques to study distant celestial objects with high precision.
b63c6d7e-b898-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter East Asia Very Long Baseline Interferometry Network

b64f6130-ba60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Horus Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Cártama, Malaga, Andalusia, Spain. It operates as a ground-based observatory dedicated to the study and observation of celestial objects.
b64f6130-ba60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Horus Observatory, Spain

b661eaee-b9b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Spherical Elementary Current Systems (SECS) Magnetometer** is a virtual instrument that aggregates data from multiple ground magnetometer arrays across North America and Greenland to derive spherical elementary currents with a 10-second resolution. This instrument serves as a proxy for the varying set of contributing ground magnetometers, which may include arrays like CANMOS, CARISMA, DMI (in Greenland), GIMA, MACCS, THEMIS, and STEP.
b661eaee-b9b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Spherical Elementary Current Systems

b66450a0-bac3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **John J. McCarthy Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located at New Milford High School in Connecticut, established in 1998 for ground-based observations and educational purposes.
b66450a0-bac3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: John J. McCarthy Observatory

b6650a24-b68e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Clayhole Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Jokela, Tuusula, Finland. It is a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code C03.
b6650a24-b68e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Jokela Observatory, Finland

b66b06be-b7e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Weipa, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) network and IUGONET observatory, used for measuring magnetic field variations.
b66b06be-b7e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of 210 Magnetic Meridian Network

b66ec488-b96d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Viking Orbiter 2 Spacecraft Visual Imaging Subsystem - Camera B (VIS) was one of the twin high-resolution cameras onboard the Viking Orbiter 2, designed to capture detailed images of Mars' surface and atmosphere for scientific study and landing site selection.
b66ec488-b96d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visual Imaging Subsystem - Camera B on Viking Orbiter 2

b67ab814-b7f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: BARREL Balloon 1C was a high-altitude balloon mission launched on January 16, 2013, and concluded on January 26, 2013, as part of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) project. It aimed to study relativistic electrons escaping from Earth's radiation belts by measuring Bremsstrahlung X-rays in the stratosphere using a NaI scintillator and a DC magnetometer.
b67ab814-b7f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star Mission of Opportunity

b67aba96-b953-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Bernezzo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bernezzo, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations.
b67aba96-b953-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bernezzo Observatory, Italy

b686ba42-b775-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) station at Yonaguni, Japan is a ground facility developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research (ISEE), Nagoya University, to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions. It operates in collaboration with the Electronic Navigation Research Institute (ENRI)/NICT and features an all-sky imager as part of its instrumentation.
b686ba42-b775-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Yonaguni Station, Japan

b6894076-b899-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMN Christmas Island Station is a ground-based magnetometer network located in Tabwakea, Kiribati (latitude 2.0, longitude -157.5) on Earth's surface, part of the IUGONET observatory facilities.
b6894076-b899-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Christmas Island Observatory, Kiribati

b68b6102-bb1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) Airglow Temperature Photometer at Shigaraki, Japan is an instrument designed to measure airglow intensities and temperatures of OH and O2, as well as specific emission lines from OI and Na, to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere.
b68b6102-bb1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Airglow Temperature Photometer part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers

b694576c-b69c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, particularly the Earth's magnetic field. The Mould Bay Ground Magnetic Field Instrument, operational from 1962 to 1997, was part of the IUGONET Observatory and contributed data under the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network.
b694576c-b69c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mould Bay Observatory

b694f298-bbbb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) Two-Channel Tilting Photometer at Shigaraki, Japan is an instrument that measures airglow emissions at specific wavelengths to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere, performing meridian-scanning and zenith observations since 1998.
b694f298-bbbb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Two-Channel Tilting Photometer part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at Shigaraki Observatory, Japan

b69dd52e-bacc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Steward Observatory 0.9-meter telescope on Kitt Peak** is a ground-based astronomical instrument located in Arizona, United States, with an effective clear aperture of 0.93 meters from the year 2002 onward due to reconfigured optics.
b69dd52e-bacc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.9 meter Telescope at Steward Observatory on Kitt Peak, United States

b6aaa2cc-ba86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **El Cielo de Consell Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in the Balearic Islands, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
b6aaa2cc-ba86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: El Cielo de Consell Observatory, Spain

b6aaf924-b771-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "DSS-33" refers to a ground-based observatory, specifically part of the Deep Space Station 33. It is used for space communication and astronomical observations.
b6aaf924-b771-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep Space Station 33, Antarctica

b6ae8bae-b729-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The North West Pacific Geomagnetic Observatory (NWP), located on Earth at coordinates 41.102° N, 159.963° E, is a ground-based facility sponsored by Japan that operates magnetometer instruments to monitor geomagnetic activity in the North West Pacific region.
b6ae8bae-b729-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North West Pacific Geomagnetic Observatory

b6aee73c-b70d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Multicomponent Investigations of Fluctuations of Magnetic Fields (MIF-M) on the Interball Tail Probe is a magnetometer designed to measure both DC and AC magnetic fields using flux-gate and search-coil sensors, providing high-quality data across various frequency ranges for studying magnetic field fluctuations in space.
b6aee73c-b70d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Multicomponent Investigations of Fluctuations of Magnetic Fields on Interball Tail Probe

b6c50f5a-b59e-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The COR1 telescope is part of the Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation (SECCHI) instrument suite aboard the STEREO-A spacecraft, designed to observe the white light corona from 1.4 to 4 solar radii.
b6c50f5a-b59e-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Coronograph part of Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation on Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory A

b6ca4e54-bb69-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 4 Energetic Ion Spectrometer (EIS) is an instrument onboard the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission that measures ion composition and angular distributions within the energy range of ~45 keV to 500 keV, utilizing a time-of-flight/pulse-height sensor with a temporal resolution of 30 seconds.
b6ca4e54-bb69-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Ion Spectrometer on Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

b6cc596a-b821-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Netherlands Institute for Radio Astronomy (ASTRON) Westerbork Synthesis Radio Telescope (WSRT) is a radio telescope array located in the Netherlands, Europe. It operates in the radio waveband and is used for astronomical research.
b6cc596a-b821-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Westerbork Synthesis Radio Telescope at Netherlands Institute for Radio Astronomy ASTRON

b6d08c82-b741-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: "The Viking Position Instrument is a platform within the CDPP Archive of CNES, providing spacecraft positional data and geomagnetic parameters for the Viking mission."
b6d08c82-b741-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Viking Position on CNES Observatory

b6d52ec6-bb2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Yamada Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Kama, Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan. It is designated by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with ID 363 and operates as a ground-based observatory focused on astronomical research.
b6d52ec6-bb2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yamada Observatory, Japan

b6e79e3c-b68c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2X Optical Photometer is an instrument designed to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm during relativistic electron precipitation events, specifically to determine the presence of accompanying protons and support the understanding of electromagnetic ion cyclotron (EMIC) waves as a precipitation mechanism.
b6e79e3c-b68c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

b6ef9810-b189-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Charge, Element, and Isotope Analysis System (CELIAS) on the SOHO spacecraft is an experiment designed to study the composition of solar wind and accelerated energetic particles using four specialized sensors. It provides detailed measurements of particle energy ranges and EUV flux from the sun, complementing other experiments on SOHO.
b6ef9810-b189-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Charge, Element, and Isotope Analysis System part of Solar and Heliospheric Observatory

b6f1768a-b783-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Willis Island Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor** is a specialized GPS receiver system located near Willis Island, Queensland, Australia, designed to monitor ionospheric scintillation levels in real time. It uses wide-bandwidth tracking loops and high sampling rates to collect detailed scintillation statistics for up to eleven visible GPS satellites.
b6f1768a-b783-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor part of Willis Island Observatory, Australia

b6fd2472-b73c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Eusebio Station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Eusébio, Brazil, part of the CPMN magnetometer network under ICSWSE.
b6fd2472-b73c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eusebio Station, Brazil

b703562e-b75c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Richardson Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, operational since January 4, 2007.
b703562e-b75c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Richardson Observatory

b726e688-b9a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: MINERVA-Australis is a set of 0.7m optical telescopes located at the Mount Kent Observatory in Australia, part of Oceania.
b726e688-b9a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.7m The MINERVA-Australis Telescope and The MINERVA-Australis Telescope at Mount Kent Observatory, Australia

b73fb4fa-bb82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Hevonen Farm Observatory in Oxford is a ground-based astronomical observatory located at Scott Road, Milford Township, Butler County, Ohio. It is situated at coordinates 39.49212° N, 84.61981° W in the United States.
b73fb4fa-bb82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hevonen Farm Observatory at Oxford

b742c02c-b81d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The KT17 is a dynamic model designed to represent Mercury's magnetospheric magnetic field, taking into account factors such as heliocentric distance and magnetic activity. It serves as an analytical tool within the BepiColombo mission under the CNES observatory and CDPP-AMDA facilities.
b742c02c-b81d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mercury Magnetic Field Model part of BepiColombo

b7505724-b5e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2.24-m Cassegrain/Coude reflector is a telescope with a 2.24-meter aperture located at the Mauna Kea Observatory in Hawaii, operational since November 1970 and managed by the University of Hawaii.
b7505724-b5e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.24m Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatory, United States

b751208e-bb3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Wisconsin Diffuse X-ray Spectrometer (DXS) is an instrument that was carried aboard the Space Shuttle mission STS-54 to observe and measure diffuse X-ray emissions in space.
b751208e-bb3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-Ray University of Wisconsin Diffuse X-ray Spectrometer on Space Transportation System 54

b7544d74-ba57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Alice Ultraviolet Imaging Spectrograph is a compact and efficient instrument aboard the New Horizons mission designed to study atmospheric compositions and ultraviolet surface reflectivity of celestial bodies like Pluto, Charon, and Kuiper Belt objects.
b7544d74-ba57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet The Alice Ultraviolet Imaging Spectrograph on New Horizons

b7698806-b787-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Yamagata Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Yamagata, Yamagata Prefecture, Japan. It operates as a ground-based observatory for conducting various astronomical studies and observations.
b7698806-b787-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yamagata Observatory, Japan

b769a4ac-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Los Molinos Observatory is an astronomical observatory in Montevideo, Uruguay, operated by the Ministerio de Educación y Cultura and the University of the Republic's Astronomy Department.
b769a4ac-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Astronómico Los Molinos, Uruguay

b76fbdd2-b996-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) mission is a NASA satellite constellation designed to study the transition from the solar corona to the heliosphere by imaging sunlight scattered off free electrons and tracking coronal mass ejections.
b76fbdd2-b996-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere part of Explorers Program

b781fdfa-b64c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Da Lat Magnetic Observatory (DLT) is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Đà Lạt, Vietnam, operating since 1991 and sponsored by the Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology.
b781fdfa-b64c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Da Lat Geomagnetic Observatory, Vietnam

b7879696-b6e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Northern Arizona University Observatory (MPC ID: 687) is an astronomical observatory located at Northern Arizona University in Flagstaff, Arizona. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and education.
b7879696-b6e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Flagstaff Observatory, United States

b78872ec-b5f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Canterbury 1m McLellan Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Mount John University Observatory in Australia. It has an aperture of 1 meter and is part of the observatory facilities on Mount John, situated within Oceania.
b78872ec-b5f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: McLellan Optical Telescope at Mount John Observatory

b795dc0c-b60c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **CWU-Lind Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in Ellensburg, Washington, United States. It is operated by Central Washington University and used for educational and research purposes.
b795dc0c-b60c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lind Observatory

b79c2b70-b170-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mount Belleview Observatory, located in Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, Quebec, Canada, is an astronomical observatory known for its ground-based observations.
b79c2b70-b170-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Mount Belleview Observatory, United States

b7a782be-bb15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Great Wall Station is a ground-based observatory located at HSM 52, Zhongzhi Road on Earth's surface, operational from January 1, 1986, to December 31, 1989, primarily known for its magnetometer instrument.
b7a782be-bb15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Great Wall Station Observatory

b7ad138e-b64f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The ELFIN mission's Energetic Particle Detector for Electrons (EPDE) is an instrument designed to measure electron energy levels between 50 keV and 4.5 MeV, featuring a narrow field of view within the loss cone to provide unique insights into relativistic electron fluxes in Earth’s radiation belts.
b7ad138e-b64f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Detector for Electrons part of The Electron Losses and Fields Investigation mission

b7ad6b90-bba9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nubbin Ridge Observatory is an astronomical observatory located on Forestridge Road in Garland County, Arkansas, USA. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
b7ad6b90-bba9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nubbin Ridge Observatory, United States

b7b15b6e-b9e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at Kap Tobin was an instrument used from 1959 to 1967 for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IAGA investigation at the observatory in Kyoto.
b7b15b6e-b9e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Kap Tobin Observatory

b7b504ee-b745-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: NOAA 6 was an operational meteorological satellite launched in 1979 to measure Earth's atmosphere, surface, and cloud cover as part of the National Operational Environmental Satellite System (NOESS) and the Global Atmospheric Research Program (GARP).
b7b504ee-b745-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer and TIROS Operational Vertical Sounder on NOAA 6

b7b83c4a-bb64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Stazione Astronomica Betelgeuse is an astronomical observatory located in Magnago, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting various astronomical observations and research.
b7b83c4a-bb64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Betelgeuse Observatory at Magnago, Italy

b7be8848-bbaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sukkertoppen Geomagnetic Observatory (SKT), located in Maniitsoq, Greenland, is a ground-based facility that monitors geophysical data, including magnetic field measurements.
b7be8848-bbaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Sukkertoppen Geophysical Observatory, Greenland

b7bf3f86-bbc8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Vanimo Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor** is a specialized GPS receiver located in Vanimo, Papua New Guinea, designed to track and record ionospheric scintillation levels in real time, providing crucial data for atmospheric research. It employs wide-bandwidth tracking loops and high sampling rates to calculate key scintillation statistics, such as S4 and Prms, even during strong scintillation events.
b7bf3f86-bbc8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor part of Vanimo Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor, Papua New Guinea

b7c3fb0e-b9aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Multan, Pakistan (URSI-code: MU230), also known as GIRO/MU320_Multan, is a ground-based facility equipped with a Digisonde that analyzes ionospheric reflections to determine their angle of arrival, polarization, Doppler frequency shift, and travel time.
b7c3fb0e-b9aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde Ionosonde at Ionospheric Station, Pakistan

b7c4ffc8-b832-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Astronomical Observatory of San Pedro Mártir is an astronomical observatory located in Baja California, Mexico.
b7c4ffc8-b832-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.5m Johnson Telescope at National Astronomical Observatory of San Pedro Mártir, Mexico

b7ce7934-b717-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Psyche Neutron Spectrometer (NS) is an instrument aboard the Psyche spacecraft designed to detect, measure, and map the elemental composition of asteroid (16) Psyche. It is mounted on a boom to minimize background radiation interference and ensure an unobstructed field of view.
b7ce7934-b717-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutron Spectrometer on Psyche Spacecraft

b7e044a0-bb3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Tenagra Observatories**: An international network of astronomical observatories located in Cottage Grove, Oregon, United States.
b7e044a0-bb3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tenagra Observatories

b7e251c4-b9d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Qiongzhong Geomagnetic Observatory (QGZ), located in Yinggen, China, is a ground facility dedicated to geomagnetic measurements and research. It has been operational since 1995 and includes the iugonet-instrument-wdc_kyoto-wdc-qgz magnetometer as part of its infrastructure.
b7e251c4-b9d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Qiongzhong Observatory, China

b7e28578-bb95-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lowell Observatory Near-Earth-Object Search (LONEOS) was a NASA-funded project based at the Lowell Observatory in Flagstaff, Arizona, aimed at discovering asteroids and comets that orbit near Earth. The project operated from 1993 to 2008 under the direction of astronomer Ted Bowell.
b7e28578-bb95-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lowell Observatory Near-Earth-Object Search part of Lowell Observatory

b7e94bf8-bc01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **HelioSwarm Ephemeris** is a platform investigation that provides the positional data (ephemeris) of the HelioSwarm spacecraft as part of the CNES-Observatory CDPP-AMDA Helioswarm.
b7e94bf8-bc01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: HelioSwarm Ephemeris part of HelioSwarm

b7ea1032-bae0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Catholic University Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at the Catholic University of America in Washington, D.C., dedicated to ground-based observations and research in astronomy.
b7ea1032-bae0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Catholic University Observatory

b7eb2dc6-b614-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** GOES 16 (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite-R) is a next-generation weather satellite launched in 2016 to enhance the detection and observation of environmental phenomena critical for public safety and economic health. It provides advanced imaging with increased spatial resolution, faster coverage, real-time lightning mapping, and improved solar activity monitoring.
b7eb2dc6-b614-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite-R Series part of Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite

b7eead1a-b8c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Manado Magnetometer is an instrument located at the IAGA-identified station MND, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the observatory network.
b7eead1a-b8c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Manado Observatory

b7ffcf88-b722-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Karmakuli Magnetometer was an instrument used from 1977 to 1980 at the IAGA observatory in Karmakuli for measuring magnetic fields.
b7ffcf88-b722-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Karmakuli Observatory

b8033a46-b75f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Wind Experiment (SWE) on the Wind spacecraft is an electrostatic analyzer designed to measure solar wind flow parameters in real time, providing three-dimensional velocity distribution functions for ions and electrons with high time resolution. It includes Faraday Cups for ion measurements and electrostatic analyzers for electron distributions, covering energy ranges from 7 eV to 30 keV for electrons and 30 eV to 5 keV for ions.
b8033a46-b75f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer on Wind Spacecraft

b80ca48a-bb9e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Shache Station in Langan Village is a ground-based astronomical observatory located at Tuhe Expressway, Odanliq, Yarkant County, Kashgar, Xinjiang, China. It operates at the coordinates 38.38447° N latitude and 77.13931° E longitude.
b80ca48a-bb9e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Shache Station at Langan Village Observatory, China

b810800a-b829-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AAS Montsec Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Sant Esteve de la Sarga, Lleida, Catalonia, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility and is part of the larger Montsec Astronomical Observatory complex.
b810800a-b829-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Observatori AAS Montsec, Spain

b81275b4-bb70-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Istanbul University Observatory is an astronomical observatory operated by Istanbul University's Astronomy and Space Sciences Department, located in the Fatih district of Istanbul, Turkey. Established in 1936, it is situated next to the historic Beyazıt Tower within the university's main campus.
b81275b4-bb70-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Istanbul Observatory

b82da174-bb6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Turin Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Turin, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
b82da174-bb6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Turin Observatory, Italy

b83700d6-b649-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NOAA 11 Solar Backscatter Ultraviolet Radiometer (SBUV/2) is an instrument designed to measure the vertical distribution of ozone in Earth's atmosphere by analyzing backscattered solar radiation at specific wavelength bands. It also includes a cloud cover radiometer (CCR) for measuring surface brightness.
b83700d6-b649-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Backscatter Ultraviolet Radiometer on NOAA 11

b83d0bb4-ba0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Pleiades Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Mandeville, Quebec, Canada, known for its ground-based facilities.
b83d0bb4-ba0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mandeville Observatory, Canada

b83fdd88-bba2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Adelaide Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Middle Beach, South Australia, part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network. It houses a magnetometer and has been operational since January 1973.
b83fdd88-bba2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Adelaide Observatory, Australia

b84c75f6-bb21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "New Horizons KBO Search-Subaru" is a ground-based astronomical instrument located at the Mauna Kea Observatories in Hawaii, United States. It was used as part of the New Horizons mission to search for Kuiper Belt Objects (KBOs).
b84c75f6-bb21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: [aperture unknown] Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatories, United States

b84def5a-b705-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LANL1991 Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer (MPA) is an instrument designed to measure three-dimensional energy/charge distributions of ions and electrons in the magnetosphere, featuring high sensitivity and moderate resolution for use at synchronous orbit. It consists of a single electrostatic analyzer coupled with channel electron multipliers, providing comprehensive coverage of spacecraft azimuth angles through rotation.
b84def5a-b705-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of LANL 1991

b8637888-bb0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Linear Etalon Imaging Spectral Array (L'LEISA) is an infrared spectrometer onboard NASA’s Lucy mission, operating within a spectral range of 1.0 to 3.6 microns and providing a spectral resolution of 10 nm, designed for imaging and spectral analysis as part of the L'Ralph instrument suite.
b8637888-bb0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared The Linear Etalon Imaging Spectral Array on Lucy

b875a9c4-b6be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Oppolzer Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in Vienna, Austria. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial objects and phenomena.
b875a9c4-b6be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Oppolzer Observatory, Austria

b8762ea8-b74a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Kakadu station with the IAGA identifier KDU, part of the WDC Kyoto observatory network.
b8762ea8-b74a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kakadu Observatory

b87a55d2-b7db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA station identified as SRO in the Srobarova observatory. It is part of the IUGONET-Observatory network managed by the WDC Kyoto.
b87a55d2-b7db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IAGA

b87cba12-b695-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Visual and Infrared Mapping Spectrometer for Cassini Orbiter (CO) is an instrument designed to capture spectral data in visible and infrared wavelengths, enabling the analysis of planetary atmospheres, surfaces, and rings. It provides crucial information on composition, temperature, and structure as part of its mission aboard the Cassini spacecraft.
b87cba12-b695-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visual and Infrared Mapping Spectrometer on Cassini Orbiter

b885fae8-bc10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Energetic Neutral Atom (ENA) Imager on TWINS-2 is an instrument designed to capture charge-exchange-produced neutral atoms over a broad energy range, part of the TWINS mission under NASA's Small Explorer program.
b885fae8-bc10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Neutral Atom Imager on TWINS-2 part of Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers

b8956978-b667-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Leuschner Observatory is an astronomical observatory jointly operated by the University of California, Berkeley and San Francisco State University, originally built in 1886 on the Berkeley campus and later relocated to Lafayette, California.
b8956978-b667-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Leuschner Observatory

b8a6318a-bbb8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 3 Energetic Ion Spectrometer (EIS), part of the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission, is an instrument that uses a time-of-flight/pulse-height sensor to measure ion composition and angular distributions in the energy range of ~45 keV to 500 keV with a temporal resolution of 30 seconds.
b8a6318a-bbb8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Ion Spectrometer part of MMS 3 EPD Suite

b8c1684a-b9f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The European Southern Observatory (ESO) VISTA is a 4.1-meter telescope located at the Paranal Observatory in South America, designed for optical and near-infrared astronomical surveys.
b8c1684a-b9f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for Astronomy at Paranal Observatory

b8c8edc2-bb6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The European Space Agency (ESA) 0.6m Infrared Space Observatory (ISO) Satellite Mission was an infrared space telescope operated by the European Space Agency, designed to observe celestial objects in the infrared waveband with a primary mirror diameter of 0.6 meters.
b8c8edc2-bb6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared European Space Agency (ESA) 0.6m Infrared Space Observatory (ISO) Satellite Mission

b8cb59cc-b89a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Greenhill Observatory is an astronomical facility operated by the University of Tasmania, located on Bisdee Tier near Spring Hill, Tasmania. It was named after astrophysicist Dr. John G. Greenhill and opened in February 2013.
b8cb59cc-b89a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.27m Harlingten Telescope at Greenhill Observatory, Australia

b8cbe30c-ba88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Au-Tau Observatory was a ground facility located in Hong Kong, China, operational from January 1928 to December 31, 1939, primarily known for its magnetometer instrumentation.
b8cbe30c-ba88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IAGA Observatory, China

b8d6f75c-bc94-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Islamabad observatory is a ground-based facility located in Zone III, Islamabad Capital Territory, Pakistan, operating since 2008. It includes a magnetometer and is part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
b8d6f75c-bc94-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Islamabad Observatory, Pakistan

b8db405a-b68b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SwarthmoreNewark Neutron Monitor is an Energetic Particle Instrument operated by the Bartol Research Institute, designed to measure neutron flux as part of the Neutron Monitor network.
b8db405a-b68b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutron Monitor part of Swarthmore Newark Investigation

b8dfb4d6-b5c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 45th Parallel Observatory in Pino Torinese is an astronomical ground observatory located in Turin, Italy. It is situated at a latitude of 45.04458 and longitude of 7.77039, offering a strategic point for celestial observations due to its position on the 45th parallel north.
b8dfb4d6-b5c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 45th Parallel Observatory, Italy

b8e5cc98-b724-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Amami-Oh-shima Station is a ground facility located in Agina, Setouchi, Oshima County, Kagoshima Prefecture, Japan, functioning as part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network to monitor magnetic fields.
b8e5cc98-b724-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Amami-Oshima Observatory, Japan

b8e6ba68-b995-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kuujjuaq Magnetometer is an instrument located at the Kuujjuaq Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG. It measures variations in the Earth's magnetic field and has been operational since November 27, 2007.
b8e6ba68-b995-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kuujjuaq Observatory

b8f01c4a-baf6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Giotto was the European Space Agency’s (ESA) first deep space mission, launched to study Comet Halley by performing a close flyby of its nucleus on 14 March 1986. Despite sustaining damage from comet dust during this encounter, most of its instruments remained operational, and the mission was extended for an additional flyby of Comet Grigg-Skjellerup in 1992.
b8f01c4a-baf6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Giotto part of ESA's First Deep Space Mission

b8f060be-bb4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Tasmania UTAS 0.4m (16-inch) telescope at Mount Canopus is a ground observatory located in Australia, part of the University's astronomical facilities.
b8f060be-bb4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 40cm Telescope at Mount Canopus Observatory

b90b3c98-b833-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tikhaya Bay Geomagnetic Observatory (TKH) was a ground-based facility located in the Primorsky District of Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia, operational from 1932 to 1958, known for its geomagnetic research.
b90b3c98-b833-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tikhaya Bay Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

b90cafaa-ba73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ISIS 2 Fixed-Frequency Sounder** is an instrument on the ISIS 2 satellite designed to study small-scale ionospheric features and plasma resonances by measuring virtual range and time, typically during specific periods of operation.
b90cafaa-ba73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fixed-Frequency Sounder part of International Satellites for Ionospheric Studies 2

b913ebf6-b8d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NEAScout camera is a monochromatic instrument designed for both optical navigation and scientific imaging on the Near-Earth Asteroid Scout mission. It offers high-resolution capabilities, allowing for target detection and detailed close-up imaging at distances up to 800 meters with resolutions of less than 10 centimeters.
b913ebf6-b8d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Earth Asteroid Scout Camera on Near Earth Asteroid Scout

b9150d0e-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Plateau Geomagnetic Observatory (PTU)** was a ground-based facility located on Earth's surface at an altitude of 3620 meters, operational from February 1966 to December 1968. It was equipped with instruments such as the Iugonet magnetometer and was part of the Kyoto WDC (World Data Center) network.
b9150d0e-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Plateau Observatory

b9177a60-bb2d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Hyperion Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Urbanización Caraquiz, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial objects and phenomena.
b9177a60-bb2d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hyperion Observatory, Spain

b91cdcd2-b80b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Double Star mission was a collaborative space project between the China National Space Administration (CNSA) and the European Space Agency (ESA), designed to study the effects of the Sun on Earth's magnetosphere using two satellites, TC-1 and TC-2.
b91cdcd2-b80b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Explorer on Double Star part of China National Space Administration and European Space Agency

b91e78b0-b8df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer onboard Pioneer 11 used to measure the magnetic fields of Jupiter and Saturn, capable of detecting fields ranging from 0.01 to 10 gauss along each axis.
b91e78b0-b8df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Pioneer 11

b92d7ae2-bbd0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometers at Narsarsuaq (NAQ) are part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation, which started on October 1, 2008.
b92d7ae2-bbd0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission

b92eaf00-ba47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Los Algarrobos Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Salto, Uruguay. It operates as a ground-based observatory focused on celestial observations and research.
b92eaf00-ba47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Los Algarrobos Observatory, Uruguay

b93874c2-b6b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Watec All-sky TV camera** is an automated optical instrument with a white-light all-sky CCD camera used for conjugate observations of auroral phenomena, operated at Syowa Station in Antarctica and Husafell in Iceland. It is part of the IUGONET Observatory network managed by WDC Kyoto.
b93874c2-b6b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Watec All-sky TV camera part of Syowa-Iceland Conjugate observation of Auroral phenomena

b9403382-b59d-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the GSJ53 Goose Bay Ionospheric Station in Canada, which is an advanced ground facility equipped with a Digisonde for studying ionospheric reflections.
b9403382-b59d-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Station at Goose Bay Observatory, Canada

b9469c8c-b7fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Casey Riometer, located at the Casey station in Antarctica since 1989, is a specialized instrument used to measure ionospheric absorption by comparing received cosmic radio noise with calibration curves, primarily for monitoring solar-generated high energy protons and detecting polar cap absorption.
b9469c8c-b7fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Riometer part of Australian Bureau of Meteorology's Space Weather Services, Antarctica

b9597d9c-bb83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The North Pole 12 Geomagnetic Observatory (NPL) was a ground-based facility located at coordinates 79.08° N, 187.22° E, sponsored by Russia and operational from 1963 to 1964. It included a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements.
b9597d9c-bb83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole 12 Geomagnetic Observatory

b95f3412-bb60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The BDI Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Belbowrie Close, Bangor, Sydney, Australia. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
b95f3412-bb60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bangor Observatory, Australia

b9624550-b915-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Lake Arrowhead Observatory is an astronomical facility located in San Bernardino County, California, USA. It operates as a ground-based observatory used for scientific research and observations of celestial bodies.
b9624550-b915-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lake Arrowhead Observatory, United States

b96898a4-b5ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan known as the JCPM Kimachi Station.
b96898a4-b5ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kimachi Observatory, Japan

b96ffbd6-b795-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a magnetometer instrument located at the Kzil-Agach station (identified by IAGA as KZA) that operated from January 1, 1974, to December 31, 1975. It was part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy's (IAGA) network and is associated with the WDC Kyoto observatory.
b96ffbd6-b795-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of World Data Center for Geomagnetism

b9760b84-b727-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A millimeter-wave spectroscopic radiometer is an instrument used to monitor the vertical distributions of minor atmospheric constituents in the stratosphere and mesosphere, equipped with a superconducting receiver installed at the Tsukuba observatory.
b9760b84-b727-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter-wave Spectroscopic Radiometer part of ISEE, Japan

b987a2d4-b792-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CORALL instrument on the Interball Tail Probe satellite is a wide-range electrostatic analyzer used for measuring ion energy distribution in three dimensions. It performs quasi-3D measurements of the Energy/Charge ion distribution function within an energy range from 30 to 24,200 eV/q and has a fan-shaped field of view of 10 x 150 degrees.
b987a2d4-b792-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser on Interball Tail Probe

b987b6c0-b5b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Moriyama Observatory (code: 900) is an astronomical observatory located in Moriyama, Shiga Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
b987b6c0-b5b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Moriyama Observatory, Japan

b98dab00-b7c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Ancon Station is a ground-based magnetometer observatory located in Ciudad Pyme, Ancón, Peru, part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network.
b98dab00-b7c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ancon Observatory, Peru

b9c5521a-b845-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **François-Xavier Bagnoud Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Luc, Switzerland, at an altitude of 2,200 meters. It is a non-profit organization funded by the Association François-Xavier Bagnoud.
b9c5521a-b845-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: François-Xavier Bagnoud Observatory, Switzerland

b9cca664-b868-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) is a collaborative project between the European Space Agency and Roscosmos, designed to investigate trace gases in Mars' atmosphere from orbit and support communications for future surface missions.
b9cca664-b868-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Trace Gas Orbiter part of ExoMars

b9d253e0-b6bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The East Asian Observatory 15m James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT) is a 15-meter telescope located at the Mauna Kea Observatory in North America, designed for millimeter waveband observations.
b9d253e0-b6bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 15.0m millimeter East Asian Observatory James Clerk Maxwell Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatory

b9ddc536-b708-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Harris (HRIS) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility in Altai, Khovd, Mongolia, part of the FALCON Air Force Magnetometer Array. It operates as a component of the THEMIS Ground Observatory network and has been active since November 1, 2009.
b9ddc536-b708-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Harris Geophysical Observatory, Mongolia

b9e47d80-b9fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tenagra II Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Nogales, Arizona, United States. It is part of the Tenagra Observatories and has been operational since January 1, 2000.
b9e47d80-b9fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Tenagra II Observatory

b9f13d52-bbde-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: BeppoSAX was an Italian-Dutch satellite designed to observe the universe in the gamma-ray waveband. It was a collaboration between the Italian Space Agency (ASI) and the Netherlands Agency for Aerospace Programme (NIVR).
b9f13d52-bbde-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma-ray Italian Space Agency and Netherlands Agency for Aerospace Programme BeppoSAX X-ray satellite

b9f1feca-bb63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ThemisC Different Magnetospheric Analytical Models** is a collection of computational tools used for analyzing and understanding the dynamics and structure of Earth's magnetosphere. It is part of the THEMIS mission and facilitates scientific research by providing various analytical models to study magnetic fields, plasma interactions, and other related phenomena within the magnetosphere.
b9f1feca-bb63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetospheric Analytical Models part of Themis Mission

b9f3888a-ba1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **North Pole 12**: A ground-based observatory located at the Earth's surface, operational from January 1, 1963, to December 31, 1964, part of the IAGA Observatory network, equipped with a magnetometer.
b9f3888a-ba1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole 12 Observatory

b9f7f654-ba19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Digitized Sky Survey (DSS) is a digital compilation of several photographic astronomical surveys conducted from the Palomar Observatory, providing a comprehensive view of the night sky.
b9f7f654-ba19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digitized Sky Survey part of Palomar Observatory, United States

ba04f03e-bc53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Floeberg Beach station (IAGA identifier FLB), used for geomagnetic measurements since 1876.
ba04f03e-bc53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Floeberg Beach Observatory

ba0b1744-b644-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Qianling Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Qian County, Xianyang, Shaanxi, China. It operates a magnetometer and has been functional since January 1, 1995.
ba0b1744-b644-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Qianling Observatory, China

ba0bf620-bbab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Malyye Karmakuly Magnetometer is an instrument located at the IAGA-identified MKL station in Malyye Karmakuly, operational since 1883, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigations.
ba0bf620-bbab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Malyye Karmakuly Observatory

ba0cf538-b990-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: MARA (MAscot RAdiometer) is a high-resolution radiometer onboard the MASCOT lander, designed to measure surface temperature and thermal variations on asteroids during their day-night cycles.
ba0cf538-b990-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radiometer on MASCOT Lander

ba0d1a60-bb0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Jaipur Magnetic Observatory was a ground-based facility located in Jaipur, India, that operated from 1976 to 1987 for the purpose of measuring and studying Earth's magnetic field.
ba0d1a60-bb0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Jaipur Observatory, India

ba11fa02-bad9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) satellites** are a series of U.S. military weather satellites operated by the Department of Defense (DoD) and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), designed to collect meteorological, oceanographic, and solar-geophysical information in the gamma-ray waveband.
ba11fa02-bad9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma-ray Defense Meteorological Satellite Program satellites

ba157df8-babb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1V Engineering Data Interface** is a component of the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) that converts analog signals such as temperatures, voltages, and currents into digital data with high precision.
ba157df8-babb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses part of BARREL

ba171982-b9d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **LANL-01A Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer (SOPA)** is an energetic particle instrument consisting of three silicon detector telescopes designed to measure differential fluxes of protons, electrons, and various ions in synchronous orbit. It features a sharp angular cutoff and passive cooling to minimize noise, providing detailed measurements across specific energy ranges for different particles.
ba171982-b9d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer part of Los Alamos National Laboratory

ba29bb98-ba2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Viking Lander 2 Spacecraft Camera 1 was a facsimile camera used on the Viking Lander 2 mission to Mars. It employed a single, stationary photosensor array and azimuth/elevation scanning mechanisms to capture images by scanning scenes in two directions.
ba29bb98-ba2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Camera 1 on Viking Lander 2

ba2f5a9a-ba87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Ingle Farm Observatory (code: D85) is an astronomical observatory located in Bryant Avenue, Ingle Farm, Adelaide, South Australia. It operates as a ground-based facility for conducting and supporting astronomical observations.
ba2f5a9a-ba87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ingle Farm Observatory, Australia

ba3013fa-ba4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Atmospheric Structure Instrument and Meteorology Package (ASI/MET) was an engineering subsystem on the Mars Pathfinder Lander that collected atmospheric data, including temperature, pressure, and wind speed, using various sensors during different mission phases.
ba3013fa-ba4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Atmospheric Structure Instrument and Meteorology Package on Mars Pathfinder Lander

ba39db6a-b608-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Estrella de Mar Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Torre de Benagalbón, Málaga, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
ba39db6a-b608-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Estrella de Mar Observatory, Spain

ba3c0b4e-b95d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cluster4 Ephemeris** is a dataset containing the positions of the Cluster-Tango spacecraft in various coordinate systems. It is part of the CDPP archive maintained by CNES and provides essential positional data for scientific investigations involving the Cluster mission.
ba3c0b4e-b95d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris on Cluster 4 Spacecraft

ba412c5e-bbac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Viking Orbiter 1 Spacecraft Mars Atmospheric Water Detector (MAWD) was an infrared grating spectrometer on the Viking Orbiter 1, designed to measure water vapor in Mars' atmosphere by analyzing solar infrared radiation reflected from the planet's surface.
ba412c5e-bbac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Atmospheric Water Detector on Viking Orbiter 1

ba4ddfe8-bbb7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The DMSP 5D-3 F19 was a satellite in the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program, designed to provide terrestrial and space weather data from a near-polar, Sun-synchronous orbit. It operated from April 2014 until a telecommand outage in February 2016.
ba4ddfe8-bbb7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Defense Meteorological Satellite Program on DMSP 5D-3 F19

ba4efcbe-bb50-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Wegberg Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Wegberg, Germany, identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code D07.
ba4efcbe-bb50-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wegberg Observatory, Germany

ba4ff7c0-b79c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Kani Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Kani, Gifu Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
ba4ff7c0-b79c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kani Observatory, Japan

ba500bb0-ba4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Summit Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAGs, used to measure magnetic fields.
ba500bb0-ba4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission

ba579a78-bb86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cointe Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Liège, Belgium, built by the University of Liège in 1881-1882.
ba579a78-bb86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatoire de Cointe, Belgium

ba6260e0-bab2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) 24-inch Telescope at the George R. Wallace, Jr. Astrophysical Observatory is an optical telescope located in North America with a 0.61m aperture, used for astronomical observations and research by MIT.
ba6260e0-bab2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.61m optical Massachusetts Institute of Technology Telescope at George R. Wallace, Jr. Astrophysical Observatory

ba77e4a4-b62c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Jiangnantianchi Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Anji County, Huzhou, Zhejiang, China. It operates as a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID P30.
ba77e4a4-b62c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Jiangnantianchi Observatory, China

ba7b0222-b66f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Purple Mountain Observatory, Lenghu-1 is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Lenghu, Qinghai, China. It operates under the Purple Mountain Observatory network and is situated at coordinates 38.58877° N, 93.88669° E.
ba7b0222-b66f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Purple Mountain Observatory at Lenghu-1, China

ba8a039a-ba15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: La Couyère Astronomical Center is an astronomical observatory located in La Couyère, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and studies.
ba8a039a-ba15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Centre Astronomique de La Couyère

ba8acbe6-b8d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Loring Air Force Base (LOB) station from 1966 to 1972, part of the IAGA investigation and the WDC Kyoto observatory.
ba8acbe6-b8d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Loring AFB

ba8cfc1e-b7bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA station in Accra, operational from January 1, 1963, to December 31, 1965, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the IAGA investigation.
ba8cfc1e-b7bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Accra Observatory

ba8f7324-bb0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Guimar, part of the WDC Kyoto observatory network, used for measuring and monitoring the Earth's magnetic field since 1993.
ba8f7324-bb0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ground Magnetic Field Instrument at World Data Center Kyoto Observatory

ba8ffd24-ba36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The US Naval Academy Hopper Hall Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located at the United States Naval Academy in Annapolis, Maryland, USA. It serves as an educational and research facility for naval cadets and the scientific community.
ba8ffd24-ba36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hopper Hall Observatory at United States Naval Academy, United States

ba97f782-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Low-Energy Proton and Electron Differential Energy Analyzer (LEPEDEA) on ISEE 1 was an instrument designed to measure the spatial and temporal variations of solar wind and magnetosheath electrons and ions, specifically protons and electrons in the energy range from 1 eV to 45 keV.
ba97f782-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low-Energy Proton and Electron Differential Energy Analyzer on ISEE 1

ba989886-b76f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Eckdorf Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Badorf, Eckdorf, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to celestial observation and research.
ba989886-b76f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Eckdorf Observatory, Germany

baa595ca-b84d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Muono (MUO) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Muonio, Lapland, Finland. It includes a magnetometer and operates at an altitude of 258 meters above Earth's surface, with its activities beginning on October 1, 1982.
baa595ca-b84d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Muono Geophysical Observatory, Finland

baabae18-bb47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Samford Valley Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Samford Valley, Greater Brisbane, Australia. It serves as a ground-based facility for studying celestial objects and phenomena from Earth.
baabae18-bb47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Samford Valley Observatory, Australia

bab1edf8-b973-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IAGA:ROK Magnetometer** is a historical instrument located at the Rostock observatory (identified by IAGA as ROK), used for measuring magnetic fields from 1890 to 1903.
bab1edf8-b973-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Rostock Observatory
