c8b28aa2-b9a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IRTF (Infrared Telescope Facility) is an observatory operated by the University of Hawai`i for NASA, featuring a 3.0-meter telescope optimized for infrared observations and located at the summit of Mauna Kea, Hawaii.
c8b28aa2-b9a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared 3.0m Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatories, United States

c8c179ea-b6df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Tartu Observatory is the largest astronomical observatory in Estonia, located on the Tõravere hill and affiliated with the University of Tartu.
c8c179ea-b6df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tartu Observatory, Estonia

c8c6d076-b9bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Titan Wind Tunnel (TWT)** is a specialized wind tunnel facility operated by Arizona State University at NASA Ames Research Laboratory, designed for studying aerodynamic phenomena relevant to planetary research, particularly Titan and Venus. It features a 20 cm diameter test section and can achieve high pressures using compressed air systems.
c8c6d076-b9bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Titan Wind Tunnel at Planetary Aeolian Laboratory

c8c85668-b63d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An observatory located in Canberra that includes the Deep Space Network's 70-meter radio telescope used for radio astronomy observations.
c8c85668-b63d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 70m Radio Telescope at Canberra Observatory

c8cf8b5a-ba10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ISEE atmospheric aerosol observation** involves using a particle detector, specifically a photoacoustic spectrometer located in Nagoya, Japan, to measure the optical properties of aerosols. This instrument is part of the IUGONET Observatory and provides data on aerosol characteristics for scientific research.
c8cf8b5a-ba10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Photoacoustic Spectrometer part of ISEE Investigation

c8d6af6e-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMN Moshiri Station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Moshiri, Japan, which operates as part of the IUGONET Observatory to monitor geomagnetic activity.
c8d6af6e-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Moshiri Observatory, Japan

c8de3c68-b628-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sherbrooke Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Fleurimont, Sherbrooke, Quebec, Canada. It operates as a ground-based observatory dedicated to studying the night sky and celestial phenomena.
c8de3c68-b628-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sherbrooke Observatory, Canada

c8e8c150-ba39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Wyncroft Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Attleborough, Norfolk, England. It is a ground-based facility used for stargazing and astronomical research.
c8e8c150-ba39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wyncroft Observatory

c8f0d65e-b64e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Measurement of Low-Energy Protons and Electrons" is an instrument on the IMP-8 spacecraft designed to measure energy spectra of low-energy electrons and protons in the geocentric range, aiding studies of magnetospheric phenomena like geomagnetic storms.
c8f0d65e-b64e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low Energy Proton and Electron Differential Energy Analyzer on Interplanetary Monitoring Platform 8

c90accee-bb71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **AMPTE-UKS (Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers - United Kingdom Subsatellite)** was a British research satellite launched as part of the AMPTE mission to study Earth's magnetosphere and its interactions with solar wind. It operated from August 1984 until its power supply failed in January 1985.
c90accee-bb71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers United Kingdom Subsatellite part of Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers

c9121904-bb17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Vector Helium/Fluxgate Magnetometer (VHM/FGM) on the Ulysses space probe is an instrument designed to measure the magnetic field vector in the heliosphere with high sensitivity and time resolution, contributing to studies of solar wind dynamics and interplanetary magnetic fields.
c9121904-bb17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetic Field on Ulysses

c91fdcce-b7b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS) 1.93m Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Observatoire de Haute-Provence in Europe, used for astronomical research. It has a 1.93-meter aperture and operates within the optical waveband.
c91fdcce-b7b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.93m Telescope at Observatoire de Haute-Provence

c923d49c-bb98-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mind's Eye Observatory** is a ground-based observatory located in Sebastian, Indian River County, Florida. It is situated at coordinates 27.76456° N and -80.53429° W (279.46571° E longitude).
c923d49c-bb98-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mind's Eye Observatory at Vero Beach, United States

c9252876-bb37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cima Ekar Observing Station is an astronomical observatory located on the crest of Cima Ekar, approximately 4 kilometers southeast of Asiago, Italy.
c9252876-bb37-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cima Ekar Observatory, Italy

c9269c7a-bad2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pulsating Aurora Project utilizes an all-sky EMCCD imager equipped with an RG665 filter located in Tromsø, Norway. This instrument is specifically the ImagEM X2 EMCCD camera (C9100-23B) produced by Hamamatsu Photonics.
c9269c7a-bad2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager at ISEE Observatory, Norway

c92def7a-b9bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Arctowski Geomagnetic Observatory (ARC) is a ground-based facility in Antarctica operated by Poland since 1978, primarily for geomagnetic measurements.
c92def7a-b9bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Arctowski Geomagnetic Observatory

c930e144-b767-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Manhay Magnetic Observatory** is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Manhay, Belgium, which has been operating since 1932 and is sponsored by Belgium.
c930e144-b767-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Manhay Magnetic Observatory, Belgium

c9345fc2-b622-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Observatorio Azahar is a ground-based observatory located in Valoria la Buena, Valladolid, Spain. It is situated at coordinates 41.79806° N and 355.43322° E, within the European continent.
c9345fc2-b622-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Azahar at Valoria la Buena, Spain

c937a880-b730-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Steward Observatory 2.3m (90-inch) Bart Bok Telescope is an optical telescope located at Kitt Peak National Observatory in North America, with an aperture of 2.3 meters.
c937a880-b730-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.3m optical Bart Bok Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory

c93a4488-b71b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover's Mast Camera Left (Mastcam-Left) is a high-resolution imaging system mounted on the rover's Remote Sensing Mast, designed to capture detailed color images of the Martian surface for studying its geology, climate, and atmosphere.
c93a4488-b71b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Left Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover part of Mars Science Laboratory

c9466884-b95b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Burke-Gaffney Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Saint Mary's University in Halifax, Canada. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and education.
c9466884-b95b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Halifax Observatory

c95a2bbe-b69d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Advanced Ionospheric Sounder (AIS)** on the SESAME observatory is a high-frequency radar instrument operated by NOAA, designed to measure radio signals reflected from the ionosphere to study its structure and dynamics. It detects phenomena such as auroral arcs and energetic particle precipitation with high accuracy over a frequency range of 0.1-30 MHz.
c95a2bbe-b69d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Advanced Ionospheric Sounder part of Substorm - Energetics, Sources And Magnetospheric Effects

c97114f0-bb84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magroforte Observatory (code: G15) is an astronomical observatory located in Montacuto, Alessandria, Italy. It functions as a ground-based facility and is identified by the Minor Planet Center with the MPC ID G15.
c97114f0-bb84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magroforte Observatory, Italy

c9715502-b858-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Shamrock Banks Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located at 301 Shamrock Court in Clare, Michigan. It is situated at the coordinates 43.83076° N, 275.23817° E (or 81.98817° W) in North America.
c9715502-b858-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Shamrock Banks Observatory, United States

c9730390-b94b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN magnetometer network in Tixie, Russia is a ground-based facility located at coordinates 71.59 latitude and 128.78 longitude within the Sakha Republic, used for monitoring geomagnetic activity.
c9730390-b94b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tiksi Observatory, Russia

c97a5d90-bb6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Soft Solar X-ray Photometer RF is an instrument designed to measure solar X-ray radiation in the soft spectral range, used for continuous monitoring and as a trigger for registering active solar events on the Magion-4 subsatellite.
c97a5d90-bb6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Soft Solar X-ray Photometer on Interball S2

c97a7942-bb01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sunriver Nature Center Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Sunriver, Oregon, United States. It serves as a ground-based observatory for studying celestial objects and phenomena from Earth.
c97a7942-bb01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sunriver Nature Center Observatory

c98cdae4-bab4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RNF Neural Network Experiment on DEMETER is an instrument designed to identify and classify electromagnetic waves ranging from extremely low frequency to very high frequency using neural network technology.
c98cdae4-bab4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neural Network Experiment part of DEMETER

c99571e8-b665-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Viking Lander 1 Spacecraft Gas Chromatograph Mass Spectrometer (GCMS) was an instrument on the Viking Lander 1 that analyzed chemical compounds in Mars' surface and atmosphere, using a combination of gas chromatography and mass spectrometry for high sensitivity and specificity.
c99571e8-b665-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gas Chromatograph Mass Spectrometer on Viking Lander 1 Spacecraft

c99b5292-b9cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Medium-Energy Neutral Atom Imager (MENA) on the IMAGE satellite is a specialized instrument designed to detect and image neutral hydrogen and oxygen atoms with energies between 1 to 30 keV, providing observations of Earth's magnetospheric environment through neutral atom imaging.
c99b5292-b9cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Medium-Energy Neutral Atom Imager on IMAGE

c9b166da-b653-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Alpha Particle X-Ray Spectrometer (APXS) is an instrument on the Mars Exploration Rover Spirit designed to determine the elemental composition of Martian soils and rocks by analyzing x-rays emitted when alpha particles interact with a sample.
c9b166da-b653-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Alpha Particle X-Ray Spectrometer on Curiosity

c9b32584-b918-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in the Teide National Park on Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain.
c9b32584-b918-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Aqawan A at Tenerife-LCO Observatory, Spain

c9c105fe-b5f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kappa Crucis Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Montevideo, Uruguay. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
c9c105fe-b5f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kappa Crucis Observatory, Uruguay

c9e02fba-bc25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISEE Muon Telescope is a multi-directional cosmic-ray muon detector constructed in Nagoya as part of Japan's program for the International Active Sun Year (IASY), originally led by Prof. Zenjiro Fujii and still operational today.
c9e02fba-bc25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Particle Detector part of ISEE Muon Telescope

c9f5f99a-b670-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IAGA:ATH Magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields at the Athens observatory from 1899-01-01 to 1908-12-31 as part of the IAGA investigation.
c9f5f99a-b670-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Athens Observatory

c9fd9ace-b85f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager (RHESSI) was a NASA solar flare observatory launched in 2002 to study the physics of particle acceleration and energy release in solar flares by imaging them at high resolution in X-rays and gamma rays.
c9fd9ace-b85f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager on RHESSI

c9fff320-bb00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
SWARM C is one of three identical satellites in the European Space Agency's SWARM mission, designed to study Earth's geomagnetic field and its temporal evolution from a near-polar orbit.
c9fff320-bb00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Satellite part of Swarm Mission

ca091dac-b870-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AGO P4 Antenna Instrument is a component of the ICESTAR observatory, designed to facilitate communication and data transmission at the AGO P4 ground station.
ca091dac-b870-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna part of International Conjunction of Elevation Spectrometers for Transient Atmospheric Research

ca1015e6-b756-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Americus (AMER) Magnetometer Station is a ground facility located in Americus, Kansas, USA, serving as one of the nine magnetometers within the Mid-continent MAgnetoseismic Chain (McMAC).
ca1015e6-b756-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain Americus Station

ca19e90e-bbd9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ebro Geomagnetic Observatory (EBR)** is a ground-based facility located in Roquetes, Catalonia, Spain, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity since 1957. It operates under the World Data Centre for Geomagnetism, Kyoto, and is part of the IAGA observatories network.
ca19e90e-bbd9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ebro Geomagnetic Observatory, Spain

ca1f756a-b623-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lauder Geomagnetic Observatory (LAU) is a ground-based facility in New Zealand that has been operating since 1979 to monitor and study geomagnetic activity. It is part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) observatory network.
ca1f756a-b623-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lauder Geomagnetic Observatory, New Zealand

ca253cbc-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Budkov Geomagnetic Observatory (BDV) is a ground-based facility located in Budkov u Husince, Czechia, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity since 1967.
ca253cbc-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Budkov Geomagnetic Observatory, Czechia

ca2aa7f6-b758-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 14 Charged Particle Lunar Environment Experiment (CPLEE) was part of the ALSEP package and used electrostatic analyzers to measure the energy spectra of low-energy charged particles, including electrons and ions with energies from 40 eV to 20 keV, striking the lunar surface.
ca2aa7f6-b758-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Charged Particle Lunar Environment Experiment on Apollo 14 Lunar Module

ca2d6038-b5ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Cuajimalpa is a ground-based observatory located in Mexico City, Mexico, known for its magnetometer facilities, which operated from January 1903 to December 1926.
ca2d6038-b5ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cuajimalpa Observatory, Mexico

ca376ed6-b1aa-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sor Rondane Mountains (SRM) station is an automated magnetometer facility located in the vicinity of Syowa Station, Antarctica. It is part of a broader network for geomagnetic observation and research on Earth's surface.
ca376ed6-b1aa-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sor Rondane Mountains, Antarctica

ca3d7bdc-b664-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Magnetic Field Fluctuations) instrument on Cluster 2/FM8 (Tango) is a search coil magnetometer and spectrum analyzer designed to measure magnetic components of electromagnetic fluctuations up to 4 kHz and compute spectral matrix coefficients for wave analysis.
ca3d7bdc-b664-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil on Cluster 2/FM8 (Tango) part of Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Magnetic Field Fluctuations

ca47532a-b8a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Panker Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Gadendorf, Panker, Germany, dedicated to ground-based observations.
ca47532a-b8a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Panker Observatory, Germany

ca4953b0-b8a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **MAGDAS Cebu Station** is a ground-based facility located in Cebu City, Philippines, part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network, used for geomagnetic observations.
ca4953b0-b8a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cebu Observatory, Philippines

ca60046e-b7cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Perpignan Observatory was a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Perpignan, France, operational from January 1, 1885, to December 31, 1910. It was part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network and featured a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements.
ca60046e-b7cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Perpignan Observatory, France

ca6b87b8-b928-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity represents a micro-barometric observation conducted using the VAISALA PTB210 barometric sensor, which is part of the IUGONET observatory at WDC Kyoto in Mineyama.
ca6b87b8-b928-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Micro-barometric Observation part of IUGONET

ca6f50d6-b7a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ASPOC (Active Spacecraft Potential Control) on Cluster 2/FM6 (Salsa) is an instrument designed to control the electric potential of a spacecraft relative to ambient plasma by emitting a variable current of positive ions, ensuring minimal interference with scientific measurements.
ca6f50d6-b7a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Active Spacecraft Potential Control part of Cluster 2

ca7f82d6-b6e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific entity refers to magnetometers located at the Zouy observatory, part of the WDC Kyoto network under IUGONET.
ca7f82d6-b6e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Zouy Observatory

ca87d7aa-bb59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Radio Science Subsystem for Mariner 9 was a set of instruments on the Mariner 9 spacecraft and NASA's Deep Space Network used to study Mars through radio signals. It analyzed Doppler shifts in telemetry signals during occultation to determine the Martian atmosphere’s vertical composition, including neutral and ionized species.
ca87d7aa-bb59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Subsystem part of Mariner 9

ca880f40-bb36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAPS Survey is an astronomical observatory located in San Pedro de Atacama, Chile, conducting ground-based surveys since 2020.
ca880f40-bb36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared MAPS Survey at San Pedro de Atacama Observatory, Chile

ca902b1c-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The 0.7m Telescope (AZT-8) is an optical telescope located at the Crimean Astrophysical Observatory in Europe, with a primary mirror diameter of 0.7 meters.
ca902b1c-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.7m optical AZT-8 Telescope at Crimean Astrophysical Observatory

ca98c178-bb1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Operational Linescan System (OLS)** on the DMSP/F18 satellite is an imager that measures visible and infrared wavelengths to provide global cloud cover imagery, with data resolution averaged to 2.7 km for full coverage and a finer 0.56 km resolution for select regions.
ca98c178-bb1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Operational Linescan System part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

ca9ed858-b7fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **OWL-Net Observatory** in Oukaimeden, Morocco (MPC ID: Z01), is an astronomical ground-based facility located at 352.13321° longitude and 31.20606° latitude, dedicated to observing celestial phenomena from its site in the Al Haouz Province of Morocco.
ca9ed858-b7fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: OWL-Net Observatory at Oukaimeden, Morocco

caa0a45e-b91c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fluxgate Magnetometer (OMAG) on the Pioneer Venus Orbiter was designed to measure magnetic fields and investigate solar wind interactions with Venus. It operated from 1978 to 1992, utilizing a triaxial fluxgate mechanism with sensors mounted on a boom to gather data crucial for understanding Venus's space environment and atmospheric dynamics.
caa0a45e-b91c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Pioneer Venus Orbiter mission

caab66aa-b5ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gemeaux Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Constant, Quebec, Canada. It operates as a ground-based facility and is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with the code 818.
caab66aa-b5ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gemeaux Observatory, Canada

caad9154-b90e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DAWEX radiosonde sounding system at Garden Point, Melville Island, Australia, is an instrument used to measure vertical profiles of atmospheric parameters such as pressure, temperature, and humidity from the troposphere to the stratosphere using Vaisala RS80 radiosondes.
caad9154-b90e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Unspecified Instrument part of Darwin Area Wave Experiment

cacdc91e-b676-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Cachoeira Paulista Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Cachoeira Paulista, São Paulo, Brazil, dedicated to geomagnetic observations and research as part of the global IAGA observatories network.
cacdc91e-b676-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cachoeira Paulista Observatory, Brazil

cad11844-bad6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cluster Ion Spectrometry (CIS) instrument on the Cluster 2 spacecraft is designed to measure full 3D ion distributions with high time and mass-per-charge resolution. It consists of two main components: a Hot Ion Analyzer (HIA) and a time-of-flight Ion Composition and Distribution Function analyzer (CODIF).
cad11844-bad6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cluster Ion Spectrometry on Cluster 2

cad131f0-b804-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pacific Lutheran University Keck Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Pacific Lutheran University in Tacoma, Washington. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
cad131f0-b804-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Keck Observatory, United States

cad1572c-bb31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital receiver located in Ho Chi Minh City, Viet Nam, designed to measure ionospheric total electron content (TEC) using signals from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. It utilizes GNU Radio software and Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) hardware for signal processing and acquisition.
cad1572c-bb31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver part of GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver), Vietnam

cadc166a-b5e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The **VLF receiver for the Canadian GO-ABOVE ground-based array**, located at Island Lake, is a specialized instrument that operates within the 100 Hz to 75 kHz frequency range. It is designed to monitor electromagnetic emissions such as chorus and hiss, as well as signals from U.S. Navy transmitters near 25 kHz, with an absolute timing accuracy of 10 ns derived from GPS.
cadc166a-b5e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Low Frequency Receiver part of Geospace Observatory - Array for Broadband Observations of Very Low Frequency/Extremely Low Frequency Emissions

cade75f8-bb5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Geneva Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Sauverny, Switzerland. It focuses on discovering exoplanets and stellar photometry, while also contributing to various European Space Agency missions.
cade75f8-bb5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geneva Observatory, Switzerland

# Venera 16 Overview

## Launch and Mission Details
- **Launch Date:** June 7, 1983 (02:32 UT)
- **Launch Site:** Baikonur Cosmodrome (Tyuratam)
- **Launch Vehicle:** Proton-K Booster
- **Arrival at Venus:** October 14, 1983 (06:22 UT)
- **Primary Mission End Date:** July 10, 1984
- **Extended Mission End Date:** June 13, 1985

## Spacecraft Specifications
- **Mass at Launch:** 5300 kg
- **Dimensions:**
  - Central Cylinder: 110 cm diameter, 5 m long
  - SAR Antenna: 6 m long, 1.4 m wide parabolic dish
  - Radio Altimeter Antenna: 1 m diameter parabolic dish
- **Solar Panels:** Two wings extending from the sides of the cylinder, each 1.25 x 2.1 meters in size, total span 6.7 meters
- **Communications:** High gain antenna and six omnidirectional helical antennas

## Instruments and Equipment
- **Radar Systems:** Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Radio Altimeter
- **Scientific Instruments:** Radiometric system, infrared spectrometer, energetic particle detectors, cosmic ray detectors, radio occultation experiment
- **Propulsion System:** KTDU-425A propulsion unit with fuel tanks and gimbaled engine nozzle for attitude control
- **Power Supply:** Solar panel wings
- **Data Storage:** Magnetic tape system

## Mission Profile
### Pre-Arrival Phase
- **Launch:** June 7, 1983
- **Course Corrections:** June 15 and October 5, 1983

### Orbital Insertion
- **Date:** October 14, 1983
- **Initial Orbit:** 977.3 x 67,078 km altitude, 24 hours, 34 minutes period
- **Operational Orbit:** 944 x 65,336 km with periapsis at 62 N

### Mapping Mission
- **Start Date:** October 20, 1983
- **End Date:** July 10, 1984

### Extended Science Mission
- **End Date:** June 13, 1985 (loss of contact due to depletion of attitude control propellant)

## Technical Details
- **High Gain Antenna Communication Bands:** Decimeter and centimeter wavelengths
- **Attitude Control:** Gimbaled engine nozzle, nitrogen cold gas jets, gyroscopes, solar sensors, Canopus star sensors, Earth sensor
- **Thermal Control:** Louvers and radiator

## Associated Identifiers
- **NORAD ID:** 14107
- **NAIF ID:** V16
- **NSSDCA ID:** 1983-054A
- **COSPAR ID:** 1983-054A

## Additional Information
### Funding and Support
- **Funding Agencies:** Soviet Academy of Sciences, NPO Lavochkin (manufacturer)
- **Data Archive:** National Space Science Data Center (NSSDC), Planetary Data System (PDS)

### Related Observatories
- **Dark Sky New Mexico observatory**
  - Latitude: 31.946944° N
  - Longitude: 251.10288° W (108.89712° E)
  - Country: United States
  - Continent: North America
  - Address: County Road C079, Hidalgo County, New Mexico, USA

### References and Documentation
- **Primary Reference:** National Space Science Data Center (NSSDC)
- **Supporting Documentation:** Planetary Data System (PDS), Venera mission archives

This comprehensive overview highlights the key aspects of the Venera 16 spacecraft, its mission to Venus, and related technical details. For further information, refer to the linked resources and documentation from NSSDC and PDS.

cb975dc8-b99c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Sky Vistas observatory (C14) is an astronomical observatory located in Eichgraben, Austria. It operates as a ground-based facility focused on sky observations and research.
cb975dc8-b99c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sky Vistas Observatory, Austria

cb98b164-ba5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Rosarno Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Rosarno, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
cb98b164-ba5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rosarno Observatory, Italy

cb9b6cc6-bc06-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cassini spacecraft, launched in 1997, was a NASA mission designed to explore Saturn and its moons. The spacecraft operated until 2017, providing extensive data through its various subsystems and utilizing the Deep Space Network for communication and radio science investigations.

cba13734-badd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Santa Mama Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Castagnoli, Subbiano, Arezzo, Tuscany, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
cba13734-badd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Santa Mama Observatory

cbaa8b1e-b80c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Koenigsberg Observatory was an astronomical research facility attached to the Albertina University in Königsberg (now Kaliningrad, Russia), which was destroyed during World War II.
cbaa8b1e-b80c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Königsberg Observatory

cbaf3ea6-b600-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Glenhope, Australia, known as the Barfold Observatory.
cbaf3ea6-b600-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Barfold Observatory, Australia

cbafa96a-b716-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The KPNO McMath-Pierce Solar Main Telescope (1.61m) Vacuum Spectrograph is an instrument used at the McMath-Pierce main telescope, which directs light to an observing room with adjustable positions for vacuum spectrographs of varying depths, facilitating image rotation compensation and precise spectral analysis.

cbb6a81e-ba40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Charged Particle Instrument (CPI) on Pioneer 11 was a spectrometer designed to measure charged-particle composition and spectra using four detector systems, providing detailed energy spectra and element resolution for particles like protons and oxygen.
cbb6a81e-ba40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Charged Particle Instrument part of Pioneer 11

cbc371e2-b807-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Iga-Ueno Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Iga, Mie Prefecture, Japan. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting observations and research in astronomy.
cbc371e2-b807-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Iga-Ueno Observatory, Japan

cbc8823a-bc9a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of the Andes Station is an astronomical observatory located in San Javier del Valle, Mérida State, Venezuela. It operates as a ground-based facility with an altitude of 3600 meters and has been active since January 1985.
cbc8823a-bc9a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Llano del Hato National Astronomical Observatory, Venezuela

cbd4aed2-b6fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Roemoe geophysical observatory is a ground facility located in Juvre, Tønder Municipality, Denmark, that houses a magnetometer and is part of the IUGONET Observatory network.
cbd4aed2-b6fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Rømø Observatory, Denmark

cbd514f6-ba0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **STAFF-DWP**: The STAFF-DWP is a magnetometer onboard the Double Star 1 satellite designed to analyze magnetic field fluctuations. It processes low-frequency data on the ground and high-frequency data onboard using a Digital Wave Processor (DWP), with results sent to ground stations for further analysis.
cbd514f6-ba0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spatio-Temporal Analyzer of Field Fluctuations and Digital Wave Processor on Double Star 1

cbd535ac-ba1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Low-Energy Neutral Atom Imager (LENA)** on the IMAGE spacecraft is an instrument designed to observe the Earth's magnetospheric environment by measuring low-energy neutral atoms, distinguishing between different types of neutrals, and determining ion outflow with high temporal resolution. cbd535ac-ba1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager part of IMAGE Mission

cbec425c-b8e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the ground observatory located in Yoshida 3-chome, Nagano, Nagano Prefecture, Japan, specifically identified by coordinates 36.66928° N latitude and 138.2239° E longitude on Earth.

cc0e7440-b81f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a spacecraft designed for conducting observations of occultations (the blocking of light from one celestial body by another) that are not centered on Earth. cc14e7d4-b7bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dynamic Science Experiment (DYNSCI) aboard the Stardust spacecraft utilized the attitude control system to assess and report the performance of the spacecraft and its response to particle impacts, using a combination of thrusters for various maneuvers.

cc448658-b71f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Radio Science Subsystem (RSS) for Galileo Orbiter was a suite of instruments and methods used to conduct radio science experiments during the Galileo mission. cc454282-b139-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ASPERA-4 Ion Mass Analyzer (IMA) is an instrument on the Venus Express mission that measures ion components in the energy range of 0.01 - 36 keV/q, with a wide field of view and electrostatic sweeping for elevation coverage.

cc4a033e-b7ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Makes Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Les Makes, Saint-Louis on the island of Réunion. It serves as a ground-based facility for celestial observations and research.

cc5083f8-b8ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Infrared Astronomical Satellite (IRAS) mission was a joint space program launched on January 26, 1983, to conduct an infrared survey of the sky and make pointed observations of selected celestial objects.
cc5083f8-b8ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Astronomical Satellite part of IRAS Mission

cc543b6a-b77a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Eastwood Observatory (code: K02) is an astronomical observatory located in Leigh on Sea, Essex, England. It is a ground-based facility used for observing celestial objects and phenomena.

cc5f8906-bb0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The "DC Electric Field Intensity and ULF Waves (IESP-2)" instrument on the Interball Auroral Probe is designed to measure the six components of waves in the ultra-low frequency (ULF) range and the three components of the DC electric field, using a combination of search coil magnetometers and spherical probes mounted on booms.

cc6bf734-b930-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Eden Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Banham, England, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects.

cc6c539a-ba21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Phoenix Lander Meteorology Suite LIDAR** was an instrument on the Phoenix Mars lander that used laser pulses to measure dust and cloud layers in the Martian atmosphere, providing data on atmospheric properties and weather patterns.

cc6d83ac-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Beilen Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Beilen, Drenthe, Netherlands. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting observations and studies of celestial objects.
cc6d83ac-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Beilen Observatory, Netherlands

cc790a16-bae1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ex Nihilo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Winder, Georgia, USA. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.

cc79a402-b6aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cambridge Bay Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility in Nunavut, Canada, operated by the Geological Survey of Canada since 2007. It is part of the Canadian Magnetic Observatory System and contributes to global magnetic field monitoring.
cc79a402-b6aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cambridge Bay Observatory

cc879e28-b7ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Iluro Observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Mataró, Catalonia, Spain. It operates as a ground-based observatory for various astronomical studies and observations.

cc916fb8-bb43-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The King City Observatory is an astronomical facility located in King City, Ontario, Canada. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is situated at the coordinates 43.914771° N, -79.5342° W.
cc916fb8-bb43-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: King City Observatory, Canada

cc974ece-bb34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Turitea Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Palmerston North City, Manawatū-Whanganui, New Zealand.

cc9ffb12-b6d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Copernico 1.82m Telescope is a Cassegrain reflector telescope located at the Asiago Astrophysical Observatory in Italy, dedicated to optical observations and named after Nicolaus Copernicus.

ccc1fb26-b6d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plasma Wave Spectrometer on AMPTE/IRM is an instrument designed to measure plasma wave activity in the magnetosphere, solar wind, and artificial plasma clouds using electric dipole antennae and magnetic search coil sensors. ccc1fb26-b6d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Wave Spectrometer on Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers/Ion Release Module

ccc2c32a-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Heron Cove Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Orcas Village, San Juan County, Washington, United States. It is a ground-based facility used for stargazing and astronomical research.
ccc2c32a-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heron Cove Observatory at Orcas Village, United States

cccbb282-b6ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to a three-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer located in Hartland, United Kingdom, part of the IUGONET observatory and CPMN observation network.

cccbdf10-b86c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Induction Magnetometer at Nain of ISEE Magnetometer Data" is a magnetometer instrument that measures variations in the 3-D vector geomagnetic field with a sampling rate of 64 Hz. It is part of the IUGONET observatory and controlled by a PC clock signal.
cccbdf10-b86c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Induction Magnetometer part of International Sun-Earth Explorer Magnetometer Data

cccc694c-b6bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Etters Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Fairview Township, York County, Pennsylvania. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
cccc694c-b6bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Etters Observatory

ccd4ae66-bc12-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fixed Voltage Analyzer (FVA) is an instrument used in space missions to measure electrons and protons by applying specific voltages to select particles of approximately 1.5 keV and 6 keV energies. It consists of pairs of cylindrical plate electrostatic analyzers, with each pair having one analyzer for electrons and one for protons.

ccd90a7a-b74d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Equatorial Magnetometer Network's (EMN) fluxgate magnetometer at Santa Maria, Brazil is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument designed to measure magnetic fields and is part of the IUGONET observatory.

ccdf1f7a-ba25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RISH meteor wind radar at Biak is an instrument located in Indonesia that measures neutral atmospheric winds at altitudes of 70-110 km by detecting the Doppler shift of VHF radio waves reflected from ionized meteor trails. ccdf1f7a-ba25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Meteor Wind Radar on RISH Observatory, Indonesia

cce08d24-b86d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Saint-Félicien Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Félicien, Quebec, Canada. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical research and observations.

**Definition:**

cd509f5e-bb62-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **LANL1989 Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer** is an instrument used to measure the three-dimensional energy/charge distributions of both ions and electrons in space, operating with high sensitivity and moderate energy and angular resolutions. cd5b037e-b7af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The Magnetometers at North Pole 8 (NPH), part of the WDC Kyoto observatory, are specifically designed for monitoring geomagnetic activity in the Arctic region.

cde3ff90-b8ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe (WMAP) was a NASA spacecraft launched in 2001 to measure temperature differences across the sky in the cosmic microwave background radiation, providing insights into the early universe and cosmological parameters.
cde3ff90-b8ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: microwave Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe part of NASA MIDEX mission

cdeff65c-b60e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The COSPIN-High Energy Telescope (HET) is a sophisticated instrument designed to detect and measure cosmic rays within the energy range of approximately 10 MeV/nucleon to a few hundred MeV/nucleon, utilizing advanced silicon detectors and electronics to determine particle trajectories and characteristics.
cdeff65c-b60e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Energy Telescope on COSPIN for ULY

cdf67f5e-ba78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Johns Hopkins University (JHU) 0.9m Hopkins Ultraviolet Telescope (HUT) is a space telescope with a 0.9-meter aperture designed for ultraviolet observations, which was deployed on the ASTRO-1 and ASTRO-2 missions.
cdf67f5e-ba78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Johns Hopkins University 0.9m Hopkins Ultraviolet Telescope on ASTRO-1 and ASTRO-2

cdf6d3e8-b9e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Dynamics Explorer 2 (DE-2 or Explorer 63) was a NASA geomagnetic satellite launched on August 3, 1981, to investigate interactions between plasmas in the magnetosphere and ionosphere, complementing the high-altitude mission DE-1 with its low-altitude measurements.
cdf6d3e8-b9e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dynamics Explorer 2 part of Dynamics Explorer mission

cdf87be4-b805-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
NASA's Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) is a space mission designed to study the Sun's outer atmosphere and the solar wind using X-ray observations.
cdf87be4-b805-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Polarimeter to UNify the Corona and Heliosphere part of NASA's Polarimeter to UNify the Corona and Heliosphere mission

ce0cfc60-bb96-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Viking Orbiter 1 Spacecraft Visual Imaging Subsystem (VIS) was a set of twin high-resolution cameras on the Viking Orbiter spacecrafts designed to aid in landing site selection, observe and map Mars' surface features, and investigate its atmosphere.
ce0cfc60-bb96-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visual Imaging Subsystem on Viking Orbiter 1

ce1adf3a-b8d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Northern Skygems Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Nerpio, Albacete, Castile-La Mancha, Spain. It is a ground-based facility situated at Camino de Mingarnao, Astrocamp Nerpio.
ce1adf3a-b8d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Northern Skygems Observatory, Spain

ce1c99bc-b80e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Cerro Tololo-LCO**: An astronomical observatory located in the Coquimbo Region of Chile, known for its dark skies and optimal conditions for ground-based observations.
ce1c99bc-b80e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cerro Tololo Observatory, Chile

ce265922-b91a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Plasma Instrument for Magnetic Sounding (PIMS)** is a Faraday cup-based instrument on the Europa Clipper spacecraft designed to study Europa's ionosphere and magnetic field interactions with Jupiter.
ce265922-b91a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Instrument for Magnetic Sounding on Europa Clipper

ce293756-b18f-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Sydney Molonglo Observatory Synthesis Telescope (MOST) is a radio telescope located in Australia, primarily used for astronomical research and observations.
ce293756-b18f-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: radio Molonglo Observatory Synthesis Telescope at Molonglo Observatory, Australia

ce2e8034-b6a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Robert Mayer Sternwarte** is a ground-based observatory located in Heilbronn, Germany. It is situated at 1102 Mönchseestraße and serves as an astronomical facility for observation and research.
ce2e8034-b6a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Robert Mayer Sternwarte at Heilbronn Observatory, Germany

ce3a1186-ba7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMN magnetometer network located in Presidente Medici, Brazil is a ground-based facility used for monitoring and studying magnetic fields on Earth's surface, situated at coordinates -11.2 latitude and -61.8 longitude in the North Region of Brazil.
ce3a1186-ba7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer Network at Estrela de Rondônia Observatory, Brazil

ce3b3528-bc6b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AUGSBURG Magnetometer Array's Search Coil instrument at Halley Bay is a geomagnetic micropulsation recorder operating below 10 Hz, situated at approximately 75.6° GLat and 26.3° East Glong.
ce3b3528-bc6b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil instrument at Halley Bay Observatory

ce48316a-b77f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The ISEE-1 was a NASA spacecraft, part of the International Sun Earth Explorer (ISEE) program jointly conducted with ESA, launched in 1977 to study solar wind and magnetospheric interactions. It operated until its re-entry into Earth's atmosphere in 1987.
ce48316a-b77f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: International Sun Earth Explorer part of International Magnetospheric Study

ce4b83da-bcaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Heiss Island Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia, primarily involved in geomagnetic measurements since 1957. It operates under the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) and contributes to global magnetic data collection.
ce4b83da-bcaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Heiss Island Observatory, Russia

ce586d56-b7c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Podkamennaya Observatory was a ground-based facility located in Russia that operated from 1969 to 1991, focusing on geomagnetic observations.
ce586d56-b7c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Podkamennaya Tunguska Observatory, Russia

ce6515d6-bc21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ishigakijima Astronomical Observatory** is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Ishigaki, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan. It began operations on January 1, 2002 and is situated at an altitude of 200 meters above sea level.
ce6515d6-bc21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ishigakijima Astronomical Observatory, Japan

ce6ba1e0-b135-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes the **BARREL Balloon 2L**, a component of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) mission, which is a multiple-balloon investigation designed to study particles escaping from Earth's radiation belts. This specific balloon operated from January 6, 2014, to February 3, 2014, and included instruments such as a NaI scintillator and a DC magnetometer to measure relativistic electron precipitation in the stratosphere.
ce6ba1e0-b135-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses and part of Living with a Star, Geospace Mission of Opportunity

ce82af32-b8f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Oishi Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
ce82af32-b8f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Oishi Observatory, Japan

ce8bd1b2-b6c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The MMS 4 FIELDS Suite, Fluxgate Magnetometer (FGM) Instrument specifically measures these properties in space as part of NASA's Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS).
ce8bd1b2-b6c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of MMS 4 FIELDS Suite

ce8e8620-b63e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Malyye Karmakuly**: A ground-based observatory located in Novaya Zemlya, Russia, established in 1883, equipped with a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements.
ce8e8620-b63e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Malyye Karmakuly Observatory, Russia

ce92db78-b7c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The HARIMAU Automatic Weather Station (AWS) is an instrument located in North Sulawesi, Indonesia, that measures various meteorological parameters such as precipitation, temperature, humidity, pressure, and wind direction/speed. It has been operated by the Research Institute for Sustainable Humanosphere (RISH), Kyoto University since 2009.
ce92db78-b7c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Automatic Weather Station part of Hydrometeorological Array for Isv-Monsoon Automonitoring

ce9f598c-ba76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Observatoire de Saint-Maur** was a geomagnetic observatory located in Saint-Maur-des-Fossés, France, operating from 1883 to 1901. It was known for its ground-based observations and contributions to magnetic field studies.
ce9f598c-ba76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Observatoire de Saint-Maur, France

cea36b52-bc20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Infrared Interferometer Spectrometer and Radiometer (IRIS) is an instrument onboard the Voyager 2 spacecraft designed to study energy balances and atmospheric compositions, including temperature profiles of planets and satellites. It also examines Saturn’s ring particles using a Michelson interferometer and radiometer.
cea36b52-bc20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Interferometer Spectrometer and Radiometer on Voyager 2

ceaa0f18-b692-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Novosibirsk, Klyuch Ground Observatory is a geomagnetic research facility located in Novosibirsk, Russia, operating since 1967 and equipped with instruments like the WDC Kyoto magnetometer.
ceaa0f18-b692-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Novosibirsk Observatory, Russia

ceae613a-b8e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Tondano station with the IAGA identifier TND, part of the iugonet-observatory-wdc_kyoto-wdc-tnd observatory.
ceae613a-b8e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at WDC Kyoto Observatory

ceb86f3c-ba65-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Etaiyapuram Magnetometer is an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields at the ground-based observatory in Etaiyapuram, operational from January 1, 1980, to December 31, 2002.
ceb86f3c-ba65-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Etaiyapuram Observatory

cebb014e-baeb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astronomical Observatory of Belgrade (AOB) 0.6m Milan Nedeljkovic Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Serbian Astronomical Station in Vidojevica, Europe. It has an aperture of 0.6 meters and is used for astronomical observations.
cebb014e-baeb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 0.6m Milan Nedeljkovic Telescope at Serbian Astronomical Station at Vidojevica

cebca9d4-b917-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Context Camera (CTX)** is a space instrument aboard the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) designed to provide contextual images for other MRO instruments and observe features of interest on Mars. It operates with a 350 mm focal length telescope, offering high-resolution imaging capabilities crucial for scientific investigations and landing site assessments.
cebca9d4-b917-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Context Camera on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter

cedfdace-b658-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Backscatter Ultraviolet (SBUV) instrument on Nimbus 7 was designed to monitor solar ultraviolet irradiance and the UV radiation backscattered from Earth, utilizing a double Ebert-Fastie spectrometer and a filter photometer.
cedfdace-b658-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Backscatter Ultraviolet Spectrometer on Nimbus-7

cee36a64-b9c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Ohzora is a Japanese research satellite launched in 1984 to study the middle atmosphere and ionospheric plasma interactions as part of the Middle Atmosphere Program (MAP).
cee36a64-b9c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ohzora part of Middle Atmosphere Program

cee4f154-b78d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Dust Impact Mass Analyzer (PUMA) for Vega 1 was a time-of-flight spectrometer aboard the Vega 1 spacecraft, designed to measure the size and spatial density of solid particles, with a specific focus on determining isotopic ratios.
cee4f154-b78d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dust Impact Mass Analyzer on Vega 1

cee53162-b654-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Universitätssternwarte Graz** is an astronomical observatory located in Lustbühel, Graz, Styria, Austria. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
cee53162-b654-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lustbühel Observatory at Graz Observatory, Austria

cef22e00-bb9d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IAGA:SAN Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at the Sanya observatory, identified by the IAGA code SAN.
cef22e00-bb9d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sanya Observatory

cef26158-ba13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Entity Definition:**
**OGO 2 (Orbiting Geophysical Observatory 2)** was an American geophysical research satellite launched in 1965 to study aurora and airglow emissions, energetic particles, magnetic field variations, and ionospheric properties, particularly over polar regions.
cef26158-ba13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label:
Near Infrared Camera and Multi-Object Spectrometer on Hubble Space Telescope

cf0589c4-b5f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Tromsø Geophysical Observatory**: A ground-based facility located in the Auroral Region on Earth's surface, established in 1930, primarily focused on geomagnetic measurements and observations.
cf0589c4-b5f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Tromsø Observatory

cf074706-b95c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Solar and Cosmic-Ray Particles** instrument on the IMP-J mission was designed to measure energy spectra, composition, and angular distributions of solar and galactic electrons, protons, and heavier nuclei up to atomic number 30 using three distinct detector systems.
cf074706-b95c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument on Interplanetary Monitoring Platform J

cf07c8b6-b6cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Ritter Observatory is an astronomical observatory owned and operated by the University of Toledo in Ohio, known for its 1.06-meter Ritchey-Chrétien telescope used primarily for spectroscopic research and public viewing events.
cf07c8b6-b6cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.06m Telescope at Ritter Observatory, United States

cf0d80d4-b5d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Beijing Station is a ground-based facility in the CPMN magnetometer network, located in Daolingjian, Changping District, Beijing, China. It operates a fluxgate instrument to monitor geomagnetic activity at coordinates 40.28° N latitude and 116.18° E longitude.
cf0d80d4-b5d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Beijing Observatory, China

cf31d46e-b5ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hobart Ionosonde is a radar instrument stationed near Hobart, Tasmania, Australia, used for investigating the Earth's ionosphere. It has been operational since December 1945 and currently employs an IPS 5D vertical sounding ionosonde that sweeps frequencies from about 1.0 to 21.5 MHz.
cf31d46e-b5ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionosonde part of Hobart Observatory, Australia

cf3895c0-b963-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ruhr University Bochum and Catholic University of the North (UCN) 0.41m Bochum Monitoring Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Cerro Armazones Observatory in South America, designed for monitoring astronomical phenomena with a 0.41-meter aperture.
cf3895c0-b963-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 0.41m Bochum Monitoring Telescope at Cerro Armazones Observatory

cf3e0ed8-b82d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Discovery Bay North Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at the IAGA station identified as DIS, located in Discovery Bay North. It has been operational since January 1, 1876.
cf3e0ed8-b82d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Discovery Bay Observatory

cf428d1a-b912-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The VLT Yepun (UT4) is an 8.2-meter telescope operating in the optical waveband, located at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile. It is one of four Unit Telescopes that comprise the Very Large Telescope (VLT) and utilizes active optics for optimal image quality.
cf428d1a-b912-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 8.2m Unit Telescope 4 on Very Large Telescope at Paranal Observatory, Chile

cf44faaa-b688-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SSJ/4 (Special Sensor for Precipitating Particles, Version 4) on DMSP-5D-2 is a spectrometer designed to measure the fluxes and energies of electrons and ions precipitated into the upper atmosphere.
cf44faaa-b688-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor for Precipitating Particles on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

cf4ad8f8-b9bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RAPID (Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors) instrument on the Cluster 2/FM8 (Tango) spacecraft is a dual-sensor spectrometer designed to analyze suprathermal plasma distributions, measuring electrons and ions within specific energy ranges and providing angular distributions over 180 degrees.
cf4ad8f8-b9bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors part of Cluster 2

cf513e40-b91d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/F17 SESS/SSI/ES-3 is a Scintillation Detector launched in 2006 as part of the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program, designed to measure electron density, temperatures, ion density, plasma drift, and scintillation at orbital altitude.
cf513e40-b91d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Ionospheric Plasma Drift and Scintillation Monitor-3 on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

cf538f7c-b5aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **La Fecha Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Arroyo de la Encomienda, Valladolid, Spain, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
cf538f7c-b5aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: La Fecha Observatory, Spain

cf593d50-b8f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lvye Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Huqiu District, Suzhou City, Jiangsu, China. It is situated at the coordinates 120.32031 longitude and 31.321361 latitude on Earth.
cf593d50-b8f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lvye Observatory, China

cf679158-b842-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EMN Alibag station** is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Koliwada, Alibag, Maharashtra, India, part of the EMN magnetometer network.
cf679158-b842-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Alibag Observatory, India

cf6f54a8-b7a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Apollo 12** was the second manned mission to land on the Moon, launched on November 14, 1969. Astronauts Charles Conrad, Jr., Richard F. Gordon, and Alan L. Bean conducted scientific experiments, deployed the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiment Package (ALSEP), and collected lunar samples during their 31.5-hour stay on the lunar surface.
cf6f54a8-b7a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package part of Apollo 12

cf80694e-b67b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DENIS instrument is a 3-channel near-infrared camera developed by the Observatoire de Paris and used for surveying the southern sky at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile. It operates with specific characteristics for its I, J, and Ks channels, enabling it to detect faint celestial sources through detailed photometric measurements.
cf80694e-b67b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep European Near-Infrared southern sky Survey 3-Channel Near-Infrared Camera on 1.0 meter Telescope at La Silla Observatory, Chile

cf8149b8-ba27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Moca Geomagnetic Observatory (MFP) was a ground-based facility located in Malabo Pequeño, Equatorial Guinea, operational from 1958 to 1971, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity.
cf8149b8-ba27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Moca Geomagnetic Observatory, Equatorial Guinea

cf819cc4-b699-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ESF Spectroheliograph at the National Solar Observatory's Evans Solar Facility in New Mexico is a specialized camera that scans images of the Sun while filtering light to specific wavelengths (e.g., from hydrogen or calcium atoms) to study the solar atmosphere’s structure at various heights, facilitating comparisons with distant stars.
cf819cc4-b699-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager at National Solar Observatory's Evans Solar Facility, United States

cf8406bc-b761-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Les Tardieux Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Julien, Martigues, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
cf8406bc-b761-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Les Tardieux Observatory, France

cf92b6a8-b748-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Scalar Magnetometer on Magsat was an instrument featuring two cesium-vapor sensor heads that measured the total magnetic field with high accuracy, providing digital data used for spacecraft telemetry.
cf92b6a8-b748-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scalar Magnetometer part of Magsat

cf9ce638-ba44-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite (LCROSS) was a NASA mission designed to search for water ice on the Moon by impacting the lunar surface with an upper stage rocket and observing the resulting ejecta plume. Launched in 2009, it successfully confirmed the presence of water in the Cabeus crater near the lunar south pole.
cf9ce638-ba44-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite

cfaa0176-bb91-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1U X-ray Instrument (XRI)** is a scintillation detector used in the BARREL project to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It utilizes a NaI crystal, photomultiplier tube, and pulse height analyzer to convert X-ray energies into charge pulses for spectral analysis.
cfaa0176-bb91-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

cfadca70-ba1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Carbuncle Hill Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in Coventry, Rhode Island, United States. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical research and observations.
cfadca70-ba1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Carbuncle Hill Observatory, United States

cfb0c5fe-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Orbis Tertius Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Cordoba, Argentina. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting various astronomical observations and research activities.
cfb0c5fe-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Orbis Tertius Observatory, Argentina

cfbdb5f6-b9af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Thule observatory (identified as THL by IAGA) used for measuring magnetic fields, operational since 1955.
cfbdb5f6-b9af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Thule Observatory

cfc05e0c-b651-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2D X-ray Instrument (XRI)** is a scintillation detector used in the BARREL project to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons, featuring an energy response from 10 keV to 10 MeV with varying time and energy resolutions.
cfc05e0c-b651-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

cfc0625e-b73b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **SWARM-A Orbital Information**: This dataset provides orbital ephemerides for the Swarm-A satellite, derived from magnetometer (MAG), electric field instrument / Langmuir probe (EFI/LP), and thermal ion imager (EFI/TII) measurements.
cfc0625e-b73b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SWARM-A Orbital Information part of Swarm Mission

cfd297ea-bb4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Göttingen Geomagnetic Observatory (GTT) was a ground-based facility in Germany that operated from 1957 to 1958, located in Göttingen, Lower Saxony. It was equipped with a magnetometer and focused on geomagnetic measurements.
cfd297ea-bb4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Göttingen Geomagnetic Observatory, Germany

cfdea806-b720-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Alabama Observatory is a ground-based observational facility equipped with a 0.25m Fecker telescope, located at the University of Alabama and dedicated to astronomical research and education.
cfdea806-b720-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: University of Alabama Observatory

cfe06ed2-b867-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Chandrayaan-1 Orbiter Mini-RF Forerunner** is a small imaging radar (Mini-SAR) designed to map the lunar poles, specifically aiming to detect and locate water ice deposits by measuring radar reflectivity and polarization ratio.
cfe06ed2-b867-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Miniature Synthetic Aperture Radar on Chandrayaan-1

cfe46940-b184-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rover Camera Left for MPFR (urn:nasa:pds:context:instrument:rclt.mpfr) is a high-resolution imaging system mounted on the left side of a rover platform, used to capture detailed images of terrain and surroundings for navigation and scientific research.
cfe46940-b184-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Rover Camera Left on Mars Pathfinder

cfe8050e-b982-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Particle Plasma Investigation (PLS) for the Galileo Mission is an instrument suite that includes four electrostatic analyzers and three magnetic mass spectrometers designed to measure the composition, energy spectra, and velocity distributions of charged particles in the Jovian magnetosphere.
cfe8050e-b982-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer part of Particle Plasma Investigation on Galileo

cff56232-bb38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **SLIM Laser Retro-Reflector Array (LRA)** is a small, passive optical instrument designed to enable precise laser ranging from lunar orbiting spacecraft. It consists of eight 1.27-cm diameter corner cube retroreflectors mounted on an aluminum structure and is used for geolocation and as a fiducial marker on the lunar surface.
cff56232-bb38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Laser Retroreflector Array on SLIM Lander

cffd6c5e-b6fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plasma Wave Receiver (PWS) on Voyager 1 is an instrument designed to detect and analyze plasma waves in space, aiding the study of interactions between solar wind and planetary environments.
cffd6c5e-b6fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Wave Receiver on Voyager 1

d0020030-b5ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: NenuFAR is a large, low-frequency radio telescope located at the Nançay Radioastronomy Station in France, designed to observe frequencies between 10 MHz and 85 MHz with high sensitivity.
d0020030-b5ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: NenuFAR radio telescope at Nançay Radio Observatory, France

d0120efa-b6c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cerro Murphy Observatory is an international astrophysical project located on Cerro Murphy in the Antofagasta Region of Chile, operated by the Nicolaus Copernicus Astronomical Center of the Polish Academy of Sciences. It houses several telescopes and is known for its high-altitude location ideal for astronomical observations.
d0120efa-b6c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rolf Chini Cerro Murphy Observatory, Chile

d0148b4a-b61e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The RAS Observatory in Biggera Waters is an astronomical observatory located on Earth at Lergessner Street, Gold Coast City, Queensland, Australia.
d0148b4a-b61e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: RAS Observatory

d016eea4-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The HUT (H16) Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Eagle, Colorado. It is a ground-based facility situated at East Royal Elk Road, Eagle County, with geographical coordinates 39.632573° N and 253.289° E.
d016eea4-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Eagle Observatory, United States

d01b286a-bb0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The UVSIPS (Auroral UV Emission Line Measurements) on the Interball Auroral Probe is a spectrometer designed to map ionospheric auroral characteristics by measuring UV emissions at specific wavelengths, utilizing a slit-less spectrograph with a plane diffraction grid.
d01b286a-bb0f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Spectrometer part of Interball Auroral Probe

d030a0ea-b70f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nachi-Katsuura Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Nachikatsuura, Wakayama, Japan, situated within the Yoshino-Kumano National Park and facing the Pacific Ocean.
d030a0ea-b70f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nachi-Katsuura Observatory, Japan

d0394032-bad5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mt. Kajigamori Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Otoyo, Nagaoka County, Kochi Prefecture, Japan (MPC ID: 421).
d0394032-bad5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mt. Kajigamori Observatory, Japan

d03b8946-ba85-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Macquarie Island Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Lochbuy Street, Macquarie, Australian Capital Territory. It is funded by Geoscience Australia and focuses on monitoring Earth's magnetic field.
d03b8946-ba85-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetic Observatory at Macquarie Island Magnetic Observatory, Australia

d03e29f0-b5ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** NOAA 18 is an operational polar orbiting meteorological satellite operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), designed to provide data for weather forecasting, oceanographic services, and space environment monitoring. It features advanced instrumentation including the Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer/3 (AVHRR/3) and other sensors for comprehensive environmental observation.
d03e29f0-b5ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label:
Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer/3 on NOAA 18
High Resolution Infrared Radiation Sounder/3 on NOAA 18
Search and Rescue Satellite Aided Tracking System on NOAA 18
ARGOS Data Collection System-2 on NOAA 18
Solar Backscatter Ultraviolet Spectral radiometer/2 on NOAA 18
Advanced Microwave Sounding Unit on NOAA 18

d045ffe6-b7fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Hornsund Ground Magnetic Field Instrument** is a magnetometer located in Hornsund, Poland, operational since January 1978. It is part of the IUGONET observatory and contributes to the World Data Centre for Geomagnetism in Kyoto.
d045ffe6-b7fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iugonet Observatory

d0571390-ba72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Toolik Lake Geophysical Observatory, established on November 2, 2013, is a ground facility located in the Unorganized Borough of Alaska, United States. It includes instruments such as a magnetometer and is situated at latitude 66.6° N and longitude 210.4° E on Earth's surface.
d0571390-ba72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Toolik Lake Geophysical Observatory, United States

d05b7206-b710-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) All-Sky Imager at Paratunka, Russia is a multi-wavelength instrument developed to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere by observing nocturnal airglow emissions.
d05b7206-b710-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: All-Sky Imager part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Investigation at ISEE Observatory, Russia

d0602c46-b702-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** GEOS-1 was a European Space Agency (ESA) spacecraft intended to be the first satellite in equatorial geostationary orbit dedicated entirely to scientific measurements of Earth's magnetosphere. Due to a launch vehicle failure, it ended up in a 12-hour commensurate orbit but still contributed valuable data to the International Magnetospheric Study (IMS).
d0602c46-b702-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: European GEOS Mission on Geos-1

d063f510-b671-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Camp Douglas Geomagnetic Observatory (CDS), located in Wisconsin, USA, is a ground facility that includes a magnetometer for monitoring geomagnetic activity as part of the global network coordinated by the World Data Center for Geomagnetism, Kyoto.
d063f510-b671-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Camp Douglas Geomagnetic Observatory

d06cfb8e-bb02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover Navigation Cameras (Navcams) are high-resolution stereo cameras mounted on the rover's mast to assist in autonomous navigation and hazard detection, providing crucial 3D images of Martian terrain for safe route planning.
d06cfb8e-bb02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Navigation Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

d075be32-b8bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Riethnordhausen Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Thuringia, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
d075be32-b8bd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Riethnordhausen Observatory, Germany

d0859f68-b64d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetometers at Binza (BIN) were instruments used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field at the BIN station from 1953 to 1973. They were part of the IAGA investigation and connected to the IUGONET Observatory, with data archived by WDC Kyoto.
d0859f68-b64d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Binza Observatory

d096d090-b8b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Hamburg-Georgswerder Observatory** (code 631) is an astronomical observatory located in Hamburg, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
d096d090-b8b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hamburg-Georgswerder Observatory, Germany

d097a2ae-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Science and Engineering Research Council (SERC)/NASA Ariel V was a space mission satellite designed for X-ray astronomy, aimed at studying celestial sources of X-rays.
d097a2ae-b7a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: x-ray Science and Engineering Research Council NASA Ariel V Satellite Mission

d0a0eb48-ba61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is a ground-based meteor radar facility located at Herwighamna, Bear Island in Svalbard, Norway. It operates under the Tromsø Geophysical Observatory and the University of Tromsø, focusing on atmospheric research and meteor detection.
d0a0eb48-ba61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Meteor Radar at Tromsoe Geophysical Observatory, Norway

d0ac5910-b976-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Augerolles Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Augerolles, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
d0ac5910-b976-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Augerolles Observatory, France

d0b84acc-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EMN magnetometer network in L'Aquila, Italy** is a ground-based observatory located at Via Casale Calore in L'Aquila, Italy (42.38° N, 13.32° E), dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity on Earth’s surface.
d0b84acc-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at L'Aquila Observatory, Italy

d0b94f80-bb88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tungsten Geomagnetic Observatory (TST) is a ground-based facility located in the Dehcho Region of Northwest Territories, Canada, designed for geomagnetic monitoring and research. It is sponsored by the United States and is part of the IAGA observatory network.
d0b94f80-bb88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Tungsten, Canada

d0c25cf4-b69e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Valinhos Observatory, also known as the Abrahão de Moraes Observatory, is an astronomical observatory located in Valinhos, São Paulo, Brazil. It operates from a ground-based facility and focuses on astronomical observations and research.
d0c25cf4-b69e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Abrahão de Moraes Observatory, Brazil

d0c2b0d0-bbff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2X X-Ray Instrument (XRI) is a scintillation detector designed to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It utilizes a NaI crystal, photomultiplier tube, and pulse height analyzer to detect and analyze X-ray energies from 10 keV to 10 MeV with varying resolutions for different scientific objectives.
d0c2b0d0-bbff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

d0caedac-b751-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lunar Prospector Spacecraft Alpha Particle Spectrometer (APS) was an instrument on the Lunar Prospector spacecraft designed to detect alpha particles and measure transient lunar outgassing events, contributing to the understanding of the tenuous lunar atmosphere.
d0caedac-b751-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Alpha Particle Spectrometer on Lunar Prospector

d0d28484-b843-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Muon Telescope at Sakashita** is a ground-based multi-directional muon detection facility operated by the Institute for Space and Astronautical Science (ISAS) in Sakashita, Gifu Prefecture, Japan. It is located approximately 80 meters water equivalent below the surface.
d0d28484-b843-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Multi-directional Muon Telescope at Sakashita, Japan

d0d351b2-b5db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Vedrus Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Azovskaya, Krasnodar Krai, Russia. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
d0d351b2-b5db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Azovskaya Observatory, Russia

d0dd8cca-b7a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The International Cometary Explorer (ICE) spacecraft, initially known as the International Sun-Earth Explorer-3 (ISEE-3), was launched on August 12, 1978, to study solar-terrestrial interactions and later repurposed to explore comets Giacobini-Zinner and Halley.
d0dd8cca-b7a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.77m International Sun-Earth Explorer 3 on International Sun-Earth Explorer Program

d0f2dfb4-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "NOAA 7 Positions" dataset provides the spacecraft positions of NOAA 7 in different coordinate systems.
