d0f2dfb4-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: NOAA 7 Positions on NOAA 7

d0f9e77e-bab7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The G. Colombo Astronomical Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Padua, Italy, dedicated to the study of celestial bodies and phenomena.
d0f9e77e-bab7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: G. Colombo Astronomical Observatory, Italy

d10196e0-bae4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hypatia Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Viserba Monte, Rimini, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
d10196e0-bae4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hypatia Observatory, Italy

d1041f3c-b7a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dominion Astrophysical Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Saanich, British Columbia, Canada, known for its 72-inch Plaskett telescope and contributions to astrophysical research since its completion in 1918.
d1041f3c-b7a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.83m Plaskett Telescope at Dominion Astrophysical Observatory, Canada

d106a12a-b84c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Jura Observatory is an astronomical observatory located near Vicques in the Canton of Jura, Switzerland, owned and operated by the Jura Astronomy Society. It was built between 1993 and 1998 and has an IAU observatory code of 185.
d106a12a-b84c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Jura Observatory, Switzerland

d109a188-b6e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Greens Norton Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Smithland Court, Bengal, Greens Norton, West Northamptonshire, England. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center code 967 and is situated at coordinates 52.13656 latitude and -0.8442 longitude (358.9778 converted to standard format).
d109a188-b6e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Greens Norton Observatory, United Kingdom

d10cb946-baba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS-B Digital Fields Board Filter Bank is an instrument component on the THEMIS spacecraft that provides band-pass filtering for EFI and SCM spectra, as well as peak and average values of the E12HF signal. It processes data through a series of filters and decimations to reduce computational power while maintaining essential signal characteristics.
d10cb946-baba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Filter Bank on Digital Fields Board part of Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms Mission

d11910bc-bba3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Magion 4 (1995-039F) is a small Czech scientific satellite that was part of the Interball Project. Launched in 1995, it aimed to study solar wind energy transmission to Earth's magnetosphere and its dissipation during substorms, carrying about ten scientific instruments on board.
d11910bc-bba3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magion 4 part of Interball

d11f1f68-b61f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lowell Observatory 1.1m (42inch) John S. Hall Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Lowell Observatory's Anderson Mesa site in North America. It has a 1.1-meter aperture and is used for astronomical observations.
d11f1f68-b61f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.1m optical John S. Hall Telescope at Lowell Observatory, Anderson Mesa

d1283a94-b7c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Haverford Observatory (MPC ID: 437) is an astronomical observatory located at Haverford College in Pennsylvania, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
d1283a94-b7c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Haverford Observatory

d12c158c-b774-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The University of Rhode Island Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Quonochontaug, Rhode Island. It serves as a ground-based facility for stargazing and astronomical research.
d12c158c-b774-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Quonochontaug Observatory

d147d7f4-bb75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: DRACO (Didymos Reconnaissance and Asteroid Camera for Optical navigation) was a high-resolution optical imager on the DART impactor spacecraft, designed to provide detailed images of asteroids.
d147d7f4-bb75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Didymos Reconnaissance and Asteroid Camera for Optical Navigation on DART

d14ef638-b5e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Little America geophysical observatory was a ground-based facility located on the Earth's surface at coordinates 194.417 longitude and -78.18 latitude, operating from July 1, 1957, to December 31, 1958. It included magnetometer instruments as part of its operations.
d14ef638-b5e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Little America Observatory

d1501642-b71c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Prairie Grass Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Camp Cullom in Clinton County, Indiana, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
d1501642-b71c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Prairie Grass Observatory, United States

d15092e0-b689-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The E2 Fluxgate Magnetometer is a triaxial instrument mounted on the Helios 2 spacecraft to measure magnetic field fluctuations up to 4 Hz, featuring dual measurement ranges and a flipper mechanism for sensor re-orientation.
d15092e0-b689-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer for Field Fluctuations part of Helios 2

d1581820-ba04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Tjornes, Iceland, used for the Conjugate Observation at Iceland investigation.
d1581820-ba04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Conjugate Observation at Iceland

d15aed00-b5b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Mars Advanced Radar for Subsurface and Ionosphere Sounding (MARSIS) is a low-frequency radar sounder on the Mars Express orbiter designed to probe beneath the Martian surface and study its ionosphere, using synthetic aperture techniques to enhance subsurface reflections.
d15aed00-b5b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Advanced Radar for Subsurface and Ionosphere Sounding on Mars Express

d15f7cb0-b783-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: River Moss Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Saint Peters, Missouri, USA, with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 852.
d15f7cb0-b783-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: River Moss Observatory

d1621cc4-b5b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Apollo 16 Lunar Surface Experiments Package Passive Seismic Experiment (PSE) was part of the ALSEP program, which deployed seismometers on the lunar surface to monitor moonquakes and other seismic activity from 1969 to 1977.
d1621cc4-b5b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Passive Seismic Experiment part of Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package

d167c2a4-bb74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Pruhonice, Czech Republic (URSI-code: PQ052), is a ground facility equipped with an advanced ionosonde called Digisonde. This station evaluates the angle of arrival, polarization, and Doppler frequency shift of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere, in addition to their travel time.
d167c2a4-bb74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Ionospheric Station Pruhonice, Czech Republic

d16f690a-b9ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Reflectance Experiment Laboratory (RELAB) Bidirectional Visible and Near Infrared Spectrometer is a highly specialized instrument originally developed for analyzing returned lunar samples, capable of measuring reflectance with adjustable incidence and emergence angles up to 70 degrees, covering wavelengths from 0.3 to 2.6 microns.
d16f690a-b9ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible and Near Infrared Spectrometer at NASA Reflectance Experiment Laboratory

d170e962-b6a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Swan Hill Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Swan Hill, Victoria, Australia. It is a ground-based facility used for stargazing and astronomical research.
d170e962-b6a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Swan Hill Observatory, Australia

d19b3c16-b7e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Mundenheim Observatory was an astronomical observatory located in Ludwigshafen am Rhein, Germany, operational from 1907 to 1913.
d19b3c16-b7e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mundenheim Observatory, Germany

d1a2a008-b715-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Sendai Astronomical Observatory Ayashi Station**, located in Sendai, Japan, is a ground-based astronomical observatory established in 1975. It is situated at the coordinates 38.265246° N, 140.77843° E and operates under the MPC ID 391.
d1a2a008-b715-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ayashi Astronomical Observatory, Japan

d1a7f720-b7f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Loysburg Magnetometer is an instrument located at the Loysburg Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation. It measures magnetic field variations and has been operational since October 28, 2005.
d1a7f720-b7f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Loysburg Observatory

d1ae9ce4-bba4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Petit Sant Feliu Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Sant Feliu de Llobregat, Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
d1ae9ce4-bba4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Petit Sant Feliu Observatory, Spain

d1b4febc-b75e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Horizon Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Petropavlovsk, Kazakhstan. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
d1b4febc-b75e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Horizon Observatory, Kazakhstan

d1bb5384-b7f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Camarillo Observatory is an astronomical facility located at 469 Rowland Avenue in Old Town, Camarillo, Ventura County, California. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is situated within the United States.
d1bb5384-b7f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Camarillo Observatory

d1bbd8ec-b856-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astronomical Observatory in Tradate is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Strada consorziale ai Ronchi, Tradate, Italy. It began operations on May 13, 2007, and is known for its contributions to astrometry and minor planet discoveries.
d1bbd8ec-b856-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory in Tradate, Italy

d1c0acc2-b631-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mazagon Huelva Observatory (Q115633532) is an astronomical observatory located in Calle Montemar, Mazagón, Moguer, Comarca Metropolitana de Huelva, Huelva, Andalusia, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
d1c0acc2-b631-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mazagon Huelva Observatory, Spain

d1cc3436-b927-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **DSS-43 64-m Radio Telescope** is a fully steerable parabolic reflector radio antenna located at the Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex in Australia, initially operational with a 64-meter aperture in 1972 and later extended to 70 meters. It is part of NASA's Deep Space Network and managed by CSIRO.
d1cc3436-b927-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 64m Deep Space Station 43 Radio Telescope at Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex, Australia

d1d6e9a8-b85a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hiroshima University's 1.5m Kanata Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Higashi-Hiroshima Observatory in Asia, used for astronomical observations and research.
d1d6e9a8-b85a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.5m Kanata Telescope at Higashi-Hiroshima Observatory

d1d94480-b924-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The JMA magnetometer at the Kakioka Magnetic Observatory includes variometers, such as a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer for vector field components (X, Y, Z) and an Overhauser magnetometer for scalar field (F), along with absolute instruments like a magnetometer theodolite for declination (D) and inclination (I), and a proton precession magnetometer for total field intensity (F).
d1d94480-b924-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kyoto World Data Center Observatory

d1ddbd72-bb76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS Solid State Telescope (SST) is an instrument on the THEMIS spacecraft that measures the intensity of superthermal electrons and ions, primarily within energy ranges of 30-100 keV for electrons and 30-300 keV for ions. It utilizes paired sensors to cover a wide angular range and includes features like magnetic contamination reduction and dynamic range enhancement.
d1ddbd72-bb76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument on THEMIS

d1e3e1f4-bbbf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The St-Martin Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Amathay-Vésigneux, France. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
d1e3e1f4-bbbf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: St-Martin Observatory, France

d1e416f4-ba1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The YNAO H-alpha Telescope, part of the Yunnan Astronomical Observatory in Kunming, China, is a full disk solar telescope with an 18 cm aperture, equipped with a tunable filter and a 2K x 2K CCD camera for high-resolution imaging.
d1e416f4-ba1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 18cm H-alpha Imager on 18cm Solar Tower at Yunnan Astronomical Observatory, China

d1e74766-baa4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at HVD is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Khovd, Mongolia, used for magnetic field measurements as part of the MAGDAS observation network.
d1e74766-baa4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MAGDAS Observation Network

d1fc1892-bc5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Teplitz Bay is a ground-based observatory located in the Primorsky District, Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia, known for its magnetometer instrument used to study geomagnetic fields and related phenomena since 1904.
d1fc1892-bc5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Teplitz Bay Observatory, Russia

d20609ea-bb4d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Explorer 33, also known as IMP-D and AIMP-1, was an American scientific satellite in the Explorer program launched by NASA on July 1, 1966. Although it failed to achieve its intended lunar orbit, it successfully conducted studies of interplanetary plasma, energetic charged particles, magnetic fields, and solar X rays from a highly elliptical Earth orbit.
d20609ea-bb4d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Explorer 33 spacecraft part of Interplanetary Monitoring Platform

d210c626-b839-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetometers at Rapid City (RPC) is an instrument located at the IAGA-identified RPC station within the IUGONET Observatory. It measures magnetic fields and contributes to geomagnetic research, part of a broader network for global observations.
d210c626-b839-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observatory

d21ade86-ba5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Observatório Astronômico da Universidade Federal do Amazonas" (OARU) is a ground-based observatory located in Manaus, Brazil. It serves as an astronomical research facility and is situated at Rua Bela Vista, Santa Etelvina, Manaus.
d21ade86-ba5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatory at Manaus, Brazil

d2252b04-b8be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA/University of California, Berkeley Space Sciences Laboratory's Cosmic Hot Interstellar Plasma Spectrometer satellite (CHIPSat) was a space mission designed to study the ultraviolet emissions from hot interstellar plasma.
d2252b04-b8be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cosmic Hot Interstellar Plasma Spectrometer on CHIPSat Mission

d229e692-b8c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Buffalo Creek Observatory** is a ground-based observatory located at 1998 Sylvester Drive in Brantley County, Georgia, United States. It is situated at latitude 31.14683 and longitude -82.0391 (or 278.0391 in positive degrees), within the continent of North America.
d229e692-b8c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Buffalo Creek Observatory

d23062f0-b7f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Alicante Observatory is an astronomical facility located in el Campello, Alicante, Spain, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects.
d23062f0-b7f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Alicante Observatory, Spain

d231369c-b67f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Silchar Observatory is a ground-based facility in Dalu, Silchar, India, dedicated to geomagnetic observations. It operates under the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) and has been active since January 1999.
d231369c-b67f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Silchar Geomagnetic Observatory, India

d2371c00-b68a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover rear Hazard Avoidance Cameras (Hazcams), specifically the left camera on string B, assist in navigation and safety by providing high-resolution images to detect potential obstacles behind the rover during its movement on Mars.
d2371c00-b68a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rear Hazard Avoidance Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

d23ff86c-b9b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bereznyaki Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Karaganda, Kazakhstan, known for its magnetometer instrument and operational since 1965.
d23ff86c-b9b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bereznyaki Observatory, Kazakhstan

d244f9c6-b67e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Geiger Tube Telescope on Pioneer 11 is an instrument designed to detect and measure cosmic rays and high-energy charged particles using a system of Geiger-Müller tubes arranged in a telescope configuration. It utilizes seven miniature Geiger tubes in three arrays to measure proton and electron fluxes near Jupiter and Saturn, providing detailed data on particle energies and distributions in interplanetary space.
d244f9c6-b67e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geiger Tube Telescope on Pioneer 11

d25809ee-bade-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Apia Magnetic Observatory** is a ground-based facility in Apia, Samoa, dedicated to monitoring magnetic fields on Earth's surface since 1905.
d25809ee-bade-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Apia Magnetic Observatory

d2738e9c-b1bc-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes JunoCam, a wide-angle visible-light camera on the Juno spacecraft designed for public engagement by capturing images of Jupiter.
d2738e9c-b1bc-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible-Light Camera on Juno Spacecraft

d27863c4-ba02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Tarui Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Iwade, Tarui, Fuwa County, Gifu Prefecture, Japan. It serves as a facility for conducting observations and research related to astronomy and astrophysics.
d27863c4-ba02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tarui Observatory

d27bf1fa-b9c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ) 45m Radio Telescope is located at the Nobeyama Radio Observatory in Asia and operates in the millimeter waveband. It has an aperture of 45 meters and is part of the Nobeyama Radio Observatory facilities.
d27bf1fa-b9c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: millimeter 45.0m National Astronomical Observatory of Japan Radio Telescope at Nobeyama Radio Observatory

d285107c-b6c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, Daytona Beach 1m Telescope is an optical telescope with a 1.0-meter aperture located at the Embry-Riddle Observatory in North America, used for astronomical observations.
d285107c-b6c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.0m Optical Telescope at Embry-Riddle Observatory

d28b51f4-ba08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Energetic Particle and Plasma Spectrometer (EPPS) with the Fast Imaging Plasma Spectrometer (FIPS) is part of NASA's MESSENGER mission. It measures the distribution and composition of magnetosphere ions within a specific energy range, utilizing advanced detection methods to analyze ion properties and generate comprehensive data for scientific analysis.
d28b51f4-ba08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle and Plasma Spectrometer and Fast Imaging Plasma Spectrometer part of MESSENGER

d28c9a56-b98f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Phobos 1 was a Soviet space probe launched in 1988 to explore Mars and its moons Phobos and Deimos. The mission ended prematurely due to a computer malfunction that caused communication loss on September 2, 1988.
d28c9a56-b98f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Phobos 1

d293e2d8-ba53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Europa Clipper Gravity/Radio Science (G/RS) instrument is part of the NASA Europa Clipper mission. It measures Europa's gravity at various points in its orbit to study the moon's internal structure and flexing caused by Jupiter's gravitational pull.
d293e2d8-ba53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gravity and Radio Science part of Europa Clipper

d29722d0-bb08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Novokazalinsk Observatory**: A ground-based magnetic observatory located in Kazakhstan, operating from 1965 to 1993 and sponsored by the country. It was part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network and contributed data to the World Data Center in Kyoto.
d29722d0-bb08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Novokazalinsk Observatory, Kazakhstan

d29a3f44-bac5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Flensburg Observatory was a ground-based facility in Flensburg, Germany, operational from 1891 to 1903, primarily known for its magnetometer instruments.
d29a3f44-bac5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Flensburg Observatory, Germany

d29b16f8-bb15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Dogsheaven Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Brasília, Brazil, primarily used for ground-based observations.
d29b16f8-bb15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dogsheaven Observatory

d29ec73e-b7dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The H.E.S.S. Collaboration High Energy Stereoscopic System (HESS) is a set of gamma-ray imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes located in Africa, designed to study high-energy astrophysical phenomena.
d29ec73e-b7dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: gamma-ray High Energy Stereoscopic System imaging atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes

d29f78a8-ba9b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS)** onboard the DMSP/F17 satellite is a multi-purpose microwave radiometer that provides imagery and temperature/humidity sounding channels for enhanced precipitation monitoring, operating with 24 channels across 21 frequencies in the 54 and 183 GHz bands.
d29f78a8-ba9b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Microwave Imager and Sounder part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

d2a1dfde-b943-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity (MER 1) Miniature Thermal Emission Spectrometer (Mini-TES) was an instrument aboard the Opportunity rover that measured infrared radiation to analyze mineralogy and thermophysical properties of Martian surfaces, aiding in understanding Mars' geology and past water activity.
d2a1dfde-b943-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: infrared Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity Miniature Thermal Emission Spectrometer on Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity

d2a8d0ea-b93f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wanapum Dam Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Wanapum State Park Campground, Kittitas County, Washington, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID 667.
d2a8d0ea-b93f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wanapum Dam Observatory, United States

d2adf7b0-b8fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Canon EOS Digital Rebel XT (also known as the EOS 350D) is a compact and user-friendly digital single-lens reflex (DSLR) camera released in 2005, featuring an 8.0-megapixel CMOS sensor and popular among beginner and intermediate photographers for its balance of ease of use and manual controls.
d2adf7b0-b8fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Canon EOS 350D

d2aefae8-b975-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fuquene Geomagnetic Observatory (FUQ) is a ground-based facility in Fúquene, Colombia, established in 1954 for geomagnetic observations. It operates as part of the IUGONET network and includes a magnetometer instrument provided by WDC Kyoto.
d2aefae8-b975-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fuquene Geomagnetic Observatory

d2b07bb2-bb27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Kingsnake Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Seguin, Texas. It is a ground-based facility established in 2001 for conducting astronomical observations and research.
d2b07bb2-bb27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kingsnake Observatory

d2baf5bc-b779-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: CHON, Stekene is a ground-based observatory located at 103A-103B Dorpsstraat in Bormte, Stekene, Belgium. It functions as an astronomical facility situated in East Flanders, Belgium.
d2baf5bc-b779-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: CHON Observatory, Belgium

d2bbb0d8-b93b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Australian National University 0.5m Uppsala Schmidt Telescope at Siding Spring Observatory (SSO), also known as the Catalina Sky Survey telescope, is a 0.5-meter optical telescope located in New South Wales, Australia.
d2bbb0d8-b93b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.5m Catalina Sky Survey Uppsala Schmidt Telescope at Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

d2c01312-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory (SAO)/Academia Sinica Submillimeter Array (SMA) is an astronomical instrument located at the Mauna Kea Observatory in North America, operating in the millimeter waveband.
d2c01312-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SubMillimeter Array on Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory and Academia Sinica Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatory

d2c1cd76-ba4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Elsterland Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Jeßnigk, Germany. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial objects and phenomena.
d2c1cd76-ba4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Elsterland Observatory, Germany

d2c5485c-b6b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the Deep Space Station 63 (DSS-63), a ground observatory used for deep space communication and observation. It is part of NASA's Deep Space Network, which supports interplanetary spacecraft missions with tracking, telemetry, and command capabilities.
d2c5485c-b6b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: DSS-63 Observatory

d2daffb2-bbbe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Gravity Science Instrument (RSS) for Dawn was a system onboard the Dawn spacecraft that included a deep space transponder and utilized Doppler tracking equipment from the Deep Space Network to conduct gravity science experiments.
d2daffb2-bbbe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gravity Science Instrument on Dawn Spacecraft

d2dd9432-b83c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Raciborz Geomagnetic Observatory (RAC) is a ground-based facility located in Bolesław, Poland, dedicated to monitoring and studying geomagnetic activity. It operates under the sponsorship of Poland and is part of the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto.
d2dd9432-b83c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Raciborz Geomagnetic Observatory, Poland

d2e8ed52-ba79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Chions Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Chions, Pordenone, Italy. It is a ground-based facility used for studying and observing celestial objects.
d2e8ed52-ba79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chions Observatory, Italy

d2eba2fa-b8b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain (McMAC) Worthington Station is a ground-based observatory located in Worthington, Minnesota, USA. It houses one of the nine magnetometers that form part of the McMAC network and is situated at the Minnesota West Community & Technical College.
d2eba2fa-b8b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mid-continent Magnetoseismic Chain Worthington Station, United States

d2ef0dc6-ba11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The OATU Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Tupi Paulista, São Paulo, Brazil. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
d2ef0dc6-ba11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatório Astronômico do Tupi Paulista at Tupi Paulista Observatory, Brazil

d2f2a084-b6f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Val-d'Or (VLDR) Geophysical Observatory is a ground facility located in Saint-Edmond-de-Vassan, Quebec, Canada, which includes a magnetometer and focuses on geophysical observations.
d2f2a084-b6f2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Val-d'Or Geophysical Observatory, Canada

d2f51a3a-b6d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A CPMN fluxgate magnetometer is a three-axis ring-core type instrument installed at Darwin, Australia, used to measure magnetic field variations. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network and operates under the ICSWSE investigation name.
d2f51a3a-b6d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometer Network Investigation

d2fe611c-b5a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Global Surveyor (MGS) Spacecraft Electron Reflectometer was an instrument on the MGS spacecraft designed to study Mars' ionosphere by measuring electron density and energy, aiding in understanding its interaction with solar wind and the Martian atmosphere.
d2fe611c-b5a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Reflectometer on Mars Global Surveyor

d305cd50-bace-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Watheroo Geomagnetic Observatory (WAT) is a ground-based facility located in Western Australia that has been operational since 1919 for monitoring geophysical data, particularly using magnetometers provided by the Kyoto World Data Center.
d305cd50-bace-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Watheroo Geomagnetic Observatory, Australia

d305e00a-ba5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Hermanus station is a ground-based magnetometer network located in Overstrand Ward 4, Western Cape, South Africa (latitude -34.34, longitude 19.24), operated as part of the ICSWSE initiative by IUGONET.
d305e00a-ba5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hermanus Observatory, South Africa

d3060a3e-b9fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2X Data Processing Unit (DPU)** is a versatile instrument controller for the BARREL project, designed to acquire and process data from various sensors such as an X-ray spectrometer and magnetometer, then transmit this information via Iridium modem.
d3060a3e-b9fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Space Particles Relativistic Electron Losses

d30ae38a-b66e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Santa Pola Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Santa Pola, Alicante, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
d30ae38a-b66e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 30 cm Santa Pola Telescope at Santa Pola Observatory, Spain

d313e5d4-b7b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) Birdsville Station is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Birdsville, Australia. It operates as part of the INTERMAGNET network and includes a fluxgate magnetometer to monitor variations in Earth's magnetic field.
d313e5d4-b7b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Birdsville Observatory, Australia

d31b5d92-bb13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Plaisance that operated from 1966 to 1976 as part of the IAGA investigation and the IUGONET Observatory.
d31b5d92-bb13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Plaisance Observatory

d3242fa8-b8e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Spacewatch 1.8m telescope is an astronomical instrument located at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona, designed for high-precision observations with a specialized optical configuration and advanced mechanical design to optimize performance and cost-efficiency.
d3242fa8-b8e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.8m Spacewatch Telescope at Kitt Peak Observatory, United States

d332a41a-b79f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Cambridge Low-Frequency Synthesis Telescope (CLFST) is a radio telescope located at the Mullard Radio Astronomy Observatory in Europe.
d332a41a-b79f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio University of Cambridge Low-Frequency Synthesis Telescope at Mullard Radio Astronomy Observatory

d33b02b2-b836-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Astro820, Samut Prakan** is a ground-based observatory located in Ban Khlong Ku Phara, Bang Pla Subdistrict, Samut Prakan Province, Thailand. It is situated at coordinates 13.57863° N latitude and 100.72972° E longitude.
d33b02b2-b836-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astro820 Observatory, Thailand

d33e8a96-b5ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Asociación Argentina Amigos de la Astronomía (AAAA) is an amateur astronomy organization based in Buenos Aires, Argentina, dedicated to promoting and spreading knowledge about astronomy through educational courses, research collaborations, and public outreach activities. Founded in 1929, it has significantly contributed to the field of astronomy, including having an asteroid named in its honor.
d33e8a96-b5ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Argentine Association of Amateur Astronomers

d33f4534-b5de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences (NAOC) 2.16m Telescope is located at the Beijing Astronomical Observatory in Xinglong Station, Asia, and operates in the optical waveband with an aperture of 2.16 meters.
d33f4534-b5de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.16m optical National Astronomical Observatories, Chinese Academy of Sciences Telescope at Beijing Astronomical Observatory

d341926c-b782-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Oberfrauendorf Observatory (G34) is an astronomical observatory located in Oberfrauendorf, Glashütte, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
d341926c-b782-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Oberfrauendorf Observatory, Germany

d342426a-bbcf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Hiratsuka Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Kitatoyoda, Hiratsuka, Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical research and observations.
d342426a-bbcf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hiratsuka Observatory, Japan

d34b7d88-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Göttingen Observatory is an astronomical institution located in Göttingen, Lower Saxony, Germany. It operates as a ground-based observatory and has been historically known by various names such as Universitätssternwarte Göttingen (Göttingen University Observatory) or königliche Sternwarte Göttingen (Royal Observatory Göttingen).
d34b7d88-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Göttingen Observatory, Germany

d3526090-b635-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **Riometer** (Relative Ionospheric Opacity Meter) is an instrument used to measure the ionospheric absorption of radio waves, typically in polar regions. The **Iqaluit Riometer Instrument** is specifically located at the Iqaluit ground station and is part of the IUGONET observatory network under the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto (WDC-Kyoto).
d3526090-b635-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Riometer part of International Geomagnetic Reference Field, IGRF

d3530e16-bab1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Saint-Saturnin-lès-Avignon Observatory (code: K21) is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Saturnin-lès-Avignon, France. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
d3530e16-bab1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Saint-Saturnin-lès-Avignon Observatory, France

d3555112-bae8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lowell Observatory/Discovery Communications 4.3m Discovery Channel Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Happy Jack site of Lowell Observatory in North America, featuring a 4.3-meter aperture.
d3555112-bae8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 4.3m Discovery Channel Telescope at Lowell Observatory

d36f1266-bac8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Reedy Creek Observatory is an astronomical observatory in Queensland, Australia, known for its observations of near-Earth objects by amateur astronomer John Broughton.
d36f1266-bac8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Reedy Creek Observatory, Australia

d372fe62-b901-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **PAO Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Prato, Tuscany, Italy. It is situated at Via Amerigo Bresci, Pizzidimonte, and serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
d372fe62-b901-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Prato Observatory, Italy

d378dafe-bb35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ulysses Interstellar Neutral Gas (GAS) Experiment is an instrument on the Ulysses spacecraft designed to study the temperature, bulk velocity, and density of interstellar neutral helium gas near our solar system using a sensor that acts like a pin-hole camera for neutral helium and ultraviolet photon measurements.
d378dafe-bb35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutral Particle Detector part of Ulysses Interstellar Neutral Gas Experiment on Ulysses

d37c7f2e-bab3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Madrid DSS-63 is a fully steerable parabolic reflector radio antenna, part of NASA's Deep Space Network, located near Robledo de Chavela, Spain. Originally operational in 1974 with a 64-meter aperture, it was later expanded to 70 meters to support deep space missions like Voyager 2.
d37c7f2e-bab3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 70m Deep Space Station 63 Radio Telescope at Madrid Deep Space Communications Complex, Spain

d37db9a4-b6b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Ager Observatory**, also known as the **Montsec Astronomical Observatory (OAM)**, is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Sant Esteve de la Sarga, Lleida, Catalonia, Spain. It operates under the MPC code L43 and focuses on various astronomical observations and research activities.
d37db9a4-b6b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ager Observatory at Montsec Astronomical Observatory, Spain

d3a23352-b69b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Kamenniyj Mys is a ground-based observatory located in Yamalsky Rayon, Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug, Russia. It operated from January 1, 1976, to December 31, 1980, and was part of the IAGA network, featuring a magnetometer as its primary instrument.
d3a23352-b69b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kamenniyj Mys Observatory, Russia

d3a7d3a6-b610-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The New Horizons Kuiper Belt Extended Mission 2 (KEM2) is a space mission focused on exploring the Kuiper Belt region of our solar system, continuing from the initial New Horizons mission and its first extended phase (KEM1), with the aim of studying various Kuiper Belt Objects and Centaurs, as well as conducting new research in planetary science, heliophysics, and astrophysics.
d3a7d3a6-b610-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: New Horizons Kuiper Belt Extended Mission 2

d3a85d9a-ba97-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Lijiang Station is an astronomical observatory located in Yulong Nakhi Autonomous County, Yunnan, China, operated by the Yunnan Observatories.
d3a85d9a-ba97-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lijiang Station at Yunnan Observatories, China

d3b51d2e-b83e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Meudon Spectroheliograph is an imaging instrument that captures daily data of the solar photosphere and chromosphere by scanning the solar disk using specific spectral lines such as CaII K 3934 Angstrom and H-alpha 6563 Angstrom.
d3b51d2e-b83e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spectroheliograph at Meudon Observatory

d3bf2216-bb49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High Energy Gamma Ray Astronomy Experiment (HEGRA) is a telescope located in Africa and is part of the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory, specialized in detecting gamma-rays.
d3bf2216-bb49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma-ray High Energy Gamma Ray Astronomy Experiment at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory

d3c23048-b863-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Assy-Turgen Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Enbekshikazakh District of Almaty Region, Kazakhstan, operated by the Fesenkov Astrophysical Institute. It is situated within a national park near the city of Esik and operates in the GMT+6 time zone.
d3c23048-b863-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Academician Omarov Assy-Turgen Observatory, Kazakhstan

d3ca4e56-b5d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Chalmers University of Technology 25m Telescope at Onsala Space Observatory (OSO) is a radio telescope located in Europe with an aperture of 25 meters, used for space observations.
d3ca4e56-b5d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio Chalmers University of Technology 25m Telescope at Onsala Space Observatory

d3cb95d0-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "ISEE Magnetometer" is an induction magnetometer located at Husafell, designed to measure variations in the 3-D vector geomagnetic field with a sampling rate of 64 Hz.
d3cb95d0-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Induction Magnetometer part of International Monitor for Auroral Geomagnetic Effects

d3cbac40-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the Raciborz Observatory, a ground-based facility in Bolesław, Poland that is part of the IAGA observatory network and includes a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements.
d3cbac40-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Racibor Observatory, Poland

d3d4e17e-b9ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Carousel Wind Tunnel (CWT) was a portable wind tunnel used by Arizona State University at NASA Ames Research Laboratory for low-gravity and reduced-pressure tests, featuring concentric cylinders to create airflow and measure particle thresholds.
d3d4e17e-b9ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Carousel Wind Tunnel at Planetary Aeolian Laboratory

d3d7e992-b79b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Infrared Radiometer (OIR) on the Pioneer Venus Orbiter was an eight-channel instrument designed for vertical temperature sounding of Venus's atmosphere from cloud tops to 150 km and for studying cloud morphology, including water vapor mapping.
d3d7e992-b79b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Radiometer part of Pioneer Venus Orbiter

d3eb797c-b795-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "NOAA 18 Positions" refers to the positional data of the NOAA 18 spacecraft, recorded in different coordinate systems as part of its operational platform investigation.
d3eb797c-b795-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Part of NOAA 18

d40b0b30-ba46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1G Engineering Data Interface** is a component of the BARREL observatory that performs analog to digital conversion of key temperatures, voltages, and currents. It has multiple inputs for voltage, current, and temperature sensors, all converted with 16-bit precision and scaled to a 5V full-scale range.
d40b0b30-ba46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

d4110888-bae5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Sakai Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Sakai, Osaka Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
d4110888-bae5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sakai Observatory, Japan

d42989ea-b74c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The magnetometer at Borga (BGA) has been operational since January 1975 and is part of the IAGA investigation, located at the Iugonet Observatory in Kyoto.
d42989ea-b74c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Borga Observatory

d4314894-b673-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SMARTS Consortium 1.5-meter Telescope is a Ritchey-Chretien Cassegrain reflector telescope located at the Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile, operated by the Small and Moderate Aperture Research Telescope System (SMARTS) Consortium.
d4314894-b673-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Small and Medium Research Telescope System 1.5m Telescope at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory, Chile

d437d348-b8f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The KOSMA Telescope is a 3-meter millimeter waveband telescope located in Europe, operated by the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn for submillimeter astronomy research.
d437d348-b8f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.0m Kolner Observatorium fur SubMillimeter Astronomie Telescope

d443ae20-b89f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Kotzebue Station is a ground-based facility in Kotzebue, United States, part of the CPMN magnetometer network, dedicated to monitoring magnetic field variations on Earth's surface. It includes a fluxgate instrument and is located at approximately 66.88° N latitude and -162.6° W longitude.
d443ae20-b89f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at CPMN Kotzebue Station, United States

d4445d7a-b6a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **MicrOmega**: A near-infrared (IR) hyperspectral microscope designed to analyze the mineralogical composition of an asteroid's surface, particularly as part of the MASCOT lander mission.
d4445d7a-b6a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Infrared Hyperspectral Microscope on Mascot Lander

d446a96c-b68e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Belem Station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Belém, Pará, Brazil (South America), part of the CPMN magnetometer network.
d446a96c-b68e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer network at Belém Observatory, Brazil

d450e110-bb44-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Copernicus (Orbiting Astronomical Observatory 3)** is a space-based X-ray observatory launched as a joint project by NASA and the UK Science Research Council.
d450e110-bb44-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Copernicus X-ray Satellite part of NASA and United Kingdom Science Research Council Orbiting Astronomical Observatory 3

d459af62-b94f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Copenhagen Geomagnetic Observatory (COP)** was a ground-based facility located in Copenhagen, Denmark, operational from 1891 to 1900, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity.
d459af62-b94f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Copenhagen Geomagnetic Observatory, Denmark

d45a35b6-bbdb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Isafjordur, Iceland, used for magnetic field measurements as part of the IUGONET Observatory.
d45a35b6-bbdb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Conjugate Observation at Iceland

d45de0fa-bbc0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The X-band weather radar at the Kototabang Observatory in West Sumatra, Indonesia is a pulsed Doppler radar designed to measure the three-dimensional structure of rain fields over several tens of kilometers. It features a 1.2 m diameter antenna that rotates at 2 RPM and operates with a radio wave frequency of 9.74 GHz.
d45de0fa-bbc0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-band Radar at IUGONET Observatory, Indonesia

d4612f20-ba7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) - 2I Engineering Data Interface** is a component of the BARREL observatory that converts analog signals, such as temperatures, voltages, and currents, into digital data with 16-bit precision. It monitors various inputs to ensure the proper functioning of the balloon payload's engineering systems during flights.
d4612f20-ba7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

d461743c-bbdd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Precision Solar Photometric Telescope (PSPT) at Mauna Loa Solar Observatory is a ground-based instrument designed to measure and understand variability in the solar radiative output by producing high-precision, seeing-limited full-disk images in specific wavelength bands.
d461743c-bbdd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Precision Solar Photometric Telescope at Mauna Loa Solar Observatory

d4663fd0-b68d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ESO 3.6 m Telescope is an optical reflecting telescope operated by the European Southern Observatory at La Silla Observatory in Chile since 1977, with a clear aperture of approximately 3.6 meters (140 inches).
d4663fd0-b68d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 3.6m Telescope at La Silla Observatory, Chile

d46d2060-b909-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Suprathermal Energy Ionic Charge Analyzer (SULEICA) is an instrument aboard the AMPTE IRM satellite designed to measure the ionic charge state and mass composition of major ions, from hydrogen to iron, within suprathermal plasma energies ranging from approximately 5 to 270 keV/charge. It utilizes electrostatic deflection, time-of-flight measurement, and energy analysis in solid-state detectors to achieve this, scanning a field of view that covers 360° by 40° in the satellite's spin plane.
d46d2060-b909-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Suprathermal Energy Ionic Charge Analyzer on Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers Ion Release Module

d47cc534-bc91-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Scintillation Fiber Detector (SFD) on Equator-S is a scientific instrument that detects ionizing radiation by measuring the light emitted from scintillating materials when struck by particles, with energy discrimination capabilities for electrons and protons at different thresholds.
d47cc534-bc91-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scintillation Fiber Detector part of Equator-S

d4882d98-b6ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Fürstenfeldbruck Magnetic Observatory**: A ground-based facility located in Bavaria, Germany, dedicated to the observation and measurement of Earth's magnetic field.
d4882d98-b6ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fürstenfeldbruck Observatory, Germany

d48a7160-b7ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IGPP-LANL Boulder Fluxgate Magnetometer** is a magnetic field measuring instrument located at the IGPP-LANL Boulder station, part of the IGPP-LANL Magnetometer Array.
d48a7160-b7ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IGPP-LANL Boulder Observatory

d48a8d18-b8e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Nastro Verde Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Sorrento, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
d48a8d18-b8e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Osservatorio Astronomico Nastro Verde at Sorrento Observatory, Italy

d492cac2-b959-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter** (**Mio**) is a space probe within the BepiColombo mission that will study Mercury's magnetic field, magnetosphere, and exosphere using specialized instruments like plasma detectors and spectral imagers.
d492cac2-b959-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter part of BepiColombo

d4a255c8-bb25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS Solid State Telescope (SST) is an energetic particle instrument designed to measure the intensity of superthermal electrons and ions primarily in the energy range of 30-300 keV for ions and 30-100 keV for electrons. It utilizes two units with opposing sensors to cover a significant portion of the sky, reducing magnetic contamination through paired electron broom magnets and expanding its dynamic range with a mechanical attenuator.
d4a255c8-bb25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solid State Telescope part of THEMIS

d4aad3aa-bb99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at Göttingen (GTT) is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, particularly Earth's magnetic field. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network managed by the World Data Center for Geomagnetism in Kyoto.
d4aad3aa-bb99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Göttingen Observatory

d4bdd510-bbba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Darwin Airport Observatory is a ground-based facility in Darwin, Northern Territory, Australia (12.4S, 130.9E), operated by the Australian Bureau of Meteorology for climate data collection and notable for its role in the 2001 Darwin Area Wave Experiment (DAWEX).
d4bdd510-bbba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Darwin Airport Observatory, Australia

d4be44d6-b5f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA station in Dombas, used for measuring and recording magnetic fields.
d4be44d6-b5f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dombas Observatory

d4c63694-bb54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Space Environment Monitor (SEM) on NOAA 7 was an instrument designed to measure proton and electron flux density and energy spectrum in the upper atmosphere, consisting of detectors like MEPED, HEPAT, and TED for various energy ranges.
d4c63694-bb54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Environment Monitor on NOAA 7

d4c68fac-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU Radio Beacon Receiver (GRBR) Station at Kwajalein is an observatory located in the Marshall Islands, designed to measure ionospheric disturbances and study middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes.
d4c68fac-b7c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU radio beacon receiver at Kwajalein Observatory, Marshall Islands

d4cdf188-b61b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fort Simpson magnetometer, located in the South Slave Region of Northwest Territories, Canada, is a ground-based facility that was part of the CARISMA magnetometer array from 2006 to 1994.
d4cdf188-b61b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fort Simpson Station, Canada

d4ddc2d6-bb5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Manila FM-CW radar station, located in Marikina, Metro Manila, Philippines, is a ground facility that operates as part of the MAGDAS FM-CW radar network to monitor and study geomagnetic activities.
d4ddc2d6-bb5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: FM-CW Radar at MAGDAS Manila Station, Philippines

d4e44a64-b800-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to magnetometers located at the World Data Centre in Kyoto, specifically within the Pondicherry observatory. These instruments are part of an investigation associated with IAGA and have been operational since January 1, 1993.
d4e44a64-b800-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pondicherry Observatory

d4ec3656-b8f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lu-Kia-Pang Geomagnetic Observatory (LUK), located in Kunshan, Jiangsu Province, China, is a ground facility dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity. It features a magnetometer and contributes data to the World Data Center for Geomagnetism, Kyoto.
d4ec3656-b8f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lu-Kia-Pang Geomagnetic Observatory, China

d4ec4a10-b617-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Imager for Mars Pathfinder (IMP):** A stereo imaging system with color capabilities used on the Mars Pathfinder mission, derived from the descent imager/spectral radiometer (DISR) instrument aboard the Cassini Huygens probe.
d4ec4a10-b617-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Pathfinder Imager on Mars Pathfinder

d4ed89ce-b992-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Asteroid Multi-band Imaging Camera (AMICA) on the Hayabusa spacecraft is designed to capture scientific images and aid in optical navigation. It features a refracting telescope, a filter wheel with eight filters, and a 1024x1000 pixel CCD, providing a field-of-view of 5.7 x 5.7 degrees.
d4ed89ce-b992-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: The Asteroid Multi-band Imaging Camera on Hayabusa

d4f270ec-b85c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The China National Space Administration (CNSA) and the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) Space Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) is a gamma-ray telescope designed to monitor variable objects in space.
d4f270ec-b85c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma-Ray China National Space Administration and the Chinese Academy of Sciences Space Variable Objects Monitor X-ray Telescope

d4fa9898-b632-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
ST5-155 is a microsatellite from NASA's Space Technology 5 mission, launched in 2006 to test innovative technologies and study Earth's auroral currents and crustal magnetic field.
d4fa9898-b632-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Miniature Magnetometer on ST5-155 part of Space Technology 5 mission

d5014e58-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Virginio Cesarini Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Frasso Sabino, Italy. It is situated at an altitude of 465 meters and focuses on ground-based observations.
d5014e58-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Virginio Cesarini Observatory, Italy

d5094612-b99e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Texas, Austin 2.7m Harlan J. Smith Telescope is an optical telescope located at the McDonald Observatory in North America. It has an aperture of 2.7 meters and is used for astronomical research by the University of Texas, Austin.
d5094612-b99e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Harlan J. Smith 2.7m Optical Telescope at McDonald Observatory

d514a86e-b939-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GEOS Ground Mobile Station was a movable research facility operational from 1977 to 1982, designed for ground-based measurements of ultra low frequency magnetic fields and other geophysical data to support satellite and rocket experiments.
d514a86e-b939-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: DC/AC Photometer and Fluxgate Magnetometer at GEOS Ground Mobile Station

d514a902-bb93-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTIs) All-Sky Imager at Tromsø, Sweden, is a multi-wavelength instrument designed to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere through nocturnal airglow emissions. Developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research at Nagoya University, it operates as part of the IUGONET observatory network to monitor atmospheric phenomena.
d514a902-bb93-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: All-Sky Imager at Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers Observatory

d516da14-b95f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The specific magnetometer referred to here has been operational since January 1957 and is located in Lhasa as part of the IAGA investigation at the Kyoto World Data Centre (WDC) observatory.
d516da14-b95f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kyoto World Data Center Observatory

d52ee230-bbd0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Northwood Ridge Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Northwood, New Hampshire, USA (MPC ID: 225).
d52ee230-bbd0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Northwood Ridge Observatory, United States

d535a8c8-b841-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plasma Electron and Current Experiment (PEACE) on Double Star 2 is an instrument designed to measure the number of low/medium energy electrons at various energy levels and directions. It aims to understand the electron population in plasma environments, with A. Fazakerley from MSSL, Dorking, UK serving as the Principal Investigator.
d535a8c8-b841-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Electron and Current Experiment on Double Star 2

d53d12b8-bb0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer onboard the DMSP/F18 satellite that measures geomagnetic fluctuations associated with geophysical phenomena.
d53d12b8-bb0a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

d541605c-bb8c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Observatory of Saint-Veran is a high-altitude astronomical observatory in France, located at 2,930 meters on the Pic de Château Renard in the municipality of Saint-Véran. It is managed by AstroQueyras and is one of the highest observatories in Europe.
d541605c-bb8c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Saint-Véran Observatory, France

d559a0c4-b801-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is the **Ionospheric Station at Trivandrum, India**, a ground-based observatory with the URSI code TM308. It uses an advanced Digisonde to analyze ionospheric reflections, located at Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.
d559a0c4-b801-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Ionospheric Station, India

d56910ea-bb3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ion Drift Meter (IDM) on Dynamics Explorer 2 was an instrument designed to measure the bulk motions of ionospheric plasma perpendicular to the satellite's velocity vector, providing insights into ion convection patterns and plasma flow in the Earth’s ionosphere.
d56910ea-bb3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Drift Meter part of Dynamics Explorer 2

d56e6cf6-bbf4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **Magnetometer** is a scientific instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The specified NIPR-LPM Magnetometer at H57 in Antarctica is part of the Automated Magnetometer Network Observatory, known for its low power consumption and near-real-time data transmission via satellite.
d56e6cf6-bbf4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Automated Magnetometer Network Observation, Antarctica

d571da7e-b732-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Danmarkshavn (DMH) Geophysical Observatory, located in Greenland, North America, is a ground-based facility that started operations on January 1, 2007. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network and includes instruments such as a magnetometer for geophysical measurements.
d571da7e-b732-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Danmarkshavn Geophysical Observatory, Greenland

d57abffc-bc93-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Galaxy Tibet YBJ Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Yangbajing, Damxung County, Lhasa, Tibet, China. It is situated at a latitude of 30.103182 and longitude of 90.52614 on the Asian continent.
d57abffc-bc93-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Galaxy Tibet YBJ Observatory, China

d580fd44-ba2d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Etaiyapuram geophysical observatory is a ground-based facility located in Ottapidaram, Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, India, primarily known for its magnetometer instruments and was operational from January 1996 to December 2002.
d580fd44-ba2d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Etaiyapuram Observatory, India

d5816d4c-b820-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The O'Gyalia Magnetometer is an instrument used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field at the IAGA station in O'Gyalia. It was operational from January 1, 1906, to December 31, 1912.
d5816d4c-b820-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at O'Gyalla Observatory

d5816ee4-b9cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The La Serena Geomagnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility located in La Serena, Coquimbo Region, Chile, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity since May 2003. It features a magnetometer and is part of the larger SAMBA observatory network.
d5816ee4-b9cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at La Serena Observatory, Chile

d5842838-bb7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The specific set of magnetometers at Kamennyj Mys (KAM) are part of the IUGONET observatory and provide valuable data on geomagnetic activity in that region.
d5842838-bb7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at WDC Kyoto Observatory

d587f1b8-b83d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The specific instance described here refers to the magnetometers operated at the Darwin observatory from January 1, 1957, to December 31, 1959, as part of the IAGA investigation.
d587f1b8-b83d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kyoto World Data Center Observatory

d58f49e6-b79c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer used for upper atmosphere physics monitoring at Syowa Station in Antarctica.
d58f49e6-b79c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Upper Atmosphere Physics Monitoring Observation at Syowa Station, Antarctica

d5973d58-b7b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mass Spectrometer Telescope (MAST)** on SAMPEX was an energetic particle instrument designed to measure the isotopic composition and energy spectra of cosmic rays with high precision. It featured an array of 11 detectors, combining position-sensitive layers and solid-state detectors, to determine the trajectories and energies of penetrating nuclei in the range of 10 MeV/nucleon to several hundred MeV/nucleon for elements with atomic numbers between 3 and 28.
d5973d58-b7b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer Telescope part of Solar Anomalous and Magnetospheric Particle Explorer

d599b308-bacc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Transition Region and Coronal Explorer (TRACE) was a space mission designed to observe the Sun in ultraviolet wavelengths, providing detailed images of the solar atmosphere.
d599b308-bacc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet NASA Transition Region and Coronal Explorer Solar Satellite Mission

d5bec370-bbec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Rock Finder Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Calgary, Alberta, Canada. It serves as a ground-based facility for celestial observations and research.
d5bec370-bbec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Calgary Observatory, Canada

d5c0fb16-b73e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The "Electron Losses and Fields Investigation (ELFIN) B, Ephemeris Instrument" is a virtual instrument launched on September 17, 2018, as part of the ELFIN mission, designed to provide ephemeris data for studying electron losses and magnetic fields in space.
d5c0fb16-b73e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris Instrument part of Electron Losses and Fields Investigation

d5c1ffe4-b5ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sunflower Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Olathe, Kansas, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
d5c1ffe4-b5ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sunflower Observatory, United States

d5c47f96-b6d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Danish Telescope Observatory is an astronomical facility located at the La Silla Observatory in Chile. It is situated on Earth and classified as a ground-based observatory.
d5c47f96-b6d2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.54m Danish Telescope at La Silla Observatory, Chile

d5cbf87e-b156-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Narrow Field Imager (NFI) is a compact externally occulted coronagraph designed to observe the Sun's corona from 6 to 32 solar radii. It is part of NASA's PUNCH mission and features a polarizing filter wheel and CCD camera assembly for detailed imaging and polarization resolution.
d5cbf87e-b156-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Coronagraph on PUNCH-NFI spacecraft

d5d5cc96-b72d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **1.5m Telescope at Observatorio Astronomico Nacional-Ensenada** is a Ritchey-Chretien reflector telescope with a 1.5-meter aperture, located in the Sierra de San Pedro Mártir, Baja California, Mexico, and operated by the Instituto de Astronomía at Ensenada since its installation in 1970.
d5d5cc96-b72d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.5m Telescope at National Astronomical Observatory-Ensenada, Mexico

d5df274a-b18e-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Zi-Ka-Wei Geomagnetic Observatory (ZKW), located in Shanghai, China, is a ground facility that conducted geomagnetic observations from 1875 to 1907.
d5df274a-b18e-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Zi-Ka-Wei Geomagnetic Observatory, China

d5e2f128-bbfb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Antibes Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Antibes, France. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
d5e2f128-bbfb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antibes Observatory, France

d5e87442-b7df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The PUNCH-WFI 1 is a space telescope, part of NASA's Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) mission, designed to image and track solar wind and coronal mass ejections using a wide field imager.
d5e87442-b7df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide Field Imager on PUNCH-WFI 1 part of Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere

d5f1f5de-b8a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 210MM Learmonth Station is a ground-based observatory located in Western Australia, part of the ISEE 210 Magnetic Meridian magnetometer network, which monitors magnetic field variations.
d5f1f5de-b8a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Learmonth Observatory, Australia

d5f3189a-b5b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High-Energy Electron Detector (HEED) on Double Star 2 is an instrument designed to measure high-energy electrons in space, with W. Zhang and J. B. Cao from CSSAR, China serving as Principal Investigators.
d5f3189a-b5b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High-Energy Electron Detector part of Double Star 2

d6029b3c-baa1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC) Two-meter Twin Telescope facility is located at the Teide Observatory in Africa and operates within the optical waveband.
d6029b3c-baa1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Two-meter Twin Telescope Facility at Teide Observatory

d602babe-b794-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing of the Electron density by Relaxation) instrument on Cluster-2 is designed to measure electron density via active sounding of plasma resonances and record natural wave emissions in the high-frequency range from 4--80 KHz. It is part of the Wave Experiment Consortium (WEC) and uses a double-sphere antenna for its measurements.
d602babe-b794-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing of the Electron density by Relaxation part of Cluster-2

d607ad04-bbad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **FedSat Magnetometer** is a scientific instrument aboard the Australian satellite FedSat, launched in 2002. It was developed by the University of Newcastle to measure Earth's magnetic field near its poles and is part of Australia’s "Federation Satellite" mission.
d607ad04-bbad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: FedSat Magnetometer on Federation Satellite

d616737e-b645-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Moonbase South Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at the Hakos Astrofarm near Gamsberg Pass in Namibia. It operates as a ground-based facility with an altitude of 1830 meters.
d616737e-b645-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Moonbase South Observatory, Namibia

d61a30ca-bbce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The White-light All-sky Watec Imager (AWI) at Kilpisjarvi, Finland is an automated optical instrument featuring a CCD camera and fisheye lens used for all-sky imaging.
d61a30ca-bbce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager part of Multiple Imager Network Observations in Northern Europe

d62b8ad4-ba55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Jupiter Energetic-Particle Detector Instrument (JEDI) is a scientific instrument designed to measure the energetic plasma in space, specifically focusing on high-energy magnetospheric ions and electrons. It operates by measuring particle energy and velocity to determine their composition, including species like electrons, hydrogen, helium, oxygen, and sulfur.
d62b8ad4-ba55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Detector on Juno Spacecraft

d6301306-b5dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Frederick C. Gillett Gemini North telescope is an 8.1-meter diameter optical/infrared telescope located on Mauna Kea, Hawaii, known for its exceptional observing conditions and being part of the international Gemini Observatory.
d6301306-b5dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 8.1m Frederick C. Gillett Gemini North Telescope at Mauna Kea Observatory, United States

d641c134-b760-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) 2M Data Processing Unit** is a versatile instrument controller designed to collect data from various sensors on balloon flights, including X-ray spectrometers and magnetometers, and transmit it via an Iridium modem. It utilizes an FPGA for flexible interface logic and has been successfully deployed in numerous high-altitude missions.
d641c134-b760-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Space Weather Test (RBSP) Relativistic Electron Losses

d64d29a8-b638-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Stone Finder Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Calgary, Alberta, Canada. It operates as a ground-based facility and is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 647.
d64d29a8-b638-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stone Finder Observatory, Canada

d65cbdb4-bbc4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Sveagruva is a ground-based observatory located in Sveagruva, Svalbard, Norway. It is part of the IAGA network and has been operational since 1933, specializing in magnetometer measurements on Earth's surface.
d65cbdb4-bbc4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sveagruva Observatory, Norway

d65d05cc-b71d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Quadrispherical Plasma Analyzer on Pioneer 10 was an instrument consisting of dual electrostatic analyzers designed to measure plasma distribution parameters, specifically the energy range of protons and electrons in space.
d65d05cc-b71d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Quadrispherical Plasma Analyzer on Pioneer 10

d665d1ae-b6f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Fluxgate Magnetometer (FGM) on Cluster 2/FM5 (Rumba) is an instrument consisting of two tri-axial fluxgate magnetometers mounted on a radial boom, designed to measure magnetic fields in space with high sensitivity and resolution. It includes a data processing unit and has multiple operating modes for capturing detailed magnetic field data during significant events.
d665d1ae-b6f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer on Cluster 2

d667783a-b926-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The TRAC magnetometer on the Aureol 3 satellite is a three-axis fluxgate magnetometer used for attitude determination and measuring Earth's magnetic field. It operates with a drive frequency of ~7 kHz and has a resolution enhanced to ±5 nT through specialized electronics, despite an initial digitization limit of 8 bits.
d667783a-b926-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of Aureol 3

d66b69e6-b970-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Maisoncelles Observatory** (code: C10) is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Martin-du-Boschet, France. It is a ground-based facility primarily used for astronomical observations and research.
d66b69e6-b970-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Maisoncelles Observatory, France

d67e3b26-b5c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: La Senda Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Cabanillas del Campo, Guadalajara, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
d67e3b26-b5c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: La Senda Observatory, Spain

d69ecb36-b8eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover is a NASA mission that landed in Jezero Crater on February 18, 2021, to search for signs of ancient habitable conditions and past microbial life on Mars. It collects samples using a drill for future return to Earth.
d69ecb36-b8eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Perseverance part of Mars 2020 Mission

d69f75b0-ba83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Kramatorsk Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Mykolaivka urban hromada, Kramatorsk, Ukraine. Established in 2009, it operates as a ground-based facility with an altitude of 76 meters above sea level.
d69f75b0-ba83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Kramatorsk Observatory, Ukraine

d69fbf30-b8de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) onboard the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) is an instrument designed to study solar variability by examining the Sun's interior and magnetic activity. It provides continuous full-disk coverage with high spatial resolution, observing in the Fe I absorption line at 6173Å, and produces both Dopplergrams and vector magnetograms.
d69fbf30-b8de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on Solar Dynamics Observatory

d6b085c2-b9dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The La Ronge (LRG) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Unorganized Division No. 18, Saskatchewan, Canada, specializing in geophysical measurements and equipped with instruments such as magnetometers. It began operations on January 01, 2007.
d6b085c2-b9dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at La Ronge Geophysical Observatory, Canada

d6c265f0-b8c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Tarbatness Observatory (I81) is an astronomical observatory located in Portmahomack, Scotland, dedicated to ground-based observations.
d6c265f0-b8c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tarbatness Observatory, United Kingdom

d6ce0e9e-b703-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Stia Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Stia, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations. It operates under the Planetario del Parco Nazionale delle Foreste Casentinesi and is situated at coordinates 43.8011° N, 11.7105° E.
d6ce0e9e-b703-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stia Observatory, Italy

d6d92e58-baca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Starphysics Observatory 0.35m Telescope is an optical telescope located in North America with a 0.35-meter aperture, used for astronomical observations and research.
d6d92e58-baca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.35m Telescope at The Starphysics Observatory

d6dac146-b10b-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Comet Nucleus Infrared and Visual Analyser (CIVA) is an instrument suite on the Rosetta Philae Lander designed to capture panoramic images and perform detailed surface and subsurface analysis of comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko using cameras and a hyperspectral imager.
d6dac146-b10b-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Comet Nucleus Infrared and Visual Analyser on Rosetta Philae Lander

d6dc1ee8-babf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The BARREL Balloon 4D was part of NASA's BARREL mission, which used high-altitude balloons to study electron losses from Earth's radiation belts by measuring X-rays produced by precipitating electrons in the stratosphere.
d6dc1ee8-babf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star Mission of Opportunity

d6de309c-b949-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP/F17 Special Sensor Magnetometer (SSM) is a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer deployed as part of the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program. It measures geomagnetic fluctuations associated with various geophysical phenomena and has been operational since November 4, 2006.
d6de309c-b949-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

d6e2bd1e-bb2f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Gemini South Observatory is an astronomical observatory located on Cerro Pachón in Chile, serving as the southern hemisphere facility of the Gemini Observatory.
