dcb92358-b734-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Learmonth observatory, operational since 1987, used to measure magnetic fields and part of the IUGONET-Observatory network managed by WDC Kyoto.
dcb92358-b734-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Learmonth Observatory

dccdc260-b813-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **RDSS Observatory:** An astronomical observatory located in Kovalevka, Russia, known for ground-based observations. It operates under the MPC ID L77 and is situated at coordinates 39.82025 longitude and 47.336868 latitude.
dccdc260-b813-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kovalevka Observatory, Russia

dccff4ae-b999-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Loiano Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Loiano, Italy, featuring the 1.52m Gian Domenico Cassini Telescope and operated by the Bologna Astronomical Observatory.
dccff4ae-b999-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gian Domenico Cassini Telescope at Loiano Observatory, Italy

dcd444f6-bb28-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 4B was part of the Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) mission, which studied particles escaping Earth's radiation belts using high-altitude balloons equipped with scientific instruments. This specific balloon operated from August 16 to August 17, 2016, in the stratosphere near Earth's surface.
dcd444f6-bb28-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses Balloon 4B part of Living with a Star Geospace Mission of Opportunity

dcd76f7a-b5b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Imaging Riometer Observation at Kapuskasing is a 60MHz riometer located in Kapuskasing, Canada. It features an 8x8-element dipole antenna array capable of producing independent beams covering approximately 180km x 180km at the D region altitude and was developed to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions.
dcd76f7a-b5b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 60MHz Riometer part of Imaging Riometer Observation at Kapuskasing

dcdc3f02-b62e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Parker Solar Probe ISOIS Investigation (EPI-Hi)** is an experiment on the Parker Solar Probe mission that uses solid-state detectors to study energetic particles in the inner heliosphere, focusing on their origin, acceleration, and transport mechanisms. It comprises three detector stacks: one High Energy Telescope (HET) and two Low-Energy Telescopes (LET1 and LET2).
dcdc3f02-b62e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Integrated Science Investigation of the Sun part of Parker Solar Probe

dce3b232-bbab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Broad Band X-Ray Telescope (BBXRT) was an instrument on the ASTRO-1 space shuttle mission designed to observe and study celestial objects in the x-ray waveband.
dce3b232-bbab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: x-ray Broad Band X-Ray Telescope on ASTRO-1

dced5114-b8ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Unified Radio and Plasma Wave (URAP) experiment on the Ulysses spacecraft is designed to study radio and plasma phenomena in the heliosphere and Jovian magnetosphere, using a sophisticated array of sensors to track solar radio bursts and investigate local wave phenomena.
dced5114-b8ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Unified Radio and Plasma Wave Experiment for ULY on Ulysses Spacecraft

dcf3a390-bb83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Madras Geomagnetic Observatory (MDS), located in Chennai, India, was a ground-based facility operating from 1851 to 1855 for monitoring geomagnetic activity.
dcf3a390-bb83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Madras Geomagnetic Observatory

dd000210-bb66-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ORFEUS (Orbiting and Retrievable Far and Extreme Ultraviolet Spectrometer) missions were a collaboration between NASA and the German Space Agency (DARA), involving satellite-based telescopes designed to observe far and extreme ultraviolet radiation from astronomical objects.
dd000210-bb66-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ultraviolet NASA German Space Agency DARA Orbiting and Retrievable Far and Extreme Ultraviolet Spectrometer part of ORFEUS Mission

dd076620-b9c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Max Planck Institute for Astronomy and Institute of Astrophysics of Andalusia (CSIC) 0.8m Schmidt Telescope is located at the Calar Alto Observatory in Europe, operating within the optical waveband with an aperture of 0.8 meters.
dd076620-b9c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 0.8m Schmidt Telescope at Calar Alto Observatory

dd095034-b825-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Serpong Observatory is a ground-based facility located in the southwest suburbs of Jakarta, Indonesia, primarily focused on studying the equatorial atmosphere using instruments such as boundary layer radar and meteor wind radar.
dd095034-b825-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Boundary Layer Radar at Serpong Observatory, Indonesia

dd12384e-b806-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Pak Chong Observatory in Nakhon Ratchasima is a ground-based observatory located in Sima Mongkhon, Pak Chong District, Thailand. It is situated at coordinates 14.66931° N, 101.40403° E and serves as an astronomical facility for observation and research purposes.
dd12384e-b806-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Nachon Ratchasima Observatory, Thailand

dd1b693a-b781-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Yevpatoria RT-70 radio telescope, also known as the Evpatoria Planetary Radar (EPR), is a large radio telescope and planetary radar located in Crimea, used for deep space communications and scientific research.
dd1b693a-b781-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio Yevpatoria RT-70 radio telescope at Center for Deep Space Communications

dd2301e2-baef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity described is the "Masia Cal Maciarol Modul 2," an astronomical observatory located in Àger, Noguera, Lleida, Catalonia, Spain. It operates as a ground-based observatory with the MPC code A01 and is situated at coordinates 42.0179°N, 0.7441°E.
dd2301e2-baef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Masia Cal Maciarol Modul 2, Spain

dd233296-bb69-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The Ekaterinburg Magnetometer, operational since January 1887, is part of the Ekaterinburg geophysical observatory and contributes to the World Data Center for Geomagnetism (WDC_GDMC).
dd233296-bb69-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ekaterinburg Observatory

dd23f0c8-b6e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Bellino Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Chiazale, Cuneo, Piedmont, Italy. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code K31 and serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
dd23f0c8-b6e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Astronomico di Bellino, Italy

dd31d6b6-b759-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NRAO) Green Bank Interferometer, located in North America, is a telescope facility designed for millimeter waveband observations.
dd31d6b6-b759-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter National Radio Astronomy Observatory Green Bank Interferometer

dd4230bc-b90f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Entity Definition:**
The Comet Nucleus Tour (CONTOUR) was a NASA spacecraft mission designed to encounter and study multiple comets. The spacecraft featured a simple design with minimal moving parts, including the CRISP imaging instrument, CFI wide-angle camera, NGIMS mass spectrometer, and CIDA dust analyzer, all aimed at gathering high-resolution data during close approaches.
dd4230bc-b90f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Comet Nucleus Tour

dd493f20-b828-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Averroes Geomagnetic Observatory (AVE), located in Morocco, is a ground-based facility operating since 1967 that monitors Earth's magnetic field.
dd493f20-b828-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Averroes Geomagnetic Observatory, Morocco

dd4be35c-b66a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2C Optical Photometer is an instrument designed to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm, specifically during relativistic electron precipitation events, to determine the presence of protons and support the study of electromagnetic ion cyclotron waves as a precipitation mechanism.
dd4be35c-b66a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

dd52e778-bada-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CLPS Task Order 19D Lunar Magnetotelluric Sounder (LMS) is a specialized instrument designed to conduct magnetic and electrical field measurements on the lunar surface, aimed at understanding the Moon's internal structure and subsurface properties.
dd52e778-bada-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer Observing Lunar Operation on CLPS Task Order 19D Lunar Magnetotelluric Sounder

dd570b4e-b70d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Purcell Geophysical Observatory (PCEL) is a ground-based facility located in Purcell, Oklahoma, dedicated to geophysical research and equipped with instruments such as magnetometers. It began operations on January 1, 2007.
dd570b4e-b70d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Purcell Geophysical Observatory, United States

dd59a98a-b8ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1C Ephemeris** is a virtual instrument that provides trajectory positions for the BARREL balloons in various coordinate systems, supporting investigations into relativistic electron losses.
dd59a98a-b8ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses Ephemeris on Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

dd69879a-b719-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS-B Solid State Telescope (SST) is an energetic particle instrument onboard the THEMIS spacecraft, designed to measure the intensity of superthermal electrons and ions, primarily within energy ranges of 30-100 keV for electrons and 30-300 keV for ions.
dd69879a-b719-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solid State Telescope part of THEMIS

dd744d92-b994-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Takapuna Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in the Auckland Region of New Zealand, known for its ground-based observations.
dd744d92-b994-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Takapuna Observatory, New Zealand

dd7d5114-ba32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Magnetometers at Aberystwyth (AWY)" is a ground-based magnetometer located at the station with the IAGA identifier AWY, part of the global network of geomagnetic observatories.
dd7d5114-ba32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

dd7fd6e2-b621-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar X-Ray/Cosmic Gamma-Ray Burst (GRB) Instrument for the Ulysses mission is an advanced astrophysical observation tool designed to monitor solar flare X-ray emissions, localize cosmic gamma-ray bursts, and detect Jovian auroral X-radiation. It features a dual-detector configuration and radiation-hardened microprocessor to overcome operational challenges such as exposure to Jovian radiation belts.
dd7fd6e2-b621-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar X-Ray/Cosmic Gamma-Ray Burst Instrument on Ulysses

dd847ac8-bb79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer (MEDA) is an instrument onboard the Mars 2020 Rover designed to measure meteorological and environmental conditions at the rover site, including dust properties, wind patterns, temperature, humidity, pressure, and radiation.
dd847ac8-bb79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer on Mars 2020 Rover

dd8a494a-ba29-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **College Geomagnetic Observatory (CMO)** is a ground-based facility in Fairbanks, Alaska, USA, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements. Operating since 2007, it is part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy's observatory network.
dd8a494a-ba29-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at College Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

dd909bf8-b9be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Madras Observatory was an astronomical observatory established in 1786 by William Petrie and later managed by the British East India Company in Chennai (formerly Madras), primarily to assist navigation and mapping through latitude recording and time standards, while also conducting observations on stars and geomagnetism until its closure in 1931.
dd909bf8-b9be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Madras Observatory, India

dd999438-b897-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Wiesbaden Observatory is a ground-based public observatory located in Wiesbaden, Germany. It was established in 1925 and is situated at an altitude of 190 meters.
dd999438-b897-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Martin-Niemöller-Schule Observatory, Germany

dda6674c-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Jovian Energetic Electrons (JoEE)** instrument is an electron particle spectrometer designed to study the behavior of charged particles within Jupiter's magnetosphere and its interaction with the planet's icy moons. It is part of the Particle Environment Package (PEP) onboard the European Space Agency’s JUICE mission, utilizing advanced technology like 3D-printed collimators to map acceleration processes in the Jovian system.
dda6674c-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Jovian Energetic Electrons part of PEP on Juice

ddaaaa52-b9b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mark Slade Remote Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Wilderness, Virginia, USA. It operates as a ground-based facility and has the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID W54.
ddaaaa52-b9b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wilderness Observatory, United States

ddabecf8-bad3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Skibotn Astrophysical Observatory (MPC ID: 093) is an astronomical observatory located in Nordlysveien, Storfjord, Troms, Norway. It is a ground-based facility situated at latitude 69.3483 and longitude 20.3647 on the continent of Europe.
ddabecf8-bad3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astrophysical Observatory at Skibotn, Norway

ddb0bc98-b81b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Chinese Academy of Science 25m Radio Telescope at Shanghai Astronomical Observatory (SHAO), Sheshan Station is a radio telescope located in Asia with an aperture of 25 meters, used for astronomical observations.
ddb0bc98-b81b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 25.0m Chinese Academy of Science Radio Telescope at Shanghai Astronomical Observatory, China

ddb75a0a-bba7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astronomical Observatory of Kyiv Shevchenko National University, located in Lisniki, Ukraine, is a ground-based astronomical observatory established in 1957.
ddb75a0a-bba7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory of Kyiv Shevchenko National University

ddb783fe-b611-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Digisonde ionospheric station at Cachimbo, Brazil (CXM9B)** is an advanced facility that measures various properties of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere, including angle of arrival, polarization, and Doppler frequency shift, to study the ionosphere. It operated from September 2002 until December 2002.
ddb783fe-b611-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde Ionospheric Station at Cachimbo Observatory, Brazil

ddb78cb8-b9c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: SOFI (Son of Isaac) is an infrared spectrograph and imaging camera mounted on the New Technology Telescope (NTT) at La Silla Observatory, equipped with a Hawaii HgCdTe 1024x1024 array sensitive to light within the 0.9-2.5 micron range, offering various observing modes including imaging, spectroscopy, polarimetry, and high time-resolution imaging.
ddb78cb8-b9c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared SOFI on New Technology Telescope at La Silla Observatory

ddbc640e-ba5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Grange Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bussoleno, Italy. It is a ground-based facility situated at Via Massimo D'Azeglio, 10053, with coordinates approximately 45.14217° N and 7.14074° E.
ddbc640e-ba5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bussoleno Observatory, Italy

ddc3d76e-bbe1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The GNU radio beacon receiver (GRBR) station at Watukosek is an observatory located in Indonesia that measures ionospheric disturbances related to middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes. It is part of the GRBR network and situated near the equator, specifically at Jalan Raya Watukosek, Pasuruan, East Java.
ddc3d76e-bbe1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU Radio Beacon Receiver Station at Watukosek, Indonesia

ddc72262-b76c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Astronomía Sigma Octante is a ground-based observatory located in Cochabamba, Bolivia. It serves as an astronomical facility for observations and research within South America.
ddc72262-b76c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomia Sigma Octante Observatory, Bolivia

ddd05968-b960-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **United States Naval Observatory Flagstaff Station (NOFS)** is an astronomical observatory located near Flagstaff, Arizona. It serves as a national dark-sky observing facility under the United States Naval Observatory and manages the Celestial Reference Frame for the U.S. Secretary of Defense.
ddd05968-b960-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Flagstaff Observatory, United States

ddd73188-bb78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The **Leeside Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Elgin, Ontario, Canada. It operates as a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center code W61.
ddd73188-bb78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Leeside Observatory, Canada

ddde773a-baac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1D X-ray Instrument (XRI) is a scintillation detector designed to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It operates with an energy response from 10 keV to 10 MeV and includes various data binning modes to balance between time and energy resolution.
ddde773a-baac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-Ray Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

dde8e3b6-b5ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ) 0.65m Telescope at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory (OAO) is an optical telescope located in Asia, specifically designed for solar observations.
dde8e3b6-b5ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 0.65m National Astronomical Observatory of Japan Telescope at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory, Japan

ddee9928-b9e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fort McMurray magnetometer is a ground-based observatory located in Tyukhtetsky Rayon, Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia, and it is part of the CARISMA magnetometer array. It operates at coordinates 56.657° N latitude and 248.790° E longitude.
ddee9928-b9e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fort McMurray Observatory, Russia

ddfb5bf0-bb3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Torino Photopolarimeter** is an instrument designed for simultaneous polarimetric measurements in UBVRI colors, utilizing dichroic filters and photomultipliers to measure each color concurrently, along with a half-wave plate and calcite block to determine the degree of linear polarization and position angle.
ddfb5bf0-bb3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: infrared Torino Photopolarimeter

ddfeac66-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Molodezhnaya Geomagnetic Observatory (MOL) was a ground-based facility in Antarctica that operated from 1965 to 2002, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
ddfeac66-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Molodezhnaya, Antarctica

ddffd41a-ba2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Dawn Positions** is a virtual instrument that provides ephemeris data for the Dawn spacecraft, detailing its positions over time.
ddffd41a-ba2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris part of Dawn

ddffea82-b601-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Campo Imperatore Astronomical Observatory**, also known as **Pulkovo Station Observatory**, is an astronomical observatory located at the Alpine Botanical Garden of Campo Imperatore in L'Aquila, Abruzzo, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
ddffea82-b601-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Campo Imperatore Astronomical Observatory, Italy

de125ec6-bbb8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Niue Ionosonde is a ground-based instrument located in Niue Island, equipped with an IPS 5D digital ionosonde that conducts vertical sounding of the ionosphere by sweeping frequencies from about 1.0 to 21.5 MHz.
de125ec6-bbb8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar Ionosonde part of Niue Observatory

de32b818-b5c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Two-Meter Twin Telescope (TTT2)** is a ground-based astronomical observatory located at TF-514 in Güímar, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, on the Canary Islands of Spain. It's situated at coordinates 28.29873° N latitude and 343.49053° E longitude.
de32b818-b5c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2m Twin Telescope at Teide Observatory, Spain

de3ebebc-ba41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Fast Plasma Investigation (FPI)** on MMS2 is an instrument suite comprising four dual electron spectrometers and four dual ion spectrometers. It measures the velocity-space distribution of electrons and ions from 10 eV to 30 keV with high time resolution.
de3ebebc-ba41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Fast Plasma Investigation on MMS

de48ae82-bac7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The THEMIS On Board Moments (MOM) system is an instrument used for calculating electron and ion moments from ESA and SST data aboard the THEMIS spacecraft, providing key plasma parameters such as number density, energy flux, velocity, pressure, and temperature in various coordinate systems.
de48ae82-bac7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: On Board Moments part of Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms

de4c4e9c-ba00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetometer at the Addis Ababa ground station is an instrument used to measure and monitor the magnetic field in the region. It has been operational since January 1958 and is part of the IUGONET Observatory network, specifically under the WDC Kyoto-WDC AAE.
de4c4e9c-ba00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Addis Ababa Observatory

de4df082-ba03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **ISEE1 Ephemeris** refers to the positional data of the ISEE1 spacecraft recorded in various coordinate systems. This dataset is part of the CDPP-AMDA observatory managed by CNES and provides essential information for understanding the spacecraft's trajectory and location over time.
de4df082-ba03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ISEE1 Ephemeris on International Sun Earth Explorer 1

de51a450-b974-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Magnetometers at Leirvogur (LRV)** are instruments used for measuring magnetic field variations and have been operational since January 1, 1957, as part of the IUGONET observatory network associated with WDC Kyoto.
de51a450-b974-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Leirvogur Observatory

de554d74-bb47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer** is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Nairobi, Kenya, used to measure magnetic fields as part of the MAGDAS observation network.
de554d74-bb47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System observation network

de598128-b778-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Los Milanos Observatory is an astronomical facility located in the Urbanización El Portanchito, Cáceres, Spain. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and observations.
de598128-b778-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Los Milanos Observatory, Spain

de5cc678-bb86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Perth Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bickley, Western Australia, originally founded in West Perth in 1896 and later relocated to its current site due to urban expansion.
de5cc678-bb86-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bickley Observatory, Australia

de610d72-b7ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sierra Remote Observatory** (MPC code: G80) is an astronomical observatory located in Auberry, California. It operates as a ground-based facility and is situated at Sierra Remote Observatories on Bald Mountain Road.
de610d72-b7ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sierra Remote Observatory

de63848c-b5d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IGPP-LANL Rapid City Magnetometer is a ground-based facility located in Rapid City, South Dakota, USA, that measures and monitors the Earth's magnetic field.
de63848c-b5d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Rapid City Observatory, United States

de64e752-b89a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The North Mesa Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Los Alamos, New Mexico. It functions as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
de64e752-b89a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Los Alamos Observatory, United States

de68ac0a-b9f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: She-Shan Geomagnetic Observatory (SSH), located in Shanghai, China, is a ground-based facility that has been operating since 1930 to monitor geomagnetic activity on Earth's surface.
de68ac0a-b9f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at She-Shan Geomagnetic Observatory, China

de794a3e-bb11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IUCAA 2m Telescope is a optical telescope with an aperture of 2.0 meters located at the Girawali Observatory in Asia, operated by the Inter University Center for Astronomy and Astrophysics (IUCAA) in Pune, India.
de794a3e-bb11-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 2.0m Telescope at Girawali Observatory

de7b8186-b6a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Tarzana Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in the Tarzana neighborhood of Los Angeles, California. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
de7b8186-b6a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tarzana Observatory, United States

de7f6ed8-b60b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2B Data Processing Unit (DPU) is an instrument controller board used in the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) project to acquire and process data from various sensors, including an X-ray spectrometer and a magnetometer. It ensures data transmission via an Iridium modem and manages command operations through flexible FPGA technology.
de7f6ed8-b60b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

de7ffdce-b649-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Equatorial Magnetometer Network (EMN) fluxgate magnetometer at MED is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Medea, Algeria, used for measuring magnetic field variations.
de7ffdce-b649-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of The Equatorial Magnetometer Network

de92645e-bb9a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Fukuchiyama and Kannabe Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Fukuchiyama, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations.
de92645e-bb9a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fukuchiyama and Kannabe Observatory, Japan

dea27c3a-b78b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **RaSo Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Chemnitz, Germany. It functions as a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial phenomena.
dea27c3a-b78b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chemnitz Observatory, Germany

dea64040-b9cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CLPS Task Order 19D SCALPSS West Long Focal Length Camera (LFL1) is an imaging device with a 50mm lens designed to capture video during lunar descent and landing, specifically for reconstructing the effects of plume-surface interaction using stereo photogrammetry.
dea64040-b9cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stereo CAmeras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies (SCALPSS) West Long Focal Length Camera, 50mm lens on CLPS Task Order 19D spacecraft

deb9ad3a-b7a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Echo Station (DSS-12) is a historic radio telescope located at the Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex in California, originally built with a 26-meter aperture and later upgraded to 34 meters. It has played a crucial role in supporting various NASA missions since its construction in 1959.
deb9ad3a-b7a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 26-m Echo Station on Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex, United States

dec84c04-b7f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RISH All Sky Camera at Shigaraki is an instrument located at the MU Observatory in Shiga Prefecture, Japan, that captures continuous color images of the entire sky with a one-minute interval.
dec84c04-b7f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible All-Sky Camera at Shigaraki Observatory, Japan

decc4586-b729-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BSCR Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Santa Maria a Monte, Pisa, Italy. It is situated at coordinates 43.689188 latitude and 10.68822 longitude on the European continent.
decc4586-b729-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: BSCR Observatory, Italy

dece2dc0-b5fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **MMS 3 Active Spacecraft Potential Control (ASPOC)** is an instrument on the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS) spacecraft that generates indium ion beams to limit positive spacecraft potentials, thereby improving measurements from other MMS instruments such as FPI, HPCA, ADP, and SDP. It started operations in 2015 and is designed to maintain the spacecraft's potential within +4V for better data accuracy.
dece2dc0-b5fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Active Spacecraft Potential Control Instrument part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

ded503d8-b92c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Pathfinder (MPF) Radio Science Subsystem is an instrumentation system used to investigate rotational and orbital dynamics through shared equipment for telecommunications and radio science.
ded503d8-b92c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Subsystem for Mars Pathfinder part of NASA Deep Space Network

dedde568-b65a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer situated at the Numto station with IAGA identifier NMT, operational from 1974 to 1978 as part of the observatory network.
dedde568-b65a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Numto Observatory

def282b6-b754-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Hobart Station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Kingston, Tasmania, Australia, which is part of the larger MAGDAS network and operated by IUGONET.
def282b6-b754-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hobart Observatory, Australia

def8a9ce-bb9c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sodankylä Geophysical Observatory VLF Receiver System is a broadband (500Hz-38kHz) instrument used for Very Low Frequency (VLF) measurements, supporting various observing campaigns and networks like AARDDVARK, WWLLN, and AWDA.
def8a9ce-bb9c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spectral Power Receiver at Sodankylä Geophysical Observatory

df002600-b821-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SARA-KP is a Cassegrain reflecting telescope located at Kitt Peak in Arizona, United States. It has an aperture of 0.91 meters and a focal length of approximately 6.858 meters.
df002600-b821-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.91m Telescope at SARA Observatory, United States

df02eee4-bb9b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LANL2001 is a geosynchronous spacecraft located within Earth's magnetosphere and radiation belt, equipped with plasma instrumentation for observing and studying space weather phenomena. It is part of the Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) satellite series, specifically designed to monitor and collect data on charged particles in near-Earth space.
df02eee4-bb9b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma instrumentation on LANL2001

df0acc26-b881-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Stratospheric TeraHertz Observatory (STO) telescope is a lightweight, balloon-borne instrument with an 80cm diameter hyperboloid primary mirror optimized for the 300-5000nm wavelength range. Originally part of the STO project, it was later refitted to be used by the BOPPS gondola.
df0acc26-b881-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.8m Stratospheric TeraHertz Observatory Telescope part of BOPPS

df0b0726-b7ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Ekaterinburg Geomagnetic Observatory (SVD) is a ground-based facility located in Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia, operating since 1924 to monitor geomagnetic activity. It includes instruments like the magnetometer and is part of the global network for geomagnetic data collection.
df0b0726-b7ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Ekaterinburg, Russia

df0b2b96-b7c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Indian Institute of Astrophysics 1m Telescope is located at the Vainu Bappu Observatory in Asia and operates in the optical waveband.
df0b2b96-b7c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical Indian Institute of Astrophysics 1m Telescope at Vainu Bappu Observatory

df178d22-b83a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES) 1.3m Devasthal Fast Optical Telescope is a telescopic facility located in Asia, specifically in Devasthal, India. It operates within the optical waveband and has an aperture of 1.3 meters.
df178d22-b83a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES) 1.3m Devasthal Fast Optical Telescope at Devasthal, Asia

df1f6234-b792-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is a fluxgate magnetometer located in Yamakawa, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network within the IUGONET observatory. It measures magnetic field variations using a fluxgate sensor.
df1f6234-b792-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of 210 Magnetic Meridian Network

df20cc5e-bbf8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The San Jose Dos Campos Magnetometer was an instrument used to measure magnetic field variations at the IAGA-identified SJB station in San Jose Dos Campos from January 1973 to December 1975.
df20cc5e-bbf8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at San Jose Dos Campos Observatory

df29b534-ba82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Skylab UV Scanning Polychromator Spectroheliometer was an instrument on the Apollo Telescope Mount (ATM) aboard Skylab, launched in 1973. It aimed to gather photometric data and EUV observations of specific spectral lines and solar structures, utilizing a high-resolution spectrometer with various observing modes for detailed solar studies.
df29b534-ba82-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Scanning Polychromator Spectroheliometer on Skylab

df2b7008-b5d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nuuk Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Nuuk, Greenland, that includes a magnetometer and is part of the IUGONET observatory network. It was established on November 1, 1981, and operates at an altitude of 1 meter above sea level.
df2b7008-b5d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nuuk Geophysical Observatory, Greenland

df3208c4-b942-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Plasma Waves and Sounder (PWS) is an instrument onboard the Akebono satellite designed to observe natural and stimulated plasma waves, as well as measure electron number density. It consists of three sub-systems: natural plasma wave observations, stimulated plasma wave experiments, and electron number density measurement.
df3208c4-b942-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Waves and Sounder part of Akebono

df3a5fb8-b7b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **White Shell Geomagnetic Observatory** is a ground-based facility located in Unorganized Division No. 1, Manitoba, Canada that operated from January 1977 to December 31, 1980, specializing in geomagnetic measurements with instruments provided by the World Data Center for Geomagnetism at Kyoto (WDC-Kyoto).
df3a5fb8-b7b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at White Shell Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

df3a7e4e-bc00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Castelmartini Observatory**, also known as the Osservatorio Astronomico di Castelmartini, is an astronomical observatory located in Castelmartini, Larciano, Italy. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial objects and phenomena.
df3a7e4e-bc00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Astronomico di Castelmartini at Castelmartini Observatory, Italy

df47d918-b809-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IRTS is a 0.15-meter infrared telescope developed by the Institute of Space and Astronautical Science (ISAS), which was part of Japan's Space Flyer Unit mission, designed to observe astronomical phenomena in the infrared waveband from space.
df47d918-b809-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Institute of Space and Astronautical Science 0.15m Infrared Telescope on Space Flyer Unit

df4ad18c-bb4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Air Force Research Laboratory Space Vehicles Directorate/National Solar Observatory (NSO) Improved Solar Observing Optical Network (ISOON) is a ground-based optical observatory located in North America, focused on monitoring solar activity.
df4ad18c-bb4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Improved Solar Observing Optical Network at Air Force Research Laboratory Space Vehicles Directorate and National Solar Observatory, Antarctica

df51263c-bad7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Brescia Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Chiusure, Brescia, Italy. It is a ground-based facility used for observing and studying celestial objects.
df51263c-bad7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chiusure Observatory, Italy

df75bd1c-bbc2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 1 Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer (HPCA) is an instrument aboard the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS) that measures ion fluxes and composition in space, utilizing advanced technologies like electrostatic optics and time-of-flight analysis to operate effectively in high proton flux environments.
df75bd1c-bbc2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

df7a7e6e-b6c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NIPR-type Low Power Magnetometer (NIPR-LPM) at Amundsen Bay, Antarctica, is a fluxgate magnetometer designed for low power consumption and near-real-time data transmission via the Iridium satellite system. It is part of an automated magnetometer network developed since 2003 to monitor geomagnetic activity in remote locations.
df7a7e6e-b6c3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: NIPR Low Power Magnetometer on Automated Magnetometer Network Observatory, Antarctica

df874ea8-bae9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity Navigation Cameras (Navcams) are imaging devices mounted on the rover to capture terrain and landscape images, aiding in its navigation across Mars. These cameras are part of the Pancam Mast Assembly and share an identical optical design with other rover cameras like the EDLcam and Hazcams.
df874ea8-bae9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Navigation Camera on Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity

df895902-b682-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2.4-m Hiltner telescope is an operational optical telescope located at the MDM Observatory in North America. It is a Ritchey-Chretien equatorial reflector that has been in use since 1985 and is part of a collaboration between Michigan, Dartmouth, and MIT.
df895902-b682-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.4m optical Hiltner Telescope at MDM Observatory

df8b95d2-bb6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Terrain Mapping Camera (TMC) is a passive electro-optical imaging instrument onboard the Chandrayaan-1 Orbiter, operating in the visible-panchromatic band to capture stereo views of lunar terrain.
df8b95d2-bb6e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible-Panchromatic Terrain Mapping Camera on Chandrayaan-1 Orbiter

df9241b6-b957-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Higashi-Hiroshima Observatory is an astronomical observatory featuring the 1.5m Kanata Telescope, used for optical and near-infrared observations.
df9241b6-b957-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.5m Kanata Optical and Near Infrared Telescope at Higashi-Hiroshima Observatory

df9c20d6-b6d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LANL1989 Energetic Sensor for Particles (ESP) is an instrument used to measure high-energy particles, specifically electrons from 0.7 to 26 MeV and protons from 11 to >20 MeV. It employs a bismuth germanate crystal coupled to a thick plastic scintillator and a photomultiplier tube for its measurements.
df9c20d6-b6d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Spectrometer for Particles part of Los Alamos National Laboratory Observatory

dfa79198-b86b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 15 is an instrument designed to measure the magnitude and direction of Earth's geomagnetic field, detect variations in magnetic activity, and provide alerts for solar wind shocks. It consists of two identical sensors mounted at different distances from the spacecraft for redundancy and calibration purposes.
dfa79198-b86b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 15

dfae9292-b693-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** OPERA is an electric field instrument on the Interball Tail Probe, designed to measure electric fields in three axes from DC to 200 kHz using a set of sensors and filters. It is part of the ASPI complex dedicated to studying plasma waves.
dfae9292-b693-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna part of Measurements of Electric Field in Range 0 to 250 KHz on Interball Tail Probe

dfb4b264-b6e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The King George Island Magnetometer is a scientific instrument located at the IAGA-identified station KGI on King George Island, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of geomagnetic research.
dfb4b264-b6e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at King George Island Observatory

dfb56772-b7db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Klagenfurt Observatory was a ground-based facility in Austria, active from 1891 to 1899, known for its magnetometer instrument and located at 46.617° N, 14.3° E in the city of Klagenfurt.
dfb56772-b7db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Klagenfurt Observatory, Austria

dfbcd0b0-b9b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Observatory of Saint-Pardon-de-Conques is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Pardon-de-Conques, France. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical research and observations.
dfbcd0b0-b9b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Saint-Pardon-de-Conques Observatory, France

dfc44584-bae3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Tebbutt Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Edgewood, New Mexico. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
dfc44584-bae3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Edgewood Observatory

dfc5e344-bb51-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory, located in La Serena, Spain, is a ground-based astronomical facility known for its telescopes and contributions to astrophysical research.
dfc5e344-bb51-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1m SMARTS Telescope at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory

dfc6641c-bb39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Narsarsuaq Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Kujalleq, Greenland, primarily involved in magnetometer observations as part of the NASA THEMIS Ground-Based Observatories network.
dfc6641c-bb39-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Narsarsuaq Observatory, Greenland

dfcbfd88-b8db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The one at the Maputo ground station has been operational since January 1, 1980, as part of the World Data Center for Geomagnetism (WDC_GDMC).
dfcbfd88-b8db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Maputo Observatory

dfcc714a-b62f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Norfolk Island Magnetometer** is a ground-based instrument located in Norfolk Island, NSW, Australia, specifically a Fluxgate Magnetometer that has been operational since March 2010. It is part of the ASWS Observatory and is used for magnetic field measurements.
dfcc714a-b62f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Norfolk Island Observatory, Australia

dfcc8f88-bb46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astronomical Observatory of Kazan University is a historic Russian astronomical observatory located in Kazan, founded in 1837 and recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site. It operates under the Department of Astronomy of Kazan University and stands at an altitude of 75 meters above sea level.
dfcc8f88-bb46-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory of Kazan University, Russia

dfd33708-baff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A scanning mobility particle sizer is an instrument used to measure the size distribution and concentration of fine particles in the atmosphere. It was part of the ISEE atmospheric observation conducted at Shigaraki Observatory, specifically a TSI model 3776 device.
dfd33708-baff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spectrometer part of ISEE atmospheric observation

dfd53ba4-bc6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Crespadoro Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Crespadoro, Vicenza, Veneto, Italy. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
dfd53ba4-bc6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Crespadoro Observatory, Italy

dfdc9bfe-bc99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Dark Sky Observatory (DSO) is an astronomical observatory operated by Appalachian State University, located near Deep Gap, North Carolina, used for research, instruction, and public viewing events.
dfdc9bfe-bc99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dark Sky Observatory

dfeb7996-b7e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "MMS4 Ephemeris" is a virtual instrument that provides the orbital position data for the MMS 4 spacecraft as part of the CDPP-AMDA observatory managed by CNES.
dfeb7996-b7e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris on Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission 4 Spacecraft

dfed808a-ba47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Karsani Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field, operational from January 1, 1905, to December 31, 1934, at a station with the IAGA identifier KAS.
dfed808a-ba47-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Karsani Observatory

e0006d92-b9a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The River Ridge Observatory (V88) is an astronomical observatory located in Conway, Arkansas, dedicated to ground-based observations.
e0006d92-b9a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: River Ridge Observatory, United States

e0112884-b905-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kanozan Geomagnetic Observatory (KNZ), located in Kimitsu, Chiba Prefecture, Japan, is a ground-based facility that has been operating since 1961 to monitor and study geomagnetic activity.
e0112884-b905-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kanozan Geomagnetic Observatory, Japan

e0126212-b7d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Sicincin station is a ground-based observatory located in Padang - Bukittinggi, Sicincin, West Sumatra, Indonesia. It operates as part of the MAGDAS magnetometer network and includes a fluxgate instrument for monitoring magnetic fields.
e0126212-b7d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Magnetic Data Acquisition System Sicincin, Indonesia

e01b33b8-bb5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cloud Particle Size Spectrometer (LCPS) was an instrument aboard the Pioneer Venus Large Probe designed to measure the sizes and concentrations of cloud particles in Venus' atmosphere.
e01b33b8-bb5f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Large Probe Cloud Particle Size Spectrometer on Pioneer Venus

e0217512-b6ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Leura Observatory 0.25-m telescope is a 25 cm telescope situated in Leura, Australia, at coordinates -33.706833, 150.341694 and an altitude of 1175 meters.
e0217512-b6ea-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.25m Telescope at Leura Observatory, Australia

e02e67aa-b9fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pine Ridge (PINE) station is an observatory located in Pine Ridge, South Dakota, USA, operated by UCLA, featuring an Educational Public Outreach magnetometer. It is part of the NASA THEMIS EPO network and focuses on magnetic field measurements while being subject to environmental noise considerations.
e02e67aa-b9fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pine Ridge Observatory, United States

e0317fac-b9a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The "Magnetometers at Penteli (PEG)" specifically refers to the magnetometers located at the Penteli observatory in Kyoto, which are part of the IAGA investigation and have been operational since January 1959.
e0317fac-b9a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Penteli Observatory

e033ebe8-ba50-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Skinakas Observatory is an astronomical observatory situated on the peak of Psiloritis on Crete, Greece. It features multiple telescopes and is operated by the University of Crete and the Foundation for Research & Technology – Hellas.
e033ebe8-ba50-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.3m Telescope at Skinakas Observatory, Greece

e04102da-b5b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Gruppo Astrofili Catanesi" is an Italian amateur astronomer association based in Catania, Italy, operating a ground observatory since 1977.
e04102da-b5b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Italian amateur astronomer association at Via L. Sturzo Observatory, Italy

e0456e9e-b998-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Rolling Hills Observatory (V83) is an astronomical observatory located in Warrensburg, Missouri, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
e0456e9e-b998-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Warrensburg Observatory, United States

e0469bea-b5cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Sample Return Capsule (SRC) was a spacecraft component designed to collect cometary and interstellar dust particles non-destructively and return them to Earth for analysis, notably used in the Stardust mission.
e0469bea-b5cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sample Return Capsule on Stardust

e050eb78-b846-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RPC-MIP (Mutual Impedance Probe) is part of the Rosetta Plasma Consortium onboard the Rosetta spacecraft, designed to measure plasma parameters such as electron density and temperature by analyzing mutual impedance between transmitting and receiving antennas. It also functions as a plasma wave analyzer in its passive mode.
e050eb78-b846-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mutual Impedance Probe part of Rosetta Plasma Consortium

e06402e0-bb4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "spacecraft.v3" refers to a specific version of a spacecraft within the context of NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS), representing both an instrument host and a part of observation facilities, identified by the provided URI.
e06402e0-bb4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: James Webb Space Telescope

e066206a-bbe8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The OSIRIS Wide Angle Camera (WAC) is a key component of the Rosetta spacecraft's primary imaging system, designed to capture wide-field images with filters covering wavelengths from 246.2 nm to 629.8 nm and featuring a double filter wheel system.
e066206a-bbe8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical, Spectroscopic, and Infrared Remote Imaging System Wide Angle Camera on Rosetta spacecraft

e06ccede-b179-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Brooks Astronomical Observatory is an astronomical observatory owned and operated by Central Michigan University, located in Mount Pleasant, Michigan (USA).
e06ccede-b179-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Brooks Astronomical Observatory, United States

e072d386-b7a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cosmic Ray and Solar Particles (SIM/COSPIN)** instrument on the Ulysses spacecraft is designed to study the energy spectra, charge, and mass of energetic charged particles in interplanetary space, focusing on protons and heavier nuclei with energies ranging from approximately 0.5 MeV/nucleon to over 1 GeV. It comprises five separate telescopes tailored to different particle populations, aiming to investigate spatial gradients and the propagation of charged particles throughout the heliosphere.
e072d386-b7a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cosmic Ray and Solar Particles on Ulysses

e0737172-b8cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Galileo National Telescope (TNG) is a 3.58-meter Italian telescope situated at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory in La Palma, Canary Islands, Spain, operated by the Fundación Galileo Galilei on behalf of the Italian National Institute of Astrophysics (INAF). Named after Galileo Galilei, it saw first light in 1998.
e0737172-b8cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.58m Galileo National Telescope at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory, Spain

e07815c4-b5ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Perth Observatory Ground Facility is a ground-based observatory located in Perth, Western Australia, which has been operational since October 2010. It includes an ionosonde instrument and is situated at Boud Avenue, Perth Airport, City of Belmont, with coordinates approximately -31.94 latitude and 115.95 longitude.
e07815c4-b5ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionosonde at Perth Observatory

e08005b8-bb41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Glasgow Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Glasgow, Scotland, dedicated to ground-based observations.
e08005b8-bb41-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Glasgow Observatory, United Kingdom

e089b3b0-b655-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU radio beacon receiver (GRBR) station at Pontianak is an observatory located in Indonesia that measures ionospheric disturbances related to middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes. It is part of the GRBR network and situated near the equator at coordinates 0.00S, 109.37E.
e089b3b0-b655-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU radio beacon receiver on GRBR Station at Pontianak, Indonesia

e0935bb0-babd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Interball-Tail** is a satellite mission within the Interball Project, launched on August 3, 1995, to study energy and mass transfer between the solar wind and Earth's magnetosphere. It focuses specifically on plasma processes in the magnetotail and interactions at the magnetopause, utilizing a pair of closely spaced satellites to distinguish wave motions from spatial structures.
e0935bb0-babd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Interball-Tail part of INTERBALL Project

e0a3eb46-b721-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the magnetometers located at the Rude Skov Observatory in Kyoto, which were operational from 1891-01-01 to 1984-12-31 as part of the IAGA investigation.
e0a3eb46-b721-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Rude Skov Observatory

e0b9dcd0-bc80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Godthaab was a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Nuuk, Greenland, operational from January 1, 1883, to December 31, 1941.
e0b9dcd0-bc80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Godthaab Observatory, Greenland

e0bbe532-ba66-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The IAGA:MOD Magnetometer, located at the MOD station, has been operational since January 1, 1975, as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
e0bbe532-ba66-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Modiim Observatory

e0bd1af4-b6bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Kodiak Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS GBO Network, used for measuring magnetic fields starting from January 1, 2010.
e0bd1af4-b6bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kodiak Observatory

e0cc073a-b9e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The St. John's Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility in Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, operated by the Geological Survey of Canada since 1968 for monitoring Earth's magnetic field.
e0cc073a-b9e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at St John's Magnetic Observatory, Canada

e0d28490-b85e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Canberra Ionosonde** is an instrument located near Canberra, ACT, Australia, used for radar investigation of the ionosphere since March 1937. It currently employs an IPS 5D digital ionosonde that operates in the frequency range from about 1.0 to 21.5 MHz with a resolution of up to 4095 steps, each at 5 kHz intervals.
e0d28490-b85e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar Ionosonde part of World Data Centre for the Ionosphere, Kyoto and WDC for the Ionosphere, Canberra

e0dca174-b966-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The PENGUIn-5 (PG5) Geophysical Observatory is a ground facility located on Earth's surface at an altitude of 2371.0 meters, equipped with instruments such as magnetometers for geophysical research.
e0dca174-b966-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at PENGUIn-5 Geophysical Observatory

e0e9d2b2-b868-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory (FLWO) is a telescope facility that includes the 2-Micron All Sky Survey (2MASS) 1.3m telescope, now known as the Peters Automated Infrared Imaging Telescope (PAIRITEL).
e0e9d2b2-b868-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.3m Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory Telescope, USA

e0f72cdc-b642-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Radcliffe Observatory in Pretoria is a ground-based astronomical facility located at 1481 Johann Rissik Drive, Waterkloof Ridge, Tshwane Ward 42, in the City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality, Gauteng, South Africa. It operates at the coordinates -25.788 latitude and 28.2288 longitude within the continent of Africa.
e0f72cdc-b642-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radcliffe Observatory, Pretoria, South Africa

e0fc3e7e-b990-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sept Iles (SEPT) Geophysical Observatory** is a ground-based facility located in Sept-Îles, Quebec, Canada. It includes instruments such as the magnetometer and has been operational since October 26, 2014.
e0fc3e7e-b990-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sept Iles Geophysical Observatory, Canada

e0fedda4-badb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kurohone Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Kurohone-cho, Kiryu City, Gunma Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility used for stargazing and scientific research.
e0fedda4-badb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kurohone Observatory, Japan

e1007e22-b714-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Divine Creation Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Fort Davis, Texas, United States. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to studying the cosmos from its strategic location in Jeff Davis County.
e1007e22-b714-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Divine Creation Observatory, United States

e1073b30-b96d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on Hawkeye 1** is a scientific instrument used to measure the ambient magnetic field in space, featuring four sensitivity ranges and mounted on a 1.52-m boom with precise calibration capabilities.
e1073b30-b96d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on Hawkeye

e11cd788-b7f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Toroidal Imaging Mass-Angle Spectrograph (TIMAS) is an instrument onboard the POLAR spacecraft, launched in 1996, designed to study solar wind and ionospheric plasma interactions within Earth's magnetosphere using advanced mass spectrometry techniques.
e11cd788-b7f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Toroidal Imaging Mass-Angle Spectrograph on Polar

e11dd720-b808-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Woogaroo Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Forest Lake, Queensland, Australia. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to studying celestial phenomena and is situated at coordinates 152.94789 longitude and -27.605675 latitude.
e11dd720-b808-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Forest Lake Observatory

e1241636-bbb3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Geotail Position is an instrument type that provides the ephemerides (positions) of the Geotail spacecraft in different coordinate systems. It is part of the CNES Observatory CDPP AMDA Geotail mission and offers data on the spacecraft's location over time.
e1241636-bbb3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geotail Position part of Geotail Mission

e12c459c-b5c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Eights Geomagnetic Observatory (EGS) was a ground-based facility located on the Earth's surface, operational from 1963 to 1965. It was part of the SMWG Observatory network and focused on geomagnetic measurements using instruments such as magnetometers.
e12c459c-b5c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eights Geomagnetic Observatory

e14583fc-bb45-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The PlasMag Faraday Cup is an instrument onboard DSCOVR that measures solar wind properties with high time resolution, enabling detailed studies of solar wind waves, turbulence, and plasma processes critical for understanding coronal heating.
e14583fc-bb45-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Faraday Cup part of Deep Space Climate Observatory

e146b754-b898-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kuchino Observatory was a ground-based facility in Russia dedicated to magnetic observations as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA), operational from 1926 to 1938.
e146b754-b898-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kuchino Observatory, Russia

e14cc826-bc24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Psyche Multispectral Imager is an instrument on the Psyche spacecraft designed to capture high-resolution images of asteroid (16) Psyche using filters to differentiate between metallic and silicate materials. It includes two identical cameras for geologic, compositional, and topographic data acquisition, with one providing redundancy for optical navigation.
e14cc826-bc24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Psyche Multispectral Imager on Psyche

e14fdb1e-b85b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Sternwarte Silbergraben, Erfurt" is a ground-based observatory located at 51, Silbergraben in Melchendorf, Erfurt, Thuringia, Germany. It serves as an astronomical facility for observations and research within Europe.
e14fdb1e-b85b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Silver Trench Observatory, Germany

e15700ba-b964-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SPECTRO experiment on the AUREOL-3 satellite is a mass spectrometer designed to measure auroral particle energy spectra, angular distributions, and ion mass spectra within specific energy ranges. It consists of several complementary instruments, including ROBE, TBE, ION1, and ION2, and has contributed to various studies on auroral phenomena and plasma dynamics in the cusp region.
e15700ba-b964-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer on Aureol 3

e15a33be-ba6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rand II Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Lake Placid, New York. It operates as a ground-based facility focused on studying celestial phenomena from Earth.
e15a33be-ba6f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lake Placid Observatory, United States

e15bad98-bb73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **DMSP_5D2-F10 Positions** dataset provides the spacecraft positions of the DMSP (Defense Meteorological Satellite Program) 5D2-F10 satellite in various coordinate systems, essential for tracking and analyzing its ephemeris data.
e15bad98-bb73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft Position part of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program 5D-2 F10

e1607c58-b7ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer onboard the DMSP/F15 satellite, specifically the Special Sensor Magnetometer-Boom (SESS/SSM-Boom), which measures geomagnetic fluctuations associated with various geophysical phenomena.
e1607c58-b7ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Magnetometer on DMSP F15

e163f066-b826-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover Navigation Camera Left String A is a high-resolution stereo camera mounted on the rover's mast, used for autonomous navigation and mapping the Martian terrain to assist in safe route planning and scientific exploration.
e163f066-b826-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Navigation Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

e1689136-b95a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMN Huancayo Station is a ground-based magnetometer network located in Huancayo, Peru, dedicated to monitoring and studying magnetic field variations on Earth's surface.
e1689136-b95a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hualmitá Observatory, Peru

e16e76ce-b977-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Regolith X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (REXIS) was a student-led instrument aboard the OSIRIS-REx spacecraft, designed to map the asteroid Bennu's surface using X-ray fluorescence with a sensitivity range of 0.3 - 7.5 keV and a resolution of 21 arcminutes.
e16e76ce-b977-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Regolith X-ray Imaging Spectrometer on OSIRIS-REx Spacecraft

e16fc888-b5c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Aedey, Iceland, used for the Conjugate Observation at Iceland investigation as part of the IUGONET-Observatory WDC Kyoto.
e16fc888-b5c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Conjugate Observation at Iceland

e17200cc-bca2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the magnetometer located at the Burlington observatory station, identified by IAGA as BRT. It was operational from January 1, 1957, until December 31, 1959, and is part of the iugonet-observatory network associated with WDC Kyoto.
e17200cc-bca2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iugonet Observatory

e174a258-baf1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1N was a component of the BARREL mission, which aimed to study relativistic electron losses from Earth's radiation belts. It operated in the stratosphere from January 8 to January 16, 2013, carrying instruments like NaI scintillators and magnetometers to measure X-rays and magnetic fields, complementing data from NASA’s Van Allen Probes.
e174a258-baf1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses Balloon part of Living with a Star Mission

e180661e-b7eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **OWL-Net Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Mitzpe Ramon, Israel. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
e180661e-b7eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: OWL-Net Observatory, Israel

e1820cd4-b16b-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ranua Magnetometer is a ground-based instrument located at the Ranua Geophysical Observatory, primarily used to measure and record magnetic field variations as part of geophysical investigations.
e1820cd4-b16b-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ranua Geophysical Observatory

e18d7880-b9e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1S magnetometer is a three-axis instrument used to measure magnetic field components with high resolution, aiding in the study of substorm activity and ULF oscillations during balloon flights.
e18d7880-b9e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

e190c942-bc0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RPF Observatory in Gagliano del Capo is a ground-based astronomical observatory located at Via dei Mille, Arigliano, in the Apulia region of Italy. It operates from coordinates 39.8426° N latitude and 18.36969° E longitude.
e190c942-bc0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: RPF Observatory at Gagliano del Capo, Italy

e1a14ee6-bc56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Galileo Orbiter Photopolarimeter Radiometer (PPR)** is a versatile instrument designed for both solar wavelength photopolarimetry and thermal infrared sounding, used aboard the Galileo spacecraft to study Jupiter's atmosphere. It features a telescope with a 2.5 mrad field of view and uses rotating filters to observe various wavelengths for polarimetry, radiometry, and photometry measurements.
e1a14ee6-bc56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Photopolarimeter Radiometer on Galileo Orbiter

e1a6c954-bac9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Beagle 2**: A British Mars lander launched in 2003 as part of the European Space Agency's Mars Express mission. It failed to establish communication after its scheduled landing on Mars and was declared lost.
e1a6c954-bac9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Beagle 2 part of Mars Express

e1b4d24e-b798-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bamberg Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Bamberg, Germany, dedicated to ground-based observation of celestial phenomena. It operates from Forchheimer Straße and contributes to the field of astronomy through its research and monitoring activities.
e1b4d24e-b798-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bamberg Observatory, Germany

e1b7de6c-b838-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astronomical Observatory of Garraf is an astronomical observatory located in Olivella, Barcelona, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
e1b7de6c-b838-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory of Garraf

e1bd2352-b830-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence (SETI) Allen Telescope Array is a radio telescope located in North America, designed to detect and analyze signals from potential extraterrestrial civilizations.
e1bd2352-b830-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Allen Telescope Array and One Hectare Telescope radio

e1c61a4a-b61c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the ALIS (Aurora Large Imaging System) station located in Tjautjas, Gällivare kommun, Norrbotten County, Sweden. It is a ground-based facility designed for observing auroras and has specific instruments such as the AWI White Light instrument.
e1c61a4a-b61c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Aurora Large Imaging System at Tjautjas, Sweden

e1cb7ff8-bb03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The PUNCH-WFI 2 is a NASA heliophysics satellite, part of the Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere (PUNCH) constellation, designed to observe and track solar wind dynamics in the inner heliosphere.
e1cb7ff8-bb03-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label:
Narrow Field Imager on PUNCH Narrow Field Imager satellite part of Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere mission
Wide Field Imager on PUNCH-WFI 1 satellite part of Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere mission
Wide Field Imager on PUNCH-WFI 2 satellite part of Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere mission
Wide Field Imager on PUNCH-WFI 3 satellite part of Polarimeter to Unify the Corona and Heliosphere mission

e1ceb1c0-b980-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **Magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure magnetic field intensity and direction. The specific magnetometer described here, known as MAG (ASM/VFM), consists of two components: the Absolute Scalar Magnetometer (ASM) for measuring magnetic field intensity, and the Vector Field Magnetometer (VFM) for measuring the magnetic field vector.
e1ceb1c0-b980-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Absolute Scalar Magnetometer and Vector Field Magnetometer on Swarm C

e1d15f84-b1a5-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Indian Institute of Astrophysics 1.3m J.C. Bhattacharya Telescope (JCBT) at Vainu Bappu Observatory is a telescope located in Asia, specifically designed for optical waveband observations and managed by the Vainu Bappu Observatory under the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.
e1d15f84-b1a5-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 1.3m J.C. Bhattacharya Telescope at Vainu Bappu Observatory

e1d65d2a-bb16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Equatorial Magnetometer Network (EMN) fluxgate magnetometer at Canete, Peru is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument used for measuring magnetic fields. It is part of the IUGONET observatory and specifically installed in Canete, Peru to monitor geomagnetic activity in the region.
e1d65d2a-bb16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Equatorial Magnetometer Network

e1e3ac2a-bb64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Lliça d'Amunt Observatory (code: K09) is an astronomical observatory located in Lliçà d'Amunt, Barcelona, Spain. It is recognized by the Minor Planet Center with the MPC ID K09 and specializes in ground-based observations.
e1e3ac2a-bb64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lliçà d'Amunt Observatory, Spain

e1e7fcae-baa5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Rimbach Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Rimbach, Bavaria, Germany (10 Hohenbogenstraße). It serves as a ground-based facility for celestial observations.
e1e7fcae-baa5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rimbach Observatory, Germany

e1fa024a-b8df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The magnetometer at the Lviv ground station is an instrument used to measure magnetic field variations as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy's (IAGA) network, operating since 1952.
e1fa024a-b8df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lviv Observatory

e1ff4996-b644-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Harsona Observatory in Nyíregyháza is a ground-based observatory located at Harsona utca in Hungary. It serves as an astronomical facility for observation and research purposes.
e1ff4996-b644-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Harsona Observatory, Hungary

e204ac2c-b736-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Crimean Astrophysical Observatory (CrAO) Five-Channel Photopolarimeter is an instrument capable of simultaneous polarimetric measurements in UBVRI colors, using dichroic filters and photomultipliers to measure each color's intensity and derive the Stokes parameters for linear polarization.
e204ac2c-b736-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Five-Channel Photopolarimeter on Crimean Astrophysical Observatory 1.25m AZT-11 Telescope

e206d184-ba4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Reilhanette Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Reilhanette, France. It is situated at coordinates 5.42106 longitude and 44.167417 latitude on the continent of Europe.
e206d184-ba4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Reilhanette Observatory, France

e2080d86-b740-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Maisach-2**: A historical ground facility located in Fürstenfeldbruck, Bavaria, Germany that operated a magnetometer from January 1927 to December 31, 1932 as part of the IAGA observatory network.
e2080d86-b740-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Maisach Observatory, Germany

e20b1912-b921-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Alpha Proton X-Ray Spectrometer (APXS) for MPFR is a sophisticated scientific instrument designed to analyze the composition of planetary surfaces by measuring the interaction of alpha particles, protons, and X-rays with materials. This spectrometer provides detailed insights into the elemental makeup of rocks, soil, and other surface materials, aiding in the understanding of planetary geology and chemistry.
e20b1912-b921-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Alpha Proton X-Ray Spectrometer on MPFR

e21101ec-b96c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tortona Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Tortona, Alessandria, Piedmont, Italy. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code A61 and situated at coordinates 44.90388° N, 8.8581° E.
e21101ec-b96c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tortona Observatory, Italy

e212a1b8-bca1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Pangnirtung Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG since October 4, 2008.
e212a1b8-bca1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pangnirtung Observatory

e215d42e-bc5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Giotto Spacecraft Ephemeris" is a virtual instrument that provides the positional data of the Giotto spacecraft, which was part of the CNES Observatory CDPP-AMDA.
e215d42e-bc5a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Giotto Positions part of Giotto Spacecraft

e21baf16-b700-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Rosemary Hill Observatory (RHO)** is an astronomical observatory located near Bronson, Florida, operated by the University of Florida since 1967. It houses two telescopes and dormitories for extended observation sessions.
e21baf16-b700-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rosemary Hill Observatory

e2331806-ba7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **MASTER-OAFA Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Calingasta, San Juan Province, Argentina. It is a ground-based facility situated at coordinates -69.32643 longitude and -31.802281 latitude.
e2331806-ba7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: MASTER-OAFA Observatory, Argentina

e2336a38-b95e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU Radio Beacon Receiver (GRBR) is a digital instrument installed in Pohnpei, Micronesia, designed to measure ionospheric total electron content using signals from Low Earth Orbit satellites. It employs open-source software and hardware, including GNU Radio for signal processing and Universal Software Radio Peripheral for signal acquisition.
e2336a38-b95e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU Radio Beacon Receiver at Pohnpei Observatory

e2377fa4-b686-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometer at Bar Gyora (BGY), operational from 1989 to 1996, was part of the IAGA investigation and located at the IUGONET observatory in Kyoto.
e2377fa4-b686-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

e2580aa4-b950-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1-m Boller & Chivens Ritchey-Chretien reflector is a 1-meter telescope situated at the Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile, operational since 1974 and originally from Yale University Observatory.
e2580aa4-b950-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1m Boller & Chivens Ritchey-Chretien Reflector Telescope at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory, Chile

e273b270-baab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Gartensternwarte Schafsweide**: An astronomical observatory located in Sehlde, Elze, Germany, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
e273b270-baab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gartensternwarte Schafsweide at Elze Observatory

e27e00c2-bbc8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT) Owens Valley Solar Array (OVSA) is a radio telescope located at the Owens Valley Radio Observatory in North America, dedicated to observing solar activity.
e27e00c2-bbc8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio New Jersey Institute of Technology Owens Valley Solar Array at Owens Valley Radio Observatory
