e280371a-b75f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hyper-dense GNSS receiver network station at Mimaki Elementary School is a ground facility in Kumiyama, Kyoto Prefecture, Japan, designed to monitor precipitable water vapor variations using GPS and QZSS satellite signals.
e280371a-b75f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hyper-dense Global Navigation Satellite System receiver network station at Mimaki Elementary School, Japan

e283819e-b80a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Posadas Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Calle Gaitán, Posadas, Córdoba, Andalusia, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
e283819e-b80a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Posadas Observatory, Spain

e28eb5e2-b81d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Chinese Academy of Sciences 7m Telescope is a radio telescope located at the Beijing Astronomical Observatory in Asia. It has an aperture of 7 meters and is used for astronomical observations in the radio waveband.
e28eb5e2-b81d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 7.0m radio Chinese Academy of Sciences Telescope at Beijing Astronomical Observatory

e29571f2-ba16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AVON (Asia VLF Observation Network) Pontianak station, located in Sungai Ambawang, Kubu Raya, West Kalimantan, Indonesia, is a ground-based facility dedicated to Very Low Frequency (VLF) radio observations as part of the Asia VLF Observation Network.
e29571f2-ba16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Asia VLF Observation Network Pontianak Station part of Tohoku University Radio Observatory, Indonesia

e29c2944-b727-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN Pohnpei Station is a ground-based magnetometer network facility located in U, Federated States of Micronesia. It operates as part of the IUGONET Observatory and includes instruments such as the ICSWSE fluxgate magnetometer for measuring magnetic field variations on Earth's surface.
e29c2944-b727-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pohnpei Station, Federated States of Micronesia

e29d0790-ba49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer situated at the IAGA Kaliningrad-1 observatory, operational from 1979 to 1992, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigations.
e29d0790-ba49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kaliningrad Observatory

e29d6116-bc3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The given entity appears to be a structured identifier for an instrument or component (designated "ch1") hosted on a spacecraft within the context of ISRO's ISDA framework, with specific labels and references to its parts and roles.
e29d6116-bc3a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chandrayaan-1 Orbiter

e2a328da-b717-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Transiting Planets and Planetesimals Small Telescope (TRAPPIST) is a pair of Belgian robotic telescopes located in Chile and Morocco, primarily used for studying exoplanets.
e2a328da-b717-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Transiting Planets and Planetesimals Small Telescope at La Silla Observatory, Chile

e2a9c9ea-ba2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: TSky Observatory, located in Mueang Chon Buri District, Thailand, is a ground-based observatory for astronomical observations and research.
e2a9c9ea-ba2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: TSky Observatory, Thailand

e2b1ab00-b8e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Apollo 15 Lunar Surface Experiments Package Suprathermal Ion Detector Experiment (SIDE) was an instrument deployed during the Apollo 15 mission to measure the energies and masses of positive ions interacting with the lunar surface, including those from the magnetosphere and solar wind.
e2b1ab00-b8e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Suprathermal Ion Detector Experiment part of Apollo 15 Lunar Surface Experiments Package

e2cffe12-b69c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RISH Lower Troposphere Radar (LTR) at Shigaraki is a powerful L-band radar located in Japan, used for studying atmospheric turbulences in the lower troposphere by transmitting and receiving radio waves. It features a large phased-array antenna capable of rapid beam steering in multiple directions.
e2cffe12-b69c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lower Troposphere Radar on RISH Radar Observatory

e2da9d7a-b8c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Seoul National University (SNU) 0.43m Lee Sang Gak Telescope (LSGT) is an optical telescope located at the Siding Spring Observatory in Australia, with an aperture of 0.43 meters.
e2da9d7a-b8c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.43m Lee Sang Gak Telescope at Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

e2df0d84-b84b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Carrollton Ground Magnetic Field Instrument was a magnetometer operated at the Carrollton ground station from January 1, 1958, to December 31, 1959, as part of the IAGA investigation and the IUGONET observatory network.
e2df0d84-b84b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iugonet Observatory

e2f8ca2a-bb21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Wind Ion Composition Spectrometer (SWICS) aboard the Ulysses spacecraft is designed to analyze solar wind ions from hydrogen to iron, providing detailed data on their composition, temperature, and velocity to enhance our understanding of solar and heliospheric phenomena.
e2f8ca2a-bb21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Wind Ion Composition Spectrometer on Ulysses spacecraft

e2fb7bee-b66c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magellan:Clay telescope, also known as the Landon T. Clay telescope, is a 6.5-meter optical telescope located at Las Campanas Observatory in South America, operated by the Carnegie Institution for Science.
e2fb7bee-b66c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 6.5m Landon Clay Telescope at Las Campanas Observatory

e300b9b0-b6cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Harvest Moon Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Waterford Township, Minnesota, United States, known for its ground-based observations.
e300b9b0-b6cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Harvest Moon Observatory, United States

e309e612-b6a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite (LCROSS) Visible Camera (VIS) was a video camera designed to capture context imagery of the Centaur impact on the Moon, monitor ejecta cloud morphology, and determine visible grain categories. It featured a 752 x 582 pixel CCD sensor with 24-bit RGB color depth, operated at 30 Hz, and had a 12 mm focal length lens providing a wide field of view.
e309e612-b6a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible Camera on Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite

e30d27d4-b772-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Altimira Observatory (G76) is an astronomical facility located in Coto de Caza, Orange County, California. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is identified by the Minor Planet Center with MPC_ID G76.
e30d27d4-b772-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Altimira Observatory, United States

e30ed44c-b7b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **CPMN Piura Station** is a ground-based magnetometer facility located at the University of Piura in Piura, Peru, part of the global IUGONET observatory network. It monitors magnetic field variations on Earth's surface.
e30ed44c-b7b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Piura Observatory, Peru

e316b390-b8a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The COR1 telescope is the inner coronagraph of the Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation (SECCHI) instrument suite aboard the STEREO-B spacecraft, designed to measure the weak light from the solar corona in the presence of scattered light from the much brighter solar photosphere.
e316b390-b8a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Coronograph on Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory part of Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation

e322587e-b84f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at BSV is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Birdsville, Australia, used to measure magnetic field variations as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
e322587e-b84f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observation Network

e3254c9e-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer used by the JMA electrometer at Kakioka Observatory, specifically an electric field sensor that combines a water-dropper with a noncontact electrostatic sensor to measure electric fields.
e3254c9e-bb8a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of World Data Centre for Geomagnetism, Kyoto

e329c396-b6f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS-02) is a state-of-the-art particle physics detector on the International Space Station, designed to search for antimatter, dark matter, and measure cosmic rays to understand the origin of the universe.
e329c396-b6f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer part of International Space Station

e332a0c0-b904-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Tbilisi (TFS) observatory, part of the IUGONET network and managed by WDC Kyoto, used for measuring magnetic field variations.
e332a0c0-b904-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tbilisi Observatory

e34312f4-b9b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **KPLO Magnetometer (KMAG)** is a set of three magnetometers developed by Kyung Hee University for the Korean Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter (KPLO) mission. It is designed to measure the lunar magnetic field with redundancy and minimal spacecraft interference, enhancing the accuracy of data collection from and around the Moon.
e34312f4-b9b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter

e349839c-bbae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Rose Cottage Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in West Morton, Keighley, United Kingdom. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
e349839c-bbae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rose Cottage Observatory, United Kingdom

e34b472a-bb5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) is a NASA space telescope launched in 2018 to search for exoplanets using the transit method, surveying a vast area of the sky to identify thousands of potential planets around nearby stars.
e34b472a-bb5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite

e355f834-b9ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Clay Center Observatory in Brookline is an astronomical observatory located at Dexter School in Massachusetts, dedicated to ground-based observations.
e355f834-b9ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Clay Center Observatory at Brookline

e3589756-b5a0-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) all-sky imager located in Zhigansk, Russia. This instrument is part of the IUGONET observatory and was developed by Nagoya University to study upper atmospheric dynamics through nocturnal airglow emissions.
e3589756-b5a0-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Multi-wavelength All-Sky Imager at Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers Observatory, Russia

e35db7ae-b93d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Belly Wind Tunnel at the University of California, Berkeley, Richmond Field Station, Building 276, was an open circulation wind tunnel with dimensions of 30.5 meters in length, 0.76 meters in height, and 1.2 meters in width, operational around 1964.
e35db7ae-b93d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Open Circulation Wind Tunnel at University of California, Berkeley, Richmond Field Station

e35f98ba-bb6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Tiouine is a ground-based observatory located in Amerzgane, Morocco (latitude 30.927°N, longitude -7.26°E) at an altitude of 1335 meters, primarily used for geomagnetic measurements with a magnetometer since January 1, 1989.
e35f98ba-bb6a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tiouine Observatory, Morocco

e369d58e-b5e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LANL Spacecraft Series consists of geosynchronous spacecraft equipped with instruments to measure energetic electrons and ions within Earth's magnetosphere. These satellites are part of the Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) mission to study space weather and radiation belts, contributing valuable data for scientific research and practical applications.
e369d58e-b5e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geosynchronous spacecraft carrying energetic electron and ion instruments part of LANL Spacecraft Series

e370a630-b685-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Star Castle Observatory is a ground-based observatory located in Black Springs, Australia (latitude -33.8981835, longitude 138.8892212), which houses the "Black Springs 0m8" telescope and is part of NASA's Planetary Data System.
e370a630-b685-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Star Castle Observatory, Australia

e375c942-bad8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2P Data Processing Unit (DPU)** is a versatile instrument controller board used in the BARREL project to gather data from various sensors like an X-ray spectrometer and magnetometer, process this information, and transmit it via an Iridium modem. It features an FPGA for flexible interface logic and has been successfully deployed on multiple balloon flights and sounding rocket experiments.
e375c942-bad8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

e375cf7e-b7d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **MAVEN Solar Wind Ion Analyzer (SWIA)** is an electrostatic analyzer onboard the MAVEN spacecraft designed to measure solar wind and magnetospheric ions around Mars, helping to understand atmospheric loss processes and solar wind interactions with the Martian upper atmosphere.
e375cf7e-b7d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Wind Ion Analyzer on MAVEN

e378dcd0-b647-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Axial Double Probe (ADP)** is an instrument on the MMS 2 spacecraft, consisting of two 10-meter antennas that measure three-dimensional electric fields with high accuracy. It operates as part of the FIELDS suite, designed to study electromagnetic fields in space.
e378dcd0-b647-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Axial Double Probe part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

e37f0abe-bb6b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Dudley Observatory** in Albany, New York, was a ground-based observatory operational before 1893, located at 575 Lark Drive in the Warehouse District.
e37f0abe-bb6b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dudley Observatory

e383579e-bb8f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Chelles Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Chelles, France. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial objects.
e383579e-bb8f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chelles Observatory, France

e388b1e8-b9ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 13 Command and Service Module (CSM), named "Odyssey," was the spacecraft intended to carry astronauts to the Moon during the ill-fated Apollo 13 mission in 1970. Despite an onboard explosion that forced the crew to abort their lunar landing, the CSM successfully returned them safely to Earth.
e388b1e8-b9ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma Ray Apollo 13 Command and Service Module

e39e6964-b723-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Neutral Mass Spectrometer (BNMS) on the Pioneer Venus Probe Bus was designed to study the composition and dynamics of Venus' upper atmosphere by measuring neutral molecules, providing insights into its origin, evolution, and interaction with solar radiation.
e39e6964-b723-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutral Mass Spectrometer on Pioneer Venus Probe Bus

e3a29516-ba52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** MERLIN, or the University of Manchester Multi-Element Radio-Linked Interferometer Network Array, is a network of radio telescopes in Europe designed for high-resolution astronomical observations in the radio waveband.
e3a29516-ba52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Multi-Element Radio-Linked Interferometer Network Array

e3ad595a-b8cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS) 1.2m Telescope at Observatoire de Haute-Provence (OHP) is an optical telescope located in Europe, specifically in the south of France, used for astronomical research.
e3ad595a-b8cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 1.2m Telescope at Observatoire de Haute-Provence

e3c6caae-b8a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT) Alfonso Serrano**, also known as Gran Telescopio Milimetrico, is a 50-meter telescope located on the Volcano Sierra Negra in North America. It operates in the millimeter waveband and is collaboratively managed by Instituto Nacional de Astrofisica, Optica y Electronica (INAOE) and the University of Massachusetts at Amherst (UMass).
e3c6caae-b8a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter 50.0m Instituto Nacional de Astrofisica, Optica y Electronica and University of Massachusetts at Amherst Large Millimeter Telescope Alfonso Serrano on Volcano Sierra Negra

e3c757fe-b68b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mount Wilson Institute 1.5m (60-inch) Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Mount Wilson Observatory in North America. It has an aperture of 1.5 meters and is used for astronomical observations within the visible light spectrum.
e3c757fe-b68b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.5m Optical Telescope at Mount Wilson Observatory

e3ca6c5c-b945-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **Magnetometer** is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields, particularly Earth's magnetic field. The Bear Island Magnetometer, part of the THEMIS Collaboration, has been operational since January 5, 2011, and is located at the Bear Island geophysical observatory.
e3ca6c5c-b945-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bear Island Observatory

e3d197e4-bb92-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The Magnetometers at Boulder (BOU) specifically refer to those operated by the World Data Center in Boulder starting from 1964 as part of the IAGA investigation, under the iugonet-observatory network.
e3d197e4-bb92-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Boulder Observatory

e3d1ed00-bbb7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Faraday Cup** on Explorer 33 was a split-collector instrument designed to measure the directional intensity of solar wind ions and electrons, operating within specific energy per charge (E/Q) windows from launch until October 1971.
e3d1ed00-bbb7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Faraday Cup part of Explorer 33

e3e1fa82-b604-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Space Environment Monitor (SEM) on NOAA 12 is an instrument designed to measure proton and electron fluxes and energy spectra in the upper atmosphere. It consists of two detector systems: MEPED for higher energy particles and TED for lower energy particles.
e3e1fa82-b604-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument part of Space Environment Monitor on NOAA 12

e3e2791c-b915-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Yatsuka Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Yatsukacho-Futago, Matsue, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It serves as a ground-based facility for stargazing and astronomical research.
e3e2791c-b915-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yatsuka Observatory, Japan

e3e6e2aa-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The US Air Force 1.5m Starfire Optical Range (SOR) Telescope is an optical telescope with a 1.5-meter aperture located at Kirkland Air Force Base in North America, used for various astronomical and defense-related observations.
e3e6e2aa-ba31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Starfire Optical Range Telescope at Kirkland Air Force Base

e3eab728-bbca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Wingst ground station, used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field.
e3eab728-bbca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Wingst Observatory

e4187394-b9b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mercury Magnetometer on Mio (MGF) is an instrument aboard the BepiColombo mission's Mio satellite that measures magnetic fields to study various processes in Mercury’s magnetosphere and the inner-heliosphere, featuring two tri-axial fluxgate magnetometers with a maximum vector rate of 128 Hz.
e4187394-b9b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Mercury Magnetometer

e41e53ce-bbbd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) magnetometer** is a three-axis instrument onboard the BARREL Balloon 2T payload used to measure magnetic field components with high resolution and identify substorm activity and ULF oscillations, crucial for studying electron precipitation modulations. It is specifically designed to function in areas where ground-based magnetometers are not available.
e41e53ce-bbbd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

e4234cd0-b5fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Jupiter magnetic field model on Juno" is a spherical harmonic representation of Jupiter's magnetic field, derived from data collected by the Juno spacecraft during its first nine polar orbits. This model provides a detailed understanding of both the internal and external components of Jupiter's magnetic field, with well-determined coefficients up to degree and order 10, offering unprecedented insights into the planetary dynamo beyond Earth.
e4234cd0-b5fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Jupiter magnetic field model part of Juno

e432a024-bad0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in El Dorado County, California, known as the Rancho Del Sol Observatory.
e432a024-bad0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rancho Del Sol Observatory, United States

e438311e-b6ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: This entity appears to represent a structured reference within the NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) for categorizing and labeling scientific instruments used in space missions, potentially including their associated data products.
e438311e-b6ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: James Webb Telescope

e44db6c0-bb2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The specific magnetometer referenced here has been operational since 1958 and is part of the IUGONET observatory in Kyoto, providing valuable data for geomagnetic research as part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) investigations.
e44db6c0-bb2a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iugonet Observatory

e459ed18-bb94-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kiel Electron Telescope (KET) is an energetic particle instrument part of the COSPIN suite on the Ulysses spacecraft, designed to measure high-energy electrons, protons, and helium particles using advanced detection techniques.
e459ed18-bb94-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kiel Electron Telescope part of COSPIN investigation on Ulysses spacecraft

e45e21de-b84d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Memambetsu Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility in Hokkaido, Japan, operated by the Japan Meteorological Agency since 1957 to monitor and study geomagnetic fields.
e45e21de-b84d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geo Electric Field Sensor at Memambetsu Magnetic Observatory, Japan

e466782a-b965-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mark Evans Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at Illinois Wesleyan University in Bloomington, Illinois. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and education.
e466782a-b965-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mark Evans Observatory

e46e2d60-babc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMN magnetometer network in Cañete, Peru, is a ground-based facility located at Imperial, Province of Cañete, Lima, dedicated to monitoring and studying the Earth's magnetic field. It includes specific instruments such as fluxgate magnetometers for precise measurements.
e46e2d60-babc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer at Canete Station, Peru

e47b80ca-b691-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU Radio Beacon Receiver (GRBR) station at Majuro is an observatory located in the Marshall Islands. It measures ionospheric disturbances related to middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes using a GNU radio beacon receiver, situated near the equator with coordinates 7.07N, 171.27E, and an altitude of 4 meters above mean sea level (MSL).
e47b80ca-b691-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU Radio Beacon Receiver at Majuro Observatory

e4817fd2-bb98-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Carina Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Sobradinho, Federal District, Brazil. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
e4817fd2-bb98-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Carina Observatory, Brazil

e486b834-bc89-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Malina River Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Ravosa-Magredis, Povoletto, Italy. It functions as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
e486b834-bc89-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Malina River Observatory, Italy

e48b6fe6-b7ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Deep Space Network's Goldstone Apple Valley Radio Telescope (GAVRT) is a North American telescope used for radio astronomy observations and deep space communications.
e48b6fe6-b7ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio The Deep Space Network on Goldstone Apple Valley Radio Telescope

e4931d28-b70b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The ULTRA Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Suzhou, China. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to studying the universe and celestial bodies.
e4931d28-b70b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultra Observatory at Suzhou Observatory, China

e494243c-bb8b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1M Optical Photometer** is an instrument used to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm during relativistic electron precipitation events, helping determine the presence of protons and supporting the study of scattering by electromagnetic ion cyclotron (EMIC) waves as a precipitation mechanism.
e494243c-bb8b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

e496ef5c-b8aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Hubble Space Telescope (HST) is a space telescope launched into low Earth orbit in 1990 by NASA and ESA, known for its high-resolution observations in visible, near-ultraviolet, and near-infrared wavelengths. It has been instrumental in astronomical research and remains operational with periodic servicing missions to upgrade its instruments.
e496ef5c-b8aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.4m Hubble Space Telescope

e49ce112-bb77-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Magnetometers at Saint Maur (PSM)** is a historic magnetometer located in Saint Maur and affiliated with the IAGA. It was operational from January 1, 1883 to December 31, 1900 as part of the observatory network under the Kyoto World Data Center for Geomagnetism (WDC-Kyoto).
e49ce112-bb77-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Saint Maur Observatory

e4a55c44-ba36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mardella Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located at Randell Road, Mardella, in the Shire of Serpentine-Jarrahdale, Western Australia. It is situated at coordinates -32.3098 latitude and 115.95533 longitude within the continent of Oceania.
e4a55c44-ba36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mardella Observatory, Australia

e4a815e8-b6ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Antofagasta (ANT) Geomagnetic Observatory, located in Antofagasta, Chile, is a ground-based facility established on May 1, 2003, to monitor geomagnetic activity.
e4a815e8-b6ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Antofagasta Observatory, Chile

e4b8f64a-bb68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SSB/X-2 is a spectrometer onboard the DMSP/F15 satellite, designed to detect and measure the location, intensity, and spectrum of X-rays emitted from Earth's atmosphere. It has been operational since December 12, 1999, as part of the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP).
e4b8f64a-bb68-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma Ray Particle Detector on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program

e4bc94fc-b74a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 1 FPI Suite, Dual Ion Spectrometer (DIS) is an instrument on the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission that measures the velocity-space distribution of ions from 10 eV to 30 keV with a time resolution of 150 ms.
e4bc94fc-b74a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dual Ion Spectrometer part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

e4c4107e-b86c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: DSS-14 is a ground-based observatory known for its astronomical observations and research activities, also referred to as "Value" in certain contexts.
e4c4107e-b86c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: DSS-14 Observatory

e4c4d502-b99f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Astronomical Ring for Access to Spectroscopy (ARAS) is a collaboration between professional and amateur astronomers focused on spectroscopic observations in the optical waveband. It facilitates access to and sharing of spectroscopic data to enhance astronomical research and education.
e4c4d502-b99f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Astronomical Ring for Access to Spectroscopy

e4c58786-b98b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The YGCO Chiyoda Station is an astronomical observatory in Chiyoda, Gunma, Japan, primarily focused on surveying near-Earth asteroids. It is maintained by the Yamaneko Group of Comet Observers and has the Observatory code number 897.
e4c58786-b98b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chiyoda Observatory, Japan

e4c60d54-b9aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ) 1.88m Telescope at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory (OAO) is an optical telescope located in Asia, specifically designed for astronomical research and observations.
e4c60d54-b9aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 1.88m National Astronomical Observatory of Japan Telescope at Okayama Astrophysical Observatory

e4ca7438-bbc7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **New Millennium Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Mozzate, Italy. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
e4ca7438-bbc7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: New Millennium Observatory at Mozzate, Italy

e4d49cc0-b79d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on GOES 12** is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields in space as part of the GOES-12 satellite. It features three-axis fluxgate sensors mounted on a boom, with a range of ±1000 nT and a sensitivity of 0.03 nT, designed for accurate space weather monitoring.
e4d49cc0-b79d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 12

e4d4ac60-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sloutzk Geomagnetic Observatory (SLU), located in Leningrad Oblast, Russia, is a ground-based facility focused on monitoring geomagnetic activity. It includes instruments such as magnetometers and is part of the global network contributing to geophysical research.
e4d4ac60-b7d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sloutzk Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

e4e7dfda-b944-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, and the one described here is located at the observatory in Brandon (BRD).
e4e7dfda-b944-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Brandon Observatory

e4f0e5dc-b63b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Segorbe Observatory is an astronomical facility located in the Segóbriga Park of Segorbe, Castellón, Spain. It operates as a ground-based observatory dedicated to astronomical research and observation.
e4f0e5dc-b63b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Segorbe Observatory, Spain

e4f74262-b607-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Electric Field Instrument: Thermal Ion Imager (EFI/TII)** is an instrument on the SWARM-A satellite that measures ion density, drift velocity, and electric field at the spacecraft's front panel. It consists of a Langmuir Probe and a Thermal Ion Imager and has been operational since December 2, 2013.
e4f74262-b607-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electric Field Instrument: Thermal Ion Imager part of SWARM-A

e4f9e748-ba70-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Observatorio de Serón** is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Serón, Almería, Spain. It provides facilities for observing celestial phenomena and is situated at the Planetario de Serón along the Vía Verde del Valle del Almanzora.
e4f9e748-ba70-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatory at Planetario de Serón-Almería, Spain

e4fd4400-bc2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nancay Decameter Array (NDA) is a scientific instrument used for routine spectral power measurements, operating since September 18, 1990. It is part of the Nancay Radio Telescope observatory and specializes in low-frequency radio astronomy observations.
e4fd4400-bc2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Decameter Array at Nançay Radio Observatory, France

e4ff298e-b97a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Maryland Space Grant Consortium Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Johns Hopkins University - Homewood Campus in Baltimore, Maryland. It is used for ground-based observations and educational purposes.
e4ff298e-b97a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Grant Consortium Observatory, United States

e52395ac-bb33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Space Facilities Control and Test Center (NCUVKZ) is a Ukrainian state institution that manages space flight operations, deep space research, space monitoring, geophysical monitoring, and testing of space technology.
e52395ac-bb33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: National Space Facilities Control and Test Center

e528db66-b59d-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Space Surveillance Telescope (SST) is a ground-based optical telescope located in Exmouth, Western Australia, used by the United States Space Force for tracking and cataloging satellites, near-Earth objects, and space debris.
e528db66-b59d-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.5m Space Surveillance Telescope at Exmouth Observatory, Australia

e5307c74-b9c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pionerskaya Geophysical Observatory was a ground-based facility located on Earth's surface, primarily focusing on geomagnetic measurements. It operated from July 1957 to December 31, 1958, and was situated at an altitude of 2700 meters with coordinates 95.5 longitude and -69.73 latitude.
e5307c74-b9c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pionerskaya Geomagnetic Observatory

e53ee112-b968-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Keyhole Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Villanova Maiardina, San Giorgio Bigarello, Mantua, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility for observing celestial objects and phenomena.
e53ee112-b968-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Keyhole Observatory, Italy

e54a6258-b9f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at Melville Air Force Base (MEV), operational from 1966 to 1972, used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of the IAGA investigation.
e54a6258-b9f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IAGA

e55b07b0-b752-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lightning and Radio Emission Detector (LRD) was an instrument on the Galileo Probe that confirmed the presence of lightning in Jupiter's atmosphere and measured radio frequency noise in its magnetosphere.
e55b07b0-b752-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lightning and Radio Emission Detector on Galileo Spacecraft

e55ed5ca-b7c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Vegaquattro Observatory** (K41) is an astronomical observatory located in Novi Ligure, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
e55ed5ca-b7c0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Vegaquattro Observatory, Italy

e5868318-b7de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Near Infrared Spectrometer (NIRS) on the Hayabusa spacecraft was an instrument designed to analyze the mineral composition and physical characteristics of asteroid 25143 Itokawa's surface by measuring wavelengths from 0.76 to 2.1 microns.
e5868318-b7de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Infrared Spectrometer on Hayabusa

e5987554-b866-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover Mast Camera Right** is a high-resolution imaging system mounted on the rover's Remote Sensing Mast, designed to capture detailed color images of the Martian surface for studying its geology, climate, and atmosphere. It supports scientific investigations by documenting the surroundings and providing contextual data.
e5987554-b866-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Right Mast Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

e59c287a-b627-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Tirunelveli Geomagnetic Observatory (TIR), located in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, India, was a ground-based facility that operated from 1999 to 2014, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements and research.
e59c287a-b627-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tirunelveli Geomagnetic Observatory

e5a23126-bb67-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Woomera Ionosonde** is an instrument used for radar investigation located at the Woomera station in South Australia, which operated from January 1962 to July 1968 and utilized a Union Radio Recorder (URR) Mark II.
e5a23126-bb67-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar on Woomera Observatory, Australia

e5bb2a04-b834-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Viking Lander 2 Spacecraft Labeled Release** was an instrument on the Viking Lander 2 designed to detect microbial life in Martian soil by measuring radioactive gas release from samples treated with nutrient solutions.
e5bb2a04-b834-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Labeled Release on Viking Lander 2

e5bd3dee-b97e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sheltozero Station Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in the Shyoltozerosky District of the Republic of Karelia, Russia. It is operated by Petrozavodsk University and has been active since January 2009.
e5bd3dee-b97e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatory at Sheltozero Station

e5bfc19c-bb20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Multispectral Visible Imaging Camera (MVIC) is a component of the Ralph instrument onboard the New Horizons spacecraft, designed to capture images in both visible and near-infrared wavelengths using seven Charge-Coupled Device detectors (CCDs), with specialized filters for color mapping and high sensitivity.
e5bfc19c-bb20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: [visible and near-infrared] Multispectral Visible Imaging Camera on New Horizons

e5c0ca58-bb19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **White County Observatory** is a ground-based astronomical facility located in West Point, Arkansas, United States. It provides opportunities for observing celestial bodies and conducting astronomical research from its site at latitude 35.23485° N and longitude -91.65017° W (268.34983°).
e5c0ca58-bb19-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: White County Observatory

e5c1f5d8-b923-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Norway House Geomagnetic Observatory (NHO) was a ground-based facility in Canada dedicated to geomagnetic measurements, operational from 1972 to 1974.
e5c1f5d8-b923-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Norway House Geomagnetic Observatory

e5d596d4-b86e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Beersel Hills Observatory is an amateur astronomical observatory located in Beersel, Belgium, established in April 1998 and focused on the study of variable stars and visual double stars.
e5d596d4-b86e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Beersel Hills Observatory, Belgium

e5ea909e-bb24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Thule 1/Dundas Magnetometer is an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields, located at the IAGA observatory in Thule with the identifier THD. It has been operational since January 1933.
e5ea909e-bb24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Thule Observatory

e5f58e80-bb89-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Tokyo's 1.05m Schmidt telescope at Kiso Observatory is an optical telescope located in Asia, specifically designed for observing visible light from celestial objects.
e5f58e80-bb89-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.05m Schmidt Telescope at Kiso Observatory

e5f68fca-b8b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mauritius Geomagnetic Observatory (MRI), located in Triolet, Pamplemousses, Mauritius, is a ground-based facility that operated from 1892 to 1965, primarily focusing on geomagnetic measurements using instruments such as magnetometers.
e5f68fca-b8b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mauritius Geomagnetic Observatory, Mauritius

e5f6b158-b872-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IRAM Plateau de Bure Interferometer is a radio telescope array located in Europe, specifically designed for millimeter wave astronomy.
e5f6b158-b872-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Institute de Radioastronomie Millimetrique Plateau de Bure Interferometer

e605b17e-b946-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **FIELDS2 Time Domain Sampler (TDS)** is a key component of the FIELDS instrument suite onboard the Parker Solar Probe mission. It is designed to collect and process transient wave phenomena from electric and magnetic sensors, with capabilities for high-frequency waveform sampling and precise time synchronization.
e605b17e-b946-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Time Domain Sampler part of Parker Solar Probe Mission

e605cf60-b900-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Almeria Geomagnetic Observatory (ALM) was a ground-based facility located in Almeria, Spain, dedicated to geophysical observations and operated from 1957 to 1991.
e605cf60-b900-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Almeria Geomagnetic Observatory, Spain

e608eae6-bb81-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** TIMMI2 (Thermal Infrared Multi-Mode Instrument 2) is a versatile thermal-infrared instrument operating at the ESO/3.6m Cassegrain telescope, capable of imaging, polarimetry, and long slit spectroscopy in the 4-20 um wavelength range.
e608eae6-bb81-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Thermal Infrared Multi-Mode Instrument 2 on 3.6m Telescope at La Silla Observatory

e618d5f4-bbcd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kodaikanal Solar Observatory’s Solar Tunnel Telescope is an optical telescope located in Asia, specifically designed for solar observations.
e618d5f4-bbcd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Tunnel Telescope at Kodaikanal Solar Observatory

e61c64b2-b777-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The magnetometer at Pilar (PIL), part of the IAGA investigation and WDC Kyoto Observatory since 1905, provides data on Earth's geomagnetic activity.
e61c64b2-b777-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Pilar Observatory

e6225eae-b78f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Collurania Observatory, also known as the Teramo Observatory, is an astronomical observatory located in Teramo, Italy. Founded by Vincenzo Cerulli in 1890, it is operated by the National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF) and focuses on ground-based observations.
e6225eae-b78f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Collurania Observatory at Astronomical Observatory of Abruzzo, Italy

e62b460a-b707-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Imaging Science Subsystem - Narrow Angle for Voyager 2 (ISSNA) is a high-resolution imaging instrument onboard the Voyager 2 spacecraft designed to capture detailed images of planetary bodies and their atmospheres.
e62b460a-b707-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Narrow Angle Camera on Imaging Science Subsystem part of Voyager 2

e62b7856-ba71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer installed at the PENGUIn-4 (PG4) Geophysical Observatory in Antarctica, operational since January 5, 2014, as part of a larger ground-based observatory network.
e62b7856-ba71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at PENGUIn-4 Observatory, Antarctica

e62cc4a0-b5b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CS3-Palmer Divide Station is an astronomical observatory located in San Bernardino County, California. It operates as a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code U82.
e62cc4a0-b5b1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: CS3-Palmer Divide Station at Landers Observatory

e62d7904-bc2d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Macquarie Island Magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at Macquarie Island, part of the IAGA investigation starting from 1911.
e62d7904-bc2d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Macquarie Island Observatory, Antarctica

e6310b92-b9e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetic Field Monitor on GOES 7 is a spinning twin-fluxgate magnetometer designed to measure the orthogonal components of Earth's magnetic field, with a sensitivity of about 0.2 gamma. Since May 1993, it has only provided data for the component parallel to the spin axis (Hp), due to instrument limitations.
e6310b92-b9e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetic Field Monitor on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 7

e632f562-ba09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Chiripa station with the IAGA identifier CRP, operational since January 1984.
e632f562-ba09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Chiripa Observatory

e658ca64-b773-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover Spectrometer and Micro-Imager Suite (SuperCam) is an advanced instrument on the Perseverance rover that uses multiple spectroscopic techniques to analyze Martian materials from a distance, including LIBS, Raman, time-resolved fluorescence, and visible/infrared spectroscopy. It also features a color camera for context imaging and a microphone to study the Mars environment.
e658ca64-b773-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover Spectrometer and Micro-Imager Suite part of Mars 2020

e65c2ff2-b8da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is the Digisonde ionospheric station at Atomic City, Idaho, USA (URSI-code: AC843), which evaluates various characteristics of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere. This ground facility, located in North America, has been operational since January 25, 2012.
e65c2ff2-b8da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde Ionospheric Station at Atomic City, United States

e661d034-bb3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Untermenzing Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Munich, Germany. It is situated at GAMMA Software GmbH on Dyroffstraße and is known for its ground-based observations.
e661d034-bb3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Untermenzing Observatory, Germany

e66245fa-b7b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IPS Toyokawa Station** is an antenna facility located in Toyokawa, Aichi Prefecture, Japan, dedicated to Interplanetary Scintillation (IPS) measurements as part of the IUGONET Observatory.
e66245fa-b7b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Interplanetary Scintillation Antenna Station at Toyokawa, Japan

e6668910-baf7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar X-ray Monitor on GOES 7 is an instrument designed to measure solar X-ray emissions in two wavelength bands, using ion chambers and a lead-lined aluminum collimator.
e6668910-baf7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar X-ray Monitor on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 7

e669fc7c-b8e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The California Institute of Technology Combined Array for Research in Millimeter-Wave Astronomy (CARMA) is a millimeter-wave radio astronomy instrument located at the Owens Valley Radio Observatory (OVRO) in North America. It is used for research in millimeter wavelengths, providing valuable data for astronomical studies.
e669fc7c-b8e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter California Institute of Technology Combined Array for Research in Millimeter-Wave Astronomy and Owens Valley Radio Observatory

e66a2860-ba73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **EMCCD Sodankyla Station** is an observatory in Finland equipped with an EMCCD imager, dedicated to studying pulsating auroras as part of the Pulsating Aurora Project. It is situated at the Sodankylä Geophysical Observatory in Northern Lapland.
e66a2860-ba73-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: EMCCD Imager Station at Sodankylä Geophysical Observatory, Finland

e66ae1d0-b6fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Millwood Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Comfort, Texas, known for its ground-based facilities and contributions to astronomical research.
e66ae1d0-b6fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millwood Observatory, United States

e6780058-ba81-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Institute of Astronomy at Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń is an astronomical observatory and research institute located in Piwnice, Poland, featuring both optical and radio telescopes.
e6780058-ba81-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 32m Radio Telescope at Piwnice Observatory, Poland

e67df1b8-bb10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Dust Impact Plasma Detector (SP-1) on Vega 2 was an instrument designed to detect the electric charges in plasma clouds generated by solid particle impacts, featuring a detection range of 3x10^-14 to 10^-8 C and an estimated mass range of 3x10^-17 to 10^-11 g.
e67df1b8-bb10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dust Impact Plasma Detector on Vega 2

e67f11d6-b7c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The IAGA:DUB Magnetometer was an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields, located in Dublin and operational from 1841 to 1850 as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
e67f11d6-b7c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dublin Observatory

e6829aca-b60f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Comprehensive Plasma Instrumentation (CPI) on GEOTAIL is an instrument suite featuring quadrispherical analyzers designed to comprehensively measure the three-dimensional velocity distribution functions of electrons and positive ions in space plasma, including detailed ion composition analysis.
e6829aca-b60f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Quadrispherical Analyzer part of Comprehensive Plasma Instrumentation investigation on GEOTAIL

e684aff0-b6f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Sterrenwacht Andromeda Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Ellecom, Gelderland, Netherlands. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
e684aff0-b6f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Andromeda Observatory, Netherlands

e68fe748-b5c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Göttingen-2 Magnetometer** is an instrument used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field, operational at Göttingen Observatory from 1832 to 1867 as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
e68fe748-b5c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Göttingen Observatory

e6989764-b77a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Walnut Creek Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Walnut Creek, California, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects.
e6989764-b77a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Walnut Creek Observatory, United States

e6a4967c-b919-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The entity refers to the ground observatory known as DSS-16, which is part of a network of observational facilities.
e6a4967c-b919-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: DSS-16 Observatory

e6b14124-b743-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Toledo that operated from 1947 to 1981 as part of the IAGA investigation for measuring magnetic field variations.
e6b14124-b743-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Toledo Observatory

e6b30b4a-b60c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Castrofilippo Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Azzarola, Castrofilippo, Agrigento, Sicily, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
e6b30b4a-b60c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory at Castrofilippo Observatory, Italy

e6b32dd4-b83f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Northolt Branch Observatories** (NBO) is an astronomical observatory located in London, England. It specializes in collecting follow-up astrometry of near-Earth asteroids and other small Solar System objects.
e6b32dd4-b83f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Northolt Branch Observatory, United Kingdom

e6bb5eb8-b9da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at GLP** is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Guadalupe, Peru, used to measure magnetic fields as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
e6bb5eb8-b9da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum Pan-Pacific Magnetic Network observation network

e6bd8010-b973-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at St. Johns is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields since 1968, contributing to geophysical research as part of the IAGA investigation within the IUGONET Observatory network coordinated by WDC Kyoto.
e6bd8010-b973-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Saint John's Observatory

e6c24f92-bbc5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LCROSS NIR1 was a near-infrared camera on the Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite (LCROSS), designed to capture context imagery of lunar impacts and analyze ejecta properties, including water concentration.
e6c24f92-bbc5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Infrared Camera 1 on Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite

e6cee62c-b6fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The RISH Boundary Layer Radar (BLR) at Shigaraki is an instrument developed by Kyoto University and Mitsubishi Electric Corporation to measure wind velocity in the atmospheric boundary layer, operating at a frequency of 1357.5 MHz with three parabolic antennas directed towards different angles for comprehensive wind component observation.
e6cee62c-b6fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Boundary Layer Radar on RISH Boundary Layer Radar (BLR) instrument at Shigaraki

e6d2b21c-bbaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **SMART/T1** is a solar full-disk chromospheric imaging telescope located at the Kwasan and Hida Observatory, designed to observe the Sun's chromosphere using the H-alpha spectral line. It provides detailed images of the entire solar disk, aiding in studies of solar activity and atmospheric dynamics.
e6d2b21c-bbaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Magnetism and Activity Research Telescope/T1 Imager at Hida Observatory

e6dfbda6-bab8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Solar Orbiter Spacecraft Ephemeris Virtual Instrument** is a platform within the Solar Orbiter mission that provides ephemeris data, detailing the precise positions of the Solar Orbiter spacecraft.
e6dfbda6-bab8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Orbiter Position part of Solar Orbiter

e6e388ca-b6bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electrostatic Analyser, AMBRE (Active Monitor Box of Electrostatic Risks), onboard the JASON-3 spacecraft measures the spacecraft's potential and auroral particle precipitation using two top-hat analyzers for electrons and ions in the energy range of 20 eV–28 keV. It operates from a nearly circular orbit at an altitude of 1,336 km with an inclination of 66°.
e6e388ca-b6bf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Active Monitor Box of Electrostatic Risks on JASON-3 spacecraft

e6e9c860-b724-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Electron Drift Instrument (EDI)** is a scientific device on the MMS 4 spacecraft that measures electric and magnetic fields by tracking the drift of approximately 1 keV electrons. It was activated in March 2015 and is part of the FIELDS Suite investigation led by R. B. Torbert from the University of New Hampshire.
e6e9c860-b724-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Drift Instrument part of MMS 4 Fields Suite

e6ea8ee4-b9b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fluxgate Magnetometer (FGM) on Cluster-2 is an instrument designed to measure magnetic fields in space. It consists of two triaxial magnetometers placed at different locations on the spacecraft's radial booms to minimize magnetic interference, and it operates within multiple ranges to capture detailed magnetic field data.
e6ea8ee4-b9b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of Voyager 1

e6ec5b3e-bb8e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1.52-m spectrographic Cassegrain/Coude reflector is a telescope with a 1.52-meter aperture, located at the European Southern Observatory in La Silla, Chile, operational since July 1968.
e6ec5b3e-bb8e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.52m Telescope at La Silla Observatory, Chile

e6f5196c-b8e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SCATHA Engineering and Wave Experiment (SC2) is an instrument on the Spacecraft Charging At High Altitudes (SCATHA) mission designed to measure ions and electrons with specific energy ranges and temporal resolutions, using electrostatic analyzers and solid-state detectors for both scientific and engineering purposes.
e6f5196c-b8e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument part of Spacecraft Charging At High Altitudes

e6f6fd50-b931-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The PLASTIC (Plasma and Supra-Thermal Ion Composition) investigation on STEREO A is an Energetic Particle Instrument designed to measure the composition, energy spectra, and directional information of ions in the solar wind and locally accelerated particles. It consists of subsystems for entrance, time-of-flight analysis, and electronics, enabling mass spectroscopy through energy vs. time-of-flight tracking.
e6f6fd50-b931-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma and Supra-Thermal Ion Composition Investigation part of STEREO A

e6f78d30-b63c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1.20-m Newtonian reflector is a telescope with a 1.20 m aperture located at the Observatory of Haute-Provence in France, operational since 1943.
e6f78d30-b63c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.20m Telescope at Haute-Provence Observatory, France

e6f9ec8e-b5e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes the North Pole 8, a ground facility located on Earth's surface that operated from January 01, 1959, to December 31, 1962. It includes a magnetometer and is part of an observatory network under IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy).
e6f9ec8e-b5e1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole 8 Observatory, Antarctica

e70816f0-b90c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Marsfield Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Marsfield, Sydney, Australia, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial objects.
e70816f0-b90c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Marsfield Observatory, Australia

e70f1fc8-b7cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Gettysburg College Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Gettysburg College in Pennsylvania, United States.
e70f1fc8-b7cb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gettysburg College Observatory, United States

e718e2be-b5f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Tiksi Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG starting from 2011, used for measuring magnetic field variations.
e718e2be-b5f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tiksi Geophysical Observatory

e71fc7fe-b9c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2 (RENU2)** was a NASA sounding rocket mission launched on December 13, 2015, to study the thermosphere in the Earth's dayside cusp region.
e71fc7fe-b9c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2 part of NASA Sounding Rocket Mission

e729134e-b9a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Cuzco observatory in Kyoto, operational from January 1965 to December 31st, 1966, used for geomagnetic field measurements as part of the IAGA investigation.
e729134e-b9a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cuzco

e72cc3b8-b7f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Photometric Camera** is a mosaic CCD instrument used for large-scale astronomical surveys, featuring 30 photometric and 24 astrometric detectors arranged to capture detailed imaging data over wide sky stripes.
e72cc3b8-b7f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sloan Digital Sky Survey Photometric Camera

e7341f82-b89b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ny-Ålesund Geophysical Observatory is a ground facility located in Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard, Norway that specializes in geophysical measurements, including magnetometer readings.
e7341f82-b89b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ny-Ålesund Geophysical Observatory

e7377784-b5b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Thermosphere-Ionosphere-Mesosphere Energetics and Dynamics (TIMED) mission is an Earth observation satellite designed to study the physical and chemical processes in the mesosphere, lower thermosphere, and ionosphere. Launched on December 7, 2001, TIMED aims to understand this hard-to-access atmospheric region by collecting data over a solar cycle.
e7377784-b5b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Thermosphere Ionosphere Mesosphere Energetics and Dynamics on TIMED

e73c8e0e-b5b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Australian National University (ANU) 3.9m Anglo-Australian Telescope (AAT) is located at Siding Spring Observatory in Australia, with an aperture of 3.9 meters and operates in the optical wavelength band.
e73c8e0e-b5b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.9m Anglo-Australian Telescope at Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

e74524ca-b81a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Burleith Observatory (MPC code I13) is an astronomical observatory located in Washington D.C., USA. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
e74524ca-b81a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Burleith Observatory, United States

e74a976e-ba24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The AGM Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Marrakech, Morocco. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
e74a976e-ba24-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Marrakech Observatory, Morocco

e74fb212-b650-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Lilienthal Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Lilienthal, Lower Saxony, Germany. It is a ground-based facility used for sky observations and research.
e74fb212-b650-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lilienthal Observatory, Germany

e7635112-b71a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Boyeros Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Wajay, Boyeros, Havana, Cuba. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
e7635112-b71a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Boyeros Observatory, Cuba

e769327a-b78e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Linden Observatory Complex is a heritage-listed former observatory and current residence, museum, education facility, and meeting venue located in Linden, New South Wales, Australia. It was built by Ken Beames between 1938 and 1948 and is known for its historical significance in optical precision manufacturing.
e769327a-b78e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Linden Observatory Complex

e76c57a8-b747-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, specifically the Earth's magnetic field in this context. The magnetometer at San Fernando (SFS) has been operational since January 1, 1880, and is part of the IUGONET observatory network managed by WDC Kyoto.
e76c57a8-b747-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at San Fernando Observatory

e76ec8b8-b5a2-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: This entity represents a magnetometer located at the Mirny station, part of the IAGA investigation, which started operating on July 1, 1956.
e76ec8b8-b5a2-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mirny Observatory, Antarctica

e77edfd8-b614-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Berlin Observatory, also known as the Berliner Sternwarte, was a prominent astronomical institution in Germany, established in the 18th century and operating in various locations around Berlin until its closure in 1913.
e77edfd8-b614-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Berlin Observatory, Germany

e79ba532-b916-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Cambridge Optical Aperture Synthesis Telescope (COAST) is an optical telescope located at the Mullard Radio Astronomy Observatory in Europe, designed for aperture synthesis observations.
e79ba532-b916-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical University of Cambridge Optical Aperture Synthesis Telescope at Mullard Radio Astronomy Observatory

e79c6e90-b7cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 3D Ion Distribution (SKA-1) (EU-1) on Interball Tail Probe is a fast plasma analyzer designed to provide rapid three-dimensional measurements of the ion distribution function, utilizing two detectors with narrow-angle analyzers and electrostatic scanners.
e79c6e90-b7cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Infrared Camera and Multi-Object Spectrometer on Hubble Space Telescope

e7a5622a-b709-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IGPP-LANL Crete Fluxgate Magnetometer** is a magnetometer located at the IGPP-LANL station in Crete, designed to measure magnetic field variations as part of geophysical and space weather investigations.
e7a5622a-b709-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics - Los Alamos National Laboratory Observatory, Crete

e7bcb24c-ba54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Marshall Grazing Incidence X-ray Spectrometer is a sounding rocket designed for studying X-ray emissions in space, enhancing our understanding of celestial phenomena through advanced spectroscopy.
e7bcb24c-ba54-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Marshall Grazing Incidence X-ray Spectrometer on Sounding Rocket

e7c7cd9c-b835-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the IAGA station identified as KEM, part of the IUGONET Observatory and WDC Kyoto network, used for measuring magnetic fields since 1973.
e7c7cd9c-b835-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Kem Observatory

e7d25eca-b708-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1G Optical Photometer is an instrument designed to detect visible light at wavelengths near 486.1 nm during relativistic electron precipitation events, aiming to determine the presence of protons accompanying these electrons and support the hypothesis that EMIC waves are involved in the precipitation mechanism.
e7d25eca-b708-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible Light Photometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

e7dcb8a8-b6ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Koror Geomagnetic Observatory (KOR)** is a ground-based facility located in Koror, Palau, that operated from 1957 to 1966, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
e7dcb8a8-b6ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Koror Geomagnetic Observatory

e7efb486-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lohrmann Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Dresden, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility and is part of the broader Lohrmann-Observatorium network.
e7efb486-bac6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lohrmann Observatory, Germany

e7fa93ee-b9e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1B Data Processing Unit** is a versatile instrument controller board used for the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) project, designed to acquire data from various sensors and manage communication through a backplane and memory interface.
e7fa93ee-b9e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses part of BARREL Observatory

e8073f0e-ba38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Nordkapp Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Skarsvågveien, Norway, dedicated to geophysical research and equipped with instruments such as magnetometers.
e8073f0e-ba38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nordkapp Geophysical Observatory, Norway

e814799a-b7e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA-identified SSO station in Simosato, operational from 1954 to 1978, used for ground magnetic field measurements.
e814799a-b7e9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at IUGONET Observatory

e8226f3c-b9fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EISCAT Tromsø VHF radar is an incoherent scatter radar system operating in the VHF band (~224 MHz) located in Tromsø, Norway. It features a 120 m by 40 m parabolic cylinder antenna and is used for atmospheric and ionospheric research, operated by the EISCAT Scientific Association.
e8226f3c-b9fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: VHF Radar on EISCAT Observatory, Norway

e838fecc-ba10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Amundsen Bay (AMB) is an automated magnetometer station located near Syowa Station in Antarctica, part of a network for monitoring magnetic fields on Earth's surface.
e838fecc-ba10-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate at Amundsen Bay, Antarctica

e83a2a08-bb56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Baugy Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Baugy, France. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with ID 237 and is situated at coordinates 47.08352° N, 2.7333° E.
e83a2a08-bb56-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Baugy Observatory, France

e83b49ba-b606-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Genesis** was a NASA sample-return probe launched in 2001 to collect solar wind particles and return them to Earth for analysis, but its sample return capsule crash-landed in Utah in 2004 due to a parachute failure.
e83b49ba-b606-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sample Collection and Return Capsule part of Genesis

e841f002-b59e-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Real Instituto y Observatorio de la Armada (Royal Institute and Observatory of the Spanish Navy) is an astronomical observatory and scientific institute of the Spanish Navy located in San Fernando, Cádiz, Spain.
e841f002-b59e-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Real Instituto y Observatorio de la Armada, Spain

e845bbc4-b6e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rokycany Observatory, located in the Czech Republic, is an astronomical observatory dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
e845bbc4-b6e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rokycany Observatory, Czechia

e8498a80-b6a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tortugas Mountain Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Doña Ana County near Las Cruces, New Mexico. It is situated at an approximate latitude of 32.29307 and longitude of -106.80468 (or 253.30194 in positive degrees).
e8498a80-b6a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tortugas Mountain Observatory, United States

e85c2b34-b12f-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tamworth Observatory, located in East Tamworth, Australia, is an astronomical observatory known for its ground-based observations and contributions to astronomy.
e85c2b34-b12f-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Tamworth Observatory, Australia

e8615fa2-ba42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Energetic Particles, MSU-TASPD" is a particle detector instrument used on the Soviet Zond 3 mission to measure energetic (MeV) particles in the interplanetary medium. This experiment was developed by the Theoretical and Applied Space Physics Division of Moscow State University's Skobeltsyn Institute of Nuclear Physics, specifically focusing on protons above 30 MeV during its early missions.
e8615fa2-ba42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Particle Detector part of Zond 3

e86a81ac-b75b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Amatsia Geomagnetic Observatory (AMT) is a ground-based facility located in Lachish Regional Council, Israel, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity. It has been operational since November 1979 and is part of the IAGA observatory network.
e86a81ac-b75b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Amatsia Geomagnetic Observatory, Israel

e86c03c6-b8b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DMSP (Defense Meteorological Satellite Program) series is a collection of military imaging spacecraft that, besides capturing visible light images, measure various environmental parameters such as downward particle fluxes, magnetic fields, electron densities, and ion drifts while orbiting the Earth in sun-synchronous polar orbits at an altitude of 830 km.
e86c03c6-b8b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetic Field and Particle Measurement Instrument on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program Series

e8724784-ba4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer from the ISEE project located in Nyrola, used to measure 3-D vector geomagnetic field variations with a sampling rate of 64 Hz.
e8724784-ba4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Induction Magnetometer part of International Sun Earth Explorer

e8843220-b6dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AGO P5 Ground Observatory, located on Earth's surface at an altitude of 3519 meters and coordinates -77.23 latitude and 123.51 longitude, is a ground facility that is part of the ICESTAR observatory network.
e8843220-b6dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: AGO P5 Observatory, Antarctica

e88dc68e-bc0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Chuguevskaya Station**: An astronomical observatory located in Kharkiv, Ukraine, featuring a 0.7-meter telescope and situated at coordinates approximately 49.9923° N, 36.2310° E.
e88dc68e-bc0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chuguevskaya Observatory, Ukraine

e88e2418-b765-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1.02-m Cassegrain reflector is a telescope located at the Mount Lemmon Observatory in Arizona, United States, operational since 1970 and part of NASA's Planetary Data System context facilities.
e88e2418-b765-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.02m Telescope at Mount Lemmon Observatory, United States

e88eeb80-b77b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **magnetometer** is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific entity described here is a fluxgate magnetometer located at Learmonth, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network under the IUGONET observatory.
e88eeb80-b77b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of 210 Magnetic Meridian magnetometer network

e8a59178-b96a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Anunaki Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Rivas-Vaciamadrid, Spain, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial bodies.
e8a59178-b96a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Anunaki Observatory, Spain

e8b440fa-bc4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Underwood Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Hubbardston, Massachusetts. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 914 and situated at coordinates 42.5311° N, 71.8608° W.
e8b440fa-bc4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Underwood Observatory, United States

e8b8ffc6-ba26-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wanniassa Observatory (E13) is an astronomical facility located in Gibb Place, Wanniassa, Australian Capital Territory, Australia. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting various astronomical studies and observations.
e8b8ffc6-ba26-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wanniassa Observatory

e8ba8be4-b6f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Geotail Low Energy Particle experiment (LEP) is an instrument onboard the Geotail spacecraft designed to measure plasma and energetic electrons and ions in the terrestrial magnetosphere and interplanetary medium using three sensor units: LEP-EA, LEP-SW, and LEP-MS.
e8ba8be4-b6f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer part of Geotail mission

e8ba9d0c-b744-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Inuvik Neutron Monitor (IAGA: INK) is a ground-based facility located in Inuvik, Canada, part of the THEMIS observatory network. It operates as a neutron monitor to study cosmic rays and has been active since August 13, 2005.
e8ba9d0c-b744-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutron Monitor at Inuvik Observatory, Canada

e8c528a6-bab6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Bétera Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bétera, Valencia, Spain. It is a ground-based facility used for stargazing and other astronomical observations.
e8c528a6-bab6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Betera Observatory, Spain

e8cafb7a-b906-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Northolt Branch Observatory 3 is an astronomical observatory located in Blandford Forum, England, dedicated to ground-based observations.
e8cafb7a-b906-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Northolt Branch Observatory at Blandford Forum, United Kingdom

e8cc4620-b97d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Dunhuang Portable Wind Tunnel** is a gasoline-powered, blower-style wind tunnel with open circulation, featuring an overall length of approximately 12.9 meters and a working section measuring 8.4 meters in length by 0.6 meters in width and height.
e8cc4620-b97d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dunhuang Portable Wind Tunnel

e8cc58de-ba60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Bjørnøya Geomagnetic Observatory (BJN) is a ground-based facility located in Herwighamna, Svalbard, Norway, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity. It has been operational since December 30, 2006, and includes instruments such as the IUGONET magnetometer provided by the WDC Kyoto.
e8cc58de-ba60-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Bjornoya Geomagnetic Observatory, Norway

e8d0b9b4-b8c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hereford Arizona Observatory (HAO) is an astronomical observatory located in Hereford, Arizona, owned and operated by amateur astronomer Bruce L. Gary.
e8d0b9b4-b8c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hereford Arizona Observatory, United States

e8d5f3be-b5a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at Minsk (MNK) is an instrument used to measure the magnetic field of the Earth, located in Minsk and part of the IUGONET observatory network managed by WDC Kyoto.
e8d5f3be-b5a9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Minsk Observatory

e8d6ba02-b5ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Solar Observatory's Global Oscillation Network Group (GONG) is a ground-based optical observatory located on Earth, dedicated to the continuous monitoring and study of solar oscillations.
e8d6ba02-b5ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical National Solar Observatory Global Oscillation Network Group

e8d8d338-b840-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hong Kong Space Museum is an astronomy and space science museum located in Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, known for its distinctive hemispherical shape housing a planetarium.
e8d8d338-b840-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stanley Ho Space Theatre at Hong Kong Space Museum, China

e8e0900c-bacd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is a magnetometer located at the MSK station in Moscow, operational from January 1, 1880, to December 31, 1888, as part of the IAGA investigation.
e8e0900c-bacd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Moscow Observatory
