e8e4beba-b7b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Karavia Observatory (IAGA: KVA) was a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Lubumbashi, Democratic Republic of the Congo. It operated from January 1, 1958, to December 31, 1961.
e8e4beba-b7b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Karavia Observatory, Democratic Republic of the Congo

e8e5fb02-b733-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The United States Naval Academy (USNA) is a federal service academy in Annapolis, Maryland, established in 1845 to educate midshipmen for service in the officer corps of the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps.
e8e5fb02-b733-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bancroft Hall Observatory at United States Naval Academy, United States

e8e64762-b7a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Yamamoto Observatory (also known as Yamamoto) is an astronomical observatory located in Niinuma, Soma, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observation.
e8e64762-b7a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yamamoto Observatory, Japan

e8ea8700-b7d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NIPR-LPM (NIPR-type Low Power Magnetometer) at Innhovde, Antarctica, is a fluxgate magnetometer designed for automated network observations with low power consumption and near-real-time data transmission via the Iridium satellite system.
e8ea8700-b7d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: NIPR Low Power Magnetometer at Innhovde Observatory, Antarctica

e9054ff0-b98d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Weston Geomagnetic Observatory (WES), located in Massachusetts, USA, operated from 1960 to 1968 and was part of the IAGA network, focusing on geomagnetic measurements.
e9054ff0-b98d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Weston Geomagnetic Observatory

e907242e-b69a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plasma Wave Receiver for Voyager 2 is an instrument designed to study plasma waves in the solar wind and planetary magnetospheres, providing insights into various space environments. It was a part of the Voyager 2 spacecraft's scientific payload.
e907242e-b69a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Wave Receiver on Voyager 2

e9083b68-bbac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Highland Road Park Observatory** (Baton Rouge Observatory) is an astronomical observatory in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, operated jointly by Louisiana State University's astronomy department, the Baton Rouge Astronomical Society, and The Recreation & Park Commission for the Parish of East Baton Rouge.
e9083b68-bbac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Highland Road Park Observatory, United States

e909acd6-b60d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** La Corte Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Antigua, Las Palmas, on the Canary Islands, Spain. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to studying and observing celestial bodies and phenomena.
e909acd6-b60d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: La Corte Observatory, Spain

e90bf1c8-b6d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** STEREO-B was one of two spacecraft in NASA's Solar-Terrestrial Relations Observatory (STEREO) mission, designed to study coronal mass ejections and their effects on interplanetary space and Earth's geomagnetic environment from a heliocentric orbit.
e90bf1c8-b6d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar-Terrestrial Relations Observatory

e90c626e-b937-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The UKS Wave Measurements spectrometer, part of the CDPP-AMDA AMPTE UKS observatory, features an electric dipole antenna and a magnetic coil to measure both electric (up to 2 MHz) and magnetic (up to kHz) wave field components. It includes a stepped-frequency analyzer and discrete filters for signal processing, along with a correlator for high-resolution frequency studies.
e90c626e-b937-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spectrometer part of UKS Wave Measurements

e918b798-b82f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Polarimetric and Helioseismic Imager (PHI) is a solar instrument onboard the Solar Orbiter mission designed to measure magnetic fields and line-of-sight velocity in the Sun's photosphere, helping to understand the links between the solar surface and its outer atmosphere.
e918b798-b82f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Polarimetric and Helioseismic Imager part of Solar Orbiter

e926a8a6-bb1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the Ionospheric Station at Gibilmanna, Italy (URSI-code: GM037), which is part of the ISWI Observatory - GIRO. This advanced ionosonde evaluates various characteristics of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere and is located in Isnello, Palermo, Sicily, Italy.
e926a8a6-bb1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Ionospheric Station at Gibilmanna, Italy

e9339972-baf6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electron Drift Instrument (EDI) on the Cluster-1 spacecraft measures the drift of test electrons to determine electric and magnetic field properties in space. It uses electron guns and detectors to emit and track electron beams, providing data on field strengths and gradients.
e9339972-baf6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Drift Instrument on Cluster-1

e9378d44-ba1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Keck I Long-Wavelength Spectrometer (LWS) is a mid-infrared imaging spectrometer at the Keck I telescope, offering high-resolution spectroscopy and imaging capabilities across the 3-25 micron range.
e9378d44-ba1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Long-Wavelength Spectrometer on 10m Keck I Telescope at W. M. Keck Observatory

e93b6778-b953-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The DSS-24 is a beam waveguide (BWG) antenna located at the Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex in California, known for its innovative design that places sensitive electronic equipment underground for easier maintenance and improved performance.
e93b6778-b953-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m DSS-24 Radio Telescope part of Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex, United States

e93d27da-b5f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Mercury Dual Imaging System Wide Angle Camera (MDIS-WAC) is an instrument on the MESSENGER spacecraft designed to capture wide-angle images of Mercury, with a primary objective of providing global stereo imaging and high-resolution targeted coverage of the planet's surface.
e93d27da-b5f6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mercury Dual Imaging System Wide Angle Camera on Mercury Surface, Space Environment, and Geochemistry Ranging

e93e765a-bb26-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer, specifically the PENGUIn-3 Magnetometer, is a scientific instrument used to measure magnetic fields and is part of the Antarctic Network's PENGUIn-3 Geophysical Observatory, operational since January 5, 2013.
e93e765a-bb26-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at PENGUIn-3 Geophysical Observatory, Antarctica

e94330c6-bb2d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1R Engineering Data Interface** is an instrument component of the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) mission, responsible for converting analog measurements of temperatures, voltages, and currents into digital data with high precision.
e94330c6-bb2d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

e94c8b08-ba74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Haleakala-LCO Clamshell #3 is an astronomical observatory located at the Haleakala Observatory in Maui County, Hawaii, United States. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID T03 and is situated on Earth with specific geographical coordinates.
e94c8b08-ba74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Haleakala-LCO Clamshell #3 at Haleakala Observatory, United States

e94e1b2a-ba57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The "Lunar Trailblazer" is a NASA SIMPLEX mission designed to map the mineralogy of the lunar surface using high-resolution near-infrared spectral images and thermal infrared data, focusing on all latitudes including Permanently Shadowed Regions.
e94e1b2a-ba57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High-resolution Volatiles and Minerals Moon Mapper and Lunar Thermal Mapper part of Lunar Trailblazer Orbiter

e94fb370-bb30-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at DES is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania, designed to measure the Earth's magnetic field as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
e94fb370-bb30-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MAGDAS observation network

e94fe2ee-b646-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: Akou Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Ako, Hyogo Prefecture, Japan. It is designated as a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID 871.
e94fe2ee-b646-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Akou Observatory, Japan

e95ae6b2-ba01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Radio Science Subsystem (RSS) for NEAR Shoemaker was an instrument suite onboard the NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft used to determine the mass, bulk density, and inner structure of asteroids like (433) Eros through analysis of gravity fields and communication exchanges with the Deep Space Network.
e95ae6b2-ba01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Subsystem on Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous Spacecraft

e962a94e-bbcb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NSF/NASA/US Department of Energy Millimeter Anisotropy eXperiment Imaging Array (MAXIMA) is a balloon-borne telescope designed to measure the cosmic microwave background radiation in the millimeter waveband. It aims to study the anisotropies in the early universe, providing insights into its structure and evolution.
e962a94e-bbcb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Millimeter NSF/NASA/US Department of Energy Millimeter Anisotropy Experiment Imaging Array (MAXIMA) Balloon

e974fdca-b6ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Armenian Academy of Sciences 2.6m Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Byurakan Astrophysical Observatory in Asia, known for its contributions to astrophysical research.
e974fdca-b6ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.6m Telescope at Byurakan Astrophysical Observatory

e9760910-ba51-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Arecibo Planetary Radar Transmitter** was a powerful radar system at the Arecibo Observatory, capable of transmitting high-power signals for studying planets and other celestial bodies. It had an output power of up to 1 MW continuous at 2380 MHz with a peak Effective Isotropic Radiated Power (EIRP) of approximately 20 TW when using the Arecibo Telescope.
e9760910-ba51-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 305m Arecibo Telescope

e976595a-ba07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) All-Sky Imager at Athabasca, Canada is a multi-wavelength instrument designed to study the dynamics of the upper atmosphere by observing nocturnal airglow emissions. It was developed by Nagoya University's Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research and operates as part of the ISEE Observatory network.
e976595a-ba07-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Multi-wavelength All-Sky Imager part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers at IUGONET Observatory

e982b7de-b680-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometer at Kotzebue (KOT) has been operational since January 1, 1958, as part of the IAGA investigation under the IUGONET Observatory network managed by WDC Kyoto.
e982b7de-b680-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kotzebue Observatory

e984d282-b5ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The A. Volta Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Lanzo d'Intelvi, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observation.
e984d282-b5ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Volta Observatory, Italy

e99025a6-bb06-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Equator-S**: A satellite operational between 1997 and 1998, part of the International Solar-Terrestrial Physics (ISTP) program, designed to provide high-resolution plasma, magnetic, and electric field measurements in key regions of Earth's magnetosphere.
e99025a6-bb06-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Equator-S part of International Solar-Terrestrial Physics program

e999f074-bb63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Thule-3/Qanaq** observatory is a ground facility located in Thule, Greenland, primarily equipped with a magnetometer for geophysical research. It has been operational since January 1, 1955 and is part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
e999f074-bb63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Qanaq Observatory, Greenland

e99b1e64-bb6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Terminated Folded Dipole and Tunable Wideband Receiver (TFD-TWB) system** at the AJ4CO Radio Astronomy Observatory in High Springs, Florida, is a specialized instrument featuring a 2 MHz bandwidth dual polarization antenna array operating from 17 to 33 MHz with simultaneous RCP and LCP capabilities.
e99b1e64-bb6c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Terminated Folded Dipole and Tunable Wideband Receiver at AJ4CO Radio Astronomy Observatory, High Springs, Florida

e9a94310-bb3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Low-Energy Proton and Electron Differential Energy Analyzer (LEPEDEA) is a particle spectrometer that uses two electrostatic analyzers to measure protons and electrons simultaneously, with additional detection capabilities for higher energy particles via a GM tube. It was employed on the Hawkeye 1 spacecraft to study angular distributions and energies of these particles.
e9a94310-bb3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low-Energy Proton and Electron Differential Energy Analyzer on Hawkeye 1

e9ab7e0c-bb72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Akebono (EXOS-D)** is a Japanese research satellite launched in 1989 to study aurora and Earth's magnetosphere environment, particularly focusing on the acceleration processes of auroral particles.
e9ab7e0c-bb72-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Aurora Observation Satellite part of EXOS program

e9afc970-bb00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, and the one located in Crozet (CZT) is part of the IUGONET observatory network operated by WDC Kyoto.
e9afc970-bb00-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Crozet Observatory, Antarctica

e9bb0f7a-bb5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NAE observatory is a virtual facility that aggregates data from various ground magnetometers to create an index for the near conjugate auroral electrojet, complementing the SAE index. It operates with contributions from multiple stations and arrays such as CARISMA and DTU, focusing on periods when complete datasets are available.
e9bb0f7a-bb5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Conjugate Northern Auroral Electrojet Index at NAE Observatory

e9f3f670-bcab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity represents an astronomical imaging instrument located at Mount Lemmon Observatory. It is a 1m54 telescope equipped with an Imager Labs 4K CCD, utilizing white light and featuring a scroll shutter, identified by the label SI_600-386.
e9f3f670-bcab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager Labs 4K CCD on Mount Lemmon Observatory 1.54m Telescope

e9f6b1a0-bb05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ruhr University Bochum and Catholic University of the North (UCN) 0.15m Robotic Bochum Twin Telescopes (VYSOS-6), located at the Cerro Armazones Observatory in South America, are a pair of optical telescopes used for astronomical observations.
e9f6b1a0-bb05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical The Ruhr University Bochum and Catholic University of the North 0.15m Robotic Bochum Twin Telescopes at Cerro Armazones Observatory

e9f77c7e-b71e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The G. Pascoli Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Castelvecchio Pascoli, Barga, Italy, that operated until June 2023. It was a ground-based facility dedicated to studying celestial bodies and phenomena.
e9f77c7e-b71e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: G. Pascoli Observatory, Italy

ea15eac8-b8c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Nordkapp Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAGs investigation since September 28, 2007.
ea15eac8-b8c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nordkapp Observatory

ea165e06-ba0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MINERVA-II2 Rover-2, also known as ULULA (University-made Landing Unit for Locomotion on Asteroid), is a small robotic rover designed to explore efficient moving mechanisms by hopping on the asteroid Ryugu, featuring various actuators and sensors for navigation and data collection.
ea165e06-ba0b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rover-2 ULULA part of Hayabusa

ea211aa4-b87f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The La Paz geophysical observatory was a ground-based facility located in La Paz, Bolivia, operating from 1974 to 1976 for the purpose of measuring and recording geomagnetic data.
ea211aa4-b87f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at La Paz Geomagnetic Observatory, Bolivia

ea2bc822-ba2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA/US Department of Energy Fermi Gamma-Ray Space Telescope (FGST) is an orbiting observatory designed to detect high-energy gamma rays, providing insights into some of the most energetic phenomena in the universe. It was formerly known as the Gamma-Ray Large Area Space Telescope (GLAST).
ea2bc822-ba2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma-ray NASA/US Department of Energy Fermi Gamma-Ray Space Telescope

ea2f3568-b608-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2.29-m Bok Telescope, operational since September 1969 and located at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona, is a Ritchey-Chretien reflector telescope designed by Boller & Chivens.
ea2f3568-b608-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.3m Bok Telescope at Kitt Peak Observatory, United States

ea47be7a-bb36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Longa Vista Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Bragança Paulista, São Paulo, Brazil. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
ea47be7a-bb36-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Longa Vista Observatory, Brazil

ea47c9f6-bb09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 1U was a component of the multi-balloon investigation aimed at studying relativistic electron precipitation from Earth's radiation belts. Launched on January 26, 2013, it operated in the stratosphere until February 9, 2013, as part of NASA’s Living with a Star program to complement measurements from the Van Allen Probes spacecraft.
ea47c9f6-bb09-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star, Geospace Mission of Opportunity

ea523152-b7a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Gelania Geomagnetic Observatory (GEL) is a ground-based facility located in Novaya Zemlya Urban Okrug, Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia, primarily focused on geomagnetic measurements.
ea523152-b7a3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Gelania Geomagnetic Observatory

ea59b49a-bb40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Las Mesas geophysical observatory was a ground-based facility located in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain, operational from 1959 to 1992. It was part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network and housed instruments like magnetometers for geophysical measurements.
ea59b49a-bb40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Las Mesas Observatory, Spain

ea639a58-ba20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Low Altitude Plasma Instrument (LAPI) on Dynamics Explorer 2 was an instrument designed to measure the velocity and pitch angle distributions of positive ions and electrons in the Earth's magnetosphere, with energies ranging from 5 eV to 32 keV. It utilized an array of electrostatic analyzers and Geiger-Mueller counters to study various plasma phenomena and dynamics at high altitudes.
ea639a58-ba20-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyser part of Low Altitude Plasma Investigation on Dynamics Explorer 2

ea666244-bba9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Digitized Sky Survey (DSS) is a digitized compilation of photographic astronomical surveys conducted by the Space Telescope Science Institute between 1983 and 2006. It provides a comprehensive digital map of the night sky based on data collected from Earth, particularly at La Silla Observatory in Chile, which is part of the European Southern Observatory.
ea666244-bba9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digitized Sky Survey at La Silla Observatory, Chile

ea6b6ec8-b7ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **SCATHA Engineering and Wave Experiment (SC1)** is an instrument on the SCATHA spacecraft designed to study spacecraft charging at high altitudes, primarily focusing on very low frequency (VLF) wave experiments using a combination of electric field receivers and magnetic loop antennas.
ea6b6ec8-b7ae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Antenna part of Spacecraft Charging At High Altitudes

ea6f563e-b1b7-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Eskimo Point Geomagnetic Observatory (EKP), located in Arviat, Nunavut, Canada, is a ground facility dedicated to geomagnetic measurements. It operated from January 1, 1974, to December 31, 1976, and was part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) network.
ea6f563e-b1b7-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Eskimo Point Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

ea71851e-bbd8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Numto Geomagnetic Observatory (NMT) was a ground-based facility in Russia that operated from 1974 to 1978, focused on geomagnetic measurements.
ea71851e-bbd8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Numto Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

ea8686dc-b613-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Magnetometer used for geomagnetic observations in Onagawa, specifically a fluxgate type operated by Tohoku University as part of the IUGONET Observatory.
ea8686dc-b613-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Tohoku University Observatory

ea96d936-bb7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at ZYK is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed at Zyryanka, Russia, designed to measure magnetic fields as part of the IUGONET observatory network.
ea96d936-bb7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometer Network

ea9712a4-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Pinto Valley Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in San Bernardino County, California, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility with the MPC code G46.
ea9712a4-b802-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Pinto Valley Observatory, United States

ea9ffad6-bb59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The "Magnetometers at Sudbury (SUB)" refers to instruments located in Sudbury that measure the Earth's magnetic field, as part of the IUGONET observatory network managed by WDC Kyoto.
ea9ffad6-bb59-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Sudbury

eaa68ee0-b9d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The GSFC Magnetometer is a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer developed by the Goddard Space Flight Center, mounted on a boom of the Explorer 35 spacecraft. It measures magnetic field fluctuations with dual ranges and high precision, operating from launch until June 24, 1973, despite a mechanical failure in May 1969.
eaa68ee0-b9d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Explorer 35

eaa6fad4-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mérignac Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Mérignac, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
eaa6fad4-b79e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mérignac Observatory, France

eab6a26c-ba7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Sencelles Observatory (K14) is an astronomical observatory located in Sencelles, on the Balearic Islands of Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility with an MPC ID of K14.
eab6a26c-ba7e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio de Sencelles, Spain

eabb5fb0-bc62-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 2 Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer (HPCA) is a particle detector launched in March 2015 as part of the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission. It uses electrostatic optics and time-of-flight analysis to measure ion fluxes and composition in the Earth's magnetosphere, particularly in regions of magnetic reconnection.
eabb5fb0-bc62-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer part of MMS 2

eac44b86-b675-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ultraviolet Nitric-Oxide Experiment (UVNO) on the AE-D satellite utilized a two-channel Ebert-Fastie spectrometer to measure nitric oxide airglow in the Earth's atmosphere, providing altitude profiles of nitric oxide density by detecting resonance fluorescence of sunlight.
eac44b86-b675-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Spectrometer part of Ultraviolet Nitric-Oxide Experiment on AE-D

eac6cee0-baaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Goodman High Throughput Spectrograph (GTHS) is an imaging spectrograph developed at the University of North Carolina, designed for both high-quality imaging and versatile spectroscopy, with capabilities ranging from UV to 850nm wavelengths. It can operate in longslit and multi-slit modes for spectroscopic observations, as well as provide a wide field of view in imaging mode.
eac6cee0-baaa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Goodman High Throughput Spectrograph on SOAR 4.1m Telescope

ead00b60-b7e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2W magnetometer is a three-axis instrument designed to measure magnetic field components with high resolution, primarily used for identifying substorm activity and ULF oscillations in regions where ground-based magnetometers are unavailable.
ead00b60-b7e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

eada0d12-b71b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IRIDIUM Magnetometer** is an instrument onboard the IRIDIUM series of spacecraft, designed to collect data relevant to studying Birkeland currents—magnetic field-aligned currents at auroral latitudes.
eada0d12-b71b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IRIDIUM Mission

eadf7a2a-b902-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS)** is an ultraviolet imaging spectrometer aboard the Hubble Space Telescope, designed to cover wavelengths from 115 to 1030 nm and featuring multiple detectors with different fields of view.
eadf7a2a-b902-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph on Hubble Space Telescope

eaf3eeec-b74f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ole Rømer Observatory** is an astronomical observatory and museum located in Aarhus, Denmark. Operated by Aarhus University, it serves as both a research facility for astronomy and physics students and a public educational center offering guided tours and lectures.
eaf3eeec-b74f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ole Rømer Observatory, Denmark

eaf974bc-b730-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Yoneyama Observatory, operated by Tohoku University, is a ground-based facility in Miyagi, Japan, specializing in the observation of decameter radio waves.
eaf974bc-b730-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Decameter radio wave Yoneyama Observatory, Japan

eb0929fc-bb1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Observatoire Solaire de Paris à Meudon" (OBSPM) is a ground-based observatory located on Earth's surface, specialized in solar observations and part of the Han network of observatories.
eb0929fc-bb1d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatoire Solaire de Paris à Meudon

eb0d9d1a-badd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NOAA 6 Positions entity represents the recorded spatial locations of the NOAA 6 spacecraft in different coordinate systems, essential for tracking and analysis within astronomical and meteorological investigations.
eb0d9d1a-badd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft position on NOAA 6

eb0fda8a-b89e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MESSENGER Neutron Spectrometer (NS) was an instrument onboard the MESSENGER spacecraft designed to measure neutrons ejected from Mercury's surface, providing insights into the planet's elemental composition and detecting hydrogen, which hinted at the presence of water ice in permanently shaded craters.
eb0fda8a-b89e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Neutron Spectrometer on MESSENGER

eb208756-b6fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, and the specific one mentioned here was operational from January 1, 1957, to December 31, 1980, at the Halley Bay ground station as part of the IAGA investigation.
eb208756-b6fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at WDC Kyoto Observatory

eb227fc0-b86a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Infrared Interferometer Spectrometer and Radiometer (IRIS)**: An instrument onboard the Voyager 1 spacecraft designed to study energy balances, atmospheric composition, and particle properties by measuring infrared and visible radiation.
eb227fc0-b86a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Interferometer Spectrometer and Radiometer on Voyager 1

eb269b54-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sulphur Flats Observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Jemez Springs, Sandoval County, New Mexico. It operates as a ground-based observatory situated at 447 Sulphur Canyon Road.
eb269b54-bb22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sulphur Flats Observatory

eb2b4ff6-b8b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Baker Lake, Canada, active since 1951 and part of the IUGONET Observatory network. It is used for measuring variations in the Earth's magnetic field under the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) guidelines.
eb2b4ff6-b8b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Baker Lake Observatory

eb3a8aea-b8d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Thompsonville Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Franklin County, Illinois, United States. It is situated at 5919 Green Meadow Road and is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) as H53.
eb3a8aea-b8d1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Thompsonville Observatory, United States

eb3ca5ac-bb4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The one located in Gilgit has been operational since 1967 as part of the IUGONET-Observatory WDC Kyoto network, providing valuable geomagnetic data for scientific research under the IAGA investigation.
eb3ca5ac-bb4a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Gilgit Observatory

eb43aef2-ba22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Cometary and Interstellar Dust Analyzer (CIDA) was an instrument on the Stardust spacecraft designed to analyze the composition of individual dust grains by using a time-of-flight mass spectrometer, capable of detecting elements and molecules ranging from 1 to a few thousand atomic mass units.
eb43aef2-ba22-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cometary and Interstellar Dust Analyzer on Stardust

eb474488-b845-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **CGK21 Campo Grande** is a former ionospheric observatory located in Terenos, near Campo Grande, Brazil. It operated from September 2002 to December 2002 and utilized a Digisonde to study the ionosphere by measuring angle of arrival, polarization, Doppler frequency shift, and travel time of reflected skywave signals.
eb474488-b845-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Campo Grande Observatory, Brazil

eb4aa272-b764-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Relativistic Proton Spectrometer (RPS):** An instrument onboard the Radiation Belt Storm Probe mission designed to measure high-energy protons in the inner Van Allen radiation belt, particularly those with energies from 50 MeV to 2 GeV, to better understand space hazards and develop improved radiation models for spacecraft design.
eb4aa272-b764-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Relativistic Proton Spectrometer part of Radiation Belt Storm Probe

eb55adaa-ba77-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **LANL-02A Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer (SOPA)** is an instrument designed to measure the differential fluxes of various energetic particles, including protons, electrons, alpha particles, and heavier ions. It consists of three silicon solid state detector telescopes positioned at specific angles to the satellite's spin axis, providing detailed measurements in synchronous orbit with a high level of precision and angular resolution.
eb55adaa-ba77-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer part of LANL Observatory

eb5d8288-b6f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **IBEX-Lo**: A single-pixel imager on the Interstellar Boundary Explorer (IBEX) that measures Energetic Neutral Atoms (ENAs) in eight overlapping energy bands from 0.01 to 2.0 keV, with a field of view covering three 90 deg quadrants at 7x7 deg and one quadrant at 3.5x3.5 deg for high resolution imaging.
eb5d8288-b6f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: NeutralAtomImager part of Interstellar Boundary Explorer

eb60cf00-bb0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Siding Spring Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Coonabarabran, New South Wales, Australia. It is known for its research and telescopes that contribute to the study of astronomy and astrophysics.
eb60cf00-bb0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Siding Spring Observatory

eb64e37c-bc90-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Ion Spectra and Anisotropy (ION) instrument on the Interball Auroral Probe is a set of mass spectrometers designed to measure ion and electron spectra in specific energy ranges, utilizing Wien filters for mass filtering and electrostatic analyzers for energy selection.
eb64e37c-bc90-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer part of Interball Auroral Probe

eb788900-b8d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 2X Engineering Data Interface is a component of the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) mission, responsible for converting analog measurements of temperatures, voltages, and currents into digital data with high precision.
eb788900-b8d4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

eb7987c6-b869-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The James C. Veen Observatory (also known as the J.C. Veen Observatory) is an astronomical observatory located in Lowell Charter Township, Kent County, Michigan, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
eb7987c6-b869-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: James C. Veen Observatory, United States

eb7de1fa-b70a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lovozero (LOZ) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Lovozero, Murmansk Oblast, Russia, established in 1957 for geomagnetic research and monitoring.
eb7de1fa-b70a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lovozero Geophysical Observatory, Russian Federation

eb8b2896-b832-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The White-light Narrow field-of-view Watec Imager (NWI) at Tromsø/Longyearbyen, Norway is an automated optical instrument equipped with a CCD camera and a narrow field-of-view lens used for atmospheric observations. It is part of the EISCAT observatory operated by NIPR under IUGONET.
eb8b2896-b832-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: White-light Narrow field-of-view Watec Imager at EISCAT Observatory, Norway

eb907690-b718-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Spirit Marsh Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Meire Grove, Minnesota, USA, identified by the Minor Planet Center code V78.
eb907690-b718-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spirit Marsh Observatory

eb92e80e-bb0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Fort Severn Geomagnetic Observatory (FSV), located in Canada, has been operating since 1977 and is a ground facility dedicated to geomagnetic measurements.
eb92e80e-bb0e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Fort Severn Geomagnetic Observatory, Canada

eb990328-bbd7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Furnace Brook Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at 46 Hillcrest Drive, Cranston, Rhode Island. It operates as a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code 836.
eb990328-bbd7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Furnace Brook Observatory, United States

eb9a1f6e-b755-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS FMCW observation network is a frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar system located in Manila, Philippines. It operates as part of the IUGONET Observatory and focuses on investigating atmospheric conditions using its specialized instrumentation.
eb9a1f6e-b755-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave Radar part of Magdas Observation Network

eba99bd8-b859-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Explorer 45, also known as S-Cubed A, was a NASA satellite launched in 1971 to study the Earth's magnetosphere, focusing on particle fluxes, electric fields, and magnetic fields. Its primary goals were to investigate the characteristics of the Earth's ring current and the relationship between magnetic storms and charged particle acceleration within the inner magnetosphere.
eba99bd8-b859-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Explorer 45

eba9be76-b96f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astronomical Observatory A.L. Kekin is a ground-based observatory located in Rostov Veliky, Russia, established in 1912 for astronomical research and observations.
eba9be76-b96f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Astronomical Observatory A.L. Kekin, Russia

ebb12b56-b7ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Crozet Geomagnetic Observatory (CZT) is a ground-based facility located in the French Southern and Antarctic Lands, France, at an altitude of 160.0 meters, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements and sponsored by France.
ebb12b56-b7ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Crozet, France

ebb4b486-b9db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sitka Ground Magnetic Field Instrument, operational since 1902, is a magnetometer located at the Iugonet Observatory in Kyoto. It measures and records magnetic field data as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA).
ebb4b486-b9db-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Sitka Observatory

ebb50e44-b82e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Dordrecht Observatory (G06) is an astronomical observatory located in Sterrenburg, Dordrecht, Netherlands. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
ebb50e44-b82e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sterrenburg Observatory, Netherlands

ebb850d8-b77d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IAGA:AUT Magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields at the Australian geomagnetic observatory, operational from 1928 until 1939.
ebb850d8-b77d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at AU.TAU Observatory

ebbc6304-b81c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dome.Fuji Magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field at the Dome Fuji station in Antarctica from 1995 to 2003 as part of the IAGA investigation.
ebbc6304-b81c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Dome.Fuji Observatory, Antarctica

ebc22f8c-b858-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **TD-TRO (Tuscany Remote Observatory)** is a ground-based observatory located in Orciatico, Lajatico, Pisa, Tuscany, Italy. It provides facilities for remote astronomical observations and research.
ebc22f8c-b858-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tuscany Remote Observatory, Italy

ebcbf05c-bad9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Express ASPERA-3 Ion Mass Analyzer (IMA) is an instrument on the Mars Express spacecraft designed to measure ions in the energy range of 0.01 - 40 keV/q, focusing on main ion components like H+, H2+, He+, O+, and molecular ions with M/q ratios between 20 and 80 amu/e.
ebcbf05c-bad9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mass Spectrometer part of Mars Express

ebdc2aea-b8f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Tokushima Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Tokushima, Japan, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
ebdc2aea-b8f8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Tokushima-Kainan Astronomical Observatory, Japan

ebe11bec-b59f-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes the **Solar Plasma Electrostatic Analyzer** used on the IMP-H mission, a hemispherical electrostatic analyzer designed to study the directional intensity of positive ions and electrons in various space environments such as the solar wind, magnetosheath, and magnetotail.
ebe11bec-b59f-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Plasma Electrostatic Analyzer part of Solar Plasma Electrostatic Analyzer on IMP-H

ebe462dc-b669-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Low Energy Charged Particle (LECP) instrument on Voyager 1 is designed to measure the flux and distribution of low-energy ions and electrons in both planetary and interplanetary environments, with a wide energy range and a dynamic detection capability.
ebe462dc-b669-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low Energy Charged Particle on Voyager 1

ebf3cf22-b701-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **HIRES (High Resolution Imaging) camera** is an advanced imaging system designed for high-resolution imaging of lunar poles, featuring a lightweight beryllium telescope and a spectral response range of 0.4 to 0.8 microns.
ebf3cf22-b701-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Resolution Imaging on Clementine 1

ebf5ae4c-bba6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Arti Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia, dedicated to monitoring and studying the Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since 1973 and is funded by the Institute of Geophysics of the Russian Academy of Sciences.
ebf5ae4c-bba6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Arti Magnetic Observatory, Russia

ec096cc0-b5b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Communications/Navigation Outage Forecasting System (C/NOFS) is a satellite launched in 2008 to monitor and forecast ionospheric scintillation, which can disrupt communication and navigation systems. It carries six instruments designed to measure various aspects of the ionosphere and provide real-time data for predicting disruptions up to six hours in advance.
ec096cc0-b5b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Planar Langmuir Probe on Communication/Navigation Outage Forecasting System

ec16229a-b704-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The PRAM instrument on the Interball Tail Probe is a digital waveform processor unit designed to process and transmit data related to fields and waves, supporting various operational modes including burst modes for detailed event analysis.
ec16229a-b704-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver part of Interball Tail Probe

ec213dda-b711-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **CANOPUS All-Sky Imagers (ASI)** were a ground-based instrument array used for remote sensing of the high latitude ionosphere during the ISTP/GGS program, later succeeded by CARISMA.
ec213dda-b711-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager part of Canadian Array for Realtime Investigations of Magnetic Activity

ec237f1e-b5f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 10cm refractor full-disk white-light imaging telescope is a solar observation instrument with a 10cm aperture, designed to capture synoptic images of the Sun's photosphere. It operates at the Solar Observatory of the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ) in Mitaka.
ec237f1e-b5f9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 10cm Refractor Full-Disk White-Light Imaging Telescope at Solar Observatory, NAOJ

ec26ae64-b77f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Sabhawala ground station, part of the IUGONET observatory network, used for measuring magnetic field data since 1964.
ec26ae64-b77f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Iugonet Observatory

ec2e50c8-b8c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GONG instrument at the Udaipur Solar Observatory in India is part of a global network using helioseismology to study solar internal structure and dynamics through continuous observations of the Sun's oscillations.
ec2e50c8-b8c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Interferometer part of Global Oscillation Network Group at Udaipur Solar Observatory, India

ec2fe772-b955-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is the Ionospheric Station at Louisvale, South Africa (URSI-code: LV12P), a ground facility that uses an advanced ionosonde called Digisonde to evaluate various characteristics of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere.
ec2fe772-b955-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde Ionospheric Station at Louisvale Observatory, South Africa

ec311828-b77e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lelekovice Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Paseky, Lelekovice, Czechia. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
ec311828-b77e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lelekovice Observatory, Czechia

ec31e714-ba1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Europa Clipper Mission:** A NASA space mission scheduled to launch in 2024 and end in 2034, designed to explore Jupiter's moon Europa through multiple flybys, aiming to assess its habitability and search for signs of life-supporting conditions beneath its surface.
ec31e714-ba1f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Europa Clipper Mission

ec5ca4e6-b92e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Radio Science Subsystem (RSS) for Clementine 1 (CLEM1), a component of the Clementine spacecraft's telecommunications subsystem, was used to conduct gravity field measurements and radio propagation analysis on the Moon through Doppler tracking and signal processing.
ec5ca4e6-b92e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Subsystem part of Clementine Mission

ec63dfd6-b5aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at the Black Forest Observatory, operational since 2005, measures magnetic field variations as part of the IAGA investigation within the global IUGONET network.
ec63dfd6-b5aa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Black Forest Observatory

ec6f0bda-b786-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Applied Physics Lab Geomagnetic Observatory** was a ground-based facility located in Riverside, Howard County, Maryland, that operated from February 1999 to October 2002. It was part of the Applied Physics Laboratory and focused on geomagnetic measurements using magnetometers.
ec6f0bda-b786-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Applied Physics Lab Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

ec723aec-bb7f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at São Luís, Brazil (URSI-code: SAA0K) is a ground facility that utilizes advanced ionosondes to evaluate key parameters of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere. It has been operational since August 22, 1999 and is part of the ISWI observatory network.
ec723aec-bb7f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionospheric Station at São Luís Observatory, Brazil

ec7dd6c6-b856-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Deep Sky Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Bad Bentheim, Germany. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation of deep sky objects.
ec7dd6c6-b856-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Bad Bentheim Observatory

ec87f610-b932-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** A magnetometer located in Ivalo (IVA), operational from 1957 to 1959 as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy's (IAGA) investigations.
ec87f610-b932-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ivalo Observatory
