ec8dafc8-b6b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The BARREL Balloon 2L Engineering Data Interface is an instrument used in the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) mission that performs analog to digital conversion of key temperatures, voltages, and currents. It features multiple inputs for voltage, current, and temperature monitoring with 16-bit precision, designed to support engineering data collection.
ec8dafc8-b6b8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses part of BARREL Balloon 2L Observatory

ec9e9a48-bb15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA station identified as PFK, also known as the Port Foulke Magnetometer.
ec9e9a48-bb15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Port Foulke Observatory

eca6547e-b74e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISOPROBE is an instrument on the AUREOL3 satellite that measures electron density and temperature in thermal plasma by analyzing the mutual impedance between transmission and reception dipoles immersed in the plasma.
eca6547e-b74e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Interferometer Self-Oscillating PROBE on AUREOL3 Satellite

ecc00228-b1a1-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity describes a magnetometer instrument located at the Glenlea observatory, which was operational from 1982 to 1987 and is part of the IAGA network.
ecc00228-b1a1-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IAGA

ecd127d8-bbb5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Nagoya University Nobeyama Radioheliograph is a radio telescope located at the Nobeyama Radio Observatory in Asia, primarily used for observing solar phenomena.
ecd127d8-bbb5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio Nagoya University Nobeyama Radioheliograph at Nobeyama Radio Observatory

ecd345d8-b5eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Table Mountain Observatory 24-inch CCD Camera is an astronomical instrument used for observing celestial objects with a 24-inch telescope at the Table Mountain Observatory in Wrightwood, California, operated by Caltech.
ecd345d8-b5eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.61m CCD Camera on 0.61m Telescope at Table Mountain Observatory

ecd7e246-b61d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Brigham Young University (BYU) Remote Observatory for Variable Object Research (ROVOR) Telescope is an optical telescope located in North America, operated remotely by Brigham Young University for the study of variable astronomical objects.
ecd7e246-b61d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical Brigham Young University Remote Observatory for Variable Object Research Telescope

ece936be-ba63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **L'Ametlla de Mar Observatory**: A ground-based astronomical observatory located in les Roques Daurades, l'Estany, l'Ametlla de Mar, Catalonia, Spain, at coordinates 40.87668° N, 0.79444° E.
ece936be-ba63-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: L’Ametlla de Mar Observatory, Spain

ecf0fc76-bb55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Australian Astronomical Observatory 1.2m United Kingdom Schmidt Telescope (UKST) is an optical telescope located at the Siding Spring Observatory in Australia, with a primary mirror diameter of 1.2 meters.
ecf0fc76-bb55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.2m United Kingdom Schmidt Telescope at Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

ecf44d98-b648-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Monte Viseggi Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Viseggi, La Spezia, Italy. It was established in 1982 and operates as a ground-based facility at an altitude of approximately 347 meters.
ecf44d98-b648-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Monte Viseggi L. Zannoni Observatory, Italy

ecf887b6-b605-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on IMP 6** is an instrument designed to accurately measure the vector magnetic field in various regions such as the interplanetary medium and Earth's magnetosphere. It features a boom-mounted detector with multiple ranges and sensitivities, capable of automatic range selection and inflight calibration, providing detailed magnetic field data throughout its operational lifespan on the spacecraft.
ecf887b6-b605-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Interplanetary Monitoring Platform 6

ecfa5bec-bad1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: Metis is a coronagraph onboard the Solar Orbiter spacecraft designed to capture images of the solar corona in visible and ultraviolet light. It aims to study the dynamics and structure of the full corona from approximately 1.7 to 9 solar radii, investigating various solar phenomena including coronal mass ejections and solar wind acceleration.
ecfa5bec-bad1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Visible light and ultraviolet Solar Orbiter visible light and ultraviolet coronal imager on Solar Orbiter

ed03c84c-b899-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Instituto de Investigacion de la Actividad Solar Mutsumi Ishitsuka Komaki** is a solar research facility located in Ica, Peru, with an altitude of 280.0 meters, focused on studying solar activity using specialized instruments like the Kwasan Hida Observatory CCD camera.
ed03c84c-b899-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Instituto de Investigacion de la Actividad Solar Mutsumi Ishitsuka Komaki, Peru

ed089150-b90d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Maui Space Surveillance Site (MSSS) 1.2m is a 1.2-meter telescope located at the Air Force Maui Optical and Supercomputing Site (AMOS) on the summit of Haleakala, Maui, Hawaii, used for space surveillance and astronomical observations.
ed089150-b90d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.2m Telescope at Maui Space Surveillance Site Observatory, United States

ed0b89d4-b799-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Combined Radiometer Spectrophotometer for Mars (KRFM) on the Phobos 2 mission was an instrument designed to record thermal radiation from the Martian surface in six subranges covering 5 to 50 microns, and spectrophotometric data ranging from 300 to 700 nm, divided into nine intervals.
ed0b89d4-b799-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Combined Radiometer Spectrophotometer on Phobos 2

ed0c8686-bb6d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The BARREL Balloon 2P was a component of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) mission, designed to study the precipitation of relativistic electrons from Earth's radiation belts using high-altitude balloons equipped with scientific instruments. It operated in the stratosphere from January 30, 2014, to February 11, 2014.
ed0c8686-bb6d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star Mission of Opportunity

ed0d6fb8-bb38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operational from 1986 to 1993 located at the Ankara station as part of the IUGONET Observatory, used for measuring magnetic fields.
ed0d6fb8-bb38-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ankara Observatory

ed0f6316-b739-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **V5 Voltage Probe** is a component of the FIELDS instrument suite onboard the Parker Solar Probe. It is designed to measure electric fields and is mounted on the magnetometer boom in the umbra (shadow) of the spacecraft.
ed0f6316-b739-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Voltage Probe on Parker Solar Probe

ed142232-b6f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Polar Different Magnetospheric Analytical Models" is an instrument that provides various analytical models to study the magnetosphere, particularly focusing on data from the POLAR mission. It is part of the CNES Observatory CDPP AMDA facility.
ed142232-b6f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Polar Different Magnetospheric Analytical Models part of CNES Observatory

ed14579c-bacf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Linhaceira Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Asseiceira, Tomar, Portugal (Q115241418). It is situated at coordinates 39.52269° N, 351.6162° E and is recognized by the Minor Planet Center with ID 938.
ed14579c-bacf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Linhaceira Observatory, Portugal

ed1bcf5a-ba15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plasma Wave Spectrometer on the AMPTE/IRM spacecraft is an instrument designed to measure electric and magnetic fields using a 42 m tip-to-tip antenna for electric field measurements from dc to 5 MHz and boom-mounted search coil magnetometers for magnetic field measurements from 30 Hz to 1 MHz.
ed1bcf5a-ba15-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Wave Spectrometer on Active Magnetospheric Particle Tracer Explorers IRM

ed2e0b02-b9a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The SHARAD (Shallow Subsurface Radar) instrument on the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) is a sub-surface sounding radar designed to probe beneath the Martian surface, using wideband radar pulses to map underground structures with high resolution.
ed2e0b02-b9a2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Shallow Radar on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter

ed3283ca-b7f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ionospheric Station at Point Arguello, California (URSI-code: PA836), is an advanced ground facility equipped with a Digisonde that evaluates ionospheric reflections by measuring the angle of arrival, polarization, Doppler frequency shift, and travel time of skywave signals.
ed3283ca-b7f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Point Arguello Observatory, United States

ed3b4d06-b896-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Oak Bay Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Oak Bay, British Columbia, Canada. It serves as a ground-based observatory for astronomical research and observations.
ed3b4d06-b896-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Oak Bay Observatory, Canada

ed414410-b6d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Yale University Observatory, also known as the Leitner Family Observatory and Planetarium, is an astronomical observatory operated by Yale University for student use, located in New Haven, Connecticut.
ed414410-b6d7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Leitner Family Observatory and Planetarium, United States

ed543cdc-b9ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ISEE Ozone Monitor is a spectrometer used for atmospheric observations, specifically employing the UV absorption method to measure ozone levels. It is part of the IUGONET Observatory and utilizes the Thermo-Electron Model 49-C instrument.
ed543cdc-b9ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: UV Spectrometer at IUGONET Observatory Fukue

ed54a3ba-b74b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The magnetometers at Tonghai (THJ), operational since 1988, are part of the IUGONET-observatory and contribute to the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA).
ed54a3ba-b74b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at WDC Kyoto Observatory

ed567ba6-b712-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Richardson Geophysical Observatory (RICH) is a ground-based facility located in Dallas, Texas, dedicated to geophysical research and equipped with instruments such as the magnetometer.
ed567ba6-b712-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Richardson Geophysical Observatory, United States

ed64dcbc-bb42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LFRTO (Low Frequency Radio Transmitter Observation) is a vertical electric monopole antenna located at the Rabben station in Ny-Ålesund, Norway, designed to detect radio frequencies ranging from 20 kHz to 100 kHz.
ed64dcbc-bb42-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low Frequency Radio Transmitter Observation Antenna part of IUGONET Observatory

ed6654f8-bab0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Italian National Institute of Astrophysics (INAF) 3.58m Telescopio Nazionale Galileo (TNG), located at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory, is an optical telescope with a 3.58-meter aperture situated in Africa.
ed6654f8-bab0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 3.58m Telescopio Nazionale Galileo at Roque de los Muchachos Observatory

ed6bffc2-b7ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NRAO) Expanded Very Large Array (EVLA), located in North America, is a powerful radio astronomy instrument designed for deep-space observations across various radio wavebands.
ed6bffc2-b7ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio National Radio Astronomy Observatory Expanded Very Large Array

ed6c37c0-ba3c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astronomical Observatory of Mallorca (OAM) is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Costitx, on the island of Mallorca in Spain. It was established in 1991 and is dedicated to astronomical research and public outreach.
ed6c37c0-ba3c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Observatory of Mallorca, Spain

ed7212da-ba64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wakkanai atmospheric radar facility** is an observatory located in Wakkanai, Japan, operated by the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT) for monitoring Earth's mesosphere.
ed7212da-ba64-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Atmospheric Radar Facility at Wakkanai, Japan

ed742c8a-b6f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer** is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Cagayan De Oro, Philippines, designed to measure magnetic field variations as part of the MAGDAS observation network.
ed742c8a-b6f1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Magnetic Data Acquisition System observation network

ed745156-b9a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Upper Atmosphere Research Satellite (UARS) was a NASA orbital observatory launched in 1991 to study Earth's upper atmosphere, focusing on the ozone layer and atmospheric dynamics. It operated until its decommissioning in 2005 and re-entered the atmosphere in 2011.
ed745156-b9a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Upper Atmosphere Research Satellite

ed7572a8-b952-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Aditya-L1 is a solar mission by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), designed to study the Sun in X-ray wavelengths and observe neutrinos, particles, and gravitational waves.
ed7572a8-b952-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray The Indian Space Research Organisation's ADITYA-L1 Solar Mission

ed7649b4-b7b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Polse di Cougnes Observatory** is an astronomical ground-based observatory located in Zuglio (Zui), Italy. It is situated at Via Pieve di San Pietro in the Friuli – Venezia Giulia region and is dedicated to observing celestial phenomena.
ed7649b4-b7b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Polse di Cougnes Observatory, Italy

ed79f926-b7dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A **magnetometer** is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The **CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at YMK** is specifically a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed at Yamakawa, Japan, part of the IUGONET observatory network.
ed79f926-b7dc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometer Network Investigation

ed8d70f0-b6ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Energetic Particle Composition (EPAC) Instrument** is a device used to measure ion fluxes, angular distributions, energy spectra, and composition across energies ranging from 300 keV/nucleon to 25 MeV/nucleon. It categorizes events based on dE/dx signals, resolving data for various ion groups and protons through multiple energy channels, with additional configurations for electrons and heavy ions.
ed8d70f0-b6ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Composition Instrument on Ulysses

eda8219a-b816-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: BARREL Balloon 1D was a scientific payload launched in January 2013 as part of the BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) mission, designed to study electron precipitation from Earth's radiation belts by measuring Bremsstrahlung X-rays and magnetic field variations in the stratosphere.
eda8219a-b816-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses part of Living with a Star Mission of Opportunity

edaa0c26-bb31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **OWL-Net Observatory** in Daedeok, South Korea is an astronomical facility located at the Korea Astronomical Research Institute. It specializes in ground-based observations and is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) as P65.
edaa0c26-bb31-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Daedeok Observatory, Korea

edac7b30-baed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Krasnaya Pakhra Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Moscow, Russia, established in 1957 to conduct geophysical measurements, including magnetometer readings.
edac7b30-baed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Krasnaya Pakhra Observatory, Russia

edb60d0c-bb61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Earls Barton Observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Northamptonshire, England. It is a ground-based observatory situated at Clare Close, Earls Barton, with the MPC ID 498.
edb60d0c-bb61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Earls Barton Observatory, United Kingdom

edb825a2-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 2 Energetic Particle Detector (EPD) Suite, Fly's Eye Energetic Particle Sensor (FEEPS) is an instrument designed to measure three-dimensional energetic ion and electron flux distributions over specific energy ranges, with a time resolution of 10 seconds. It was launched on March 13, 2015, as part of the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS).
edb825a2-b6e7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fly's Eye Energetic Particle Sensor part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

edd0724a-b9af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Batavia, operating from 1884 to 1944, used for measuring the Earth's magnetic field as part of the IAGA investigation.
edd0724a-b9af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Batavia Observatory

eddb207a-bb2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: SWARM-C orbital information is data derived from the MAG, EFI / LP, and EFI / TII datasets to describe the positioning and movement of the SWARM-C satellite.
eddb207a-bb2e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris part of Swarm C

eddca26c-b1c7-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Las Campanas Observatory is an astronomical observatory in Chile's Atacama Region, managed by the Carnegie Institution for Science. It is known for its high altitude and clear skies, making it ideal for astronomical observations.
eddca26c-b1c7-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Las Campanas Observatory, Chile

ede3b446-b783-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in Logrono (LGR), operational from 1957 to 1976, used for magnetic field measurements as part of the IAGA investigation.
ede3b446-b783-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Logrono Observatory

ede7baa0-bb34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Primo I is a photomultiplier detector equipped with infrared filters, utilized at the IRTF telescope on Mauna Kea for astronomical observations.
ede7baa0-bb34-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Primo I Photometer on 3.2m Infrared Telescope Facility

ede8829e-ba87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital receiver installed in Kosrae, Micronesia, designed for measuring ionospheric total electron content (TEC) using Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite signals. It utilizes GNU Radio software and Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) hardware to process 150 and 400 MHz beacon signals.
ede8829e-ba87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU Radio Beacon Receiver at Kosrae Observatory

ede9a1f6-b6fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Baldwin station with the IAGA identifier BAL, operational from January 1, 1901, to December 31, 1909.
ede9a1f6-b6fe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Baldwin Observatory

edf27c1a-b7b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Zadko Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in the Wallingup Plain of Gingin shire, Western Australia. It is operated by the University of Western Australia and focuses on ground-based astronomical observations.
edf27c1a-b7b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Zadko Observatory, Australia

ee06a800-bb18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields, specifically the Earth's magnetic field in this context. The one referenced here has been operational since January 1, 1889, and is located at the Krasnaya Pakhra observatory near Moscow, as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) investigation.
ee06a800-bb18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Krasnaya Pakhra Observatory

ee1b97b2-bbd9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **MISCHA magnetometer** on Vega 1 was an instrument designed to measure magnetic fields and their fluctuations during Comet Halley's approach, featuring a dual-sensor fluxgate system with high sensitivity and dynamic range.
ee1b97b2-bbd9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Vega 1

ee1bc0dc-b78a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mars Global Surveyor (MGS) Electron Reflectometer** was an instrument on the Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft that measured electron flux in 19 different energy channels, ranging from 10 eV to 20 keV, to study Mars' plasma environment.
ee1bc0dc-b78a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Reflectometer on Lunar Prospector

ee1d8c96-b5be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BAS A81 Geomagnetic Observatory, located at approximately 81.5° South latitude and 3.0° East longitude on Earth's surface, is a ground-based facility dedicated to studying geomagnetic activity, particularly in the Antarctic region.
ee1d8c96-b5be-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Augsburg, Antarctica

ee3a4230-b8ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Square Kilometer Array (SKA) Mid Telescope is a radio telescope located in Africa, designed to operate within the radio waveband as part of the larger SKA project.
ee3a4230-b8ef-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Square Kilometer Array Mid Telescope

ee4c0728-b9fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Dual Full Distribution Electrostatic Analyzers are instruments on the ARTEMIS-P2 spacecraft that measure the flux, density, velocity, and temperature of thermal ions and electrons in a 360° field of view over an energy range from ~3 eV to 30 keV.
ee4c0728-b9fc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer part of Acceleration, Reconnection, Turbulence and Electrodynamics of Moon's Interaction with the Sun Mission

ee5d50f0-b763-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The National Observatory of Athens (NOA) is an astronomical observatory and research institute located in Athens, Greece. Founded in 1842, it stands as the oldest research foundation in the country and one of the earliest scientific institutions in Southern Europe.
ee5d50f0-b763-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: National Observatory of Athens, Greece

ee5dec3a-b6b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Smart Lander for Investigating Moon (SLIM), also known as "Moon Sniper," is a lunar lander mission developed by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) to demonstrate precise landing techniques on the Moon. Launched in September 2023, SLIM aims to advance the study of lunar and planetary exploration using smaller, more efficient systems.
ee5dec3a-b6b0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Smart Lander for Investigating Moon part of Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency

ee6081bc-ba1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ottmarsheim Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Ottmarsheim, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
ee6081bc-ba1a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ottmarsheim Observatory, France

ee64f9ca-b706-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN St. Paratunka station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Paratunskoe Sel'skoye Poselenie, Russia (coordinates 52.94° N, 158.25° E). It operates under the CPMN magnetometer network and is part of IUGONET's observatory infrastructure.
ee64f9ca-b706-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Paratunskoe Observatory, Russia

ee69bbec-b6c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The BARREL Balloon 1A Data Processing Unit (DPU) is an instrument controller board designed to acquire and process data from various sensors, including an X-ray spectrometer and magnetometer, for the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) mission. It formats and transmits this data via an Iridium modem while controlling critical systems through a flexible FPGA-based interface.
ee69bbec-b6c8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

ee6e19da-ba33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Discovery Bay South:** A ground-based observatory in Antarctica, established in 1903, equipped with a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements. It is part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) observatory network.
ee6e19da-ba33-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Discovery Bay South Observatory, Antarctica

ee7468bc-b72c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2O Ephemeris** is a virtual instrument that provides trajectory positions for the BARREL (Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses) mission in various coordinate systems.
ee7468bc-b72c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses part of BARREL Observatory

ee83dbae-bbd6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTIs) station at Nyrola, Finland is a ground-based facility developed by the Institute for Space-Earth Environmental Research (ISEE) to study upper atmospheric dynamics using nocturnal airglow emissions. It collaborates with the Sodankyla Geophysical Observatory and Finnish Meteorological Institute.
ee83dbae-bbd6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers Station at Nyrola, Finland

ee974d6c-ba21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Canadian Space Agency's Near-Earth Object Surveillance Satellite (NEOSSat) is a spacecraft designed to detect and monitor asteroids and other objects that come close to Earth's orbit, primarily operating in the optical waveband.
ee974d6c-ba21-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical The Canadian Space Agency Near Earth Object Surveillance Satellite

ee98e22a-b86f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Brisbane Ionosonde is an instrument located near Brisbane, Queensland, Australia, used for investigating the ionosphere through radar since 1943. It has undergone several upgrades from analog to digital models, currently operating as a vertical sounding ionosonde that sweeps frequencies from approximately 1.0 to 21.5 MHz.
ee98e22a-b86f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar Brisbane Ionosonde at World Data Centre for Ionospheric Sounding

ee996854-b7d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Exploration Rover Spirit Navigation Cameras (Navcams) are imaging instruments on the MER 2 rover designed to capture images of Martian terrain and landscape for navigation purposes. There are two Navcams per rover, positioned on the Pancam Mast Assembly, with optical designs similar to other cameras like EDLcam and Hazcams.
ee996854-b7d3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Navigation Camera on Mars Exploration Rover Spirit

ee9e1e96-bbb4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is the ground observatory located at 14, Gernotstraße in Rimbach, Hesse, Germany (latitude: 49.62054, longitude: 8.7689). It is also known by the alternative label of "Rimbach."
ee9e1e96-bbb4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 14m Telescope at Rimbach Observatory, Germany

ee9e59d2-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Orbiting Solar Observatory 8 (OSO-8) was a space mission designed to study the Sun in the gamma-ray waveband, providing valuable observations of solar phenomena.
ee9e59d2-b9df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma-ray OSO8 Satellite part of NASA Orbiting Solar Observatory 8 Satellite Mission

eeaa6b4c-b641-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Kiel Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Kiel, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany, operated by the Fachhochschule Kiel. It serves as a ground-based facility for studying celestial phenomena.
eeaa6b4c-b641-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Kiel Observatory, Germany

eeac84d8-ba40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 1.3m McGraw-Hill Telescope is an optical telescope located at the MDM Observatory in North America with an aperture of 1.3 meters.
eeac84d8-ba40-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 1.3m McGraw-Hill Telescope at MDM Observatory

eeb053bc-b831-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **CPMN Rikubetsu Station** is a magnetometer network facility located in Rikubetsu, Hokkaido Prefecture, Japan. It operates as part of the Circum-pan Pacific Magnetometer Network (CPMN) and includes instruments such as fluxgate magnetometers for geomagnetic field measurements.
eeb053bc-b831-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at CPMN Rikubetsu Station, Japan

eeb36afa-b7bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plasma and Supra-Thermal Ion Composition (PLASTIC) investigation on STEREO B is an instrument designed to measure the composition, energy spectra, and directional information of ions in space, focusing on solar wind ions and locally accelerated particles within specific energy ranges. It uses mass spectroscopy via energy vs. time-of-flight analysis to achieve its measurements.
eeb36afa-b7bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma and Supra-Thermal Ion Composition Investigation on STEREO B

eeb7c0da-b948-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover Navigation Camera Right String A** is a high-resolution stereo camera positioned on the mast of NASA's Curiosity rover, used for autonomous navigation and mapping the Martian terrain to ensure safe movement and support scientific exploration.
eeb7c0da-b948-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Navigation Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

eeb9b0a4-ba13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Collonges Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Collonges, France. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the study of celestial objects and phenomena.
eeb9b0a4-ba13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Collonges Observatory, France

eec043b0-ba18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The European Southern Observatory (ESO) 1m Schmidt Telescope at La Silla Observatory is an optical telescope located in South America with a 1.0-meter aperture, designed for astronomical observations and research.
eec043b0-ba18-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.0m optical European Southern Observatory Schmidt Telescope at La Silla Observatory

eec21a64-b653-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer operated from 1964 to 1980 in Nairobi as part of the IAGA investigation, located at the WDC Kyoto Observatory.
eec21a64-b653-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers at Nairobi

eec5e288-b6e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2A X-ray Instrument (XRI)** is a scintillation detector used in the BARREL project to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It utilizes a NaI crystal, photomultiplier tube, and pulse height analyzer to detect and analyze X-ray energies ranging from 10 keV to 10 MeV.
eec5e288-b6e0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

eece1b7c-bb88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Riverside Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Riverside City College in California, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and education.
eece1b7c-bb88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Riverside Observatory

eed770a4-ba35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Thule Air Base (TAB) Geophysical Observatory** is a ground-based scientific facility located in Pituffik, Thule, Greenland, known for its magnetometer and other geophysical instruments. It has been operational since July 1, 2013.
eed770a4-ba35-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Thule Air Base Geophysical Observatory

eed8a9e0-bb04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Geophysical Institute Magnetometer Array (GIMA) is a network of geomagnetic stations in Greenland that provides high-resolution vector data on Earth's magnetic field, with key observatories calibrated to INTERMAGNET standards. It previously included stations on the Greenland Ice Cap in collaboration with Virginia Tech.
eed8a9e0-bb04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geophysical Institute Magnetometer Array

eeda4990-bb53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 2 Fast Plasma Instrument (FPI) Suite, Dual Ion Spectrometers (DIS) is part of the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission and measures the velocity-space distribution of ions from 10 eV to 30 keV with a time resolution of 150 ms.
eeda4990-bb53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fast Plasma Investigation Suite, Dual Ion Spectrometer part of MMS 2

eef79e0a-b928-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Assonet Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at 4 Ken Street in Freetown, Bristol County, Massachusetts, USA. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
eef79e0a-b928-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Assonet Observatory, United States

eefe70e0-b761-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Platanus Observatory (K80) is an astronomical observatory located in Lusówko, Poland. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
eefe70e0-b761-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platanus Observatory, Poland

ef015802-b737-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 1R X-ray Instrument (XRI)** is a scintillation detector used in the BARREL project to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It operates with an energy response from 10 keV to 10 MeV and provides data in various time and energy resolutions to study electron precipitation events.
ef015802-b737-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

ef042440-b6d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Runcorn Observatory (Z47) is an astronomical observatory located in Halton Brook, Runcorn, England. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to observing and studying celestial objects and phenomena.
ef042440-b6d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Runcorn Observatory, United Kingdom

ef22238c-bad6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The North Scituate Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Smithville – North Scituate, Rhode Island, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
ef22238c-bad6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: North Scituate Observatory, United States

ef2810c8-bb97-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The High Resolution Mass Spectrometer (MASS) is an instrument designed to measure elemental and isotopic abundances of energetic particles within the energy range of 0.5 to 12 keV/e. It is part of the Wind spacecraft mission, focusing on solar wind and magnetospheric plasma studies.
ef2810c8-bb97-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Resolution Mass Spectrometer on Wind Spacecraft

ef28d908-b5f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kotzebue Geomagnetic Observatory (KOT) was a ground-based facility in Northwest Arctic Borough, Alaska, USA, that operated from 1957 to 1958, sponsored by the United States.
ef28d908-b5f3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kotzebue Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

ef2f3526-b99c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity represents the Etah Observatory, a ground-based facility in North America that operated from 1908 to 1947 and was located in Avannaa, Greenland. It housed magnetometers for geomagnetic measurements.
ef2f3526-b99c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Etah Observatory, Greenland

ef2fb3b8-b940-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ion Composition Instrument (ESIC) on Equator-S is an energetic particle instrument designed to measure the 3D distribution functions of major ion species, including H, He+, He++, and O+, using a combination of analyzers and time-of-flight techniques. It provides detailed information about ion fluxes and distributions with high temporal resolution.
ef2fb3b8-b940-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument part of Equator-S

ef30dbca-b67b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Repulse Bay Magnetometer, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG since 2008, is an instrument located at the Repulse Bay Geophysical Observatory designed to measure magnetic fields.
ef30dbca-b67b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of THEMIS Mission

ef337868-b7c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar Diameter Imager and Surface Mapper (SODISM) is an 11-cm diameter telescope on the PICARD space mission, designed to measure solar irradiation and provide wide-field images of the Sun's photosphere and chromosphere in five specific wavelength bands.
ef337868-b7c4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Diameter Imager and Surface Mapper on PICARD

ef3fb50c-bb74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Guirguillano Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Navarre, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting various astronomical observations and research.
ef3fb50c-bb74-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Guirguillano Observatory, Spain

ef486462-b8af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Radio Science Experiment (REX) on the New Horizons mission was designed to study the atmospheric and ionospheric structure, surface conditions, and planetary radii of Pluto and Charon by analyzing occultations of Earth-based radio signals.
ef486462-b8af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Science Experiment on New Horizons

ef496148-bbf0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
TIMED Positions refer to the orbital and positional data of the Thermosphere Ionosphere Mesosphere Energetics and Dynamics (TIMED) spacecraft, provided in various coordinate systems as part of the CDPP AMDA observatory dataset.
ef496148-bbf0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: TIMED Ephemeris on TIMED Spacecraft

ef4e4fea-bb01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Heidelberg-Königstuhl State Observatory** is a historic astronomical observatory located on Königstuhl hill in Heidelberg, Germany, operated by the University of Heidelberg.
ef4e4fea-bb01-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heidelberg-Königstuhl State Observatory, Germany

ef58116a-b769-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IMAP-3 is a magnetometer aboard the Interball Auroral Probe, designed to measure three components of the DC magnetic field in the Earth's plasma environment. It studies the structure and dynamics of the inner magnetosphere magnetic field and field-aligned currents during substorms.
ef58116a-b769-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Interball Auroral Probe

ef5db256-b8d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Polar Ionospheric X-ray Imaging Experiment (PIXIE) on the Polar spacecraft is an instrument designed to measure and map X-ray emissions from Earth's atmosphere, helping understand their spatial distribution and temporal variations.
ef5db256-b8d0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager part of Polar Ionospheric X-ray Imaging Experiment on Polar

ef6860ae-ba27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 0.5m telescope is a 50 cm instrument located at the Palmer Divide Observatory in Kent County, Delaware, USA.
ef6860ae-ba27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.5m Telescope at Palmer Divide Observatory, United States

ef76a7be-b7d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Prognoz 9 was a Soviet satellite launched in 1983 to study electromagnetic radiation, magnetic fields, plasma, and charged particles. It carried instruments like a hard X-ray spectrometer and an 8-mm radio telescope, aiming to investigate residual radiation from the Big Bang and gamma-ray bursts in deep space.
ef76a7be-b7d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 8-mm Radio Telescope on Prognoz 9

ef83364a-b6da-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CPMN fluxgate magnetometer at GAR is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Garoua, Cameroon, designed to measure variations in the Earth's magnetic field. It is part of the IUGONET observatory network and contributes to the broader study of geomagnetic activity.

ef888218-b927-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Midway geophysical observatory, used for measuring variations in the Earth's magnetic field.
ef888218-b927-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Midway Observatory

ef91ce38-b993-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AeroCube-6A Dosimeter is an instrument onboard the AeroCube-6 vehicle designed to measure electrons and protons within specific energy ranges, contributing to NASA's Heliophysics University Space Physics Initiative (HUSPI).

ef965be8-b69f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The International Cometary Explorer (ICE) is a pioneering spacecraft, originally launched as ISEE-3 in 1978 for studying Earth's magnetic field and solar wind. efa34f48-b80b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Wave Complex KEM-3** is an instrument on the Interball S2/Magion-4 satellite designed to measure electromagnetic waves in the Very Low Frequency (VLF) and Ultra Low Frequency (ULF) ranges. It measures one electric field component and three magnetic field components using various detectors and antennas.

efb26438-bb17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: CANGAROO is an international collaboration between Australia and Japan that operates gamma-ray observatories using atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes located in the Australian outback.

efb47682-ba23-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX) is a 12-meter diameter radio telescope located at the Llano de Chajnantor Observatory in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile, operated by European research institutes to conduct millimeter waveband observations.

efbdb0a4-b626-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Chichijima Observatory

efce0ab6-b726-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Three-Component Magnetometer SG-R8 is a triaxial flux-gate magnetometer aboard the Interball S2-X satellite, designed to measure space and time variations of magnetic field intensity and determine the subsatellite's attitude relative to the magnetic field vector.

efd3f8fa-b9b9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Global Surveyor (MGS) Spacecraft Mars Orbiter Camera (MOC) was an instrument on the Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft that captured high-resolution images of Mars' surface, providing valuable data for understanding the planet's geology, weather patterns, and potential landing sites.

efd48432-bb62-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Munchen Geomagnetic Observatory (MNH), located in Munich, Germany, is a ground-based facility dedicated to geomagnetic measurements that operated from 1841 to 1926.
efd48432-bb62-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Munchen Geomagnetic Observatory, Germany

efd4a3a4-baae-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The IAGA magnetometer in Okinawa has been operational since January 1977 as part of the iugonet-observatory-wdc_kyoto-wdc observatory, contributing to geomagnetic research under the IAGA investigation.

efe986ea-b9fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Observatory Gromme - Oudsbergen** is a ground-based observatory located at 25 Bampsstraat in Opglabbeek, Limburg, Belgium. It is situated at the coordinates 51.03274° N latitude and 5.60094° E longitude within Europe.

eff920d8-b60a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Ka-Dar Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Kuzminskoye, Russia. It operates as a ground-based facility and began operations on January 1, 2010.

effdbba0-b9c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Goat Mountain Astronomical Research Station** is an astronomical observatory located in San Bernardino County, California. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
effdbba0-b9c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Goat Mountain Astronomical Research Station, United States

f0012c62-b671-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ostrov Observatory in Constanța is an astronomical observatory located in Esechioi, Romania. It serves as a ground-based facility for studying celestial bodies and phenomena from Earth.
f0012c62-b671-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ostrov Observatory, Romania

f0042fd4-b8ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is a magnetometer, identified as IAGA:HLL or Hallet Magnetometer, operational from 1957 to 1962 at the Hallett observatory, used for measuring magnetic fields under the IAGA investigation.
f0042fd4-b8ba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hallet Observatory

f012eaea-bb87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Baihuashan Observatory in Beijing is a ground-based astronomical facility located at 百花山登山步道, 石塘铺, Mentougou District. It is situated at the coordinates 39.83755° N latitude and 115.57333° E longitude in Asia.
f012eaea-bb87-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Baihuashan Observatory, China

f0170ef4-b92f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2O magnetometer**, specifically the Tilt Compensated Magnetometer (TCM2), is a commercial three-axis instrument used to measure magnetic field components with high resolution. f025d0d6-bafd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Meter Wave Aperture Synthesis Radio Telescope at Beijing Astronomical Observatory

f0270c5a-b7b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Aurora Camera at Poker Flat** is an imager located in Alaska with a sampling rate of 100 Hz, designed to capture and study auroral activity.
f0270c5a-b7b3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager part of Aurora Camera Investigation

f0270d38-b72f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS Jerusalem station is a ground-based magnetometer facility located in Malchingui, Pedro Moncayo Canton, Pichincha, Ecuador, which operates as part of the international MAGDAS network for magnetic field observations.

f045ce8c-b624-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The L'Ampolla Observatory (MPC code: B29) is an astronomical observatory located in l'Ampolla, Tarragona, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
f045ce8c-b624-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: L'Ampolla Observatory, Spain

f04bbd30-b681-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The VLF/ELF crossed loop antenna at Husafell, Iceland is a scientific instrument used to measure magnetic field variations in the Very Low Frequency (VLF) and Extremely Low Frequency (ELF) ranges. It consists of two perpendicular loops, each with 10 turns and a height of 5 meters, and has a sensitivity peak at 8kHz with a sampling rate of 100kHz.

**Definition:**
BARREL Balloon 1S was a scientific payload launched in January 2013 as part of the BARREL mission, designed to study relativistic electron losses from Earth's radiation belts by measuring X-rays and magnetic fields in the stratosphere.
f055167a-b6b6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Investigation part of Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses

f05b48e4-bb1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Pujalt Observatory**, located in Pujalt, Barcelona, Spain, is an astronomical observatory situated at an altitude of 750 meters. It has been operational since January 1, 2003.
f05b48e4-bb1e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Astronomico Nacional at Pujalt Observatory, Spain

f05d716a-b7b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer on Advanced Composition Explorer

f06ffef2-b62c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electric Fields Investigation (EFI) on the Polar spacecraft is an instrument designed to study various electric field phenomena in Earth's magnetosphere using three orthogonal double probes, including large-scale parallel and perpendicular electric fields, high latitude convection electric fields, and electric field structures in different regions of the magnetosphere.
f06ffef2-b62c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electric Fields Investigation part of Polar

f0756eba-bbc1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. f0756eba-bbc1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Mbour Observatory

f077ee60-b978-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GRBR (GNU Radio Beacon Receiver) is a digital receiver located in Fukui, Japan, designed to measure ionospheric total electron content (TEC) using signals from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. It utilizes GNU Radio software and Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) hardware for signal processing and acquisition at 150 and 400 MHz frequencies.

f07c157a-b6c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lyford Geophysical Observatory, United States

f0850312-b85a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **River Oaks Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in New Braunfels, Texas, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
f0850312-b85a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: River Oaks Observatory, United States

f08caf16-b7a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Griffith Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Los Angeles, California, offering panoramic views of the city and hosting various space and science exhibits.
f08caf16-b7a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Griffith Observatory

f08d27e6-b64c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity refers to the MARIAMIR ground observatory located in Saint-Jeannet, France. It is situated at Chemin de la Cabergue, Grasse, Maritime Alps, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, with coordinates 43.74777° N, 7.15617° E.
f08d27e6-b64c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared MARIAMIR Telescope at Saint-Jeannet Observatory, France

f0912aba-b95f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Possum Observatory is a ground-based observatory located in Gisborne, New Zealand.
f0912aba-b95f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Possum Observatory, New Zealand

f0920918-b805-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The BC840 Boulder, located in Colorado, USA, is a Digisonde ionospheric station that measures various properties of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere to study its characteristics.
f0920918-b805-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde at Boulder Observatory, United States

f0963ccc-bb9d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Micro-Imaging Dust Analysis System (MIDAS) is an instrument aboard the Rosetta spacecraft consisting of an Atomic Force Microscope and a dust collection system designed to gather and image cometary dust.

f0a0d4c6-ba0c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Casey Geomagnetic Observatory

f0addbf8-b5f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Cuteip Remote Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Changhua County, Taiwan, primarily used for ground-based observations.
f0addbf8-b5f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Remote Observatory at Changhua Observatory, Taiwan

f0afeeb0-bb57-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Indian Astronomical Observatory (IAO) is a high-altitude astronomy station located in Hanle, India, operated by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics. Situated at an elevation of 4,500 meters in the Western Himalayas, it is one of the world's highest sites for optical, infrared, and gamma-ray telescopes.

f0b2a202-ba78-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rochedale (APTA) Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Rochedale, Queensland, Australia. It is a ground-based observatory used for astronomical research and observations.

f0b2f5ac-b750-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMN fluxgate magnetometer at LAQ is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument located in L'Aquila, Italy, used for measuring magnetic field variations as part of the Equatorial Magnetometer Network.
f0b2f5ac-b750-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of The Equatorial Magnetometer Network

It supports eight voltage and current pairs, four voltage-only inputs, and sixteen temperature sensors that can also monitor voltage, with all inputs converted at 16-bit precision.
f0b5208e-b728-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Engineering Data Interface part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

f0bc1740-bbba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Radio Occultation Experiment for V15 is an instrument that measures changes in radio signals passing through a planet's atmosphere to determine its structure, temperature, and composition.
f0bc1740-bbba-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio Occultation Experiment on Venus Express

f0be194e-b8a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Medicina Radio Astronomical Station is an observatory located in Italy, notable for housing the Bologna University Northern Cross radio telescope array. It is part of a ground-based astronomical facility dedicated to radio astronomy research.
f0be194e-b8a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Northern Cross Radio Telescope Array at Medicina Radio Astronomical Station

f0be9772-b782-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Deerlick Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Crawfordville, Georgia, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
f0be9772-b782-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deerlick Observatory

f0beeda6-b784-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Morning Star Observatory (code H14) is an astronomical observatory located in Tucson, Arizona, United States. It is a ground-based facility situated at 3801 North Cherry Creek Place, Rinconada Hills, Pima County.
f0beeda6-b784-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Morning Star Observatory, United States

f0c00ba4-b811-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Beijing Geomagnetic Observatory (BJI)** is a ground-based facility located in Beijing Botanical Garden, Haidian District, China. f0c00ba4-b811-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Beijing Geomagnetic Observatory, China

f0c37952-ba7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The Yellow Springs Observatory is an astronomical ground-based facility located in Yellow Springs, Ohio, dedicated to conducting observations and research in astronomy.
f0c37952-ba7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yellow Springs Observatory

f0ca5328-ba75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The DSS-13 26-m Radio Telescope was a fully steerable research and development radio/radar antenna that operated from 1962 to 1991 as part of the NASA Deep Space Network, notable for its role in the first radar detection of Venus.
f0ca5328-ba75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 26m Radio Telescope part of Deep Space Network

f0ce3818-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "DSS-65" is a ground-based observatory, known as Deep Space Station 65, used for astronomical observations and research.
f0ce3818-b9a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Deep Space Station 65, Australia

f0e02ea4-bad5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Foxfire Village Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Moore County, North Carolina, United States. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to the observation and study of celestial objects.
f0e02ea4-bad5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Foxfire Village Observatory, United States

f0f2d0a6-ba92-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. At the Hobert observatory in Kyoto, magnetometers are employed to monitor and study variations in Earth's magnetic field as part of the IUGONET network.
f0f2d0a6-ba92-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hobart Observatory

f0fac3f4-bb52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Prognoz 7** was a Soviet spacecraft launched in 1978 as part of the Prognoz series to study solar activity, interplanetary environment, and Earth's magnetosphere by measuring charged particles, plasma, magnetic fields, and solar electromagnetic radiation.
f0fac3f4-bb52-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Prognoz 7 part of International Magnetospheric Study

f1103cb0-bab3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Elgin Observatory (code: V12) is an astronomical observatory located in Santa Cruz County, Arizona, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.

f116d744-ba4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Les Engarouines Observatory is an astronomical ground-based observatory located in Mallemort, France. It serves as a facility for conducting Earth-based observations and research in astronomy.
f116d744-ba4c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Les Engarouines Observatory, France

f118dcd6-b9cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Amatsia Ground Magnetic Field Instrument, operational since 1976, is part of the IUGONET observatory network and provides data for the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA).

f11adcce-b941-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of The Equatorial Magnetometer Network

f11d43ea-bba0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kumasi Geomagnetic Observatory (KUM) is a ground-based facility located in Asokore Mampong, Ghana, dedicated to the study of geomagnetism and has been operational since 1972.
f11d43ea-bba0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kumasi Geomagnetic Observatory, Ghana

f12a5de0-bba1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Irkutsk Geomagnetic Observatory (IRT), located in Ушаковское сельское поселение, Russia, is a ground-based facility that has been operating since 1887 to monitor and study geomagnetic activity on Earth.
f12a5de0-bba1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Irkutsk Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

f138dbb0-babe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Infrared Astronomical Satellite (IRAS) was a joint mission by NASA, the Netherlands Agency for Aerospace Programs (NIVR), and the Science and Engineering Research Council (SERC). It carried a 0.57m telescope system designed to conduct an infrared survey of the sky, including detectors, star sensors, a Low Resolution Spectrometer (LRS), and a Chopped Photometric Channel (CPC).
f138dbb0-babe-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.57m Infrared Astronomical Satellite part of Infrared Astronomical Satellite Mission

f13c3712-bae4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Serra La Nave Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Belpasso, Catania, Sicily, Italy, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial phenomena.
f13c3712-bae4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Serra La Nave Observatory, Italy

f146d4ce-baee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The La Maddalena Geomagnetic Observatory (LMD) is a ground-based facility located in Villaggio Trinità, Sardinia, Italy, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity. It operates under the sponsorship of Italy and is part of the IUGONET observatory network.
f146d4ce-baee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at La Maddalena Geomagnetic Observatory, Italy

f14a606a-b767-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GPS receiver at Kototabang, Indonesia (KTB), is a ground-based facility operated by ISEE, Nagoya University, in collaboration with RISH (Kyoto U.) and LAPAN. It is located in Baringin, Agam, West Sumatra, Indonesia.
f14a606a-b767-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Single-frequency Global Positioning System Receiver at Kototabang Station, Indonesia

f151a794-bb7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Abisko Magnetic Observatory** is a ground-based facility in Abisko, Sweden, dedicated to monitoring and studying Earth's magnetic field. It has been operational since 1951 and is funded by the Geological Survey of Sweden.
f151a794-bb7c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Abisko Magnetic Observatory, Sweden

f156bcc4-b844-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Escaldarium Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located in Caldes de Montbui, Catalonia, Spain. It is situated at the coordinates 41.6198° N, 2.18286° E and provides a site for celestial observations within Europe.
f156bcc4-b844-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Escaldarium Observatory, Caldes de Montbui, Spain

f156e1a2-ba0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Electrons and Hydrogen and Helium Isotopes on IMP-J** is an instrument designed to measure the differential energy spectra of hydrogen through oxygen isotopes (2 to 40 MeV/nucleon) and electrons (0.2 to 5 MeV), using a stack of silicon detectors and a plastic scintillator anticoincidence cup, providing anisotropy data with high angular and temporal resolution.
f156e1a2-ba0d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: EnergeticParticleInstrument on IMP-8 part of cnes-observatory-cdpp-amda-imp8

f159eb6a-bbaf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Crystal Lake Observatory in Ngutunui is a ground-based astronomical facility located at 2331 Kawhia Road in the Otorohanga District of Waikato, New Zealand. It is situated at coordinates -38.09433 latitude and 175.09104 longitude on the continent of Oceania.
f159eb6a-bbaf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Crystal Lake Observatory, New Zealand

f15f4b0c-b7f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Manzhouli Magnetometer** is an instrument used to measure the Earth's magnetic field, located at Manzhouli station with the IAGA identifier MZL. It has been operational since January 1984 and is part of a ground observatory under the SMWG network.
f15f4b0c-b7f7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Manzhouli Observatory

f1600096-b807-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Wallhausen Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Wallhausen, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany (MPC ID: K55). It is a ground-based facility situated at coordinates 49.88688 latitude and 7.765 longitude.
f1600096-b807-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wallhausen Observatory

f160cd6c-b7b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kashi Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Kashgar City, Xinjiang, China, that specializes in geomagnetic measurements and has been operational since 1987.
f160cd6c-b7b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kashi Geomagnetic Observatory, China

f18412d0-b6d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 14 Cold Cathode Ion Gage Experiment (CCIG) was part of the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments package and was designed to measure the density of neutral particles at the lunar surface, helping scientists understand the sources and loss mechanisms of the moon's thin atmosphere.
f18412d0-b6d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cold Cathode Ionization Gauge on Apollo 14 Lunar Surface Experiments Package

f1889a5a-babf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Roscosmos State Corporation Soviet Gamma Gamma-ray Observatory is a spacecraft designed for gamma-ray astronomy, operated by the Russian space agency.
f1889a5a-babf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma-ray Roscosmos State Corporation Soviet Gamma Observatory

f18950c4-ba1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Bigmuskie Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Mombercelli, Italy. It operates as a ground-based observatory for studying celestial phenomena and has the MPC (Minor Planet Center) code B88.
f18950c4-ba1c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mombercelli Observatory, Italy

f1918700-b8fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Polaris Public Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Budapest, Hungary, dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial bodies.
f1918700-b8fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Polaris Observatory, Hungary

f1b0b268-b68e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity represents the United States Ultraviolet Space Telescope (USUDA), a ground observatory dedicated to astronomical observations in the ultraviolet spectrum.
f1b0b268-b68e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: USUDA Observatory

f1b4b7b4-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NASA Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) Mission is a space-based observatory designed to study the Sun and its influence on Earth. It operates in the X-ray waveband and provides continuous observations of solar activity, contributing significantly to our understanding of solar variability and space weather.
f1b4b7b4-b72e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray Solar Dynamics Observatory

f1bc17b8-b790-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Couvaloup de St-Cergue Observatory (code A64) is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Cergue, Switzerland. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
f1bc17b8-b790-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Couvaloup de St-Cergue Observatory, Switzerland

f1bd9872-b7e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The OAO University Observatory Station Aras is an astronomical observatory located in El Brollador, Aras de los Olmos, Valencia, Spain. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
f1bd9872-b7e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatorio Astronómico de la Universidad at Aras, Spain

f1bdeff6-b679-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Electron Drift Instrument (EDI) on Cluster-4 measures the drift of test electrons to determine electric and magnetic field properties in space. It uses modulated electron beams and detectors mounted on opposite sides of the spacecraft to track these drifts, providing insights into the local electromagnetic environment.
f1bdeff6-b679-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electron Drift Instrument part of Cluster-4

f1bf4064-b61e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hin Hua Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at Hin Hua High School in Klang City, Selangor, Malaysia. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical observations and research.
f1bf4064-b61e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hin Hua Observatory

f1cc8c5e-b5df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The INTEGRAL (International Gamma-Ray Astrophysics Laboratory) satellite mission is a European Space Agency (ESA) project dedicated to observing gamma rays in space, providing crucial data for astrophysical research.
f1cc8c5e-b5df-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gamma Ray European Space Agency International Gamma-Ray Astrophysics Laboratory Satellite Mission

f1d17b6a-b62a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetospheric Imaging Instrument on MIMI-LEMMS is a spectrometer aboard the Cassini spacecraft that measures ions and electrons within specific energy ranges using dual telescopes, employing magnetic deflection and detector stacks for precise particle discrimination.
f1d17b6a-b62a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetospheric Imaging Instrument on Cassini

f1dcec5e-b925-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The IGPP-LANL Boulder Magnetometer Station is a ground facility located in Routt County, Colorado, USA, used for magnetic field measurements. It is part of the Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics (IGPP) at Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL).
f1dcec5e-b925-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Boulder Observatory, United States

f1dd1fe4-ba88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) High Altitude Observatory telescope at Mauna Loa Solar Observatory (MLSO) is an optical telescope located in North America, specifically designed to observe the Sun and is part of the Mauna Loa Solar Observatory.
f1dd1fe4-ba88-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical National Center for Atmospheric Research High Altitude Observatory Telescope at Mauna Loa Solar Observatory

f1ddb86a-b8bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LANL01A is a geosynchronous spacecraft operating within Earth's magnetosphere, equipped with instruments to measure energetic electrons and ions in the radiation belt.
f1ddb86a-b8bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Electron and Ion Instruments on Geosynchronous Spacecraft

f1e15918-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Observatoire des Côtes de Meuse is an astronomical observatory located in Vigneulles-lès-Hattonchâtel, France. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
f1e15918-b76a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatoire des Côtes de Meuse, France

f1e243cc-bae5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The **Saguaro Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Tucson, Arizona, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
f1e243cc-bae5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Saguaro Observatory, United States

f1f8e314-b637-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The SPECULOOS Northern Observatory comprises a set of three 1-meter infrared telescopes located at the Teide Observatory in South America, dedicated to searching for habitable planets around ultra-cool stars.
f1f8e314-b637-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: infrared Search for habitable Planets EClipsing Ultracool Stars Northern Observatory three 1.0m Telescope at Teide Observatory

f205de84-b7c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The L'Aquila Geomagnetic Observatory (AQU) is a ground-based facility located in L'Aquila, Italy, which operates magnetometer instruments to monitor geomagnetic activity.
f205de84-b7c7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at L'Aquila Geomagnetic Observatory, Italy

f22059aa-b9cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Research Council (NRC) Herzberg Institute of Astrophysics 1.22m McKellar Telescope at Dominion Astrophysical Observatory (DAO) is an optical telescope located in North America, operated by the NRC Herzberg Institute and situated within the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory.
f22059aa-b9cd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 1.22m McKellar Telescope at Dominion Astrophysical Observatory

f2228206-bb90-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Frasnes-Lez-Anvaing Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Frasnes-lez-Buissenal, Belgium. It operates as a ground-based observatory dedicated to studying celestial phenomena.
f2228206-bb90-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Frasnes-Lez-Anvaing Observatory, Belgium

f225f1c8-b9e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: DSS-28 is a ground observatory used for astronomical observations, also known as the Deep Space Station 28.
f225f1c8-b9e4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: DSS-28

f22e354a-b9c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Faulkes Telescope South is a 2-meter Ritchey–Chrétien telescope located at Siding Spring Observatory in New South Wales, Australia, designed for remote operation to promote scientific interest among young people.
f22e354a-b9c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.0m Faulkes Telescope South at Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

f2347618-b623-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Cassini Orbiter Spacecraft Sensors" refer to the suite of instruments aboard the Cassini Orbiter designed to gather and analyze data from its environment during its mission around Saturn.
f2347618-b623-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cassini Orbiter Spacecraft Sensors on Cassini Orbiter Spacecraft

f234ebba-b8f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Express Orbiter (MEX) Radio Science investigations involve using both spacecraft and ground-based instrumentation to conduct radio science experiments. This setup includes shared equipment for telecommunications and is supported by ESA and NASA Deep Space Network ground systems, with the spacecraft capable of operating in both S-band and X-band frequencies.
f234ebba-b8f4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars Express Orbiter Radio Science part of Mars Express

f249cb92-ba80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Genesis Plasma Spectrometers** are two instruments (GIM and GEM) on the Genesis spacecraft designed to collect solar wind samples by determining solar wind type in real-time and adjusting collection parameters accordingly. They also gather high-quality solar wind data for scientific research.
f249cb92-ba80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Genesis Ion Monitor and Genesis Electron Monitor part of Genesis

f2528f06-bac2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hale Telescope is a 5.1-meter optical telescope located at Palomar Observatory in California, operated by the California Institute of Technology since November 1949.
f2528f06-bac2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 5.08m Hale Telescope at Palomar Observatory

f2554d60-bc4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cosmic-Ray Telescope on Pioneer 11** (CRT) is an energetic particle instrument consisting of three 3-element telescopes designed to measure high-energy particles and electrons in the interplanetary region, with varying energy resolutions.
f2554d60-bc4b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument on Pioneer 11

f258d6ae-b65d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The BARREL Balloon 1J Data Processing Unit (DPU) is a versatile instrument controller used in the BARREL project to collect and process data from various sensors, including an X-ray spectrometer and magnetometer, and to manage communication and control systems.
f258d6ae-b65d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Data Processing Unit part of Balloon Array for Radiation Belts Relativistic Electron Losses

f259c250-b971-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: TWINS (Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers) is a NASA mission consisting of two instruments on separate spacecraft designed to provide stereoscopic neutral atom imaging of the Earth's magnetosphere, aiming to understand global connectivities and causal relationships within different regions.
f259c250-b971-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers part of Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers

f25db0b6-b662-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The RISH Ionosonde at Shigaraki is an FMCW (frequency modulated continuous wave) instrument located in Shiga Prefecture, Japan, used to transmit high-frequency radio waves for ionospheric studies. It operates with an average power of 30 W and a peak power of 80 W.
f25db0b6-b662-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radarinvestigation RISH Ionosonde at Shigaraki, Japan

f25f4592-bab4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Lukiapang-2 was a ground observatory located in Lujia, Kunshan, China, operational from January 1908 to December 31, 1933. It was part of the IAGA observatory network and included magnetometers for geophysical measurements.
f25f4592-bab4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lukiapang Observatory, China

f2621298-b7fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Mercury Ion Analyzer (MIA) is an instrument onboard the BepiColombo spacecraft's Mio module, designed to measure both solar wind ions and magnetospheric ions at Mercury with high precision and versatility through various energy sweep modes. It is part of the Mercury Plasma Particle Experiment (MPPE) suite aimed at studying Mercury’s plasma environment.
f2621298-b7fa-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ElectrostaticAnalyser Mercury Ion Analyzer on Mio

f26a8702-b930-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Blanquita Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Rivas-Vaciamadrid, Community of Madrid, Spain. It is used for ground-based observations and research in astronomy.
f26a8702-b930-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Blanquita Observatory, Spain

f2730d3c-bbc9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Parker Solar Probe's Wide-field Imager for Solar Probe (WISPR) is an instrument featuring two visible light cameras designed to capture images of the solar corona and inner heliosphere, providing insights into solar wind structures and their evolution close to the Sun.
f2730d3c-bbc9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide-field Imager for Solar Probe on Parker Solar Probe

f27904ec-b676-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 0.8m Southern Photometric Local Universe Survey (S-PLUS) Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in South America, designed for conducting photometric surveys of the local universe.
f27904ec-b676-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.8m optical Southern Photometric Local Universe Survey Telescope at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory

f27ba77c-baa6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The magnetometer located at Chambon-La-Foret (CLF), identified by IAGA code CLF, has been operational since January 1936 and is part of a ground observatory.
f27ba77c-baa6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Chambon-La-Foret Observatory

f27f92f0-b8d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
The **Super Dual Auroral Radar Network (SuperDARN)** is an international network of high-frequency radars designed to study plasma convection and electric fields in the Earth's upper atmosphere. It consists of 14 radars in the northern hemisphere and 7 in the southern hemisphere, providing global coverage for investigating geophysical parameters derived from radar data.
f27f92f0-b8d6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radar part of Super Dual Auroral Radar Network

f28640e2-b9ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Spacewatch 1.8m FLI Camera** is an astronomical camera used on the Spacewatch Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona, primarily for observations of near-Earth objects like asteroids and comets.
f28640e2-b9ca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: FLI Camera on Spacewatch 1.8m Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory

f286582e-b7e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GNU radio beacon receiver (GRBR) station at Fukui is an observatory in Japan dedicated to studying ionospheric disturbances and middle-upper atmospheric coupling processes. Located at Kitagatako Hamming Road, Awara, Fukui Prefecture, it operates a GNU radio beacon receiver as part of the GRBR network.
f286582e-b7e6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GNU radio beacon receiver station at Fukui Observatory, Japan

f28d27c8-b852-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Kamennyj Mys Geomagnetic Observatory (KAM)** is a ground-based facility in Russia, located at Yamalsky Rayon, dedicated to monitoring and studying geomagnetic activities. It operates under the sponsorship of Russia and contributes to global geomagnetic data collection.
f28d27c8-b852-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kamennyj Mys Geomagnetic Observatory, Russia

f28fd99a-b68c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
Explorer 51, also known as AE-C (Atmospheric Explorer-C), was a NASA scientific satellite launched in 1973 to study the thermosphere and photochemical processes in Earth's atmosphere.
f28fd99a-b68c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Atmospheric Explorer-C part of Atmosphere Explorer Mission

f2912f3a-bc4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **LOFAR FR606 High Band Array** is a component of the LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR) interferometer located in Nançay, France. It operates within the spectral range from 120 to 330 MHz and contributes to various astronomical studies including deep sky surveys, cosmic ray detection, and the study of variable sources like pulsars and exoplanets.
f2912f3a-bc4e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 10-80 MHz Low Band Array on LOFAR at Nançay Observatory, France
