f86a9e52-b6ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Closed-Source Neutral Mass Spectrometer part of AE-C

f86e4642-ba30-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The medium frequency (MF) radar at the EISCAT Tromsø radar site is an instrument operated by a collaboration of universities that measures neutral wind velocity at altitudes between 70 and 90 km.
f86e4642-ba30-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Medium Frequency Radar at IUGONET Observatory

f86ed756-bbf7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1O Tilt Compensated Magnetometer (TCM2) is an instrument aboard the BARREL mission that measures magnetic field components with a resolution of 50 nT at a 1-second cadence to identify substorm activity and ULF oscillations.
f86ed756-bbf7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

f871fa8a-b841-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at CAN is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Canberra, Australia, used for measuring magnetic fields as part of the MAGDAS observation network.
f871fa8a-b841-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of MAGDAS observation network, Antarctica

f87a7196-b6a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) Airglow Temperature Photometer at Sata, Japan is an instrument designed to measure airglow intensities and temperatures of various atmospheric constituents like OH, O2, OI, and Na lines, providing insights into the dynamics of the upper atmosphere through nocturnal airglow emissions.
f87a7196-b6a8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Airglow Temperature Photometer part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers, Japan

f8949d9a-b8ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GOES 2 Energetic Particle Monitor (EPM) is an instrument launched in 1977 that uses silicon solid-state detectors to measure the energy and type of particles, including protons, alpha particles, and electrons.
f8949d9a-b8ed-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Monitor on GOES 2

f89a5400-bb96-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ivalo Geomagnetic Observatory (IVA) is a ground-based facility located in Inari, Finland. It was operational from 1957 to 1959 and focused on geophysical and magnetic measurements.
f89a5400-bb96-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Ivalo Geophysical Observatory, Finland

f89df912-b749-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **W Crusis Astronomical Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in San Justo, Buenos Aires, Argentina. It is dedicated to ground-based observations of celestial bodies and phenomena.
f89df912-b749-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: W Crusis Astronomical Observatory, Argentina

f8a259e2-b651-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Rand Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at 672 Forest Home Road in the Town of Harrietstown, Franklin County, New York. It is a ground-based facility situated on Earth.
f8a259e2-b651-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rand Observatory, United States

f8a47b96-b7a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The South African Astronomical Observatory (SAAO) is the national centre for optical and infrared astronomy in South Africa, conducting research in astronomy and astrophysics.
f8a47b96-b7a0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 9.3m Southern African Large Telescope at South African Astronomical Observatory, South Africa

f8a68836-bab7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Arizona/Lunar and Planetary Laboratory (LPL)/Steward Observatory 0.9m Spacewatch Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Kitt Peak National Observatory in North America, used primarily for astronomical research and observations.
f8a68836-bab7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical 0.9m Spacewatch Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory

f8aace10-b7ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The North Pole 8 Geomagnetic Observatory (NPH) was a Russian ground-based facility located at latitude 77.32 and longitude 188.3, operational from 1959 to 1962, which included a magnetometer for geomagnetic measurements.
f8aace10-b7ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at North Pole 8 Geomagnetic Observatory, Antarctica

f8ac2ac0-b6cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Grav.JNO is a gravity instrument aboard the NASA Juno mission, designed to measure Jupiter's gravitational field with high precision for understanding the planet’s internal structure and dynamics.
f8ac2ac0-b6cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Gravity Science Instrument part of Juno Mission

f8b07f86-ba43-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The HAO Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Oukaïmeden, Morocco. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to studying the night sky and conducting astronomical research from its site on Earth.
f8b07f86-ba43-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Oukaimeden Observatory

f8c269d6-b713-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Magnetometers at Nida" are instruments used to measure magnetic fields and are situated at the observatory station with the IAGA identifier NDA. They are part of the IUGONET Observatory network associated with WDC Kyoto and WDC ND.
f8c269d6-b713-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Nida Observatory

f8ccdd14-bb76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Voyager 2 spacecraft sensors consist of a suite of instruments including magnetometers, plasma detectors, charged particle instruments, and imaging systems designed to investigate planetary environments and interstellar space.
f8ccdd14-bb76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometers, plasma detectors, charged particle instruments, and imaging systems on Voyager 2 Spacecraft

f8db56e0-b933-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Virtual Telescope Project is an astronomical observatory consisting of a pair of robotic optical telescopes located in Ceccano, Italy. It has been operational since 2006 and provides remote-controlled access for astronomical observations.
f8db56e0-b933-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical Telescopes at Ceccano Observatory, Italy

f8e567e2-b59c-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BARREL Balloon 1L X-Ray Instrument (XRI) is a scientific device designed to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons. It consists of a NaI scintillator, photomultiplier tube, and pulse height analyzer, offering various resolutions for telemetry constraints.
f8e567e2-b59c-11f1-8724-405b7f7031a0.label: X-Ray BARREL 1L X-Ray Instrument on Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

f8ef963c-b663-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**
BepiColombo is a joint mission by the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) to study Mercury. It comprises two orbiters: the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and the Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), launched in 2018 and expected to reach Mercury in November 2026 after multiple flybys and a nearly 8-year interplanetary cruise.
f8ef963c-b663-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label:
Mercury Planetary Orbiter part of BepiColombo
Near Earth Object Telescope on Mercury Planetary Orbiter

f8f45276-b9d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Definition:**

GOLD (Global-scale Observations of the Limb and Disk) is a NASA mission launched on January 25, 2018, designed to image Earth's thermosphere and ionosphere from geostationary orbit over a two-year period. It operates as a hosted payload on the SES-14 commercial communications satellite, utilizing a far-ultraviolet (FUV) imaging spectrograph built by the University of Colorado Boulder.
f8f45276-b9d8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: far ultraviolet Global-scale Observations of the Limb and Disk on SES-14

f8fb9afc-bb79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Alter Satzberg Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in Vienna, Austria, known for its ground-based observations.
f8fb9afc-bb79-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 3.6m Telescope at Alter Satzberg Observatory, Austria

f908f0c4-bb80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An **Imaging Spectrometer** named the DMSP/F19 SSULI (Special Sensor Ultraviolet Spectrographic Imager) operated from 2014 to 2016 as part of the Defense Meteorological Satellite Program, providing observations of Extreme and Far UV radiation from Earth's limb.
f908f0c4-bb80-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Special Sensor Ultraviolet Spectrographic Imager on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program F19

f90ead74-b64a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The European Southern Observatory (ESO) 39.3m European Extremely Large Telescope (E-ELT) is an optical telescope located at the Cerro Armazones Observatory in South America, known for its large aperture of 39.3 meters.
f90ead74-b64a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 39.3m European Extremely Large Telescope at Cerro Armazones Observatory

f914280c-bbb9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Pan-STARRS 1.8m PS1 Telescope is an optical telescope located at Haleakala Observatory in North America, designed for wide-field astronomical surveys and rapid response to transient events.
f914280c-bbb9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical Panoramic Survey Telescope and Rapid Response System 1.8m Telescope at Haleakala Observatory

f918fc92-b759-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EG Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Lippstadt, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility situated at the Evangelisches Gymnasium on Beckumer Straße.
f918fc92-b759-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lippstadt Observatory, Germany

f92dff6a-bade-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Beppe Forti Astronomical Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Montelupo Fiorentino, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observation.
f92dff6a-bade-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Beppe Forti Astronomical Observatory, Italy

f9339698-ba55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Port Alfred Magnetic Observatory** is a ground-based magnetic observatory located in the French Southern and Antarctic Lands, established in 1974 for studying Earth's magnetic field.
f9339698-ba55-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Crozet Magnetic Observatory

f9378b94-b1c3-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Durtal Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Bazouges-sur-le-Loir, France. It operates as a ground-based observatory and is also known by its MPC ID 949.
f9378b94-b1c3-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Durtal Observatory, France

f93dd826-b83c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The International Centre for Eremology Wind Tunnel at Ghent University, Belgium is a closed-circulation, blower-type wind tunnel with dimensions of 12 m in length and a cross-section of 1.2 m by 3.2 m, designed for various aerodynamic and environmental simulations.
f93dd826-b83c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wind Tunnel at International Centre for Eremology, Belgium

f946f818-b817-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Castle Rock Geomagnetic Observatory (CRC) was a ground-based facility located in Santa Cruz County, California, operational from 1970 to 1974, dedicated to geomagnetic measurements.
f946f818-b817-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Castle Rock Geomagnetic Observatory, United States

f947ed5a-b7fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hawker Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Woolner Circuit, Hawker, Australian Capital Territory, Australia. It is designated with MPC ID 429 and is a ground-based observatory used for astronomical observations.
f947ed5a-b7fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hawker Observatory, Australia

f94d754a-b67c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MCD Observatory in Saint-Anaclet is a ground-based astronomical facility located at Rue Langlois, Saint-Anaclet-de-Lessard, Quebec, Canada. It provides observations and research opportunities within the Bas-Saint-Laurent region of North America.
f94d754a-b67c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: MCD Observatory, Canada

f9664630-b616-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ion Composition Analyser (ICA) on the Rosetta spacecraft is a mass spectrometer designed to measure ion compositions and energies, specifically focusing on H+, H2+, He+, O+, and molecular ions with M/q ratios between 20 and 80 amu/e in an energy range of 0.01 - 36 keV/q, featuring a wide field of view and electrostatic sweeping for elevation coverage.
f9664630-b616-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Composition Analyser part of Rosetta

f9744182-baac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Eastern Illinois University Observatory is an astronomical facility located at Eastern Illinois University in Charleston, Illinois. It serves as a ground-based observatory for conducting astronomical research and education.
f9744182-baac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Eastern Illinois University Observatory

f9790698-b6b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CAS Observatory in Preetz is a ground-based astronomical facility located at Castöhlenweg, Preetz, Kreis Plön, Schleswig-Holstein, Germany. It serves as an observational site for studying celestial phenomena.
f9790698-b6b2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: CAS Observatory, Germany

f97d3160-bc3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Four Winds Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Lake Leelanau, Michigan, United States. It operates as a ground-based facility for stargazing and astronomical research.
f97d3160-bc3d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Four Winds Observatory, United States

f9840f32-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Ähtäri Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Ähtäri, Finland. It operates as a ground-based facility for conducting various astronomical observations and research.
f9840f32-b9bb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ähtäri Observatory, Finland

f990cfaa-b7f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The OSIRIS-REx Laser Altimeter (OLA) is a lidar instrument onboard the OSIRIS-REx spacecraft used for ranging and mapping asteroid surfaces with high precision at varying distances.
f990cfaa-b7f0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: OSIRIS-REx Laser Altimeter on OSIRIS-REx Spacecraft

f997b896-b936-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Stereo/Waves (Swaves) on STEREO A** is an experiment designed to measure radio bursts and plasma waves from the Sun and in situ, using multiple receivers and antenna systems to capture data across various frequencies and distances.
f997b896-b936-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Stereo/Waves on STEREO A

f9990240-b69e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Chirorin Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Chikuni, Otari, Kita-Azumi County, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. It is identified by the Minor Planet Center (MPC) with the code 383 and primarily operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
f9990240-b69e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Chirorin Observatory, Japan

f9a9d0d0-b779-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Sørøya (SOR) Geophysical Observatory is a ground-based facility located in Hasvik, Finnmark, Norway. It includes instruments such as a magnetometer and operates as part of the broader network of geophysical observatories to monitor Earth's surface conditions.
f9a9d0d0-b779-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Soroya Geophysical Observatory, Norway

f9b03c86-b837-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** PICARD is a French solar physics satellite launched in 2010 to simultaneously measure the Sun's total and spectral irradiance, diameter, shape, and interior structure through helioseismology.
f9b03c86-b837-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SODISM 11 cm imaging telescope on Picard

f9b462c4-b9a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity Rover Front Hazard Avoidance Camera (FHAZ) Right String B is a component of the rover's hazard detection system, specifically one of the front-mounted cameras used for navigating and avoiding obstacles during its missions on Mars.
f9b462c4-b9a5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Front Hazard Avoidance Camera on Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity Rover

f9bf5c74-b6c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Lerwick Magnetic Observatory is a geomagnetic research facility located in the Shetland Islands, Scotland, UK, operated by the Met Office since 1923.
f9bf5c74-b6c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lerwick Observatory, United Kingdom

f9c044a8-b154-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Small Probe North Net Flux Radiometer (SNFR) was an instrument aboard the Pioneer Venus mission, designed to measure solar and infrared flux in Venus's atmosphere, determining regions of radiative convergence and divergence. It operated within specific spectral ranges and altitudes, featuring two modules with various electronic components for data collection.
f9c044a8-b154-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Net Flux Radiometer on Pioneer Venus

f9c4f23e-b71f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers (OMTI) Fabry-Perot Interferometer at Chiang Mai, Thailand, is an instrument designed to measure thermospheric neutral wind through airglow emissions at a wavelength of 630.0 nm, contributing to the study of upper atmospheric dynamics.
f9c4f23e-b71f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fabry-Perot Interferometer part of Optical Mesosphere Thermosphere Imagers

f9c6afe4-bab1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LANL1997 (or LANL-97A) is a geosynchronous spacecraft positioned in Earth's magnetosphere, specifically within the radiation belt, equipped with instruments to measure energetic electrons and ions.
f9c6afe4-bab1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geosynchronous spacecraft carrying energetic electron and ion instruments

f9d8d9a8-b98f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The EMN magnetometer network in Kuju, Japan is a ground-based facility located at Kokonoe, Kusu County, Oita Prefecture. It operates as part of the ICSWSE network and includes a fluxgate instrument for monitoring magnetic fields.
f9d8d9a8-b98f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kokonoe Observatory, Japan

f9da60fc-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Space Environmental Monitor-2 (SEM-2) is an energetic particle instrument onboard the MetOp-B satellite that measures the intensity of Earth's radiation belts and charged particle fluxes to monitor solar terrestrial phenomena and provide warnings of potential space weather impacts.
f9da60fc-b697-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Environmental Monitor 2 on MetOp-B

f9f98b44-b8c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cassini Plasma Spectrometer (CAPS) was an instrument onboard the Cassini spacecraft consisting of three sensors—the Electron Spectrometer (ELS), Ion Beam Spectrometer (IBS), and Ion Mass Spectrometer (IMS)—designed to study plasma interactions in Saturn's magnetosphere, auroral phenomena, and Titan’s atmosphere and ionosphere.
f9f98b44-b8c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cassini Plasma Spectrometer on Cassini Spacecraft

f9f9ff0e-b6a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate magnetometer installed at the Nagycenk observatory in Hungary, which is part of the IUGONET network and used for magnetic field measurements.
f9f9ff0e-b6a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of Cirum-Panonic Magnetometer Network Investigation, Hungary

f9fb98cc-bafb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Murrumbateman Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Murrumbateman, New South Wales, Australia. It operates as a ground-based observatory for conducting various astronomical observations and research.
f9fb98cc-bafb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Murrumbateman Observatory, Australia

fa02f52e-b8fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **EPI-Hi/LET1:** A low energy telescope (LET1) part of the EPI-Hi instrument onboard the Parker Solar Probe mission, designed to measure energetic electrons from approximately 0.5 MeV to 6 MeV, as well as protons and Helium nuclei in the upper portion of its energy range.
fa02f52e-b8fb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Energetic Particle Instrument on Parker Solar Probe

fa0aabb0-bc8f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mariner 9 Spacecraft Ultraviolet Spectrometer (UVS) was an instrument on NASA's Mariner 9 spacecraft that orbited Mars from 1971 to 1972. It studied the Martian atmosphere by analyzing ultraviolet light to determine its composition, detect gases like carbon dioxide, ozone, and water vapor, and monitor atmospheric phenomena such as dust storms and cloud formations.
fa0aabb0-bc8f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Mariner 9 Spacecraft Ultraviolet Spectrometer on Mariner 9 Spacecraft

fa0b723c-b601-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The TRZ Observatory is an astronomical ground-based observatory located in Bétera, Valencia, Spain.
fa0b723c-b601-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: TRZ Observatory, Spain

fa191976-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The AG_Sarajevo Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
fa191976-b6c1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: AG_Sarajevo Observatory, Bosnia and Herzegovina

fa1d5ff0-ba08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover Lander Visual System (LVS) is a camera-based navigation tool that captures images of the terrain during the rover's descent, comparing them with onboard maps to determine a safe landing position and avoid hazards within seconds.
fa1d5ff0-ba08-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover Lander Visual System part of Mars 2020

fa1df468-b7bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Multi-Channel Analyzer (MCA) is a type of Spectral Power Receiver used in the Very Low Frequency Wave Instruments onboard the Akebono spacecraft, designed to study low-frequency electromagnetic waves in Earth's magnetosphere. This instrument is part of the observatory network managed by Kanazawa University in Japan.
fa1df468-b7bc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Very Low Frequency Multi Channel Analyzer on Akebono Spacecraft

fa2a18fe-b70f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lourenco-Marques Geomagnetic Observatory (LMM) is a ground facility located in Maputo, Mozambique, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity since 1957. It operates under the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA).
fa2a18fe-b70f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lourenco Marques Geomagnetic Observatory, Mozambique

fa2fe7de-ba84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The SMARTS 1.3-meter Telescope, also known as the 2MASS 1.3m Telescope, is a Cassegrain reflecting telescope located at the Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile, used primarily for infrared astronomy.
fa2fe7de-ba84-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared The 2 Micron All Sky Survey 1.3m Telescope at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory, Chile

fa37ae0c-b9c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Genoa Observatory (also known as Osservatorio Astronomico di Genova) is an astronomical observatory located in Genoa, Italy. It serves as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical research and observations.
fa37ae0c-b9c5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Genoa Observatory, Italy

fa37dca6-b894-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Laboratorio Nacional de Astrofisica (LNA) 0.6m Zeiss Jena Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Pico dos Dias Observatory in South America, with an aperture of 0.6 meters.
fa37dca6-b894-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: optical Laboratorio Nacional de Astrofisica 0.6m Zeiss Jena Telescope at Pico dos Dias Observatory

fa39eeb0-b77c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Immanuel Kant Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Limbach-Oberfrohna, Germany. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to stargazing and astronomical research.
fa39eeb0-b77c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Immanuel Kant Observatory, Germany

fa4796fe-b72d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "MMS 2 Spacecraft Position" is a virtual instrument that provides the ephemeris data for the MMS 2 spacecraft, which is part of the CNES Observatory CDPP Archive.
fa4796fe-b72d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: MMS 2 Spacecraft Position part of Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission

fa4d1c78-b99e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Yap, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network and IUGONET Observatory. It measures magnetic field variations using the fluxgate principle.
fa4d1c78-b99e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of 210 Magnetic Meridian Network

fa5aabea-b5d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The University of Arizona/Lunar and Planetary Laboratory (LPL) 1.8m Spacewatch Telescope is an optical telescope located at the Kitt Peak National Observatory in North America, used primarily for astronomical research and space observation.
fa5aabea-b5d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.8m optical Spacewatch Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory

fa5b15a6-b865-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Savissivik (SVS) Geophysical Observatory** is a ground-based facility located in Savissivik, Greenland, which includes a magnetometer and operates as part of the DTU Space observatory network. It has been functional since January 1, 2007.
fa5b15a6-b865-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Savissivik Geophysical Observatory, Greenland

fa6076a8-bb2c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Zvjezdarnica Graberje Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Zagreb, Croatia. It is a ground-based facility used for sky observations and astronomical research.
fa6076a8-bb2c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Zvjezdarnica Graberje Observatory, Croatia

fa61e88c-bb7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the Laurel Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS GBO Network, operational since January 1, 2012.
fa61e88c-bb7a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Laurel Geophysical Observatory

fa66be52-b7a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The South Pole Photometer Instrument is a photometric device located at the South Pole ground station, designed to measure light intensity and other related optical properties.
fa66be52-b7a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Photometer part of Investigation of Cosmic Evolution with Star and Particle Tracking at Antarctica

fa694d8e-b17a-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **CPMN Garoua Station** is a ground-based magnetometer observatory located in Djim, Cameroon, part of the CPMN network. It provides magnetic field measurements and contributes to geophysical research within Africa.
fa694d8e-b17a-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Garoua Observatory, Cameroon

fa73e7e2-b73f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ultraviolet Spectrometer (UVS)** on board of Voyager 1 & 2 is a compact instrument designed to measure atmospheric properties and radiation by recording the entire ultraviolet spectrum within its range in a single exposure. It operates without moving parts and has specific spectral resolutions and optical configurations for different observation modes.
fa73e7e2-b73f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Spectrometer on Voyager 2

fa7b8b28-b924-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Observatory Großschwabhausen is an astronomical observatory located in Großschwabhausen, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility with the MPC (Minor Planet Center) ID 134.
fa7b8b28-b924-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Großschwabhausen Observatory, Germany

fa7ce44e-ba25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Operational Linescan System (OLS)** on the DMSP-5D3 F19 satellite is an imager that captures visible and infrared wavelengths to provide global cloud cover imagery at a resolution of 2.7 km, with limited high-resolution data at 0.56 km.
fa7ce44e-ba25-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Operational Linescan System on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program F19

fa829d12-ba61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** DSS-53 is a 34-meter radio telescope in Madrid, Spain, part of NASA's Deep Space Network, featuring an innovative beam waveguide design for enhanced signal transmission and reception.
fa829d12-ba61-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Radio Telescope part of The Deep Space Network, Spain

fa96b9c2-b7dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Agrupació Astronòmica de Terrassa (AAT) in Terrassa, Spain, is a ground observatory located at 7 Carrer de Martí Díez. It serves as an astronomical facility for observation and research within the Catalonia region of Europe.
fa96b9c2-b7dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomical Association of Terrassa Observatory, Spain

fa98dc8e-b9e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Talkeetna Geomagnetic Observatory (TLK) is a ground-based facility in Denali Borough, Alaska, dedicated to measuring and monitoring the Earth's magnetic field. It operates under the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy (IAGA) and contributes to global geomagnetic research.
fa98dc8e-b9e5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Talkeetna Geomagnetic Observatory

faa2195a-b843-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Uppsala Geomagnetic Observatory (UPS), previously known as the Uummannaq Geophysical Observatory, is a ground-based facility located in Ścinawa, Poland. It specializes in geomagnetic measurements and has been operational since January 1, 2007.
faa2195a-b843-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Uummannaq Geophysical Observatory

faa6c184-bae2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Ridge A**: An Antarctic ridge identified as the optimal site for astronomical research, located in the Australian Antarctic Territory.
faa6c184-bae2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: High Elevation Antarctic Terahertz Telescope on Ridge A, Antarctica

faa9a008-b6c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer at Syowa Station is an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields and has been operational since January 1958 as part of the IAGA investigation within the WDC Kyoto observatory.
faa9a008-b6c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Syowa Observatory, Antarctica

fab510aa-bb9f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Zinzen Observatory was a ground-based magnetic observatory located in Hwado-ro, Incheon, South Korea, operational from January 1921 to December 31, 1941. It was part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network and situated at an altitude of 50 meters above sea level with coordinates approximately 37.48°N latitude and 126.63°E longitude.
fab510aa-bb9f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Incheon Observatory, South Korea

fad24180-b63f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Langmuir Probe**, part of the Swarm Electric Field Instrument (EFI), is a space-based instrument launched on December 2, 2013. It utilizes two probes operating in harmonic mode to measure currents and admittances, representing a novel approach not previously used in orbit.
fad24180-b63f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Langmuir Probe part of Swarm Mission

fae1f804-b113-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Apollo 11 Early Apollo Scientific Experiment Package (EASEP) Passive Seismic Experiment (PSE) was the first seismometer placed on the Moon's surface, which detected lunar "moonquakes" and provided insights into the Moon's internal structure.
fae1f804-b113-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Passive Seismic Experiment part of Apollo 11 Early Apollo Scientific Experiment Package

faf01356-baca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Garching Observatory is a ground-based astronomical facility located at 6 Mitterweg, Garching bei München in Bavaria, Germany. It is situated at coordinates 48.25659° N latitude and 11.6569° E longitude on the continent of Europe.
faf01356-baca-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Garching Observatory, Germany

faf14978-b99a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The THEMIS Electrostatic Analyzers (ESAs) are instruments onboard the THEMIS spacecraft that measure the flux of thermal particles in a 360° field of view over an energy range from ~3 eV to 30 keV, providing full 3-D distributions, density, velocity, and temperature of ambient electrons and ions. There are two ESAs on each spacecraft, one for ions and the other for electrons.
faf14978-b99a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Electrostatic Analyzer part of Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms

fafcc90e-b71c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "TWINS 2 Positions" is a dataset that provides the ephemeris, or positional data, of the TWINS 2 spacecraft. It is part of the Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers (TWINS) observatory mission.
fafcc90e-b71c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers Positions on Spacecraft

fb04ed04-bb7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Infrared Optical Telescope Array (IOTA) is an astronomical facility located at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in North America, specifically designed for observations in the infrared waveband.
fb04ed04-bb7d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Infrared Infrared Optical Telescope Array at Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory

fb0c5d42-bb27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Poste-de-la-Baleine Magnetic Observatory**: A magnetic observatory located in Whapmagoostui, Quebec, Canada, that operated from September 1984 to June 2007.
fb0c5d42-bb27-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Poste de la Baleine Observatory, Canada

fb18c350-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Aalto University 13.7m Telescope is a radio telescope located at the Metsahovi Radio Observatory in Europe. It operates within the radio waveband and has an aperture of 13.7 meters.
fb18c350-ba3e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio 13.7m Telescope at Metsahovi Radio Observatory

fb1e41f8-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Inastars Observatory** is an astronomical facility located in Potsdam, Germany, known for its ground-based observations and research activities since 2006.
fb1e41f8-bb1b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Inastars Observatory, Germany

fb3c4fbe-ba16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Blanes Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Blanes, Catalonia, Spain, used for ground-based observations.
fb3c4fbe-ba16-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Blanes Observatory, Spain

fb3d521a-b9ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity is the **Digisonde ionospheric station at College, Alaska, USA** (URSI-code: CO764), an advanced ground facility that measures angle of arrival, polarization, and Doppler frequency shift of skywave signals reflected from the ionosphere to determine range to the reflection point.
fb3d521a-b9ad-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Digisonde ionospheric station at College Observatory, United States

fb4a53b8-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Owens Valley Radio Observatory (OVRO) is a radio astronomy facility located in Owens Valley, California, operated by the California Institute of Technology and known for its contributions to astronomical research.
fb4a53b8-b5af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: radio Owens Valley Radio Observatory at Big Pine, United States

fb4e3e9c-b7c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kakioka Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility in Ishioka, Ibaraki Prefecture, Japan, dedicated to the observation and study of magnetic phenomena on Earth.
fb4e3e9c-b7c6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kakioka Magnetic Observatory, Japan

fb4ee35a-b99d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Phoenix Lander Microscopy, Electrochemistry, and Conductivity Analyzer (MECA) Common Electronics managed power distribution, control systems, and data communication for the MECA instrument suite aboard the Phoenix Mars lander. It coordinated operations among instruments like the Atomic Force Microscope and Wet Chemistry Laboratory to analyze Martian soil and ice.
fb4ee35a-b99d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Microscopy, Electrochemistry, and Conductivity Analyzer Common Electronics on Phoenix Mars Lander

fb5613f4-b68d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The San Diego State University (SDSU) 1m (42-inch) Telescope, also known as the Illinois telescope, is an optical telescope located at Mount Laguna Observatory in North America.
fb5613f4-b68d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 1.0m San Diego State University Telescope at Mount Laguna Observatory

fb56fd72-ba53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Oulujärvi Geophysical Observatory (OUJ) is a ground-based facility in Vaala, Finland, that conducts geomagnetic measurements and has been operational since January 1993.
fb56fd72-ba53-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Oulujarvi Geomagnetic Observatory, Finland

fb5b2a9e-b72b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the IAGA station in Discovery Bay South, operational since 1903 and used for measuring magnetic field variations.
fb5b2a9e-b72b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Discovery Bay South Observatory

fb6cf202-b12b-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The 2.3-m Advanced Technology Telescope (ATT) is a 2.3 m telescope located at Siding Spring Observatory in Australia, operational since 1984.
fb6cf202-b12b-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: 2.3m Advanced Technology Telescope at Siding Spring Observatory, Australia

fb7930f4-b797-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Lindby Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Skurups kommun, Skåne County, Sweden. It is situated at the coordinates 55.435949° N, 13.51069° E and operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations.
fb7930f4-b797-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Lindby Observatory, Sweden

fb8a4b46-b8ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Osservatorio Antonio Grosso is an astronomical observatory located in Brugherio, Monza and Brianza, Lombardy, Italy. It is situated at the coordinates 9.3065 longitude and 45.545063 latitude on Earth.
fb8a4b46-b8ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Osservatorio Antonio Grosso, Italy

fb99d9c2-ba5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The specific magnetometer referenced here (IAGA:KUP) is located at Kupang station as part of the International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy's network, operational since January 1, 2006.
fb99d9c2-ba5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kupang Observatory

fba35372-b85d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Campo dos Amarais Observatory (X74) is an astronomical observatory located in Lagoa Azul, São Paulo, Brazil. It operates as a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
fba35372-b85d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Campo dos Amarais Observatory, Brazil

fbab8fb8-b634-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **GOES 12 Solar X-ray Imager (SXI)** is an instrument on the GOES-12 satellite that captures full-disk solar images in the 0.6-6.0 nm bandpass with a spatial resolution of ~10 arcsec and a temporal cadence of one minute, providing continuous monitoring except during orbital eclipse seasons.
fbab8fb8-b634-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar X-ray Imager on GOES 12

fbb37a10-b860-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The LFRTO (Low Frequency Radio Transmitter Observation) is a vertical electric monopole antenna located in Athabasca, Canada, designed to detect radio frequencies ranging from 20kHz to 100kHz. It operates as part of the THEMIS ground observatory network for magnetic field and auroral studies.
fbb37a10-b860-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Low Frequency Radio Transmitter Observation Antenna part of THEMIS Ground Magnetometer Array, Antarctica

fbcea596-b7ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** Deep Space Station 42 (DSS-42) is a retired 34-meter radio telescope located at the Tidbinbilla tracking station near Canberra, Australia. It was part of NASA's Deep Space Network and played a crucial role in early space missions, including returning the first close-up images of Mars from the Mariner 4 spacecraft.
fbcea596-b7ee-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 34m Deep Space Station 42 Radio Telescope at Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex, Australia

fbcfd116-bb2f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **St. Michel sur Meurthe Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Saint-Michel-sur-Meurthe, France. It is known for its ground-based observations and contributions to astronomy.
fbcfd116-bb2f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Saint-Michel-sur-Meurthe Observatory, France

fbd64560-b714-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Osservatorio astronomico di Cima Rest is an astronomical observatory located in Magasa, Italy, known for its ground-based facilities and observations.
fbd64560-b714-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cima Rest Observatory, Italy

fbdcd482-ba5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located in L'Aquila, Italy, specifically a 3-axis ring-core type fluxgate instrument used for geomagnetic field measurements.
fbdcd482-ba5e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IUGONET Observatory

fbe41c72-bac4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "GEOS-2 Conjugated Points" dataset consists of the footprints of magnetic field lines intersecting with the GEOS-2 spacecraft, derived from the Tsyganenko 1989 magnetic field model.
fbe41c72-bac4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GEOS-2 Conjugated Points part of GEOS-2 Observatory

fbed67da-ba2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Byrne Observatory is an astronomical observatory located at the Sedgwick Reserve in Santa Barbara County, California. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observation.
fbed67da-ba2b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sedgwick Reserve Observatory

fbf6ae64-b853-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MAGDAS fluxgate magnetometer at KRT is a 3-axis ring-core type instrument installed in Khartoum, Sudan, designed to measure the Earth's magnetic field as part of the MAGDAS observation network.
fbf6ae64-b853-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of MAGDAS Observation Network

fbf94dd0-b683-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Near Infrared Camera and Multi-Object Spectrometer (NICMOS) is a near-infrared spectrometer aboard the Hubble Space Telescope that operates at wavelengths from 800 to 2500 nm, featuring three detectors and three resolution modes. It is currently dormant, with its functions superseded by the Wide Field Camera 3 (WFC3).
fbf94dd0-b683-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Near Infrared Camera and Multi-Object Spectrometer on Hubble Space Telescope

fc06e426-ba85-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Las Cumbres 0.4m Telescopes equipped with the SBIG STL6303 Camera are part of the Las Cumbres Observatory Global Telescope Network (LCOGT), which operates a network of telescopes around the world for astronomical research and education.
fc06e426-ba85-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.4m Las Cumbres Telescopes at Las Cumbres Observatory Global Telescope Network

fc08b1f8-ba4d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A Photomultiplier Tube (PMT) is a highly sensitive detector of light that converts incident photons into electrical signals. The RENU2 mission used three PMTs to measure auroral emissions at specific wavelengths during its 2015 sounding rocket launch.
fc08b1f8-ba4d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Photomultiplier Tubes part of Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2

fc0caa2c-ba04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Javalambre Observatory (also known as the Observatorio Astrofísico de Javalambre) is an astronomical observatory located in Arcos de las Salinas, Gúdar-Javalambre, Teruel, Aragon, Spain. It functions as a ground-based observatory for astrophysical research and observations.
fc0caa2c-ba04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Javalambre Observatory, Spain

fc230968-b61f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Volkssternwarte Köln** is a public observatory located at the Elisabeth-von-Thüringen-/Schiller-Gymnasium in Cologne, Germany. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and educational purposes.
fc230968-b61f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Volkssternwarte Köln Observatory, Germany

fc290986-b8b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The S-300 search coil magnetometer is an instrument aboard the GEOS-2 satellite designed to measure AC magnetic fields up to 30 kHz, DC/AC electric fields, plasma resonances up to 80 kHz, and impedance. It features two vitreous carbon spheres on radial booms and sets of three-axis search coil magnetometers for different frequency ranges.
fc290986-b8b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Search Coil Magnetometer part of GEOS-2

fc31a2ec-b157-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The PENGUIn-5 (PG5) Geophysical Observatory Magnetometer is a scientific instrument located in Antarctica, designed to measure magnetic fields as part of the broader observational network known as "Antarctic Network."
fc31a2ec-b157-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at PENGUIn-5 Geophysical Observatory, Antarctica

fc37f8c8-b8cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Interball-1 Wide-range 3D Ion Spectrometer (CORALL)** is an electrostatic ion energy spectrometer on the Interball Tail Probe satellite, designed to perform quasi-3D measurements of the energy/charge ion distribution function in the range from 30 to 24200 eV/q. It has a fan-shaped field-of-view and operates with an accumulation time of approximately 100 msec per energy step, scanning one energy spectrum in about 4 minutes.
fc37f8c8-b8cc-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Wide-range 3D Ion Spectrometer on Interball Tail Probe

fc3a394a-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Vostok Magnetic Observatory** was a ground-based magnetic observatory located at Vostok Station in Antarctica, operational from 1958 to the end of 2017.
fc3a394a-baec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Vostok Geomagnetic Observatory, Antarctica

fc3ddf7a-b7e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Radiation Belt Storm Probe Ion Composition Experiment (RBSPICE) is an instrument onboard the Radiation Belt Storm Probe (RBSP) designed to measure the composition, energy, and pitch-angle distribution of ring current ions in Earth's inner magnetosphere, particularly during geomagnetic storms. It aims to understand the processes involved in creating and sustaining hazardous radiation particle populations.
fc3ddf7a-b7e3-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radiation Belt Storm Probes Ion Composition Experiment part of Radiation Belt Storm Probe

fc4232ee-b821-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Observatory "Stellar Society"** is an astronomical observatory located in Yundola, Bulgaria. It is a ground-based facility dedicated to astronomical research and observations.
fc4232ee-b821-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Observatory Stellar Society, Bulgaria

fc517956-b8a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **NOAA-17**, also known as NOAA-M before launch, was a polar-orbiting weather satellite operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), designed to provide meteorological data for prediction, warning, and environmental monitoring.
fc517956-b8a4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Advanced TIROS-N part of Polar Operational Environmental Satellites

fc564f22-bb32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Solar X-Ray Sensor (XRS) on GOES 14 is an instrument designed to observe and measure solar x-ray emissions, providing real-time data on the intensity and duration of solar flares to issue alerts for potential disruptions in radio communications and GPS signals.
fc564f22-bb32-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: x-ray Solar X-ray Sensor on GOES 14

fc5b8208-b8d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Yebes Observatory (Spanish: Centro Astronómico de Yebes) is an astronomical observatory located in Yebes, Castilla-La Mancha, Spain. It includes the Yebes 40m radio telescope and is part of unique scientific and technical infrastructure.
fc5b8208-b8d5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Yebes Observatory, Spain

fc5e8ec0-b7af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Mariner 7 Spacecraft Ultraviolet Spectrometer (UVS)** was an instrument aboard NASA's Mariner 7 spacecraft used to study the Martian atmosphere and surface by measuring ultraviolet light during a 1969 flyby, contributing valuable data on atmospheric composition.
fc5e8ec0-b7af-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ultraviolet Mariner 7 Spacecraft Ultraviolet Spectrometer on Mariner 7

fc66e522-ba05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **GOES 12 Positions** dataset provides the spatial coordinates and trajectory information for the GOES 12 spacecraft. This data is crucial for understanding the spacecraft's location and movement during its operational period.
fc66e522-ba05-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GOES 12 Position on GOES 12

fc6bb562-b8a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Magnetometers at Chiclayo (CCL) were instruments used to measure the Earth's magnetic field from January 1957 until December 31, 1960. They were part of the IUGONET observatory in Kyoto and were identified by the IAGA code CCL.
fc6bb562-b8a6-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Chiclayo Observatory

fc6cbd20-b73b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Union Observatory was an astronomical observatory that operated from 1903 to 1971 in Johannesburg, South Africa. Located atop Observatory Ridge, it was also known as the Transvaal Observatory and Republic Observatory.
fc6cbd20-b73b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Union Observatory, South Africa

fc711456-b920-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The ESO Boller and Chivens Spectrograph was an instrument used at the European Southern Observatory's La Silla 1.52m telescope, featuring a special dioptric camera for spectroscopic observations until its decommissioning in 2002.
fc711456-b920-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Boller and Chivens Spectrograph on 1.52m Telescope at La Silla Observatory

fc78fae4-b6ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rixeyville Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Culpeper County, Virginia. It operates as a ground-based observatory with the MPC code 783 and is situated at the coordinates 38.650286° N, 77.98° W on Holly Springs Road.
fc78fae4-b6ab-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rixeyville Observatory, United States

fc806fc6-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Lukiapang-1 was a ground-based observatory in Kunshan, China, operational from 1908 to 1933, primarily known for its magnetometer instrumentation.
fc806fc6-b913-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Lukiapang Observatory, China

fc86b9c2-b7eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Lake Forest Observatory**: An astronomical observatory located in El Dorado Hills, California, known for its ground-based facilities used for celestial observations.
fc86b9c2-b7eb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Forest Hills Observatory

fc8f04ea-ba3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Solar Optical Telescope (SOT)** is a space telescope designed to study the Sun's magnetic field and its impact on solar dynamics with high spatial resolution. Launched as part of the Hinode mission, it provides continuous observations with unparalleled temporal coverage and sensitivity.
fc8f04ea-ba3b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Solar Optical Telescope part of Hinode

fc9412a6-b94f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer deployed at Barter Island from 1957 to 1959, part of the IAGA investigation and associated with the Kyoto World Data Center for Geomagnetism (WDC-B).
fc9412a6-b94f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of International Association for Geomagnetism and Aeronomy

fc949d38-bae0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Serra Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Serra Riccò, Genoa, Liguria, Italy (Q115607650). It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial objects and phenomena.
fc949d38-bae0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Serra Observatory, Italy

fc95bbd2-b7a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Rantiga Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Tincana, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility and has been active since March 1, 2012.
fc95bbd2-b7a7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Rantiga Observatory, Italy

fc9b8a96-ba02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Amanecer de Arrakis Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Alcalá de Guadaíra, Sevilla, Spain. It operates as a ground-based facility with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) code Z74.
fc9b8a96-ba02-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Amanecer de Arrakis Observatory, Spain

fca08d62-b943-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Aarhus Wind Tunnel AWTSII 2010 is a low-pressure recirculating wind tunnel housed in a large tank, offering a significantly larger test volume compared to its predecessor.
fca08d62-b943-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: AWTSII 2010 at Aarhus Wind Tunnel

fca54aa8-b602-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Ion Chamber** on the Solar X-Ray Monitor (XRS) aboard GOES 5 was a scientific instrument designed to measure solar X-rays in two specific wavelength bands using ion chambers filled with different gas mixtures. It had high sensitivity and dynamic range, and utilized a magnetic field to prevent interference from charged particles.
fca54aa8-b602-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ion Chamber on GOES 5

fcac69d2-ba17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: GOES 13 is a geostationary weather satellite operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), launched in 2006 to monitor Earth's atmosphere and space environment.
fcac69d2-ba17-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Space Environment Monitor on GOES 13

fcb0c6c6-b986-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Eldagsen Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Eldagsen, Lower Saxony, Germany. It is classified as a ground-based observatory and operates under the MPC ID 573.
fcb0c6c6-b986-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Eldagsen Observatory, Germany

fcc0b592-baf1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Whitestar Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Tricesimo, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and observations.
fcc0b592-baf1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Whitestar Observatory, Italy

fcc962b0-b690-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Matosinhos Observatory (J11) is an astronomical observatory located in São Pedro d'Arcos, Ponte de Lima, Portugal. It is a ground-based facility focused on astronomy research and observations.
fcc962b0-b690-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Matosinhos Observatory, Portugal

fcca2bd0-b6e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Linear Etalon Imaging Spectral Array (LEISA) is an infrared spectrometer aboard the New Horizons spacecraft designed to map the distribution of various ices on Pluto and Charon by analyzing the unique spectral signatures of different molecules.
fcca2bd0-b6e2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Linear Etalon Imaging Spectral Array part of New Horizons

fcd2db0e-bb83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hopen (HOP) Geophysical Observatory, located in Svalbard, Norway, is a ground-based facility that includes a magnetometer and is part of the IUGONET observatory network.
fcd2db0e-bb83-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Hopen Geophysical Observatory, Norway

fcd396ae-b8de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The LICIACube Unit Key Explore (LUKE) instrument is a wide field RGB camera onboard the LICIACube satellite designed for multicolor analysis and imaging.
fcd396ae-b8de-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: The LICIACube Unit Key Explorer on LICIACube

fce946b4-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The W68 Observatory, also known as the ATLAS–CHL Observatory, is an astronomical facility located at El Sauce in Río Hurtado, Chile. It is part of the Asteroid Terrestrial Impact Last Alert System (ATLAS) and operates as a ground-based observatory.
fce946b4-b6dd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: El Sauce Observatory, Chile

fcea7a1c-bb91-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is an instrument used to measure magnetic fields. The PENGUIn-2 (PG2) Geophysical Observatory Magnetometer, deployed since January 8, 2009, is part of the Antarctic Network and is located at the PENGUIn-2 observatory.
fcea7a1c-bb91-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at PENGUIn-2 Geophysical Observatory, Antarctica

fced0964-b90a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Sanderphil Urban Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located in Civitavecchia, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
fced0964-b90a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sanderphil Urban Observatory, Italy

fcf0500a-bc71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS) 1m Sunrise balloon-borne solar observatory is an airborne telescope with a 1.0-meter aperture designed to observe the Sun in the ultraviolet waveband.
fcf0500a-bc71-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: ultraviolet Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research 1m Sunrise Balloon-Borne Solar Observatory

fcf056ce-b63e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Leningradskaya Observatory was a ground-based observatory located in the city of Leningradskaya. It operated from January 1, 1977, to February 28, 1979, and featured instruments including magnetometers.
fcf056ce-b63e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Leningradskaya Observatory

fcfb363c-b9ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) is a NASA space probe designed to explore Mars from orbit. It was launched in 2005 and has been studying the planet's climate, geology, and potential landing sites for future missions using advanced scientific instruments.
fcfb363c-b9ce-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label:
High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
Context Imager on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
Mars Climate Sounder on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
Shallow Subsurface Radar on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
Mars Color Imager on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter

fcfe30d6-b770-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Heavy Ion Telescope (HIT) from the Charge and Mass Magnetospheric Ion Composition Experiment (CAMMICE) suite is an instrument onboard the Polar spacecraft designed to measure ion mass, elemental identification, and incident energy in the range of ~100keV/ion to 60MeV/ion using a three-element Solid-State Detector.
fcfe30d6-b770-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Charge and Mass Magnetospheric Ion Composition Experiment Heavy Ion Telescope on Polar part of Charge and Mass Magnetospheric Ion Composition Experiment

fd0a38e4-baff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Middlebury College Observatory** is an astronomical observatory located at Middlebury College in Vermont, United States. It is a ground-based facility used for astronomical observations and research.
fd0a38e4-baff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Middlebury College Observatory, United States

fd0da346-ba49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: An astronomical observatory located in Fremont County, Colorado, United States, known as the Angel Peaks Observatory.
fd0da346-ba49-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Angel Peaks Observatory

fd1687a2-b8e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer in Trivandrum (TRD) that was operational from 1957 to 1999 as part of the IAGA investigation and IUGONET observatory network, used for measuring magnetic fields.
fd1687a2-b8e8-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Trivandrum Observatory

fd21bade-b7ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Moorpark College Observatory is an astronomical observatory located on Campus Road in Moorpark, Ventura County, California, dedicated to ground-based observations and education.
fd21bade-b7ec-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Moorpark College Observatory

fd24db5c-b19c-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "Imager Labs 4K CCD, white light, scroll shutter" is an astronomical instrument used for capturing high-resolution images in white light, with detailed specifications available through NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS).
fd24db5c-b19c-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Imager Labs 4K CCD on Mount Bigelow Observatory

fd34a26a-b96e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer is a scientific instrument used to measure the strength and direction of magnetic fields. The Kamenniyj.Mys Magnetometer was operational from January 1976 to December 31, 1980, as part of the IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) network at the Kamenniyj Mys observatory.
fd34a26a-b96e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Kamenniyj Mys Observatory

fd3a9f2c-ba5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity represents a lander spacecraft, specifically "lander.slim," from the JAXA DARTS context. It includes information about its components and is associated with the VOParis Observatory facilities schema.
fd3a9f2c-ba5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: SLIM on Lander

fd45bd6e-b84e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The HOB Observatory (MPC ID: L63) is an astronomical observatory located in Capraia Fiorentina, Italy. It operates as a ground-based facility for conducting astronomical observations and research.
fd45bd6e-b84e-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Capraia Fiorentina Observatory, Italy

fd489fa6-b6b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The "SNOE Positions" refers to the dataset containing the spacecraft positions of the Student Nitric Oxide Explorer (SNOE) mission, provided in various coordinate systems. This data is part of the SNOE observatory records and facilitates understanding the spacecraft's ephemerides during its operations.
fd489fa6-b6b5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Spacecraft Position on Student Nitric Oxide Explorer

fd491ee0-b868-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A magnetometer located at the San Antonio Geophysical Observatory, part of the THEMIS Mission GMAG investigation since 2007.
fd491ee0-b868-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at San Antonio Observatory

fd51b7e2-b6fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: Astronomical observatory located in Gdansk, Poland.
fd51b7e2-b6fd-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Danzig Observatory, Poland

fd661568-b93a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Port Moresby Ionosonde is a ground-based instrument located near Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, used for radar investigation of the ionosphere since 1961. It has employed various models over the years to collect and provide hourly scaled data and median data on parameters like foF2 and M(3000)F2.
fd661568-b93a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ionosonde at Port Moresby Observatory, Papua New Guinea

fd6b995e-baeb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The US Department of Energy Array of Low Energy X-ray Imaging Sensors (ALEXIS) Satellite Mission was a space mission designed to detect and image low-energy X-rays, primarily for astronomical observations.
fd6b995e-baeb-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray US Department of Energy Array of Low Energy X-ray Imaging Sensors Satellite Mission

fd724296-bc75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Astronomihagen Observatory is an astronomical facility located in Orkland, Trøndelag, Norway. It serves as a ground-based observatory for studying celestial objects and phenomena from Earth.
fd724296-bc75-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Astronomihagen Observatory, Norway

fd882a70-b9b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: K77, also known as the EHB01 Observatory, is an astronomical observatory located in Engelhardsberg, Germany. It operates as a ground-based facility for astronomical observations and research.
fd882a70-b9b4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Engelhardsberg Observatory, Germany

fd88456e-bb99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The National Radio Astronomy Observatory (NRAO) Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) is a radio astronomy observatory located on the plains of San Agustin in North America, known for its powerful telescopes used to study celestial phenomena through radio waves.
fd88456e-bb99-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Radio National Radio Astronomy Observatory Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array

fd88bb00-b6ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Meyer-Womble Observatory (MWO) is an astronomical observatory operated by the University of Denver, located near Mount Blue Sky's summit in Colorado. It stands as one of the highest optical/infrared observatories globally.
fd88bb00-b6ff-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Meyer–Womble Observatory

fd894c42-b8d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: A fluxgate magnetometer located in Zyryanka, part of the 210 Magnetic Meridian (210MM) magnetometer network and the IUGONET observatory. It measures magnetic field variations using a fluxgate sensor type.
fd894c42-b8d9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fluxgate Magnetometer part of 210 Magnetic Meridian Magnetometer Network

fd9e3dec-b748-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **United States Naval Observatory (USNO)** is a scientific and military facility in Washington, D.C., that provides geopositioning, navigation, and timekeeping data for the United States Navy and Department of Defense. Established in 1830, it is one of the oldest scientific agencies in the U.S. and a leading facility for astronomical and timing information.
fd9e3dec-b748-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: United States Naval Observatory

fda14c70-b794-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NSF NOIRLab 4m Nicholas U. Mayall Telescope is an optical telescope with a 4-meter aperture located at the Kitt Peak National Observatory in North America, funded by the National Science Foundation (NSF).
fda14c70-b794-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Optical 4.0m Nicholas U. Mayall Telescope at Kitt Peak National Observatory

fdb1c0ca-b620-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2L X-ray Instrument (XRI)** is a scintillation detector used in the BARREL project to measure the energy spectrum and flux of Bremsstrahlung X-rays produced by precipitating electrons, with an energy response ranging from 10 keV to 10 MeV.
fdb1c0ca-b620-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: X-ray Scintillation Detector part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

fdb745b4-b917-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Cha-Pa Geomagnetic Observatory (CPA) is a ground facility located in Sapa, Vietnam, specializing in geomagnetic measurements since 1957.
fdb745b4-b917-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Cha-Pa Geomagnetic Observatory, Viet Nam

fdb924ce-b665-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Plasma Experiment for Planetary Exploration (PEPE) was a general-purpose plasma sensor onboard the Deep Space 1 spacecraft, capable of measuring electrons and mass-resolved ions over a wide energy range using an electrostatically scanned field-of-view and a time-of-flight spectrometer.
fdb924ce-b665-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Plasma Experiment for Planetary Exploration on Deep Space 1

fdce4d40-bad4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Cluster Ion Spectrometry (CIS) on Cluster 2/FM8 (Tango)** is a mass spectrometer instrument on the Cluster II spacecraft, designed to measure full 3D ion distributions with high time and mass-per-charge resolution. It consists of two main sensors: the Hot Ion Analyzer (HIA) and the Composition and Distribution Function analyzer (CODIF).
fdce4d40-bad4-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cluster Ion Spectrometry on Cluster 2/FM8 (Tango) part of Cluster

fde527c8-b9cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Baker Lake Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility in Nunavut, Canada, dedicated to monitoring and studying the Earth's magnetic field.
fde527c8-b9cf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Baker Lake Magnetic Observatory, Canada

fde7e258-b6b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The MMS 4 FPI Suite's Dual Ion Spectrometer (DIS) is an instrument onboard the Magnetospheric Multiscale Mission (MMS) spacecraft that measures the velocity-space distribution of ions from 10 eV to 30 keV with a time resolution of 150 ms. It is part of the Fast Plasma Investigation (FPI) suite, which also includes dual electron spectrometers and instrument data processing units.
fde7e258-b6b7-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Dual Ion Spectrometer part of MMS 4 FPI Suite

fdf2c4ce-bc5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Astropriorat Observatory is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Carrer del Esports, la Torre de Fontaubella, Priorat, Tarragona, Catalonia, Spain. It is situated at coordinates 41.12333° N latitude and 0.86386° E longitude on the continent of Europe.
fdf2c4ce-bc5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 43 cm Telescope at Astropriorat Observatory, Spain

fdfb3026-b86d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **IGPP-LANL Rapid City Fluxgate Magnetometer** is a magnetometer instrument located at the IGPP-LANL observatory in Rapid City, used for measuring magnetic field variations. It is part of the broader IGPP-LANL Magnetometer Array network.
fdfb3026-b86d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer part of IGPP-LANL Magnetometer Array

fdfead18-b8f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **BARREL Balloon 2T Engineering Data Interface** is an instrument that performs analog to digital conversion (ADC) of key temperatures, voltages, and currents for the Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses (BARREL) project. It monitors eight voltage-current pairs, four voltage inputs, and sixteen temperature sensors with 16-bit precision.
fdfead18-b8f5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Platform part of Balloon Array for RBSP Relativistic Electron Losses

fe0358e0-b67a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Lord Howe Island station is a ground-based observatory located on Lord Howe Island, NSW, Australia. It has been operating a GPS Ionospheric Scintillation Monitor (ISM) since December 2009 to study ionospheric disturbances.
fe0358e0-b67a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: GPS ISM at Lord Howe Island Observatory, Australia

fe0b8e82-b672-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The NURO 0.79m (31-inch) telescope is a refurbished instrument originally installed in 1964 at Lowell Observatory's Anderson Mesa Dark Sky Site, initially used for lunar mapping by the U.S. Geological Survey and later becoming a key research tool for undergraduate astronomical studies.
fe0b8e82-b672-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.79m Telescope at Lowell Observatory, United States

fe0dc2a4-bbbf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The CoRoT satellite mission is a joint venture between the French Space Agency (CNES) and the European Space Agency (ESA), designed to study stellar convection, rotation, and search for exoplanets using a 0.27m optical telescope in space.
fe0dc2a4-bbbf-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: 0.27m optical Convection, Rotation, and planetary Transits on French Space Agency/European Space Agency CoRoT Satellite Mission

fe0e1f16-ba5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The GOES 10 Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer is an instrument aboard the GOES 10 satellite designed to measure magnetic field variations in space with high precision and accuracy. It operates within a range of ±1000 nanoTesla (nT) and provides essential data for monitoring space weather conditions.
fe0e1f16-ba5b-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer on Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 10

fe0f520a-bc04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition**: The Surface Electric Sounding and Acoustic Monitoring Experiment (SESAME) was a scientific experiment onboard the Rosetta Philae lander, designed to study the properties of comet surfaces using acoustic sounding, dust impact monitoring, and permittivity measurements.
fe0f520a-bc04-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: The Surface Electric Sounding and Acoustic Monitoring Experiment for the Rosetta Philae Lander part of Rosetta mission

fe1e53d2-b974-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Casselman Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Casselman, Ontario, Canada, with the Minor Planet Center (MPC) ID G30.
fe1e53d2-b974-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Casselman Observatory

fe200896-b76f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Fast Plasma Experiment (FPE) and Solar Wind Ion Experiment (SWE)** on the International Sun-Earth Explorer 1 (ISEE-1) satellite were designed to study plasma velocity distributions and their variations in various regions of space, including the solar wind, magnetosphere, and magnetotail. The instruments used electrostatic analyzers to measure proton and electron energies, providing detailed insights into space plasma dynamics.
fe200896-b76f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Fast Plasma Experiment and Solar Wind Ion Experiment on International Sun-Earth Explorer 1

fe214660-ba4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Radio Science Subsystem (RSS) on Voyager 1 is an instrument designed to conduct radio occultation experiments by analyzing signals to study planetary atmospheres, ring systems, and gravitational fields.
fe214660-ba4f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waveform Receiver on Voyager 1

fe2f1430-ba76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Kihei-AMOS Remote Maui Experimental Site is a ground observatory located in Hawaii, specifically at Lipoa Parkway in the Maui Research Technology Park. It serves as an astronomical research facility, positioned at coordinates 20.74607° N latitude and 153.5683° W longitude (note: longitude corrected from 203.5683).
fe2f1430-ba76-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Remote Maui Experimental Site at Kihei Observatory, United States

fe54d574-baf5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The European Consortium for VLBI European Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) Network is a ground-based observatory on Earth that operates in the radio waveband, using intercontinental arrays of telescopes to achieve high angular resolution and sensitivity.
fe54d574-baf5-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: European Very Long Baseline Interferometry Network

fe604472-b9c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Cherryvalley Observatory**, located in Rathmolyon, Ireland, is an astronomical observatory dedicated to ground-based observations.
fe604472-b9c9-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Cherryvalley Observatory, Ireland

fe6a68ac-b88a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The HID (Heavy Ion Detector) on Double Star 1 is an energetic particle instrument designed to detect heavy ions with atomic mass units greater than 4.
fe6a68ac-b88a-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Heavy Ion Detector on Double Star 1

fe6c5e86-b6a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The **Hamburg Observatory**, also known as the **Hamburg-Bergedorf Observatory**, is an astronomical research facility located in Bergedorf, Hamburg, Germany. It was founded in 1825 and has been operated by the University of Hamburg since 1968.
fe6c5e86-b6a1-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Hamburg-Bergedorf Observatory, Germany

fe6e78f4-b176-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.definition:
**Entity Definition**:
Apollo 16 was the fifth mission to land humans on the Moon and return them safely to Earth. Launched on April 16, 1972, it included a lunar module landing in the Descartes highland region, three moonwalks totaling over 20 hours, and the collection of 94.7 kg of rock and soil samples.
fe6e78f4-b176-11f1-8a57-405b7f7031a0.label: Lunar Surface Magnetometer part of Apollo 16

fe813fc0-bb5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Charge and Mass Magnetospheric Ion Composition Experiment (CAMMICE) on the Polar spacecraft is an instrument designed to determine the composition of Earth's plasma populations, their sources, and the mechanisms that energize and transport these populations within the magnetosphere/ionosphere and magnetosphere/solar-wind systems. It incorporates two sensor systems, MICS and HIT, which measure ion composition over a range from <10 keV/Q to 15 MeV/Q for elements from hydrogen through iron.
fe813fc0-bb5d-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Charge and Mass Magnetospheric Ion Composition Experiment part of Polar

fe87b22c-bace-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The entity "RBSP A Positions" refers to the position data of the Radiation Belt Storm Probes (RBSP) A spacecraft, providing its locations in various coordinate systems. This data is part of the RBSP observatory mission and facilitates understanding the spacecraft's trajectory for scientific investigations.
fe87b22c-bace-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Ephemeris part of Radiation Belt Storm Probes

fe892f6e-bbd0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The BAS A80 Geomagnetic Observatory, located at approximately 80.8 degrees geographic latitude and 339.6 degrees east longitude, is a ground-based facility established on January 7, 1997, dedicated to monitoring geomagnetic activity on Earth's surface.
fe892f6e-bbd0-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Geomagnetic Observatory at Augsburg Observatory

fe8fc260-b8ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Wartburg College Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Waverly, Iowa, United States. It serves as a ground-based facility for astronomical research and education.
fe8fc260-b8ac-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Waverly Observatory

fe974d0a-bb13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The Orcadas Magnetic Observatory is a ground-based facility located in the Antarctic region, specifically at Orcadas Base on Laurie Island, South Orkney Islands. It has been operational since 1903 and specializes in monitoring Earth's magnetic field using magnetometers.
fe974d0a-bb13-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Orcadas Del Sur Observatory, Antarctica

fe9a04c0-ba3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The OMNI observatory is a virtual space facility that aggregates data from multiple spacecraft, such as ACE and Wind, to provide the best available datasets for research purposes. It operates within the Heliosphere near Earth and selects optimal data records from various contributing observatories based on specific criteria.
fe9a04c0-ba3f-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: OMNI Observatory

fea5f734-b5c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Breslau Magnetometer was an instrument used for measuring magnetic fields, operational from 1852 to 1895 at the IAGA observatory in Breslau.
fea5f734-b5c2-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Magnetometer at Breslau Observatory

fea8dc54-b970-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Schiaparelli Gallarate Station is a ground-based astronomical observatory located in Cascinetta, Gallarate, Varese, Lombardy, Italy. It functions as a facility for conducting various astronomical observations and research activities.
fea8dc54-b970-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Schiaparelli Gallarate Observatory, Italy

feaafd8e-bb5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: **Definition:** The CLPS Task Order 2-AB Linear Energy Transfer Spectrometer (LETS) is a radiation monitor featuring a solid-state silicon Timepix detector, designed to measure incident radiation rates on the lunar surface, crucial for understanding and mitigating radiation hazards during Moon exploration. It is derived from hardware used on Orion EFT-1 and planned for the Orion EM-1 mission.
feaafd8e-bb5c-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Linear Energy Transfer Spectrometer on Peregrine Lunar Lander

feb3090c-b729-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.definition: The Hatamae Observatory is an astronomical observatory located in Aoba Ward, Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture, Japan. It is a ground-based facility used for studying celestial bodies and phenomena.
feb3090c-b729-11f1-985a-405b7f7031a0.label: Sendai Observatory, Japan
